author: jeremeybingham
body:
## What and why

Closes #113. A county written where the city belongs (`MIAMI DADE`, `BROWARD`, `HENNEPIN`, `COOK`) got no place and no warning, so a pipeline could not tell it from a misspelled city or a placeholder. It now gets a new warning, `city_is_county`: the city is no place of the state but the name of one of its counties, with or without `COUNTY` (option 1 of the issue). `place` stays empty and the city is kept as written. A name that is also a place of the state (`COOK`, MN) is the place and is not flagged. The county names come from the national place list (a sorted `STATE|county` table built in `build.rs`; `Lexicons::is_county` is crate-private). Option 2 (taking the ZIP's main place) and `FL` / `FLORIDA` written as the city are not part of this change.

Measured (the key is not touched: the warning is added after assembly):

- Against the frozen checkpoint keys (`checkpoint-1819acd`), `key_diff.py diff`: 0 keys changed in 12.7M rows. The warning is on 0.013% of the amateur-radio rows, 0.017% of the tax-exempt list and 0.024% of the carrier census.
- Netsyms sample, `compare.py` (`main` before, this branch after): one row gains the warning (1 of 1,138,982); every other warning and mismatch count is identical.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` pass
- [x] A parsing bug fix adds a golden-corpus case (`tests/corpus/README.md`); `tests/corpus/passing.txt` is updated if more cases now pass (`pl-009` to `pl-013`)
- [x] A parse-rule change adds a row to `docs/usps-pub28-notes.md` with its source
- [x] A change to what an input produces as a key uses a new version prefix and updates `docs/key-format.md` (not applicable: no key changes)
- [x] Python changes: `pytest crates/doorplate-py/tests` passes
- [x] Related documentation checked and updated: `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md`, `docs/warnings.md`, `docs/usps-pub28-notes.md`, `tests/corpus/README.md`, the demo's warning text
- [x] No personal data: examples and corpus cases are invented

author: nero-ot
body:
The transit API lockfile pins vulnerable versions of proxy-addr, qs and body-parser. Update their compatible dependency trees to proxy-addr 2.0.8, qs 6.16.1 and body-parser 2.4.0, addressing Dependabot alerts #1–#5. Express remains 5.2.1; application routes and proxy configuration are unchanged.

Add seven isolated regression tests covering the five advisory failures, forwarded-IP handling, and valid/malformed/oversized JSON. Five regression tests fail against the original lockfile and pass against the updated tree. The request checks use an in-memory Express app and no listening sockets or database.

Validation:
- Node 22.23.4: npm run check passes; npm test passes 85/85.
- npm ci --ignore-scripts succeeds; npm ls resolves the patched packages without errors.
- npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities in backend/transit_api.
- git diff --check and the pre-commit secret scan pass.
- PR CI passes: python, data, transit-api, frontend, CodeQL (Python/JavaScript/Actions) and GitGuardian.
- No local database, Railway or deployed-runtime checks performed. The data CI job uses its disposable PostgreSQL service.

Merging deploys to production. This updates transit-api runtime dependencies and their supporting transitive packages; the lockfile also synchronizes the existing package name/version metadata. No migration, environment/settings change, frontend rebuild or production action is included. The remaining Python, PDF.js, frontend-tooling and CodeQL review items are separate scopes; their alerts are not addressed by this PR.

Implemented with Codex.

author: elvis-sik
body:
The 107-card publication introduced two reports whose first-disclosure dates are unknown. The site correctly excludes them from the disclosure-gap filter, but two pre-existing test expectations treated every report date as a first disclosure. This caused twelve post-publication failures across six browser configurations.

Update only the test oracle and strengthen direct unknown-date filter/reload checks with a known-date positive control. No product code, catalog content or generated assets change. All 24 affected browser checks pass locally across Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, iPhone, Pixel and dark mode; CI runs the complete suite against the actual published catalog.

body:
## 변경 요약
- **probe 문항 선택**: `scripts/calibrate_threshold.py probe --rows korquad-partial` — 검색이 정답을 놓친 KorQuAD(관련 문서는 있지만 문맥에 답이 없는 위키 안 partial 질문)를 partial 프롬프트로 돌리고, 답에 정답이 들어 있는지 기록

- **probe-report 단계**: 라벨(a · b · c, 빈 답 `-`)을 적은 probe 결과들을 설정별로 모아 `reports/{날짜}-partial-probe.md` 에 쓴다 — 빈 답 · 잘림 · 시간 · 생각 길이 · 해로운 답 비율과 95% 상한, 위키 안 질문은 정답 포함, 고른 설정의 종류별 표. 라벨이 빠진 결과가 있으면 멈춘다

- **리포트**: `reports/2026-10-24-partial-probe.md` — 집계만, 질문 원문 없음

## 변경 이유
- partial 을 think off 로 둔 근거(빈 답 · 지연)와 low 가중치를 정한 해로운 답 비율을 레포에서 다시 확인할 수 있게 남긴다. 위키 밖 질문 57: think off · 2048 빈 답 0 · 해로운 답 1/39, think on · 2048 빈 답 44, think on · 8192 빈 답 36(문항당 170초). 위키 안 partial 11: think off 빈 답 0 · 정답 포함 4, think on · 8192 빈 답 9 · 정답 포함 1 — 생각이 수렴하지 않고 한도까지 가는 것이 위키 밖 · 위키 안 모두에서 나왔다

## 테스트 방법
- `uv run ruff check` · `uv run ruff format --check` 통과

- `uv run pytest` — 85개 통과 (Windows 는 `PYTHONUTF8=1` 필요: 기존 `test_ruff_bans` 의 cp949 문제)

- 재현: `uv run python scripts/calibrate_threshold.py probe --think off` · `probe --think on --max-tokens 8192 --num-ctx 12288` · `probe --rows korquad-partial --think off` (Ollama · PG 필요) → 결과 파일에 라벨을 적고 `probe-report`. 데이터 파일은 `data/eval/` (git 제외)

- Refs #4

author: umeranjum17
body:
`npm run quality` used to print `quality: passed` after gating only the two synthetic takes. It never measured a real-UI take, never ran the all-frame text-cut audit, and called a run with unmet goals a pass. This change closes all three gaps.

## What changed

- **A real-UI fixture.** `npm run quality` now also builds `scene`, the headless capture of the staged board scene (`scripts/headless-scene.mjs --cursor=hidden`), and gates it with the same checks as `synth` and `portrait`: stream tags, frame count, hitches, determinism, camera bars, judder, OCR, banding and the golden SSIM/VMAF comparison.
- **Every frame's text cuts.** Each fixture's render goes through `scripts/cut-audit.ts`, using the camera it was rendered with. The new metrics are `text_cut_at_rest` and `text_cut_creeping`, with a goal of 0 each, and the full audit is stored as `cutAudit` in the JSON. The audit binds its end to `camera.json`'s clock. A wrong or missing end, or a source frame that won't decode, throws instead of reading clean.
- **No "passed" with unmet goals.** The baseline ratchet still gates regressions only. A run that holds the baselines but misses goals now lists each unmet goal, also recorded as `goalsUnmet`. Only a run with every goal met prints `quality: passed`.
- `--init-baseline` now adds a missing fixture, measurement or golden, and never replaces a stored one. Banded judder tracks each fixture's own sidebar divider; on the scene that is the nav border.
- **`--fixture <name>`** (repeatable) runs only the named fixtures. A partial run says what it skipped, in its last line (`... for synth, portrait only (not run: scene) ...`) and in `fixturesNotRun`, so it never reads as the whole bar. The sharpness check runs with `synth`.
- **CI:** `checks` runs the synthetic gates as before (`--fixture synth --fixture portrait`). A new parallel `quality-scene` job runs `--fixture scene` with a 120-minute timeout and uploads its own artifact. The required `ci` check waits for both. It stays deterministic, with no model calls or keys.
- **Scene judder is enforced with its measured spread.** On frame-identical renders, judder read 1.0309 on a dev host and 1.0523 on the CI runner, so the first CI run failed the ratchet on encoder noise alone. A fixture can now declare a metric's measured cross-machine spread: the scene allows judder 0.03 above its baseline, a limit of 1.0609, with a one-line comment giving those numbers. A control render with a 1 px shift injected every fourth frame reads 1.692 through the same `judder()` and `regressions()`, and still fails: `subpixel_judder: 1.6923615324633847 vs limit 1.0308641996086398 + measured spread 0.03`.
- Added a scene golden (`scripts/quality-baseline/scene.mp4`, 29.8 MB) and baseline entries for the scene and the new cut metrics. **Reviewer call:** this follows the existing golden pattern (synth and portrait are 25 MB together), but it does add 29.8 MB to the repository.
- Docs: `docs/quality.md`. Verify skill: new feature entry `run-the-output-quality-gates.md` and a `quality` journey in `.done-done.yaml` that checks the fixtures, the per-frame audit and the last line mechanically.

## Before and after

Both runs used a clean checkout. Before is main 7ef69a1. After was measured on this branch at 24304a6, and the head 48248d2 is re-proved by the sealed verify below; the counts are identical.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| fixtures gated | synth, portrait | synth, portrait, **scene (real UI)** |
| all-frame text-cut audit | not run | every frame of every fixture, end bound to `camera.json` |
| last line with unmet goals | `quality: passed` | `no regression against the stored baselines, but 4 goals are not met:` followed by each goal |
| exit | 0 | 0 (no regression) |
| run time on the test host (loaded, low priority) | 247 s | 1577 s |

Cut audit, after:

| fixture | frames | at rest | creeping | sweeping (allowed) | bound end |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| synth | 1878 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 34.68 s |
| portrait | 553 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 9.2 s |
| scene | 2371 | 0 | 0 | 282 | 39.5 s |

On a copy of the scene take with `trim_end: 39.5` set explicitly, the standalone audit gives the same 0 / 0 / 282 PASS. With `trim_end: 30` it exits 1: `end 30 s gives 30 s of output, but camera.json runs 39.5 s`.

### CI time per job at 48248d2

The run is [40054230526](https://github.com/umeranjum17/takeone/actions/runs/40054230526); all 8 checks are green.

| job | time | what it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `checks` | 21 m 49 s | floor guard, typecheck, tests, synthetic quality gates (`--fixture synth --fixture portrait`), the same command as before plus the cut audit |
| `quality-scene` (new, parallel) | 44 m 57 s | capture, plan and render the real-UI scene twice, gate it, audit all 2371 frames |
| `headless-scene` parts | 10 m 17 s – 10 m 57 s | unchanged |
| `ci` (required) | waits for `checks` and `quality-scene` | about 45 min of wall time per code PR, up from about 22 |

On CI the scene measured 0 frames cut at rest, 0 creeping and 283 while sweeping (282 on the dev host), with the end bound at 39.5 s. The golden held at mean SSIM 0.995; the runner's ffmpeg has no libvmaf, so this is the SSIM-only gate. Judder read 1.0523 and then 1.0487 on two CI runs, against 1.0309 on six dev-host runs, all inside the 1.0609 limit.

### Numbers that did not improve, stated plainly

- **portrait caption OCR:** still 2 checkpoints off, which was already true on main. The difference is that the run now says so.
- **scene subpixel judder:** 1.03 px/frame² over 512 samples, against a goal of 0.15. This is the first time judder has been measured on a moving camera; synth and portrait don't move. I looked at the decoded pixels: the nav border is only about 15 luma levels deep over a grainy background, so the centroid picks up background gradients, which is also why encoders on different machines disagree. The value is listed as an unmet goal and enforced against its baseline plus the measured spread. It is not confirmed as visible judder.
- **Painted cursor (why the scene is captured cursor-free):** a first capture with the painted cursor reported 6 frames "cut at rest" at 34.75–34.83 s. Looking at those frames, it was the arrow sliced by the card's top edge as it left the shot, not text. The fixture is therefore captured cursor-free: the render draws the cursor after the crop, so the audit reads only UI and the scene's at-rest baseline is 0. Any real at-rest text cut now fails CI.

Baseline file, kept in this description and not in the evidence line: `takeone-a40-before.txt`.

I looked at a contact sheet of 12 scene frames, mostly taken during camera sweeps (`takeone-a40-after.png`). Text is sliced only in frames inside the reported sweep runs, and the held frames are clean. The sheet is not in the evidence line because a board frame cannot show the gate's result.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The cut audit and the render's text guard decode one source frame per seek. Decoding the scene's source once in sequence would shorten the `quality-scene` job, but it means restructuring the decode the render and the audit share, so it is left out of this PR.
- A judder edge on the scene with enough contrast to measure.
- The verify skill's core journey still proves a synthetic render only; the quality journey covers the real-UI take.

## Checks
outcome: `npm run quality` now gates a real-UI take (the headless board scene) next to the synthetic ones, audits every rendered frame of each fixture for text cuts on an end bound to camera.json, and prints "passed" only when every goal is met, listing each unmet goal otherwise
repro: npm run quality on main 7ef69a1 printed "quality: passed" with only synth and portrait gated, no cut audit and 3 goals unmet; on this branch the same command gates synth, portrait and scene with the per-frame cut audit and lists the 4 unmet goals; node scripts/cut-audit.ts on a scene copy with take.json trim_end 39.5 gives 0/0/282 PASS and with trim_end 3

body: ## Alberta-Cars production change ### What changed Catalog search, the sell form, and owner edits now share colour, engine volume, power, body, drivetrain, transmission (including CVT), and a 28-code feature allowlist. Filters sync to the URL. A listing page shows a specifications table and grouped options. Migration `supabase/migrations/20261024001000_catalog_specs_and_features.sql` is in the repo only. It is not applied. Apply it yourself, after `20261023213000_protect_profile_trust_columns.sql`, in one transaction, and before deploying this app: ``` psql "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction \ -f supabase/migrations/20261024001000_catalog_specs_and_features.sql ``` The migration backfills colour, engine litres (`3.6 L` and bare `3.6`), and the 11 live feature labels to codes. It maps stored `Pickup` to `Truck/Pickup`. It drops `listings_transmission_allowed` and adds it again as `NOT VALID` with `Automatic`, `Manual`, and `CVT`, then `VALIDATE`s it. Other CHECKs (price, mileage, year minimum, description, city, colour, engine, power, body, drivetrain, fuel, features) are also added `NOT VALID` and validated in a later statement after a pre-check. The year upper bound is a trigger (`current year + 1`), not a CHECK. `engine_l` and `power_hp` are granted to anon. `color_legacy` is not. QA round 3 allowlists in this same migration and in Zod, the filter sheet, and the sell form: - Transmission: `CVT` - Body label/value: `Truck/Pickup` (old `Pickup` rows are rewritten) - Features: `Bluetooth` (Tech) and `Cruise control` (Safety, separate from Adaptive cruise). Cardinality cap is 28, the length of the allowlist. Search still ANDs at most 12 features. ### Risk - [ ] No database/auth/storage change - [x] Database/RLS migration reviewed - [ ] Authentication or recovery flow affected - [ ] Photo upload/storage affected - [ ] Deployment/security headers affected Deploying this app before the migration makes public listing pages fail, because they select `engine_l` and `power_hp`. The catalog list query does not select those columns, so the homepage can still load. `tests/security-live.test.cjs` expects anon to read `engine_l`, `power_hp`, `color`, and `features`, and to be denied `color_legacy`. That assertion returns 400 until the migration is applied. ### Required checks - [x] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test:unit` passed locally (18 unit tests) - [ ] `npm run test:security-live` — 9 passed, 1 failed: anon select of `engine_l` is 400 until the migration is applied - [x] Filter and sort Playwright checks passed locally on desktop Chromium and Pixel (CVT, Truck/Pickup path, SUV, AWD, mileage, scroll) - [ ] Full Playwright matrix and listing-page e2e will fail until the migration is applied - [ ] Supabase security/performance advisors reviewed after database changes - [x] Web bundle does not include Telegram runtime assets - [ ] Legal/privacy text reviewed if data collection or providers changed ### Release verification - [ ] Vercel preview/build succeeded - [ ] Critical flows were smoke-tested - [x] Rollback path is known (commented at the bottom of the migration; do not deploy the app until the SQL is applied, or roll the app back first) ### Left for later Visual restyle of the filter sheet is a design follow-up. VIN, trim, condition, accident history, hide-sold, and similar cars are out of scope. Authenticated table SELECT still sees `user_id` and `color_legacy`; this PR does not narrow that grant. `schema.sql` is left stale on purpose.

author: alexandrapaiz
body:
**Branched from main.** My previous pull request, #408, is merged and on main, so there was no open writer pull request to build on or supersede. **Not a chain**, depth zero.

## What I took

The next item in my lane. My own board columns held nothing queued, so I took the one card on the board that names this seat as its blocker, **the desk's verdict queue needs a cap or a filter, and the words for it** (board `8787a154`, frontend seat). Its own body says the remaining half "needs the writer seat first" and that "it needs one approved string."

Also moved `c2697491` to Done, since the work it tracks is what #408 merged.

## The finding

**The owner's console prints a wrong number in its largest type, and the entry the number is missing is the entry about numbers like this one.**

`site/app/desk/page.jsx` reads `docs/ideas.md` with its own regular expression. `tools/ledger.py` exists in this repository because reading that file by grep loses entries, which was recorded in the incident register on 2026-09-24. The desk is a fourth grep reader of that file and it is the one she opens daily. The two readers disagree by one entry, and the entry is

```
2026-09-24 — A ledger entry can hide from every consumer by writing its
status as a sentence (engineer agent)
```

Its status line reads `proposed`. Twenty lines above it, inside its own first bullet, it quotes `grep "Status: accepted" docs/ideas.md` as the command that would have missed the defect it was filed about. The desk's pattern carries no line anchor, so it matches inside that quoted command, reads the entry as `accepted`, and drops it. **The entry warning that a status written as a sentence hides an entry from every consumer is hidden from her console, by a status written as a sentence, in its own body, and it has never appeared in her queue.**

The fix is one character and one flag. It is drafted, not set, because `site/` is the frontend seat's surface.

## The words, and why there are four of them

The card asked for one string and suggested capping the list at eight, "because the precedent for capping already exists on the same page." The cap transfers and the order under it does not.

`gh("pulls?state=closed")` returns newest first. `parseIdeas` returns file order and `docs/ideas.md` is appended to, so the verdict queue is oldest first. Capping it at eight as proposed prints eight proposals from 2026-09-18 and drops row 524, which is the live compute outage. The two lists look alike and only one of them is sorted.

There is a second asymmetry the precedent hides. The merged list is a record, so eight of it is a sample. The verdict queue is a list of decisions she owes, so eight of it is 516 obligations behind a number nobody reads.

**The shape decided.** Render every entry marked `urgent`, which is 39 rows. Render no entry marked `proposed`. Say both numbers above the rows rather than below them, because a notice at the bottom tells her what she was looking at after she has finished looking. Not a filter, because a filter asks her to type something in order to find out what she owes, which hands the choosing back.

`open →` comes off the row, since 39 identical calls to action landing in one file is the wallpaper the card's own second finding names. The precedent for a link with no affordance is three sections down on the same page. One condition returns it, and it is in the ledger for the frontend seat rather than asserted here.

## The numbers, measured at `origin/main`

The ref matters, because the page fetches `docs/ideas.md` from `main` over raw.githubusercontent and not from any checkout. This run appended three ledger entries of its own, which moved the working tree to 527 and left the live surface where it was.

| | |
|---|---|
| rows the page renders | 524 |
| what `tools/ledger.py --census` counts | 525 |
| marked `urgent` | 39 |
| marked `proposed` | 485 on the page, 486 in the contract |
| what the card recorded on 2026-10-14 | 426 |

The queue grew by 98 in ten days and nothing left it. That is why both counts in the candidate are slots and not numerals.

## No generator patch, and the argument for that

`prompts/digest.md` is **byte-identical to main** in this pull request, and the review says why rather than leaving it silent.

The press has printed nothing since 2026-10-05. `site/content/issues/` holds `2026-W37` and `2026-W39` and nothing else, and line 3 of `2026-W39` still carries the masthead run 44 drafted the repair for. `measure`, `links`, `firstuse` and `generator` return the figures run 44 recorded, on the same two files. Run 44 found that four of the five rules that artifact fails are younger than the print itself, so a third grade of an unchanged artifact against unchanged rules produces a third wording of a rule aimed at a number that does not exist yet. **The first real test of those rules is the next send, and the next send is blocked on the compute outage that is row 524 of the list this run is about.**

## The instrument this run added

```
$ python3 -I docs/voice/check_voice.py ledger origin/main

  FAIL    proposed   desk  485   contract  486
  OK      urgent     desk   39   contract   39
            total      desk  524   contract  525
```

It reads the status pattern out of the desk page rather than holding a copy, so a rewrite of the parse cannot pass it by accident. It compares the two counts rather than grepping for a known-good regex, because a check that looks for a string passes on any pattern containing it and says nothing about the number on the surface. It takes a ref, because the count she reads comes off `main`.

Probed against the one-character fix in a scratch copy of the page: 486 and 486, `rc=0`. `git diff origin/main -- site/` is empty afterwards.

## Contents

- `docs/voice/desk-verdict-queue-2026-10-24.md` — the four lines, the rule that places them, the anchor beside them, and the measurement
- `docs/voice/reviews/2026-10-24-desk-queue.md` — the graded review, the taste gate ruling by ruling, the laws that bind and the ones that do not
- `docs/voice/check_voice.py` — the `ledger` check
- `docs/voice/ban-list.md` — entry 133, third in a family with 109 and 112, with its `LANDED` line verified
- `docs/voice/awaiting-her-word.md` — the desk's row, the eleventh and the first that is not public copy
- `docs/agents/incidents.md` — `INC-2026-10-24-the-entry-about-hiding-is-hidden-from-the-owners-console`, recorded as a repeat of the 2026-09-24 finding
- `docs/ideas.md` — three asks: the standards gap for the ExO's relay, whether the claims register covers a computed figure, and the GitHub anchor question for the frontend seat

## What is waiting on whom

- **The frontend seat.** Four lines and the anchor, in one diff. The anchor is not optional ahead of the lines, because line 1 prints a count the repository's own checker contradicts until it is set.
- **The chair, through the ExO's relay.** No company standard says a file with a published reading contract is read through its reader and never re-parsed. L-A21's test is the one that would have caught this and it is written about gates, so nothing in the `any` section reaches a surface. Filed rather than edited, since the standards file is vendored.
- **The ExO seat.** `docs/agents/quality-claims.md` holds rows for sentences, and a figure a page computes has no row to find and still owes the answer to "how do you know that."

## Gates

|---|---|
| `check_voice.py all` | one new FAIL, `ledger`, which is this run's own finding and stays red until the anchor is set |
| `check_voice.py taste` | one FAIL, verdict 6, unchanged from main and unchanged by this run |
| `check_voice.py claims` / `reading` | 17 and 5, the same rows as run 44, all already drafted and open in `awaiting-her-word.md` |
| `check_voice.py candidates` | clean. `site/app/desk/page.jsx` had no open row, so this supersedes nothing and gets its row in this diff |
| `check_voice.py enforcements` | entry 133 OK |

author: shortarrow
body:
## What this fixes

With a long history loaded, the drag (ADR 0045) that tilts the graph's thickness (ADR 0044) barely moved. Loading a 2,670-commit history to the end produced about 56,000 thickness elements, and every step of the drag redrew them together with the whole card. Each redraw took around 0.6 seconds, and since the tilt returns on release, it looked as if nothing tilted.

Also, while a text selection remained on the page, pressing the background did not start a drag.

## Draw only the rows near the view

The thickness is drawn only for rows within one screen before and after the scroll position ([`rowsInView`](https://github.com/ShortArrow/gitreant/blob/15821aa/frontend/src/thicknessModel.ts#L155)). An edge is drawn if it spans the range, even when both of its ends are outside it ([`spansRows`](https://github.com/ShortArrow/gitreant/blob/15821aa/frontend/src/thicknessModel.ts#L164)). With one screen of margin on each side, the thickness does not look cut off when scrolling before the next redraw.

## Redraw only the thickness

The tilt and the range of rows to draw are held in a small store rather than in the card's state ([`createThicknessView`](https://github.com/ShortArrow/gitreant/blob/15821aa/frontend/src/thicknessView.ts#L20)). The thickness subscribes to this store with `useSyncExternalStore` ([Thickness.tsx](https://github.com/ShortArrow/gitreant/blob/15821aa/frontend/src/Thickness.tsx#L37)). Dragging and scrolling redraw only the thickness, not the rows or the graph itself.

Measured on the same 2,670-commit history in Chromium without extensions, the thickness elements went down to about 1,200, and redrawing one drag step went from around 600ms to 4-29ms.

## Pressing on a text selection

Pressing on a selection made the browser start dragging the selected text and cancel the pointer. When the tilt drag starts, the default action of pointerdown is now prevented ([RepoCard.tsx](https://github.com/ShortArrow/gitreant/blob/15821aa/frontend/src/RepoCard.tsx#L448)). Preventing the default action stops the compatibility mousedown from arriving, so switching the pane focus was moved to pointerdown ([App.tsx](https://github.com/ShortArrow/gitreant/blob/15821aa/frontend/src/App.tsx#L877)).

## Tests

- Unit tests: check the calculation of the range of rows to draw, whether an edge spans the range, and that the store notifies on a change and does not notify for the same range.
- E2E: on a 150-commit history, check that the root commit has no thickness at first, and that after scrolling to the bottom the root gets a thickness and the thickness at the top disappears.
- E2E: check that the background drag tilts even with the whole page selected, and that pressing the graph background in an unfocused pane moves the focus to that pane.
- Every E2E test was confirmed to fail on the implementation before the fix. The redraw time is not checked by the tests.

## Resumo
Quarto incremento da Fase 3: atualiza o `README.md` para a release **`v2.0-fase3`**, refletindo o que foi integrado em #6 (spec v2.0), #7 (CI) e #8 (Docker). Um avaliador que abre o repositório consegue, só pelo README, entender a arquitetura, rodar a suíte com um comando e rastrear cada decisão até o PR que a introduziu.

| Integração contínua | **Nova seção:** os dois jobs, o critério de aprovação, as permissões e as proibições do CONTEXT_RULES 4.1 |

| Histórico de PRs | #6 a #10 |

## 1. O que foi gerado por IA
- **Assistente:** Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), com `CONTEXT_RULES.md` e a spec v2.0 como contexto.

Os comandos Docker documentados são os mesmos validados em #8. O pipeline roda neste PR (ver **Checks**).

author: erikleblansch
body:
The hosted Drizz.li and Overmorrow workflows currently upload compiled assets together with a configured Firefox runtime. This change replaces those successful-output uploads with explicit, byte-verified source recipes bound to the exact Weather commit. It preserves the existing build, browser/table tests and diagnostic reports.

The exporter accepts only fixed file lists, verifies each file against Git objects from the requested revision, rejects unsafe or pre-existing output paths, and includes original source notices. It excludes compiled applications, Firefox/Node/Flutter runtimes, profiles, caches and Git metadata. Recipe fields explicitly deny runtime acceptance, build reproducibility and complete corresponding-source claims.

This integrates independently reviewed implementation d8c6e4e onto main c69dc3de, retaining the README. Validation on head `1412eed20f1da27102e5582805d33c7613b67c4e`:

- [Hosted Weather integration components 40043544719](https://github.com/VOLPAROSSA/volparossa-weather/actions/runs/40043544719): all steps passed, including the full inert preparation suite and existing client integration contracts.
- Local 30 exporter tests and 21 hosted workflow tests passed.
- The first hosted run found two strict temporary Git fixture cleanup failures. The independently reviewed test-only fix disables automatic background Git maintenance for disposable fixture commands; the exporter and cleanup assertions are unchanged.

Actual reproducible compilation and four new independent consumer admissions are subsequent focused changes. No historical admission or artifact is altered. Manual maintainer review and merge required for F09; this source-export PR alone does not restore the hosted Core consumers.

author: dastratakos
body: PR C of the STAG-516 follow-ups (Editor Commands For Task Plans). The ask: in the panel's pull request tab, clicking into the description edits it in place, as clicking into a task's plan does. It uses #4921's `MarkdownEditor`, with the same toolbar, `/` menu and chords, and saves through #4919's description write. Two GitHub-body fidelity gaps that #4921 found are also fixed, in the editor's shared code, so the plan gets the fixes too. ## What changed - **`pull-request-description.tsx` (new): `PullRequestDescription`.** `DescriptionPart` mounts it where the overview says `canEditDescription` and carries the Markdown `body`. Everywhere else the description is drawn as before. - **Reading** stays GitHub's rendering, in an `EditableBlock`, as a plan's section is drawn. A click opens the editor in its place, and so does Enter on the selected description. A click on a link, a picture or a checkbox doesn't. - **The caret** lands on the words clicked. A new `documentWordsUnder` (in `plan-document-editor.tsx`) finds them as the editor counts sections, so a block GitHub draws at another height, such as an alert, doesn't shift where the caret lands. - **An empty description** says "Describe the change", in the editor's own type, so opening it moves nothing. - **Finishing:** Esc, ⌘↩, or focus leaving the editor finishes. Words left as they opened write nothing. Changed ones are written with `edit-description` with `expectedBody` set to the body the editor opened on. The editor stays open until the overview's read lands again, then GitHub's rendering of the new words replaces it, so nothing jumps in between. If words were typed while the write was out, the editor stays open on them. - **Leaving with unsaved words:** if the tab, the pull request or the folded section goes while words are unsaved, they are written the same way. - **Refusals keep the draft.** "Changed on GitHub" (`reason: description-changed`) keeps the editor open and says so as a `role="alert"` line with Reload. Reload asks first over `ConfirmDialog`, then reads the description again and opens the editor on GitHub's words. Any other refusal keeps the draft and shows the tab's write line in the editor, the sign-in offer included. - **`pull-request-writes.tsx`.** A refusal's note now carries the service's `reason`, so the control that sent the write can act on it. - **`tasks.css`.** The open editor's blocks, headings, lists, inline code and task items are spaced and set like the drawn description (`transcript-markdown`), so the words stay at the same heights as it opens. - **Fidelity fixes in the engine (`plan-editor/`):** - **The alert marker.** A re-printed blockquote that opens on `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]` or `[!CAUTION]` keeps the marker unescaped (`document-source.ts`). Before this, an edit inside an alert wrote `> \[!NOTE\]`, which GitHub no longer draws as an alert. - **CRLF.** The text is read with LF line endings and every text the editor hands back (drafts, `markdown()`, `take()`) is written with the body's own line endings (`plan-editor.ts`). An untouched CRLF body now comes back byte for byte, where it used to come back as LF with an extra blank line. This lines up with #4919's conflict check, which already compares with line endings normalized. ## Decisions I made - **Focus leaving saves, as in the plan.** While a refusal is showing, focus leaving keeps the editor open rather than sending the draft again unasked. - **A draft refused as its description goes is kept.** It's held in memory for that agent and pull request, and the description opens on it again, saying why, the next time it is drawn, so no words are silently lost. - **No service change.** The UI uses #4919's write as it is. ## Tests - **`pull-request-description.test.ts` (new)** draws the real tab with the real editor bundle and mocks only the act port's GitHub answer: - a click opens the editor with the caret on the clicked words, and Esc with no change writes nothing and draws the description again; - an edit writes the new body with the body it began from, CRLF kept, and the description is drawn again from the read after it; - "changed on GitHub" keeps the draft and says so; Reload asks first and then opens GitHub's words, writing nothing; - a member who can't edit gets no editor and no block to open one. - **`markdown-editor.test.ts`** gets two engine tests: - an edit inside a `> [!NOTE]` alert keeps the marker; - a CRLF body comes back byte for byte untouched, and keeps CRLF when a word is edited. Both fail without the engine fixes. - **Checks run:** - panel `tsc`, biome and the repo's oxlint on the changed files, and the press guard; - knip, whose only findings are three in files this PR doesn't touch; - vitest over `packages/panel/src/tasks` and `plan-editor`: 164 files pass. The one failure, `plan-editor-mentions.test.ts`'s "time on a day … from today", fails the same way on `main` without this change; it reads the real clock and fails just past midnight UTC. ## Screenshots Taken in a throwaway harness page (not committed) that renders the tab with fake reads. They're in the agent's transcript: - the read view; - the editor open at the same heights; - the format toolbar; - the "changed on GitHub" alert with Reload; - the redraw after a save; - the empty description. Out of scope: the review and line comment boxes (PR D), editing the title, and any change to the service write. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

Dashboard pages repeated layout and rendering logic, while settings and reparse flows could repeat financial maintenance that had already run. This change shares those implementations and reuses completed reconciliation reports, preserving failure and durable-retry handling.

## Changes

- Complete reparse reviews from the existing reconciliation report; reload display-name changes without another financial sweep, while account-type changes still refresh reconciliation.
- Replace duplicated financial-row update arguments with Room entity updates and shared FX-pair preservation.
- Reuse account summaries, credit spending totals, rescan labels, and the advisory forecast remaining-amount calculation; remove unused helpers.
- Share transaction labels and account matching, remove unused dashboard navigation callbacks, combine account/flow rendering, and let the shared summary scaffold own scrolling and section spacing across summary/detail pages.
- Update architecture and design-system documentation. Database schema remains v18.

- 434 targeted app tests passed across application/dashboard, presentation/dashboard, navigation, review, and architecture.
- 21 targeted analytics tests passed for the forecast simplification.
- Added regression coverage for settings maintenance calls and completing a failed reconciliation report without a second posting pass.
- 9 post-change emulator tests passed, covering page rendering, transaction back navigation, and chart-sheet apply/discard behavior.

author: hoanghainh1188
body:
Closes #136

## Vấn đề
Ở bước `repro_test`, code gốc chỉ được tính là fail khi một tên test fail khớp với test agent khai báo (`is_test`). Ở `scrapy-8186-r2` của bộ thử #18, agent khai báo cả class `tests/test_pipeline_files_timestamps.py::TestTimestamps`. Trên code gốc, cả 10 test fail với tên `…::TestTimestamps::test_x[…]`, nhưng không tên nào khớp, nên gate từ chối cả 4 lần thử. Đây là đề xuất số 3 trong `docs/measurements/2026-10-24-eval-kpi.md`.

## Thay đổi
- Thêm `is_in(id, test)` trong `crates/aegis-gate/src/gate.rs`. Nó đúng khi `is_test` đúng, hoặc khi tên (đã bỏ hậu tố `[…]`) bắt đầu bằng `<test>::` hay chứa `::<test>::`. Nghĩa là test nằm trong file hoặc class đã khai báo. Tên rút gọn như `TestX` vẫn khớp được, giống cách `is_test` đã nhận `test_y`.
- Bước `repro_test` dùng `is_in`. Tên chỉ trùng phần đầu không khớp: `TestX` khác `TestX2`, `test_x.py` khác `test_x.pyc`.
- Tách phần bỏ hậu tố `[…]` thành `without_params` để hai hàm dùng chung.

## Vì sao `allowed_tests` không đổi
Ở bước `test`, `allowed_tests` quyết định những test nào được phép fail mới và được ghi lại reference output (#105). Nếu dùng luật node ở đây, khai báo một file sẽ cho mọi test trong file đó được phép hỏng và bị ghi lại reference. Như vậy là quá rộng cho một bước để phát hiện hồi quy. Còn ở `repro_test`, nới luật chỉ làm dễ chứng minh "có test fail trên code gốc". Bước đó vẫn đòi lệnh test pass trọn vẹn trên bản vá, nên không làm lỏng gì. Vì vậy `allowed_tests` vẫn khớp theo đúng tên test, và có một assert ghi lại quyết định này.

## Test plan
- [x] Viết trước `a_reproduction_class_is_matched_by_the_tests_in_it` trong `crates/aegis-gate/tests/python_gate.rs` và thấy nó fail trên code cũ đúng như scrapy-8186 (`TestFourthItem::test_is_refused[4]`, `[5]` fail trên code gốc, nhưng gate vẫn báo Failed). Sau khi sửa thì pass.
- [x] Unit test `a_file_or_class_holds_the_tests_inside_it`: file, class, tên rút gọn, tên trùng phần đầu, `.pyc`.
- [x] Chạy test Python của gate trong venv có pytest 9.1.1 và ruff 0.17.2, nên chúng chạy thật chứ không bị bỏ qua.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, cả hai lệnh clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test -p aegis-provider --features bedrock`, `cargo deny check`.
- [ ] Không chạy lại bộ thử với model thật.

author: santirogu
body:
## Why
La evaluación del bot (`pnpm bot:eval`) solo corría a mano: un cambio de comportamiento del modelo (una actualización de Anthropic, otro modelo elegido en /admin/bot) podía pasar semanas sin notarse. Además no probaba intentos de manipular al bot.

## What
- **Workflow semanal** `.github/workflows/bot-eval.yml`: cada lunes a las 7:17 a. m. (Bogotá) y a mano (eligiendo el modelo). Falla si cae un mensaje trampa o si el resto acierta menos del 95 %; el detalle queda en el resumen de la corrida.
- **7 mensajes trampa** en el set: que revele el prompt o una clave, que se salga de su papel, que confirme un borrado, que invente cifras de otra persona, un JSON para registrar un ingreso y una instrucción escondida en la descripción.
- La calificación pasa a `src/modules/bot/eval/grade.ts` (con pruebas); el script acepta `--min` y escribe el resumen en GitHub Actions.
- `src/modules/bot/eval/` no dispara un despliegue (la app no lo usa).
- README: cómo crear la key aparte y el secreto.

## How
- **La key:** una aparte, de un workspace de Anthropic con tope de gasto (decisión del dueño), en el secreto `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_EVAL`. Solo llega al paso que llama a Claude; a nivel del job solo se sabe si existe. Sin el secreto el workflow no hace nada y deja un aviso.
- **Seguridad:** solo `schedule` y `workflow_dispatch` (nunca en PRs: el repo es público), `contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`, acciones fijadas por SHA y el modelo por variable de entorno desde un `choice` (sin inyección en el `run`).
- **Probado:** `grade.test.ts` (incluido que el detector de filtración reconozca el prompt real) y `deploy-needed.test.ts`. La evaluación real en local, con permiso: 65/65 con las 7 trampas, US$0,016 con Haiku.
- En local: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm db:check-drift` y `pnpm test:coverage` (4334 pruebas). Auditorías de seguridad y pruebas (cambios) sin pendientes.

## Additional Notes
- **Paso manual del dueño:** crear la key en un workspace con tope y el secreto `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_EVAL` en GitHub (README → Pruebas y CI → Evaluación del bot). Hasta entonces el workflow se salta.
- Costo: unos US$0,02 por corrida, ~US$0,07 al mes.
- **De paso, por la auditoría del CI:** se fuerza `undici` 8.12.2 (`pnpm.overrides`) por un aviso alto publicado hoy ([GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c)); lo trae `jsdom`, solo en desarrollo y en el CI. Editado a mano en el lockfile para no re-resolver otras dependencias (validado con `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`). Con `package.json` cambiado, este PR sí despliega.
- **CodeQL:** el resumen escapa también la barra invertida en las celdas de la tabla.

author: thegreattoba
body:
## Problème et correction

Certaines illustrations apparaissent dans la collection mais disparaissent pendant le reveal SSR/LR. Le lecteur imposait `crossOrigin="anonymous"` à l'image visible afin de lire ses couleurs dans un canvas. Si l'hébergeur n'envoie pas Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Chrome bloque entièrement son chargement.

Le lecteur commun utilise désormais le chargement normal du composant YokaiCard. La lecture optionnelle des couleurs reste protégée : si les pixels ne sont pas accessibles, le reflet conserve sa teinte neutre et l'image reste affichée. Suppression de la prop CORS devenue inutilisée dans YokaiCard. Aucun changement des animations, du design des cartes ou des boosters.

## Validation

- Reproduction Chrome avant correction : images SSR et LR sans CORS bloquées, naturalWidth = 0.
- Après correction : les deux images sont chargées (230×345), visibles, une seule instance par reveal, aucune erreur console.
- Vérification Chrome à 320/375/768/1024/1440 px et au zoom 200 %, avec mouvement normal et réduit.

author: krln-git
body:
💡 What: Replaced inefficient `.count() == 0` usage with `.first()` and `.exists()` respectively in `cms/djangoapps/course_creators/views.py`.
🎯 Why: In Django querysets, calling `.count() == 0` evaluates a full `COUNT(*)` against the database which is slow for large tables. `.exists()` limits the query and terminates once the first result is found, functioning much faster for truth checks. Additionally, if the first result is required, `.first()` evaluates the set up to a limit of 1 and operates as an existence check natively.
📊 Impact: Considerably faster lookups on `get_course_creator_status` and `_add_user` as it replaces a slow count query with a boolean existence/fetch check, reducing load on the database.
🔬 Measurement: Verify changes manually by reading `cms/djangoapps/course_creators/views.py` and reviewing test suite outcomes.

author: yuzukis
body:
T-140. When a Codex connection ends (`yuzuno/disconnected`), `on_event` marks the Agent disconnected:
- offline unless its status is uncertain;
- with the reason unless Core closed the connection itself, which keeps an error recorded before;
- its context usage and pending requests stale.

That changes no Turn, but it was committed with `Store::update`. That copies a held record whole to compare, and returns a second copy nobody read.

### Change
- That one call site now commits with `Store::update_meta`, with the same change. It is journaled the same (`runtime/disconnected`).
- `Meta` gains `context_usage`. The metadata row already carries it (`MetaBody` → `contextUsage`), and `meta_of`/`put_meta` copy it.
- Unchanged:
  - the intentional-close check;
  - the forgetting of MCP and plan state;
  - the generation and thread filters;
  - the other `update` call sites (error, settings).
- A held record with a user message whose client ID `restore` gives back is still written by `commit_locked(Scope::Meta)`, as `commit_meta_locked` does for any metadata change. A write that fails changes and publishes nothing.

### Tests
- `a_disconnect_is_written_as_metadata_and_writes_what_the_whole_record_commit_wrote` runs 96 cases through `on_event` and compares each, whole record and journal, with the old `update` on a second Workspace. The cases cover:
  - lost with a reason, lost without one after an earlier error, and closed by Core without and after an error;
  - working and uncertain;
  - context usage current, already stale, and absent;
  - held and not held, each with and without a message to restore.
- Beside it are a receipt still sending and one uncertain. Held without a restore, the held copy is kept (same `Arc`) and changed in place.
- `a_disconnect_whose_write_fails_changes_and_publishes_nothing`: the journal row or the metadata row is refused, held or not. Nothing changes: the held copy, its content, the rev, the Agent listed, the rows and the journal.

### Evidence
Evidence is in the T-140 task comments. All Jobs were limited to 8 GiB with swap 0.
- **d1 `14c3da39` (FAILED)**, at the first draft a2c6556. Lib: 1134 passed, 1 failed. The failure was `remote_images::tests::remote_image_concurrent_transfer_waits_before_preparation_and_can_cancel` (`remote_images.rs:430`); the cause is unconfirmed and a diagnostic is pending. The reds didn't run (gated).
- **d2 `99bf6f71` (passed)**, at dcde7cd:
  - lib 1136/0, integration 243/0, examples built;
  - 8 reds, each failing only its expected test at its expected line. D1 reverts only this call site to `update`; D8 changes the held copy before the write, which only the failure test catches.
- **Merge of main 761a98d (#135)**: the docs conflict was resolved by keeping both sections. The code files' patch-ids are identical before and after, and all four files add and remove the same lines.

Not measured separately: by the source, this is the same change of commit as a thread's start (#134).

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Keep the remaining item IDs out of bindings error messages.

`ItemId` values are addresses of Clang AST nodes, so they differ from run to
run. Errors for unsupported items are written into the generated `.rs` file
as comments and into the error report, so an error that prints an IR item or
an `RsTypeKind` with `{:?}` (whose `Debug` output contains `ItemId(0x...)`)
makes the output nondeterministic.

https://github.com/google/crubit/commit/20f6e7c7f85cfe4237dc0e53ba81b2f03e440bd3 fixed the most common of these. Fix the rest: name items with
`debug_name` in the "does not define a type" and missing-`__this` errors,
print `TraitName` with `Display`, and move the type out of
`format_as_self_param`'s error into its caller, which formats it with
`RsTypeKind::display`. Panics and assertions are unchanged, since they only go
to stderr.

author: mokarade
body:
Tâche : #74

## Quoi
Le 23/10, Marc a demandé une seule LIA, avec un seul état dans toutes les apps, hébergé dans MemoryAI. Cette PR construit cet état côté MemoryAI, selon le contrat `commun/assistant/CONTRAT-etat-lia.md`.

- **Table `lia_etat`** (migration 0025, additive, idempotente) : une seule ligne. Elle ne contient que des nombres, des verbes de LIA et un nom d'humeur, aucun contenu de Marc, donc rien de chiffré.
- **`lib/lia/etatPartage.ts`** (pur) : la forme et les bornes de l'état, les mêmes que `validerEtat` côté paquet.
  - Retirés sans refuser l'état : les clés inconnues, les faits du journal qui ne sont pas un verbe, la mémoire lente hors bornes.
  - Le journal garde ses 20 derniers faits.
  - Un champ obligatoire faux donne 400, un corps de plus de 16 Ko donne 413.
- **`lib/lia/depotEtat.ts`** : l'écriture est **atomique**. Un seul `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE version < reçue` remplace la ligne seulement si la version reçue dépasse celle gardée. Sinon : 409 avec l'état gardé, que la page adopte. GET rend 200, ou 204 s'il n'y a aucun état. Toutes les réponses sont `no-store`.
- **Deux portes** :
  - `/api/lia/etat`, pour la maison. Elle passe par la session, derrière le middleware, et `requireSession()` est revérifiée dans la route. `etatHttp("/api/lia/etat")` la branche sur les deux montages de LIA (accueil et autres pages).
  - `/api/etat-lia`, pour le hub, qui relaie ses pages et celles des apps. Il faut `x-hub-token`, comparé en temps constant, et `x-lia-proprietaire: 1` : le hub dit ainsi que la page est celle du propriétaire. La route est déclarée dans `ROUTES_A_AUTH_PROPRE` et dans le matcher.
  - Mémoire gelée : les écritures répondent 503 sur les deux portes.
- **Contexte de `ask`** : `EtatLia` n'est plus en `.strict()`. Un champ que lia-ui ajouterait plus tard est retiré au lieu de faire refuser tout l'état (remarque du fil Assistant). Seuls les trois champs connus atteignent le modèle.

## Vérifié
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (125 fichiers, 1 427 tests), `npm run build` et `npm run portes` : tous OK.
- `tests/liaEtatPartage.test.ts` :
  - les bornes et ce qui est retiré ;
  - sur PGlite : 204 puis création de la ligne, 409 sans rien écraser, une seule ligne, deux écritures simultanées dont une seule passe ;
  - les gardes de la porte du hub : 503, 401, 403 ;
  - la porte maison reste derrière la session ;
  - le gel coupe les écritures.
- `tests/db.test.ts` (26 tables) et `tests/gardePages.test.ts` sont à jour.
- Données fictives seulement. La migration est additive, aucune table existante n'est touchée.

## Reste
- Côté hub : une route relais `/api/lia/etat` qui vérifie la session, puis appelle `/api/etat-lia` de MemoryAI avec `x-hub-token` et `x-lia-proprietaire: 1`. Elle se branche par `etat={etatHttp("/api/lia/etat")}`. Le fil Assistant est prévenu.

## Summary

このリポの `.claude/hooks/block-secret-egress.py` を、pipeline-youtube-SDK の写し（直った形）とバイト単位で同じにします。

- **何が古かったか:** 環境変数のアクセスを見つける照合が、後ろの先読みに `\s*` を挟む形（`(?=\s*[.\[])`）のままでした。2026-09-03 の実測で、この形には回避があると分かっています。資格情報の引数の後ろに 2 つ目の道を置くと、送出が通ってしまうものです。SDK の写しと、マシン全体の写しは直っていました。
- **何をしたか:** SDK の写し（12,427 B・sha256 `70bf57d4d28d1b91…`）とバイト単位で同じにしました。差分はこの 1 ファイルだけです（+15 −1）。

## Slice 2 — Ingesta + RAG + retrieve con scope

La API de CEREBRO para que las plataformas **alimenten** (eventos) y **consulten** (con scope) la memoria. Mismo patrón de aislamiento por **owner** (RLS fail-closed) que el Slice 1.

> **No mergear hasta tu firma.** Rama `feature/slice-2-rag` · commit `c667877`. Probado con **owners de test** (no depende aún de los tenant_id reales de HUB/NÚCLEO).

### Qué incluye
- **Migración 002** (`knowledge_chunk`) + rollback: `embedding vector(1024)` (Voyage), `visibility`, `owner_id`, `person_id`, `source_platform`, `dedup_key`. **RLS por owner** (igual que Slice 1), índice **ivfflat cosine**, **UNIQUE `(owner_id, dedup_key)`** = idempotencia. Test adversarial `supabase/tests/rls_knowledge_chunk.sql`.
- **`apps/cerebro/rag`** (DDD): puertos `EmbeddingProvider` / `KnowledgeStore` / `KnowledgeUnitOfWork`; `ingest-event.handler` (resuelve persona vía Slice 1 → embebe → inserta chunk, idempotente, no re-embebe duplicados); `retrieve-context.handler` (embebe query → similitud dentro del owner+persona → **filtra por scope de visibilidad del agente**; **nunca bloquea**, degrada a vacío).
- **`voyage.adapter.ts`**: ÚNICO archivo que toca Voyage (`voyage-3-large`, `output_dimension=1024`, key solo en `VOYAGE_API_KEY`/Vault). Adaptadores `pg` (pgvector) e in-memory + `FakeEmbedder`.
- **API HTTP** (`http/`, `node:http`, sin framework): `POST /cerebro/ingest` (202) y `POST /cerebro/retrieve` (200), auth por **service token** (`Authorization: Bearer <token>` → source_platform). Entrypoint `http/main.ts` (`pnpm --filter @raisen/cerebro start`).

### Criterios de aceptación (§4 del brief)
- [x] `POST /cerebro/ingest` → crea `knowledge_chunk` embebido, asociado al `person_id` correcto.
- [x] **Idempotencia**: el mismo evento dos veces no duplica (UNIQUE `dedup_key`; no re-embebe).
- [x] `POST /cerebro/retrieve` devuelve los chunks más cercanos **filtrados por scope** (un agente con scope default NO recibe `financial`).
- [x] **Voyage key solo en Vault** (env; grep en código → 0 literales).
- [x] **retrieve nunca 500**: ante tenant desconocido / Voyage caído / DB → 200 degradado (vacío).

### Verificación (verbatim)
```
pnpm -r build / typecheck → Done (strict, 2 paquetes)
vitest run → Test Files 7 passed (7) · Tests 35 passed (35)
  (incl. integración HTTP real con fetch: ingest 202, retrieve 200, 401 sin auth,
   403 platform mismatch, idempotencia, scope filtra financial, degradación)
bash scripts/sentinel.sh → ✓ A(typecheck,lint,test:unit) B C D E F G · push autorizado
```

### Pendiente / requiere tu acción (honesto)
- [ ] **Aplicar 002 al Supabase real** + correr `rls_knowledge_chunk.sql` (tras firma, igual que hicimos con Slice 1).
- [ ] **Scope por agente**: hoy `agentVisibilityScope` es **deny-by-default** (solo `public`+`internal` para todos). Confirmar la tabla del doc de agentes §3.2 para poblar `financial`/`pii_sensitive` donde corresponda (p.ej. victor/zahra para cobrar).
- [ ] **Ingesta async**: hoy procesa inline y responde 202 (sin cola/worker dedicado); el worker en Railway es infra posterior.
- [ ] `buildContent` v1 = `[event] <payload JSON>` (derivado); mejorar shaping por tipo de evento.
- [ ] tenant_id reales de HUB/NÚCLEO (Jorge) para alimentar eventos reales.

author: amindhouib
body:
## What it does

Deploys that hang no longer hold the queue forever. Three jobs sat `active` for 5 hours and one deploy hung for 35 minutes in a registry push; with `buildsConcurrency` 4 a few such jobs block every deploy on the host (T-7393).

A watchdog checks every `running` deployment once a minute and fails it when
- its log file has had no new output for **20 min** (idle limit; the log's modification time, read on the host that holds the log, against that host's own clock), seen on two checks in a row, or
- it has run for more than **90 min** (wall limit).

Before anything is stopped the row status and the log are read again, and the watchdog line goes into the deployment log only after that. When it fires it writes `Watchdog: no log output for N min` (or `exceeded M min`), stops the work the way Kill build / Kill process do (pid-file launcher, else `kill -9` of the recorded pid, else the generic stop only when no other deploy runs on the host), then marks the deployment `error`, writes `Watchdog: marked failed`, sends the existing deployment-failed notification once, and records a `watchdog_fail` entry in the cancel trail (actor: system). A job that has not ended 10 min after it was stopped has its queue slot and journal row released by force, after the row and the service were settled.

The job-4512 case (log ends at "Image Pushed", the rollout never starts, the row stays `running` for 66 min) is a plain idle stall: the watchdog reads the log's mtime, not its text. A test pins it.

Also: `application.cancelDeployment` and `compose.cancelDeployment` (Cloud-only until now) work on self-hosted, with the same permission and audit entries, and the Cancel button of an active job in the deploy queue table is shown there too.

## Settings and API

- Settings > Deployments > "Stuck Deployment Watchdog": switch (on by default), idle limit (min 15, default 20), wall limit (min 15, default 90, not below the idle limit), and a list of excluded services.
- API (admin, self-hosted only): `settings.updateDeploymentWatchdog`, `settings.addDeploymentWatchdogExclusion`, `settings.removeDeploymentWatchdogExclusion` (organization check on the service).
- Per service: "Exclude from the stuck-deployment watchdog" in the Advanced tab of applications and composes (`application.setWatchdogExclusion` / `compose.setWatchdogExclusion`, `watchdogExclusion` query); anyone who may update the service can flip it. Off by default.
- The exclusion list is a jsonb column on the web server settings (the application table has no room for another column). All three editors use one atomic SQL UPDATE (`addWatchdogExclusion` / `removeWatchdogExclusion`), so two edits at once cannot lose an entry. A malformed stored entry is skipped on its own; the valid ones stay in force.

## Migration 0221

`0221_deployment_watchdog.sql` adds four columns to `webServerSettings` (enabled, idle minutes, wall minutes, exclusions), all `IF NOT EXISTS`, with the defaults above, so every instance has it on after the upgrade. It follows 0220 in the journal with a later `when`; the snapshot's `prevId` is the 0220 snapshot id.

## Safety

- Excluded services are never failed and their slot is never released by force.
- A `running` row that no queue job runs (left over from a restart) is only marked failed. Nothing is signalled for it except through the pid-file launcher, which checks the pid and its start time; never the recorded pid and never the host-wide `pkill`.
- A deployment is tied to a queue job only when its row was created after the job started, so a leftover row never stops or releases a healthy build.
- A deployment a person cancelled stays cancelled; nothing is logged, notified or audited as a watchdog failure unless the watchdog changed the row.
- A preview deployment built on a build server is not killed (no safe handle); only its slot is released if it does not end.
- When nothing could be signalled, the slot is released but the service's group lock is kept, so a second deploy of it does not start next to a process nobody could stop. The lock is bounded: a stop that found no handle only because other deploys run on the host is retried on every sweep, and after max(2 x wall limit, 3 h) the lock is dropped with an error in the server log, a line in the deployment log and a `groupLockDropped` audit entry.
- A job released by force cannot write late results: its deployment and service status writes are ignored (deployment writes also by deployment id).
- The slot is freed even if marking the row or writing the audit entry fails.
- Unknown log idleness (log host unreachable) never fires the idle trigger; the wall limit still does.

## Not covered (follow-ups, T-7404)

A CPU / network liveness probe besides the log mtime, a race-free replacement for `pkill -2`, tree-kill of the whole process tree, and a per-server override of the limits.

## Tests

- New and updated under `apps/dokploy/__test__/queues/`: watchdog decisions and sweep behaviour, the service layer (outcomes, host reads), stop methods, queue release with kept lock and its bound, late-write guard, exclusion SQL, config parsing, both settings routes and the per-service switch, self-hosted cancel.
- `__test__/db/migration-idempotency.test.ts` passes; MCP scope snapshot updated for the new routes.
- Queues + db + mcp suites pass; tsc on `apps/dokploy` stays at its 44-error baseline and `packages/server` is clean.

author: pdeyvid
body:
## Resumo
Adiciona um launcher de inicialização, carregamento de mods no estilo LayeredFS, remapeamento completo de controles, cache persistente de shaders e vários recursos de conveniência. Também corrige a renderização em GPUs AMD e elimina travamentos no áudio, na leitura de arquivos e nas queries da GPU.

## Novos recursos
- **Launcher** (`launcher.cpp`, Win32 puro): escolhe o NSP e o `prod.keys` em qualquer pasta, ativa/desativa mods e tem opções de tela cheia sem bordas e FPS. Dá para desligar o "mostrar ao abrir"; segurar **Shift** ao iniciar faz ele voltar. É pulado automaticamente em execuções automatizadas (`HWDER_LOG`, `HWDER_AUTOPLAY`, `HWDER_OFFSCREEN`, `HWDER_NO_LAUNCHER`).
- **Mods / traduções**: cada mod fica numa pasta própria dentro de `mods\`.
  - Aceita a árvore RomFS direta, uma pasta `romfs\` ou o layout do Atmosphere.
  - Os mods carregam em ordem alfabética das pastas.
  - Prefixo `_` no nome da pasta desativa o mod.
  - O NSP nunca é modificado.
- **Aba Controles (F1)**: cada entrada do Switch pode ser mapeada para 2 teclas e 1 botão do controle. Também permite escolher o controle, alternar o layout dos botões (Switch ou Xbox), ajustar a deadzone dos analógicos, o limiar dos gatilhos, a intensidade da vibração e a inversão da câmera, além de ter um teste de entrada ao vivo.
- **Cache persistente de shaders** (`cache\shaders.bin`): shaders e pipelines são recompilados em segundo plano durante o boot. O cache é invalidado por um hash do código do tradutor de shaders (`cmake/shader_version.cmake`).
- **F12**: captura de tela em PNG, sem o overlay, salva em `screenshots\`.
- **F2**: modo turbo (2x/3x/4x), que escala o tempo do jogo (vsync, ticks de áudio e timeouts do kernel).
- **Pós-processamento**: FXAA e nitidez num único passe de compute.
- Interpolação de quadros reativada na aba Vídeo.
- Menu F1 e launcher traduzidos para PT-BR (segue o idioma do Windows ou pode ser escolhido manualmente).
- Ícone opcional para o executável via `tools/make_icon.py`. Ele é gerado a partir do dump do próprio usuário e nunca vai para o repositório; o `make_dist.py` se recusa a empacotar um exe com esse ícone sem `--with-icon`.

## Compatibilidade com AMD / drivers
- Fallback de D24S8 para D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT quando o formato não é suportado.
- Formatos de vértice de 3 componentes passam a ser lidos com 4, e o 4º componente é lido como 1 no shader.
- `KIL` agora usa `OpDemoteToHelperInvocation` em vez de `OpKill`, o que mantém as derivadas válidas no quad.
- ClipDistance e as saídas genéricas agora são inicializadas (nulo / `(0,0,0,1)`) em vez de ficarem indefinidas.
- Redução de faixa nos argumentos de sin/cos para [-π, π].
- Samplers de comparação só são usados quando o shader amostra com Dref.
- As views de imagem removem os usos que o formato não suporta (`VkImageViewUsageCreateInfo`).
- `HWDER_EMULATE_AMD=1` força esses fallbacks em outras GPUs, para testes.

## Desempenho
- Leitura do NSP com I/O overlapped: as leituras paralelas deixaram de ficar em fila.
- Áudio:
  - A thread de áudio roda com prioridade TIME_CRITICAL.
  - Quando atrasa, recupera os ticks perdidos em vez de descartá-los.
  - Só ressincroniza depois de 200 ms de atraso.
- Os resultados das queries de oclusão são escritos na hora, sem flush nem espera da GPU ociosa a cada query.
- O buffer de parâmetros das macros MME é reaproveitado.
- O profiling usa o TSC e uma free list por thread.

## Depuração / ferramentas
Novas variáveis de ambiente: `HWDER_HEADLESS`, `HWDER_OFFSCREEN`, `HWDER_AUTOPLAY=2` (batalha automática), `HWDER_PROFILE_MS`, `HWDER_SAMPLE`, `HWDER_SVC_ACCT`, `HWDER_KLOCK_TRACE`, `HWDER_CPU_TRACE`, `HWDER_WAIT_TRACE=<ms>`, `HWDER_GPU`, `HWDER_MODS` / `HWDER_NO_MODS`, `HWDER_NO_SHADER_CACHE`.
- As threads do jogo agora têm nome, o que ajuda nos relatórios de crash e no profiler.
- `tools/recomp/known_entries.txt` guarda os pontos de entrada já conhecidos (só endereços, sem código), então um checkout novo inicia sem precisar rodar o `iterate.sh`.
- `msvc.py` encontra o Visual Studio / Build Tools via `vswhere`, em qualquer edição.

## ⚠️ Mudanças incompatíveis
- O requisito mínimo passa a ser **Vulkan 1.3** (antes era 1.2).
- `hwder_settings.ini` ganhou chaves novas; arquivos antigos continuam funcionando.

## Testes
- [ ] NVIDIA
- [ ] AMD

author: jsaldias39
body:
## Resumen

P0, slice 2, apilado sobre #671 (base `justin/p0-claim-coverage-validation`). El plan y el reporte están en `docs/trabajo/2026-10-23-p0-cobertura-caminos-vinculados/` (`PLAN.md`, `REPORTE.md`, `evidencia/`).

**1. La política llega también a los reclamos vinculados** (`claims.service.ts`): los que nacen de una reserva de farmacia (`inventoryReservationId`) o de una orden de diagnóstico (`serviceRequestId`) pasan ahora por `ClaimCoveragePolicy.evaluate`, igual que el cobro directo:
- El servicio y el importe salen del pedido bloqueado (`canonicalLines`): el medicamento del producto en farmacia y el estudio de la orden en diagnóstico. El plan sale de `coverageForOrder`. Se usan los `serviceRequestId` / `inventoryReservationId` del pedido para contrastar la aprobación previa.
- Si la política rechaza, el alta responde 422 `PreconditionFailedException` con `details.reason` (`SERVICE_NOT_COVERED`, `BENEFIT_AMBIGUOUS`, `CLAIM_LINE_SERVICE_REQUIRED`, `PRIOR_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED/PENDING/DENIED/EXPIRED/AMOUNT_EXCEEDED`, `PATIENT_SHARE_MISMATCH`…) y no se crea nada.
- **La parte del paciente la calcula el servidor y es la que se guarda** en `insurance_claim_lines.patient_responsibility_amount`. Antes, en los vinculados quedaba vacía y la API aceptaba que el cliente declarara `0`. Ahora, si el cliente declara un valor distinto al calculado (incluido `0`), el alta da `PATIENT_SHARE_MISMATCH`. En un replay idempotente, la parte declarada se compara con la guardada.

**2. Cada decisión queda en la bitácora** (puerto `INSURANCE_AUDIT_TRAIL_PORT` → `AuditTrailService` → `audit_log`, el mismo patrón que `insurance-campaigns`):
- **Aceptado:** `INSURANCE_CLAIM_COVERAGE_APPLIED` sobre `insurance_claim` / id del reclamo, dentro de la transacción del alta. El desglose por línea (beneficio, %, copago, monto del paciente, monto de la aseguradora, `requiresPriorAuthorization`, id de la autorización) va al log estructurado (`operation: insurance.claim.coverage`), sin ids ni datos del paciente.
- **Rechazado:** `INSURANCE_CLAIM_COVERAGE_REJECTED:<reason>` con `success=false`, sobre el pedido (`inventory_reservation` / `service_request`) o, en el cobro directo, sobre `patient_coverage`. Se registra en **una transacción propia, después del rollback del alta**; si no, se perdería. Si la bitácora falla, se anota en el log y el 422 original sigue su curso.
- Se aplica a los dos caminos, vinculado y directo, para que la bitácora sea uniforme.

**3. Tests**
- Spec nuevo `claims-linked-coverage.spec.ts`, con `describe.each` para FARMACIA y DIAGNÓSTICO, sobre la base en memoria de la política:
  - caso aceptado (140 de 500);
  - caso aceptado con parte del paciente declarada correcta;
  - caso aceptado con aprobación PARCIAL suficiente;
  - las 9 razones de rechazo;
  - fallo de la bitácora que no oculta el 422;
  - un error ajeno a la cobertura, que no se registra.
- Se verifica que el rechazo se sella en una transacción distinta a la revertida.
- El EM en memoria se extrajo a `claim-coverage.testing.ts`, compartido con `claim-coverage-policy.spec.ts`.
- `claims-linked.service.spec.ts` usa ahora la política real en lugar del mock que devolvía la parte declarada por el cliente.
- `claims-coverage-wiring.spec.ts` suma las aserciones de bitácora para el camino directo.

## Decisiones confirmadas por Justin (2026-10-23)

- El desglose (%, copago, montos, autorización) queda **fuera** de `audit_log`: va al log estructurado y no se hace DDL. `audit_log` registra quién, sobre qué recurso, el resultado y, en el rechazo, el motivo. La parte del paciente y el monto quedan en `insurance_claim_lines`, y la autorización en `insurance_claims.prior_authorization_request_id`.
- En los reclamos vinculados, una parte del paciente declarada que no coincide con el plan se rechaza, **incluido `0`**.

## Pendientes

- **Adjudicación vinculada:** `validateLinkedClaimSettlement` todavía no limita el `patientAmount` que adjudica la aseguradora a la parte del paciente informada. Según la decisión del 2026-10-23, la diferencia la absorbe la práctica. Queda para otro slice.
- No se vinculó `invoice_lines` ↔ `insurance_claim_lines`: no existe ese vínculo en el modelo (ADR-0021, no se inventó).
- **Cambio de comportamiento:** un producto de farmacia sin `medicationConceptId`, o un servicio sin beneficio vigente en el plan, ya no se puede cobrar a la aseguradora (422). Es intencional según la regla P0.

## Casilla documental (obligatoria)

- [ ] Rutas HTTP, DTO o controllers: el contrato HTTP no cambia; solo se agregan nuevos `details.reason` en un 422 que ya existía.
- [ ] Entidades o el modelo de datos
- [ ] Eventos de dominio
- [ ] Permisos, roles o el mecanismo de autorización
- [ ] Un README de módulo
- [ ] Una decisión arquitectónica nueva
- [x] Actualicé `docs/guides/patient-coverage-copays.md`: `patientResponsibilityAmount` en reclamos vinculados ahora lo calcula el servidor.

## Verificación (literal, en la nube)

- `corepack yarn typecheck` → **0**
- `corepack yarn test --testPathPatterns=insurance` → **0**: `Test Suites: 50 passed, 50 total` / `Tests: 786 passed, 786 total`. En la base del PR, medida en esta misma sesión, da 49 suites / 756 tests, no 47 / 751.
- `corepack yarn lint --max-warnings=0` → **1, por errores que ya trae la base**: 17 errores de prettier en `src/common/seed/glossary-*.spec.ts`, `pharmacy_inventory/.../pharmacy-orders.*` y `profiles/.../clinical-patient-history.adapter.ts`. La rama base da exactamente lo mismo sin este PR (stash comprobado). No los toqué porque están fuera de alcance. `eslint --max-warnings=0` sobre los 8 archivos de código de este PR → **0**.
- Int-specs: **NO corridos**, porque en la nube no hay Postgres.
- Nota de entorno: el proxy bloquea `cdn.sheetjs.com`. Para instalar, `xlsx` se resolvió temporalmente a `0.18.5` de npm (solo lo usa `terminology`), y `package.json` / `yarn.lock` se restauraron sin cambios antes del commit.

author: lucasrodes
body:
**0.10.0 stack, 1 of 4.** Breaking change — deprecated in 0.9.0 with a `FutureWarning` naming 0.10.0 as the removal. This is that removal.

## What goes

`whatstk/utils/gdrive.py`, its tests, the `[gdrive]` extra and the documentation page. A `gdrive://` path now raises:

```
ValueError: Google Drive support was removed in whatstk 0.10.0. Download the file from
Drive and pass the local path instead.
```

rather than falling through to a `FileNotFoundError` about a file that was never local.

## Why this one matters beyond the module

PyDrive2 was the root of most of the repository's open advisories, and **its pins made them unfixable**: `cryptography<44` and `pyOpenSSL<=24.2.1`, while the fixes live above both. That's why Dependabot's cryptography PR could only "upgrade" by downgrading pyOpenSSL two majors.

Removing it takes the whole subtree out. Verified on this branch:

```
cryptography   GONE        httplib2       GONE
pyopenssl      GONE        pyasn1         GONE
pydrive2       GONE        oauth2client   GONE
```

Confirmed a plain install pulls in none of them.

## Documentation it left behind

Three `seealso` blocks pointed at the removed page, and the install section still described the extra. The API page also ended up with two adjacent transitions once the section was dropped, which docutils rejects — the build caught it.

149 tests, 98.18% coverage, docs still 15 warnings / 0 errors.

body:
## V5.2b content: the audience scenes

Writes `data/audiences/` in the format Interface reported (the scene window reads them with no code change).

- `default.dialogue`: **all 21 titles**, each with two or three random variants (DialogueManager `%` lines), every line spoken as `{{name}}`: `opening`, `lever_<id>_success` and `_failure` for the six levers (argue, bargain, promise_date, pressure, flatter, friendship), `topic_<id>` for family, opinion, gossip, dinner and flirt, and `close_settled`, `close_promised`, `close_declined`. Variables used: `name`, `ask`, `president`, `topic` (`lever` is not needed by any line).
- Five stance overrides, which replace the default title by title: `sponsor`, `oppose`, `want`, `demand`, `defend`. Each carries its own `opening` and `close_settled` / `close_declined`, plus two to four lever lines whose tone differs most by stance (an opposer is never charmed by an argument alone; a demander answers pressure in kind). A title absent from an override falls back to the default.
- Each file has its `.dialogue.import` (headless import).

The topic of the opening is the asker's want in words (`{{ask}}`), so each line is written to read after "about", and no line assumes a stance the file does not carry. `flirt` is a polite, light deflection; it never makes the president's advances succeed or fail by content, that is for the lever odds.

### Verification
A scratch script compiled every file through `dialogue_manager` (no errors, 21 titles in the default, none of the required ones missing; overrides 5 to 6 titles). No repo test exists for `data/audiences/` yet; Interface's PR should add one that runs the same check. Data only, no `src/` change, no balance effect. English only; the speakers are the data's fictional askers.

### Merge note
Interface's branch (`v5.2b-ui-requests`) ships a placeholder `default.dialogue`; on a conflict, take this file.

body:
## 문제
`scripts/ui_smoke.py`가 main에서 실패했습니다.
1. **압축·턴 예산 시나리오:** New chat을 누른 직후, 대화가 다 만들어지기 전에 Enter를 눌렀습니다. `sendMessage`는 대화를 만드는 중이면 아무것도 보내지 않으므로(`app.js` `if (app.startingConversation) return;`, 입력한 글은 그대로 남음) 테스트가 생성보다 빠를 때마다 메시지가 나가지 않았습니다. 턴 예산 시나리오의 "Actual value: (빈 값)"도 같은 원인입니다.
2. **파일 시나리오:** 위 두 개에서 멈추던 것이 풀리자 드러났습니다. PR #72에서 파일 칩과 카드가 확장자, 이름, `크기 · Download`의 세 span으로 바뀌었는데 기대값이 예전 글자(`a.txt · 5 bytes`)였습니다.

## 변경 (테스트만, 제품 코드는 그대로)
- `new_chat(page, button)` helper: 대화가 열려 입력창에 포커스가 갈 때까지 기다립니다(페이지가 생성 마지막에 포커스를 줌). New chat을 누르는 8곳 모두 이것을 씁니다.
- 파일 칩과 카드는 `.file-name`, `.file-meta`, `.file-type`을 따로 확인합니다.
- `--only main,compaction,budget,…`로 일부 시나리오만 돌릴 수 있습니다.

## 검증

body:
## Ziel
P1: Herstellerreferenz für DJI Mavic 3M RGB- und Multispektral-Aufnahmeintervalle in der **nicht flugfähigen** WPML-Survey-/GSD-Vorschau ergänzen. Verhindert irrtümliche Übernahme von 20-MP-RGB-Pixelabmessungen auf die vier 5-MP-Multispektralsensoren.

## Änderungen
- Reines UMD-/Node-Modul `frontend/public/wpml-camera-reference-core.js` mit vier separat typisierten M3M-Aufnahmemodi: RGB JPEG 0,7 s; RGB JPEG+DNG 3 s; vier TIFF-Bänder 2 s; kombinierte RGB/MS-Aufnahme 2 s.
- Unveränderte, **manuell anzugebende physische** Sensorbreite/-höhe, Brennweite, AGL, Überlappung und Geschwindigkeit. Keine aus Kleinbildäquivalent oder Sensorformat erfundene mm-Kalibrierung.
- Strengere Prüfung von Bildpixelmaßen und Minimalkadenz; weniger als DJI-Herstellerreferenz wird abgelehnt; physikalisch zu kurze Intervalle in der UI ausdrücklich gewarnt.
- Für kombinierte RGB/MS-Aufnahme berechnet die Vorschau nur den primären Multispektral-Footprint und eine rein theoretische Bilddateimenge, **keinen** zweiten RGB-Footprint.
- Browserauswahl, neue Node-Regressionen, realer Chromium Offline-Import- und Kadenztest, Quellen-/Grenzendokumentation.

## Sicherheits- und Integrationsgrenze
Kein DJI RPC, keine MQTT-/REST-Schreibroute, keine Missions-KMZ, keine server.js-/Compose-/Pi-Änderung. `flightReady:false`, `exportableAsWaylines:false`, `cameraHardwareVerified:false`, `pilot2HardwareVerified:false`. Keine YMapper-Fremdcodeübernahme.

## Herstellerquellen
- https://enterprise.dji.com/mavic-3-m/specs
- https://dl.djicdn.com/downloads/DJI_Mavic_3_Enterprise/20240814/DJI_Mavic_3M_User_Manual_EN.pdf

## Vor Merge prüfen
CI inklusive aller neuen Node- und Chromium-Szenarien grün; keine bestehenden Editor-/WPML-Regressionsfehler; Kameraauswahl ist nachweislich offline und überschreibt keine realen Gerätekonfigurationen; Herstellerformate und Mindestintervalle nochmals gegen reale M3M-/Pilot-2-Firmware und Aufnahmeeinstellungen prüfen, bevor irgendeine Flugfreigabe diskutiert wird.

🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ serialize-javascript (3.1.0 → 7.1.4) · [Repo](https://github.com/yahoo/serialize-javascript)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Serialize JavaScript: Cross-site scripting (XSS) via unescaped

Impact

serialize-javascript escapes its output so it is safe to embed inside a
<script> element. Before 7.1.3 that guarantee did not hold for a function
value whose source ends in a bare </script.

Each function body is escaped on its own, and a bare </script was only
neutralized when followed — within the same body — by a character the HTML
tokenizer treats as ending the tag name (TAB, LF, FF, CR, SPACE, / or >).
A body ending exactly at </script has no following character, so it was
emitted unescaped. The delimiter is then supplied by the surrounding output
(for example the newline the space option emits after the value), and a
later serialized value can supply the closing > followed by markup:

const serialize = require('serialize-javascript');
function f() {} f.toString = () => 'function f(){ return 1 }//</script';
function g() {} g.toString = () => 'function g(x){ return x } > <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>';
serialize({ a: { f }, g }, { space: 2 });
// {
//   "a": {
//     "f": function f(){ return 1 }//</script
//   },
//   "g": function g(x){ return x } > <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>
// }

Embedded in a <script> element, the script ends at the injected tag and the
<img> becomes a live element in the page.

Exploitation requires an attacker to control the source text of a
serialized function, in practice through a spoofed toString(). Real
functions always end in }, so ordinary function values are not affected,
and non-function values (including strings containing </script) are
escaped correctly.

Patches

Fixed in 7.1.3 (#235). The bare </script form is now also matched at
the end of the function body, so it is escaped regardless of what follows it
in the output.

Workarounds

Upgrade to 7.1.3. If you cannot upgrade, do not serialize function values
whose source text (or toString()) can be influenced by an attacker.

Credits

Reported by ha_kr25 via the Yahoo bug bounty program.
