Impact

serialize-javascript escapes its output so it is safe to embed inside a
<script> element. In 7.1.1 that guarantee does not hold for function
values: a crafted function body can carry a literal, unescaped </script>
into the output, terminating the script element early so the remainder is
parsed as HTML.

SCRIPT_CLOSE_REGEXP used <\/script[^>]*> as its first alternative. The
character class excludes only >, so a single match could run from one
</script all the way to the next > anywhere in the source — swallowing a
second, complete </script> along the way. Only one replacement is emitted
per match, and the plain-code branch neutralizes just the leading <
('< ' + match.slice(1)), so the swallowed tag was re-emitted verbatim.

Reaching that shape requires </script in code position, which is legal
JavaScript: x</script=+/ parses as x < /script=+/, a comparison against a

author: philpem
body:
V.34 body family, wave 10. One source fact recovered beyond PR355; two
hypotheses measured to a negative and reported with their forcing addresses.

| symbol | LCS before -> after | longest run | instruction count (blob / before / after) | grade |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `V34demodulate` | 191 -> 199 | 36 -> 36 | 283 / 279 / 277 | SIZE |
| `V34agc` | 206 -> 206 | 36 -> 36 | 222 / 221 / 221 | BYTES unchanged |
| `receiver` | 475 -> 475 | 16 -> 16 | 994 / 987 / 987 | SIZE unchanged |

## `V34demodulate`: the mixer step is read at its use

The object reads `mix_carrier_step` (+0x1b8) at 0x5b2ae, between the two
demodulator products, and never stores it. Ours cached it in an `int step`
whose live range spans `cos_v`/`sin_v` and both `demod_i`/`demod_q`
products, so register pressure gave it a stack home:

```
blob  V34demodulate %esp slots: 0x4 0xc 0x10 0x16 0x18 0x1a
after V34demodulate %esp slots: 0x4 0xc 0x10 0x16 0x18 0x1a     (identical)
before                         0x4 0x8 0xc 0x12 0x14 0x18 0x1a (two extra)
```

The cached local forced `g0` to 0x8 and `g1` to 0xc; with the field read at
the point of use the allocator places them at the object's 0xc/0x10. LCS
191 -> 199 and the live slot set now matches exactly. The remaining 6
instructions are placement, not content: the object keeps the frame-end
`lea 0x10c(%eax)` in-line at 5af29 and defers the `rx_samples` load to
5af5f, while ours hoists both (oracle 5af10..5af60, ours 0x900..0x950),
and the AGC-adapt block sits after the mixer here and before it in the
object. Re-writing the `count <= 3` arm order as `count > 3` was measured
and produces byte-identical code, so the placement is not an arm-order
fact.

## `V34agc`: residual is a combiner/register fold, no source fact

The one-instruction gap is the object's `movzwl %si,%eax; cwtl` before
`cmp $0x1f,%ax` at 0x5b879/0x5b87c (and the same pair in `V34demodulate`
at 0x5b0c9/0x5b0cc). It materialises the `(short)(unsigned short)` return
conversion; the compare then reads only `%ax`, so both instructions are
dead. Three source spellings were measured and are byte-identical to the
baseline: `static short agc_rms`, a short return type with the redundant
`(short)` removed from the body, and an explicit `(short)` at both call
sites. The fold follows the pseudo's register (`%esi` here, `%ebx` in the
object, under `-frename-registers`), so this is allocation state and not
a source fact. Nothing adopted.

## `receiver`: the frame gap is a 12-byte address-taken group

Frame is 0x8c against the object's 0x9c. Every `%esp` access was mapped:

```
blob  0x4 0x8 0xc | 0x14..0x30 | [0x34..0x3f DEAD] | 0x40..0x88 0x8c/0x8e | [0x90..0x9b DEAD]
ours  0x4 0x8 0xc | 0x14..0x30 | 0x34..0x88 0x8a
```

The 0x14..0x30 block is identical in both. The object's `virtual-stack-vars`
`mant`/`shift` are at frame offsets -0xe/-0x10 (0x8c/0x8e) while ours are
at -2/-4 (0x88/0x8a): the object therefore has 12 bytes of address-taken
local storage allocated *before* the inlined `agc_rms` body, at 0x90..0x9b,
and a further dead 12-byte spill run at 0x34..0x3f. Ours has neither. The
only address-taken locals in our source before that call are `eq_re` and
`eq_im` (8 bytes, passed to `V34EqualizerFilter`), and rewriting them as
pointer locals is byte-identical because the address is materialised as a
stack temp at lreg rather than as a `virtual-stack-vars` reference. No
source shape producing the 12-byte group was found; the frame residual is
open with these offsets recorded.

## Validation

- `make period J=3`: **394 differential fixtures passed, 0 failed**; structural checks pass.
- Census unchanged: EXACT 1,146 / UNRESOLVED 0 / REGALLOC 36 / BYTES 87 / SIZE 583; grade 0-or-1 1,182; link-selected 1,149. Ratchet OK.
- `V34agc` and `receiver` objects are byte-identical to the parent build; only the `V34demodulate` body changes.
- No padding, flags, attributes, fixtures or ratchet policy changed.

Note: the first local `make tc` in this worktree was interrupted and left
two zero-symbol 441-byte objects (`V92bitsToSymbol`, `V92EchoCanceller`)
newer than their sources, which briefly read as an 18-symbol census loss.
Deleting them and rebuilding reproduced the 1,146 baseline; the finding is
the same trap HANDOVER records for `src_service_Fdspkrnl.c.o`.

body: ## What does this PR do? Adds a LAN/tailnet-only phone pairing endpoint and makes `hydi-update` securely obtain and atomically store the phone read token without human copying. ## Why? Remove manual secret transfer while preserving narrow network, authentication, rate, audit, and filesystem controls. ## Changes - Add `GET /api/phone/pair`, authenticated with a constant-time comparison against `HYDI_BOARD_HUMAN_TOKEN` and returning only the configured phone read token. - Restrict pairing by the real socket address to loopback, `192.168.0.0/16`, or Tailscale `100.64.0.0/10`; forwarded headers are ignored. - Add five-requests/minute/IP limiting, `Cache-Control: no-store`, non-secret audit outcomes, and fail closed with 503 when the phone token is absent. - Update `hydi-update` to validate an existing revenue token, pair over each `FRANK_HOSTS` entry when absent/rejected, and print only a fixed paired/failure status. - Add an atomic mode-600 token-line replacer that receives the pair response through a private temporary file and emits no token output; update the Termux runbook. ## Subsystems affected - [ ] Ingestion Layer - [ ] RAW EVENT LEDGER - [ ] CASCADE (classifier) - [ ] KILO (hypothesis generator) - [ ] ProtoForge (policy engine / DSL) - [ ] Emission Layer - [ ] Replay Engine - [ ] PAO System (`pao-system/`) - [x] API Layer (`api/`) - [ ] Supabase Edge Functions (`supabase/functions/`) - [ ] Revenue Engine (`revenue-engine/`) - [ ] Workers (`workers/`) - [ ] Frontend (`pages/`, `components/`) - [ ] HeidiOrchestrator / HybridModelStack / HeidiCoreLoop - [x] Config / Infrastructure ## Pipeline integrity - [x] Not applicable — no pipeline layer was modified ## Database / migrations - [x] No new migrations in this PR - [ ] New migration has a corresponding test in `tests/migrations/.test.js` - [ ] Any enum or allowed state-machine transition changed → add `STATE_MACHINE_APPROVED` to the PR description body - [ ] Superseded migration uses `.sql.skip` suffix ## Worker registration - [x] No new workers added - [ ] New worker added to `workers/` and registered in `WorkerOrchestrator.js` ## Testing - [x] `npm run typecheck` passes — zero new TypeScript errors introduced - [x] `npm test` passes (528 suites; 6,087 passed, 6 skipped) - [ ] `npm run test:integration` passes, or intentionally skipped with reason (local route/shell behavior is covered without external services) - [x] New behaviour covered by a new test - [x] Coverage not decreased Tests cover required auth, real-socket network allowlisting, per-IP limiting, no-store, 503 configuration failure, token-free logs/stdout, replacement of duplicate token lines, preservation of other settings, and mode 600. `sh -n termux/hydi-update.sh` and focused ESLint also pass. ## Security - [x] No secrets, API keys, or service-role credentials committed - [x] `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is server-side only — never passed to client bundles - [x] All `catch` variables typed `unknown` and guarded: `error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'` ## Checklist - [x] No breaking changes to public API — or breaking changes are explicitly documented in this PR - [x] Modified Edge Functions remain pure ESM (Deno-compatible; no `require()`) - [x] `system_dashboard` Supabase view is unaffected, or health endpoints updated to handle any schema change gracefully - [x] `nnotification.service.ts` double-`n` filename preserved (do not rename until all imports are updated together)

body:
## Summary

Implements M4's provider-neutral inbound event envelope and delivery lifecycle for Numou omnichannel.

## Included

- Adds `InboundEventEnvelope` with trusted channel context, provider event ID/type, SHA-256 payload fingerprint and timestamps.
- Adds `InboundDeliveryState` with explicit verification, processing, retryable failure, rejection and dead-letter transitions.
- Adds unit tests for normalization, malformed fingerprints, identifier bounds, lifecycle transitions and terminal states.
- Documents durable inbox invariants and production acceptance criteria.

## Safety and architecture

- No raw payload is copied into the metadata envelope.
- Provider event IDs must be scoped by tenant and provider account in persistence.
- A duplicate ID with a different payload fingerprint is a conflict, not an overwrite.
- State transition checks are not a substitute for atomic persistence.
- Authentication, tenant/branch authorization and application-port dispatch remain required before business effects.
- Existing commerce domains remain authoritative; no duplicate order/catalog/inventory models are introduced.

## Validation

Tests and the full Maven reactor have **not** been run in this environment. CI must validate Java/compiler compatibility, the foundation API and module graph before merge.

## Not included

No database-backed inbox, broker, HTTP endpoint, provider signature implementation, retry scheduler, dead-letter UI or provider connector is claimed by this PR. Those require runtime infrastructure and concrete provider contracts.

## Issue

Issue 340 · Varningen innan inmatning går förlorad (M45 Itemets sida)

Closes #990

## Vad ändringen gör

`ItemForm` frågar nu innan ändrad inmatning går förlorad, i skapandet och i redigeringen. En Inertia-`GET` till en annan adress avbryts i `router.on('before')` medan `form.isDirty`, och `UiConfirmDialog` frågar: *Leave* gör om besöket, *Cancel* stannar. `beforeunload` är satt bara medan formuläret är ändrat. Sparande, *Save and add another* och väljarens *Create "X"* är skrivningar (`POST`/`PATCH`) och frågar inte; efter *Leave* frågar ingenting igen, så *Cancel* efter bekräftelse går rakt igenom. Lyssnarna tas bort när formuläret avmonteras.

- [x] `AGENTS.md` och `CLAUDE.md`
- [x] GitHub-issue #990
- [x] `docs/Backlog/M45 Itemets sida.md` § 340

## Acceptanskriterier

Alla prov är källkodsprov i `tests/Feature/Frontend/OsparadInmatningTest.php`, som grannfilerna. Beteendet i webbläsaren går inte att köra här; se handprov nedan.

| Klart när | Test |
|---|---|
| ett ändrat formulär frågar innan en länk lämnar det | `avbryter en navigering i router.on before och frågar med UiConfirmDialog`, `frågar bara när formuläret är ändrat` |
| *Cancel* i dialogen stannar och *Leave* lämnar | `låter Leave göra om besöket och Cancel stanna` |
| ett oändrat formulär frågar inte | `frågar bara när formuläret är ändrat`, `frågar bara vid en GET till en annan adress` |
| att spara frågar inte | `frågar inte vid ett sparande, Save and add another eller väljarens Create` |
| att skapa en tagg i väljaren frågar inte | `frågar inte vid ett sparande, Save and add another eller väljarens Create` |
| `beforeunload` är satt bara när formuläret är ändrat | `sätter beforeunload bara medan formuläret är ändrat` |
| lyssnarna tas bort när formuläret avmonteras | `tar bort lyssnarna när formuläret avmonteras` |

Handprov för granskaren: ändra ett fält och klicka en länk i sidomenyn (dialog; *Cancel* stannar, *Leave* navigerar), tryck *Cancel*-länken i skapandet med ändrad inmatning (en fråga, sedan ut), ladda om med ändrat fält (webbläsarens fråga), skapa en tagg i väljaren (ingen fråga), spara (ingen fråga).

- [x] Inget under `Out of scope` är rört

Ändrade filer: `resources/js/components/ItemForm.vue`, `lang/en/ui.php`, `tests/Feature/Frontend/OsparadInmatningTest.php`. Inget utanför rutan.

**Welcome to Depfu** 👋 This is one of the first three pull requests with dependency updates we've sent your way. We tried to start with a few easy patch-level updates. Hopefully your tests will pass and you can merge this pull request without too much risk. This should give you an idea how Depfu works in general. After you merge your first pull request, we'll send you a few more. We'll never open more than seven PRs at the same time so you're not getting overwhelmed with updates. [Let us know](mailto:hi@depfu.com) if you have any questions. Thanks so much for giving Depfu a try!
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ serialize-javascript (3.1.0 → 7.1.4) · [Repo](https://github.com/yahoo/serialize-javascript)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Serialize JavaScript: Cross-site scripting (XSS) via unescaped

Impact

serialize-javascript escapes its output so it is safe to embed inside a
<script> element. Before 7.1.3 that guarantee did not hold for a function
value whose source ends in a bare </script.

Each function body is escaped on its own, and a bare </script was only
neutralized when followed — within the same body — by a character the HTML
tokenizer treats as ending the tag name (TAB, LF, FF, CR, SPACE, / or >).
A body ending exactly at </script has no following character, so it was
emitted unescaped. The delimiter is then supplied by the surrounding output
(for example the newline the space option emits after the value), and a
later serialized value can supply the closing > followed by markup:

const serialize = require('serialize-javascript');
function f() {} f.toString = () => 'function f(){ return 1 }//</script';
function g() {} g.toString = () => 'function g(x){ return x } > <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>';
serialize({ a: { f }, g }, { space: 2 });
// {
//   "a": {
//     "f": function f(){ return 1 }//</script
//   },
//   "g": function g(x){ return x } > <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>
// }

Embedded in a <script> element, the script ends at the injected tag and the
<img> becomes a live element in the page.

Exploitation requires an attacker to control the source text of a
serialized function, in practice through a spoofed toString(). Real
functions always end in }, so ordinary function values are not affected,
and non-function values (including strings containing </script) are
escaped correctly.

Patches

Fixed in 7.1.3 (#235). The bare </script form is now also matched at
the end of the function body, so it is escaped regardless of what follows it
in the output.

Workarounds

Upgrade to 7.1.3. If you cannot upgrade, do not serialize function values
whose source text (or toString()) can be influenced by an attacker.

Credits

Reported by ha_kr25 via the Yahoo bug bounty program.

🚨 Serialize JavaScript: Cross-site scripting (XSS) via unescaped in serialized function bodies

Impact

serialize-javascript escapes its output so it is safe to embed inside a
<script> element. In 7.1.1 that guarantee does not hold for function
values: a crafted function body can carry a literal, unescaped </script>
into the output, terminating the script element early so the remainder is
parsed as HTML.

SCRIPT_CLOSE_REGEXP used <\/script[^>]*> as its first alternative. The
character class excludes only >, so a single match could run from one
</script all the way to the next > anywhere in the source — swallowing a
second, complete </script> along the way. Only one replacement is emitted
per match, and the plain-code branch neutralizes just the leading <
('< ' + match.slice(1)), so the swallowed tag was re-emitted verbatim.

Reaching that shape requires </script in code position, which is legal
JavaScript: x</script=+/ parses as x < /script=+/, a comparison against a
regex literal.

author: dan-petty
body:
## Summary

An OpenSpec change folder is now the record of every item. `devops pr check-readiness` no longer requires a task file. It requires that the pull request add the archived change folder of the issue that it closes. The task files, the test and the baseline that checked them, and every code path, message and document sentence that read them are deleted. Git history keeps the old task files. The owner decided on 2026-10-23 that new work uses OpenSpec, and ADR 0010 is the design. This pull request also delivers #1846: readiness checks the archived folder.

Readiness (`src/devops_cli/commands/pr.py`):

- A pull request that closes #N must add a file (GitHub status `added`, `renamed` or `copied`) in `openspec/changes/archive/<date>-N-<slug>/`. `uv run devops openspec archive <change>` writes this folder in the last commit. The blocker names the expected folder and the archive command, with the slug of the change when the pull request has an active folder.
- A pull request that changes a file in `openspec/specs/` and adds no archived folder of its own issue is blocked. A pull request that changes a file in `openspec/changes/archive/` outside the archived folder of its own issue is blocked. The blocker names each file.
- The rule applies where the base holds `openspec/changes/`. The base probe reads that directory in place of `docs/agent/tasks`, so readiness sends the same number of requests. Every other grounding rule is kept.
- The closed grammars of the active folder and of the archived folder are in `config/constants.py` (`CONST_OPENSPEC_CHANGE_FOLDER_RE`, `CONST_OPENSPEC_ARCHIVED_FOLDER_RE`). The archived grammar is separate, because the date prefix would make the active grammar read the year as the issue.
- Readiness does not read `tasks.md`. In a scratch repository with the opt-outs set, `openspec archive <change> --yes` archived a change with one unticked task and only warned, and `openspec validate --archived` then exited 1. The `openspec` row of `devops ci` runs that check, and a failing check run already blocks readiness.

Deleted: `_writes_task_file`, `_changes_its_task_file`, `_base_has_task_files`, `CONST_AGENT_TASKS_DIR`, `CONST_AGENT_TASK_FILE_RE`, `CONST_PR_FILE_WRITTEN_STATUSES`, the messages `grounding_task_file_missing` and `grounding_tasks_dir_unread`, `tests/test_agent_task_files.py`, `tests/fixtures/task_files_baseline.txt`, and `docs/agent/tasks/` (632 files with the template). The task-file entries of the docs inventory and of review routing (`CONST_REVIEW_ROUTED_PATH_PATTERNS`) are gone.

Documents: AGENTS.md (rule 1 names the change folder and its archive, rule 2 says to record the feasibility check in the proposal's `## Feasibility` section, and one routing row sends "plan and record the item" to `openspec/config.yaml` and ADR 0010; 6,370 of 6,500 characters), the pull request template ("Change: `openspec/changes/<issue>-<slug>/`"), `CONTEXT.md` ("Change" and "Spec" replace "Task file"), `docs/SDLC.md`, `docs/ROUTINE_TASKS.md`, `docs/SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`, `docs/DEVCONTAINER_USAGE.md`, `docs/agent/README.md`, `docs/_config.yml`, the two knowledge-base guides, the route of the generated AGENTS.md, and the generated references. The Loki values comment that named a task file now states the procedure itself.

This pull request plans itself as `openspec/changes/1847-openspec-change-folders/` and archives it in the same commit. The commit adds `openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-23-1847-openspec-change-folders/` and the first living spec, `openspec/specs/pr-grounding/spec.md`. Its `pr-grounding` delta has a Purpose and three requirements, and each scenario is a test in `tests/test_pr_cmd.py`.

Tests:

- `tests/test_pr_cmd.py`: a pull request that adds, renames or copies the archived folder of its issue passes, also with the living specs that its archive writes. A pull request with no folder, an active folder, a modified or removed archived folder, or the folder of another issue is blocked, and the message names the expected folder. A spec write without the archive, a change to another issue's archive and a change to a stray file of the archive directory are blocked. A base without `openspec/changes/` is exempt, and another lookup failure is one blocker. On the base, 25 tests of the file failed against these changes.
- `tests/test_architectural_invariants.py`: `test_the_task_files_are_decommissioned` keeps `docs/agent/tasks` out of the tree and out of `src/`, `tests/`, `k8s/`, `.github/` and the hand-written documents, with a negative control. It failed while the directory was in the tree.
- The tests that used task-file paths as fixtures use change-folder paths.

A pull request that is open when this merges and adds a task file must convert it into a change folder and archive that change when it updates from `main`. Readiness and the decommission test refuse the task file.

### Task files that merge while this PR is open

Pull requests that were opened before this change still add task files, and they can merge before this one. So this PR does not turn red when one does:
- The docs inventory keeps the one glob `docs/agent/tasks/task-*.md`.
- `test_the_task_files_are_decommissioned` allows only `task-*.md` files in that directory (no guide, no template) and that one glob in the source. Every other mention of the directory still fails.
- After this PR merges, readiness refuses a new pull request that adds a task file. #2041 then deletes the late task files, the glob and the allowance, and makes the check strict.

## Item

Closes #1847

Also delivers #1846.

Change: `openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-23-1847-openspec-change-folders/`

#2251 item 23: "The jump menu opens with Ctrl+F everywhere (already so on some pages)."

author: richardparslow-commits
body:
## Why

The worker and sandbox paths import `app.evaluate`, `app.agiloop_telemetry` and
`app.condition_selector` in environments that have neither Streamlit nor the
OpenAI wheel. A bare `import streamlit` aborted those imports, so nothing
downstream ran.

## What changed

- **Headless imports.** `app/evaluate.py` and `app/agiloop_telemetry.py` fall
  back to a session-state stub; `app/condition_selector.py` imports but raises a
  named `RuntimeError` if the selector is actually rendered, instead of a
  `'NoneType' object has no attribute` cascade.
- **`app/llm.py`.** Resolves `OpenAI`, `NOT_GIVEN` and `DefaultHttpxClient`
  through lightweight stand-ins only when the wheel is absent, and still raises
  `ModuleNotFoundError` from the call itself. With the SDK installed the real
  objects are used, which `test_not_given_sentinel_is_the_sdk_object` pins.
- **`app/job_payload.py`.** The result helpers import the pipelines lazily, as
  the module docstring already claimed ("stdlib-only"); the `encode_result`
  docstring stays a docstring.
- **Telemetry.** `feature.error` / `app.error` now send the exception class
  rather than `str(error)`, which can embed record or statement text.
- **Tracing.** `unavailable_reason()` reports "disabled" before reporting an
  import error, so a deliberately-disabled build does not look broken.
- **Archil runner.** `scripts/archil_sandbox_runner.py` implements the same
  extractor contract as the Vercel runner using a serverless microVM over a
  copy-on-write disk: one branch and one `exec` per file instead of five CLI
  round-trips, with the branch deleted on every exit path, including SIGTERM.
  `--check` emits the JSON verdict `scripts/check_sandbox.py` consumes.

## Verification

- Full suite: **3,403 tests OK, 72 skipped** (254 s).
- `mypy app`: clean (100 files).
- `python -m tests.harness_imports --all`: clean.
- New guard in `tests/test_condition_selector.py` proven to fail on the
  `st = None` variant (`AttributeError` instead of the named error).
- Pre-commit hook (secret scan, hermetic harness, Streamlit-option rule) passes.

## Caveat

The Archil tests exercise a hand-written fake `disk` CLI, so they prove the
runner's own logic and command shapes, not that Archil's CLI accepts them. No
call has been made against a live Archil account.

author: frankischilling
body:
Adds per-game cheats, physical memory inspection and RAM search, console CPU/register/disassembly tools, execution breakpoints, CPU/DMA watchpoints, trace capture and graphics/audio inspection. The shared modal tools retain machine ownership and pause/input behavior; exports use atomic replacement and keep errors available for retry. Opening read-only views does not execute hardware or read consuming device ports.

Cheats support console and handheld code formats, individual/global toggles and per-game persistence. CPU tools step at instruction boundaries while retaining crossed display fields and live DMA work. The graphics/audio window shows raw CGRAM, planar/Mode 7 tiles, OAM objects, console DSP voices/registers and the recent decoded sample ring, with explicit field advance and BMP/TSV exports.

Applies the requested LLVM/C++20 four-space style across all C/C++ sources, including the optimized test template. The README stays concise; full controls, formats and build guidance live in docs. Windows CI uses a shared four-process compiler scheduler; a local MSVC core build fell from 163 to 75 seconds in one comparison.

- New model, UI, storage and renamed test translation units compile directly with MSVC.
- All 256 opcode operand lengths match CPU fetches across E/M/X combinations; mapped peeks and hardware captures retain exact state across 78 cartridge/region profiles.
- Four 600-field game runs retain picture, timing and PCM hashes, reaching 157-182 FPS locally. These cover fixed input sequences, not full game playthroughs.
- All 431 C/C++ source files pass the requested format. Documentation links and whitespace checks pass.

This retro covers #97 (start, pause, and finish a workout), green on Xcode Cloud at its merged head 6e4d736, and the two sessions since the last run: the end of #97 (a CI failure, its fix, the merge and wrap-up) and a session that rebased the open retro PRs #96 and #98 onto `main` and asked for go-aheads. It fixes two findings, one of them on `main` instead of deferring it to #96 a second time, corrects one rule #97 made incomplete, and reports three that no change in the repo can prevent.

**For #96: drop its `/onward` hunk on waking about every 15 minutes** (the sentence starting "A subagent in the background says nothing until it ends"). This PR carries that sentence, widened to a CI watch, so the two conflict on that one bullet; every other hunk of #96 still applies.

## Fixed

1. #97 merged without its last commit in its body. Xcode Cloud failed one workout UI test on bb06c8e; a builder found a real race (Start pressed while an added row still entered), fixed it, and added a test that fails without the fix (6e4d736). The lead's prompt asked it to push, and auto-merge was armed, so the PR merged as soon as CI passed, with a body that names neither the fix nor, in its Friction line, that CI found it. Today the builder definition says to open or update the PR with `/pr` when the work is done. With this change, it says every later push updates the body too, a fix the lead asked only to push included, because the body is the commit `main` keeps. *(agent definition)*
2. In both sessions the lead said nothing for about 43 minutes while work ran in the background: a builder fixing the CI failure, then a watch on the two retro PRs' runs. That watch chained `gh pr checks --watch` for #96 and #98; both runs finished 13:32 to 13:33 UTC, but the watch never returned and was stopped at the harness's background time limit at 14:04, so the green results reached the maintainer about 30 minutes late. Why the watch didn't exit isn't established from the record (the same command exits at once on a finished PR today). #98 deferred the silence to #96's 15-minute hunk once; this is the second time, so the fix goes on `main`. With this change, `/onward` says to wake about every 15 minutes while a subagent or a CI watch runs in the background, read where it is at that moment (the subagent's last entry, the PR's `gh pr checks`), send that line, and take a finished check as the result whatever the watch says. *(skill)*

- The CI failure on bb06c8e was a real bug that the local runs missed on timing; CI worked as intended, and the fix added a test that catches it locally. Not a finding.

Neither session drew design options, chose between rules, or wrote a card's answers, so its fixes had no new occasion: the design board, tables for a choice, and reading a card back stay as #96 and #98 recorded them (worked); the dark-only Status line, `known` covering the lead's prompt, and the memory note on friction stay too early to tell. author: eduardopicado
body:
Builds on #98 (merged): it uses the shared sight-word code in `src/content/sight.ts`. It doesn't depend on #100, so the two can merge in either order.

The last of his teacher's sight word activities: *"Choose simple books and ask your child to point out sight words as you read together."* This is a new reading game, 👉 **Read and Point**.

## The game

- **Stories:** sixteen short ones, two at each level from 1 to 8. Ants in a tin, a big kick, a fox and a frog, lunch at the shop, a goal in the rain, football at the park, a kite on a windy day, a big match.
  - Every word, the title's too, is one he can read at the story's level, from the word lists or the school's sight words.
  - Each story's level is exactly its hardest word's.
- **What he finds** (chosen in ⚙):
  - **One sight word:** "Find every **the**", with a count (*1 of 3*), so he knows when he has them all. The word is one that comes at least twice and isn't a single letter.
  - **Every sight word:** all the school's sight words up to his level, wherever they are.
- **A wrong tap** shakes, says the word he tapped, and names it ("That says they."). That's the useful part of a mistake: he hears the difference.
- **A word found** lights up with its tricky letters marked, as in Tricky Words.
- **🔊 Read it to me** reads the story a sentence at a time with the sentence lit, for reading along. A tap on a word stops it.
- The stories come from his level and below, his own level first; ⚙ can change the level and how many stories (3 or 5). The game's own sticker 👉 at the end.

## Content

- `STORIES` in `words.ts` (`Title | story @level`), loaded as `ALL_STORIES` with their sentences.
- `src/content/stories.ts` cuts a story into tappable words (each keeps its punctuation on its line, so a full stop never starts a line), counts its sight words and picks the one to hunt for.
- The content test checks:
  - every word is readable at the story's level;
  - the level is exactly the hardest word's;
  - there are two stories at every level;
  - each story has a sight word of its level to hunt for, more than once;
  - cutting a story into words loses no letter or mark;
  - no blocked words.

## Checks

- `npx tsc --noEmit`, the unit tests (330) and the content test (93, six new) are clean.
- New `tests/e2e/read-and-point.spec.ts`:
  - a round of three stories: find every copy; a wrong tap shakes, is said and named; the results show the story with a miss;
  - every sight word, with the story at the chosen level or below;
  - read aloud sentence by sentence, in order, and stopped by a tap.
- 489 browser tests pass at 820×1180, 1180×820 and 375px with zero console errors, including the catalog-wide ones (home tiles, offline, leaving a game, accessibility of every game).

author: molina211
body:
## User story

code-corhuila/multi-tour-docs#203 (HU-WRK-007), task RT-06 of spec 001-hu-wrk-007 (code-corhuila/multi-tour-docs#498), AC3.

## What changes and why

The relay never told anyone that an event had stopped for good. Now, when the owner of an outbox answers the attempts route with an event in status `FAILED` (after its 20 attempts), the relay writes one `ERROR` line with `alert="event_failed"`, the event id, type and publisher, and never the payload or the raw error. When it reads a pending event with `occurredAt` more than five minutes before its clock, it writes one `WARN` line with `alert="event_pending_too_long"` (ADR-004 D8), once per event per run. The alerts are structured log lines a Grafana rule can match; that rule does not exist yet (DP-WRK7-3 of the spec). `RecordFailedAttempt` now returns whether the owner ended the event, read from the `status` of its answer; a 2xx answer whose body cannot be read counts as recorded and not ended.

## How it was tested

The CI is red because GitHub Actions is locked for billing on the organization, not because of this change: jobs fail in seconds with "The job was not started because your account is locked due to a billing issue" ([run 38650773906](https://github.com/code-corhuila/multi-tour-worker-event-relay/actions/runs/38650773906)). Local checks instead:

- `gofmt -l .` empty, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` passes in every package.
- Red first: commit `1b2accf` carries the tests with a compiling skeleton (the port signature and a clock hook); the three tests failed on assertions. After the review, tests for the age limits (exactly five minutes, no date), a forged event type and a non-JSON answer were added; the non-JSON one failed before the one-line fix.

The pull request will be run again in CI when Actions is back.

## Checklist
- [x] Meets the criteria of the spec (RN-WRK7-06 and -07)
- [x] No secrets; the payload never reaches a log line
- [x] No database, no new dependency
- [x] Under 400 changed lines, excluding tests

author: resonaura
body:
After a source restart, the first camera viewer can fail with FFmpeg “dimensions not set”; a later open works. Cached parameter sets can retain timestamps from older GOPs, creating a long synthetic interval before the cached IDR during a new reader's short probe.

Replay every packet in the cached picture at that picture's timestamp. Publish readiness after a complete bounded IDR cache and SPS/PPS are available, so an orphan IDR tail cannot release a waiting viewer prematurely. Copied media payloads, recording clocks, source recovery and the fresh live IDR gate remain unchanged. Bumps NVR to 0.3.10.

Validation: the old-timestamp regression fails before the fix; all 70 tests pass with the real native binary and no skips. Coverage includes nearly twenty-second-old STAP parameters, multi-slice IDRs, incomplete readiness, RTP bursts/clocks, writer backpressure and repeated browser signaling. Real first-open/restart acceptance follows deployment.

author: tpsjasper
body:
## Summary

Two correctness fixes, with regression tests, docs and the `1.1.2` patch release metadata.

### Pinecone: a failed async list page now raises (#794)

`PineconeIndex._async_get_all()` used to log `Error fetching vectors` and stop paging on any non-200 reply. It returned an empty list when the first page failed, and a partial list when a later page did, so `adelete()`, `aget_routes()`, `arefresh()` and a sparse-encoder `aadd()` could act as if routes were missing. It now raises the HTTP error (`aiohttp.ClientResponseError`); a 404 still reads as an empty index, matching the synchronous `_get_all()`.

`tests/integration/test_pinecone_list.py` runs a local aiohttp server, so it needs no Pinecone service. It covers 401/403/429/500/503 on the first and on a later page, 404, pagination parameters and metadata, and the four downstream operations.

### Isotonic: tied scores no longer depend on order (#788)

`_isotonic()` kept equal scores as separate PAV blocks, so the same labelled multiset could pool differently and produce repeated interpolation knots with different values. Equal scores are now grouped before pooling, each block is weighted by its sample count, and block endpoints are emitted once. Output without ties is unchanged, and calibrators saved by older versions still load and interpolate as before.

The tests cover repeated-score permutations, weighted pooling, threshold decisions, interpolation and serialization.

### Release metadata

- `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`: version `1.1.2`.
- `docs/user-guide/changelog.md`: the `1.1.2` entry.
- `docs/integrations/pinecone.md` and `docs/user-guide/features/calibration.md`: describe the new behavior.

If you would rather land the fixes first and cut `1.1.2` separately, I can drop the release commit.

## Tests

- `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_pinecone_list.py -q` — 35 passed
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/routers/test_calibration.py -q` — 16 passed
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/routers -q` — 56 passed
- `uv run ruff check ...` and `uv run ruff format --check ...` — pass
- `uv lock --check` — pass
- On the pre-fix tree (`1fa1937`), the new tests fail: 30/35 Pinecone cases and 5/16 calibration cases.
- Full `make test` was not run locally (Docker is unavailable here); CI runs it with the service containers.

Fixes #794
Fixes #788

author: aaronbuxbaum
body:
## Before

A production deploy with a mistyped `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` went out, as long as the key was set to something that isn't 32 base64 bytes. The app then treated the key as missing, which locks every two-factor staffer out. On a slow link, the offline manifest's banner also repeated the saved time already shown in the header just above it.

## After

The production build refuses a malformed `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` or `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS`, and names the variable but not its value. The slow-link banner says it is the saved list, not the live one, and leaves the time to the header.

## What

- `scripts/check-env.mjs`: in production, each sealing key must decode to 32 bytes, exactly as `parseKey` in `src/lib/secret-box.ts` reads it. There are 3 new tests in `scripts/check-env.test.mjs`, 2 of which fail on main's version. Two doc lines are corrected: `docs/agents/repo-checks.md` and the deploy runbook.
- `src/components/offline-manifest/TripHeader.tsx` and the en-US/es-ES `staff/shared.json`: the banner drops its repeated "saved {when}" clause.

## How

These are the two small, certain fixes from the nightly check of the 2026-10-23 batch. The check walked the offline manifest as the captain on a dead link at 390 and 1280. Ran lint, typecheck, `check:repo`, `check:copy`, `check:voice`, 23 focused test files (217 tests) and the e2e slow-copy test. `verify:push --quick` passed its static checks, but its related-unit-test step hit the background time limit on this box, so CI runs the rest.

## Reviews launched

- `security-reviewer`: launched on the key check. It came back clean: no key material is printed, and the check agrees with `parseKey` on every input it tried (standard base64, base64url, unpadded, whitespace, hex). The rotation gap a build check can't see is filed as #2999.
- `dive-domain-expert`: launched on the banner, framed as a captain mid roll call on a dead link. It came back clean: the chip and banner still say it is the saved copy, and the header still shows when it was saved. Its follow-ups (the saved time names no zone; the Spanish stale pill reads "expired") are filed as #2998.

## Visual diffs

6 changed at e4209d7, all intended: `offline-manifest-unanswered` and `offline-manifest-live-answering`, light 1280 and 390 and dark 1280. Each differs only in the slow-link banner, which went from "…the list this phone saved (Jul 21, 2026, 9:30 AM), not the live one." to "…the list this phone saved, not the live one." At 1280 the geometry is unchanged. At 390 the banner wraps one line fewer, so the page is 24 px shorter.

#2999

author: mahtradr
body:
**What was wrong**

In the Forging Calculator, a mix like 5 Tin + 5 Zinc showed two orange warnings stacked on top of each other: "Ingot Will Alloy" and "Ingot Will Alloy: No metal reaches 67% of the total quantity." They mean the same thing, so the second box just added clutter.

The first one fired when more than one metal was over 33%. The second fires when no metal reaches 67%. The 67% one is the rule experienced crafters describe: if one metal makes up 67% or more, the ingot stays pure; anything less alloys. If two metals are both over 33%, the biggest one has to be under 67%, so in practice the two warnings almost always showed together.

The one exception makes the first box worse than redundant. The 67% check rounds away tiny computer arithmetic errors, but the 33% check didn't. On an exact 67/33 split entered with decimals or across repeated rows, the smaller share can come out a hair over 33% (for example 0.33000000000000007). The page then showed "Ingot Will Alloy" on its own while the Ingot Stats showed the pure metal's numbers. That's a false alarm, and removing the box removes it too.

**What this changes**

It removes the "Ingot Will Alloy" box and the few lines of script that showed or hid it. The 67% warning is unchanged, text included. Nothing else on the page is touched.

**How to check it yourself**

On the Forging Calculator:

- 5 Tin + 5 Zinc: you should now see one warning (before this change you saw two).
- 20 Tin + 10 Zinc (2:1, about 66.7%): one warning.
- 60 Tin + 20 Zinc + 20 Silver: one warning.
- 67 Tin + 33 Zinc, or 46.9 Tin + 23.1 Zinc (exactly 67/33): no warning.
- 10 Tin on its own: no warning.

To see the false alarm on the current live page (before this change): enter Tin 2.9, Zinc 2.2, Tin 3.8, Zinc 1.1 in the first four rows (that's exactly 6.7 Tin to 3.3 Zinc). You'll see "Ingot Will Alloy" by itself, while Hardness shows 25.00, which is pure Tin. With this change, no warning shows for that mix.

This PR makes the same edit in `Page Raw Code.txt`, so your plain-text copy stays in step with index.html. It doesn't depend on any of my other PRs, and they don't depend on it: merge any of them, in any order, or none.

author: ccprince
body:
## Summary

Slice 4 of five, and the one #11 is about. The **draw**'s first two stages are real: the galaxy the
player flies is the one the motifs assembled. The authored chart and the authored start location
come out of the content set with it.

```text
draw(content, rng)
  drawMotifs      motifsPerCampaign of them, with replacement   (d5, d7)
  fillSlots       typed slots first, then untyped               (ADR 0006 d4)
                    a location leaves the reserve once drawn    (d6)
  joinMotifs      motif k -- motif k-1, one lane each           (d6)
  hubOf           the busiest place drawn, ties by id           (ADR 0006 d16)
```

Three choices worth reading:

- **Typed slots are filled first.** An untyped slot takes whatever is left and a typed one does
  not, so filling the fussy ones first stops an untyped slot taking the last `market` and starving
  a slot that needed it.
- **Motifs join as a chain**, each to the one before it. The lane count follows from the dial
  rather than being a second one, and the assembly comes out in one piece.
- **The campaign opens at the busiest place drawn.** A start on a spur makes the first decision
  "fly out, or fly out" (ADR 0006 d16); lane degree is the reading of that the assembly can make
  alone. The *guarantee* — a market, three neighbours in range, one of them a spur — is #12's.

A slot the reserve cannot fill throws, naming the slot and its motif. The bounded re-roll and the
loud load failure that should replace it are #12 (ADR 0008 d17), and the authored content never
reaches it.

## Evidence

`npm run check` green, 117 tests. What the real content set now draws, by seed:

```text
seed 20261022  opens at Bellwether Yards   4 places, 3 lanes
seed 1         opens at Thennet Shoals     4 places, 3 lanes
seed 2         opens at Caravel Station    5 places, 4 lanes
seed 7         opens at Grieve's Hollow    5 places, 4 lanes
```

Four or five places out of a reserve of six, a different start and a different shape each time,
every lane inside baseline range, every galaxy connected. Two motifs from three, so one or two
locations are **hidden** per campaign.

- Size: 243 production insertions across 5 files, against 400/15 (ADR 0010).
- Reviewed on the branch before this PR, both axes. The findings are the second commit, and the
  standards axis found a **hard breach of ADR 0009 decision 3** — four places where an outcome the
  player sees was decided by `Map` insertion order or the order content was written in, including
  which end an inter-motif lane lands on. All four now sort over authored ids.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way for content. A content set must declare motifs; `lanes` and `start.locationId`
are no longer read at all. The one content set in the repo is updated here, and the loader catches
a set that has not been.

**Blast Radius:** where the player starts, and therefore most fixtures.

The campaign no longer opens where a fixture said — it opens at the hub. Three fixtures grew a
fourth place and a second lane out of Kestrel to make Kestrel that hub, which is the honest
version of the change rather than asserting a start the engine no longer takes orders about. The
page's end-to-end departure test stopped naming Thennet Shoals: it takes the first departure the
chart offers and flies the leg day by day, because which places a campaign is dealt is not the
page's business.

Two things are left for #12 and written into the commit rather than silently: the unfillable-slot
throw escapes `startCampaign` instead of failing the load with a **problem**, and a chain makes
every inter-motif lane a cut edge, so no ring can run *between* motifs.

The mod side works: each eye's vectors are drawn and published (about 900 every 10 s), and the game's own vectors are found. The bridge refuses them because of how ReShade wraps D3D12:
- **Run 1:** every V1 copy failed ("snapshot failures" = publications).
- **Run 2:** the device log showed why. The vectors report device `…5C060`, while the list, the queue and ReShade's device all report `…637C0`. ReShade wraps the device and the queue but not resources, so resources report the device beneath the wrapper. V1 requires all three to report one device. The fallback to the bridge's FidelityFX flow worked.
- **V2:** the bridge's V2 input (`OFXR_PublishDlssGuidesV2`, no registration) takes a device the producer has checked. That gets past the copy, but the bridge's synthesizer then requires the vectors' device to be the session's (`same_device`).
- **Run 3:** starting the headset session on the native device, with ReShade's queue, crashed the game in `xrCreateSession`. dbf0e36 removes that binding.

Now, under ReShade, choosing Game motion logs why it can't work, shows "the bridge refused game motion" on the Perf line, and runs FidelityFX flow. Ways forward:
1. Ask the bridge's author to compare adapters (LUID) instead of COM identity for the vectors; their synthesizer already has a `same_adapter` check. A small upstream change.
2. Give the session a queue of its own on the native device, synchronized with the game's queue by fences. This is a large transport change.


## What it adds

**VR Settings > Perf > Frame generation** gets a fourth choice: **Game motion**. The bridge no longer uses optical flow. The mod tells it, through its DLSS-style vector input (`OFXR_PublishDlssMotionVectorsV1`), where each pixel of an eye's image was in the same eye's image a frame back. The bridge then makes the in-between frame from those vectors.

Where the vectors come from (`steamvr/frame_motion.h`):
- **The world:** each pixel is put back in the world from the scene's depth (infinite reverse-Z), then seen from where the same eye stood a frame back (`TurnMove`). This is exact for everything standing still, through head turns, walking and the body's turn. Those are the cases optical flow gets wrong, especially in the dark and where near and far things mix.
- **What the hero carries** (within about a metre: hands, weapon, body) goes along with the hero's step and turn (`TurnCarry`), as By turns already moves it.
- **What moves by itself** (monsters, missiles) comes from the game's own motion vectors (`motion_vectors.cpp`, brought over from the shelved #281 work).
  - The camera's part against the render before (the other eye's) is taken out, and what is left counts twice: the same eye's frame back is two renders.
  - It is gated where #281's trial found the game's vectors hold:
    - only from 2 m out;
    - only where a surface's texels agree;
    - only above 1.5 px;
    - only while the head turned less than 0.25° and the hero moved less than 0.5 cm between renders.
  - Otherwise moving monsters blend.
  - `[render] frame_generation_monsters` (default 1, live) turns this part off.

How it reaches the bridge:
- Each eye's vectors (R16G16_FLOAT, half the depth's size, uv units) are drawn as its image is copied.
- They are published just before that eye's image is released. For a swapchain with one image layer, the bridge takes the newest publication at release, so each eye's vectors must go right before its own release.
- The bridge copies them through a command list of the mod's, executed before the frame ends.
- Without a depth or a previous frame, the vectors are zero, so the bridge turns the image by the poses alone. Stale vectors are never reused.
- Game motion needs **Both eyes**. With By turns, the mod asks the bridge for FidelityFX's optical flow instead, switching live. The Perf line says so, in amber.
- The vector input doesn't check who's calling, and the bridge's API notes describe callers as producers "such as OptiScaler". Depth guides (V2) need OptiScaler's registration and aren't used.

Also:
- The log reports every 10 s: eyes drawn, eyes using the game's vectors, eyes with no vectors, publications; and the bridge's own published, matched, used and status counts.
- The menu swapchain's failure (the Escape menu fallback seen once with the bridge) now logs its size and result code.

## Verified
- `steamvr/build_windows.ps1 -Test`: build OK, 141/141. New:
  - `frame-motion-test` checks the vectors against hand-worked cases: nothing moved; a 10° head turn; walking half a metre (parallax); carried things during a step and a body turn; a walking monster's own motion and every gate. It also compiles the shaders with d3dcompiler_47.
  - `frame-generation-test`: the Game motion control and status lines.
  - `vr-settings-test`: the fourth choice, stepping, help.
- Help cards and Perf lines fit (the art and line tests).

## Not verified yet: no headset testing
- That the bridge accepts and uses the vectors (the 10 s log line: matched and used, status "used").
- The look: head turns, walking, thin weapons, moving monsters with and without `frame_generation_monsters`.
- GPU cost of the pass (expected small: one full-screen pass at half resolution per eye).
- Switching Both eyes ↔ By turns while playing.

Testing uses offline local characters only.

author: ragdoll-git
body:
**Problem**
With a desktop-icons extension that keeps its window at the bottom (Zorin Desktop Icons / DING), clicking the wallpaper hides the icons, and clicking again brings them back.

**Cause**
Both DING's window and the `mpv` wallpaper window call `lower()` on themselves when raised. A click on the desktop raises DING, which lowers itself, but it ends up *below* `mpv`, so the video covers the icons. The next click reaches `mpv`, which gets lowered and ends up under DING again. `set_input_region` is wrapped in a try/catch, so it doesn't stop the click from reaching `mpv` on Wayland.

**Fix proposed**
Connect to `global.display`'s `restacked` signal and lower the wallpaper window again, so it always stays at the very bottom. The signal is disconnected in `stop()`.

**Testing**
Zorin OS (GNOME 46, Wayland), `zorin-desktop-icons` enabled. After the patch, repeated clicks on the desktop keep the icons visible. No CPU spike from `lower()` re-triggering `restacked`.

Only `modules/wallpaper.js` changes. I haven't touched or tested `wallpaper50.js` (GNOME 50+).

## Change

Adds a historical-replay simulator for the 2018 Camp Fire and a web view for it.

- **Simulator (`sim/`, stdlib Python)**
  - Satellite perimeter replay, plus a calibrated simulated morning fire front.
  - Mesoscopic link-queue traffic on the 2018 OSM road network: spillback, rerouting, contraflow, closures from fire and events.
  - 44 NIST CodeRED alerts and 12 snapped NIST road events drive the timeline.
  - Responder and evacuee insights.
  - What-if variants and a departure-schedule optimizer.
- **Agent simulation, kept separate from the replay:** `python3 -m sim ... simulate` runs resident agents plus rule-based CHP, fire-closure and evacuation-officer agents, compares their actions with 2018, and runs a Claude-driven stress-test agent (offline `--dry-run`).
- **Web app**
  - `/replay` (historical) and `/simulate` (agents).
  - MapLibre top-down, 3D oblique and ground POV views.
  - Guided tour, calm default panel, what-if compare, responder/evacuee tabs.
  - AI "Ask / Explain" backed by `POST /api/replay/explain`.
- **Data**
  - Package artifacts (`raw/`, `normalized/`) are no longer tracked in Git and move to MongoDB Atlas GridFS (ADR 0006). Manifests, sources, quality and curated tables stay.
  - `sim` fetches missing artifacts on demand and verifies them by hash.
  - Earlier commits on this branch still contain the data in history; nothing was rewritten.
- Merges `origin/main` (MapLibre maps page); our ADR was renumbered to 0005 to avoid a collision.

## Integration

- **Contracts:** `docs/replay-bundle.md` (bundle and variants) and `docs/plan-api.md` (draft, not implemented yet).
- **Generated bundles** are gitignored. Build them with:
  - `python3 -m sim --package data/incidents/camp-2018-paradise-slice/a6d2cc03f525ed65 bundle --roads-package data/incidents/camp-2018-evacuation/b1b318c16bbd3270 --output app/public/replays/camp-2018.json`

- **Simulation assumptions:**
  - Demand zones, vehicle counts and per-zone order times are still **fixture** data, labelled in the UI.
  - Lanes and speeds are mostly class defaults.
  - The morning fire is a model fitted to the first satellite perimeter.

  All of these are stated in bundle `assumptions` and `limitations`.

author: sarperim
body:
## Ticket
**TKT-foundation-078** — the disclosures lane never completes: the per-company walk started at `EarlyDisclosureIndex = "0"` and re-read ~140k index positions per company, so it is structurally guaranteed to time out (P0, user directive 2026-10-24).

## Why (evidence from the ticket, verified live 2026-10-24 02:30–02:50 UTC)
- Gateway reachable and credentialed: `/members` 1,037 companies (ASELS = `866`), `/lastDisclosureIndex` = `1231017`, `?companyId=866&disclosureIndex=0` → 39 real rows, paging confirmed.
- ASELS spans **1092199 → 1231017 = 138,818 positions ≈ 39 pages** ≈ 8 min/company at the ≥12 s pace ⇒ ≈4 h per XU030 pass.
- Ledger **run 208** = `10:41:24 → 13:41:24` (exactly 3 h), `written=0`, killed by the watchdog; `kap_disclosures` empty.
- `ER005` is the gateway's end-of-list answer (index at/above a company's latest disclosure), **not** the cause.

## What changed
1. **Bootstrap from the platform head, never zero.** A cursor-less company starts at `lastDisclosureIndex − Ingestion:Disclosures:BootstrapLookback` (shipped **5,000**, configurable, arithmetic documented in the option). The seed is recorded as **provenance** (`bootstrapped N cursor(s) … BOOTSTRAPPED` log + per-symbol stat `written 0 / failed false / BOOTSTRAPPED`) — never as "no disclosures". A **persisted cursor wins** (one incremental page, no re-walk, no reset); a stale cursor's single ER005 reset retargets the **bounded window**, not `0`. Missing anchor while a bootstrap is needed → loud `SourceFetchException` (refuse to walk from zero).
2. **Market-wide feed is the normal pass.** `Ingestion:Disclosures:Feed = market` (shipped) pages `GET /disclosures?disclosureIndex={n}` with **no** `companyId` from one market cursor; only bound-universe rows are fetched/written, out-of-bound rows are **counted + logged** (`OUTSIDE_BOUND_UNIVERSE`) and never detail-fetched (their index still advances the cursor, so they cannot be re-read forever). `company` keeps the bounded per-constituent walk for first-seed/backfill. Market cursor = one `coverage_metadata` row (`scope = market`, `kap-disclosures-market-cursor`, outside `InstrumentScoped`, no migration); an honest-empty pass persists **no** cursor (no backwards reset).
3. **The run finishes.** `MaxListPages = 24` and `MaxDetailFetches = 200` bound one pass: **24 × 12 s = 288 s + 200 × 12 s = 2,400 s ≈ 44.8 min**, inside the scheduler's 90-minute `MaxRunDuration` attempt bound with ~2× headroom. A budget-truncated pass records `truncated`, persists the last index it **completed** and resumes exactly there.

**Honesty rules unchanged (load-bearing):** no fabricated disclosure/subject/body; unmapped identity = named, counted skip; unfetchable detail = quarantine with the gateway body verbatim; genuine gateway-down = `failed`; honest empty = a skip with a reason.

## Acceptance TCs
- **TC-MDF-099** (`TC_MDF_099_a/b`) — a huge-range company (2,000 dense rows far below the head, ≈41 pages from zero — the run-208 shape) completes inside the page budget, pages only the head window, writes its two in-window disclosures, persists the last read index and records the bootstrap as provenance; the window is configuration (200-position window → start `1230817`); shipped defaults pinned (5,000 / 1,000 / 24 / 200).
- **TC-MDF-100** (`TC_MDF_100_a/b`) — a persisted cursor is one incremental page, no reset, no re-bootstrap (`0` written / `0` unchanged on the second run — the 046 disclosures semantics); a stale cursor past the tail resets **once** to the bounded window (`["1231018", "1226017"]`), recorded and persisted, next run one page.
- **TC-MDF-101** (`TC_MDF_101_a/b/c/d`) — the market feed pages with no `companyId` (`["1230017","1230066"]`), writes only bound rows, counts the out-of-bound ones without a detail fetch, advances/resumes its own `market` cursor in one page; ER005 is an honest empty that persists no cursor; a market list 500 is still `failed`; `MaxListPages = 1` truncates, persists the completed index `1230066` and resumes exactly there.
- Regression: `StatementsAndEventsIngestionTests` (incl. the 034/046/061/063 isolation family), `VykCompanyDirectoryTests`, `VykStatementsSourceTests`, `EodChainTests`, `MorningChainTests`, `SchedulerTests`, `EodStallWatchdogTests`, `MarketSnapshotTests`, `MetricsRecomputeIdempotencyTests`, `EodStaleServingTests`.

## Test evidence
- **Red** (pre-078 from-zero start restored in `ResolveEarlyIndex`): **3 failed / 5 passed** — `TC_MDF_099_a` `Expected: 2, Actual: 0` (the from-zero walk exhausts its 24-page budget inside the dense archive and never reaches the recent window), `TC_MDF_099_b` (window ignored) and `TC_MDF_100_b` (reset target `0`). The 5 passing are the cases whose subject (persisted-cursor incrementality, market feed, ER005, source-down) is untouched by the defect — expected.
- **Green** (fix restored): **8/8** (`dotnet test --filter "TC_MDF_099|TC_MDF_100|TC_MDF_101"`).
- Neighbouring suites: **122/122** green after the rebase onto `dev` (`StatementsAndEventsIngestionTests` 55/55 + the nine listed classes, incl. 064's newly landed scheduler cases).
- CI: **Backend pass (2m23s), Web pass (1m12s), E2E pass (4m24s)**.
- `dotnet build Degerli.sln`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Tests are L2 doubles only (WireMock `/members`, `/lastDisclosureIndex`, `/disclosures`, `/disclosureDetail`); **no live gateway call**.

## Docs
- `01` §10.9.15 extended (new v1.5.52 subsection: bootstrap, market feed, budget arithmetic, honesty pin; §10.9.11 cursor note + §10.4 config list updated), **§13.1 row v1.5.52** (allocated above the landed max v1.5.42 and the 064/065 + 056-wave reservations v1.5.43–51).
- `.pipeline/testing/market-data-foundation.md` **§17** (TC-MDF-099/100/101) + change record **v1.18** (renumbered from v1.17 on rebase: TKT-foundation-064 merged first and took v1.17).

## Flagged items
- Rebase note: the branch was rebased onto `dev` after 064 merged; the one conflict (test-plan change-record numbering) was resolved inside this ticket's scope.
- `01` §13.1's table already carries v1.5.25/v1.5.26 rows **after** v1.5.42 (out of order, from earlier merges); the new v1.5.52 row was inserted above the landed max as the allocation rule says — the stray rows were not reordered (out of scope).
- The live criterion (a paced dev-stack run with `kap_disclosures` > 0, newest stored index within ~50 of `lastDisclosureIndex`, a completed pass and an incremental second run) is the orchestrator's post-merge step; it is **not** asserted here.
- `VykCompanyDirectory.cs` was in the ticket's scope but needed no change (it already fetches `lastDisclosureIndex`).

Stacked on #45 (both edit `components-image/build.gradle.kts`). GitHub retargets this to `main` when #45 merges.

## What

- `components-image` adds the `wasmJs` target (browser), configured like `:components`. `ktor-client-js` 3.6.0 is Coil's network engine there; it is the latest release and matches the other Ktor engines. The Wasm `yarn.lock` gains its one npm dependency, `ws` 8.20.1.
- Coil has no disk cache on JS/Wasm (`singletonDiskCache()` returns `null` in `coil-core/src/jsCommonMain`). `CachedAsyncImage`'s KDoc and the README now say `diskCachePolicy` has no effect on the web, where the browser's HTTP cache applies.
- The ABI dump only gains `wasmJs` in the klib target list. No public API changes.
- README, `llms.txt`, the consumer skill, `docs/using-with-agents.md`, the catalog generator, and `AGENTS.md` no longer say the image artifact skips Wasm.

## Tests on every Skiko target

A new `skikoTest` source set (a default-hierarchy-template group of JVM, iOS arm64/simulator, and Wasm) holds Compose UI tests that need a Skiko renderer. Android host tests have no Skiko renderer and still run only `commonTest`.

`CachedAsyncImageRenderTest` decodes and draws an embedded 4×4 red PNG and checks the fallback painter. It ran on all three targets:

| Target | Tests | Failures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jvmTest` | 2 (+4 network tests in `jvmTest`) | 0 |
| `iosSimulatorArm64Test` | 2 | 0 |
| `wasmJsBrowserTest` (ChromeHeadless) | 2 | 0 |

The first Wasm run timed out. `waitUntil` busy-waits, so Coil's decode never got a turn on the browser event loop. The fallback test moved out of `jvmTest`. `jvmTest` keeps the tests that need the JDK HTTP server.

- `:components-image:allTests` (Android host, JVM, iOS simulator, and Wasm browser)

author: iberi22
body:
This PR implements the new-device recovery flow using Shamir's Secret Sharing as per spec section 9. 

- Splits the Master Recovery Secret (MRS) among trustees based on the provided threshold and number of trustees (`shamir-secret-sharing`).
- Wraps each share using the specified cryptographic primitives (`AES-GCM` via `HKDF` from `crypto/index.ts`).
- Enforces policy validation (k >= 2 unless explicitly allowing a 1-of-1 exception). 
- Implements opening and re-wrapping of shares for the temporary keypair during a new-device recovery request. 
- Implements reconstruction of the MRS from k shares.
- Custom `RecoveryError` class handles errors with stable error code strings.
- Added comprehensive test coverage in `recovery.test.ts`.

Note: Since the specification did not explicitly state the AAD string to be used when rewrapping the share for the recovery request, we implemented `rewrapForRequest` with `info="orion/v1/recovery-share"` and `aad=utf8("orion/v1/recovery|" + memberId + "|temp")`.

Closes #1790

author: mahtradr
body:
**What was wrong**

In the Reverse Ingot Calculator, if you picked the same metal in two rows (say Iron 30% in one row and Iron 20% in another), the breakdown listed Iron twice: "Iron (30.00%)" and "Iron (20.00%)". The totals at the top were already right. Only the list repeated the metal. The Forging Calculator already adds repeated metals together when it works out its totals.

**What this changes**

When a metal shows up in more than one row, its percentage and volume now get added to that metal's first line instead of starting a new one. Each metal appears once, in row order: a metal's line sits where its first (top-most) row is. The total percentage, weight, density, remaining volume and status message work the same as before. The change is a few lines inside the loop in `calculate()` that builds the breakdown list.

**How to check it yourself**

Open the page and scroll to the Reverse Ingot Calculator. Set Total Ingot Volume to 100, then try:

1. Iron 30 in row 1 and Iron 20 in row 2. The breakdown should show one line, "Iron (50.00%)" with 50.00 volume. Before this change it showed two Iron lines.
2. Iron 30, Tin 20, Iron 10 in rows 1 to 3. You should see "Iron (40.00%)" 40.00 volume, then "Tin (20.00%)" 20.00 volume, in that order.
3. Iron 20 in all five rows. You should see one line, "Iron (100.00%)" with 100.00 volume, and the "ready to craft" message.

In each case the numbers at the top (total percentage, weight, density) should match what the live site shows for the same inputs, because only the list changed. If you'd rather check from the browser console after entering case 2, this prints the breakdown lines:

```
[...document.querySelectorAll('#breakdown li')].map(li => li.textContent)
```

This PR makes the same edit in `Page Raw Code.txt`, so your plain-text copy stays in step with index.html. It doesn't depend on any of my other PRs, and they don't depend on it: merge any of them, in any order, or none.

body:
## What this does

Step 7 is the last of M2.4. With it, every [auto] gate of the milestone passes.

**The dealer bot** (`packages/sim/src/dealer.ts`)
- It buys whenever it runs low and stands the corner through the night.
- It joins the crew, takes fronts, pays them back, and recruits the coworker.
- When caught, it posts bail if it can and pleads. In prison it works the job, writes letters, and lets the days pass.
- Like the thief bot, it sees only options, facts and previews.

**Sweeps** (`deal/week.test.ts`)
- The dealer, a police recruit (under the steady bot) and the line cook each play 500 seeded weeks with nothing refused.
- The dealer's weeks reach buying, selling, sales seen, raids, arraignment and the crew.
- In 20 weeks, all 10 recruits finish the academy and make arrests on patrol.

**B6: crime pays less than work** (`packages/sim/test/pays-bench.ts`, in Readings)
- After 8 weeks, net worth counts cash minus what is owed to the court, the landlord and the supplier.
- Dealers' median is −$2,203 and their best is −$244. Line cooks' median is $3,016, and their worst is about $2,900.
- The test asserts that every dealer ends below every cook.
- With the police switched off, dealers' median is $6,034, twice the cooks'. So arrests and time are what make crime lose. This is in line with Reuter et al.: street selling pays more by the hour, at a large risk.

**A caught mistake**
- The first dealer bot bought only when it held nothing. It earned less than a cook even with no police, so B6 passed for the wrong reason.
- A planted bug (no raids at all) was what showed it. The bot was fixed before the reading was taken.

## Checks

- `pnpm check` is green: 524 unit tests, 37 e2e.
- 3 bugs planted, 3 caught after the fix: no raids, a ladder never climbed, a pay-back offered when it would be refused.

## Not yet

- The [you] gate: a dealer's week and a recruit's week played on Evan's phone.
- Raids come about four times a life in 8 weeks (open question 76); the phone week will say if that's too often.

author: egvictorino
body:
## Qué
Hallazgo del informe de #43. En las variantes `bare` (solo subrayado) de `BipInput`, `BipSelect`, `BipTextarea`, `BipNumberInput` y `BipMultiSelect` (búsqueda en el trigger), el foco de teclado solo cambiaba el subrayado de primary a primary-hover: lo mismo que el hover, 1.37:1 en light y 1.30:1 en dark (WCAG 1.4.11). Con error no cambiaba nada (`box-shadow: none`; WCAG 2.4.7). `BipSearchInput` bare ya usaba el anillo completo, así que la librería era inconsistente.

Ahora todas usan `box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)`, y con error `--focus-ring-color: var(--color-danger)` (patrón de `search-input--bare`). El subrayado danger del error y el hover se conservan. En multi-select se quita el `box-shadow: none` que anulaba el anillo de `--inline:focus-within`, y **multi-select con error pinta en danger el anillo de todas sus variantes** (outlined y filled incluidas), como ya hacían input, select y textarea.

Diverge de la referencia React, que tiene el mismo problema en `bare`.

## Medido en Chromium (Docker), light / dark / RTL
- Antes: `box-shadow: none` al enfocar en todas las variantes bare, con y sin error.
- Después: hueco `--color-surface-1` + banda primary (`#2939cc` / `#5468e8`) o danger con error (`#cc242a` / `#ff5a5f`); contraste contra el hueco 8.23:1 / 4.03:1 (primary) y 5.45:1 / 6.14:1 (danger). Sin recorte en las stories.

## Guard
`testing/bare-focus-ring.spec.ts` (parser de #43): ninguna regla de foco de esos seis CSS anula o sustituye el anillo (allowlist: el listbox de multi-select, cuyo foco real va a cada opción), cada variante bare enfoca con `var(--focus-ring)`, bare inline hereda el anillo y todos los errores fijan `--focus-ring-color` danger. Falla con el CSS anterior (16 de 19).

## Verificación
- `pnpm lint`, `typecheck`, `test` (1355), `build`, `lint:package`, `size`, `format:check` en verde.
- `pnpm test:visual:docker` completo con `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0`: 259 pasan, ninguna baseline cambia (ninguna captura el foco).

## Fuera de alcance (reportado por la revisión, ya existía)
En input y textarea, `--bare:hover:not(:disabled)` y `--outlined:hover:not(:disabled)` tienen más especificidad que la regla de error, así que el hover cambia el borde danger a primary-hover (también en React). Con este PR, un campo bare con error, enfocado y con hover muestra anillo danger y subrayado azul. Va en un fix aparte.

author: allduf
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"allduf"} -->
_Requested by **alex** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FAanoZcGbKDfgG1Tn3uVQG?thread=cmsg_01FAanoZcGbKDfgG1Tn3uVQG6r7a5pL6TGmxp3kEewk7HN)_

## Why
With #317 and #318 live, the AI answered for all 6 test pictures ([issue #315](https://github.com/allduf/trail-finder/issues/315)). The right trail came first for 2 of them (Hanging Gardens, Pretty Slabs). The run also showed three problems:

- **The online check never ran.** Google Search has its own free allowance, and this key has none left (newer models may have none on the free tier). Since #317, a search 429 marked every model as used up, so the photo comparison right after it had no model left and was skipped. A live probe confirmed it: 4 photos were found, no ranks came back, and the call took 2 s.
- **The AI named the right trail, but the app ignored it.** For the In and Out Burger picture, the AI guessed "In-N-Out Burger". Guesses could only lift a trail that was already listed, they had to match exactly, and the trail was 6.7 km from where the AI put the camera, outside the 6 km it searched.
- **False matches from place names.** "British Columbia" matched Columbia Trail in Golden. "Mount Garibaldi" matched the Mount 7 riding area (one typo). The AI's "Sea to Sky" (the region) put the Sea to Sky Trail on top three times. "Callaghan Valley" matched the Valley Trail.

## What changes
- **Function (`which-trail`):**
  - A 429 on a Google Search call now marks only that model's search as used up, so plain answers keep working.
  - Without search, the comparison is told to use what it knows about the trails.
  - Each step's model notes come back as `detail`, including Google's quota name and limit, so the test shows why a step had no answer.
  - The AI also says where each landmark it sees sits across the picture (`views`, 0 = left edge to 1 = right edge). This prepares a next step: working out where the camera stood from which landmarks it sees, and in what order.
  - The AI's viewpoint gets `alt`: about how high the camera is, in metres.
- **App (`photo-find.js`):**
  - The AI's guesses are matched loosely, so "In-N-Out Burger" matches "In and Out Burger".
  - A guessed trail within 25 km of where the AI places the photo joins the list as Possible.
  - Up to 2 guesses always reach the online check.
  - The app searches 8 km around the AI's spot (was 6 km). It takes the 60 best trails there (was the 60 nearest): trails that reach the camera's height go up, ones 700 m or more off go down.
  - "British Columbia", "Canada" and "Alberta" are dropped from the AI's places.
  - A number in a name must match exactly.
  - Landscape words like valley, canyon, meadow, pass and alpine don't count as a one-word trail name.
  - A trail whose name only matches a place or landmark the AI named is dropped. It can still join as a trail near the spot or the landmark.
- **Accuracy test:** the report now shows which model answered, the AI's terrain words and camera height, where each landmark sits across the picture, the online check's fit for the right trail and its best pick, and the check's notes when it had no answer.

Scripts ?v=323, sw tf-130.

## After merging (alex)
Supabase → Edge Functions → smooth-worker: paste the new `supabase/functions/which-trail/index.ts` and Deploy. Until then, the online check stays skipped and the AI won't report landmark positions or camera height.

## Checked
- The function type-checks with `tsc --strict`.
- Replayed in a test browser with the AI's real answers from the last runs (no words read, online check stubbed):
  - In and Out Burger was not listed; now 7th and sent to the online check. When the check rates it 0.9, it moves to 2nd.

author: psaab
body:
## Summary
For an ambiguous fabric arrival (#15916 — claimed zone withheld pending the owner-RG gate), pre-routing NAT resolved its scope from the LOCAL fabric/logical identity (fabric interface zone / config name / routing-instance) and could select a translation under that identity. The session-miss policy later promoted the claimed zone, so the translated action was keyed to a zone the policy never adjudicated (RN-01).

Fix direction per the validated refutation in #16045: suppress the fabric fallback identity only; never grant the claimed zone before owner proof.

- `PreroutingIngressScope` gains `ambiguous_provenance`; `prerouting_ingress_scope_ambiguous` resolves the same local identity stamped ambiguous (claimed zone and V2 peer scope ifindex never substituted). Flow-backed miss and flowless pre-routing paths both stamp it.
- NAT-layer ambiguous-provenance siblings (ordinary matchers untouched): pool DNAT -> Poisoned fail-closed (needs the winner's scope tier, so `DnatOutcome::Translate` now carries it), static DNAT withholds, NPTv6 -> Untranslatable, NAT64 -> MatchUnavailable; the persistent-NAT reader is skipped (ingress-keyed lease scope).
- UNSCOPED rules still fire (identity-independent), native owner-scope ingress unchanged, session-hit revalidation untouched.

## Decisive regression (co-moved owner fixture)
`*_16045` in `poll_descriptor/prerouting_scope_tests.rs`: fabric-scoped DNAT cannot fire prematurely; native `fabric`-zone ingress still translates; claimed-zone DNAT stays withheld; unscoped DNAT still translates; interface-scoped static, NAT64 and NPTv6 legs.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16045`: 7/7. RED-on-revert verified for the NAT64/NPTv6 legs (fail on clean master code). Note: in the poll harness the DNAT/static legs are broker-gated (session installs via the fabric-link binding end in MissingNeighbor), so the DNAT invariant is additionally pinned at the NAT-table tri-state; see `docs/log/16045.md`.
- `nat::` suite: 751 pass. Fabric zone-stamp suite: 66 pass.
- Three `prerouting` VLAN failures reproduce identically on clean master (pre-existing, unrelated).

## Risk
Fail-closed only: ambiguous arrivals with scope-constrained pre-routing NAT now drop/withhold instead of translating under the fallback identity. Unscoped and validated flows are byte-identical.

Closes #16045
