- [ ] A changeset is added for a change to a pack's shipped code (`pnpm changeset`). Not needed: no shipped code changes.
- [x] The title follows Conventional Commits, with `!` before the colon for a change that breaks users (`feat!:` or `feat(api)!:`).

author: olemarkus
body:
With meter areas, a device the owner moved into a zone created after PELS last read the zone tree resolved to the Main home, because a zone missing from the tree walks the same fail-safe as a broken chain. Main then planned and actuated it against its own meter until the next tree fetch, and Homey sends no zone event to shorten that.

Per the owner's ruling, such a device is now no home's to plan: the membership service records zone-rule devices whose zone the committed tree lacks (`isDeviceZoneUnknown`, logged once as `home_membership_zone_unknown`), and the planning filter drops them from every home while meter areas run. Its membership still reads Main for listings and diagnostics. A device pinned to a home that exists keeps it; a pin to a deleted home resolves by zone, so it is held out like any other. The plan-invalidation fingerprint counts held-out devices, so holding one out of Main and releasing it both re-plan Main. To make the hold short, the realtime zone move that put the device there now refetches the tree at once (`refreshZoneTreeIfUnknown`, at most one fetch per ten seconds), so the device joins its area as soon as that fetch lands. Single-home installs are unaffected.

The zone-tree TODO entry keeps the interval it asked for, with the two readers that still need a fresh tree first.

author: genffy
body:
Fixes #105.

## What and why

A single clip on X intermittently wrote **two entries with different ids**, identical content and the same status permalink (issue #105: 3 clips → 5 entries, two sources doubled).

Reworked after the first attempt failed CI: the original worker-level window ("same source + content within 5s returns the saved entry") broke `selection-clip.spec.ts:154` — the metrics test **deliberately** saves the same content twice back to back to fill duration buckets, and content at the worker layer cannot tell that apart from a replay. That approach is fully reverted; the guard now lives where the distinction exists: **the gesture**.

The capsule binds one click to one save and removes itself on the first fire, so a second save requires the click delivered twice — on X, a page that repaints the timeline under the dwell re-arms the capsule while the gesture is still in flight, and each delivery mints a fresh entry id, slipping past the message-retry cache (requestId-scoped) and the store's id-idempotency alike.

So the same block firing the capsule's clip **within 1.5s of the previous fire is dropped** (`offerClip` in `block-hover.ts`); a deliberate clip of the same block re-hovers it, which already takes longer than the window. The keyboard block mode's Enter goes through the same gate. Deliberate quick re-saves anywhere else — worker, library, metrics tests — are untouched: nothing at the worker layer inspects content any more.

## How it was verified

- [x] `npm run verify` — format, lint, types, **55 files / 827 tests** green, including the new unit test (first click fires, a replayed click on the same button is dropped, a click after the window fires again).
- [x] `npm run build` + e2e `block-clip`, `selection-clip` (including the duration-bucket test this fix's first version broke), `cold-start` — **19/19 green**.
- [x] Shared contracts unchanged; docs updated with the code: `capture.md` §6.2 悬停入口 (一次手势只剪一次).
- [x] Environment/dependency/deploy: not applicable.

Stack note: this branch sits on #119 (merged-clean after #118 landed); #121 sits on this one — merge in order and each PR collapses to its own commit.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, page content or attachment bytes in logs, fixtures or screenshots
- [x] No test was skipped, disabled or loosened to get green
- [x] Docs describe what the code in this PR does; delivery status is only in `docs/product/roadmap.md`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches user-facing save paths (clip dedup window) and non-trivial DOM cloning for screenshots, including an extra visible-tab capture for protected video; mitigated by targeted unit and E2E tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes duplicate **block clips** when the page redelivers the same click (issue #105) and fixes **element screenshots** that lost live video frames and carousel scroll state (issues #102, #103).
> 
> **Block hover / keyboard clip:** Capsule and block-mode `Enter` now go through `offerClip` in `block-hover.ts`, which ignores a second clip on the **same block element** within **1.5s** so one gesture cannot create two entries; deliberate re-clips after re-hover still work. Product docs (`capture.md` §6.2) describe “一次手势只剪一次.”

author: doomtickle
body:
Fixes doomtickle/passdesk-ops#138

- **Job index:** dispatch keeps a host-side job index (`FACTORY_STATE/.../jobs.json`). It is written atomically and in order at every status change, and reloaded at start, so `job_status`, `wait_for_job` and `factory packet` keep working for recent jobs (up to 200) after an update or a dropped Coordinator. Each field is validated on reload. Symlinks, FIFOs and oversized files are refused. Only one-line summaries are stored.
- **Interrupted jobs:** a job that was running when the bridge stopped reloads as **interrupted**. The dashboard and `factory watch` show a lane as RUN only while the bridge is alive, so ghost RUN lanes are gone.
- **Update plan:** `factory update --plan` says what each step drops and keeps. Lane sessions are lost only when that role's sandbox is recreated, because they live on the sandbox's disk.
- **Docs:** a "What survives an update or a disconnect" table in `docs/guides/05-troubleshooting.md`. The README, CLAUDE.md and the dashboard guide are updated. The Coordinator stays read-only: a plan worth keeping is committed through a developer job.

Tests: dispatch 126 OK, scripts 389 OK, `test_factory_update.sh` 100 passed (factory-test). Reviewed: APPROVED after one REVISE (save ordering).

body:
## Summary

Keep proxy transport test sockets within the Unix pathname budget regardless of inherited TMPDIR length. The shared fixture owns a short private temporary directory; production behavior and existing assertions are preserved.

## Problem

An unrestricted temporary root makes UnixListener::bind fail with SUN_LEN before proxy behavior is exercised. The recorded failing upstream pathname is 201 bytes on macOS.

## Reproduction

Run the new short/long-root subprocess regression against the previous fixture. Its real proxy diagnostic child fails to bind upstream.sock under the long root and exits 101; the short-root control passes.

## Issues Found

Refs #2852 and #2894.

## Fix Approach

Use the existing tempfile::tempdir_in("/tmp") fixture convention and retain TempDir ownership. Include the socket pathname byte count in fixture bind failures. The new subprocess regression varies TMPDIR without changing global environment in the parent.

## Test-First Evidence

Before the root fix, cargo test --locked -p nils-agent-session --lib proxy_fixture_works_with_short_and_long_temporary_roots -- --nocapture exited 101: UnixListener::bind rejected the 201-byte upstream socket pathname with path must be shorter than SUN_LEN. After the fix, the regression and all existing proxy transport tests pass.

## Test plan

### Test changes

- Retain all existing proxy transport and final-error diagnostic assertions.
- Add one subprocess regression that executes the real proxy diagnostic case under short and over-budget temporary roots, without mutating the parent environment; require the child to run exactly one case.
- Add socket pathname byte length to fixture bind failures.

### Validation

- PASS: all six `codex_app_server::proxy_transport::tests` cases.
- PASS: proxy diagnostic attempts 1–10 under each of the 16-byte and 167-byte temporary roots on macOS (20 PASS, zero retries).
- PASS: workspace formatting, strict file-size ratchet, devlog structure, pre-PR static/docs checks, and package Clippy with all targets/features and warnings denied.
- INCOMPLETE: canonical pre-PR package test phase was stopped after 204 passes when it expanded to 2,325 cases, honoring the requested focused-tests-only scope. It exited 143 during cancellation and is not a local-fast PASS. The earlier system-shell plan attempt failed to parse; using the supported Bash executable resolved planning and static checks.
- PENDING: scheduled Linux ten-attempt short/long-root acceptance, required CI, and steward review. No local full workspace suite or release.

## Risk / Notes

Test fixtures only. The shadow-writer hypothesis did not reproduce; its existing assertions remain unchanged. The sibling socket-fixture sweep is recorded on #2852 as independent follow-up work, avoiding concurrent serve/history files. Linux repeated acceptance, required CI, and steward review must complete before merge. No release.

body:
First implementation layer of the `repositories` OpenSpec change (proposal #1401).

## Concern

The owner-scoped repository catalog: `repositories`, `repository_aliases`,
`checkouts`, and `worktree_leases` tables (FORCE RLS, composite owner foreign
keys, row-only cascades), remote normalization, `packages/git-executor` with
`inspect`, the repositories/aliases/checkouts API with its registration gates,
negative isolation tests, and the operator document.

```text
POST /api/v1/checkouts { path, repositoryId? | remote? }
  derive executor (local tools.nativeExecutorId; machine:// -> 503 until layer 3)
  gate: executor configured -> enter_workspace allowlisted (403 tool_not_allowed)
        -> submitted path decision -> git.inspect -> main-clone decision (403 permission_denied)
  store toplevel as kind main, or the worktree under its main row
```

No issue tracks the change (as `remote-machines`); tasks 2.1–2.8 of
`openspec/changes/repositories/tasks.md` are checked here.

## Stack

```text
master <- proposals/repositories-and-chat-start-location (#1401)
  <- repositories/schema-and-registration (this PR) <- repositories/executor-git
  <- repositories/workspace-worktree <- repositories/finalize <- chat-start-location/...
```

## Size

Authored +4,884 lines against an estimate of 1,600–2,000 (named exception,
reason: the spec requires 46 integration paths at the SQL/HTTP boundary plus
six routes; a self-review simplification pass removed 433 lines and eight
files, and further cuts would drop spec-required coverage). Generated and
reported separately: +5,450 (`openapi.json`, Drizzle snapshot/migration, web
client). Migration safety verified on an empty database and on one staged at
the previous migration with live rows.

## Review record

- SR: two reviewers (correctness, simplification), 14 + 22 findings; all P0/P1
  applied (concurrent-adoption 500 → `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; parent/repository
  mismatch; toplevel storage; PATCH race → 409), one rejected (alias/remote
  cross-table uniqueness, not in spec). Reconciled with the proposal head
  `b97a92e8` (`base_commit` on leases).

## CI note

`API DAST / Schemathesis` and `API DAST / ZAP` fail on `master` as well (every
historical run of `dast.yml`); their findings here are the pre-existing classes
(undocumented status codes on existing routes, NUL bytes in `projects`). This
layer's own routes were made to boot under the DAST stack (the `api-build`
artifact now ships `packages/git-executor/dist`). CodeQL `js/path-injection`
on the guarded `realpath` probe is dismissed with its reason; the guard order is
tested. GitHub did not start the `pull_request` CI run for head `4cb82222`;
`workflow_dispatch` run 40079041619 on the same head shows every job green
except DAST.

- `pnpm --filter api lint`, `typecheck`, `db:check`; second `db:generate` clean
- `vitest --project unit src/repositories` (29), `--project integration src/repositories` (46)
- `pnpm --filter git-executor test` (16), `lint`, `typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter api build` twice (identical `openapi.json`), `pnpm --filter web generate:client` clean
- `pnpm exec knip`, `pnpm lint:markdown`, `pnpm format:check`, `git diff --check`

author: bitxbit-aus
body:
Narrowly scoped fix for the defect the R-007 independent review found. **Separate PR, per the owner's instruction; not merged.**

## The defect
Every middleware redirect branch returned a freshly constructed `NextResponse.redirect(...)` — a **new** response that never receives the `Set-Cookie` headers the Supabase SSR cookie adapter wrote onto the response being built. So on any redirect path the browser was never handed the refreshed session: it kept an expired access token, re-refreshed on every request, and would lose the session outright once the refresh token it still held stopped being accepted.

**Invisible by design** — no error, no log, just occasional sign-outs. That is why it survived.

**Measured before the fix** (deploy preview, expired-access cookie, suspended user):
```
/dashboard -> 307 -> /auth/login?error=account_inactive    Set-Cookie: NONE
```
versus `Set-Cookie` **present** on the 200 branch.

**Pre-existing.** `main` has the identical structure, as does the canonical Supabase middleware example — this is not a Next.js 15 regression. The migration preserved it faithfully.

## The fix
- **`lib/middleware-redirect.ts`** — `redirectWithCookies(target, from)`: builds the redirect and copies every cookie from the response the adapter wrote to.
- **`middleware.ts`** — all four redirect branches route through it; **no bare `NextResponse.redirect` remains**.
- **`lib/middleware-redirect.test.ts`** — 5 tests, registered in `package.json`'s explicit test list (main lists files individually, so an unregistered test would silently never run).

## Mutation-verified — a green suite is not evidence a guard can fail
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove the cookie copy (the fix itself) | **2 tests fail** |
| Keep the copy but drop cookie attributes | **1 test fails** |
| Restored | **172/172 pass** |

## Gate
`tsc` **0 errors** · **172/172** tests (was 167) · production build **exit 0**.

**Sequencing note:** the Next.js 15 migration (PR #49) rewrites `middleware.ts` and currently carries the same defect. If this lands first, **#49 must carry this fix forward** or merging it would revert the fix. I will apply the same change to #49 and say so explicitly.

No production configuration or data touched.

author: zahara-nour
body:
## Pourquoi

Les 9 constructions de la prod ont `author_id` vide (comptes supprimés) : avec les policies « own », personne ne pouvait plus les modifier dans l'appli, et le brouillon « repérage » n'était lu par personne. Mono-professeur : la propriété ne sert à rien, le rôle suffit (décision de David, 2026-10-24).

## Ce qui change

- **Prof seul** : crée, modifie, publie, supprime et lit **toutes** les constructions, brouillons compris.
- **Admin et élève** : lisent les publiées ; écriture → 403 ; brouillon demandé → 404 (ne pas confirmer qu'il existe).
- `/constructions` : sections « Publiées » et « Brouillons » (prof seul), au lieu de « Mes constructions ».
- `author_id` n'est plus lu ni écrit par le code ; colonnes rendues = `CONSTRUCTION_COLUMNS`. La colonne sera supprimée dans une PR séparée, après `deploy:prod`.
- Conversion XML (page + API) : prof seul, puisqu'elle enregistre une construction.
- Scripts de démo : **inchangés** (prof et admin), avec leur propre constante `DEMO_SCRIPT_AUTHOR_ROLES`.

## Migration `20261024120000` (additive : fonction + policies, aucune donnée touchée)

- `is_teacher()` (SECURITY DEFINER, stable, `pg_temp`, EXECUTE retiré à anon), ajoutée à la liste blanche de la garde DEFINER.
- Policies SELECT (brouillons) / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE : `is_teacher()`. Rollback en commentaire.
- Question d'accès tranchée par David : le prof gagne la lecture et l'écriture de tout ; l'admin perd l'écriture (aucune construction écrite par lui en prod) ; rien ne change pour les élèves.

## Preuves

- Tests d'intégration **rouges sans la migration** (7 échecs : création sans auteur, brouillon sans auteur, admin auteur, `is_teacher`…), **verts avec** (46/46, garde SECURITY DEFINER comprise).
- Tests serveur : 44/44 (API, pages, conversion, scripts de démo).
- `check:incremental` 0 erreur · `types:cliquet` tenu · `lint:fast` propre · `docs:check-a-jour` OK.

author: kaelplayground
body:
## 배경

#616(주문안을 휴장 첫날 주말 보강판으로)의 결함 수정이다. 10-24에 데이터베이스 세션이 10-23 주말 보강판을 지었지만, S07 예약 prepare가 그 판을 찾지 못했다. 10-31(토) 09:00 예약 실행 전에 고쳐야 한다.

## 기존 문제점

- **상황**: quant-ledger는 주말 보강판을 아침 확정판과 같은 연구 모델 루트(`data/model/latest_supplement.json`, `data/factor_inputs/`)에 쓴다. 모델 DB(`data/model_db`)에는 장 마감 빌드(`latest_evening.json`)만 있다.
- **인풋**: 휴장 첫날 `weekly_rebalance_cron.sh prepare`가 `signal-status`·`prepare`에 `--model-root "$S07_MODEL_DB"`(= `data/model_db`)와 `--basis supplement`를 넘긴다.
- **에러 위치**: `backend/scripts/weekly_rebalance_cron.sh` prepare 절의 `--model-root "$S07_MODEL_DB"` 두 곳. 신호 어댑터 `scope_signal/_source.py`는 `<루트>/model/latest_<basis>.json`을 읽으므로 모델 DB 아래 `latest_supplement.json`을 찾는다.
- **위험성**: 보강판이 있어도 신호를 읽지 못해(`unreadable`) 주문안을 만들지 못한다. 매주 주문지가 실패 알림으로 끝나고 그 주 리밸런싱이 빠진다. 10-24에는 서버 대기 작업이 같은 이유로 판을 못 찾아, 연구 루트로 손으로 주문안을 만들어 보냈다(14:08).

## 변경 내용

- `weekly_rebalance_cron.sh`의 prepare 절이 `--model-root "$S07_LEDGER_HOME/data"`(연구 모델 루트)를 넘긴다. 머리 설명에서 쓰이지 않게 된 `S07_MODEL_DB`를 빼고 `S07_LEDGER_HOME` 설명에 보강판 위치를 더했다.
- 재현 테스트 `backend/tests/test_weekly_rebalance_cron.py`를 더했다.
  - 임시 폴더에 보강판은 연구 루트에만, 장 마감 빌드는 모델 DB에만 둔다.
  - quant-ledger 달력과 backend python은 대역이다. `signal-status`만 진짜 명령줄로 돌린다.
  - 스크립트 prepare를 실행해 `signal-status`가 rc 0이고 `prepare`가 연구 루트·`--basis supplement`로 불리는지 본다.
- 설명을 바로잡았다: 신호 어댑터 모듈 설명, `--model-root` 도움말, S07 계획 문서(A절 신호, G절), `.claude/rules/strategy-workbench-sot.md` S07 행. 장 마감 빌드는 모델 DB, 보강판은 연구 모델 루트라고 적는다. G절의 빌드 점검 설명도 연구 루트 기준(보강판 앞 판 = 같은 날 아침 확정판)으로 고쳤다.

## 제약사항

- quant-ledger(원장) 코드·배포는 건드리지 않는다(10-24 원장 배포 동결).
- 서버 crontab은 바꾸지 않는다. 스크립트만 바꾼다.
- 신호 어댑터 코드는 그대로다. 두 루트의 배치(`model/`·`factor_inputs/`)가 같아 루트만 맞으면 읽힌다.

## 설계 결정

### 1. 보강판 루트를 어디서 정하나

- **선택**: 스크립트가 `$S07_LEDGER_HOME/data`로 정한다.
- **대안**: 서버 설정의 `S07_MODEL_DB` 값을 연구 루트로 바꾼다. 또는 새 설정 이름을 더한다.
- **선택 이유**: 스크립트는 이미 `S07_LEDGER_HOME`의 quant-ledger 배치(`src`·`.venv`)를 알고 달력을 읽는다. quant-ledger도 연구 루트를 `data`, 장 마감 루트를 `data/model_db`로 고정해 쓴다. `S07_MODEL_DB`를 연구 루트로 바꾸면 이름이 실제와 달라지고, 새 설정은 서버 설정 파일 수정만 늘린다.

## 테스트 계획

- [x] 기존 테스트 통과 (회귀 확인) — S07 관련 63건 통과(`test_weekly_rebalance_cron.py`·`test_weekly_rebalance_cli.py`·`test_adapters_weekly_rebalance.py`·`application/test_weekly_rebalance.py`·`architecture/`)
- [x] 추가 테스트 통과 (새 동작 검증) — 재현 테스트가 수정 전 실패(`signal-status rc=1`, prepare `--model-root …/data/model_db`), 수정 뒤 통과
- [x] 문서 갱신 필요 여부 확인 — S07 계획 문서·SoT 규칙 갱신
- [x] 유저 스토리 하네스 갱신 — 해당 없음(서버 예약 실행 스크립트, 앱 동작 변화 없음)
- [x] lint·type — `ruff check src tests examples scripts tools` 통과. `pyright`는 맥에서만 나는 기존 오류 1건(`tests/run_worker_support.py` `os.waitid`)뿐이고 CI(Linux)와 무관하다.
- [ ] 배포 뒤 서버 확인 — 서버 임시 폴더에서 10-23 보강판 `signal-status` `[ok]`, 10-31 09:00 예약 prepare rc 0

## 관련 컨텍스트

- #616 주문안을 휴장 첫날 주말 보강판으로(10-23 사용자 결정)
- 10-24 데이터베이스 세션이 경로 차이를 짚음. 이번 주 주문지(10-23 보강판, 10종목 유지·주문 0건)는 연구 루트로 손으로 만들어 보냄

author: rhoerr
body:
Fixes #22

`etc/crontab.xml` registered `mageos_update_remote_templates_informations` with `Cron\UpdateRemoteTemplates`, but that class doesn't exist. The job class is `Cron\UpdateRemoteTemplateList`. Magento's cron runner fails to instantiate the class and marks the job `error` every night, so the Dropbox template list was never refreshed by cron.

**Behavior change:** the job now actually runs at midnight. Without Dropbox credentials configured, `getDropboxCredentials()` returns `[]` and the job does nothing. With credentials, it runs the same sync the admin already triggers, and it catches and logs any exception.

author: jverkoey
body:
Eight reads decoded values that cannot be right. Each was checked against this repo's own replies.

Changed (fixture value range before, after):

- `NIRO_INVRT_CV` (`7E4 22 0101`, 2023+): -> `nullmax` 1000, `max` 1000. The 16-bit layout is right where it holds a voltage (0x017E = 382 beside pack 382.8 V on the 2025, 0xE6 = 230 beside 229.7 V on the 2024 hybrid). Hybrid replies also carry 0x07EC28 in bytes 50-52 (22 replies), which read 60,456. Range 0-60,456 becomes 0-399. The 27 zeros are unchanged.
- `NIRO_BAT_UNKNOWN_11_T` and `_12_T` (`7E4 21 05`, bytes 14-15): raw bytes, unit scalar. Byte 14 is 0xF8 in 42 of 48 replies of the 48-byte layout and 0x68 in 33 of 34 of the 34-byte one, while byte 10 reads 15-31 as the module temperature. -96..109 and -103..127 become 3..252 and 0..189.
- `NIRO_MAX` and `NIRO_MIN` (`7E4 21 05`, bytes 25 and 28): raw 16-bit, unit scalar. Replies read `FF 0B`-`FF 1C`, `21 21`, `27 1F`, so tenths of a percent gave up to 6,531.6. 0-6531.6 becomes 0-65316 and 0-819.2 becomes 0-8192.
- `NIRO_BAT_UNKNOWN_03_T` and `_05_T` (`7E4 21 01`, bytes 18 and 20): raw bytes, unit scalar. The module temperatures at bytes 14-17 read 27-28; these read 0x10-0xE2 with no relation to them. -109..120 and -125..125 become 21..240 and 6..226.
- `NIRO_HVBAT_HTR2_T` (`7E4 22 0105`, byte 24): raw byte, unit scalar. Bytes 23-24 of the 2020 and 2022 replies read as one 16-bit value (`01 8A`, `07 B9`, `1E B0`) and are zero from 2023. -127..127 becomes 0..199.

None of the eight feeds a metric. Every read and id is kept; no filter was added. The other changes in `default.json` are column realignment by the formatter.

Left alone: `NIRO_HVBAT_HTR1_T` (the high byte of the same 16-bit value, in range at 0-30) and the 0 readings of `NIRO_INVRT_CV`. No second reading in the captures proves a replacement for any raw read.

Checks: `gobdb check` shows 0 new lint findings, 0 schema errors, 0 fixtures deleted or added, 300 tests passed; `rename_check.py` shows no answered reply lost.

author: wustep
body:
`/playground` and `/playground/dom-ino` now unfurl as looping videos wherever `og:video` plays. Both pages keep their existing `og:image` card, `twitter:image` and `summary_large_image`, so unfurlers that don't play video show the same card as before.

## /playground: `playground.mp4` (10 s, 1.6 MB)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f392d250-a2e0-485f-95da-7bdba17ea896

This is the share card come alive, recorded from the live page and restaged in place at 1200×630. On the left are the sidebar's flask mark and the page's own `h1` and lede. On the right, the real cover grid scrolls up through all 14 cards once. A spotlight wakes one cover at a time, using the same `data-cover-awake` flag the page sets on touch screens: Contraptions, Splash Panic! (the balloon pops), the Lenses Lab bow, DOM-ino, Bookshelf, Spot it!, MIDI Visualizer, then Bomberman (the bomb blooms). It's light mode, to match the card. The last frame runs straight into the first.

| Poster (frame 0) | 0.9 s | 5.6 s |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| ![playground poster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa6d7df6-ccf5-4098-af4b-ded8c1664bce) | ![splash panic pops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21999018-aab3-4344-8506-3afbda9be44a) | ![midi visualizer plays](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a67e7826-3e56-4b67-aa9c-480ee7ec9eee) |

Two covers stay asleep. Starry Night's cover is an animated WebP that plays in real time, so it can't be posed frame by frame. Shadcn's words fall out and leave an empty black card next to MIDI's dark rest frame.

## /playground/dom-ino: `dom-ino.mp4` (7 s, 1.6 MB)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d307646-4bc6-47f5-bc99-52da9ec186e7

Recorded from the app in the DOM-ino repo (`scripts/og-video/` there) and copied in. A cursor grabs the glowing orbs and throws them through the article, and the columns reflow around them. Its poster is a raw app frame, which says less than the titled DOM-ino card, so the card stays `og:image`.

## How the /playground video is made

`scripts/og-video/record-playground.mjs` (README alongside) uses Playwright and ffmpeg:

- **Deterministic.** A virtual clock (`clock.js`) pauses every CSS animation and transition and sets its `currentTime` each frame. An animation advances only while its computed `animation-play-state` is `running`. Two full runs gave byte-identical frames and an identical MP4.
- **Seamless.** The grid is cloned so the strip is three copies long, and the loop scrolls exactly one copy after a warm-up loop. The would-be frame 300 matches frame 0 at 71.5 dB PSNR (sub-pixel raster noise).
- **No dropped tiles.** Chromium sometimes took the screenshot before a newly exposed tile was rastered, and a cover blinked out for a frame. Every frame is now retaken until two shots agree, and a per-frame luma scan shows no blanks or flashes.
- Captured at 2× and Lanczos-downscaled to 1200×630. H.264 High, yuv420p, 30 fps, `+faststart`, no audio track. No cursor or dev overlay.

## Code

- `lib/share-card.tsx`: a `ShareVideo` type, `shareVideo(name)` (an absolute `${host}/….mp4` at 1200×630, `video/mp4`) and `shareVideoMeta(video)`. `shareVideoMeta` emits `og:video`, `og:video:secure_url`, `og:video:type`, `og:video:width` and `og:video:height`.
- `PageHead` and `PlaygroundHead` (through `PlaygroundLayout`) take an optional `shareVideo`. It's wired on `pages/playground/index.tsx` and `pages/playground/dom-ino.tsx`.
- `playwright` is a new devDependency, for the recorder.

Assets live in `public/playground/og/`: `playground.mp4` (1,582,702 B), `playground.png` (253,306 B) and `dom-ino.mp4` (1,574,153 B).

## Checks

- `pnpm test:lint`, `pnpm test:prettier`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test:unit` (158 tests) pass.
- `curl` on local dev returns the `og:video` tags on both pages, and both MP4s are served as `video/mp4`.
- CI (typecheck, lint and build) and the Vercel preview build pass. The preview (https://me-git-og-video-playground-wustep.vercel.app) is behind Vercel Authentication, and every path, MP4s included, returns a 302 to `vercel.com/sso-api`, so it couldn't be curled from here. As with the existing cards, the tags use `host`, which resolves to `https://wustep.me`, so they point at the production asset paths. Those paths start serving once this merges.

author: shj00007
body:
Tightens the shared "Code Review Rules" block in `AGENTS.md`, from findings raised on the previous revision's PRs. The shared block now uses the same wording in every repository.

- **G3**: documentation never waives authentication, authorization or other security checks. Only a documented availability fallback that touches no security check is exempt, and prescribed retries / credential refreshes may lead to access only after those checks succeed. Config-loading failures fail closed for required or authority-bearing settings; an unreadable optional setting that grants nothing may fall back to a conservative default.
- **G2**: a database transaction counts as atomic only if its isolation level, row lock or single statement actually serializes the writers. Event-loop atomicity covers only state that loop owns alone.
- **G1**: a revert that is the PR's stated purpose is allowed.
- **G7** (public repositories only): the default-endpoint rule itself now allows intentional loopback defaults; the scanner exemption stays limited to secret and redaction scanners.
- **R1** (this repository): aligned with G1 — only accidental reversions of work already on `main` are flagged.

Documentation only; no code or test changes.

body:
## Summary

duckdb 2.0.0 (released 2026-10-21) removed `DuckDBPyConnection.pl()`. `duckdb>=0.10` now installs 2.0.0, so every test that turns a query into a polars frame fails. Running the query through `con.sql(...)` returns a relation, which still has `.pl()`:

```diff
-feats = con.execute("SELECT ... FROM account_features").pl()
+feats = con.sql("SELECT ... FROM account_features").pl()
```

The change touches five call sites in `tests/test_enrichment.py` and nothing else. The one remaining `con.execute(...).fetchone()` still works in 2.0.

## Evidence

- **Before (duckdb 2.0.0):**
  ```text
  test_enrichment.py  con.execute(...).pl()  -> AttributeError   x4
  pytest: 134 passed, 4 failed   pyright: 5 errors
  ```
  **After (duckdb 2.0.0):**
  ```text
  pytest: 138 passed   pyright: 0 errors   ruff: pass
  ```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Test-only change, easy to revert.

**Blast Radius:** tests

Nothing under `src/` changes. Merging this unblocks #2, which fails CI on the same four tests.

author: sonaiengine
body:
## 요약

10/23 데모 영상에서 "BO 들어가서 로그인하고 상품등록 화면까지" 가 약 100초 걸렸다. 그중 브라우저 도구 쪽 원인 두 가지를 범용으로 고친다(사이트 분기 없음).

1. **Navigate goto 가 느린 리소스 하나를 끝까지 기다리던 것** (`54b419f1`) — `loadURL()` 이 load(모든 하위 리소스)까지 시간 제한 없이 기다려 25.2초, 그 사이 페이지가 주소를 옮기면 ERR_ABORTED 로 15.2초 뒤 실패했다. 새 문서의 dom-ready 뒤 load 를 2초만 더 기다리고, 스스로 주소 이동은 실패로 보지 않는다.
2. **이동·클릭 뒤 화면을 보려고 BrowserSnapshot 을 따로 부르던 턴** (`a3267ad8`) — 페이지를 옮긴 Navigate·Interact 결과에 새 화면 스냅샷을 붙인다. 페이지가 그대로면 붙이지 않는다(앞 ref 유지). 조작이 보낸 XHR·fetch 가 끝나고 새 화면이 데이터를 부를 틈까지 기다린 뒤 읽는다(Playwright MCP 와 같은 방식).

## 실측 (숨긴 dev 앱)

| 동작 | 전 | 후 |
|---|---|---|
| 20초 이미지가 있는 페이지 goto | 20,027ms | 2,009ms |
| 로드 중 주소가 바뀌는 페이지 goto | ERR_ABORTED 실패 | 2,009ms 성공 |
| BO 상품등록 goto | 결과에 화면 없음 | 1.96초, 폼 전체 14,439자 첨부 |
| BO 공지 '더보기'(SPA 경로 이동) | 결과에 화면 없음 | 1.23초, 5,645자 첨부 |
| 요청만 하는 클릭(화면 그대로) | — | 0.3초, 첨부 없음 |

## 이어서 쌓은 것 (4단계 — 박소민 프롬프트 규칙을 범용 도구 수정으로 대신하기)

3. **설명 없이 번호(-3)만 온 로드 중단** (`efb0efd8`) — 1번의 "스스로 주소 이동은 실패로 보지 않는다" 가 errno 문자열이 빠진 경우를 놓치던 것.
4. **BrowserFill 이 이미 그 값인 칸은 판단 모델을 부르지 않는다** (`aff9a146`, 4a) — 다시 채우기에서 줄마다 판단 모델을 부르던 것. 앞 줄이 바꾼 칸은 다시 읽어 판단 모델로 넘긴다.
5. **사이트 확인창의 확정 버튼은 채팅 카드로 사용자에게 묻고 누른다** (`5e274b1a`, 4g) — 10/22 trace 54448 에서 승인요청 확인창의 확인까지 눌려 시연 상품이 실제 승인요청됐다(저장 가드를 걷어낸 뒤).
   - 버튼 이름·메시지 해석이 아니라 화면 구조로 판단한다: 맨 위 대화상자에 입력칸이 없고, 버튼 2~3개 중 취소·닫기류와 다른 버튼이 함께 있으면 확인창. 그 창의 확정 버튼 클릭·Enter·마우스만 묻는다(저장 버튼 자체, 알림, 조회·고르기 팝업은 묻지 않음).
   - 카드: 1 이번만 / 2 이 대화에서 같은 창은 다시 묻지 않기 / 3 누르지 않고 할 말 적기. Esc 는 말 없이 거절.
   - 말 없는 거절·90초 무응답은 `user_denied`(런타임 denial guard 가 같은 턴 재시도를 막음), 할 말은 `browser_denied` 결과에 실어 모델이 따르게 한다. 원격 턴은 묻지 않고 누르지 않는다. 창이 가려져 있으면 OS 알림만(포커스 안 뺏음).
   - BrowserFill 은 확인창이 뜨면 남은 줄을 멈춘다. 클릭 결과에 떠 있는 대화상자(`dialog`)와 `role=alert` 문구(`alerts`)를 싣는다.

### 4g 실측 (숨긴 dev 앱 + 로컬 시험 페이지)

| 상황 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| 필수 칸 비우고 승인요청 클릭 | `alerts: ["검색키워드는 필수입니다"]` |
| 채우고 승인요청 클릭 | `dialog: {승인요청하시겠습니까?, [취소, 확인]}` |
| 확인 클릭 → 말 없이 거절 | `user_denied`, 제출 0건 |
| 확인창 떠 있는 채로 BrowserFill | 1ms 에 멈춤, 까닭 남김 |
| Enter → 할 말 적고 거절 | `browser_denied` + 사용자의 말, 제출 0건 |
| 확인 클릭 → 이번만 | 제출 1건 |
| 2번(이 대화에서 다시 묻지 않기) | 처음 한 번만 물음 |
| 취소 클릭 | 묻지 않음 |

막지 못하는 경우: 확인창 없이 첫 클릭에 저장하는 사이트, iframe 안 확인창, 네이티브 `confirm()`, 음성 고속 조작 경로.

6. **BrowserFill 이 알림을 닫고 실패한 줄을 한 번 다시 한다** (`328f4692`, 4e) — 10/22~23 기록에서 알림을 닫고 실패한 줄 13개 중 12개는 그 줄의 값이 아니라 다른 칸 때문이었다(먼저 채울 협력사가 비어 있음, 앞 칸의 포커스 검사 알림이 이 줄의 클릭을 가로챔). 줄마다 LLM 이 BrowserFill 을 다시 불러 첫 Fill 뒤 3~5회가 더 들었다.
   - 알림 문구에 든 칸 이름으로만 판단한다(사이트 분기 없음). 뒤 줄의 칸을 부르면 그 줄 뒤로 미루고 그 줄이 성공했을 때만, 앞에서 못 한 줄이나 이 줄의 칸을 부르면 다시 하지 않고(LLM 이 고침), 그 밖은 바로 한 번 다시 한다.
   - 파일 올리기 줄과 남은 시간 15초 미만은 다시 하지 않는다. 결과 줄에 `retried: true`.
   - 실측(로컬 시험 페이지): 협력사보다 먼저 온 판매가 줄 실패 → 미뤄서 성공(`complete=true`), 알림에 가로채인 체크박스 → 바로 다시 해서 성공, 지난 판매기간(값 거절) → 다시 하지 않음.
7. **작업 공간에 올리는 이름과 하위 폴더를 NFC 로 맞춘다** (`1185242f`, 4f) — 맥이 주는 한글 파일 이름(NFD)이 sandbox 에 그대로 남아, 모델이 다시 적는 NFC 이름으로는 리눅스에서 열리지 않았다(`FileNotFoundError` 9턴 11번). 채팅 첨부만 NFC 였고 기기 폴더 복사(`CopyToWorkspace`)가 빠져 있었다. 모든 올리기가 지나는 `packages/protocol` `workspaceUpload` 한 곳에서 맞춘다.
   - 같은 4f 의 다른 원인(UserPc get 이 `sandbox_path` 를 늘 폴더로 만들어 `prod.xlsx/신상품_정보.xlsx` → `IsADirectoryError` 8턴)은 xgen-workflow !2302 `c19bdebe` 에서 고쳤다.
8. **끝 이름만 준 트리 줄이 맨 위에서 실패하면 전체 경로로 보내라고 알린다** (`f94b7218`, 4d) — 표준카테고리를 끝 이름으로만 준 줄이 3번 실패했다(펼치지 않은 하위는 화면에 없어 맨 위에서 고를 수 없음). 결과 글에 "트리는 맨 위 항목부터 전체 경로로 보내 주세요(예: 「상위 > 하위」)" 를 붙인다. 트리를 다 펼쳐 찾기는 실패 근거가 적어 하지 않았다.

문서만 바뀐 커밋: 4h 조사(`b625beba` — placeholder 거짓 성공은 10/22 수정 뒤 재발 없음), 4f 기록(`b69c6b7f`), 측정 방법(`96b71f53`).

## 테스트

desktop 744개 중 738개 통과·실패 0(6개 건너뜀), typecheck·typecheck:node 통과. 새 테스트 `test/browser-page-after.test.ts` 11개, `browser-security.test.ts` 4개, `browser-confirm.test.ts` 10개, `fast-act-brief.test.ts`(4a·4e), `fast-act-labels.test.ts`(4d) 1개. protocol 374개 통과(`workspace-copy.test.ts` NFC 1개), typecheck 통과.

## 반영 뒤 측정 (아직 안 함)

4단계의 목표는 박소민 프롬프트의 규칙 문장 없이도 같은 결과가 나오고 빨라지는 것이다. 이 PR·xgen-workflow !2302·런타임 #174 가 dev 에 반영되면 같은 두 메시지로 소민 프롬프트(A)와 규칙을 뺀 판(B)을 번갈아 돌려 잰다. 프롬프트 두 판, trace 내보내기 SQL, 턴마다 세는 스크립트는 `apps/desktop/docs/agent-turn-speed-2026-10-24/measure/` 에 있다.

기준선(A, 수정 전 1회, `fast-act-baseline-28`): 두 턴 296초. 둘째 턴("진행해줘") 257초 중 도구 136초(Navigate 3번 65.5초, BrowserFill 4번 59.2초), 나머지는 LLM 30번(한 번에 약 4초). memory 가 꺼져 둘째 턴이 엑셀을 다시 읽었다(파일 도구 6번, 실패 2번).

## 같이 보는 변경

- xgen-workflow `fix/connector-browser-guide` — BrowserGuide 안내문에 BrowserFill·BrowserFormValues 가 빠져 있던 것, 실패 사유가 전부 가려지던 것, UserPc get 이 파일 경로를 폴더로 만들던 것(4f)
- xgen-agent-runtime `feature/fold-superseded-snapshots` — 같은 탭·같은 주소의 옛 스냅샷을 요청 사본에서 접기

분석·단계별 기록: `apps/desktop/docs/agent-turn-speed-2026-10-24/README.md`. 남은 4단계는 4b(결제수단 "전체")·4c(공급원가 자동 계산 칸)로 근거가 적어 낮은 우선순위다. 반영 뒤 측정 결과를 보고 Draft 를 푼다.

author: ymichael
body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

The sidebar's multi-select menu (`sidebarMultiSelect` experiment) was a hardcoded component in the thread-list plugin. Plugin thread actions such as push-notifications' Notifications could not appear in it, and it had no Delete. Its Archive called `sdk.threads.archive` directly for each thread. That skipped core's archive flow, so selecting a parent archived all of its children without the child-thread confirmation, even with that setting on, and it never ran core's pane cleanup and route repair. Separately, the single-thread delete dialog counted only direct children, although delete removes the whole tree.

## What changed

- **Plugin SDK (0.6.79 → 0.6.80):**
  - Thread action registrations can add `experimental_bulkItem({ threads, data, sdk, navigate })`.
  - `experimental_ThreadActionsContextMenu` takes `experimental_bulkThreads` and `onEscapeKeyDown`. With 2+ threads it shows a "N threads selected" bulk menu; otherwise it shows the normal menu. A row keeps a single Radix menu, so joining or leaving a selection doesn't remount it.
  - The registration collector keeps and validates `experimental_bulkItem`.
  - The test fake takes `threadBulkActions`.
- **Core actions:**
  - Mark read/unread, Pin/Unpin, Archive (Unarchive when every selected thread is archived) and Delete have bulk items.
  - Archive and Delete go through new `requestArchiveThreads` / `requestDeleteThreads` in `ThreadActionsProvider`, which single-thread archive and delete also use.
  - Each asks once per selection, acts on the topmost selected threads only, and cleans up panes and routes once. Archive honors the confirmation setting and shares the environment-group Undo toast.
- **Counting what goes with a thread:** new `POST /threads/cascade` / `sdk.threads.experimental_listCascade({ threadIds, action })` returns the visible threads that archiving or deleting each thread would also affect. It's built on the same helpers as `archive-all` and `delete`, so single-thread and bulk dialogs count the same way, lifecycle-owned threads included. Single-thread delete now counts the whole tree instead of direct children.
- **Plugins:**
  - thread-list's Move to section and push-notifications' Notifications have bulk items.
  - The thread list passes its selection to the host menu with a Clear selection item.
  - Threads that disappear from the sidebar are dropped from the selection.
- **Docs:** `docs/api_to_audit.md` (bulk items, `experimental_listCascade`), `docs/configuration.md`, the plugin-authoring guide (bulk docs live in `frontend-sidebar-navigation.md` because `frontend-registration.md` is at its 500-line cap), and the Plugin Guide surface.

## What this tests

The agreed drawing (the design ruling recorded on #4287) keeps the 1px `--line` border and the `--surface-strong` fill on a select trigger inside a toolbar, as the artifacts screen draws the Type facet. `src/components/artifacts/library-toolbar.tsx` already renders the Type trigger with `border-line bg-surface-strong`, so this pull request changes no product file. author: satoshikawato
body:
## What changes

The 114 integration-test files `LOSAT/tests/*.rs` were 114 test binaries. With the new guard (115 files) they build
into eight:

| binary | files |
| --- | --- |
| `blastn` (`blastn_*`, `megablast_xdrop`, `run_local_blastn`) | 26 |
| `blastp` (`blastp_*`, `run_local_blastp*`) | 22 |
| `blastx` (`blastx_*`) | 9 |
| `tblastn` (`tblastn_*`, `run_local_tblastn`) | 11 |
| `tblastx` (`tblastx_*`, `run_local_tblastx`) | 22 |
| `common` (`cli_*`, `outfmt*`, `default_bundle`, `pairwise_par`, ... and the new `suite_layout`) | 23 |
| `blastn_report_stream_api`, `unit_tests` | 1 each |

- The files stay where they are (`git log`, ledger rows, prompts, fixture paths and `include_bytes!` keep working).
  `LOSAT/Cargo.toml` sets `autotests = false` and lists the eight binaries; each suite root
  `LOSAT/tests/suites/<suite>.rs` declares its files as `#[path = "../<file>.rs"] mod <file>;`.
- `blastn_report_stream_api` and `unit_tests` stay alone: they change the process environment
  (`set_var` / `remove_var`; `unit_tests` through `tests/unit/common/diagnostics.rs`), and the tests of a suite share
  one process under plain `cargo test`.
- Member edits, all for files that now share a process: `run_local_blastp_blocks.rs` re-runs its own test as
  `child_test_name()` (`run_local_blastp_blocks::child_search` in the suite); `outfmt11_blastp.rs` and the five
  `outfmt16_*.rs` get file-specific temporary names; `run_local_support/mod.rs` `temp_path` and
  `reach_support/mod.rs` `Reach::new` put the module path into their names (a helper module is compiled once per file
  that declares it, so its counter is per copy).
- `tests/suite_layout.rs` (in `common`) fails when a `tests/*.rs` is in no binary or in two (its message names the
  suite and the two lines to add), when a `[[test]]` has keys other than `name` and `path`, when a member's module
  name is not its file stem, when a `tests/<dir>/main.rs` exists, and when a suite member or any module file it pulls
  in changes the process environment or process-wide state (`set_var`, `remove_var`, `set_current_dir`, `set_hook`,
  `take_hook`, `build_global`).
- Docs: AGENTS.md "Testing Expectations" (where a new file goes; the reason in the unit-test rule reworded), skills
  losat-gates and losat-worktree, LOSAT/tests/README.md, changelog fragment. No CI file changes.

## For anyone who runs one test file

- `cargo test --all-features --test blastn_strand` becomes `cargo test --all-features --test blastn blastn_strand::`.
  Keep `--test <suite>`: the filter is a substring, so `blastx_hitbf::` alone also runs `tblastx_hitbf::`.
- nextest: `-E 'binary(blastn_strand)'` becomes `-E 'test(/^blastn_strand::/)'`; the binary id is `LOSAT::blastn` and
  a test is `LOSAT::blastn blastn_strand::<test>` in reports and JUnit.
- An edit of one test file rebuilds its suite (numbers below).
- Plain `cargo test --test <suite>` runs all of that suite's files' tests at once, up to the CPU count; a timing gate
  passes `-- --test-threads N`.
- A new test file needs two lines in its suite root; `suite_layout` says which.

## Measured (local, this machine: 32 vCPUs shared with other sessions; CI's test profile, `--all-features`)

Base b1f09848 against this layout on the same base (6dd335b9, before the rebase and the review fixes):

| | base | this PR | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| target dir after a cold `cargo test --no-run` | 3.33 GB | 1.81 GB | -1.53 GB (-46 %) |
| test executables (incl. lib tests and the bin) | 2,431 MB in 116 | 905 MB in 11 | -1.53 GB |
| plain `cargo test --no-fail-fast` | 1,044.7 s | 388.3 s | -63 % |
| plain `cargo test -- --test-threads=1` | 1,628.5 s | 1,349.7 s | -17 % |
| 4 CPUs (`taskset -c 0-3`), after touching src/lib.rs, paired base / PR / PR / base | 154.0 s wall, 558 CPU-s (load 4-5); 176.0 s, 641 CPU-s (load 9) | 138.1 s, 512 CPU-s; 138.7 s, 516 CPU-s (load 4-6) | -16 s wall, -8 % CPU (against the run at the same load) |
| 4 CPUs, after touching one test file | 0.3-1.9 s wall, 0.4-2.9 CPU-s | 3.8-4.1 s wall, 12-13 CPU-s | +2-4 s wall, +9-12 CPU-s |
| nextest `--test-threads 8` | 544.6 s | 366.2 s | not paired (load 13-30 against 7-10) |

Pass sets: plain `cargo test` at default threads and at `--test-threads=1`, and nextest: base 2,461 passed + 19
ignored in each; this PR the same 2,461 + 19 plus the 6 `suite_layout` tests (`passset.py --flat` maps
`<file>::<test>` back to the file). `--list`: 2,480 names, identical (+6).

After the rebase on dev 66d31553 (which added #446's `blastx_unit_cap.rs` and #450's `reach_support/`) and the
review fixes (d569ff5f): `--list` = dev 66d31553's 2,482 names + the 6 `suite_layout` tests; nextest `-j8` 2,469
passed, 19 skipped (281.8 s); plain `cargo test --no-fail-fast` 2,469 ok + 19 ignored, 0 failed (271.3 s); fmt;
clippy `--all-targets --all-features -D warnings`; `scripts/changelog_fragments.py check`. The guard's negative checks
by hand each fail it: an unlisted file, `set_var` in a member, `set_var` in `run_local_support/mod.rs` and in
`reach_support/mod.rs` (message: move it out of the helper), `build_global` in a member, `harness = false` on a suite,
a `#[test]` with `set_var` in a suite root, a member wrapped in an inline `mod`, `autotests` moved out of `[package]`.

Rebased again on dev a0d11554 (#452-#457 edit four tblastn test files): fmt, clippy, `changelog_fragments.py check`,
nextest `-j8` 2,453 passed, 19 skipped (2,472 names).

CI (this PR's run 40067274725, both cargo test shards pass):

| run | build part of the nextest step | test part | job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this PR (10 binaries) | 302 / 285 s | 841 / 766 s (1,228 / 1,225 tests) | 19.6 / 17.9 min |
| #446's run 40062297291 (116 binaries, a few hours earlier) | 214 / 322 s | 501 / 741 s (1,256 / 1,207 tests) | 12.2 / 18.1 min |
| dev push 39932155351 (design reference, 10-23, with the since-removed reference step) | 310 / 343 s | 1,274 / 1,152 s | 29.8 / 29.8 min |

The build part did not change beyond runner variance (the two shards of one run differ by 100 s; the paired local
4-CPU measurement predicts -16 s). The slower shard's job is 19.6 min here against 18.1 min in #446's run; runner
speed varies by x1.1-1.6 between runs (ci-rust-speed), so the +0.5 min shard shift the design simulated cannot be
told apart. CI time is not a reason for this PR: target size, plain `cargo test` time and fewer binaries are.

## Costs

- An edit of one test file rebuilds its suite: +9-12 CPU-s, 4 s wall on four CPUs (was 0.3-2 s).
- nextest's `--partition count:k/2` deals each binary's tests in turn, so shard counts stay even but the time split

author: younatics
body:
`YALSunnyRefreshControl` loads its nib and images from the class bundle, which fails when the control ships in a Swift package (resources live in a separate resource bundle). This PR:

- makes `+internalBundle` return `SWIFTPM_MODULE_BUNDLE` when that macro is defined (Swift Package Manager builds) and keep `[NSBundle bundleForClass:]` otherwise;
- adds a `Package.swift` with one library target (`YALPullToRefresh`) built from `YALTourPullToRefresh/YALSunnyRefreshControll`, with the xib and `Images.xcassets` as processed resources. The target is named `YALPullToRefresh` rather than `YALSunnyRefreshControl` because SwiftPM treats a header named like the target as an umbrella header and then rejects the asset catalog folder next to it.

Verified with `xcodebuild -scheme YALPullToRefresh -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'` on Xcode 27.1; used by MotionBook 3.5, which runs the Rentals pull-to-refresh example inside the app.

## What changes

### Contact button on touch screens
On a phone, the Copy and Open halves sat permanently under the address. After one tap, the address part disappeared, because the browser kept its `:hover` state after the tap.

- **Phones:** the first tap on the address splits it in place into **Copy | Open**. That is the hover behaviour, the same size and in the same spot. A tap anywhere else closes it again.

### Listing rows below 720px
The meta under a title took three lines: domain, status, then the arrow. It now takes one line, in this order:

The word "Open" on the Tools index (`.lr-trail-word`) is hidden there, because the arrow already says it. When the line can't fit, as with the German labels at 320px, it wraps.

author: zhavior
body:
## Problem
On seolaquest.com, `/blog` says "No articles match" and every article returns 404. Both causes come from running on Cloudflare Workers:

1. `lib/blog.ts` read `content/posts` from disk at request time, and a Worker has no project files.
2. The article route set `dynamicParams = false`. No OpenNext incremental cache is configured, so the prerendered pages were never served.

## Fix
- **Posts are bundled at build time.** `scripts/generate-blog-posts.mjs` writes `lib/generated/blogPosts.ts` (published posts only) and `lib/generated/blogSlugs.ts`. It runs first in `npm run build`, and `npm run blog:generate` runs it on its own. A test fails if the committed files drift from `content/posts`.
- **Articles render on demand** (`dynamicParams = true`).
- **Unknown slugs still get a real 404**, now returned by `middleware.ts`. A `notFound()` thrown under the Clerk rewrite answers with HTTP 200, which search engines treat as a soft 404.

## Evidence
I built the real Worker (`npm run cf:build`) and ran it with `wrangler dev`:

| URL | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/blog` | 200, lists the 3 posts once bundled | 200, lists the 3 posts |
| `/blog/guild-lore-origin` (and the other 2 articles) | 404 | 200 |
| `/blog/does-not-exist` | 404 | 404 |
| `/blog/monetizing-saas-apis` (unpublished) | 404 | 404 |
| `/sitemap.xml` | lists the 3 articles | lists the 3 articles |

The "Before" column is the same build with only fix 1 applied. The live site at the time had `/blog` empty and articles at 404.

Full suite: 1007 passed, 25 skipped, 0 failed. `tsc` and lint are clean.

## Not covered
- **Production.** The live site changes only after a deploy (`npm run cf:deploy`). Check `/blog` and one article on seolaquest.com afterwards.
- `lib/aiBlogger.ts` (the `/api/v1/blog/generate` endpoint) still writes posts to disk, which can't work on Workers. This PR doesn't change it.
- `wrangler dev` logs `WebAssembly.compile(): Wasm code generation disallowed by embedder` twice at startup. It does that before this change too.

author: olemarkus
body:
A flow-backed stepped device whose report-back Flow is missing or mistargeted kept its card on "Increasing to 16 A" or a retry countdown for as long as PELS kept asking. The 2026-07-05 deadlock was only diagnosable from raw logs.

The stepped command state now counts the commands for one step that expired unconfirmed in a row (retryCount also counts a reissue that never went stale). The executor reads the tracked step and its count from the command session and concludes stepCommandUnanswered once two have expired for the step the plan still wants and the device still reports another level. The card's reason line then says what to check, ahead of every other stepped line: the Flow that reports the level back, or the device itself under built-in control. Simulation sends no commands, so it shows no such line. The built-in-control predicate moved to the device action projection seam so the plan read model can ask it.

Layer 7 of 10 in one stack, based on `feat/powerhour-export-price`. Every layer passes `npm run ci:checks` on its own.

author: vgvassilev
body:
The reverse pass can replace an operand with a saved copy of it. When the replacement is an lvalue and the operand was a value, clad put the lvalue in directly. A conversion above it, such as the int to double in `k * b.a`, then applied to the lvalue. Clang does not allow that. A clang built with assertions aborts with "can't implicitly cast glvalue to prvalue with this cast kind", and a release build accepts the malformed tree.

Load the lvalue first, as clang does.

## Sprint T — simultaneous Trivia

Completes the existing T0 review unit with the real module, production integration and T-A1–T-A7 evidence. SDK `next-round-game/0.1` is unchanged; no database migration or external dependency was added.

### Delivered
- `games/trivia`: strict import/manifest schemas; canonical SHA-256 bank identity; pure reducer with simultaneous private submissions, round-index fencing, stable deadlines, scored public reveals, late join/rejoin rules and all-disabled pause/resume.
- Solo and 2–8-player group modes; bank-free final result/career projection; explicit eligibility reasons.
- GameBridge client: private radio choices, countdown, authoritative stale refresh + explicit retry, same-command/same-revision recovery after unknown transport results, round history and retained final-round reveal.
- API/worker loaders, startup metadata install, browser entry, Admin bank import/catalog and create-match setup; stock Docker dependency/layout integration. Server-only game source is rejected by the web build.
- Six original agent-drafted CC0 starter questions with honest provenance; imported by Admin, not embedded in browser assets or auto-seeded.
- Updated `docs/trivia-design.md` and README with shipped rules, operator workflow, bounded SDK verdict and acceptance evidence.

### Verification
- Full `pnpm test --maxWorkers=2`: **37 files / 411 tests on each of PostgreSQL 18.6 and 17.11**, using isolated Docker databases.
- Focused module + real API transaction suite: **9/9 on each major**.
- Frozen install, `pnpm build` + 15-artifact browser scan, `pnpm typecheck`, zero-warning `pnpm lint`, SPDX source check: pass.
- Real compiled browser + production API/worker: Admin import (including duplicate), resource setup, private answer selection, two-round scoring/reveals and retained final reveal; actual stale submission stayed at revision 3 until explicit retry advanced to 4 with original deadline unchanged.
- Lost-result browser probe forwarded and committed an actual action, dropped its response and refresh, then explicitly replayed the **same command ID and revision** successfully. No automatic replay.

author: vedhavyas
body:
Closes #2541.

Each CI job now runs only for the paths it serves. A docs-only pull request skips the Rust and client jobs, and a Rust-only one skips the client's CEF job. `ci-required` always runs, depends on every job, and fails when a job whose paths changed was skipped, so it is the single check to require in the ruleset; with `build site` still required, the ruleset's list becomes those two. The macOS CEF distribution is cached on its pinned version rather than the lockfile.

Locally, `just check` runs its four independent groups concurrently - the fast checks, the Rust workspace, the client web steps and the shell crate - capped by `FORGE_CHECK_JOBS` (default 4), keeps every step's log under `target/check-logs/`, prints a failing group's log tail, and ends on the same verdict line naming the first failing step. `just check-serial` keeps the step-at-a-time form. Measured back to back on this machine with sccache warm: 157-159 s for `just check` against 325 s for `check-serial` at load ~12 on 16 cores, and 210 s against 358 s at load ~40 from other sessions. When `sccache` is on `PATH` the recipes export `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, so compiled objects are shared across worktrees and branches; without it they build normally.

Two client shell tests raced production wall-clock bounds under the gate's load, so they now pass a larger budget from the test build and production's constants are unchanged. `just check-delta <crate>` gives review rounds the slice of the gate they need. The final head still runs `just check` and `just check-feature-configs`.

- [x] `just check` and `just check-feature-configs` are green
- [x] New wire surface, if any, ships with a captured baseline under the pinned CLI version

### Description

The project files panel (#14956) answers "browse or commit my repo", but not "what did the agent just do". Its Git view shows the whole uncommitted working tree, so the agent's edits are mixed with your own and with earlier sessions, and there was no way to see what the last turn changed.

This splits the two questions into two controls and adds an entry point from the chat:

- **Header:** a **Changes** button carrying the session's line counts, and the folder button (now icon-only) for the existing Files + Git panel. Both open in the same right-hand slot.
- **Changes pane:** `Last turn | Session` tabs, a file list (same rows as the Git view), and a diff of the selected file. A footer link, **All uncommitted changes**, jumps to the Git view. Without git checkpoints (plain folders, SSH) it falls back to the tool-event reconstruction of the session with a notice.
- **Receipt:** when the last turn finishes, a small card under it lists what it changed (`Changed 1 file +1 -0`). Clicking it, or one of its files, opens the pane on Last turn. Sending the next message removes it; a new one appears when that turn finishes.

**How changes are computed (sidecar, `session-changes.ts`).** Core already writes a git checkpoint before each turn's first model call. The last turn is the latest checkpoint against the working tree; the session is the first checkpoint against the working tree. Each point becomes a git tree:
- a checkpoint's tree overlaid with its untracked-files third parent (`git read-tree <tree> <untracked-tree>` into a temp index), so files the agent created but never staged are included;
- the working tree via a temp copy of the real index plus `git add -A`, which keeps the stat cache and never touches the real index.

Then `git diff-tree --raw` / `--numstat` gives paths, statuses, and line counts. `read_session_change` returns both sides of one change by blob id (1 MiB cap, binary-aware, object ids validated). Both commands require the trusted desktop connection, like source control.

Supporting refactors: the panel's width tracking and drag handle moved into `WorkspacePanelFrame` (shared by both panels), and the Git view's `ChangeRow` is exported with optional actions.

Not included: an "Uncommitted" scope (it duplicates the Git view), revert/undo, and reviewing older individual turns.

### Test Procedure

- `sidecar/session-changes.test.ts` builds real temp repos with stash-shaped checkpoints (including the untracked third parent) and checks the last-turn and session diffs, that a pre-existing untracked file never shows, that the real index is untouched, binary handling, and object id validation.
- New `changes-panel.test.tsx` (two scopes, blob reads, Git/close callbacks, tool-event fallback forcing Session), receipt cases in `chat-messages.test.tsx` (shown after the finished last turn, hidden while running and once a new user message exists), and updated `agent-header.test.tsx` for the two-button header.
- Rebased onto main (including the header PR menu and terminal toggle from #15303); `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test:sidecar` (1315 pass), `bun run test:settings-ui`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run build:web` pass.
- Manual: ran a real multi-turn agent session in a demo repo that already had an uncommitted edit of mine, then opened it in the headless desktop app. One receipt sat under the last turn, my pre-existing edit stayed out of the session view, Review opened Last turn, sending a new message removed the receipt immediately, and a new receipt appeared when that turn finished.

### Type of Change

-   [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
-   [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
-   [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
-   [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes
-   [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes
-   [ ] 📚 Documentation update
-   [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Screenshots

Receipt under the finished last turn:

![Last turn receipt in the transcript](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-2b5b9e53-5b09-42bd-854d-698697c8fb78)

Last turn opened from the receipt:

![Changes pane on Last turn](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-6f4f3391-4f3a-44e7-b1b8-bf0b28bafc93)

Session scope from the header's Changes button:

![Changes pane on Session](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-5083e536-3729-45aa-9fce-46dc6d1a272d)

"All uncommitted changes" opens the existing Git view:

![Git view opened from the Changes pane](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-7a9f3b1a-6a85-4ae0-a96e-c2a90f52d54a)

### Additional Notes

- The header count now prefers the git-based session total and falls back to the tool-event total, so it also includes edits you made by hand after the session started.
- The snapshots refresh on a 400ms debounce when the session status or its tool edits change. The working-tree snapshot costs about the same as Core's own per-turn checkpoint.
- SSH environments get a "not available yet" notice and the tool-event fallback.

author: olemarkus
body:
Whether a headroom-blocked restore was the budget's was read off one plan-wide flag: the daily pace binding with no physical limit breached. That was wrong both ways. An off budget-exempt device's projection can make capacity the binding pace while the measured budget axis is what turns a non-exempt device down, so the hold read as a power shortage; and a daily pace can bind while capacity would turn the device down as well, so the hold read as the budget's and counted as unserved budget demand that a budget release would not have served.

The materialization stage now resolves budgetHeldDeviceIds once from the post-hold ledger: a device is the budget's when its admission gap closes with the budget axis set aside. A running stepped device denied a step-up is judged on its own gate's need, the step it would climb, since the ledger arithmetic prices it at its whole draw. The reason fold and the device diagnostics read the same set, so the card's reason, the starvation cause and the budget's unserved-demand evidence agree; a keep-state hold, which the fold never visits, is covered in diagnostics. The plan-wide budgetReleasableHeadroomHold flag is gone, and observeDiagnostics reads the cycle's instant from the context.

Layer 8 of 10 in one stack, based on `feat/stepped-unconfirmed-level-line`. Every layer passes `npm run ci:checks` on its own.

author: khubaibqaiser
body:
## Summary

Make the CI claims true: third-party actions are pinned to commits, every job has a timeout, the nightly AI eval says what it did, and dependency updates come from Dependabot instead of an unused Renovate config.

## Track

- [ ] Roadmap (Phase \_\_ — slice \_\_)
- [ ] Alignment (P\_\_ — checklist item \_\_)
- [ ] AI-native / agent eval (workflow change, no agent-eval task)
- [ ] Bugfix / hotfix
- [x] Infra / deploy
- [ ] Docs-only (no executable change)

## Spec / ADR

- Link: N/A. CI hygiene; the reasoning is written up in `docs/ai-native-workflow.md` (separate docs PR).
- Invariant touched (one line): none; no runtime behavior changes.

## Problem

- Every workflow referenced actions by a mutable tag such as `actions/checkout@v5`. If a tag is moved or an action is compromised, the new code runs in jobs that hold the `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and in `deploy.yml` SSH credentials.
- No job had a `timeout-minutes`, so a hung job could run for the 6-hour default.
- The nightly "AI live eval" ended with `exit 0` inside a green step when `AI_BASE_URL` was not set. The run showed green for a live check that never happened.
- `renovate.json` was in the repo, but no PR in the repo history came from Renovate or Dependabot.

## Solution

- Pin all 10 third-party actions (29 references in 6 workflows) to the commit their release tag points to today, with the tag kept as a comment, for example `# v5.1.0`. I resolved each tag to its commit through the GitHub API and checked that the commit exists in the action's own repository.
- Add `timeout-minutes` to all 9 jobs (5 to 25 minutes, several times the longest duration seen in recent runs; the 4-minute `quality` job gets 20).
- `ai-eval.yml` is now "AI eval (nightly)". A small gate step reads the secret, and the live step runs only when it is set; otherwise it shows as **skipped**. The secret is visible to the gate step and the live step only, not to the whole job.
- Add `.github/dependabot.yml`: npm (root entry; dependabot-core reads `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and fetches the workspace packages) and GitHub Actions, monthly, minor and patch updates grouped, 5 open PRs at most. Packages bound to the Expo SDK (`expo*`, `react`, `react-dom`, `react-native*` and friends) are ignored on purpose: they must move together with the SDK (`npx expo install --fix`), and this repo pins them with `~` and exact ranges.
- Delete `renovate.json`.

## Risk

- [ ] Low — localized, no contract / auth / AI boundary change
- [x] Medium — API or UI behavior, migrations, or module-boundary touch
- [ ] High — auth / tenancy, nutrition safety, Layer-3, infra, or breaking contract

Why not Low: this touches the deploy workflows (`deploy.yml`, `deploy-paas.yml`, `mobile-deploy.yml`). They run only on push to `main`, so this PR's CI cannot exercise them. Each pin is the commit its tag resolves to today, so behavior should be unchanged.

---

## Nutrition & AI safety

- [x] N/A — this PR does not touch nutrition, Layer-3, or meal-plan flows

## Security & tenancy

- [x] N/A — this PR does not touch auth, API routes, schema / RLS, or list queries

## Architecture boundaries

- [x] N/A — docs-only or no app / package code change

## Tests

- No unit test applies to workflow YAML. Checked instead:
  - All 6 workflows and `dependabot.yml` validate against the SchemaStore JSON schemas (structure only; GitHub validates `dependabot.yml` itself once it is on `main`).
  - I dispatched `AI eval (nightly)` on this branch: [run 40079492114](https://github.com/KhubaibQaiser/fitness-app/actions/runs/40079492114) finished green with `Offline eval` passed and `Live eval (llama.cpp; needs secret AI_BASE_URL)` **skipped**. The three pinned actions in it (checkout, pnpm/action-setup, setup-node) resolved and ran.

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm format:check` (or formatted touched files)
- [ ] `pnpm lint`
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test` — scope: full workspace
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @gymos/web build` (if web / app / ui / platform touched)
- [ ] `./scripts/eval-agent-diff.sh` (if agent-eval task or harness-relevant change)

Only workflow and Dependabot YAML changed, so I formatted and schema-checked those files and did not re-run lint, typecheck or tests.

**CI on this PR is red for a reason outside this change.** The `Audit production dependencies` step (`pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high`) now fails on `main`'s dependency tree: new advisories since the last green run on 2026-09-13 (Next.js, zod, sharp and others, 5 critical and 16 high). Every other step in that job passes. [#67](https://github.com/KhubaibQaiser/fitness-app/pull/67) fixes the audit.

## Rollout & rollback

- Deploy order / migration notes: none. Merge #67 first, then press "Update branch" here so CI re-runs. After merging, check **Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot** to confirm the first run reads the workspace packages.
- Rollback: `git revert` this PR.

## Out of scope / deferred

- Pinning `eas-version: latest` in the Expo workflows, moving Docker base images to digests, and verifying the checksum of the gitleaks binary that `ci.yml` downloads.
- Branch protection and security settings (done separately through the GitHub API).

## Review notes

- The Expo ignore list in `dependabot.yml` is a judgment call; delete it if you prefer to review every Expo bump.
- Dependabot's handling of pnpm 10 settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`overrides`, `onlyBuiltDependencies`) is not documented; the first Dependabot PR will show whether it works.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open Actions → "AI eval (nightly)" → Run workflow: the live step shows as skipped while `AI_BASE_URL` is unset.
- [ ] After merge, open Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot and confirm `npm` and `github-actions` are listed without errors.

author: david-tejada
body:
Fixes #708.

On a page without a `<title>`, like the Talon changelog, the browser shows a fallback in the tab, usually the URL. When Rango decorated an inactive tab, it replaced that fallback and left only "A | ".

## What changed

- A new `getTabTitle` message lets the content script ask the background for the tab's title, which is the browser's fallback when the document has none. Rango puts that between the decorations, and uses the URL without its scheme when the browser doesn't give one. This also covers PDFs in Chrome, where the tab shows the file name.
- When the tab becomes current, the title goes back to empty, so the browser shows its own fallback as before.
- Once a tab is decorated, its title is our own output. So I reuse the fallback while the URL stays the same, and rebuild it from the URL when it changes (hash links, `pushState`).
- If the page sets its own title while we wait for the background, we leave it alone and decorate it on the next update.
- A failed message falls back to the URL instead of stopping the content script from initializing.
- A page that starts untitled and sets a title later now gets decorated. Every title includes an empty one, so the Bandcamp-style check for pages editing their own title no longer counts an empty previous title. And the title is only cleared on becoming the current tab while it's still the one we set.

## Testing

I added three e2e tests to `e2e/decorateTitle.test.ts`, using a new `untitled.html` page:

- an untitled tab shows the fallback while inactive and goes back to empty when current
- the fallback follows a URL change
- a title the page sets later gets decorated

All seven title tests pass locally once the expected tab marker is `C`. The four existing tests already fail on `main` in my environment, because the test browser gives the page marker `C` instead of `B`, so that isn't caused by this change. I only tested in Chrome, not Firefox or Safari.

body:
## Summary

The T8 spike had one live agent table while orchestration state remained process-local. This adds the full §4.7 schema and an environment-selected `SpacetimeStateStore`, sharing deterministic transition/audit logic with memory.

```text
workers / approvals / gateway audit
  → StateStore (memory | spacetime)
  → atomic reducers + policy + append-only SHA-256 chain
  → agent / room / escalation / audit_entry subscriptions
```

Includes database-time leases and fencing, persisted payment receipts, current-vendor policy checks, passkey-bound approvals/bank changes, policy-bound plans/links, fixture ingress, immutable owner policy versions, cross-client LLM OFF fencing, and one generated client shared with the web app. Memory stays the unit-test default.

Closes #15.

## Evidence

- **Before:** full-state reducer test failed with `set_llm_enabled is not a function`; T8 only covered the agent/room spike.
  **After:** Workspace tests (including the latest 79-test web suite) and 84 existing adapter contract tests pass; workspace build/typecheck and script/harness typecheck pass.
- `SPACETIME_LIVE=1 pnpm state:live`: real local 2.13.0 server publish, idempotent company seed, anonymous office subscriptions (4 ms maximum local callback latency), cross-client OFF/ON, reconnect reads, anonymous write rejection, and fail-closed disconnect pass.
- The actual `STATE_STORE=spacetime pnpm demo:core` passes collection, ON/OFF bank-change traps, and frozen Northfield AP. All 31 collection audit bodies equal memory replay modulo timestamps and derived hashes; both original chains verify.
- Table/reducer/setup contract: `spacetime/README.md`. Evidence and limits: `docs/spacetime-state.md`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Use a fresh local database for this schema expansion, or plan migration before replacing an existing database. Writer tokens remain server-only; browsers get read-only public projections.

**Blast Radius:** state

Maincloud still needs browser authentication (the T8 attempt returned 401). Complete gateway call/outbox, voice, and FinanceRepository bindings remain separate integration work; their explicit memory/local adapters do not become durable merely by selecting a StateStore. External calls in the proof remain labeled fakes.

author: v0lumehi
body:
Switch games render 16:9 and current iPhones are about 19.5:9, so the picture is pillarboxed (#93). This PR adds a general way for a game to render at the screen's aspect and turns it on for Hades.

**How it's general.** A stub in a profile's `patches.py` can replace the game's output size with the host's. The stub names itself in `main`'s rewriter table (`OUTPUT_W` / `OUTPUT_H`), and the loader writes the size (`DM_OUTPUT_SIZE`, or the screen's aspect) into the state page only for such a build. A profile with `aspect any` then gets width = height × the screen's aspect, rounded to a multiple of 8 and never narrower than 16:9 (1568x720 on an iPhone 17 Pro Max). The iOS game view covers the whole screen, and touches map onto the same canvas. Only the profile key and the rewriter table decide; the host knows no game. The launcher's Picture switch (Wide / 16:9) turns it back. Other games' `main` rewrite byte-identically.

**Hades.** A stub replaces its fixed 1280x720 window size. At a wider output the game uses its own ultrawide layout, as on PC: the 16:9 view and HUD stay in the middle, and its side-bar art fills both sides. There are no black bars, no crop and no stretch. A truly wider view would need the game's UI scripts and layouts changed as well; that would be a separate PR.

**Checked:**
- An iPhone 17 Pro Max ran a build of the same changes on top of #76. Hades filled the screen edge to edge, with the side-bar art at the sides.
- On the Mac at 1568x720: the title, the save choice and the House of Hades.
- The `main` of Breath of the Wild 1.9.0, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe 4.0.0 and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate 13.0.5 rewrites byte-identically to main.
- The host unit tests pass, and the Mac host and the iOS app build.

**Not checked:** Tears of the Kingdom, Age of Calamity and Paper Mario (no NSPs here), an iPad, and a room of a run.

**Relation to #76.** The output-size part comes out of #76 (Breath of the Wild above 60 fps), with the same form and names. #76 needs it and will rebase onto this.

author: thymikee
body:
## What

`network dump` on a hosted provider reported success it had not earned.

The WebDriver provider runtime implemented `networkDump` by scanning the session app log for HTTP
request lines. A hosted provider owns the network path for its session, and the app writes those
lines only when it chooses to, so the scan answered an empty dump. A caller reads that as "the app
made no requests" when the truth is "this runtime has nothing to read".

This PR makes the refusal explicit and typed, and puts the typed reason on the wire. Nothing else
changes.

## How

- `RuntimeOperationUnavailability['reason']` gains `network-capture-post-session`: a hosted provider
  delivers traffic evidence only as a report finalized after its own session ends, so a live dump has
  no source.
- The WebDriver provider runtime drops the app-log scan and declares `network` unavailable with that
  reason at bind time, so the operation is never admitted (ADR 0019 §2: no stubs that throw after
  binding). This covers BrowserStack, AWS Device Farm, and TestMu AI, which share this runtime. Limrun
  is unaffected and keeps live capture.
- The hint points at the provider dashboard, where a provider publishes a traffic report when it
  records one at all.
- `handleNetworkCommand` reports the refusal through `unsupportedOperationResponse` from
  `core/runtime-admission.ts`, the one shared wire shape every runtime-admission refusal already
  uses, so `details.reason` reaches the caller. Its hand-built response helper dropped the reason and
  left the hint text as the only discriminator.

## Live proof

One short BrowserStack session (Google Pixel 8, Android 14.0, `com.callstack.agentdevicelab`), then
`network dump`:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION",
    "message": "network is not supported on this device",
    "hint": "The provider publishes any network capture only after its session ends, on the provider dashboard.",
    "diagnosticId": "mvnmz1hg-8784bf9e",
    "details": {
      "reason": "network-capture-post-session"
    }
  }
}
```

`details.reason` and the hint are both on the wire. The session ended and is gone: `disconnect`
returned its video and log URLs, and BrowserStack reports it `status: "done"` with
`reason: "CLIENT_STOPPED_SESSION"` (session `dcad99ef7fc20b17fb5b10e5afd3cd3a237ef64e`). Nothing is
left running and `session list` is empty.

## Deliberately not here

Fetching that post-session report is its own design question, so this PR carries no new flag, no
provider capability row, no artifact kind, and no post-session fetch. One candidate design for that
sits on the parked branch `feat/provider-network-har` (unopened, stacked on this head) so the decision
does not start from scratch. This PR stands without it: the refusal is right whether or not we ever
fetch the report.

## Tests

- `session-network-runtime-parity.test.ts` pins `details: { reason }` on the refusal the route already
  returned, so a lost reason fails the parity test.
- One new case takes a `network-capture-post-session` fact through `handleSessionCommands` under a
  BrowserStack provider owner and asserts `error.details.reason`, with `operations.networkDump` never
  called. Its runtime stub answers the empty `app-log` dump the removed scan produced, so the case
  fails if the refusal ever stops winning. Reverting the handler to a hand-built response makes both
  the new case and the existing one fail, so neither is vacuous.
- One new test: a provider with no capture of its own states the same refusal, so the wording is not
  written per provider. It runs under AWS's own provider id and device, not BrowserStack's.
- One test removed: it proved the app-log scan's entry cap, which no longer exists here.

## Docs

- `debugging-profiling.md`: what a provider session's `network dump` answers and where traffic
  evidence lives instead, naming the three providers that refuse and noting Limrun keeps the
  operation.
- `device-clouds.md`: the comparison table now states live `network dump` support per provider.

## Verification

- `pnpm check:affected --run --head 0d088d0d60` — all runnable checks passed, `exactCommit=true`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit-core` — 15,979 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project provider-integration` — 214 passed.
- `npx tsc -b` clean.
- The live BrowserStack run above.

## Size

7 files, +96 / −116.

body:
## Project Overview

- **Project Name:** video-analysis-agent
- **Category:** `agents/video-analysis-agent`
- **Frameworks & Technologies Used:** Python, FFmpeg, faster-whisper (open-source Whisper), Pydantic v2, Gemini / OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic APIs

### Description
A terminal-only agent that turns a video (MP4, MOV, and others) into a structured, evidence-backed report. It extracts the audio with FFmpeg, transcribes it locally with Whisper, and has an LLM extract a summary, confirmed decisions, proposals (not agreed), action items with owners and deadlines, key facts, and open questions, each with a timestamp.

The problem: LLM meeting summaries often invent decisions, owners, or deadlines. Here, every item must carry a verbatim transcript quote. A Pydantic-based validator drops anything the transcript doesn't support, and removes owners and deadlines that aren't stated near the quote. Reports are exported as Markdown and JSON.

Highlights:
- Bring your own LLM key via an environment variable, a `.env` file, or a hidden prompt. The key is never logged or saved.
- Handles long recordings (chunked analysis), low-confidence transcription (flagged), unsupported or corrupt files, and API failures (retries; the transcript is saved so analysis can be re-run alone).
- Optional audio cleanup: `--denoise` and `--separate-vocals`. Both are off by default.

---

## Contribution Checklist

- [x] **Directory & Naming:** The project is contained in its own folder under `agents/video-analysis-agent/` using lowercase kebab-case.
- [x] **Documentation:** A complete `README.md` based on `template/README.md` is present in the project folder with all relevant sections completed.
- [x] **Reproducible Setup:** Setup and installation instructions were verified from scratch in a clean environment.
- [x] **Core Functionality Tested:** The agent was executed and confirmed to work as described.
- [x] **Example Usage:** Realistic input and output examples are provided in the project documentation.
- [x] **Dependencies Declared:** All external dependencies are tracked in `requirements.txt`; FFmpeg is documented as a system prerequisite.
- [x] **Secrets & Security:** No API keys, credentials, tokens, local `.env` files, or personal data are included in this PR. A `.env.example` is provided.
- [x] **Scope Limitation:** Changes are confined to `agents/video-analysis-agent/` plus one row in the `agents/README.md` index.

---

## Testing & Verification Notes

- **Environment:** Windows 11, Python 3.12, FFmpeg 9.0, fresh virtualenv with `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
