author: m-agahi
body:
> **MERGE BLOCKED UNTIL** Max grants **Contents: read** to the `yadgarhq-settled-dispatch` App installation on `argocd-verify`. `find_verdict` now reads `branches/<default>` and `compare/...` on the PRIVATE `argocd-verify`. The App's installation grant today (ADR-0912) is metadata read plus actions read/write. `actions/create-github-app-token` fails when it is asked to mint a permission the installation lacks, so without the grant `settled-dispatch` goes red on every push to main. The ADR-0912 amendment is filed by the orchestrator, not in this PR.
>
> **CI-invisible risk:** the test fakes answer whatever the permission is, and the `settled-dispatch` workflow does not run on this PR. CI green here says nothing about the grant.

## What

`find_verdict` and `reachable` in `scripts/settled_gate.py` no longer trust a branch NAME. `find_verdict` also requires the run's `head_sha` to be the default branch head or an ancestor of it. `reachable` compares each branch's head sha from the branch listing, not the bare name. Both mint steps in `settled-dispatch.yaml` gain `permission-contents: read` for the new reads. A default-branch answer with no full sha is an `InfrastructureError` (exit 3).

Closes yaadgaar #165 and #206 only in the narrowed sense under Risk.

## Why

A tag named `main` reports `head_branch == "main"`, so a run on that tag passed the default-branch filter in `find_verdict`. In `reachable`, `compare/main...<sha>` resolves a tag `refs/tags/main` before the branch. Either path lets a verdict or a sha from outside the default branch pass the settled gate. Settled-dispatch and auto-merge depend on this gate. The CLI interface and the return shapes are unchanged.

## Changelog

- fix: the settled gate rejects a verdict run or a sha that reaches the default branch only by a tag of the same name

## Verification

Red first: tests for a tag-`main` run (`test_find_verdict_rejects_a_run_on_a_tag_named_like_the_default_branch`, `..._only_a_tag_run_names_the_epoch`, `..._without_a_full_head_sha`, `..._compares_shas_never_names`) and `test_a_tag_named_like_a_branch_cannot_make_a_sha_reachable` failed before the change. Mutant M10 (drop the full-sha check on the branch answer) is killed by `test_find_verdict_refuses_a_default_branch_answer_without_a_full_sha` (4 cases) and the CLI exit-3 test; I saw them fail with the check removed. `python -m pytest scripts/tests` passes and pre-commit passes. The `settled_dispatch` fake gains the branch-head and compare answers the new check reads. The permission grant is NOT verified by any test.

## Risk

- **Narrowed, not closed.** The check proves ANCESTRY, not the ref type. A tag named `main` that points at an ancestor of `main` still passes. #165 is narrowed, not closed.
- **Slot use (fails closed).** Rejected tag runs still take `MAX_VERDICT_CANDIDATES` slots, so enough tag runs can crowd real verdicts out. The gate then finds no verdict and re-runs. That is a denial of service, not a bypass. Moving the ancestry filter before the slice needs one run read plus one compare per artifact, unbounded, so I did not.
- A verdict run whose sha is not on the default branch (rewritten history) is now ignored. Cost: one extra branch read and one compare per candidate. Undo: revert this commit.

author: m-agahi
body:
## What

The `release:` job now passes `RELEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` and `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, by name, to `ci-release.yaml`. `ci-release.yaml`'s new `argocd-pin-nudge` job uses them to send `chart-published` to `yadgarhq/argocd` (car C7 of `plans/auto-deploy-parent-chart.md`).

**Merge order: yadgarhq/actions#126 first (it adds the `argocd-pin-nudge` job), then this PR.** If this PR merged first, the secrets would reach a release that has no job to use them. `parent` skips here, and `examples` reads no secret, so no harm follows, but nothing is nudged.

## Why

ADR-1004 approves NEEDS-MAX item 5, this wiring. With the wiring, each parent chart version starts argocd's auto-pin in seconds. Without it, the version waits for argocd's auto-pin schedule, which runs every 15 minutes (ADR-0946, ADR-0948 R3-a).

## Changelog

- ci: pass the release App secrets to the release job so the argocd pin nudge can dispatch chart-published to yadgarhq/argocd

## Verification

- Red first: `test_the_release_job_passes_the_release_app_for_the_argocd_nudge` in `scripts/tests/test_parent_chart.py` failed before the edit and passes after it. The test asserts exactly the two named secrets and no `inherit`.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes after `helm dependency update chart`: actionlint, helm lint and render, and the full pytest suite.
- `zizmor 1.29.0 --persona=regular` with the ci-pr policy reports no findings.
- CI does not cover the live dispatch. The first proof is the next `v*` tag after both merges: the `release / argocd-pin-nudge` job log and its summary line `nudged argocd: chart-published <v>`.

## Risk

A failed nudge warns, and the release stays green. To undo, revert this PR. The release run then gets no key, and the job warns.

Exposure: the org release App key now reaches the chart tag run as well as the `main` push run. Measured: the `release-tags` ruleset (`refs/tags/v*`; creation, update and deletion) has only the release App as bypass actor. The `main` ruleset requires a pull request and `ci / passed`. So only commits on `main` that were reviewed or App-written get a tag that runs with the key. No new principal gets the key; the change adds one more trigger path.

author: psaab
body:
Closes #16134.

## Why
The three string protocol carriers (filter `Protocols []string`, app `Protocol string`, DNAT `Protocol string`) cannot be retyped to `u8` until (a) atomic `__unsupported__` poison preservation, (b) a `ProtocolVersion` bump with rolling mixed-version refusal, and (c) per-carrier protocol-0 semantics are proven. Converting first would strand the poison channel (fail-open) and old helpers under an unchanged version. This PR files the validation cells only — no carrier is retyped, no Rust mirror table is deleted.

## What
- Go cells (`protocol_carrier_validation_16134_test.go`): every poison path (unrepresentable term, partial-drop DENY, lenient-dropped, undefined-scheduler DENY/REJECT + PERMIT control) atomically carries the sentinel alone, on the wire, named by the mirror, keep-armed; both mixed-version orders refused through the required-protocol orchestrator before apply; HOPOPT `"0"` vs unknown vs empty per carrier; Junos aliases.
- Rust cells pin the mirror halves (whole-snapshot reject, scoped filter HOPOPT, DNAT exact-vs-wildcard, both version orders already in `main_tests.rs`).
- Defect found while validating, fixed: Rust `proto_number`/`parse_protocol` accepted non-canonical numerics (`+6`) the Go SSOT rejects — commit/apply drift on a security leaf. `proto_number` is now digit-only; `parse_protocol` delegates to it (also closing missing Junos aliases). `"0"` still `Some(0)`; unknown stays `None`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestCarrier...` PASS
- `cargo test carrier_16134` 4/4 PASS; `proto_number`/`protocol_`/`named_protocol`/`unrepresentable` neighbours PASS

## Risk
Production change confined to rejecting previously-accepted non-canonical protocol tokens in Rust snapshot resolvers — fail-closed only; every token Go builders emit resolves identically.

Main agent: run full Go package + full Rust bin suites before merge.

author: jan-kubica
body:
Copy breaks a sentence with a period, comma, colon or parentheses instead of an em dash, in every language.

**Rule.** `no-em-dash-copy/no-em-dash-copy` reports an em dash written into string literals, template text and JSX text, plus `—` and its numeric entities in JSX. It covers shipped source in `apps/*/src` and `packages/*/src`, excluding tests, fixtures and generated files. Comments are not copy and are not checked.

**Data, not copy.** Code that handles the character as data (citation parsers, normalizers) writes the `—` escape or uses a regular expression, which the rule allows.

**Empty-cell marker.** A value that is only the glyph stays allowed. Tables and cells render it for a missing value; it is a placeholder, not punctuation.

**Catalogues.** oxlint does not read JSON, so `i18n-lint` applies the same check to the web and landing catalogues, and the desktop catalogue test applies it to the desktop catalogues. Every catalogue is rewritten with the punctuation each language uses: French keeps its space before colons and semicolons, and Arabic uses its own comma and semicolon.

**Two reasoned disables.** The case-law search titles in `case-law-search-index.ts` and `corpus-index-projection-descriptor.ts` keep their format. They are stored in search projections, and changing them would re-project the corpus, which belongs in its own change.

Prompts, tool descriptions, error messages and UI strings follow the same rule. The CLI help text, the generated agent skill and the affected capability description are regenerated from their sources.

author: kekko7072
body:
## Problem
`firmware_contract.yml` checked `cli/` and `harness/` out **sparse** in the `targets` and `report` jobs, and **full** in the `contract` job, all into the same folders of the persistent self-hosted workspace. `actions/checkout` makes a sparse checkout a blobless partial clone, and a later full checkout into that folder reports success with only the sparse paths on disk. The same mechanism broke cloud-rules on `linux-3` (`deploy.sh` / `tests/` missing).

Nothing cleaned the workspace after a job either, including the Windows build leg.

## Change
- `targets` / `report`: `cli/` and `harness/` are full checkouts (2.8 MB and 38 MB trees; usually an incremental fetch on a reused workspace).
- `targets`, `contract`, `report` first drop a sparse clone an older run left in `cli/` or `harness/`, so the first runs after this change cannot hit it.
- Every self-hosted job (build matrix incl. Windows, `fwu-e2e`, `release`, the three contract jobs) ends with an inline **Clean the workspace** step (`if: always()`, skipped on GitHub-hosted runners): each checkout's `.git` and tracked files stay, everything else (build output, `node_modules`, downloaded trees, loose files) goes. `core.longpaths` for Windows. Never fails the job.

Inline because this repository is public and cannot use the private `firmware-workflows` actions the firmware repos now share.

## Verification
- `actionlint` clean; `node scripts/check-workflows.js`: no fork-controllable triggers on self-hosted runners.
- This branch's push runs `firmware_contract.yml` end to end.

body:
## Summary

CA3, the full scope in one PR:

1. **Dividend importer** (`data/ca_dividends.py`). Loads equity dividends from 2011-01-01 out of NSE's corporate-actions feed. Each is stored in `hat_corporate_action` as a `dividend` row with factor 1, with the rupees per share in the new column `cash_amount NUMERIC` (model + `PG_DDL`).
   - Each row records its kind (interim/final/special), parsed per clause of the purpose text.
   - Unclear texts go to review and are never guessed: percent of face value, no amount, amounts that disagree, cash above 50% of the previous close.
   - Dry run by default; `--apply` writes in one transaction, journalled as `corporate_action.imported`. A rerun stores nothing.
   - A stored dividend with no amount gets the amount filled in. A different stored amount is a conflict and is never rewritten.
2. **Total-return series for signals** (`data/store.py`, `data/lineage.py`, `data/features.py`).
   - `bars_daily`/`bars_daily_adj` are now the total-return series: the price factors times `1 - D / previous raw close` for every dividend.
   - `bars_daily_cap`/`bars_daily_cap_adj` are the price basis. Both views carry `div_factor`.
   - All dividends are included, with no threshold: each is cash a holder receives, and leaving small ones out biases returns down.
   - Level features (SMAs, 52-week high/low, ADTR) are stored point in time, on their own date's scale, so a later dividend never changes a stored row. The features' inputs digest covers the dividends.
3. **Backtest P&L** (`backtest/data.py`, `backtest/loop.py`).
   - Bars are read from the price basis; fills, marks, ticks and circuit bands use it.
   - Every signal read (the scan window, SMA, swing low, ATR) is the total-return series rescaled to the day it is read for.
   - A position open at the start of an ex-date session gets `qty_open x D` (D per price-basis share) credited to cash that day; a buy on the ex-date earns nothing.
   - No double counting: the ex-date drop is in the price, and the cash is credited once. New metrics `dividend_income` and `dividend_credits`; the dividends are part of `content_digest`.
   - Live: there is no paper cash ledger (shadow equity is capital plus realised P&L), so nothing is credited live. Noted as a follow-up.
4. **Bonus debentures/NCRPS** (research file f).
   - Stored as a dividend of `value_per_share` when it is ≥ 1% of the previous close. Below 1% it stays price-neutral (D1); BRITANNIA 2021 is 0.85%, skipped.
   - The ex-date is NSE's own ex-date for the company's non-equity bonus from the feed (within −7/+3 days of the research date). It is checked against the bars' gap, with the close as a second witness because the open can lag (SUNDARAM-CLAYTON 2023: open 0.92, close 0.80, expected 0.76).
   - Without an NSE date, it must be whichever one of the research date and the session before it the bars confirm.
   - MBLIMITED (non-promoters only) → review. Low confidence → review.
   - Live order behaviour is unchanged: the rescale and GTT check read only price-changing types.

## Verification (real data, no backtest per owner rule)

Scratch copy of hat_live (`hat_ca3_scratch`), with `HAT_DATA_ROOT` a hard-link copy of hat-data-isin (build state and `features_daily` copied). Both were dropped and removed after.

feed                    19413         0         0        85       468    19966
bonus_research              8         0         0         1         2       11
rows to write: dividend 19420, amounts added 0
reasons feed: review/amount_vs_price 4, review/no_amount 20, review/no_bars 56, review/percent_of_face_value 1, review/rows_disagree 3, review/several_amounts 1, skipped/before_bars 252, skipped/not_equity_share 216

Stored rows by source/type, with the count that has a `cash_amount`: `nse_ca_feed|dividend|19413|19413` and `ca_research|dividend|7|7`. The 8 bonus rows include 1 merged into a feed dividend of the same day: COROMANDEL 2012-07-13. Events: `corporate_action.imported|engine|nse_ca_feed|19420`.

body:
Remaining slices of spec #1437 (former employees). #1438 and #1439 already merged (#1446, #1447).

Closes #1437
Closes #1440
Closes #1441
Closes #1442

## Summary

*Deactivate* now has the same consequences as a departure (Organization ADR 0006). *Reactivate* restores nothing and offers a re-grant checklist. A one-off script backfills employees deactivated before this change.

```text
deactivateEmployeeAction({ employeeId, requestId, replacementManagers })
  readDeactivationByRequest            # same request → replay stored result
  withAuthorizationMutation
    beforeProtection: absence + period-submission write gates, org configuration guard (exclusive)
    user guards: person, reports, own managers, chosen replacements
    lockLifecycleOrganization
    planDeactivationConsequences       # same code the preview runs
    refuse when a report with no current manager has no eligible replacement
    UPDATE employee SET is_active = false, deactivated_at = <at>
    insertDeactivation                 # employee_deactivation ledger row
    applyDeactivationConsequences
      manager links    → end both directions; replacement for reports with no current manager; former reports just lose the link
      team links       → team memberships, project assignments, project manager links end   (user decision)
      approval duties  → handover tasks to the replacement / re-resolved stage / review; audited
      shifts           → after <at>: open shifts; one planner notice
      absences         → starting after <at>: cancelled via the normal path (allowance restored); spanning and closed-month ones kept and listed
      access ends      → expense officer, payroll, personnel file officer, verifier grants; driving authorizations; kiosk badges; share links
    recordDeactivationOutcome (applied + plan snapshot), history event employee_deactivated
  after commit: audit forward, planner notice, sessions, seat reconcile, export pause, deputy notices
```

```text
src/lib/employee-lifecycle/
├── deactivation/      # types, plan, apply, preview, command + one module per area, backfill
├── receipts.ts        # request fingerprints, receipts, employee_deactivation ledger
├── reactivation.ts    # restores nothing, closes follow-up, history event
├── reactivation-checklist*.ts, lifecycle-history.ts
scripts/backfill-former-employees.ts   # dry run by default, --apply
```

- **Preview:** the *Deactivate* dialog lists every consequence, with a replacement-manager picker per report that would have no current manager. The server recomputes on submit; a test compares the preview with what was applied.
- **Approval handover** reuses the departure's pipeline, anchored on the deactivation. Deactivation tasks are delivered while the offboarding release gate stays closed; departure tasks stay gated.
- **Retention:** a deactivated employee's documents count from `deactivated_at`; reactivation stops the clock.
- **Reactivation:** clears the left-on instant, closes the deactivation's open follow-up, writes *Reactivated on …* in the employment history, and shows a checklist (dialog + employee-page card until dismissed) of what was ended, each linking to where it's granted again.
- **Backfill:** recovers *Former since* from surviving audit entries (else "date not recorded"), applies the consequences only from the run instant on (user decision), keeps manager links of reports with no current manager, and sends admins one notice each.

### Migrations

- `0284_employee_deactivation_shifts_opened`: notification type `employee_deactivation_shifts_opened`
- `0285_employee_deactivation`: `employee_deactivation` ledger; `deactivation_id` on departure tasks/reviews; event kinds `employee_deactivated` / `employee_reactivated`
- `0286_employee_deactivation_checklist`: `plan`, `checklist_dismissed_at/by`
- `0287_former_employee_reports_without_manager`: notification type

### Decisions

User (2026-10-24): deactivation also ends team memberships, project assignments and project manager links; the backfill opens shifts and cancels absences only from the run instant on. Earlier user decisions are in the spec. Notable implementation choices:

- One `employee_deactivation` row per deactivation is the request-ID replay ledger, the checklist source and the backfill's idempotency marker.
- When a requester has no chosen replacement, the stage is re-resolved without the person; if nobody remains, a *no replacement* review is raised.
- Kiosk badge and share-link column reasons are unchanged (`revoked`, `creator_lost_access`); `employee_deactivated` is in the audit metadata.
- The approval write-boundary scanner's production file cap went from 4096 to 8192 (the new modules pushed the scan past it).

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- One anchor module to replace the repeated departure/deactivation branches in handover, notifications and authority.
- Move `absences/cancel-absence-core.ts` from `app/` to `lib/absences`.
- Pending shift requests on opened shifts and document requests are left as they are at deactivation.

## Evidence

- **Before:** deactivating an employee left their manager links, team and project links, future shifts and absences, grants, badges, share links and pending approval duties in place; their documents never became due.
- **After:** `deactivation/deactivation.integration.test.ts` (action level) deactivates a manager of two reports who holds every grant type, a suspended driving authorization, a kiosk badge, pending duties, past/running/future shifts, spanning/future absences and a share link, and asserts each consequence and its audit row, the refusals, preview == applied, and a replayed request changing nothing. Reactivation and backfill scenarios live in the same suite and `backfill.integration.test.ts` (dry run, real run, no-op second run, two organizations). `jobs/employee-departures.integration.test.ts` delivers a deactivation handover with the gate closed.
- Final run on the integration branch (c232d138b): typecheck passes; PostgreSQL 179 suites / 2168 tests pass on a fresh database (employee-lifecycle, approvals, absences, departure jobs, driving licence, kiosk, report share, personnel-file retention, billing seats, roster, settings/employees, migration schema); unit project 19285 pass, 6 load timeouts in `native-source-analysis`, `event-append-only-typescript` and `rollout-script` that pass alone.

Not run: signed-in browser QA (en + de) of the dialog, checklist, history and offboarding card, and the Tolgee sync. The new keys (namespaces `settings/people` and `common`, English + German) are listed in the orchestration notes for the sync.

## Deploy notes

1. Deploy (migrations through 0287); webapp and worker run the new code.
2. **Dry run on production** from the worker image: `tsx --import ./src/worker-preload.mjs scripts/backfill-former-employees.ts --json > backfill-dry-run.json` (full command in `deploy/README.md` → "After Deploying #1440").
3. **Review it:** employees per organization, those with `leftAt: null`, `shiftsToOpen` / `absencesToCancel` (from the run instant on), closed-month absences listed as kept, `failed` entries, and `reportsWithoutManager` + the admins who'll be notified.
4. **Real run** with `--apply --json > backfill-applied.json`. A non-zero exit lists employees left unchanged; fix and re-run (processed employees are skipped). A second dry run should list nobody.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way

The migrations are additive, but deactivating after merge ends links, grants and absences, and the backfill applies the same to existing former employees. Reactivation restores nothing by design.

**Blast Radius:** wide

Deactivate, Reactivate, the employee page's offboarding card and employment history, approval handover and stage resolution, absence cancellation, retention due lists, notification registries. Departure behaviour is unchanged and its suites pass.

body:
## 무엇을

- `krpatch nds info|ls|unpack|pack` (`kr_patch.nds.rom`): DS 롬 헤더·FNT·FAT·오버레이 표 읽기, 파일시스템 풀기, 바뀐 파일만 넣어 다시 묶기
- `krpatch lz11 decode|encode` (`kr_patch.lz11`): 닌텐도 LZ10/LZ11 코덱(결정적 탐욕 인코더, `--vram`)
- `krpatch xdelta make|apply` (`kr_patch.vcdiff`): `xdelta3` 로 패치 만들기(2차 압축·파일 이름 없음), 순수 Python VCDIFF 디코더(창마다 Adler-32 확인)
- `krpatch linear` (`kr_patch.linear`): 선형 1/2/4/8bpp 비트맵 렌더링
- CI 에 `xdelta3` 설치(make 테스트용)
- README·CHANGELOG 영·한

## 왜

NDS 한글패치(고스트 트릭)를 이 툴킷으로 빌드하기 위해서다. 롬이 128 MiB 라 IPS 를 쓸 수 없고, 스크립트는 LZ11, 폰트는 선형 비트맵이다.

## 다시 묶기 규칙

- 들어가면 제자리(남는 곳은 뒤 바이트에 따라 0xFF/0x00), 안 들어가거나 다른 FAT 항목과 바이트를 나눠 쓰면 끝으로 0x200 정렬해 옮긴다. 바뀌지 않은 파일의 오프셋이 그대로라 패치가 작다.
- 마지막 파일 뒤의 채움이 아닌 데이터(다운로드 플레이 서명)는 덮어쓰지 않는다.
- 오버레이 표는 고치지 않으므로 오버레이는 같은 크기로만 바꿀 수 있다. DSi 확장 롬은 거부한다.
- 아무것도 바꾸지 않으면 원본과 같은 바이트가 나온다. 헤더 사용 크기가 실제보다 작게 남은 롬도 그대로 둔다.

## 검증

- `uv run pytest -q`: 229 passed, 1 skipped(비 macOS 경로용 기존 테스트)
- `uv run ruff check .`: 통과
- 로컬 실물 확인(롬은 커밋하지 않음)
  - 일본판 128 MiB 롬 + 배포된 한글패치 v1.1 xdelta → `xdelta apply` 결과가 `xdelta3 -d` 결과와 SHA-1 이 같다
  - 일본판·한글판 롬 모두 `nds unpack` → `nds pack`(변경 없음)이 원본과 바이트 단위로 같다
  - 스크립트 하나를 LZ11 로 다시 압축해 `pack` → `xdelta make` → `xdelta apply` 왕복이 같은 롬을 낸다
- 별도 리뷰에서 나온 지적(공유 FAT 덮어쓰기, 서명 덮어쓰기, 오버레이 표, DSi, 경로 탈출, xdelta3 오류 메시지, VCDIFF 틀 검사 등)을 반영하고 회귀 테스트를 더했다.

author: edanisko-xarabot[bot]
body:
Built Story 2.2 (stale takeover): builders now take over stale claimed and builder-held merging records, parking at the attempts cap, and parked records never expire.

Story 2.2 makes a unit whose lane died claimable again 30 minutes after its last heartbeat (FR3, AR7, AR10, AR16). The spec is _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-2-2-stale-takeover.md.

- `next` (src/core/next/next.ts) gains `NextStory.take_over`.
  - A `claimed` record, or a `merging` record held by a builder, is eligible once `heartbeat_at` is 30 min or more before the snapshot's `now`. The check is the shared, now exported `isStale`.
  - `parked` records and coordinator-held `merging` records never expire.
  - Every other eligibility rule still applies. An Infrastructure takeover whose approval does not match its manifest gets a `record-state` reason and is never parked.
- `takeOverStale` (src/core/ledger/edits.ts) gains `globs`, `adoptPr` and `baseSha`.
  - A `claimed` takeover behaves like a claim: the manifest's globs are re-resolved and checked for overlap, the claim's PR fields are set, and the review SHAs are cleared.
  - A `merging` takeover changes only `head_sha`, to the queue's head.
- Lane process (src/lane/lane-process.ts):
  - **Stale `claimed`:** it inspects the branch's PRs. A merged PR gets `markMerged` with no takeover. Otherwise it takes the record over at generation + 1 and attempts + 1, adopting the open PR at its head (fetched by `Workspace.prepare` before the session) or starting from main. The 3rd attempt parks it blocked attempts-cap instead.
  - **Stale `merging`:** the PR's `queueState` decides, through the pure `staleMergingAction` (src/core/lane/takeover.ts). Merged gets `markMerged`; still queued is taken over and watched; any other state gets `releaseStale` (attempts + 1, pr kept).
  - The heartbeat keeper starts only for a unit held `claimed` or `merging` after the takeover.
  - The sweep's `merged` records now reach `next`.
- Merge step (src/lane/merge-step.ts):
  - A `merging` input skips the gate, fence, `startMerging` and enqueue, and only watches the queue.
  - A queued head other than `passed_sha` fails the attempt (fence, dequeue, failAttempt). This guard was added in review.
- Small changes:
  - The unused `CiStepInput.specPath` is removed (src/lane/ci-step.ts).
  - `releaseHeld` (`stop --now`) now runs a fencing heartbeat swap before its dequeue (Story 2.1's deferral, src/lane/stop.ts).
- Tests: case tables for 29:59/30:00, each merging outcome, the cap, and the never-stale states. Lane-level cases against the fake forge cover every matrix row. There are also watch-only merge-step cases and a lost-fence `releaseHeld` case.

Review: 28 findings (high 0, medium 3, low 15, false 10). 4 patch entries were applied: the passed_sha guard, plus tests for the keeper, globs and queue head. Nothing was deferred, and 21 findings were rejected with their reasons logged in the spec.

Known limits:
- A stale record in a Story that is no longer eligible is not met until it becomes eligible again.
- Cross-owner close-and-reopen (AR10 v1) is not implemented; a takeover adopts the PR as today's claim does.

The changes are left uncommitted in the working tree for the runner.

body:
## Summary
Keeps the Mac, iBuyPower and DGX Spark busy with training, harvesting, translation, voice-data ingest and evaluation, without starving each other and without orphans or zombies.

- Durable per-machine SQLite queue (`aoep_shared/fleet_queue.py`): leases + heartbeats, retries with backoff, dedupe keys, per-resource caps (one GPU job per machine), windows in Pacific time (the Spark clock is UTC+8), priority preemption, deterministic sharding by site.
- Worker (`aoep_shared/fleet_worker.py`, `scripts/gs_worker.sh`, `scripts/fleet/queue.py`): every job runs through `gs_run.sh`; GPU jobs need the CUDA policy check (`devices.cuda_smoke`); memory-pressure shedding stops the lowest-priority preemptible job (SIGSTOP would not free RAM); only processes it started are ever signalled (pid + start time + `gsq-<id>-` name); every child is reaped.
- 7 job manifests (`scripts/fleet/jobs`). `harvest-crawl` refuses non-commercial licenses (exit 78) while the allowlist still contains `cc-by-nc` / `cc-by-nc-sa`.
- systemd: `gs-worker` (Type=notify, watchdog, bounded restarts, control-group kill), hourly revive timer, daily summary timer, `boot_check.sh`, installer with `--enable-worker`, `--disable-type`, `--uninstall`.
- `fleet_status`: queue section in the probe, WORKER_DOWN / QUEUE_STALE_LEASE / CUDA_BLOCKED / IDLE_WITH_WORK / QUEUE_DEAD_JOBS / QUEUE_SUMMARY findings. `daily_report.sh` + launchd plist for the Mac.
- `docs/ops-schedule.txt`: roles, 24 h calendar, priorities, reboot/power-loss behavior, per-machine install steps with verification and rollback.

## Test plan
- [x] 97 tests (queue, worker, ops, fleet_status): lease expiry, crash recovery with real child processes (identifies only its own runner, never a reused pid), caps, windows, preemption, memory pressure, CUDA gate, no zombies, CLI works with stdlib only (`python -S`), units/installer render, shard determinism, license guard.
- [x] End-to-end smoke on the Mac with a temp state dir: job ran through `gs_run`, license guard refused the crawl, no leftover processes.
- [ ] First real run on the iBuyPower, then the Spark (systemd-run limits, linger and the CUDA check have not run there).

…-Bytes auf 0xA2/0xA3 und füllt bei zu kurzer Quelle mit 0xA0 auf; der zweite CopyTo auf 0xA5 entfällt, so daß der von CreateBAM gesetzte DOS-Typ '2A' unberührt bleibt.

author: dilipna
body:
## Pull Request Description

The gateway re-exports every engine histogram it scrapes with `_p50`, `_p90` and `_p99` gauges (`EmitMetricToPrometheus`, called by the pod metrics worker in `pkg/cache/cache_metrics.go`), and the Envoy gateway plugins Grafana dashboard plots them.

When a histogram has no observations, `HistogramMetricValue.GetPercentile` returns the upper bound of the smallest bucket, with no error. Every bucket count is 0 and the target is 0, so the first bucket already satisfies `count >= target`. For a histogram with buckets `0.3, 0.5, 0.8, ...`, it reports p50 = p90 = p99 = 0.3. This is the case for every latency histogram of a pod that has not served a request yet, or whose engine has just restarted, and the gateway exports those values. A pod with no traffic therefore shows a latency nobody observed.

**Change**
- `GetPercentile` (`pkg/metrics/types.go`) returns an error when the histogram has no observations. A missing `Count` still falls back to the bucket counts, as before.
- `EmitMetricToPrometheus` (`pkg/metrics/custom_metrics.go`) deletes a percentile gauge whose value cannot be computed, instead of exporting it. Before this change, the error was ignored and the returned value exported. Deleting the series, rather than skipping the update, also clears the old value when an engine restarts and its counters return to 0.

**Tests**
- `TestHistogramPercentileWithoutObservations`: a histogram with no observations returns an error, and a missing count still uses the bucket counts.
- `TestEmitHistogramWithoutObservationsExportsNoQuantiles`: a pod with no observations gets no `_p50`/`_p90`/`_p99` series, and a pod that had observations loses them when its counters return to 0.
- Both tests fail on `main`. Reverting either half of the change makes a test fail again.
- `make test-race-condition` passes (76 packages, as on `main`). `go vet` and golangci-lint v2.13.1 report nothing on `pkg/metrics`.

#2569 plans a broader clean-up of these exported series (part 3). This change only stops exporting values that were never observed, and I'm happy to fold it into that work if you prefer.

## Related Issues

None filed; found while reading the metrics code.

(Found and drafted with an AI assistant, Claude Code. I reviewed the change and can explain it.)

author: meros
body:
`run.sh` copies the UEFI variables to `vars.fd` with `cp`, which keeps the mode of the source. When the source is read-only in its place, `vars.fd` is read-only too and QEMU cannot open it. Every file in the Nix store is mode 444, so this is what happens with `QEMU_VARS` set to a firmware file from nixpkgs:

```
qemu-system-aarch64: Could not open 'vars.fd': Permission denied
```

The change is `chmod u+w vars.fd` after the copy (two lines, one of them a comment). `chmod u+w` works the same on Linux and macOS; `cp --no-preserve=mode` would not.

**What I ran**, in an empty directory, with `QEMU_VARS` pointing at `share/qemu/edk2-arm-vars.fd` of nixpkgs' QEMU 11.1.1 (mode `r--r--r--`):

| | `vars.fd` after the `cp` line | QEMU opening it as the pflash |
|---|---|---|
| main | `r--r--r--` | `Could not open 'vars.fd': Permission denied` |
| this change | `rw-r--r--` | opens |

A writable source (the default path on a normal distribution) gives the same `rw-r--r--` as before, and a missing source still does nothing (the `2>/dev/null` case). `shellcheck` reports the same 3 findings on `run.sh` before and after.

<details><summary>Repro that does not start a VM</summary>

```sh
Q=$(nix build nixpkgs#qemu --no-link --print-out-paths)
mkdir /tmp/r && cd /tmp/r
export QEMU_VARS=$Q/share/qemu/edk2-arm-vars.fd
cp "$QEMU_VARS" vars.fd                       # what run.sh line 14 does
ls -l vars.fd                                 # -r--r--r--
printf 'quit\n' | $Q/bin/qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a76 -display none -S \
    -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=vars.fd -monitor stdio
# main: qemu-system-aarch64: Could not open 'vars.fd': Permission denied
chmod u+w vars.fd                             # the change; run the last command again: it opens
```
</details>

Not run: a full iOS boot with this change (the failure is at opening `vars.fd`, before the guest starts, and nothing else in `run.sh` changes). #6 also edits `run.sh`, a few lines below this one; I have not tried the two together.

body:
Stage537 builds the Stage536 CD-ROM queue-initialization candidate against the exact pinned PCSX-Redux commit. The patched binary has not yet been accepted; the original-game patched-vs-unpatched replay is a separate gate.

## Corrected unpatched baseline
The first expanded v2 matrix was superseded after discovering that `-testmode` enables safe mode and prevents PCSX-Redux from loading `pcsx.json`. The v3 runner removes that flag and verifies logging by actual output before accepting a run.

Eight v3 runs completed: neutral/RIGHT × `LoggingCDROM` off/on × two repeats, with 12 checkpoints per run (96 samples).
- Logging off: zero `CD-Rom:` debug lines in each run; inactive payload bytes 8–9 varied at all 12 checkpoints in every run.
- Logging on: 992 `CD-Rom:` debug lines in each run; bytes 8–9 were `2e00` at all 12 checkpoints in every run.
- Active DataReady response remained stable in 96/96 samples: cause 1, payload[0]=0x22, size 1, index 1.
- All initial VRAM buffers matched; neutral and RIGHT final VRAM matched the corresponding Stage535 baseline.
- Full 16-byte traces show variation in inactive `responseFifo0` payload bytes 1–15. They also show that `responseFifo1` is semantically inactive in all 96 samples, yet retains stale payload `2208000000000000371f180000000000` and stale value 1.
- A private full-state audit now checks both FIFO slots. The unpatched negative control fails as intended; no gameplay defect is inferred from stale serialized bytes alone.

## Candidate patch
The pinned-source patch initializes the full `QueueElement` payload/value and clears payload, value and `hitMax` when a queue slot is reused. The savestate schema serializes the full 16-byte payload. The patched runtime must prove:
1. `responseFifo0` active byte/metadata match the baseline and inactive bytes 1–15 are zero at every sample.
2. Inactive `responseFifo1` has all 16 payload bytes, value and queue metadata zero.
3. Logging on/off is verified by actual CD-ROM debug-line counts.
4. Initial/final raw VRAM matches the baseline.
5. Final savestates match byte-for-byte after narrowly canonicalizing only FIFO0 inactive payload bytes and FIFO1's known-inactive payload/value fields. Explicit checks above prevent normalization from hiding a bad queue state.
6. Repeat and logging-toggle final savestates match after canonicalization.

## Build and test status
- Corrected-head Disc analysis unit tests on the earlier build revision: SUCCESS — https://github.com/stanmasked/wild-arms-switch-remaster/actions/runs/40080568935
- Full PCSX-Redux compile, synthetic MIPS/OpenBIOS build, synthetic CD-ROM ISO smoke test and native tests passed in run 40080568946.
- AppImage packaging failed because the workflow runs under `/bin/sh` and used Bash-only short-SHA syntax. The command was corrected to POSIX `printf | cut -c 1-8`.
- Corrected full build rerun remains queued: https://github.com/stanmasked/wild-arms-switch-remaster/actions/runs/40083502327. No patched AppImage has been accepted yet.
- Synthetic QueueElement patch suite: 3/3 PASS locally. Private full-payload analyzer tests: 7/7 PASS.
- The patched runtime has not yet been tested against the original game.

The build workflow uses the pinned upstream source and maintained Noble build container. It does not include original Wild Arms BIN/CUE, savestates, raw VRAM, screenshots or private logs. The corrected v3 baseline, analyzer v3, unit tests and negative-control report are retained in owner-only Google Drive.

Keep this PR Draft until the corrected build succeeds, the artifact is independently verified, and the patched runtime passes the two-FIFO eight-run A/B gate.

author: bernd-als
body:
Three changes, on top of the sync commit (687c931).

## Group suggestions in the add/edit form

The Group field offers the groups that already exist:

- Typing shows the first matching group as faint text after the cursor; `←`/`→` step through the other matches.
- `tab`, `enter` and `^s` all take what the field shows, so the two ways forward never disagree.
- The line under the field lists the matching groups, or says `new group: …` when the name is none of them.
- The first `⌫` with an offer showing only dismisses it, so a new group that prefixes an old one (`cloud` beside `cloudflare`) can still be saved.

## Columns sized to the list

- The group column is as wide as the longest group, up to 20 characters, and gives way on a narrow window so names keep at least 12.
- The date follows the longest name instead of sitting at the right edge, and drops out below 48 columns (was 58).
- Sized over every listed item, not the visible rows, so the columns hold still while scrolling.

## `^s` after `^z` and `fg`

ncurses keeps its own copy of the terminal modes, taken before `IXON` is cleared, and restores it when `^z` is followed by `fg`. After a suspend, `^s` therefore froze the terminal as XOFF instead of saving. `run` now calls `curses.def_prog_mode()` once `IXON` is cleared.

## Tests

- `tests/test_units.py`: `group_matches` and `layout`.
- `tests/tui.py` §19: offer, `→` to the next group, `⌫` keeping a prefix group, "new group" hint.
- `tests/tui.py` §20: `^s` saves after `^z` and `fg`. The TUI runs as a job of an interactive `zsh -f -i`, since a pty session leader is never stopped by `^z`. This test fails on 687c931 and passes with the fix.

`test_units.py` and every `tui.py` check up to §20 pass, repeated runs, no flakes. The sync tests pass too: with `age` v1.3.2 from MacPorts and #2 merged on top (needed so the tests find a MacPorts `age`), `test_units.py` 17/17, `test_sync.py` 11/11 and `tui.py` 42/42. None of the sync code is touched.

README: the form's group field, the column sizing, and the `def_prog_mode` note under flow control.

body:
Auf dem Handy eines Testers wurde das Spiel in 1.1.0 im Endlos-Modus hineingezoomt angezeigt (rechts und unten abgeschnitten, Steuerknöpfe nicht sichtbar). Auf dem Emulator (Android 14/16, auch mit großer Systemschrift, Doppeltipps und Vollbild-Knopf) war es nicht reproduzierbar. Gefunden wurden aber Schwachstellen, die genau so einen Zoom ermöglichen.

**Gefunden (Emulator + WebView-DevTools via Playwright `_android`)**
- Die Seite war 2 px breiter als der Bildschirm (`scrollWidth 322` bei 320): Der Container wird per `transform` skaliert, seine Layoutbox bleibt aber 486 px breit. Nach dem Vollbild-Knopf war die Seite tatsächlich um 2 px gescrollt.
- Der Browser-Vollbild-Knopf schaltet in der App den Vollbildmodus der WebView um, obwohl die App schon im Vollbild läuft.
- Android 16 meldet beim Start kurz ein 0×0-Fenster, das ergibt `scale(0)`.

**Fixes**
- `html, body`: kein Overflow/Scrollen, `touch-action: manipulation` (kein Doppeltipp-Zoom), `text-size-adjust: 100%`
- Vollbild-Knopf in der App ausgeblendet (`html.native-app`)
- Skalierung wird bei jedem Spielzustandswechsel und sekündlich geprüft, wenn sich die Fenstergröße ohne resize-Event ändert; 0×0 wird ignoriert
- `capacitor.config.json`: `zoomEnabled: false`

author: vaggeliska
body:
Top layer of #195. When the clipboard holds a link, the add-food sheet shows a slim "Food from your chatbot" row with the system **Paste** button. Tapping it reads the chatbot's `caloryn://log?…` line and opens a confirmation screen. Add saves one entry; nothing is saved before that.

- **When the row appears:** only when `UIPasteboard.detectedPatterns` reports a link. That check doesn't read the clipboard or show a prompt; content is read only through the `PasteButton` tap. The journeys copy text from the test app, so to Caloryn it's content from another app, and they confirm no "Allow Paste" prompt appears. A version that read `.string` directly does trigger the prompt and fails that journey.
- **Other links:** iOS can't tell a `caloryn://` link from an `https://` one without reading, so any copied link shows the row. A rejected paste hides it until the next pasteboard "generation": relaunch, return from background, or an in-app copy. `changeCount` can't be used for this because it rises by 4 every time the keyboard appears.
- **The confirmation screen** shows exactly what will be saved. A missing macro reads "Not provided". Add stays disabled until the portion weight is valid and at least as heavy as each macro. Changing the weight doesn't rescale the numbers. If today already has the same name and calories, Add asks "Already logged — add again?" first.
- **The chatbot instructions** are copied from a new "Log from a chatbot" section in Settings.
- **Tests:** a snapshot of the confirmation screen in light and dark; `PasteFromChatbotJourneyTests` with 8 journeys, running in the catch-all shard; the theme harness captures the paste row and the Settings section.

author: klausricharz
body:
## Beschreibung

Neue Admin-Seite *Housekeeping* (Menü *Wartung*). Sie findet Datenleichen und inkonsistente Daten über alle Services und bereinigt sie auf Nachfrage.

Jeder Service meldet und bereinigt nur die Daten, die er selbst speichert. Andere Services fragt er dafür höchstens nach Daten:
- `GET /admin/housekeeping` liefert die Prüfungen mit Anzahl, bis zu zehn Beispielen oder einem Fehler.
- `DELETE /admin/housekeeping/{check}` löscht, was die Prüfung in diesem Moment findet, und schreibt Anzahl und IDs ins Log.

| Service | Prüfungen | liest dafür |
|---|---|---|
| Profile | Profileinträge ohne Typ (#236), Einträge/Projekte/Skills ohne Profil, Benachrichtigungen ohne Eintrag, Profilbilder ohne Berater | – |
| Report | Dokumente ohne Berater, hängende Dokumente (`RUNNING` > 1 h), Vorlagen-Dateien ohne Vorlage | Profile `GET /consultants/names`, View-Profile `GET /admin/template/files` (neu) |
| View-Profile | View-Profile ohne Berater (oder ohne Besitzer), Vorlagen ohne Datei | Profile `GET /consultants/names`, Report `GET /admin/file` |

**Fehlerfälle:**
- Antwortet ein benötigter Service nicht, oder liefert er gar keinen Berater, zeigt die Prüfung einen Fehler statt Treffern. Bereinigen ist dann gesperrt, und der Endpunkt antwortet `503`.
- Antwortet ein ganzer Service nicht, zeigt die Seite das bei diesem Service; die anderen laufen weiter.

**Ausdrücklich keine Datenleichen:** unbenutzte Profil-Elemente und eigene Skills.

**Bereinigen:** Es fragt einfach nach und nennt die Anzahl, wie „Nicht mehr benutzte löschen“. Projekte ohne Profil werden nur von ihren Skills gelöst, weil das die Skills des Profils sind (#243).

**Nebenbei:** `GET /admin/file` des Report Service lud alle Dateien samt Inhalt, um ID und Namen zu liefern. Jetzt liest er nur ID und Namen.

Die Regel steht in AGENTS.md: Wer neue Verweise über Service-Grenzen oder nicht transaktionale Löschvorgänge einführt, ergänzt eine Prüfung.

Closes #242

## Akzeptanzkriterien / Testplan

- [x] Admin-Menü *Wartung → Housekeeping*; *Prüfen* fragt alle Services ab und zeigt je Prüfung Beschreibung, Anzahl und bis zu zehn Beispiele
- [x] Alle Quellen aus der Tabelle im Issue werden geprüft, unbenutzte Profil-Elemente und eigene Skills nicht
- [x] Bereinigen mit einfacher Rückfrage, die die Anzahl nennt; es wirkt nur auf das, was beim Ausführen noch zutrifft, und loggt Anzahl und IDs
- [x] Ein nicht erreichbarer Service: Die Prüfung zeigt einen Fehler und ist gesperrt, die übrigen laufen weiter (Test je Service; lokal mit gestopptem View-Profile Service durchgeklickt)
- [x] Jeder Service löscht nur eigene Daten, von anderen liest er nur
- [x] Alle Endpunkte liegen unter `/admin/`; die Edge sperrt `/pwr-{profile,report,view-profile}-service/admin/**` ohne `Power.Admin`
- [x] Statistik: Die Bereinigungen betreffen nur Daten ohne Profil und ändern kein Profil, daher kein Neuladen
- [x] Tests je Service: Datenleichen anlegen, erkennen, bereinigen, Service nicht erreichbar, leere Beraterliste
  - Profile: `HousekeepingServiceITest`
  - Report und View-Profile: je `HousekeepingAdminControllerITest`
- [x] AGENTS.md beschreibt die Prüfungen und die Regel
- `./mvnw verify` ist grün in Profile, Report und View-Profile Service; `npm run build` ist grün.
- Lokal durchgeklickt:
  - Prüfen zeigt die Treffer.
  - Bereinigen von 6 alten Projekten und einem hängenden Dokument entfernt die Treffer, mit Erfolgsmeldung und erneuter Prüfung.
  - Bei gestopptem View-Profile Service erscheint ein Fehler beim Service und bei „Vorlagen-Dateien ohne Vorlage“.

## Operations / Deployment Notes

- Der Report Service ruft jetzt den View-Profile Service auf (neue Property `pwr-view-profile-service-url`). Der Standardwert ist der Compose-Hostname wie bei den anderen Service-URLs; das Deployment setzt diese URLs nicht, es ist also nichts zu tun.
- Kein Schema- und kein Redis-Modell geändert.
- Vor dem ersten Bereinigen in der Produktion lohnt ein Blick auf die Beispiele.

---

Reviewed AGENTS.md; changes comply with architecture and security guidelines.

author: spydon
body:
<!-- Exclude from commit message -->
# Description
<!-- End of exclude from commit message -->
Every `flame_cli` command that prints a result now takes `--json`, so that scripts and AI coding agents never have to parse prose. That is all of them except `run`, which passes its arguments on to `flutter run` (which has `--machine` for this). Before this PR only `tree`, `inspect` and `overlays` had it.

With `--json` the result is printed as a single JSON value on stdout. For example, `snapshot` prints the path, width, height, pixel ratio and byte size of the image. `diff` prints the differing and total pixels, the percentage, the bounds and the output path. `pause`, `resume` and `step` print the paused state, and `step` adds the frames and times. `debug` prints the debug mode and its target. `overlay show`/`hide`/`only` print the overlay and its state, and `input tap`/`drag`/`key` print what was sent. `reload` and `restart` print `ok`, `message` and all `output` lines. `logs` prints the log path and the last lines, and `create` prints the name, path and template. `devtools --json` starts `dart devtools --machine`, so its output is one JSON object per line. `--json` cannot be combined with `logs --follow`.

When a command called with `--json` fails, `FlameCommandRunner.run` prints `{"error": {"message": ..., "exitCode": ..., "kind": ...}}` instead of the text message, with the same exit code as without `--json`. The `kind` is the name of the exit code (`usage`, `data`, `unavailable`, `software`, `cantCreate`). The error also goes to stdout, so stdout of a `--json` command always holds exactly one JSON value, either the result or the error. Other output that is not the result, such as the output of `flutter` in `flame create` or the "enabled the extension" notice of `devtools`, goes to stderr in JSON mode. Arguments that fail to parse are also reported as JSON when `--json` is among them.

`--json` is a per command flag rather than a global one on `FlameCommandRunner`. With `package:args`, global flags have to come before the command name, so a global flag would not have supported `flame tree --json` as it works today. The shared plumbing lives in `json_output.dart`: `addJsonFlag`, a `JsonOutput` mixin with `jsonOutput` and `writeResult(result, text)`, and `jsonError`. `FlameCommand` adds the flag and mixes in `JsonOutput` itself, so new commands that talk to the game get `--json` without extra work. Other commands call `addJsonFlag` and mix in `JsonOutput`. A test checks that every command except `run` has the flag. `FlameCommand` now also uses the `GameConnector` that is passed to `FlameCommandRunner`, so the game commands can be tested with a fake connection.

The exit code usage was audited and was already consistent with the docs. The docs now list every exit code with its `kind`, including `1` from `diff --exit-code`. They also have a new section about using the CLI from scripts and agents, which describes the result of every command.

Changes that scripts could notice:
- The `--json` help text of `tree`, `inspect` and `overlays` is now the shared one. Their JSON output is unchanged.
- In text mode, `diff --output` no longer prints the summary before failing when the diff image cannot be written. Only the error is printed now.
- Otherwise the text output and exit codes without `--json` are unchanged.

author: shd101wyy
body:
## Summary

Z11, decision 48's leak oracle (W6 precondition 2): `--allocator debug` for `yo compile`, `yo test` and `yo build` (`allocator : AllocatorKind.Debug` on an `Executable`).

- **The runtime** (`src/codegen/c/allocator_debug.yo`, new; same header/code split and one-family rule as the fixed arm) is a tracking allocator over the system heap. Each block has a header holding the system pointer, the size, the allocation number and an address-keyed canary. It sits on a live list and is registered in a **block table keyed by payload address**. `free`/`realloc` trust a pointer only after the table names it, so a foreign pointer, or one whose block already went back to the system, aborts with a message instead of a crash. Fresh payloads are filled with 0xAA. Freed payloads are poisoned with 0xDD and kept in a 64 MiB FIFO quarantine, and the most recently freed block always stays whatever its size. The quarantine is checked when a block leaves it and at exit, so a write after free is reported with its offset. A double free aborts and names the block. `realloc` always moves. Locking is a C11 `atomic_flag` spinlock, as in the fixed arm.
- **The exit report** always prints `debug allocator: peak …, N allocations, live at exit: B blocks / S bytes`, the same `live at exit:` phrase as `--debug-heap`.
  - Roots: module globals are never dropped, so `__yo_main_module_init` registers each one with `__yo_debug_alloc_root`. The runtime registers its process-lifetime statics the same way: the worker-pool array and the GC-state list.
  - A conservative scan in the style of LeakSanitizer counts what the roots reach as `still reachable from module globals or runtime state`. Up to 32 **leaked** blocks are then listed by allocation number.
  - When `main` returned normally and a block leaked, the process exits 23 (`leak check failed`).
  - Listed but not judged: an `exit()` from inside the program; a thread of the program still running after the report's one-second wait; `YO_DEBUG_ALLOC_VERDICT=0`.
  - `main` calls `__yo_debug_alloc_init()` first, so the report is the last atexit handler. WASM's direct-call main calls the report itself and returns its status.
- **Threads** (review finding Z11-R1/F1). A running thread's stack is no root, so a block that only a live thread reaches used to be reported as leaked. A correct `ThreadPool` program failed 7 of 800 loaded runs with exit 23, and a detached thread still sleeping at exit failed every time, with the collector on or off.
  - The parallelism runtime now counts the program's threads under `--allocator debug`. `__yo_debug_alloc_thread_enter` runs before `__yo_raw_thread_create` (undone if creation fails), and `__yo_debug_alloc_thread_leave` is the entry's last statement.
  - The report waits up to 1 s on a monotonic clock for the count to reach zero; the pool's atexit shutdown has already told idle workers to stop. Only then does it judge.
  - A thread still running after the wait gets `N threads of the program were still running 1000 ms after main returned, so the live blocks are not judged`.
  - The filed issue is re-scoped and closed: `issues/fixed/2026-10-23-the-debug-allocator-judges-blocks-that-a-still-running-thread-owns.md` (S2). It is not a cycle-collector bug. `send_sync` now passes 15/15 under `--allocator debug` with the collector on.
- **`yo test --allocator debug`** forwards the flag to every batch compile, like `fixed`. A test whose binary exits 23 with `leak check failed` is reported as `Memory leak detected:`, and the runner decodes the exit code rather than comparing the raw wait status. There is one leak-verdict rule (review Z11-R3/F2):
  - `YO_TEST_LEAK_VERDICT=0` stages this verdict off too. The runner passes `YO_DEBUG_ALLOC_VERDICT=0|1` to native, emcc and wasmtime children.
  - The `Pragma.NeedsLeakVerdict` pre-scan counts `--allocator debug` as a verdict source, so those files RUN under `--allocator debug --disable-sanitize` or on wasm instead of being skipped as "would pass vacuously".
- **Flags and build:** `--allocator debug` is validated in `compile` and `test` (`Choices: mimalloc, system, fixed, debug`), with help text in en and zh-CN, and `std/build.yo` gains `AllocatorKind.Debug`. The build runner forwards the string unchanged, so there is no new builtin and no seed gate; the v0.2.68 seed checks the tree's `std` cleanly.
- **Program-visible hook:** `__yo_debug_alloc_on()` (extern "Yo", beside `__yo_debug_heap_on`) is now emitted into EVERY program: `static inline bool __yo_debug_alloc_on(void) { return false; }`, or `true` under debug. `tests/debug_allocator.test.yo` uses it to arm its fault checks. The seed does not emit it, so that test file compiles only with a tree-built compiler. No workflow runs `tests/` with the seed.
- **CI on every OS** (review F3): `test-native`'s shard-0 legs (macOS arm64/x64, Windows x64/arm64) now also run `yo test ./tests/debug_allocator.test.yo --allocator debug`. Linux runs it through the cli-case `test-allocator-debug-suite`. The test's children force `YO_DEBUG_ALLOC_VERDICT=1`, so the job-wide `YO_TEST_LEAK_VERDICT=0` cannot make them vacuous.
- **Docs** in en-US and zh-CN:
  - `MEMORY_SAFETY.md`: the "`--allocator debug`" section, now with the quarantine/eviction rule, runtime roots, the thread rule, `YO_DEBUG_ALLOC_VERDICT`, and the missing type and arena names.
  - `BUILD_SYSTEM.md`: an `AllocatorKind.Debug` row and paragraph.
  - `CYCLE_COLLECTION.md`: the leak witness under `off`, and that `YO_TEST_LEAK_VERDICT=0` turns the debug verdict off too.
  - Also updated: `c-codegen.instructions.md` (block table, thread hooks: a new thread-creation site must call the pair), `testing.instructions.md`, and the "As built" notes in `ZIG_ADOPTION_CANDIDATES.md` Z11 and `WEAK_AND_UNCOLLECTED_RC.md` §6. No new diagnostics, so there are no `yo explain` entries.
- **What the emitted C changes** (correcting the previous body's "every new line is behind `allocator == "debug"`", review Z11-R5/F4):
  - Codegen of user code is unchanged.
  - Every program's runtime gains the one unused `static inline` `__yo_debug_alloc_on` declaration above.
  - The fixed arm's `--debug-heap` size formatter is now emitted by a shared helper (`emit_heap_format_size`, same function text).
  - Everything else is behind `allocator == "debug"`, including the thread hooks and the roots.
  - No dup/drop emit-diff was run: no drop or dup emission changed.
- **Issue updated** (review Z11-R6/F6): `issues/2026-10-17-the-non-routable-connect-test-leaks-its-pending-task-at-exit-where-test-net-stays-pending.md`. The 2026-10-20 mitigation does not hold on io_uring/WSL2. LeakSanitizer and the debug allocator both report the same 80 bytes in 2 blocks, and the file fails 1/25 under `--allocator debug`. It is a known W6a corpus failure.

### Review findings declined or partly declined

- **Z11-R2, double free of an evicted block: no crash any more, but not always named "double free".** The block table removes the SIGSEGV for any block that left the quarantine, and an immediate double free of a >64 MiB block is named a double free. Once another free has evicted the block, its memory is back with the system. A second free then aborts as `… did not hand out (or whose block already left the quarantine)`; the reviewer's p5 probe hits this, because a `println` frees between its two frees. Keeping ghost records of evicted blocks would need an unbounded or arbitrarily capped side table, so the limit is documented next to the double-free bullet in both languages instead.
- **F7, arena names: deferred, not built.** std's `Arena` tracking would have to read `__yo_debug_alloc_on`, which the v0.2.68 seed does not emit, and CI's stage 1 compiles the tree's std with the seed. That is a Generation A/B step. The gap is documented in MEMORY_SAFETY (en/zh) and in Z11's As-built note.

author: krystophny
body:
Large captured input trees make manifest alias validation compare every name with every earlier name. In [SIMPLE](https://github.com/itpplasma/SIMPLE/pull/625), the owner remained inside this check beyond the original 120-second startup and 20-second stop windows. This change indexes names using the existing platform comparison relation while preserving canonical byte ordering and serialization.

## What to review

- [Native comparison index](https://github.com/lazy-fortran/fx/blob/88efbce363e08d57fac7dc92f29a0d495e933167/src/proc/fx_immutable_names.c), preserving the macOS normalization/case comparison, Windows ordinal comparison and Linux ASCII case relation.
- [Manifest validation](https://github.com/lazy-fortran/fx/blob/88efbce363e08d57fac7dc92f29a0d495e933167/src/fx_immutable_manifest.f90) and [focused regression](https://github.com/lazy-fortran/fx/blob/88efbce363e08d57fac7dc92f29a0d495e933167/test/test_immutable_manifest_index.f90). Serialization remains unchanged.

## Verified

- Exact head 88efbce363e08d57fac7dc92f29a0d495e933167: the complete eight-command native CI authority passed GNU12, GNU14 and Flang21, including the 62,922-entry regression. Source content and modes remained unchanged for all 107 tracked paths in each export.
- The affected resident set passed 17/17 with complete inventories, a clean quiescent green gate and generation 9261b0d52f49b9b82727339b9e78c69fd24cad1e4a602a149433fc0c8497aaf0. The pinned Fo driver is 619aca19cf7875e220acf52685c0d8964324c79cd8555258bdaedc645fa6ae6a. All 94 captured source files match the exact head, all 13 runtime/compiler/tool/driver hashes match their approved values before and after execution, and the owned container namespace is closed. This covers 17 affected cases out of 33 ordinary cases, rather than claiming a full resident campaign.
- The three-file patch is byte-identical after restacking onto published Fx66 cabd7b606a7346e650d5e6c3a24453e143d44d7e. Its unchanged macOS GNU16 regression passed 20/20. A separately compiled original e5a3a70 C predicate agrees on 324 case, Unicode, near-collision and invalid-encoding pairs, and independent original/changed manifest implementations produce identical canonical bytes and SHA256. The original 62,922-entry regression exceeds 120 seconds, while the indexed helper takes about 0.03 CPU seconds on the same Mac.

The final Linux wrapper remains FAILED: it compared raw `ldd` output containing changing ASLR addresses. Its final `sha256sum -c` command was consequently not reached. A separate controller audit verified that only those addresses differ and that every saved post-execution file hash equals both its pre-execution hash and its approved value. The original failure and unexecuted command remain disclosed. Controller acceptance receipt SHA256: 8c2cbd0908e78548227c0cfa9b676fb18758c85d232c0bef06f19a8e43b52480.

The subsequent task-private SIMPLE cold check progressed beyond manifest serialization but still failed its unchanged startup/stop windows in Fo input-inventory revalidation. That separate upstream repair remains required, so this PR does not claim SIMPLE qualification. Three broader macOS process/file-fixture suites retain their identical baseline failures. No test, alias rule, startup limit or stop limit is weakened.

Chris&AI

author: cljiahao
body:
## Summary

Phase 4 (K3) for merqo, v0.8.0. Backlog: X-05, X-06, X-07, X-08, X-09, X-10, X-11, X-25, X-29 (X-28 is loopkit only).

- **X-05 nonce CSP.** `proxy.ts` sets a per-request nonce CSP (`@merqo/ui/security`) on per-request routes (`/admin`, `/mfa`, `/dashboard`, `/auth`, `/login`, `/profile`, `/reset-password`, `/no-access`, `/post-login`, `/legal/accept`) and the static policy everywhere else. `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` is gone from every dynamic route; `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` stays.
- **X-06.** `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` (from the proxy) and a disallow-all `robots.txt` on every non-production deployment.
- **X-07.** Zod now parses the auth callback query, kit slugs in upgrade/downgrade/waitlist actions and the legal-accept redirect. Every other route and action already parsed with Zod; no boundary was left without it.
- **X-08.** No `select("*")` exists in merqo `src`, nothing to change.
- **X-09.** `docs/security/2026-10-24-data-inventory.md`.
- **X-10.** No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in merqo.
- **X-11.** `e2e/signed-in-smoke.spec.ts` runs `renderSmoke` over the dashboard, profile and every admin page; `e2e/csp.spec.ts` checks a dynamic and a static page for violations.
- **X-25.** `requireMerqoTeam()` (used by every admin page and action) redirects any session below `aal2` to the new `/mfa` enrol/verify page.
- **X-29.** `no-restricted-imports` keeps `createServiceClient` to `src/lib` and `src/app/api`; the 3 Server Actions outside carry a one-line reason.

## Deviations from the plan (and why)

- **CSP lives in `proxy.ts` for static routes too, not in `next.config.ts`.** `next.config.ts` loads as CommonJS and `@merqo/ui/security` is ESM-only (`exports` has only an `import` condition), so the config cannot import it. Same header value, one source. A `default` export condition in `@merqo/ui` would let the config use it again.
- **next-themes inline script.** Its inline bootstrap has no nonce, so it is allowed by hash (`THEME_SCRIPT_HASH`, the production-minified text). A next-themes or Next bump that changes it fails `e2e/csp.spec.ts` in CI. In dev the static policy is kept (React needs eval and the script differs).
- `/login` and `/reset-password` were prerendered, which cannot carry a nonce, so they now render per request (`force-dynamic` layouts).
- CI e2e now serves the production build (`pnpm build && pnpm start`).
- `/account` in the plan's prefix list does not exist in merqo; `/profile`, `/reset-password`, `/no-access`, `/post-login`, `/legal/accept` and `/mfa` were added.

## Owner decisions

Proposed drops (nothing dropped here; migrations only after you approve):

1. `merqo.customers.name`: no reader in `src`.
2. `merqo.legal_acceptances.user_agent`: written, never read.

## Owner steps

1. Supabase Auth: enable TOTP MFA (staging project first, then prod).
2. Enrol every admin account on staging, then prod: sign in, you land on `/mfa`, scan the QR. Until enrolled an admin cannot reach `/admin`.
3. After the staging deploy:

```bash
curl -sI https://staging.merqo.io/login | grep -i content-security   # nonce + strict-dynamic, no unsafe-inline in script-src
curl -sI https://staging.merqo.io/ | grep -i -E "content-security|x-robots"   # static policy, noindex
curl -s https://staging.merqo.io/robots.txt   # Disallow: /
curl -sI https://merqo.io/ | grep -i x-robots   # prod: no output
```

## Verification

`pnpm check`, `pnpm test` (768), `pnpm build` pass locally; public Playwright specs pass against the production build in a real browser with no CSP violations. The MFA-cleared admin e2e (`global-setup.ts`) can only run in the CI `e2e-admin` job (needs local Supabase with TOTP enabled, set in `supabase/config.toml`).

## README unchanged (mechanical)

None: every changed folder now has a README that describes the change (new READMEs for `src`, `src/app/auth/callback` and `supabase`).

author: stanback
body:
## Problem
On the converter's **Compare methods** card, each spectrum pin centred its name and time under its dot. When two methods convert to nearby times, the labels printed over each other. With women's 1650 SCY 17:36.20 → 1500 SCM, NCAA (17:33.04) and Equivalence (17:45.52) are about 10% of the track apart, so the card showed "NCAAEquivalence" and "17:33.0417:45.52".

## Fix (`src/lib/MethodComparison.svelte`)
- Each dot stays on a zero-width anchor at its true position, the same anchor idea as the MCP card.
- The track and labels are measured with Svelte `bind:` bindings. Each label centres on its pin when it fits, is clamped inside the track, and moves to the first lower row where it touches no other label, with a leader tick back to its dot. Rows where no leader runs through a label are preferred. Labels have an opaque surface background, so an unavoidable leader passes behind text, not over it.
- The row pitch comes from the measured label height, so enlarged text still separates. Before measuring, labels are centred under their pins with a rem fallback pitch.
- The label is now the `<button>`, so its focus ring and hit area match what is drawn.
- No new dependencies, and the common cases look the same as before (e.g. 100 free → LCM, where all three labels fit on one row).

## Test
New Playwright case `method spectrum keeps close method labels apart and inside the card`. It uses the 1650 example at desktop and 390px, in light and dark, and asserts that:
- no two name/time boxes overlap
- every label stays inside the card
- dots keep their true order and relative spacing

It fails on `main` with "NCAA overlaps Equivalence".

## Other surfaces
- **iOS / Android:** these show only a "Method spread (all 3)" text row, with no spectrum, so they're unaffected.
- **MCP card:** has the same collision (at 390px "NCAA" spans x 76–109 and "Equivalence" x 91–159). It's left unchanged here because the fix isn't small. The card builds its DOM imperatively, so it needs post-layout measurement, a resize observer and harness changes. It's best as a follow-up.

## Verification
`npm run check`, `npm test` (187), `npx playwright test` (57 passed, 1 pre-existing mobile-only skip), `node --test scripts/ci-changes.test.mjs scripts/native-test-support.test.mjs` (84).

## Purpose

实现已批准方案（`docs/evidence-governance-plan-2026-10-24.md` 第 3 节）中的 **STRATEGY-VALUE**，并落实 Codex 在 #35 复核中提出的实施验收提醒。在战绩页新增“如果按信号操作”一节：用**假设性收盘价评分（非真实交易收益）**对比各信号策略与一直持有。

Task ID: STRATEGY-VALUE
Author agent: Claude Code
Reviewer agent: Codex

## Handoff

- Base branch and SHA: `main` @ `d774bd0`（#36、#37 已上线）
- Changed paths：
  - `股票预测/frontend/netlify/functions/_shared/strategy-score.ts`（新，纯函数）
  - `api.mts`：scoreboard 的 `per_asset.strategy.{live, backtest}`
  - `scripts/generate-cloudflare-worker.mjs`：新增 `_shared` 导入路径替换
  - `components/strategy-comparison.tsx`（新）、`components/forecast-track-record.tsx`、`lib/types.ts`、`app/globals.css`
  - 测试：`tests/strategy-score.test.ts`、`components/strategy-comparison.test.tsx`
  - `docs/TASKS.md`
- Completed（对应方案第 3 节和验收提醒）：
  - **按目标交易日对齐**：基准日 B 的信号对应目标日 T = B 的下一交易日，收益 `r = Close(T)/Close(B) − 1`，绝不用 B 当天的涨跌配 B 生成的信号。序列的起止都按目标日确定。
  - **策略**：一直持有（w=1）；只做多（预测上涨时 1，否则 0）；按方向多空（预测的符号）；只按实盘可操作信号（`Action_Signal` 为 Up/Down 时 ±1，**只有实盘有**，回测不提供）。
  - **成本与净值**：
    - 初始仓位为 0；`cost_t = 0.0005·|w_t − w_{t−1}|`，0→1 扣 5bps，1→−1 扣 10bps；从持仓退回空仓的当天也扣成本；一直持有只扣一次入场成本；
    - 净值 `NAV_t = NAV_{t−1}·(1 + w_t·r_t − cost_t)`，初始为 1，且计入回撤的峰值；
    - 期末按市值计，另外给出含平仓成本的数值；
    - 交易次数 = 仓位变化次数；胜率 = 持仓日中盈利的比例，没有持仓日时为 null（界面显示“无持仓”）。
  - **缺口处理**：
    - 区间内没有信号的交易日，信号策略按空仓计，并单独计数；基准仍按实际收益计算；
    - **缺收盘价时直接停止评分**（`incomplete_price`，并给出日期），不当作零收益，也不跳过；
    - 基准日不在已核验交易日历内（2026–2027 之外）时不纳入，不臆测交易日。
  - **数据口径**：
    - 实盘只用 `Verified === true`（即当前政策版本的 `scoredOutcome`）的已结算记录；回测用 walk-forward 行（每个日期一行，`Orivane Ensemble`）；
    - 价格使用同一份历史的不复权 Close；按单资产计算，不跨资产拼接；
    - 样本数少于 60 时标注“样本不足，不能作为结论”。
  - **界面**：
    - 标题写明“假设性收盘价评分（非真实交易收益）”；
    - 可切换资产和来源（实盘·当前版本 / 走步回测·模拟）；
    - 表格列出扣成本后的累计收益（附扣成本前和含平仓的数值）、相对一直持有、交易次数、胜率、最大回撤；
    - 说明文字写全全部限制：发布时间错配不可执行、价格收益不含分红、做空可能被高估、5bps 不含借券和融资费用、空仓日处理、不跨资产，以及不构成投资建议。
- Forecast policy version：**不变**。只新增派生报告，不改变预测输出、候选模型、选模或门槛。scoreboard 的 KV 和边缘缓存已按版本隔离，新字段随下一次计算出现；没有该字段的旧响应，组件不显示这一节。
- Notes for the other agent / 真实数据观察：
  - 本地用真实 Yahoo 行情跑了一遍 scoreboard（内存存储，未写生产）。走步回测 2026-05-05 至 10-23，共 120 个交易日，三个资产都显示**只做多和多空策略扣成本后都跑输一直持有**：
    - SPY：持有 +5.79%，只做多 −3.37%（相差 −9.16 个百分点），多空 −11.96%；
    - QQQ：持有 +4.63%，只做多 −2.55%（相差 −7.19 个百分点），多空 −10.10%；
    - NVDA：持有 +6.23%，只做多 −11.23%（相差 −17.47 个百分点），多空 −28.58%。
  - 实盘目前没有当前版本的样本（显示“暂无”）。这与战绩页上为负的回测方向优势一致；这一节正是为了把这个事实直接展示给用户。

  - Worker 生成 + `npm run typecheck` → 通过

Les 8 lots du sprint 24 choisis par Joseph (« ok pour tout », 24/10/2026), regroupés dans une seule demande de fusion.

**Fluidité**
- **S1** Ma semaine sur téléphone : « Préparer » et « Planifier » (ou « Compte rendu », « Déplacer ») écrits en toutes lettres sous chaque magasin ; « Tournée » et « Visite » en haut (`Semaine.tsx`).
- **S2** Fiche avant visite sur téléphone : le dernier mois en tuiles, les deux précédents en lignes ; le tableau reste pour le PC et le PDF (`PreparationVisite.tsx`).
- **S3** Nine box : les Coachs en prénom et initiale du nom (« Noé M. 1 ») au lieu de « NM 1 » (`SanteParc.tsx`).
- **S4** Évolution du parc : toutes les années de la première à la dernière, même sans ouverture.

**Fonctionnalités**
- **F1** « Je suis au magasin » : sur téléphone, à moins de 300 m d'un magasin de son périmètre, l'accueil propose « Saisir la visite », « Préparer » et « Fiche ». La position n'est jamais enregistrée (`AuMagasin.tsx`).
- **F2** Dictée gratuite du navigateur dans la tâche, le message, les notes de visite et de préparation, la note du journal et le commentaire (`Dictee.tsx`).
- **F3** Situation des magasins, refaite après la relecture de Joseph : le Directeur la saisit depuis la fiche (« … » > « Changer la situation », `DialogSituation.tsx`). C'est une liste datée qui contient :
  - les fermetures provisoires du … au … : pastille « Fermé jusqu'au … », pas d'alerte de visite, affichage dans l'agenda ;
  - le passage en intégré ou en franchisé ;
  - la sortie du réseau (fermeture, liquidation, tombée d'enseigne, cession hors réseau) : le magasin passe dans `reseau.fermes` à sa date et sa fiche reste consultable ;
  - la soirée d'inauguration, affichée dans l'agenda.
  
  Évolution du parc compte les sorties et le solde. Elle liste aussi ce qui arrive dans les 12 mois : ouvertures, inaugurations, fins de mandat, passages, sorties, fermetures provisoires.
  
  **Migration `0033_situations_magasins.sql`** : une colonne `store_overrides.situations` (jsonb), règles d'accès inchangées. Elle remplace l'ancienne 0033, qui n'avait jamais été passée.

**Tests**

body:
## Summary

Fixes #3352

`saveCustomAlbum`이 같은 트랙 ID의 오디오를 교체한 뒤에도 재생 URL이 이전 Blob을 반환하는 문제를 수정합니다. 성공한 저장의 오디오를 캐시에 반영하고, 다음 재생 데이터 조회에서 새 URL을 생성한 뒤 기존 URL을 해제합니다. 메타데이터만 바꾸거나 동일 바이트의 Blob을 다시 읽으면 기존 URL을 유지합니다.

늦게 끝난 비교가 최신 저장·삭제 후 재생성을 덮어쓰지 않도록 세대를 확인합니다. 비교 실패는 저장 성공과 구분해 다음 읽기에서 재검증하며, 그동안 바뀐 저장소는 한 번만 다시 읽고 계속 경합하면 읽기 오류를 반환합니다. 실패한 청크도 양쪽 읽기가 끝난 뒤 다음 트랙을 처리합니다.

현재 일반 편집 UI는 오디오 추가 시 새 ID를 만듭니다. 이번 수정은 기존 테스트가 보장하는 **동일 ID 오디오 교체 저장 API와 이후 새 조회**의 계약이며, 기존 플레이어·대기열에 보관된 `PTrack` 참조를 자동 갱신하는 기능은 추가하지 않습니다.

## Testing

- Wallaby: 커스텀 앨범 단위 10파일 **72/72 통과**. 변경·동일 바이트, 다른 앨범, 지연·중첩 저장, 삭제·재생성, URL 생성·Blob 비교 실패와 복구, 실패 읽기 중첩을 확인했습니다.
- 통합 **8/8 통과**: 실제 reader의 삭제 후 cold 캐시·교차 트랙 경합, 최대 두 번의 읽기 후 오류, 손상 레코드 단일 보고, 기존 앨범 편집 저장 경로입니다.
- native Blob URL·fetch 수명: Chromium·Firefox·WebKit **6/6 통과**. native IndexedDB 저장→새 URL 조회→fetch는 Chromium·Firefox에서 통과했습니다. 오디오 디코딩·청취 검증은 수행하지 않았습니다.
- 이 호스트의 WebKit은 제품 코드를 제외한 Blob 한 건의 IndexedDB 저장도 `UnknownError: Error preparing Blob/File data to be stored in object store`로 실패했습니다. 저장 통합 검사는 이 정확한 순수 기능 확인이 실패한 실행에서만 명시적으로 건너뛰며, 모든 WebKit을 제외하지 않습니다.
- 실제 100MiB(25MiB×4) 메타데이터 저장: Chromium 약 **354ms**, Firefox 약 **555ms**, 기존 URL 네 개 유지. 순차 1MiB 비교이며 청크 버퍼 쌍은 2MiB입니다. 전체 프로세스 최대 메모리는 측정하지 않았습니다.
- 변경 파일 oxlint·oxfmt 및 `git diff --check` 통과.
- Pomo 전체 타입 검사는 **통과하지 않았습니다**. 변경 없는 동일 기준 checkout에서도 `PPlayerUtilityButton.story.tsx:77`의 기존 `TS7006` 한 건이 동일하게 발생했고, 수정 파일의 타입 오류는 없습니다. 해당 스토리는 변경하지 않았으며 정확한 원격 head의 공식 필수 CI 결과를 별도로 확인합니다.

author: abhash-chakraborty
body:
Stacked on #88 (temp files); I'll rebase once that merges.

The 0.20 window on Windows was drawn by hand in Win32 and had one fixed screen. Testing it on the laptop showed:
- After the first close, clicking the tray icon did nothing; only Quit worked. The window thread created the mutex `Local\InyonWindow-<role>` and never released it, so every later Open found "another window" and handed over to nothing.
- It asked for a pairing code each time it opened, so the code card said "Starting the tunnel…" and looked as if a change to the reach hadn't applied.
- Its status checked Task Scheduler through PowerShell for three roles every two seconds.
- No settings, no way to join, open or create a hub, no Pages, no temp files.

**What it is now.** A Win32 frame with two WebView2 views (wry 0.57). One shows the app's pages, served from the binary at `http://inyon.localhost`; the other lies over a placeholder for a hub's web app or a page from Pages. The window is made once on its own thread and shown or hidden after that. Calls from the pages go through `window.ipc`: the window answers those that touch it (the view, native menus, the folder picker, the clipboard), and the rest run on a thread each in `desktop::Desk`.

**Pages.**
- This computer: the link, and LAN, VPN and Tunnel switches that apply at once. The last way in can't be turned off.
- Phones: pairing and the phone list.
- Hub: paste the Add a machine command to join, open any hub by address, or create one in WSL. The hub's machines and sessions show in the window. A hub joined by its certificate's SHA-256 is pinned through `ServerCertificateErrorDetected`.
- Pages: open, add a folder, remove.
- Temp files: select, delete, preview.
- Activity: checks and logs.
- Settings: start at sign-in, show the window at sign-in, what closing does, theme, updates, uninstall.

**Tray.** A click toggles the window. The menu gains the reach as a submenu, start and stop the link, the pages, start at sign-in, check for updates and open the logs, drawn in the app's theme.

**Docs:** new page The Inyon app on Windows; install (On Windows, The Inyon window), configuration (`desktop.json`, `window.log`, `webview/`), troubleshooting (WebView2 missing, the window not reopening, the "Starting the tunnel" card).

**Checked:**
- `cargo test -p inyon-cli`
- clippy with `-D warnings` on Linux and for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`
- a release build with cargo-xwin (5.9 MB)
- `tests/app/check.mjs`: every page at 1200 and 720 wide, light and dark, plus the pairing, reach, temp, join and theme flows, against a stand-in for the app
- site build

The laptop was offline today, so the real WebView2 run is still to do before release.
