author: chrisgeo
body:
The five injective ".v2" edge refs (work-item-dependency.v2, work-item-hierarchy.v2, work-item-team.v2, deployment-incident.v2, project-team.v2) now expand from their source row without a result_id, like the repository-anchored and incident refs before them. The sourcerow resolver and its gates are unchanged. Team, project, organization, the retired legacy kinds and the record-only kinds still need result_id. No new field or shape; only description text changed (source_evidence request schema, tools.v1.json, both copies each, docs/mcp-sidecar.md, the guide).

## TEST-EVIDENCE

Base red, tip green (RowKeyedEvidenceRef in contracts/v1 reverted to base, restored and checked by sha256): 15 subtests of `TestEvidenceRouteEdgeRefsExpandWithoutResultID` (api), `TestHandleSourceEvidenceRowKeyedRefsResolveWithoutResultID` (mcp) and `TestRowKeyedEvidenceRefIsExactlyTheSingleRowKinds` (contracts sweep over the vocabulary) fail on base and pass on the tip.

`TestEvidenceRouteEdgeRefsExpandWithoutResultID` drives the real hosted handler and the real sourcerow resolver over fake tables, with refs minted by the production evidenceref.Mint. Per kind: a served source row without result_id; an absent ref gives 404 with no stored-result fallback and 200 from the stored result with its result_id; and 14 refusal arms (source, target, child, parent, edge repository, incident mapped elsewhere or unmapped, work item, team refused by the subject gate, discovery over the bound, review repository, restricted project-team caller) each return the same 404 body and headers as an absent ref of the same ref and read no row.

One gate clause at a time was planted in resolver.go (restored by content digest) and each turned exactly its own arms red: anchor grant filter (5 arms), endpoint grant (3), endpoint presence (2), team gate (1), discovery bound (1), restricted project-team (1). The planting also exposed and fixed three vacuous arms that asked for the granted ref while seeding the secret one.

Local (capped.sh): go test for api, mcp/..., contractcheck, contracts/v1 and sourcerow ok; TestNoSecondPhysicalSourceOutsideTheDeclaration and TestReachableEmissionArtifactIsRegenerated ok; go vet and gofmt clean. Review: one codex round (gpt-6-luna xhigh) on the local tip, 0 P0, 0 P1, 0 P2, 1 P3 (the project-team.v2 route test uses a "*" credential; accepted, see RISK-NOTES); VERDICT: CLEAN. Real-ClickHouse rows (sourcerow chaos7252 and clickhouse integration tests) run in hosted CI only. Image under test: ghcr.io/full-chaos/dev-health-acr.

Consumers on main dd537f6b: RowKeyedEvidenceRef has 2 callers in acr (internal/api/read_routes.go, internal/mcp/source_evidence.go); 0 files in ask-dev, ops and web name RowKeyedEvidenceRef or evidence_ref_unscoped. The server only accepts more, so no pin bump.

## RISK-NOTES

- Behavior change, a .v2 edge ref sent WITHOUT result_id: before = evidence_ref_unscoped error from the MCP tool, and a stored-result record fallback from the HTTP route; after = 200 with the source row when every gate admits it, otherwise the same 404 as an absent ref. Sent WITH result_id: unchanged.
- NOT pinned: a row whose endpoint, service mapping or ownership aged out and that only an old stored result cites gets 404 without result_id; the record is served only with the result_id.
- Accepted: project-team.v2 is served to unrestricted callers only, so a repository-restricted caller gets 404 without result_id (it never had a source row for this kind).
- Surviving mutant, NOT pinned: `allowed := len(readable) > 0` forced to true leaves every test green. It is an equivalent mutant (an empty readable set builds no targets), kept as defence in depth.
- The unrestricted project-team.v2 route test uses a credential granted "*", not a credential with no repository list (the credential service requires at least one scope); the no-list principal is covered by the sourcerow unit tests.
- Authorization is unchanged (encodedSpecs: anchor repository grant, every endpoint, team by the subject gate's ownership reach, discovery bound).

author: abayomiwav
body:
## Summary

Turns the interface from a landing page into a working payments app on the
new contracts and oracle (SETTLIX/settlix-contracts#1,
SETTLIX/settlix-oracle#1).

Before this PR:
- The Merchant, Pay and Get Started links all returned 404.
- "Connect Wallet" did nothing.
- `src/lib/stellar.ts` imported `SorobanRpc`, which no longer exists in
  stellar-sdk 14.
- The QR code encoded an invented `settlix://` scheme with the amount inside
  it.
- Next.js was pinned to 15.1.0, from before the CVE-2025-29927 fix.

## What it does now

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `/merchant` | Connect Freighter and apply; the business ID is SHA-256 hashed in the browser. Then wait for approval, which the page detects by itself. After that, create invoices priced in USD (signed oracle quote) or directly in XLM/USDC, and show a QR code that stamps itself **PAID** when the customer pays. |
| `/pay/[id]` | The invoice as a receipt, read from the payment contract. Pay with Freighter in one transaction. Expired, cancelled, paid and suspended-merchant cases are handled. |
| `/admin` | Look up an applicant, compare the business hash, approve. The contract enforces that only the admin can do this. |
| `/` | Explains the real flow; the fee is read live from the settlement contract. |

- `src/lib/contracts.ts` is one Soroban client for the whole app: reads by
  simulation, writes through a `Signer` (Freighter in the browser, a keypair
  in the smoke test). Contract error codes become plain sentences.
- The QR code is a normal `https://.../pay/<id>` link. Amount, token and
  merchant are read from the chain on that page, so editing a QR code cannot
  change the amount.
- Money is bigint stroops throughout, with the contract's fee rounding.
- New design: receipt paper, ink, a terracotta accent, and ledger green for
  settled money. Fraunces and IBM Plex. Replaces the dark slate template.
- Defaults point at the testnet deployment, so `npm run dev` works with no
  `.env`.

## How it was tested

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (18 tests: money,
  contract decoding, error messages, status, components, storage), and
  `npm run build`.
- `npm run smoke` against the live testnet contracts, using the same client
  code as the UI:
  - A fresh merchant applied (`Pending`) and was approved (`Active`).
  - Invoice #2 was created (`Open`) and paid
    ([tx](https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/tx/bf6a7d3c33dc871f5c1f052cb5716933cb71259b472d65f33f065e486578d1ab)):
    `Paid`, fee 0.0617283 XLM.
  - A second payment was rejected with contract error #10.
- Production build served and loaded in headless Chrome at 1280 px and
  390 px:
  - Landing page with the live 0.5% fee.
  - `/pay/1` and `/pay/2` render the paid testnet invoices.
  - `/pay/999` shows "not found".
  - `/merchant` and `/admin` show the wallet gate.
  - No console errors, no horizontal overflow.
- Browser-to-oracle quote: CORS allows the interface origin and refuses
  others.
- Not tested: clicking through with the Freighter extension itself, which
  cannot run headless. The smoke test covers the same transactions.

## Summary

Patches the npm advisories that make both `pnpm audit` CI lanes (and so `ci-final-gate`) fail on every PR. Only the affected packages change. This is not the monthly Dependabot batch.

**Direct bumps (exact pins kept)**
- `zod` 4.4.3 → 4.6.6 in `apps/front` and `packages/shared-ts`.
- `vitest` 4.1.11 → 4.1.12 in `apps/front`, `lint-ts`, `scripts-ts` and `shared-ts`. This brings in `@vitest/mocker` 4.1.12.

**pnpm overrides**
- New, scoped to the vulnerable ranges:
  - `zod@<4.6.6` → `^4.6.6` (pulled in via `shadcn`)
  - `dompurify@<3.4.17` → `^3.4.17` (via `posthog-js`; even the latest posthog-js only requires `^3.4.13`)
  - `undici@>=7.0.0 <7.30.1` → `^7.30.1`
  - `undici@>=8.0.0 <8.12.2` → `^8.12.2`
- Raised existing overrides:
  - `body-parser` → `^2.4.0`
  - `fast-uri` → `^3.1.9`
- `auditConfig` is unchanged: nothing is ignored.

**Changes the zod 4.6 bump required**
- `generate-zod-i18n-map.mjs`: zod's French label for a string is now the multi-word "chaîne de caractères", so the expected-token probe no longer rejects spaces.
- `zod.fr.json` is regenerated by postinstall. Some French validation messages change wording, as zod's own locale did: "Chaîne de caractères invalide…", and "motif" instead of "modèle". `interzod-format-key.test.ts` is updated to match.
- The two `zod-version.pin.test.ts` probes now read `email` through a typed view. zod 4.6 moved chain methods to the prototype, so the own-property lookup failed.

## Verification

- `node packages/scripts-ts/src/npm-audit-runner.ts prod moderate` and `dev moderate` (the CI audit commands): no known vulnerabilities.
- `pnpm --filter front typecheck`: OK. shared-ts typecheck: OK.
- shared-ts tests: 120/120. lint-ts tests: 1058/1058.
- Front vitest: 3445 passed, 1 failed. The one failure was the zod pin test, fixed afterwards; it then passes 2/2 in isolation. The full suite was not re-run.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format` and `pnpm exec knip`: clean.
- scripts-ts: 810 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped. The failures look environmental: an EACCES check fails because the cloud sandbox runs as root, and one test makes a GitHub GraphQL call that the sandbox blocks. CI will confirm.

- **Fallen Bridge** (`daybreak/fallen_bridge`, 52,-11): four floating spans, each a stride apart, with hornets in the wind. A fall lands on the old footing, where a beetle walks.

author: ennalalala
body:
## 背景

CacheStore / P2P 在 RDMA 模式下，本地 RDMA 设备可能被移除，也可能持续不可用。目前进程无法主动发现这类故障，只能等传输失败后才暴露。本 PR 在外源侧提供 RDMA 设备健康监控的配置、校验和透传，健康探测与监控由内源实现。

健康监控会在后台线程里上报指标。如果不接入统一的关闭顺序，`KMonitorFactory::Shutdown()` 之后仍可能有上报在进行，访问已释放的指标资源。本 PR 为此增加关闭回调机制。

## 本 PR 的改动

- 新增 7 个配置项（均带 `rdma_device_health_` 前缀）：
  - `enabled`
  - `fault_handler`（`LOG` / `ABORT`）
  - `probe_interval_ms`
  - `device_fault_confirm_ms`
  - `fault_window_ms`
  - `unavailable_threshold_ms`
  - `flap_warn_threshold`

  支持 CLI 和 env 两种方式配置，Python 侧默认开启。
- 新增 `RdmaDeviceHealthConfig.h`，统一定义各配置项的取值范围。Python 参数解析通过 pybind 读取同一组常量，两侧不再各自维护边界。
- 启动时校验配置：
  - 整数类型和取值范围。
  - 确认时长至少覆盖 2 个探测间隔。
  - 累计阈值不超过窗口。

  `flap_warn_threshold` 超过理论上限时只打 WARN，不拒绝启动。
- `CacheStoreConfig` 新增 `toRdmaDeviceHealthConfig()`，配置经由 `CacheStoreInitParams`、`MessagerInitParams` 和 `TransferBackendConfig` 透传到 RDMA 实现。
- `CacheStoreConfig` 的 pickle 同时兼容 20 字段旧格式和 27 字段新格式；`to_string()` 输出新增字段。
- kmonitor 生命周期：
  - 新增 `registerKmonitorShutdownHook` / `unregisterKmonitorShutdownHook`。
  - `stopKmonitorFactory()` 先执行全部停止回调，等在途上报结束后再关闭 factory。
  - 关闭期间拒绝新注册。

## 测试

- `rtp_llm/cpp/config/test:cache_store_config_test`：4/4 通过。
- `rtp_llm/server/server_args/test:server_args_test`：64/64 通过。覆盖默认值、CLI/env 配置、非法值、边界值和组合约束。

author: teamleaderleo
body: Leo, 2026-10-24: "why arent nightlies up yet". From the coordinator: "On a non-2xx response, print the response body and the x-ratelimit-* and retry-after headers. Classify 403s: retry the rate-limit ones … with backoff until the reset time, capped at about 10 minutes. A permission 403 still fails at once." From nightly-opus: "list what was actually uploaded … and say 'nothing is live' when the failed POST was the asset upload." ## Incident nightly-next run 40076543798 at `03846a44af` (build 4007654379801) built, signed, notarized and verified. Then job publish-nightly 120828438329 failed in "Publish nightly release assets": ``` GitHub API rate limit reached during deletion; prune pass is incomplete. Release publication failed: POST HTTP 403 ##[warning]Published assets, release metadata, and appcasts are live; the nightly-next tag marker is stale because its final update failed. ``` The 403 was the spent Actions installation quota. The error printer dropped GitHub's message, and `RequestError.retryable` never retried a 403. The warning was false: at about 08:47Z both nightly-next appcasts still served 4005999011801, and the release had no 4007654379801 asset. ## Fix **`scripts/ci/publish-release-assets.py`** - curl now writes `--dump-header`. A non-2xx error reads `POST HTTP 403: (retry-after=…, x-ratelimit-limit=…, x-ratelimit-remaining=…, x-ratelimit-reset=…, x-ratelimit-resource=…, x-github-request-id=…)`, with the token redacted. - `rate_limit()`: a 403/429 with `retry-after`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, or "rate limit" in the body is rate-limited and retryable. It waits for `retry-after`, else until `x-ratelimit-reset`, else 60 s. - Every rate-limit wait in one process shares a 600 s budget (`RATE_LIMIT_BUDGET_SECONDS`), which keeps the publish job inside its 30 min timeout. Past the budget it fails with "GitHub rate limit did not reset within 600 s". - A permission 403 (none of those signals) still fails at once. - POST and PATCH JSON calls (create a draft, rename an alias) retry only when rate-limited, since GitHub rejected them unprocessed. Uploads keep their reconcile-then-retry loop, which now uses the rate-limit wait. **`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`**, "Record nightly publication marker outcome": that step runs on `always()`, while the tag move only runs after every publish step succeeds. A `skipped` or `cancelled` move therefore means publication stopped. That case is now `tag_status=unpublished`, with a warning that names it, says the appcasts still serve the previous build, and says the tag didn't move, plus a "Not published" summary. It no longer says "are live". A `failure` of the move itself keeps the true "published, tag marker stale" message. Consumers compare `tag_status` only against `stale` and `updated`, so they are unaffected. ## Tests `tests/test_github_release_publication.py` gains real-curl cases against a local HTTP server: - remaining=0 waits until the reset; - retry-after waits that long; - "rate limit" only in the body waits 60 s; - the wait is capped by the budget; - a limit that outlasts the budget fails; - a permission 403 fails at once, with no sleep, and names GitHub's message, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and the request id; - the token is never in the error. All 37 tests pass. `tests/test_nightly_universal_build.sh` now requires the unpublished branch; it fails with the branch removed and passes as is. `tests/test_nightly_next_recovery.py` passes. The step's own job (`prune` reporting "rate limit reached during deletion") is unchanged here. Moving publish and prune onto the release App's own token is tt-ci's. Agent session: [big-red](https://cmux.com/deeplink/agent?harness=claude&session=01a16c8f-6944-7083-a90d-5f8ca9521b70&host=big-red) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes nightly release publication so a rate-limited GitHub API rejects retries correctly and a failed publish is never reported as live. - Rate-limit 403/429 responses (`retry-after`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, or a "rate limit" body) now retry with backoff until reset, capped at a 600 s budget; permission 403s still fail at once. - Errors now name GitHub's message and the `retry-after`, `x-ratelimit-*`, and `x-github-request-id` headers, with the token redacted. - A skipped or cancelled release-tag step now reports `tag_status=unpublished` and warns that appcasts are unchanged, naming what each publication part did, instead of claiming assets are live. **Tests** - Added real-curl cases covering reset waits, budget caps, permission 403 behavior, and token redaction; all 37 pass. Written for commit 9105cc8220cee7aebf3ff646edd6168c95321530. Summary will update on new commits.

author: eduardoben
body:
**Problem and root cause:** The `GalleryLiteRtBackend` was failing to initialize the LiteRT-LM `Engine` on the Google Pixel 10 Pro XL for the Tensor G5 TPU model. The root cause was that `EngineConfig` was instantiated without explicitly setting `maxNumTokens`. By default, this assigns a non-null value (likely a fallback value within LiteRT-LM). However, as noted in `AGENTS.md` and confirmed by checking the Google AI Edge Gallery application implementation, Pixel Tensor TPU AOT models have baked-in tensor shape dimensions and **require** `maxNumTokens = null` during initialization.

**Evidence and current documentation consulted:**
1. Checked `AGENTS.md` which explicitly states: `Must pass maxNumTokens = null during EngineConfig creation to preserve baked-in AOT EdgeTPU tensor shape dimensions.`
2. Checked the implementation of `LlmChatModelHelper.kt` in the official Google AI Edge Gallery repository (`/tmp/gallery`), which passes `maxNumTokens` to `EngineConfig` depending on the device/model. The gallery dynamically adjusts it, and explicitly states the requirement.

**Architecture or design decisions:**
I've updated `GalleryLiteRtBackend.kt` to explicitly pass `maxNumTokens = if (isTensorTpuModelFile) null else 2048` for the primary `EngineConfig`, which resolves the issue specifically for TPU models but sets it safely for standard CPU/GPU backends. I've also set it to `2048` on the pure GPU fallback route. 

**Implementation and affected files:**
Modified `app/src/main/java/com/local/interviewassistant/data/llm/GalleryLiteRtBackend.kt`.

**Tests and validation results:**
1. Built the project via `./gradlew app:assembleDebug` successfully.
2. Unit tests passed via `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`. 

**Performance impact:** None.
**Risks and remaining limitations:** None known. The model file loading logic handles both NPU/GPU implementations based on naming schemas which matches our current state machine safely.

author: gouranshu
body:
## Project Overview

- **Project Name:** dead-code-reaper
- **Category:** `tools/dead-code-reaper`
- **Frameworks & Technologies Used:** Python 3.9+ (standard-library `ast`, zero runtime dependencies), pytest, optional Gemini / Anthropic / OpenAI-compatible APIs for AI notes

### Description

dead-code-reaper finds dead Python code, proves each deletion is safe by running the project's own tests without it, and lets developers review everything in a browsable HTML report before a single line is removed.

- **Five kinds of dead code:** unused functions, classes, and methods; unused imports (including single names in a multi-name import); unused local variables; unused modules; and unreachable code. It also finds code that is only used by other dead code.
- **Verified, not guessed:** removals are tried in a temporary copy of the project and kept only if the test suite still passes. Batches are split in half on failure, so a whole project usually needs only a few test runs.
- **Conservative:** decorated functions, framework hooks, overridden methods, and names appearing in strings or config files are protected; code looked up by name at runtime gets a low confidence score and starts unticked.
- **Human review:** a self-contained HTML report with a file tree, highlighted dead lines, and checkboxes. Unticking an item keeps everything it depends on, and the report builds the `apply` command.
- **Safe apply:** `apply` re-runs the tests on exactly the selection, refuses if files changed since the run, and saves a patch that can be undone with `git apply -R`.
- **Optional AI notes:** with a Gemini, Anthropic, or OpenAI-compatible key, each removal gets a one-line explanation and a risk warning for likely framework hooks. AI never decides what is dead (see `docs/adr/0001`).

Try it on the included example:

```bash
cd tools/dead-code-reaper
pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -e .
cp -r examples/inventory_app /tmp/inventory_app
dead-code-reaper run /tmp/inventory_app --app
```

---

## Contribution Checklist

Please verify the following requirements before submitting your PR:

- [x] **Directory & Naming:** The project is contained in its own folder under `agents/<project-slug>/` or `tools/<project-slug>/` using lowercase kebab-case.
- [x] **Documentation:** A complete `README.md` based on `template/README.md` is present in the project folder with all relevant sections completed.
- [x] **Reproducible Setup:** Setup and installation instructions were verified from scratch in a clean environment.
- [x] **Core Functionality Tested:** The agent or tool was executed and confirmed to work as described.
- [x] **Example Usage:** Realistic input and output examples are provided in the project documentation.
- [x] **Dependencies Declared:** All external dependencies are tracked in a project manifest (e.g., `requirements.txt`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`).
- [x] **Secrets & Security:** No API keys, credentials, tokens, local `.env` files, or personal data are included in this PR. A `.env.example` is provided if environment variables are required.
- [x] **Scope Limitation:** Changes are strictly confined to the project's own directory (plus an optional entry in `agents/README.md` or `tools/README.md` index). Unrelated files have not been modified.

---

## Testing & Verification Notes

- **Environment:** Linux (Ubuntu), Python 3.12. macOS and Windows are untested (noted in the README).
- **Clean install:** a fresh virtual environment following the README (`pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pip install -e .`) installs the `dead-code-reaper` command successfully.
- **Unit tests:** `python -m pytest` runs 30 tests covering each kind of dead code, the protection rules, source edits, verification (including projects without tests, failing baselines, the run cap, and editable installs), the full `run` → `apply` flow, and AI response parsing. All pass in about 10 seconds with no network or API key.
- **Evaluation:** `python eval/run_eval.py` compares results against a hand-labelled ground truth for `examples/inventory_app` (14 dead items, 10 traps). Deleting everything static analysis flags breaks the example's tests; after verification and confidence scoring, the default selection finds 14/14 dead items with 0 wrong removals and the tests still pass.
- **Real-world check:** on [HTTPie](https://github.com/httpie/cli) (commit `5b604c3`, 133 files), the scan took 0.5s and found 13 items, 11 confirmed by hand as genuinely unused. `run` verified all 13 against HTTPie's ~1,000-test suite in 3 runs; `apply --dry-run` passed and produced a 173-line patch that applies cleanly with `git apply`. Three HTTPie tests that fail on an unchanged checkout in this environment were excluded via `--test-cmd`, as documented in the README.
- **AI notes:** tested with a stand-in provider (no API key was available during development); provider selection and response parsing are covered by unit tests.

Before #113, running SE agents had added real cases from five tickets (275, 269, 278, 280, 282) to the local checkout's `design-examples.md`, following the old rule. They were local commits and were never pushed. Their provenance goes to the AutoByteus project's design cases file (autobyteus-293). Their general lessons go here, written neutrally, +10 lines:
- **Case 3, notice it by:** also only the server side of a changed rule. User-visible text that states the rule is a consumer, and so is code that matches an error code to a message; a new field or mark with no named reader is a sign of the same gap.
- **Case 5, notice it by:** a module called production code without listing its importers; "unchanged" for a merge of copies never compared line by line; "unrecoverable" or "the layout matches" without opening the files or asking how they were made.
- **New Case 7, "One Rule Applied By Several Callers" (Principle 13):** three callers each apply one sequence, and the pending state is left to defaults. Better: one owner that all callers call, with the pending state set explicitly.

This is case-study text only, with no rule change; the case-study structure was evaluated in #113. `check-links.py` reports 0 broken links. `design-examples.md` is now 1,059 lines (1,271 before #113).

body:
## Web Calendar: dense days (owner-accepted mock-up v2)

The owner accepted `calendar-dense-mockup` v2 on 24 Oct 2026. It replaces location v4 step 2's accepted difference #2 ("the length is never truncated"): **the title wins**. The iPhone native Calendar follows in its own PR.

### What changes
- **No stacking.** Overlapping blocks, counting the 18 px minimum label height, sit side by side in greedy columns. Each spreads right while the next columns are free (`layoutCalendarBlockColumns(…, { expandRight })` adds `spanCount`). Nothing is drawn on top of another block.
- **Suggestions in the grid.** Open Review suggestions are hatched blocks with a dashed bar and a "?". They share the same columns, so the separate review lane is gone. With room they show times and length.
- **Fill.** A tinted fill (20 % light, 30 % dark; suggestions 12 % / 16 %) and a 3 px colour bar. No outlines, primary text colour.
- **Text.** The title wraps to the whole lines that fit and ends with an ellipsis after a whole word (words are unbreakable). Times and length appear on a second line only with room (≥ 34 px high and ≥ 120 px wide). Compact 11 px semibold under 34 px high or 90 px wide, and colour only under 22 px. The shared rules live in `CALENDAR_DENSE_LABEL` / `calendarDenseLabel`.
- **Moments.** A finished block of a minute or less is a short line with a dot at the column's left edge.
- **Pattern label.** In Day view the pattern name is written level beside its bracket (44 px rail); Week view keeps the bare bracket.

### Acceptance (side by side with mock-up v2)
I seeded a synthetic Exampleton day (made-up names, Fri 23 Oct) into a throwaway Postgres. Screenshots are kept outside Git:
- desktop 1440 and phone 390, light and dark: `.codex-dayframe-qa/location-v4/calendar-dense-screens/build-web/side-by-side-web-{light,dark}.png`

Desktop matches the mock-up block for block. Differences:
1. The seeded school-run pattern has three parts (trip there, stay, trip back), the only shape a real bracket can take; the mock-up shows two. Data only; the bracket and label look the same.
(After Codex r1, the earlier second difference is gone: a word wider than its title is left out, along with every word after it, so no word is ever shown in part. When none fit, the block shows colour only, and its name still carries the full title.)

Phone width after the whole-word fixes, light and dark: `build-web/build-phone-{light,dark}-wholewords.jpg`. A third difference shows there, for the owner to look at:
3. In this narrow three-column phone layout, "Standup", "Expense receipts" and "Supplier call" are colour-only. Each one's first word is wider than its roughly 44 px title area, so the never-mid-word rule leaves no whole word to show. Their names stay in the tooltip and for screen readers. When the last whole word fills its line, there is no room for the "…" after it.

### Checks
- Web 2228 and shared 1250 tests pass (two load timeouts in untouched files pass alone); typecheck passes; lint shows 0 errors; `check:docs` passes.
- No API, migration, mobile or hosted change.

### Documentation impact
`docs/feature-fix-tracker.md` gains a row. The design doc note, which records the replacement of accepted difference #2, is in the private location-v4 design doc.

author: arun-elr
body:
Follow-up to #552.

## What does this PR do?

Three small things left over from the #552 review:

- `ensure_deployment_token` keeps a `MSTAR_DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN` the launcher set, since separately started processes have to agree on it. A fixed value (a systemd `Environment=` line, a pod template shared by replicas) comes back on every launch and brings back the #767 race, so it now logs a warning when it keeps one. A per-launch nonce would split separately started processes apart, so this stops at the warning.
- `_run_worker` ran its unlinks with SIGTERM and SIGINT ignored and never put the handlers back, so a worker that hung later in teardown ignored every further stop and got SIGKILLed after 5 s, skipping the arena's exit-time finalizer. It now restores them, and the arena's `unlink_owned_files` also unlinks its own segments, so a worker killed in a hung teardown (or hard-exited by the orphan watchdog) no longer leaves them behind.
- A test pins the namespace formula, `sha1(f"{token}\0ipc://<realpath of conductor.ipc>")[:12]`, which the e2e harness rebuilds by hand (#772).

## How was it tested?

- 5 new tests in `test/modular/test_shm_shutdown_cleanup.py` and `test/modular/test_shm_shared_tmpfs.py`, 4 fail on main (list below); both files 22 passed on dbf35f6e1 (head, on main 82375ad11). `ruff check .` clean.
- CPU Core as `ci.yml` runs it, on 86e9b3b67 (same commits on main 294cbab66): 6,331 passed, 1,138 skipped, 6 failed, the same 6 as main here (`ftfy` and `prometheus_client` missing from this venv, 2 signal-timing tests that pass alone). `test/rust/` plus the row store 374 passed, 89 skipped; `cargo test --release --no-default-features` 77 passed.
- One H200, merged with #772 and #637: `compare --stress --models qwen3_5_2b` (arena on) 0 of 20 failed runs on head; `compare --models qwen3tts_1p7b_split_shm,qwen3tts_1p7b_split_shm_arena` no `/dev/shm` leftovers or crash lines on either arm, WER and UTMOS equal, latency and throughput within 2%.

<details><summary>Tests in detail</summary>

Fail on main:
- the warning for a launcher-set token, and none for a minted one;
- the handlers are back after the unlinks;
- a real spawned worker whose teardown hangs on a thread join is SIGKILLed after the 5 s join; on main its arena segment is still in `/dev/shm`;
- a stop injected while the handlers are saved and another right after they're restored: the unlinks still run and `run()`'s error is still the one raised.

The formula test passes on main, as it should.

</details>

<details><summary>GPU runs in detail</summary>

- `python -m benchmark.eval compare --base 294cbab66 --head HEAD --stress --models qwen3_5_2b`, `MSTAR_SHM_ARENA=1` in the model's `cases.yaml` env, head = main + #772 + #637 + this PR: 20 runs per arm of 32 clients cancelling, dropping, retrying and reusing ids. Head 0 of 20 failed runs; base 4 of 20, one session where the cold start's Inductor compile workers exited and the stress check took it for a crash (#772 fixes that check).
- `python -m benchmark.eval compare --base 82375ad11 --head HEAD --models qwen3tts_1p7b_split_shm,qwen3tts_1p7b_split_shm_arena` (worker-to-worker SHM over files and over the arena; head 2b88715e6 = main + #772 + #637 + this PR): WER 2.90% and UTMOS 4.30 on both arms, c=1 latency 391 to 391 ms and 393 to 390 ms, c=8 throughput +0.3% and +1.8%. The `timeout` case is "incomplete" because base did not time the long request out, as on main.

</details>

<details><summary>Not tested</summary>

A real systemd or k8s restart with a fixed token (the warning is a unit test). A second SIGTERM breaking a hung teardown in a served worker (the restore is tested directly; no served run hung).

</details>

- [x] `ruff check .` passes
- [x] Added or updated tests / docs where relevant

body: # ExtraBiomes for Java Edition v3.10.0 **The first official release of ExtraBiomes for Java Edition.** The Java version of the mod has been in development on and off since 2023 so I am very happy to finally have the first non beta release :D this release has been developed to maintain almost full parity with the bedrock version v3.1.0 (yes this is also supposed to be 3.10.0 but made a typo in the first beta so kept it lmao), yet there are some very minor differences between the 2 platforms. this changelog is a brief overview of the whole java mod :) ## Supported versions and Requirements - Minecraft 1.20.1, 1.20.2, 1.20.4, 1.20.6, 1.21.1, 1.21.3, 1.21.4, 1.21.5, 1.21.8, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1.2, 26.2 or 26.3. - Fabric (every version), NeoForge (1.20.2 and up) or Forge (1.20.1 and 1.20.2). - Required mods: [TerraBlender](https://modrinth.com/mod/terrablender), [Architectury API](https://modrinth.com/mod/architectury-api) and [GeckoLib](https://modrinth.com/mod/geckolib), plus [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api) on Fabric. - Optional: [Create](https://modrinth.com/mod/create), which gives The Netherlands' windmill moving parts. ## Biomes 26 new overworld biomes. ### Highlights - **Floating Jungle:** a jungle on the world's tallest peaks, with sky islands hanging 28 to 60 blocks above them. Islands have vines, roots and waterfalls trailing from their undersides, and some are joined by giant log canopy bridges. The rarest archipelago has an overgrown ruin around a chest of loot, and one rare island carries a vanilla jungle temple. Colossal jungle trees, 100 to 130 blocks tall, rise from the peaks. - **Glacier:** an enormous block of ice stretching down to bedrock. - Underground, the caves are geothermal. They have basalt-lined lava pools, lavafalls, glowing magma veins, deep blue ice, snow and basalt pillars, meltwater pools and frozen lakes. Chests are sealed inside blocks of ice, and snow golems spawn deep down. - On the surface there are crevasses with snow bridges, and meltwater streams ending in plunge pools, some with geysers of potent sulfur (26.2 and up). Streams can sink into shafts that bore down through the ice into large chambers. The water is a clear pale blue. - It rains instead of snows, so surface water doesn't freeze. - **The Netherlands:** tulip fields, wheat fields and windmills on the surface, with a mini Nether underneath. The netherrack runs down to bedrock, with basalt, blackstone and its own nether ores. **The Netherlands Mutated** swaps the tulips for wheat fields. - **Sky City (structure):** a floating city above the mountains, see [Structures](#structures). ### Surface biomes - **Charred Forest** A burnt forest biome with petrified trees, some smoke and fire, plus a thick smokey fog in the air. - **Cold Mesa:** a mesa in a cooler climate, with the underground mesa generating beneath it. **Cold Mesa Plateau** is its eroded mountain form, and **Cold Mesa Bryce** adds Bryce pillars. - **Deep Dark Forest:** a forest corrupted by sculk. - **Desert Bryce:** a desert with towering Bryce pillars. - **Fungle Jungle:** a jungle that has met a mushroom island, with mycelium, new mushrooms and hoppleshrooms. - **Future Desert:** a very rare desert of white concrete "sand" and little futuristic trees. - **Grand Oasis:** a desert with streaks of red sand, lots of palm trees, hidden treasure and the bones of giants. - **Jellyfish Fields:** a mossy sea floor with custom coral structures and sea pickles, home to jellyfish. - **Jungle Marsh** A swampy jungle biome. - **Jungle Pillars:** a jungle with huge stone pillars covered in vegetation and weathered with moss, vines and varied stone. - **Lush Mesa:** a mesa humid enough for jungle to spread over its lower sections. **Lush Mesa Bryce** adds Bryce pillars. - **Moorlands:** hilly lowlands of long grass, mud and podzol dotted with lakes, with plenty of wildlife. - **Mystic Forest:** a fantasy swamp with purple-hued mystic trees, glowing leaves, purple fog and glowing goo on the floor. - **Shattered Swamp:** a swamp with stone and tuff pillars, moss patches and bamboo. - The tallest has a reward chest at its summit. - Jellycoral structures, Bryce pillars, boulders, stick piles, huge mushrooms, palm groves and oasis fossils. ## Mobs - **Puckoo:** a chicken, koi and duck hybrid that likes eating the moss off pebbles. Tame it with a Mossy Pebble or by riding it. It can be saddled, and spawns on beaches. - **Giant Tortoise** Inspired by the giant tortoises from terraria, a hostile mob that drops scutes. - **Jellyfish:** found in Jellyfish Fields, and washes up on beaches and milked for jellyfish jam. - **Piranha:** comes in small, normal and large sizes. they are lured away with bait, they spawn in jungle and swamp water, a single one does little damage, but they can spawn in large groups which is where they get scary and there is a config option to make them less aggressive. - **Treefrog** spawns in swamps jungles and drops frogs legs which can bee food or turned into a frog helmet. - **Hoppleshroom:** found in mushroom biomes. - *

body:
Part of #1425.

Two needless costs the nightly bisect of #1425 found; the rest of #1425 is growth that is the point of its commits (the table is on the issue).

**sema: FxHash for the throws inference's span-keyed maps**
- `throws/fn_types.rs` (#1326) kept its maps (`written`, `closure_sites`, `flows`, `var_of`, ...) in `std::collections` maps, which hash with SipHash. `written` gets an insert for every parameter and field of every checked function, so SipHash was about half of what #1326 added to `velt check bench/compile/all_std.vlt`.
- Now `FxHashMap` / `FxHashSet`, as the rest of the checker since #1354. The maps' contents are unchanged; nothing reads them in hash order.
- Regression test `hasher_tests::checker_maps_use_fxhash`: no `std::collections` hash maps in `velt_sema/src`, except the three files where the HIR contract's maps are built. It fails on the old `fn_types.rs`.

**velt_rt: a promise start reads the reader state only once the program has an `RwLock`**
- `refuse_tasks_in_read` (#1355) is `RWLOCKS && in_read()`. LLVM read the thread's reader state ahead of the `RWLOCKS` test, so each start ran 8 more instructions (cachegrind on `bench/async/fanout_all`, which starts 1M promises: exactly +8,000,000 in `velt_rt::task::local::start`).
- Now the inline part is the `RWLOCKS` load and a branch, and the reader-state check is its own function, called only once an `RwLock` exists. The behavior is the same, and `lang/rwlock_read_tasks_stop` still stops the program.

**Instruction counts** (cachegrind, `VELT_THREADS=1`, Linux, release, each ref built from `git archive`; `bench/compile/count_check.sh` for `check_all_std`; `fanout_all` built with `velt build --release --backend llvm`)

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `compile/check_all_std` | 490,992,530 | 488,770,427 (−0.45%) | 488,718,727 (−0.46%) |
| `async/fanout_all` | 857,239,248 | 857,174,357 | 852,266,351 (−0.58%) |

The nightly baseline for `fanout_all` is 830.8M, so with this change it is +2.6% over that baseline, below the limit. The rest comes from #1332 (timer order and unhandled rejections at the checkpoint, about 18 instructions per promise start), which its PR measured at +2.26%.

author: emmmmdeee
body:
Before: the web UI server answered some requests before reading the body they announced: the `503` when the one inspection place is in use, the `413` for a file over 64 MiB, the `403` for a request without the page's header, and the `408` for an upload that stalled. It wrote the answer and closed the connection with the rest of the body unread, and Linux then answers the client's next segment with RST rather than FIN. Chrome re-reads a response after a reset during an upload and usually still showed the status, but Firefox for Android, and any client without that special case, surfaced a network error, so the page reported that Huntsman did not answer when it had refused with a reason.

After: the refusal reaches the browser as the status it is. After writing the answer the server half-closes its write side, which sends the FIN behind the answer, and reads and discards what the request announced, at most 64 MiB and within the 90 s an admitted upload would have had, each read within the 5 s I/O timeout, so a client that stops sending ends the drain at once. The inspection place is given back before the drain, as before.

How: `read_request_with` in `src/web_server.rs` returns, with the request, how much of the announced body was left unread; `handle_stream_with` calls `drain_unread` after the answer is flushed when that is more than zero. Test: `a_refusal_during_an_upload_is_read_not_reset` holds the inspection place with a dribbling upload, sends a second 32 MiB upload, larger than any socket buffer, and checks every write succeeds and the `503` is read whole, then that the held upload still completes and is inspected once; on the baseline the second client's writes fail with a connection reset.

body:
`createDownedState` could snapshot a bleed-out but not resume one, so Scrap Signal rebuilt the state around a remaining-time countdown.

Root cause: `downed.ts` was in `check-stateful-ratchet`'s baseline from the day the ratchet shipped (#1576), and the check only polices primitives that appear after the baseline.

- `createDownedState` (`@jgengine/core/combat/downed`) gains `restore(next)`, the counterpart to `snapshot()`. A resumed bleed-out keeps its remaining seconds, revive progress, phase and banner timer. Scrap Signal can delete its countdown rebuild (`bleedoutSeconds = remaining`) and restore the saved entries instead.
- `findStatefulPrimitives` now reports which gap a primitive has: `state-out-only` (can snapshot, cannot resume — the invariant's class) or `no-state-out`.
- `check-stateful-ratchet` caps the `round-trip` group in the baseline (8, printed on every run), fails when it grows or when it is paid below the cap, and `--write` refuses to raise a ceiling, so the class cannot be re-grandfathered.
- Baseline: 113 entries at birth → 99 now; `round-trip` 9 → 8.
- `--root` on the check so fixtures drive it from `.scratch`.

Still open, same class (all baselined, not edited here): `areaEffectField`, `castRunner`, `hostedGameRunner`, `hostedWorldSession`, `selectionBookmarks`, `decayMeter`, `buildPermissions`, `buildSocketCatalog`. Two lose state their snapshot never carries: `castRunner.state()` drops the move budget (`moveTolerance`/`moveDeadzone`/`movedTotal`), and `decayMeter.snapshot()` drops rate modifiers set by `setRateModifier`.

author: osovlanski
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"osovlanski"} -->
_Requested by **itay** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TbJ6NyzVdjWotNBqSxg2JK?thread=cmsg_01TbJ6NyzVdjWotNBqSxg2JKERzoupELos6oCSa6kH6rVB)_

Closes the open finding from #108: every composed compare/race candidate got the task's whole remaining budget, so N candidates could together spend N times the cap.

## What changes

- **Core stage 5** takes an optional `budgetShare: { candidates: N }` input. With it, each candidate's token and cost caps are an equal share of the task remainder (`shareBudget`: tokens `floor(R/N)`, cost floored to the micro-dollar), so N shares never sum past R. Runtime is a per-run timeout and is not split. A share at or below zero fails `budget_exhausted` with the reason "the task's remaining budget cannot give each of N candidates a share".
- The stage keeps the task's own `task cap C, consumed U, remaining R` line and adds `parallel share 1 of N: S`. The why says `(equal share for each of N candidates composed together)`.
- **`TaskAccounting.latestTaskCaps`** reads C back from that pair, so a dispatch after a comparison carries the task cap and gets `C − everything consumed`, not a share.
- **`startParallel`** passes `budgetShare: assistantIds.length` through `composeForDispatch`. Without the input, a single start's inputs, decision and digest are unchanged.
- PROJECT_MEMORY: the #108 finding is replaced by what shipped, plus one new finding (below).

## Tests

- core: `shareBudget` for 2, 3 and 1001 candidates (sums never exceed the remainder, runtime not split), an exhausted remainder, a zero candidate count; stage 5 shares and evidence, a remainder too small to share, and no share leaves the stage unchanged.
- api (`provisioning-parallel.test.ts`): 2- and 3-way compare revisions get 5000 and 3333 of a 10000 cap with the evidence lines; after a compare with 4000+ tokens of usage records, a `run-now` recomposition gets `10000 − consumed`; a race whose share rounds to zero is refused with `budget_exhausted`, the task stays CREATED and no run exists.

Gate: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` green (core 584, adapters 146 + 1 skipped, web 83, api 1600 + 83 skipped).

## Drive

The API ran under tsx with the composer on, using fake-claude, fake-codex (codex harness) and fake-claude2, against real Cockpit main `760db1c` on loopback with a scratch HOME and one tagged skill. The cap was `maxTokens: 10000`.

- A 2-way compare gave both revisions `max_tokens: 5000` with evidence `task cap 10000, consumed 0, remaining 10000` and `parallel share 1 of 2: 5000`. The budget read afterwards showed 3300 consumed.
- A 3-way race gave all three revisions `max_tokens: 3333` and completed.
- With the plane restarted on `maxCostUsd: 0.000001`, a race answered 409 `fake-claude cannot start: budget_exhausted`. The task stayed CREATED, with 0 runs and one `run-now failed budget_exhausted` attempt.
- `demo:a` 1 passed, `demo:a5` 1 passed, `demo:b` 5 passed. These ran with a `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` shim, because the container now ships headless shell build 1243, not 1194.

**Not driven through the API: a dispatch after the comparison.** No route re-dispatches a compare task waiting for a pick, so this path is covered by the in-process test only:

- Run-now answers 409 `stale`, because compare tasks never park.
- `POST /handoff` fails at `git worktree add -b task/<id>`, because the comparison already made that base branch. The task is left in `HANDING_OFF`. This failure predates this PR and is recorded in PROJECT_MEMORY as a finding. It is not fixed here.

**Verdict: PASS**

author: tomixrm
body:
Closes #1732

## 原因
conflict 下書きは `std::fs::write`(truncate → write)で書かれ、load → merge → write がロックなしだった。同じ repo を 2 つの Kagi で開くと一方の決定が消え(実機再現)、途中で落ちると壊れた JSON が「下書きなし」として読まれていた。さらに同期的な保存(flock + fsync + rename)を Result の Change ごとに走らせると、この機械で p95 477 ms(3 ファイル 5 hunk 200 KB)で UI の閾値 4 ms を超えた。

## 変更
- 書き込みは ADR-0191 と同じ同ディレクトリ temp → `sync_all` → rename(crate 境界をまたぐため意図的に同じアルゴリズムを複製、`docs/decisions.md` に明記)。`.prev` を検証付きで残し、壊れた primary + 有効な prev なしは **空で上書きせず** `.corrupt[.N]` に退避して Failed receipt + EN/JA 通知(settings store と同じ)。
- `<draft>.lock` は fd ベースの advisory lock(std `File::try_lock`、約 2 秒の有界待機、プロセス死亡でカーネルが解放)。oplog の append / retention もこの helper に統一(ロック実装は 1 つ)。
- load → merge → write を hash / CAS でロック下に再マージ。独立した hunk 決定は 3-way で両方残る(A→B / B→A 同一)。同じ hunk / 手動の衝突はロック順で後の本文を live、他方を recovery に保持。
- 保存失敗後の preservation clone が古い disk を優先して最新編集を捨てない(Opus P2)。
- **順序付き・coalesce(≤250 ms)の背景 writer** API を追加: `queue_autosave()`(受理 ≠ 永続)、`DraftSave::wait()`、`flush()`、`has_unflushed_drafts()`、generation 検査。UI は現時点では従来の blocking `autosave()` のまま(消費側の切替は次の PR)。計測: capture p95 0.11 ms。
- 復元の非破損 I/O エラーは原因付きで EN/JA 通知し、render ごとの再検出ループをしない(Opus P2)。
- 形式検証: `draft-torn` / `draft-two-writers` / `draft-lost-update` を HOLD、`draft-crash` は flush 前の編集について正直に REFUTE のまま(無効な negative control は削除)。

## 検証
domain 909 / kagi-git 1513(子プロセス 2 writer 同一ファイル両順序、SIGKILL 後の再取得、半端 temp からの復旧、ロックタイムアウト、queue→restore の provenance 保持)/ Tier A `conflict_draft` 12/12 / workspace 3796 / clippy 新規なし / check-all / formal 54 checks(14 negative controls 赤)。
Tier B(実機、同じ `KAGI_LOG_DIR` を共有する 2 プロセス): **before**(834a1796)A の hunk 1 採用が消える → **after** 再起動後に hunk 1 の採用と hunk 2 の行チェックが両方復元(2/3)。refs / staged diff / 操作メタデータ / worktree / raw index 不変。

This supports the lean contract, not complete native observer coverage.

author: judahzf
body:
A new extension, **Sweep Synth** (`tetrad.sweep-synth` 0.1.0): two static, mono DSP blocks in the Synth list, **Sweep Synth** and **Bass Sweep Synth**. Each block mixes sub octave, dry, octave up and square wave voices into a resonant filter that restarts its sweep on each note, then an attack delay. It plays one note at a time, like the analog synth pedals that it models.

- **Half the CPU.** The blocks are mono (IR 2): 4.0% each in Tetrad's estimate, against 7.7% for the stereo synth in DSP Examples 0.2.0. Host renders are byte-identical to that block's channel A.
- **Own names.** The blocks no longer use the pedal maker's product names (JudahZF/qcdsp#5 renames qcdsp's example to `examples::sweep_synth`).
- **DSP Examples 0.3.0** drops its synth, so a unit with both extensions does not show the synth twice. 0.2.0 stays in the catalog. A preset saved with 0.2.0's synth plays its placeholder (Gain 0 dB) after an update to 0.3.0.
- **Published** in the default repository with tag `extensions-2026-10-24`. The catalog is signed with the default key (`c702 baa2 …`), and the old entries keep their tags.
- Docs: `docs/extensions.md` (list and a Sweep Synth section) and `extensions/repository/README.md`.
- qcdsp moves to JudahZF/qcdsp#5 (`9c74e99`). `tetrad-sharc`'s raw-machine test now runs the mono blocks.

Tests: `tetrad-extensions`, `tetrad-extension-cli` and `tetrad-sharc` pass, including the decode test of every published package. `tetrad-ext build`, `check` and `preview` pass for both packages. qcdsp#5 passes its corpus and emulator tests.

Not tested on a unit: the QC is offline. The mono copy path is already measured on a unit with the Saturator (2e-6), and the synth graph is the same as in DSP Examples 0.2.0.

body:

A full source audit established that all 23 registered routes remain reachable (including specialist/deep links) and should **not** be removed merely because only three appear on the primary navigation. body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Part of #19713.

Adds a reproducible nightly entry point for comparing DeepSeek V3.2 W8A8 on MRV1 and MRV2 with the official single-node A3 topology (DP2 + TP8 + EP + MTP + `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`).

The new harness:

- records the model revision, software/hardware configuration, complete serve command, and runner-specific environment;
- covers greedy and fixed-seed non-greedy generation, logprobs, and short/long Chinese, English, and code prompts;
- checks greedy token/text parity and logprob deltas across runners, plus fixed-seed reproducibility within each runner;
- retains cross-runner sampled-token agreement as diagnostic data because MRV1 and MRV2 use different RNG streams;
- records per-request TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, prefill/decode throughput, batch throughput, and peak HBM across configurable batch/sequence-length cases;
- writes raw accuracy responses, performance measurements, summaries, and regression findings to a JSON artifact.

This is a resource-heavy manual nightly test and is not registered for the PR 1/2/4/8-card runners. No production environment variables or user-facing configuration are added.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Test-only change; no release note fragment is required.

### How was this patch tested?

Local checks on Windows:

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed for the new file.
- `python -m compileall` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Direct helper checks passed for logprob deltas, fixed-seed result comparison, latency/throughput calculations, summary generation, missing-data rejection, and warmup exclusion.
- `coverage_taxonomy.validate_coverage_marker` accepted the new test's coverage metadata.
- Serve configuration checks confirmed DP2, TP8, EP, MTP, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, 65536 max model length, and model revision forwarding.
- In `bash format.sh ci`, Ruff, codespell, typos, clang-format, markdownlint, actionlint, and the other Python/package hooks passed. `check_logger`, `check_long_functions`, and `check_symbolic_meta` also passed when invoked directly with Bash/Python.
- The complete `format.sh ci` wrapper could not finish on Windows: several script hooks require `/bin/bash`, while `python3` and `shellcheck` are unavailable in the Windows PATH. The gitleaks helper also could not download its binary because `wget` is unavailable. These environment limitations are not being hidden as a green full-suite result; Linux CI remains required.

Not run:

- The 16-card A3 end-to-end test has not been executed because the requested Atlas 800I A3 (16 x 64GB) resource is not available yet. This PR is therefore opened as a draft.
- Local pytest collection was attempted but the existing Windows test environment lacks `huggingface_hub`; this does not provide NPU validation.
- Shellcheck and gitleaks did not complete locally for the Windows tool availability reasons above.

On the A3 resource, run:

```bash
DSV32_MODEL=/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8 \
DSV32_MODEL_REVISION=<immutable-commit> CANN_VERSION=<version> \
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/model_runner_v2/test_deepseek_v3_2_mrv1_v2_parity.py
```

The default output is `/tmp/deepseek_v3_2_mrv1_v2_parity.json`. Hardware results, accuracy tables, performance data, and conclusions will be attached to #19713 before marking the PR ready for review.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves boundary conditions. Full model-specific abnormal/boundary coverage remains part of #19713.
- [ ] **Regression test**: This PR adds comparison coverage; any runner regression found on hardware will be fixed or linked from #19713.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: Streaming responses without text or final usage fail explicitly; full model error-path coverage remains follow-up work.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: The new checks compare real MRV1/MRV2 behavior and preserve raw evidence rather than only checking process startup.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: No production performance-sensitive code is changed; hardware benchmark execution is pending the 16-card A3 resource.

author: trevo88423
body:
Closes #14

## What changes
Suspending or banning a member now takes effect on their next request, on every protected page and server action, through one shared check. The ban also ends their sessions.

- **`lib/auth.ts`**: `requireActiveUser({ requireAdmin?, requireVerified? })` for pages and layouts (redirects) and `requireActiveUserForAction(...)` for server actions (throws a typed `AccessDeniedError`). Both are built on `getUser()` plus `get_my_profile()`; `profiles.status` is the source of truth.
  - Suspended or banned: signed out (global scope), then sent to `/login?error=account_inactive` with fixed wording. Server Components can't clear cookies, so pages hand off to a new `/auth/inactive` route handler. It only signs out a member who really is inactive, so a link to it can't log anyone else out.
  - Unverified email goes to `/verify-email` with **no address in the URL**. The verify page now reads the address from the session when there's no `?email=`. The signup flow's `?email=` is left for #16.
- **Used everywhere**: the `/contribute` and `/dashboard` layouts and pages, `/my-contributions` (which had no status check before), `/admin` (`requireAdmin`), and every server action in `contribute/actions.ts`, `comment-actions.ts`, `completion-actions.ts` and `admin/actions.ts`. The admin file's internal `requireAdmin()` now calls the shared check, so each admin action's edit is one line.
- **Ban and suspend end sessions**: these admin actions also set `ban_duration` in Supabase Auth, which blocks sign-in and token refresh and makes GoTrue reject the member's existing access tokens. They then call a new service-role-only `revoke_user_sessions()`, which deletes the member's `auth.sessions` (refresh tokens cascade). Without that, old sessions would come back to life after a reinstatement. Warn and a new **Reinstate** action (shown under "Suspended and Banned" on /admin) set the ban back to `none`.
- **Login** refuses suspended and banned members with fixed wording. That covers both the Auth block (`user_banned`) and status-only bans from before this change.
- **Migration `20261024121400_reject_inactive_members_writes.sql`** adds `is_current_user_active()`. Comment, vote and completion inserts and deletes, and contribution and comment updates and deletes, now reject suspended and banned members at the DB level, as do flags (`increment_comment_flags`). Before this, only contribution inserts checked status. It also adds `revoke_user_sessions()` (EXECUTE for `service_role` only) and the `reinstate` moderation action. It's idempotent and safe with the current app code: active and warned members pass as before, and admin writes use the service role.

## Fit check
- **Philosophy:** no `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md` in this repo. This is a moderation and security fix: moderation has to actually work.
- **Stop lines:** none crossed. No new data collected; emails stay out of URLs (#16 untouched).

## Verification (local stack only)
Test users `member14`, `admin14` and `bystander14` (`@example.test`) were created through the local admin API. The admin was set via psql. Member and admin used separate hosts (`member14.localhost` / `admin14.localhost`) so their cookies didn't mix.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Active member: /contribute, /dashboard, /my-contributions, add comment, vote | ✅ works |
| Admin clicks **Ban** while member is signed in | `profiles.status=banned`, `auth.users.banned_until` set, moderation log entry |
| Member's next page load (/dashboard) | → `/login?error=account_inactive` with the fixed message; session cookie cleared |
| /contribute, /dashboard, /my-contributions, /admin after ban | all redirected away |
| Member signs in again (login form) | refused: "This account has been suspended or banned…" |
| Leftover refresh token after ban | GoTrue: `user_banned` |
| Admin **Suspend** (after Reinstate) | status `suspended`, Auth blocked, `auth.sessions` for member → 0 |
| All 18 server actions called directly (`Next-Action`) with the member's old cookie after suspend | all refused; DB unchanged |
| Status-only ban (no Auth block, live session, like pre-existing bans): each of the 18 actions with a fresh session | all throw "This account is suspended or banned."; first call clears the cookie |
| Status-only ban: direct PostgREST writes with member's valid JWT (contribution/comment/vote/completion insert, comment update/delete, vote delete, flag RPC) | inserts 403 (RLS), flag RPC 403, updates/deletes affect 0 rows; DB unchanged |
| Status-only ban: login | 403 with fixed wording, no session cookie set |
| Admin **Reinstate** | member signs in, pages load, can edit comment |
| Normal member (`bystander14`) throughout | unaffected: pages load, `markWordComplete` works |
| Non-admin on /admin and calling `reinstateUser` | redirected to `/`; action throws "Admin access required." |
| Signed-in member with unconfirmed email (temporarily nulled) | → `/verify-email` (no email in URL); page shows address from session |
| `revoke_user_sessions` via anon key | `permission denied`; via service role: sessions and refresh tokens deleted |
| Migration applied twice locally | idempotent |
| `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` | pass (also after merging current `main`) |

## Notes
- After a ban the member's sessions are deleted, so GoTrue answers `session_not_found` before `user_banned`. Their next request then lands on `/login` without the inactive banner, and they see the fixed message as soon as they try to sign in. When a live session still exists (status-only bans, or if the revoke ever fails), they get the banner straight away.
- The login's `user_banned` message tells whoever types that email address that the account is blocked. That's a small disclosure, accepted for clear wording.
- `app/reset-password/actions.ts` (#15) is account recovery, not a member write. Auth already refuses a blocked member's recovery link, so it's left unguarded.
- Existing banned members in production have no Auth block; the app and RLS checks still refuse them. Re-banning them from /admin adds the block.
- Not in scope, and spotted but not changed: `comment_votes` has no UPDATE policy, so switching a vote's direction silently does nothing.

body:
## Linked issue

See the **Related** block at the end. The tracking issue deliberately stays open after this merges: it collects every failed nightly, and its last three reds were three different flaky E2E tests. This PR fixes one of them.

- [ ] This issue exists and a maintainer **explicitly agreed it in a comment** before this PR was opened.
- [x] The issue is **labelled** — exactly one type and at least one `area:*` — and its title reads as the nightly reporter writes it.
- [x] **This PR carries its own labels and milestone.**

## Intent (what & why, in human terms)

The nightly gate on master was red on `1e5b20f4` (run 39883310554) for one reason only: `window-chord-resolution.e2e.ts:398` — "from a focused real terminal, Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Numpad0, Ctrl+Shift+Alt+M and Ctrl+Shift+Alt+PageDown reach the app and the shell receives nothing (046 T049)" — failed twice and passed on its third attempt, and the gate treats a flaky test as a failure.

## Outcomes (what changed, in human terms)

- **Cause — a test defect, not a product one.** The probe read the terminal's live write log in a 0 ms timer queued from the chord's keydown, assuming the new project's layout reply was queued behind it. The window dispatcher's capture listener runs first, so the layout request is already in flight; on a slow runner the reply won, the view unmounted, and its log was gone before the timer fired. Unmounting the view on a project switch is correct behaviour.
- **Fix.** The renderer's terminal diagnostics keep a bounded copy (the 8 most recent) of each unmounted view's final state, exposed to tests as `__throngRetiredTerminalDiagnostics`; the live store is unchanged. The test now waits for the view to leave and reads that copy — everything the view wrote up to its unmount, with no timing in the read. The assertion is unchanged: nothing from the chord reaches the shell.
- **Also fixed: a component-test flake found by this PR's own CI run** (40086868072): `drag-no-entry.test.ts` "keeps `copy` when a target chose it". `mountExplorer` returned as soon as the tree was in the DOM, which can precede that commit's passive effects — among them the tree's window `dragover` listener, which must follow react-dnd's to override it. A listener-order probe caught the two failures in ~176 loaded runs with react-dnd's listener registered and the tree's not yet; the harness now flushes effects with `act()` before returning, and 192 loaded runs then registered both, in order, every time.
- **Not fixed here:** the two earlier reds were other flaky tests — `tab-presentation.e2e.ts:222` (run 37085645106) and `explorer.e2e.ts:409` (run 39352560229).

- [x] `npm run test:unit` — green: 597 files, 8,302 tests. `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` green. The two new tests in `terminal-diagnostics.test.ts` were watched failing before the change.
- [ ] `npm run test:integration` — not run locally; CI.
- [ ] `npm run test:contract` — not run locally; CI.
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` — the affected spec only, `window-chord-resolution.e2e.ts`: 9/9 on five consecutive local runs at one worker with no retries; a deliberately injected keystroke still fails it ("Ctrl+Shift+Alt+PageDown reached the shell"). Full suite on CI: `________`
- [ ] Any user-facing UI change ships **passing E2E coverage** — N/A, no user-facing change.
- [ ] New OS-abstraction seams have **contract tests** — N/A.
- [ ] `@admin` / elevation-dependent behaviour — N/A.

- [x] **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — unaffected.

## Constitution compliance

body:
## Description

Two additions to FitQuest (`fitai-app/`): a gym pass (opens the Synergym app, optional saved QR) and a meal plan that hits the user's calorie and macro targets.

## What changed

- Gym pass (`gym.js`): "Open Synergym" via an Android intent link (default package `digifit.android.virtuagym.pro.synergym`, editable), optional saved QR screenshot shown full screen. No Synergym credentials are read or stored.
- Meal plan (`recipes.js`, `meals.js`): 56 recipes (breakfast, lunch/dinner, snacks) with nutrition computed from ingredient weights. Diet (any, pescatarian, vegetarian, vegan), allergen avoidance, 3 to 5 meals a day, and a cooking-time limit per day (15, 30 or 60 min). Portions are scaled to the calorie target and chosen to match protein, carb and fat targets. Swap per meal, shuffle the week, weekly shopping list with checkboxes and copy, warnings when filters leave few recipes.
- Game hooks: logging a meal earns XP, plus a new "Eat 3 planned meals" daily quest.
- Plan tab now has Training / Meals switch; Today shows a meals card. Service worker v7.

## Results

In a headless phone browser: full flow (setup, day view, recipe, mark eaten for XP, shopping list), no page errors. Checked 6 diet/time/meal-count configurations over a week: calories within ±1% of target on every day; recipes never exceeded the day's cooking time except when filters left nothing faster, which the UI warns about. Average macros on a fat-loss day were 143/160 g protein, 204/195 g carbs, 67/65 g fat. Found and fixed two bugs along the way (setup screen not refreshing after building the plan, a leaked click listener). Not tested on a real phone or against the real Synergym app.

## Notes

Nutrition figures are estimates, not dietitian advice. Only `fitai-app/` changed; no Python files.

- [ ] `ruff check .` reports no warnings
- [ ] New behaviour is covered by a test

## Qué cambió

- Nuevo `docs/optimizaciones.md`: registro de optimizaciones investigadas sobre `dev`, **sin cambios de código de la app**.
  - **6 mejoras seguras**, cada una con archivo y línea, costo actual, cambio propuesto, por qué es seguro y cómo comprobarlo.
  - 2 mejoras de riesgo bajo. La de mayor impacto está medida: sacar `three.js` del chunk de entrada baja ese chunk de 1 105 kB a 356 kB (312 a 112 kB gzip) al cargar `Hud` y `DioramaOverlay` con `lazy`. La landing sigue descargando three.js por su vista previa 3D; la ganancia es en el primer render, no en bytes totales. Medido con un build temporal, ya revertido.
  - Ideas descartadas y por qué.
- `docs/README.md`: se añade el documento al índice.

## Las 6 mejoras seguras

1. `DioramaRuntime.tsx:314`: un `Set` de conceptos se reconstruye en cada frame dentro del diorama.
2. `shared/sources.ts`: `locateFragment` re-normaliza todos los apuntes por cada pieza.
3. `server/cache.ts`: la caché expulsa por orden de inserción (FIFO), no por uso (LRU).
4. `server/images.ts`: no se deduplican peticiones simultáneas idénticas a Wikimedia.
5. `Landing.tsx:182-183`: `dueCountFor(saved)` se evalúa 3 veces por render.
6. `Hud.tsx:149-150` y `memory/hooks.ts:43`: `allConcepts(palace)` se recalcula varias veces por render.

## Cómo revisarlo

- Leer `docs/optimizaciones.md` y contrastar las referencias de archivo y línea con `dev`.
- El impacto es estimado por inspección de código, salvo los tamaños de chunk, que salen del build.

author: chumva
body:
Follow-up to #26525 for #20551 (problems 2-3 of the [second review](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd/issues/20551)).

## Problem

`PhoneNumberFormatter` regroups two kinds of numbers wrongly on the POI card:

- **+7 numbers with a 4- or 5-digit area code** (Kazakhstan, Russian regions) get the 3-digit plan even when the mapper wrote the right grouping: `+7 7172 123456` → `+7 717 212 34 56`.
- **International prefixes longer than `00`** are read as `00` + a country code: Australia's `0011` makes `001161298765432` a US number, `+1 161 298 765 432`.

## Fix

- When a known plan (+1, +7, +33) does not fit the number's length, the country code was misread: the number is shown as written instead of being grouped generically.
- For +7, a 4- or 5-digit area code written by the mapper is kept. A 3-digit one is still normalised: `+7 (727) 123-45-67` → `+7 727 123 45 67`.

Calling and copying still use the stored value, as before.

## Verification

JVM test `PhoneNumberFormatterTest` (3 cases added), about 25 s per run:

| | master [be64519](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd/commit/be6451993c0) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `+7 7172 123456` | fails: `+7 717 212 34 56` | passes |
| `001161298765432` | fails: `+1 161 298 765 432` | passes |
| other cases | pass | pass (4 tests, 0 failures) |

```
./gradlew :OsmAnd-shared:jvmTest --tests net.osmand.shared.util.PhoneNumberFormatterTest
```

Device: Redmi Pad Pro (2405CRPFDG), Android 16, `gplayFreeOpenglArm64Debug`, UI in Ukrainian. GPX waypoints with `amenity_phone` / `amenity_mobile`, opened from My places > Tracks > Points:

| Stored value | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `+7 7172 123456` | `+7 717 212 34 56` | `+7 7172 123456` |
| `+7 8442 12-34-56` | `+7 844 212 34 56` | `+7 8442 12-34-56` |
| `001161298765432` | `+1 161 298 765 432` | `001161298765432` |
| `+7 (727) 123-45-67` | `+7 727 123 45 67` | `+7 727 123 45 67` |
| `+79123456789` | `+7 912 345 67 89` | `+7 912 345 67 89` |
| `0033612345678` | `+33 6 12 34 56 78` | `+33 6 12 34 56 78` |

Not verified: iOS and web (the code is common Kotlin without platform calls); RTL, dark theme and font scale (the change only affects which text is shown).

## Known gap

- An ungrouped +7 number with a long area code (`+77172123456`) is still split 3-3-2-2: without area code data the formatter cannot know where the code ends.
- Prefixes that are read as a country without a plan (Taiwan `002`, Brazil `0021`) are still converted to `+`.
- Generic 3-3-4 grouping for other countries (`+44 207 946 0958`) is unchanged; `testGenericGroups` keeps it as intended.

## AI disclaimer

Produced with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).

Prompts used (summarised):
1. Look at issue #20551.
2. Fix the remaining problems and verify on the tablet or an emulator.

Decided by the agent, not requested explicitly: the scope (Kazakhstan / long +7 area codes and the `0011` prefix, not the generic grouping), keeping such numbers as written rather than regrouping them, the test cases, and the GPX waypoints used for the device check.

body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing! Quick checklist / 提交前快速自查 -->

- [x] I added **one file** at `data/plugins/mr-mihu__dsh-dbhub-live.yml` — that single file is the whole submission. I did not touch either README or any other entry. / 只新增了一个 `data/plugins/mr-mihu__dsh-dbhub-live.yml`，没有改 README、也没有动别人的条目
- [x] My repo's `package.json` declares **`dsh.bundle`** (not just `dsh.client`) — `{ "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } }`, with `cordis.patch.yml` beside it; verified through the API at `main` @ `2bef25f` (tag `v5.2.0`) / 仓库 `package.json` 已声明 `dsh.bundle`（只有 `dsh.client` 无法安装）
- [x] My repo is at least **1 day old** — created 2026-08-18 / 仓库创建满 1 天
- [x] `category` is `tools` (one of the listed ids), matching the other database plugins / `category` 取值正确
- [x] Description states what the plugin does, no superlatives, and every clause maps to code below / 描述只说功能、不带营销词，逐条对应下方证据
- [x] My repo has the `dsh-plugin` topic / 仓库已打 `dsh-plugin` topic

**Recommended (not required) / 推荐但不强制：**

- [x] 📦 Published to npm — `dsh-dbhub-live@5.2.0`, and the package's `repository` field points back at this repo. No `tarball:` field needed; the GitHub release also carries a tarball / 已发布 npm，`repository` 指回本仓库；条目不需要 `tarball` 字段
- [x] 🔗 Official `@deepseek-ai/*` packages are `peerDependencies`, with **explicit prerelease branches per tuple** (the node-semver pitfall documented in `contributing.md`) / 官方包为 `peerDependencies`，并按 contributing.md 的要求写了每个 patch 元组一段的预发布分支
- [ ] 🖼️ Screenshots: nothing added in this PR (the convention is a `screenshots.json` in the plugin repository). I will add it there in a follow-up commit; until then storefronts can fall back to README images / 本次 PR 不加截图；截图按约定放在插件仓库，稍后单独补

## What it is

`dsh-dbhub-live` connects [DBHub](https://github.com/bytebase/dbhub) — Bytebase's database MCP server — to DeepSeek Harness. The plugin owns the DSH-side integration (workspace/environment-scoped connection store, credential handling, settings UI, tool surface); the SQL execution, engine dialects, read-only enforcement and tunnel plumbing are DBHub's.

Concretely: a user configures connections per workspace and per environment (`default`, `prod`, `dev`, any name including Chinese). The agent sees a `source` handle and metadata shaped like `mysql://host:3306/db`, never a password and never a DSN. It can configure a connection (credentials are collected by the UI, not by the tool call), list sources, run SQL, and search objects. Each call spawns its own short-lived `dbhub` process; there is no daemon and no shared port.

The four tools are fixed (`dbhub_configure`, `dbhub_list_sources`, `dbhub_execute_sql`, `dbhub_search_objects`) no matter how many connections exist, so the tool surface does not grow with the configuration.

## Relationship to the database entries already on the list

I read the existing entries before submitting — `blkpne/dsh-database`, `STARDUSTLC666/dsh-sql`, `mengqi1436/dsh-db-tool`, `JohnXu22786/db-connector`, `xing-he888/dsh-database-explorer` — and they are all more feature-complete than this one as *administrators*. Rather than claim a difference that is not there, here is what is actually different, all verifiable in the code:

| | existing entries | this entry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| execution | own driver layer / own SQL engine | delegates to the **DBHub MCP server**; if you already run DBHub, this is the same engine from inside DSH |
| credential model | connection configured from the UI (varies per plugin) | **no `dsn` tool argument exists at all** — a `dsn` argument is refused (`result.noDsnViaModel`), and a test asserts no tool declares one |
| connection identity | one connection list | **workspace × environment** sources: a source belongs to exactly one workspace, look-alike connections are never interchangeable, ambiguous references return candidates instead of guessing, and cross-workspace reuse is a server-side copy |
| remote access | — | **per-environment manual SSH tunnel** (single hop, key or password) with a **separate SSH-layer probe**, so a tunnel failure is reported as a tunnel failure rather than as a database error |
| process model | usually a persistent pool | **one short-lived process per call**, no daemon: a hung query cannot wedge the next one |
| read-only | per connection or per grant | **per environment**, enforced by DBHub's `[[tools]] readonly`; the model may enable it but is refused when clearing it (user-only action) |

The UI work in 5.2 (dialog / full-page / phone layouts, version and update check, a model-facing access-policy prompt section) is secondary — I mention it only because the description names the layouts.

If a maintainer judges this covered by an existing entry, say so and I will withdraw it — I am not asking for a slot on tenure grounds.

## Claims in the entry, and where they live (`main` @ `2bef25f`, v5.2.0)

| Claim | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| four fixed tools | `lib/tools.mjs` — `dbhub_list_sources` :866, `dbhub_configure` :939, `dbhub_execute_sql` :1019, `dbhub_search_objects` :1051 |
| MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server | `lib/tools.mjs` :766 (picker), :968 (schema enum) |
| passwords / full DSN never accepted as tool arguments | `lib/tools.mjs` :496 (`result.noDsnViaModel`); `lib/i18n.mjs` :50; asserted by `test/zero-knowledge.test.mjs` :5 and :31 |
| model sees metadata such as `mysql://host:3306/db` | `lib/config.mjs` — `connLabel` / `describeEnvOptions`; `test/zero-knowledge.test.mjs` :31 (`summarizeRows` is metadata-only) |
| per-environment read-only, enforced by DBHub | `lib/toml.mjs` :114-119 (two `[[tools]]` with `readonly = true`); `lib/config.mjs` `readOnlyOf`; `test/toml.test.mjs` |
| the model may enable read-only but not clear it | `lib/tools.mjs` :506 (`result.readOnlyUserOnly`) |
| manual SSH tunnel per environment | `lib/config.mjs` :204 `normalizeSshOptions`, :244 `DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH`, :255 `withDefaultSshKey`; independent layer probe `lib/adhoc.mjs` `probeSshTunnel`; `test/configure-ssh.test.mjs`, `test/ssh-probe.test.mjs` |
| one short-lived dbhub process per call | `lib/adhoc.mjs` :394 `runAdhoc`, :426/:432 argv, :486 `terminate()` |
| dbhub installed automatically when missing | `lib/runtime.mjs` :3 (install-once prefix; a user-managed dbhub is never overwritten) |
| DSH 0.2.1+ gets the adaptive layouts | `lib/meta.mjs` :22 `DSH_MODERN_BASE`, :241 gate; `lib/client.js` :1163 `modern`, :2407 `dbh-modern` |
| model-facing access-policy section | `lib/policy.mjs` :41 section id, :45 order 8900; `test/policy.test.mjs` |

## Version support

DSH 0.1.5 through the 0.2.1 line (prereleases included) is exercised on a per-release matrix: six pinned DSH versions boot a real `dsh web` with an isolated home and are probed end to end. The current table, with per-version evidence, is in `doc/SUPPORT-MATRIX.md` and the README's collapsed “supported version range” section. `0.1.x` keeps the previous layout; the new UI starts at `0.2.1`.

## Extras

- npm: `dsh-dbhub-live@5.2.0` is published and its `repository` field points back at this repo, so the storefront mapping can pick it up. No `tarball:` field is needed; the GitHub release also carries `dsh-dbhub-live-5.2.0.tgz`.
- Screenshots: the repo does not declare `screenshots.json` yet. If that is wanted I will add it in a follow-up commit (paths `doc/images/settings-page.png`, `doc/images/chat-query.png`, `doc/images/row-editor.png`) rather than putting URLs in the entry — happy to wait for the list's preference.
- Tests: 24 test files, including the zero-knowledge gate that enforces the credential claim above.

대표 2026-10-24 「행 열 간격 정리 해라」 · 「빨간색 팝업은 어떻게 정리해야 칸넓게 안늘어나는지도 검토해라」.

- **행·열 맞춤** — 접힌 줄의 이름 칩이 같은 폭 칸(`grid` · `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(…, 1fr))`)에 선다. 줄마다 세로 열이 맞는다. 칸 수는 화면 폭을 따라 준다(PC 6칸 · 폰 2칸).
