author: gaojunran
body:
## What and why

The terminal mirrors Ghostty's keymap, but three groups of Ghostty's default chords never reached the shell.

**Cmd+Backspace did nothing.** Ghostty's macOS "natural text editing" defaults send Ctrl+U for Cmd+Backspace and Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E for Cmd+Left/Right. Those chords land on the stand-down that leaves every Super chord to the app's menu accelerators, and no accelerator registers them, so the key was swallowed. They now send the line-editing bytes.

**Option+Left/Right only worked at a plain prompt.** Ghostty binds them without the performable flag, which means they apply on every screen and for Kitty keyboard programs too; the old translation checked the screen and the Kitty flags first, so vim's insert mode got a modified arrow key instead of a word motion. They now always send ESC+b/f. Option+Backspace was translated to Ctrl+W, a byte no terminal emulator sends for that key; it keeps the key encoder's native output again (ESC+DEL, `CSI 127;3u` under Kitty).

**The viewport scroll chords scrolled nothing.** Cmd+Home/End/PageUp/PageDown on macOS and Shift+the same keys on Windows and Linux scroll the terminal's own viewport in Ghostty and never reach the pty. They now scroll exactly like the scrollbar keys.

Deliberately left alone: Cmd+K (Ghostty's `clear_screen`) needs a clear-screen call the pinned `libghostty-vt` ABI does not expose, so it stays a dead key rather than an invented behavior.

## Affected surfaces

Terminal input is shared UI; the change is in the key path every surface uses.

| Runtime | Behavior after this change |
|---|---|
| Web | Same chords as the desktop shell, plus Cmd+Left/Right now `preventDefault` while the terminal is focused, so the browser's back/forward gesture no longer fires. |
| Desktop (Electron) | The intended target: Cmd+Backspace, Cmd+Left/Right, Option+Left/Right, Cmd+Home/End/PageUp/PageDown reach the shell; unregistered Cmd chords still stand down for menu accelerators. |
| VS Code | Same shared key path. |
| Hosted mobile | Not applicable: no hardware Cmd/Option modifier. |
| Capacitor mobile | Not applicable: same reason, and touch input has its own path. |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun test packages/ui/src/lib/ghostty` | 90 pass, 0 fail — includes new unit cases for the three helpers and real-surface integration cases driving the real WebAssembly encoder (line bytes, no spurious Kitty release, alternate screen, app-cursor mode, Kitty flags, scroll claiming the key). |
| `bun run check:changed` | Pass: type-check, lint, Knip at zero, anti-slop ratchet unchanged. |
| macOS hand check, dev server in the browser, fish 4.7.1 | Cmd+⌫ deletes to the line start, Cmd+←/→ jump to line start/end, Option+←/→ jump by word, Option+← by word in vim insert mode, Cmd+PageUp/Home scroll the viewport, all repeated under a Kitty keyboard session (`\x1b[>11u`), and Cmd+B, Cmd+C, plain PageUp and IME input are unchanged. |

**Live run:** Web dev server on macOS in the browser, driving the real shell through the terminal panel: the chords above behaved as listed against fish 4.7.1, and inside vim. Not run through the packaged Electron build, which shares this key path.

One note for the reviewer, because it looks like a regression that is not: Option+Backspace on `foo/bar` now deletes the whole token in fish, while Ctrl+W deletes only `bar`. That is fish's own split (it binds Alt+Backspace to `backward-kill-token` off macOS and to `backward-kill-word` on macOS, and Ctrl+W to `backward-kill-path-component`), and it is what every terminal emulator produces for that key. The old Ctrl+W byte made bash and zsh delete more than the key asks for.

## Visual evidence

No visible change: these are key bindings, so the diff cannot alter anything rendered.

## Risks

- A future menu accelerator that registers Cmd+Backspace, Cmd+Left/Right or Cmd+PageUp would now lose to the terminal while it is focused. Ghostty resolves this the same way, and none of the current accelerators use these keys.
- On the alternate screen the scroll chords consume the key and scroll nothing, matching Ghostty; programs that bind Cmd+Home/End/PageUp/PageDown themselves cannot receive them.
- Rollback is deleting the three helpers and their call sites; the removed `core.encodeMacWordShortcut` had no other caller.

author: yaeldillies
body:
We had two conflicting instances of `CompleteLattice (WithTop <| WithBot α)` from `CompleteLattice α`: one going through `ConditionallyCompleteLattice α` and adding the top and bottom elements simultaneously, and another one adding them one by one by first going through `CompleteLattice (WithBot α)`. These didn't agree because `sSup ∅` on `WithTop α` would be defined as a junk value even if `α` already happened to have a bottom element.

Changing `sSup ∅` on `WithTop α` to be a bottom element if one exists leads to a better solution: have an instance deducing `ConditionallyCompleteLattice (WithTop α)` from `ConditionallyCompleteLattice α`, and another one deducing `CompleteLattice (WithTop α)` from `ConditionallyCompleteLattice α` + `OrderBot α`, and similarly for `WithBot`.

This is strictly more general than the previous instances, and avoids the diamond.

author: alesaiani
body:
`props-are-read` holds every prop a component declares to being read. It found a descriptor's props only when they came first, or (since #627) right after `variants`. Most value controls open their descriptor with `models` (#125, #135), so 32 components were skipped silently, and none of their props was ever checked.

## What changes

- **The scan.** It steps over each top-level entry of a descriptor until it reaches `props`, with strings and comments stepped over whole and brackets balanced. It has no backtracking regex (CodeQL flagged one in #657). It also reads every registration of a module: `pdx-toggle.ts` registers two.
  - It now reaches **114** components, every registration with a props block, against 82 before.
  - The floor of the "not vacuous" case is raised to 114.
- **What the wider scan found.** 18 props: `name` on 17 value controls, and `pdx-switch.value`. The issue said 19, which was a miscount.
  - All 17 declare a model `{ form: true }`. Core's `wireFormModel` (`packages/core/src/form/form-model.ts`) reads the host's `name` (line 138), which the form submits under, and the declared `value` (line 135), a boolean model's checked value. It reads them there, not in the component's module, so the scan could not see the reads.
  - The test now counts those two as read for a component whose own descriptor declares a form model. A new case holds them to those two lines of form-model.ts, so the exception goes away when core stops reading them.

## Review

1. **Did the test that passes now pass before?** Not with the wider scan. Widened, it was red with exactly those 18 findings until the form-model reads were recognised. An unread prop added to `pdx-switch`, a models-first component, fails the test now. The previous scan never reached that component. Measured by adding `probeNeverRead` and reverting it.
2. **Is the check really there?**
   - The category applies only to a descriptor that declares a form model, not to a module-wide `name`.
   - It covers only `name` and `value`, the two props `wireFormModel` reads by name.
   - Any other unread prop of a models-first component fails.
3. **Is the gate green?** The pre-push passed: ui 2349, core 4694, compiler 6517, router 665, lsp 420, cli 1028, plus the browser suites and benchmarks. The ui test typecheck passes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The scan reads every component with a `props` block: 114, against ~82 before.
- [x] Every finding is read or recognised with a reason. The 17 `name`s and `pdx-switch.value` are read by core's form model, and that is held to its source. The test is green.
- [x] A prop added to a models-first component and read by nothing fails the test.

## Not verified

- Whether every one of these components needs `name` declared as a prop at all, given core reads the attribute. Declaring it keeps it in the manifest and the editor's completion, so it is not dead API. This PR does not change it.

Closes #658

body:
## What changed
- `gitGuard.ts`: `.git/config` compared semantically, not byte-exact. Allowed changes, nothing else:
  - `[branch "<own>"]` entries for the stage's own branch only (passed from `sandboxRunner` into `snapshotGitControl`), keys limited to remote, pushRemote, merge, rebase, description, gh-merge-base; `remote`/`pushRemote` must name a remote that has a url in the pre-stage config, never a URL.
  - `remote.<existing-with-url>.gh-resolved`.
- Anything else refused + whole file restored: other branches' sections, URL/unknown remotes, core, alias, filter, include, credential, url, new remotes, deleted config. Integration-harness containers pass no branch → no branch config allowed.
- Parser mirrors git: ASCII whitespace only, values decoded like git parse_value (quotes, escapes, comments, bare key vs empty), BOM; unparseable config (continuations, malformed lines) → refused. `info/attributes` still byte-exact.
- Prompt: `git push -u origin` → `git push origin`.
- Fixes false park seen on nivnoiman/chatlane#2.

## How tested
- `gitGuard.test.ts`: own-branch push -u/gh-merge-base passes (incl. BOM/CRLF); refused + restored: other branch, remote/pushRemote URL, unknown remote, gh-resolved on unknown remote, no own branch, hooksPath, alias, filter, include, remote url, new remote, header/continuation/quoting tricks, deleted config, attributes.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (1022 passed); sandboxRunner test proves branch wiring end to end.

author: richardvzyl
body:
## What

The web board ignored NIP-34 `maintainers` tags on lane events (kind 30617), so status events from lane maintainers didn't count and cards showed in a different column than the CLI.

- `spa/src/lib/board.ts`: parse lane maintainers and count their status events in `deriveCard`; `fetchBoard` passes them through; `attachChannel` fetches the newest lane event and keeps all its tags when re-publishing (so maintainers aren't dropped).
- `spa/src/lib/board.test.ts`: tests for maintainer status moves, non-maintainer rejection, and tag preservation.
- README: one line documenting maintainer permissions.

## Verification

- `tsc` passes, `vitest` 44/44 passes, production build passes.
- Parity check against the CLI on a live lane: 120 cards, 0 status mismatches (before this change, a card moved by a maintainer showed in Backlog on the web).

Draft: not for merge yet.

author: elio-swello
body:
## Pourquoi

Closes #59

Empilée sur #29 (`chore/infra-tests`).

Retour d'Elio : « j'aimerais également des filtres pour n'afficher que certaines entités ». Sur la démo, la vue 3D affiche 26 boutons répartis sur 19 étiquettes, et certaines se chevauchent : le volet de la cuisine cache sa température.

## Quoi

- **Rangée de puces en haut de la vue 3D** (`LabelFilter`) : une puce à icône par catégorie présente dans la maison (Lumières, Climat, Volets, et Ordinateurs dans l'appartement). Chaque puce mesure 44 × 44 px. L'icône est ambre quand la catégorie est affichée, grise quand elle est masquée. Le nom s'affiche dans une infobulle au toucher. La rangée mesure 148 × 52 px et se place à 16 px du haut de la vue.
- **Table `labelCategories`** (`src/utils/labelCategories.ts`), seul endroit à compléter : catégorie → libellé, icône, types d'items. `climate` et `temperature` partagent la catégorie « Climat ». Un type absent de la table reste toujours affiché.
- **Mémorisé par appareil** : `hiddenCategories` rejoint les options d'`AppContext`, stockées dans `graphics-options`. On stocke les catégories *masquées*, pour qu'une catégorie ajoutée plus tard s'affiche d'office. `OptionRow` exclut cette clé, qui n'est pas un interrupteur.
- **Les étiquettes de pièce se filtrent aussi** : chaque élément d'une étiquette de pièce suit sa catégorie, et l'étiquette est démontée quand elle n'a plus d'élément. Sans cela, la puce « Lumières » ne servirait presque à rien, puisque 12 des 13 lumières de la démo sont dans une étiquette de pièce.
- **Les lumières 3D restent allumées** : `Room3d` filtre la liste passée à `Room`, mais pas celle de `RoomItem3d`.
- **Démontage plutôt que `display: none`** : une étiquette masquée n'a plus de `useFrame`, de racine React ni de DOM.

Une autre branche ajoute son type en une ligne :

```ts
{id: 'plug', label: 'Prises', icon: PowerIcon, types: ['plug']},
```

## Comment vérifier

```sh
E2E_PORT=4630 pnpm test:e2e e2e/filtres-entites.spec.ts
```

Maison `demo`, mock, à 1280 × 800 : toucher « Volets », puis « Lumières ». Les étiquettes correspondantes disparaissent, l'éclairage de la maison ne change pas, et le choix est conservé après rechargement.

Mesures sur le build de production de la démo (Chrome avec GPU, Mac, 1280 × 800, DPR 2, CPU bridé ×4 pour le mouvement et les appuis, `__dashboardMotionBenchmark(120)` et métriques CDP) :

| Mesure                                  | Avant      | Après, tout affiché | Après, tout masqué |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------- | ------------------ |
| Draw calls par image au repos           | 46         | 46                  | 46                 |
| Programmes compilés pendant la rotation | 0          | 0                   | 0                  |
| Tâches longues pendant la rotation      | aucune     | aucune              | aucune             |
| Recalcul de style par image en rotation | 0,6–0,8 ms | 0,6–0,7 ms          | 0,1–0,2 ms         |
| Temps de tâche par image en rotation    | 3,1–3,8 ms | 2,7–2,9 ms          | 1,7–2,2 ms         |
| Nœuds DOM                               | 280        | 290                 | 105                |

Entre « Avant » et « Après, tout affiché », les écarts relèvent du bruit de mesure. Un appui sur une puce compile 0 programme et rend 1 ou 2 images, puis plus aucune dans la seconde qui suit. L'interaction dure de 24 à 56 ms. Réafficher les lumières ou le climat remonte de 7 à 18 étiquettes, ce qui produit une tâche longue de 50 à 100 ms (CPU ×4), une seule fois et hors rotation. Le budget de l'ADR 0009 est respecté.

Ces mesures portent seulement sur la démo : le sous-module `apartment` est absent de ce worktree, et le mock ne simule pas ses entités.

## Définition de « terminé »

- [x] Spec : `docs/specs/filtres-entites.md` (fonctionnalité)
- [x] ADR : `docs/adr/0033-filtre-des-etiquettes-par-categorie.md` (décision structurante)
- [x] Documentation à jour (`docs/guides/filtrer-les-etiquettes.md`, index `docs/README.md`)
- [x] Tests unitaires (`src/utils/labelCategories.test.ts`)
- [x] Tests E2E (`e2e/filtres-entites.spec.ts`, 5 scénarios)
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e` passent (E2E : 3 fois en parallèle et 1 fois avec `CI=1`)
- [x] Budget de performance respecté (ADR 0009), si le rendu est touché

Remarque pour la fusion : la branche `feat/mode-veille` modifie la même ligne d'`OptionRow`. La résolution donne `Exclude<keyof ConfigurationOptions, 'hiddenCategories' | 'screensaverMinutes'>`.

author: jorgenspange
body:
## Problem

`nxos_igmp_snooping` only manages the global on/off switch and four global settings through flat parameters and the legacy `state: present|default`. It cannot manage the per-VLAN `vlan configuration <id>` context (static groups, multicast router ports, the IGMP querier and its timers, report filters), the global `ip igmp snooping vxlan` that is required for snooping on VXLAN VLANs, or `disable-nve-static-router-port`; it has no `gathered`, `rendered` or `parsed` states, no replaced or overridden semantics, and its example used an option (`optimize_mcast_flood`) that does not exist.

Two device behaviours also make `nxos_config` a poor substitute: `no vlan <id>` leaves `vlan configuration <id>` and its settings behind (an orphan), and a lone `no ip igmp snooping static-group ...` creates an empty `vlan configuration` block and reports a change on every run.

## Solution

**This is a breaking change.** The module is rewritten as a resource module (argspec / config / facts / rm_templates) and keeps its name. The flat parameters and the `present` and `default` states are removed. The migration of every removed option and state is listed in the `breaking_changes` changelog fragment (for example `link_local_grp_supp` becomes `config.link_local_groups_suppression`, `state: present` becomes `state: merged`, `state: default` becomes `state: deleted`).

The module covers the whole IGMP snooping surface of the platform, globally and per VLAN:

```yaml
config:
  snooping: true
  group_timeout: "300"                 # 1-10080 or never
  link_local_groups_suppression: true
  report_suppression: true
  v3_report_suppression: false
  vxlan: true                          # ip igmp snooping vxlan
  disable_nve_static_router_port: false
  max_gq_miss: 3                       # 3-5
  syslog_threshold: 90                 # 1-100
  holddown_timer: 210                  # 1-300
  proxy:
    general_queries: true
    mrt: 8                             # 1-25, not 5
  vlans:                               # one `vlan configuration <vlan_id>` block each
    - vlan_id: 100
      snooping: true
      querier: 192.0.2.1               # IGMP snooping querier address
      querier_timeout: 255             # 1-65535
      query_interval: 125              # 1-18000
      query_max_response_time: 10      # 1-25
      startup_query_count: 4           # 1-10
      startup_query_interval: 100      # 1-18000
      robustness_variable: 2           # 1-7
      last_member_query_interval: 1    # 1-25
      version: 3                       # 2 or 3
      fast_leave: false
      explicit_tracking: true
      group_timeout: "300"
      link_local_groups_suppression: true
      report_suppression: true
      v3_report_suppression: false
      proxy:
        general_queries: true
      proxy_leave_use_group_address: false
      mrouter_interfaces:
        - port-channel20
      report_flood:
        all: false
        interfaces:
          - port-channel20
      report_policy:                   # one policy per interface
        - policy_type: route_map       # or prefix_list
          name: RM_REPORTS
          interface: port-channel20
      access_group:
        - policy_type: route_map
          name: RM_GROUPS              # without interface: ip igmp snooping access-group RM_GROUPS
      static_groups:
        - group: 224.0.208.85
          source: 192.0.2.10           # optional
          interfaces:
            - port-channel20
            - Ethernet1/10
state: merged                          # replaced, overridden, deleted, gathered, rendered or parsed
```

- Everything the old module could configure is expressible (`state: default` is `state: deleted`).
- The IGMP querier of a VLAN (`querier`, `querier_timeout`, `query_interval`, `query_max_response_time`, `startup_query_count`, `startup_query_interval`, `robustness_variable`, `last_member_query_interval`, `version`) is managed in the `vlan configuration` block. A VLAN without PIM needs a querier; with several queriers the one with the lowest address wins.
- NX-OS does not show a setting that has its default value, so a value equal to the default counts as unset: it sends nothing when the device already has it and removes the line when the device has another value. The defaults are in the module notes.
- The module never sends the `vlan configuration` context when the diff is empty, so it is idempotent where `nxos_config` is not.
- `replaced`, `overridden` and `deleted` remove orphan `vlan configuration` blocks (`no vlan configuration <id>`). `replaced` and `overridden` return everything in a listed block that is not given to its default.
- Global commands are sent before any `vlan configuration` block. Interface names are normalised (`Eth1/10`, `Po20` become `Ethernet1/10`, `port-channel20`).
- Validation before anything is sent: numeric ranges, IPv4 addresses, `proxy.mrt` needs `general_queries: true` and cannot be 5 (the device removes the line for the default value), and a `report_policy` and an `access_group` cannot use the same interface (the device keeps one policy per interface and the second replaces the first).
- Not managed: `event-history` (debug buffer sizes), `optimise-multicast-flood` (the command does not exist on the tested platform) and the hidden `evpn` sub-commands.
- New for a resource module: `nxos_facts` knows `igmp_snooping`, the module has fresh examples for every state and a cisshgo molecule scenario.

## Testing

### Unit and static checks

- 76 unit tests for the module (parsed, rendered, gathered, merged, replaced, overridden, deleted, orphan blocks, empty diff, name normalisation, `source` variant, idempotency, every global and per-VLAN option, defaults, validation, a VLAN `group-timeout` that must not become a global one); the old test and the old integration scenarios are carried over as equivalent tests for the new interface (parity). Full nxos unit suite passes.
- pre-commit hooks, ansible-lint (production profile), validate-modules, pep8 and yamllint pass; the docs generation passes.

### Hardware (N9K-C93180YC-FX, NX-OS 10.6(4))

Run on two switches with the same changes in the same window on a scratch VLAN, everything reverted (`show running-config diff` empty afterwards):
- `gathered` on a clean switch returns the defaults; `merged` of the global settings and of a VLAN with every option set is accepted in the order the module sends, stored as written and idempotent; the gathered data fed back as `merged`, `replaced` and `overridden` is empty.
- Setting an option to its default on a clean VLAN sends nothing and creates no block; on a VLAN with other values the module sends the valued `no` forms or the positive command and the lines are gone.

body:
## Summary
This PR records the approved U-1 design contract for switching between CSRF observation mode and enforcement mode. It is documentation only.

- New file: `docs/audit/web-bff-csrf-v1-mode-contract-2026-10-24.md`. That is the only file changed.
- Base: `develop@de4fed3`, which includes #3323, #3324 and #3325. All three references were read and left unchanged.
- **A-0 and L4 remain NOT APPROVED.** No runtime implementation or mode-switching mechanism exists, and no environment or production change is authorized. Do not merge; STOP.

## Decisions recorded (design only, §1)
- **U-1a = A:** explicit server-side mode configuration.
- **U-1b = A:** fail closed when the mode configuration is missing or invalid.
- **U-1c = A:** manual switching only, after an explicit Mother Ship authorization.

## Contents
- **§2 Mode configuration.**
  - A server-only `WEB_CSRF_MODE` with the values `observe` and `enforce`. The name is a proposal (U-1h).
  - There is no implicit default. No client input — header, query, cookie or body — can select the mode.
  - The mode is read once at request entry, and the same D0–D13 evaluator runs in both modes.
  - No automatic or time-based change.
- **§3 Invalid configuration.** Unset, empty, unknown or ambiguous values fail closed with the existing rejection contract: 403 `{"detail":"forbidden"}`, `no-store`, no `Set-Cookie`, no backend call, no refresh, the body not read. Nothing ever falls back silently to `observe`.
- **§4 `observe`.**
  - The same rules are evaluated and would-be rejections are logged, using only the route, D-row, reason code and a mode marker.
  - Requests continue as they do today. **CSRF exposure remains during observation.**
  - `DELETE /api/users/me` keeps its existing `isAllowedOrigin` decision, so observation does not weaken it.
  - The instrumentation does not exist yet and needs A-0.
- **§5 `enforce`.** D0–D13 applied exactly, rejection before the body is read, JSON-only (A-4), logout-failure behaviour (A-5), and the `users/me` reconciliation as in contract §4.3.
- **§6 Runtime failures.**
  - F-1, invalid mode: fail closed in every mode.
  - F-2, D0: logged and processed in `observe`; 403 in `enforce`.
  - F-3, internal evaluator error: 403 in `enforce`; in `observe` it is **U-1d, a Mother Ship decision**. Fail-open is not authorized.
- **§7 Manual switching (M-1 to M-6).**
  - A recorded decision, the target mode and environment, the revision, evidence, confirmation that the change took effect, and a recovery plan.
  - A configuration change alone is not proof that the mode changed.
  - There is no automatic promotion. Going from `enforce` back to `observe` is a rollback under O-5 / O-6.
- **§8 Future tests T-1 to T-12**, which require A-0.
- **§9 Dependencies.** A-0, L4, A-3, A-6 (O-1 to O-6), A-7 (the clock starts at the V-1 implementation PR merge and is not reset), A-8, U-2 to U-6, and S-6, the rest of S-8, and S-14.

## Unresolved (§9.2)
- **U-1d:** what happens after an internal evaluator error in `observe`. `observe` must not ship until this is decided.
- **U-1e:** whether the A-4 JSON-only 415 is enforced in `observe` or only recorded.
- **C-1:** confirm that the D0 fail-closed rule in contract §3.5 applies to `enforce`, and the rollout plan §2.1 to `observe`.
- **U-1h:** whether the name `WEB_CSRF_MODE` needs its own approval.

## Checks
- `markdownlint -c .markdownlint.json` on the new file: clean. One MD038 warning in the first commit was fixed in `2831206`; the content did not change.
- Repository hooks ran on the commits and pushes, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Runtime code, routes, cookies, auth, environment variables, production and deployments: none touched.

author: bborbe
body:
## What

The second coverage gap the #101 review named: the reconcile floor has its own eligibility path and nothing pinned it against the event path. **No behaviour change** — four table entries plus a CHANGELOG bullet.

## Why it matters

`reconcileTask` does not see the Kafka event the event path filters — it re-derives eligibility from the in-memory task view on every pass. It shares `isForeignCluster` and the stage check today, so there is no divergence now; but nothing asserted that. If the two paths ever disagree, the floor spawns a task the event path refuses, and for a stage-mismatched or pinned task that is a run on the wrong cluster — precisely the duplicate this work exists to prevent.

## Tests

Four entries: a matching stage with no pin is re-driven; a stage mismatch, a pin naming another cluster, and a pin naming this cluster outside its stage pool are each not re-driven.

The first entry is a **spawn-expected control**. Without it a table of three zeros would pass if the harness were broken, which is the vacuous-pass shape this repo has already been bitten by.

`make precommit` green.

## Note

Complements #145 rather than duplicating it: that one pins the *reporting* label for the event path, this one pins the *spawn decision* on the floor.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"HuAxX27"} -->
_Requested by **TheHuAx** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01B8zdXNFJmsUpogKMT4vmyp?thread=cmsg_01B8zdXNFJmsUpogKMT4vmypEWjRjgHZ6EchLuMbixqMgS)_

Ticket: ninguno. Lo pidió TheHuAx para que las sesiones de la laptop instalen los `.deb` en el iPad sin preguntarle; los artefactos de Actions piden iniciar sesión y la laptop no tiene `gh`. TheHuAx aprobó publicar los `.deb` como pre-release público.

## Summary

- **`ios-ci.yml`, job nuevo `Publish the .debs (pre-release)`.** Después del build del iPad, `ios/toolchain/publish-debs.sh` sube sus `.deb` a un pre-release público: `ipad-main` en cada push a `main` e `ipad-pr-<N>` en cada push a un PR de este repo (el token de un fork no puede escribir releases). Mueve el tag al commit que armó, sube los `.deb` con `--clobber` y quita los que esa corrida ya no armó, como el de una versión anterior. Si mientras tanto llegó un commit más nuevo o el PR se cerró, no publica nada. Solo este job tiene `contents: write`, y corre de uno en uno por pre-release.
- **`ios-debs-cleanup.yml`**: al cerrar un PR, fusionado o no, borra su pre-release y su tag. Lo fusionado sigue en `ipad-main`.
- **`ios/toolchain/fetch-debs.ps1`**: `fetch-debs.ps1 -Pr 93 -Package chiakiport` baja el build del último commit del PR (sin `-Pr`, el de `main`) desde la API de GitHub sin sesión, revisa el tamaño y el sha256 que lista GitHub, y lo instala con `deploy.ps1 -BatchMode`. Si ese commit todavía se está armando o falló, se detiene y lo dice; `-AllowStale` instala el anterior. `-NoDeploy` solo baja. Para un PR de un fork baja el artefacto con `gh`. Compatible con Windows PowerShell 5.1 (TLS 1.2, `-UseBasicParsing`, UTF-8 con BOM como `deploy.ps1`).
- **`deploy.ps1 -BatchMode`**: SSH no pide contraseña (falla) y se rinde a los 15 s si el iPad no contesta, así una sesión de Remote Control no se queda colgada. `-SetupKey` ahora sirve sin `.deb` en la carpeta.
- **Docs:** `ios/toolchain/README.md` (sección nueva "Bajar e instalar lo del CI", la tabla de archivos y el CI), `docs/ipad/guia-de-pruebas.md` (secciones 1 y 2, como pidió A0) y la línea de pruebas en el iPad de `CLAUDE.md`.

GitHub avisa a quien sigue el repo cuando se publica un release nuevo: será un aviso por PR (el primer push), no uno por cada push. No cambia `lib/` ni ningún contrato.

## Tests / verification

- **De punta a punta, en el CI de este PR:** el job `Publish the .debs` creó [`ipad-pr-97`](https://github.com/HuAxX27/IpadMini-Chiakiport/releases/tag/ipad-pr-97) con los tres `.deb` (`ckctl` 0.3.2, `ckdirect` 0.2.1, `ckhola` 0.1.0), su sha256 en las notas, y GitHub lista el mismo `digest`. `fetch-debs.ps1 -Pr 97 -Package ckhola -NoDeploy` lo bajó sin sesión y pasó la revisión de tamaño y sha256.
- `publish-debs.sh` con un `gh` falso: crea tag y release la primera vez; la siguiente mueve el tag, edita el release y quita el `.deb` de la versión anterior; no publica si el commit ya no es el último o si el PR está cerrado.
- `fetch-debs.ps1` en PowerShell 7.4 en Linux:
  - Contra la API real: PR inexistente, PR sin pre-release y `main` sin pre-release fallan con su mensaje.
  - Con la API simulada: baja todo, filtra con `-Package`, falla si no coincide ningún paquete, se detiene ante un build viejo, `-AllowStale` lo instala, falla si el sha256 no coincide, vacía la carpeta en cada corrida y llama a `deploy.ps1`.
- `deploy.ps1 -BatchMode` contra un puerto cerrado falla con el aviso de la llave; con `-SetupKey` se niega.
- `actionlint`, `shellcheck` y `.github/quality/check.sh` en verde.
- Falta Windows PowerShell 5.1 en la laptop: la primera sesión de Remote Control que instale un PR con esto lo prueba (A4 y A6 lo esperan).

## Design docs

Design docs: updated `docs/ipad/guia-de-pruebas.md` (cómo baja e instala TheHuAx o un agente) e `ios/toolchain/README.md` (los detalles); `CLAUDE.md` nombra el comando.

author: wjr-z
body:
新增通用的多秩选择与一维线性分位数，复用整批请求的划分过程，避免逐个 quantile 重新选择完整源。

- `partition_at(values, ranks)` 原地定位多个有序目标秩，允许重复；源为连续借用 view，ranks 只读，不分配工作区。
- 共享三点采样 pivot，用标准库 partition 形成小于/等价/大于区间。请求首尾即可 O(1) 判断整批同侧；全左时跳过第二次 partition。等价值区间一次满足所有相关请求。递归请求较少侧，另侧循环；退化预算耗尽使用 sort，单秩复用 nth_element，端点秩复用 min/max_element。
- 小区间阈值和预算倍率使用私有 `inline constexpr` 常量 `partition_sort_cutoff`、`partition_depth_factor`，不保留 magic number 或公开微调策略。
- `quantile_inplace_to` 避免数据副本；`quantile_to` 使用调用方数据和秩工作区保留源。概率可乱序/重复，输出保持查询顺序，所有相邻插值秩一起选择。源 dtype 保持至最终插值，避免提前转 double 丢失大整数排序信息。
- 支持传播/忽略 NaN、空域、无穷的明确插值合同，以及 source/query/output 正 stride 和 padded 的相应子集。有限插值复用 C++20 lerp；没有隐藏分配、输出预清零或运行时通用校验框架。

附示例、完整语义/成本文档和四种选择策略基准：共享 pivot、平衡请求 nth_element 分治、升序缩短后缀选择、完整排序。所有基准均包含复制恢复输入，quantile 基准还包含秩构建、排序和插值。覆盖均匀/中部聚集/低端/高端请求及 int64/double。

验证：Clang 18/C++20、C++23、ASan 和 MSVC 19.38/C++20 各通过 10 项针对性 GTest 与示例；含真正插值的 C++20 static_assert、512 项 NaN/Inf/零的同侧/equality-block 测试、预算耗尽 fallback。GCC 12/C++20 示例通过；仓库 benchmarks target MSVC Release 构建通过。新增文件显式 stage 后 clang-format 全量 hook 和 diff 检查通过。额外子代理只读审查未发现阻塞问题。

Windows x64、i5-13500HX、Clang 18、Release baseline 初测（每组3次，随机交错）：N=65536 的 257 个分散秩约 2.08ms，平衡 nth_element 为 2.46ms、升序后缀为 6.93ms、完整排序为 3.38ms；double 的3/31个 quantile 完整流程约 0.71/1.38ms，对照完整排序插值为 3.84/3.75ms。小输入直接排序仍可更快，没有据此加入请求密度调度。未采集硬件分支/缓存计数；NaN 数据集性能和 Linux 性能尚未本机测量，不承诺普遍加速或全平台零开销。

边界：partition 首版仅一维连续数据；quantile 首版仅 linear，不含加权/多轴/多线程。单秩 nth_element 的最坏复杂度仍依赖标准库，自有预算不能扩大为整个算法的纯标准最坏保证。本机老 MSVC 的既有完整 NP expression_math 整数分类重载问题不在此 MR 范围；本机 GCC win32 线程工具链未运行 GTest。

author: jorgenspange
body:
## Problem

`nxos_l2_interfaces` has no way to manage per-interface spanning-tree and storm-control settings, and no other cisco.nxos module does either. Host ports need `spanning-tree bpduguard enable`, `spanning-tree port type edge [trunk]`, `spanning-tree guard root` and `storm-control broadcast level <n>` on many interfaces, so users fall back to `nxos_config`, which is not idempotent against decimal storm levels and cannot replace or remove lines per interface.

## Solution

New options in `nxos_l2_interfaces`, next to `access`, `trunk`, `mode`, `link_flap`, `cdp_enable`, designed for NX-OS:

```yaml
spanning_tree:
  port_type: edge | edge_trunk | network | normal
  bpduguard: true | false        # enable / disable, unset = no line
  bpdufilter: true | false
  guard: loop | root | none
  cost: 100
  port_priority: 64              # multiple of 32, 0-224
  link_type: auto | point_to_point | shared
  mst:
    - instances: "0,2-4"
      cost: 10
      port_priority: 64
  vlans:
    - vlans: "1,3-5"
      cost: 10
      port_priority: 64
storm_control:
  broadcast:
    level: "0.01"                # also multicast and unicast
  action: shutdown | trap
```

- `merged` adds and changes, `replaced` and `overridden` remove the lines that are not listed (`no spanning-tree ...`, `no storm-control ...`), `deleted` removes all of them for the listed interfaces. An empty diff emits nothing.
- Storm levels are decimals, validated 0-100 with at most two decimals and compared numerically (`1` equals `1.00`). `port_priority` must be a multiple of 32 within 0-224 and an mst `cost` at least 1; invalid values fail before any command is sent, so no partial configuration is left behind.
- Values equal to the device default are not shown by NX-OS (storm level `100.00`, link type `auto`, port priority `128`, `cost auto`), so they count as unset; lines the device does show (`port type normal`, `bpduguard disable`, `bpdufilter disable`, `guard none`) stay explicit values.
- The options apply to layer-2 interfaces only. An interface counts as a switchport only when it has a `switchport` line, or no `no switchport` line while the system default is switchport; for any other interface `merged`, `replaced` and `overridden` fail before a command is sent, because the interface-level commands do not exist on a routed port and the CLI would fall back to the global spanning-tree commands. This costs one extra `show running-config all | include 'system default switchport'` per run, and only when `spanning_tree` or `storm_control` is configured.
- Interface-level `storm-control ... level pps` is not supported by this module: N9K-C93180YC-FX with NX-OS 10.6(4) accepts it but never stores or shows it, so it could never converge.
- Notes document that spanning-tree settings on a vPC port-channel must be identical on both peers and belong on the port-channel, not on its member ports.

## Testing

### Unit and static checks

- 61 unit tests for the module (34 before): parsed, rendered, gathered, merged, replaced, overridden, deleted with the interface block above, removal of a single line, tri-state `bpduguard`, mst and vlan lists, validation errors, decimal comparison, default values as unset, routed ports refused, idempotency. Full nxos unit suite passes.
- pre-commit hooks and the docs generation pass.

### Hardware (N9K-C93180YC-FX, NX-OS 10.6(4))

Run on two switches; everything applied on a spare shut port was reverted (`show running-config diff` empty afterwards):
- `gathered` (87 interfaces) and `parsed` from the device output are equal; `rendered` of a full sample is correct and normalised; `merged`, `replaced` and `overridden` with the gathered data fed back are empty in check mode.
- A full configuration (16 commands) is applied; the second run is empty and `gathered` returns exactly the input. `replaced` with a smaller configuration removes exactly the right lines and `deleted` removes all of them.
- With the switches in MST mode (`spanning-tree mode mst`, both vPC peers together, reverted afterwards): `mst` cost 10 and port priority 64 on a port-channel took effect (`show spanning-tree mst 0 interface ... detail` shows them); `spanning-tree vlan ... cost` is accepted and stored but ignored in MST mode; on a spare port `mst` and `vlans` were applied, idempotent and round-tripped through `gathered`.
- Every removal form the module uses is accepted by the device and effective: value-less `no spanning-tree bpduguard|bpdufilter|guard|cost|port-priority|link-type`, `no spanning-tree mst|vlan <list> cost|port-priority`, `no spanning-tree port type [edge|edge trunk]`, `no storm-control <type> level [<n>]`, `no storm-control action <action>`.
- Invalid values (`port_priority: 48`, `mst cost: 0`) fail before any command; default values listed by the user produce no command and a reset when the device shows a different value; a routed, unconfigured port is refused with a clear message and left unchanged.

### Repository integration tests

- New case `spanning_tree_storm_control.yaml` for the `nxos_l2_interfaces` target; it was not run on a switch.
- The existing `l2_interfaces` molecule/cisshgo scenario is extended with four hosts (merged, replaced, deleted and a gathered host with the block above, one play each); it runs in this PR's CI and involves no hardware.

### Not tested / platform limits

- The new integration case on a real switch.
- Interface-level `level pps` (accepted but not stored on this release, not supported), `storm-control multi` variants, and cost ranges other than the mst minimum, which the device enforces.
- vPC port-channels were deliberately not changed on one peer only (a mismatch makes the vPC type-1 inconsistent); the identical-on-both-peers requirement is documented in the module notes.

author: zsomborrajki
body:
## What this changes

The watch's trail-following GPS now runs only for a map that can show it. `WatchFollowClaim` remembers which trail its screen asked for and is told which trail the watch holds. It also hears the scene leave and return, so the feed stops when the app goes to the background and restarts on the way back for a map still asking. A return is a restart: the tracker forgets where the hiker was before the gap, and the figures wait for a new fix.

Fixes #1022

## Why

Two cases in #1022 left the `kCLLocationAccuracyBest` receiver running with nothing on screen reading it:

- **(b) A map waiting for trail B, with trail A held.** `WatchModel` passed `holdingTrail: trail != nil` (any held trail) to `screenAppeared` and `recordingStopped`, so B's waiting screen got `.start` and every fix advanced A's tracker.
  - The model now passes `trail?.followableHikeID`. `WatchTrailPackage.followableHikeID` is the package's ID once it `isDrawable` (the same test `TrailMapScreen` draws by), and `nil` for a one-point package. The claim compares it with the trail its screen named, so a waiting map starts nothing until its own trail lands.
  - `screenAppeared` and `trailArrived` also answer `.stop` when the held trail is not the claimant's. That covers the next map appearing before the previous one's `onDisappear`, where the previous map's feed would otherwise keep running under the new one's waiting view.
- **(a) The app leaving the screen with a map still pushed.** That map gets no `onDisappear`, and the receiver has `allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates` and the `location` background mode for the recorder's sake.
  - `OpenHikesWatchApp` now reports `scenePhase` to `WatchModel.sceneMoved(onScreen:)`, starting from the initial phase: `.background` counts as leaving, `.active` as returning, and `.inactive` as neither.
  - `WatchFollowClaim.appLeftScreen` stops the feed unless a recording owns it, and keeps the claim. `appReturned` answers `.restart` only for a claimant whose trail is held.
  - While the app is off screen, nothing starts the feed: not a trail landing, not Stop, not a map appearing.

A return answers `FeedChange.restart`, not `.start`, because the hiker walked on while nothing was matched.

- **What the model does with it:** it forgets the tracker's continuity anchor and clears `WatchFollowState`, then starts the feed. `resumeRecording()` does the same across a pause.
- **Without that:** take a 6 km out-and-back left at km 1 and reopened at km 5. It read about 17% done with 5 km left, and stayed on the outbound leg all the way home, because the ±1000 m window around the old anchor holds only the outbound leg there.
- **The figures:** they also showed the pre-background reading as current until the first new fix.

This makes the documented behaviour true: the `startFollowingFeed()` header and AGENTS.md *The watch app* both say that following without a recording updates only while the app is on screen.

## How it was verified

Final runs on the branch rebased onto `main` at `ca2c394a`:

- [x] `Scripts/lint.sh` passes (exit 0)
- [x] `swift test --package-path OpenHikesShared -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` passes (exit 0, 466 tests in 53 suites), and again with `--configuration release` (exit 0, 466 tests in 53 suites). `swift test --package-path OpenHikesData -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` passes too (exit 0, 160 tests in 21 suites).
- [x] `xcodebuild build -scheme OpenHikesWatch -destination 'generic/platform=watchOS Simulator'` succeeds (exit 0)
- [x] New behaviour has a test that fails without the change. The old API cannot express "which trail", so I checked by mutation:
  - On the first commit: putting back main's "any held trail counts" (`held != nil` in place of the ID comparisons) fails 5 tests in `WatchFollowClaimTrailTests` and `WatchFollowClaimOnScreenTests`.
  - On the first commit: putting back main's "leaving the screen does nothing" fails `leavingStopsTheFeedAndReturningRestartsIt`.
  - Answering `.start` instead of `.restart` from `appReturned` fails 4 tests with 5 issues. One of them is the out-and-back reading in `returningLetsGoOfThePosition`, which goes back to the outbound leg.
  - Dropping `isDrawable` from `followableHikeID` fails `onePointTrailIsNotFollowable` with 3 issues.
- Not run: the app and widget unit tests and the UI tests, because no app or widget code changed. `WatchFollowClaim` and `followableHikeID` are used only by the watch. Nothing was exercised on a watch or a watch simulator; this repository has no watch test bundle.

The suites:
- `WatchFollowClaimTrailTests` covers whose trail it is, including a one-point trail.
- `WatchFollowClaimOnScreenTests` covers the scene phase, including a return that drives a `WatchRouteTracker` through the out-and-back.
- `WatchFollowClaimTests` moves to the new signatures. Its one changed expectation: a map opening with no trail held now answers `.stop` instead of `.unchanged`. The stop is harmless when nothing is running, and it is the answer that stops another map's feed.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

- **Product call: `.inactive` stops nothing.** The issue left this open. Only `.background` stops the feed.
  - A lowered wrist makes the app the inactive frontmost app on every watch: dimmed with Always On, and dark on the models whose screen turns off.
  - Apple documents that the frontmost app stays in the foreground until Return to Clock moves it to the background. That is two minutes by default, longer if the hiker changed it ([Taking advantage of frontmost app state](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/watchkit/taking-advantage-of-frontmost-app-state)). So the feed runs for that window after the wrist drops.
  - Stopping at `.inactive` instead is a one-line change in `OpenHikesWatchApp`: treat `.inactive` as `.background`. It would save GPS for that window, but it would also stop and re-acquire the feed at every glance away, notification and Control Center pull.
- **The feed restarts at `.active`, not at the first phase out of the background.** The review asked whether Core Location starts a When In Use feed from `.inactive`.
  - One developer's watchOS 11 and 26 trace shows the app's `scenePhase` reading `.inactive` before `applicationWillEnterForeground` is called ([forum thread](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/806734)). So the old `phase != .background` could start the feed while the app was still in the background.
  - Waiting for `.active` is the safe choice, and costs nothing a hiker would see. It is not verified on a watch.
- **A background launch that builds no scene cannot leave the feed on.** The review also asked about this case. Nothing claims the feed without a map on screen, and the first phase the scene reports when it is built sets `isAppOnScreen`. This is read from the source and not verified on a watch.
- **Product call: a held trail that is not drawable counts as not held.** A package with fewer than two points draws the waiting view and gives an unusable tracker, so the feed no longer starts for it either.
- **Overlap with #1043 (issue #1021, not merged).**
  - That PR moves Stop's `recordingStopped` call into a new private `recordingEnded()`, fired by `WatchRecorder.onRecordingEnded`, and rewrites `recordingStopped`'s doc comment.
  - After this PR, that call is `applyToReceiver(followClaim.recordingStopped(holding: trail?.followableHikeID))`, and `recordingStopped(holding:)` keeps its signature.
  - With #1043, a session that fails off screen answers `.unchanged` and leaves the feed to the return, which is a `.restart` (`recordingEndingOffScreenWaitsForTheReturn`).
- **Not changed here: two older gaps where the anchor also goes stale.** A map popped and reopened after a long walk, and a Stop pressed after a long pause. Both start the feed with `.start` and keep the tracker's anchor. They behave this way on `main` too.
- Precedent: #1006 (issue #996), the claimant-ID half of the same type.

author: entanglesoftware
body:
Brings the Go SDK to the standard of Google's and Stripe's Go client libraries.

## Runtime
- **Per-call options**: every method takes a trailing `opts ...RequestOption`, so existing calls compile unchanged. Options: `WithRequestHeader`, `WithRequestTimeout`, `WithRequestMaxRetries`, `WithExtraQuery`, `WithExtraBodyField` (parameters this version does not know yet), and `WithResponseInto(*ResponseMeta)` for the status, headers and request id of a successful call.
- **Logging**: `WithLogger(*slog.Logger)` logs each attempt, retry and refresh. A test proves keys, secrets and tokens never reach the log.
- **User-Agent** `cruworldwine-go/<v> go/<v> (<os>; <arch>)`, plus `WithAppInfo(name, version, url)`.
- **Credentials stay on their host**: redirects to another host or from https to http are refused, and a market must be a market code.

## Quality gates
- golangci-lint v2 (govet, staticcheck, errcheck, revive, gosec, errorlint, misspell, …): 0 issues, generated code included.
- govulncheck: clean on the current Go patch release.
- Fuzz tests for the tolerant decoder and request encoding; leak tests (bodies closed, no goroutines left).
- Coverage 91% without the captures (was 59%); all 168 real API answers replay.

## Repository
- CI: gofmt, vet, golangci-lint, govulncheck, race tests on Go 1.23, 1.24 and stable (Linux) and stable (macOS). Actions pinned to commit SHAs.
- Release workflow on `v*.*.*` tags: tests, tag-matches-Version check, GitHub Release from the CHANGELOG, proxy.golang.org warm-up.
- API compatibility check on PRs (apidiff), failing on incompatible changes unless labelled `breaking-change`.
- Dependabot, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, issue and PR templates.

## Breaking
The added variadic `opts` changes 39 method signatures: calls are unaffected, but code that stores a method in a variable of the old function type does not compile. Hence the `breaking-change` label. Behaviour changes are listed in the CHANGELOG.

No tag or release: `CHANGELOG.md` keeps this under `[Unreleased]` until v0.1.1 is cut.

author: nateisern
body:
## What

Development bundles of `packages/app` now use Noxcturnal, Expo SDK 58's oxc transformer. This follows OxyHQ/Mention#1618 and OxyHQ/oxy#1953 (`@oxy.so/app-preset` 4.0.0).

Noxcturnal runs only when the Babel config is the bare Expo preset and Metro has no custom Babel transformer. Alia had both problems: a custom Babel config (module-resolver, worklets plugin, `unstable_transformImportMeta`, the dynamic-import and export-namespace-from plugins) and `react-native-svg-transformer`. Either one sends every file back to Babel.

- **`babel.config.js`** is now `module.exports = require('@oxy.so/app-preset/babel');` with the preset bumped from `^3.3.0` to `^4.0.0`. In development that is bare `babel-preset-expo`. In production it adds the preset's build-id inliner, which Alia's own config never had. `@oxy.so/services` now busts its persisted caches on each production build, as it does in the other Oxy apps.
- **`@/` alias:** it resolves from `tsconfig.json` `paths` (`@/*` → `./src/*`, the same target as the old module-resolver). `vitest.config.ts` already had the same alias. `babel-preset-expo` 58 adds the worklets plugin and the `import.meta` transform itself.
- **Flag:** `experiments.noxcturnalTransformWorker: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` in `app.config.ts`. The app doesn't use the `withOxyAppPreset` plugin. `@expo/config-types` 58.0.3 doesn't declare the flag yet, so the `experiments` object is typed wider. Production exports stay on Babel because Noxcturnal 0.1.9 keeps the requires inside dead `Platform.OS` branches.
- **SVG:** `react-native-svg-transformer` is removed. Nothing imports an `.svg` as a component, so no files needed converting. Also removed: the Metro `babelTransformerPath`, the `svg` sourceExts/assetExts change and the `declare module '*.svg'`.
- **xterm:** `agent-terminal.tsx` now loads xterm through a platform-split module (`xterm.web.ts` on web, a types-only `xterm.ts` on native). Native only ever runs the WebView terminal, so xterm also leaves the native bundle. Without this, the Android dev bundle fails: Noxcturnal 0.1.9 can't transform `@xterm/xterm/lib/xterm.js` for Hermes (`Identifier 'n' has already been declared … captured-loop-post-rewrite-semantic-error`). This is a hard error, not a fallback.
- **Expo:** `expo` is bumped to `~58.0.19`, which brings `@expo/metro-config` 58.0.17 and `noxcturnal` 0.1.9. 0.1.5 mis-parses TS generic arrows. The Expo modules are aligned to what 58.0.19 declares (`expo install --check` is clean) in both the app and the root `overrides`. The hoisted `@expo/metro-config`/`noxcturnal` copies were moved to 58.0.17/0.1.9 in place; the lockfile was not regenerated.
- **One `react-native-css`:** main had two copies: the app's 3.0.7 and Bloom's own 3.1.0-rc.0. Under Noxcturnal, 8 of Bloom's wrapped components (Image, ActivityIndicator, FlatList…) required their own module id in the web dev bundle. The root `overrides` now pin `react-native-css` 3.1.0-rc.0 and `nativewind` 5.0.0-rc.0, which is what Bloom's peer range expects; the app's own entries match. This is the same fix as oxy#1954 and Mention. After it, the web dev bundle has 0 self-requires. `@alia.onl/sdk`'s peer range (`react-native-css ^3.0.7`) is left as it is, because changing it would mean an SDK release.
- **Dependencies removed:** `babel-plugin-module-resolver`, `@babel/plugin-syntax-dynamic-import`, `@babel/plugin-transform-export-namespace-from`.
- **Docs:** `docs/app-architecture.mdx`.

## Measured (`LOG_EVENTS`, `--dev --clear`)

| | Modules | Noxcturnal full | Fallback to Babel | `transform:failed` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Android | 6044 | yes | 509 (8.4%) | 0 |
| Web | 4691 | yes | 246 (5.2%) | 0 |

author: fbmoulin
body:
## Problema

`audit.rotate_logs` só rodava no `create_app`, ou seja, quando o dashboard sobe. Um dashboard que fica meses no ar nunca rotaciona, e a reinicialização seguinte apaga de uma vez tudo que passou da janela de retenção (120 dias). Era um item aberto no `CLAUDE.md`.

## Mudança

- `config.AUDIT_ROTATE_INTERVAL_SECS` (env de mesmo nome, padrão 86400 = 1 dia, mínimo 60 s para não brigar por disco/lock).
- `dashboard_api._audit_rotation_loop`: dorme o intervalo, depois roda `rotate_logs(max_days=AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS)` em `asyncio.to_thread` (é I/O síncrono). Dorme primeiro porque o `create_app` já rotacionou no boot.
- Falha na rotação: loga só `error_type` (sem caminho nem conteúdo) e segue para o próximo intervalo; o loop só para por cancelamento.
- `_on_startup` cria a task **antes** do retorno antecipado do syncer, então ela existe com `AUDIT_SYNC_ENABLED` desligado (o caso da produção). `_on_cleanup` cancela e aguarda.
- A rotação do startup e o padrão de retenção (120, nos quatro lugares que `tests/test_audit_retention_default.py` mantém iguais) não mudaram.

## Atenção do dono

Com `AUDIT_SYNC_ENABLED` desligado, `/data/audit` não tem cópia em lugar nenhum nas ferramentas do repositório. A rotação periódica **apaga de forma permanente** os logs além da janela, no ritmo diário, em vez de tudo de uma vez numa reinicialização. O efeito total é o mesmo; só deixa de depender do reinício. Esse risco continua aberto e está registrado no `CLAUDE.md`.

## Verificação

- 10 testes novos em `tests/test_audit_periodic_rotation.py`: a task existe sem syncer e rotaciona mais de uma vez com o `max_days` certo; dorme antes da primeira rotação; o cleanup cancela e aguarda; cleanup sem task não dá erro; erro na rotação não mata o loop nem vaza o caminho; a rotação roda fora da thread do event loop; `create_app` + `TestClient`; limites da constante de config.
- Escritos antes do código (falharam com `AttributeError`); 6 mutações (sem `cancel`, sem `except`, dormir depois, sem `to_thread`, task depois do retorno antecipado, sem o mínimo de 60 s) foram todas detectadas.
- Suíte inteira com Redis real: **1199 passed**.
- `ruff==0.14.14` check e format: limpos.

author: aa-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary

Migration-only PR for AA-943 (CRM-15). It merges alone, before the code that needs it (S249 lesson).

New file `api/migrations/012_crm_modules_1_2.sql` (key crm-012; Guard 0 needs crm-011):

- **Trip stage edges.** Every remaining trip edge is added: lost is reachable only before booked; cancelled only from booked, pre_departure or travelling; the date-rule edges are added too.
- **Stage trigger.** `crm.enforce_stage_transition()` is replaced:
  - Gates (CRM19): qualifying -> proposal needs `intake_completeness.s2 >= 80` or `app.gate_override = 'stage2'`. proposal -> booked needs `'booking'`, and booked -> pre_departure needs `'stage3'`, until CRM-18 / CRM-25.
  - Undo (CRM20): `app.stage_undo` may only take back the trip's latest move. That move must be at most 15 s old, made by the same actor, not itself an undo, not a move into cancelled, and (review round 1) must itself record an edge of `crm.status_transition`.
- **New columns.**
  - `trip`: `intake_completeness` (CHECK function `crm.completeness_ok`), `cancel_reason_code`, `last_activity_at`, plus indexes for the quiet flag and the date rule.
  - `trip_stage_history`: `override_reason_code`, `undo_of` (same-agency key) and `batch_id`. A BEFORE INSERT trigger pins `at` and `created_by` for every role except crm_owner. The table stays append-only.
  - `task.priority`.
  - `tenant_settings`: `timezone`, `stage2_auto_send` and `call_slot_rules` (CHECK function `crm.call_slot_rules_ok`).
- **`crm.client_link`.** The Stage 2 signed link, built on the base template. It stores only the SHA-256 of the token, expires after at most 30 days, has status transitions, and has `revoked_at` / `reissued_from` (Fix B11) and a `dispatch_id` that is set to NULL on delete. The SELECT-only policy `client_link_token_lookup` TO crm_app reads `app.client_link_hash` and finds live links only.
- **`crm.meeting_slot`** (R15), on the base template: at most one live slot per agency start time (partial UNIQUE).
- **`form_submission` for Stage 2 / 3.** `intake_form_id` is required for s1 only. `client_link_id` gets a composite key to the link's own trip and traveller. Outcome `applied` is added.
- **Erasure.** `crm.erase_subject`, `crm.erase_held` and the hold guard triggers now cover both new tables (trip, traveller and agency scopes). The final `erase_subject` text is recorded in `docs/implementation-notes/AA-943.md`; crm-014 / crm-015 must start from it. `lifecycle_purge_expired` is unchanged: it never reaches the new tables.
- No reader role gets a grant. crm_app never deletes a link or a slot.

Outside the migration:

- `app/pipeline.py` `move_stage` now refuses moves outside the Slice 1 `ALLOWED_MOVES` before the UPDATE. Without that, the deployed code would answer 500 on the new gated edge after the apply. This is safe before the apply too.
- `test_crm002_tenancy.py` lists the new policy.
- `CONTEXT.md` has the crm-012 row.
- New `docs/implementation-notes/AA-943.md`, which also holds the `waiting_on` hook contract for AA-944.

## Review round 1

An independent reviewer checked this branch. The one finding on it (a nit) is fixed in a second commit:

- crm_app can write a history row of its own (only `at` / `created_by` are pinned). With such a row plus `app.stage_undo`, a session could move a trip along a non-edge (for example inquiry -> completed).
- The undo branch now also requires the undone row to record an edge. A forged row can therefore at most take a trip back along the reverse of a real edge, the same trust level as `app.gate_override`.
- New test: `test_a_forged_history_row_cannot_move_a_trip_past_the_edge_table`.
- The implementation notes record the decision.

## Test plan

- Local PostgreSQL 15 container with the RDS role shape (`bootstrap_roles`), fresh database, full integration suite: 268 passed. This includes `tests/integration/test_crm012_schema.py` (44 tests):
  - every edge with its gate met, and the non-edges refused;
  - R: s2 60 / 79 without an override -> CRM19, 80 or override -> moved;
  - booking and stage3 gates;
  - undo: same actor within 15 s, refused if older, another actor, not the latest, an undo, a cancel, or a forged non-edge row; history pin;
  - CHECKs on completeness, tenant settings and cancel reason;
  - token lookup finds live links only; readers 42501; crm_app cannot DELETE; link and slot status rules; one live slot per start;
  - Stage 2 submission composite key;
  - trip, traveller and agency erase with links and slots present; the hold rule reaches them (CRM10); the erase text names the new tables.
  - The crm-010 erase tests run unchanged on the new function.
- Earlier round: unit suite with coverage 1062 passed, 98 %. Not re-run on this branch in round 1: the round touched only SQL, a test and docs.
- ruff check and ruff format; resource-ID scan (0 findings); docs front matter.
- gitleaks not run locally (not installed).
- CI is the final judge.

## Risk

Risky: schema, a new lookup policy, and replaced deletion functions (`erase_subject` / `erase_held`). An independent review has run (round 1 applied). Open review questions:

- Can the token lookup policy leak rows from other agencies?
- Can a crm_app session abuse the undo or override settings? The remaining trust is documented in the notes.
- Does erasure stay complete with the new FK tables?

Order after merge:

1. AA-CIS-Infra byte-copy PR.
2. Root R2 schema-ownership sentence for crm-012, in the session-end root PR. No new DM-7 row: `client_link` and `meeting_slot` are already in §7.
3. DB Migrate check, then apply, in a wave gap.
4. Merge `bot/db-schema-reference`.
5. Then the stage-engine PR.

## Summary

Ticket: FRE-1669 (finding F7 of the FRE-1666 Hermes study). Backing design: ADR-0102 / FRE-681 (PDF utility), ADR-0028 (native tool tier).

`download_text` judged a body by its header only. An `application/pdf` body came back as its raw bytes decoded as text. It now decides on the body too:

- `application/pdf`, or a body that starts with `%PDF`, goes to pypdfium2 text extraction. It reuses `extract_page_text` from ADR-0102. No new dependency.
- A PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, ZIP, gzip, 7z, RAR, xz, bzip2, Zstandard, ELF or Mach-O body raises `FetchError` `unsupported_binary` that names the type. So does a body with a NUL byte early and no UTF-16 or UTF-32 byte-order mark.
- A PDF that PDFium cannot open raises `pdf_unreadable`. A PDF with no text layer raises `no_readable_text` with a PDF-specific message.
- PDFium is not thread-safe, so the open, read and close run under one process-wide `PDFIUM_LOCK` in `pdf_utils.py`.
- The tool description says that a PDF URL returns its text.

Diff class: self-serve. The diff has no production write path, no deleting code, no schema change and no cost or governance code.

## Test mock fold-in

The `MagicMock` responses in four existing test files had no `content` attribute. A real `httpx.Response` always has one. Each mock gains one `content` line. No existing test function changes.

**Do not merge before maintainer approval.**

### Screenshots on the GitHub homepage

- Add the **two user-supplied Spider-Man screenshots** immediately below the status badges and before the project description.

## 概要
`worker-ci.yml` に inputs を 4 つ追加します。既定値は現行の挙動と同一なので、既存の呼び出し（marketing-hub）は変更なしで同じステップが走ります。stocktake / export-docs / yojitsu / price-list / internal-app-template の `ci.yml` を寄せるために必要な差分だけを入れています。

| input | 型 | 既定値 | 用途 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test-command` | string | `bun test` | `run-tests: true` のときのコマンド（yojitsu は `bun test src`、price-list は `bun run test`） |
| `dev-vars-example` | string | `.dev.vars.example` | `wrangler types` 前にコピーするファイル。空文字ならコピーしない（yojitsu） |

- `dev-vars-example` が空でない場合にファイルが無ければ従来通り失敗します（黙ってスキップはしない）。
- トリガー・paths-ignore・draft スキップ・concurrency は引き続き呼び出し側の責務です。組織固有の値は入れていません（public リポジトリ）。

> **All [contribution rules](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md) are required.**
> Stay within the approved MVP and PRD. Prove a useful improvement. Prefer removal,

> contributor penalties. Write in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English for a
> non-technical reader. Every UI change needs an uploaded explainer and walkthrough
> video, evidence that the changed flow works, and detailed steps to test it.


# Relates to

Voice profile routes, `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/routes/voice-profiles-management-routes.ts`, `voice-speaker-profile-routes.ts` and `src/runtime/voice-entity-binding.ts`. No issue: repository rules require a human to write issues.

# Change

**Problem.** Each of these built its own `VoiceProfileStore`. The live voice pipelines use the shared store from `getSharedVoiceProfileStore()`, which caches the profile index and the records. The factory exists so that consumers do not race on `index.json`. When the owner deleted a profile in Voice Profiles (`DELETE /api/voice/profiles/:id`), only the route's own store changed. The shared store still had the profile. The next turn from that speaker still matched and refined it, and the next index write put it back on disk. The deleted profile then showed in the UI again.

| After `DELETE /api/voice/profiles/:id` while voice is running | develop | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared store `refine` for that speaker | returns the record and writes it back | returns `null` |
| Shared store `list()` | still lists the profile | profile gone |
| `profiles/<id>.json` | recreated by the next refine | stays deleted |

**Fix.** All three call sites use `getSharedVoiceProfileStore()`, so the delete, rename, merge, split and bind routes act on the store that the pipeline reads. This removes code. The test overrides (`set*Store`) are unchanged.

# Why this implementation

- The shared store is the documented single registry. Using it removes the second instance.
- Alternative rejected: reload the shared store's cache after each route write. That keeps two writers on one `index.json`.

# Testing

New case in `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/routes/voice-profiles-management-routes.test.ts`: "a deleted profile is gone from the store the voice pipeline uses". It uses a real `VoiceProfileStore` on a temp state dir and the real route, with no override.
- develop: fails, `expected { …(18) } to be null`. The live store still refines the deleted profile.
- this PR: passes.
- Related plugin-local-inference tests (routes, runtime, plugin routes): 180 of 180 pass. Typecheck and lint: clean.
- Root `bun run verify`: result posted as a PR comment.

## How to test

1. `cd plugins/plugin-local-inference && npx vitest run src/routes/voice-profiles-management-routes.test.ts`
2. Expect 6 pass.
3. Revert the three source files to develop. Run step 1 again. Expect the new case to fail.

- [ ] Ran `bun install` and `bun run verify` after syncing; record blockers below.

sets the marker from the live PR head; rerun after each push.

## Summary

Refactor Orbit's styling architecture to strictly follow PrimeVue v4 Design Tokens (`@primeuix/themes`) integrated with Tailwind CSS v4, completely eliminating ad-hoc `.p-*` CSS overrides and hardcoded corner radii.

## Changes

### 1. Preset & Token Layer
- **`src/assets/base.css`**: Define centralized system CSS variables (`--ui-radius-control`, `--ui-radius-card`, `--ui-control-bg`, `--ui-card-bg`, `--border`, `--ui-glass-blur`, `--ui-sheen-highlight`) across `:root`, `.my-app-dark`, and all 5 UI style presets (`flat`, `glass`, `aero`, `liquidglass`, `ios`). Purge all ad-hoc `.p-*` CSS selector blocks.
- **`src/assets/main.css`**: Remove `.p-tooltip` and `.p-tooltip-text` overrides in favor of PrimeVue theme tokens.
- **`src/theme/orbitTheme.ts`**: Map PrimeVue semantic tokens (`borderRadius`, `formField`, `content`, `overlay`, `colorScheme.light`, `colorScheme.dark`) and component tokens (`card`, `datatable`, `button`, `select`, `inputtext`, `textarea`, `inputnumber`, `multiselect`, `checkbox`, `popover`, `drawer`, `dialog`, `contextmenu`, `menu`, `tabs`, `paginator`, `toast`, `tooltip`, `tag`) to centralized system CSS variables.
- **`src/main.ts`**: Set `cssLayer.order: 'theme, base, primevue, utilities'` so Tailwind utilities cleanly cascade over PrimeVue defaults without requiring `!` important modifiers.

### 2. Component Clean-up & Token Hygiene
- Replace hardcoded corner-radius classes (`rounded-lg`, `rounded-xl`, `rounded-2xl` → `rounded-[var(--ui-radius-card)]` and `rounded-md`, `rounded-sm` → `rounded-[var(--ui-radius-control)]`) across all `.vue` components and views.
- Purge Tailwind `!` important modifiers across components and utility styles.
- Replace native `title` attribute on `<Button>` in `WorkloadPodsTab.vue` with PrimeVue's `v-tooltip.top` directive.

### 3. Tests & Quality Gates
- **`src/theme/__tests__/orbitTheme.test.ts`**: Verify semantic and component token mapping to centralized dynamic CSS variables.
- **`src/theme/__tests__/appearanceTokenHygiene.test.ts`**: Add automated checks ensuring all 7 core design tokens exist across all 5 styles, zero `.p-*` CSS overrides exist, and zero hardcoded corner radii or `!` modifiers remain in `.vue` files.

## Testing

author: sophia486
body:
## Che cosa cambia

`detect_iban()` (`src/app/detectors.py`) scartava il candidato IBAN quando l'ultimo gruppo era più
lungo del primo. Un documento che stampa l'ultimo gruppo **intero** attaccato al resto lo fa lungo
`len(gruppo) + resto` (`IT60 X054 2811 1010 0000 0123456` ha una coda di 7 caratteri su un IT di 27),
e il candidato cadeva nella guardia «gruppi disuguali: è prosa»: l'IBAN restava in chiaro e la coda la
prendeva la regex dei telefoni, uscendo come `[TELEPHONENUM_1]`. Il GB dello stesso report non lo
mostrava solo perché il suo resto è di 2 caratteri, quindi la coda non superava il primo gruppo.

La guardia ora ammette la coda fino a `len(g[0]) + resto` (`resto = n % len(g[0])`), cioè un gruppo
intero assorbito nel resto. Oltre quel limite la coda ha inghiottito una parola e il candidato resta
scartato come prima. Le altre condizioni non cambiano: gruppi interni uniformi, lunghezza del paese
da `IBAN_LEN`, mod-97 e nessun carattere alfanumerico subito dopo il codice.

Perché non basta normalizzare prima del match (la prima ipotesi dell'issue): `iban_ok()` normalizza già
spazio, punto, trattino e a-capo. Il testo stampato non arrivava mai al mod-97, veniva buttato prima
sulla forma dei gruppi.

## Verifica

- `python -m unittest discover tests` (lo stesso comando di `.github/workflows/tests.yml`): Ran 84
  tests, OK (skipped=8), su Python 3.15.
- Con il codice di `main` e i test nuovi: 2 failed (`ultimo_gruppo_unito_al_resto`,
  `test_il_documento_dell_issue_135`). Con la modifica: tutto verde.
- Differenziale su README, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/*.md` e `tests/fixtures_economico_giuridiche.jsonl`
  (14 testi): 12 span IBAN prima e 12 dopo, nessun candidato nuovo.
- Sul testo del report: prima `TELEPHONENUM` sulla coda e nessun IBAN; dopo un IBAN sull'intera riga
  con `validated: true`. Nella fusione (`_merge`, `src/app/app.py`) una span validata ha la precedenza
  sui candidati non validati, quindi il frammento `TELEPHONENUM` non resta etichettato.

Non ho eseguito `/analyze` end-to-end con il modello: qui non c'è torch e `detectors.py` è
volutamente testabile senza. La verifica è sulla rete regex+checksum, che è dove stava il difetto.

## Limite noto

Una coda che assorbe **due** gruppi interi (`IT60 X054 2811 1010 00000123456`) resta fuori, ed è
fissata in un test: allargare ancora la guardia vorrebbe dire accettare come coda una parola qualsiasi
fino a 11 caratteri per un IT. Se serve, si può aprire a parte.

## File

- `src/app/detectors.py`: la guardia sulla coda.
- `tests/test_iban_formato_stampa.py`: la coda unita tra i casi che escono per interi, il documento del
  report, il limite della coda.
- `docs/CHANGELOG.md`: voce del 2026-10-24 con la motivazione.

body:
Angle : 224

**Entrées écrites : 3 🔴, 1 🟠, 0 🟢** (P224.01 à P224.04), toutes `à mesurer`.

## Ce qui a été relu par l'explorateur lui-même (aucun sous-agent)

- `MaintenanceRequestObserver` : la facture naît au passage à `completed`, par `insertOrIgnore` contre l'index unique partiel `sp_bills_one_open_per_request`.
- `MaintenanceStateMachine` : `completed → in_progress` (contestation) et `in_progress → cancelled` sont permis.
- `MaintenanceRequestService` : `complete`, `contestResolution`, `assign`. Aucun ne touche la facture.
- Les trois gestes d'argent : `ServiceProviderBillController::decide`, `PayoutService::createForBill` et `PayoutCalculator::rechargeableBills`. Aucun ne lit `maintenance_requests.status`.
- Côté front : `ServiceProviderBillsTable.tsx` et `lib/queries/payments.ts`.

## Ce qui a été mesuré

Un test temporaire, retiré avant le commit, reprend les aides de `ServiceProviderBillTest`. Charge relevée : `{ 2.46 2.53 2.65 }` sur 8 cœurs.

- **Contestation puis annulation** : la facture reste `pending_validation`. `validate` rend 200, `pay` rend 201, et `rechargeableBills` la compte toujours (P224.01).
- **Contestation, réassignation, fin des travaux de B** : il reste une seule facture, celle de A ; B n'en a aucune (P224.02). Raccourci du test : le statut et le devis de B sont posés par `forceFill`, ce que l'entrée dit.
- **Seconde fin des travaux à 80 000** : la facture reste à 50 000 et `exceeds_quote` reste à `false` (P224.03).

Commande lancée : `php artisan test tests/Feature/Tmp/Angle224MesureTest.php`. Les 3 tests sont « risky », sans assertion : c'était voulu, le test ne faisait qu'imprimer ses mesures.

Vérification : `node scripts/check-pistes.mjs --role explorateur --base origin/pre-dev` → vert.

## Ce qui a été écarté

- **Les devis** (`MaintenanceQuoteController`) : la table d'états ferme déjà tout geste depuis `cancelled`.
- **La suppression d'une intervention** : aucune route ne la permet.
- **La lecture du bailleur par `properties.user_id` dans `rechargeableBills`** : l'angle 232 la couvre déjà.

## Angle proposé

- **238** — Observateurs et écouteurs qui créent une ligne fille au passage d'un statut, face aux retours arrière de la machine d'état du parent. Le défaut des entrées P224.01 et P224.03 tient à cette forme (`wasChanged('status')` + `insertOrIgnore`), pas aux seules factures. Aucun angle existant ne vise les observateurs sous cet aspect.

## Ce que le passage n'a pas fait

- Il n'a pas vérifié qu'une facture déjà imputée à un reversement au bailleur, avant la contestation, reste imputée : c'est déduit, et marqué « à vérifier » dans P224.01.
- Il n'a touché à aucune autre ligne du tableau. Le tableau porte deux lignes numérotées 224 : la seconde (« Lectures TanStack… », ligne 302) n'a pas de cellule de statut. Elle est laissée telle quelle, pour le porteur.

## صقل الواجهة والتجربة — الدفعة الأولى (أسطح المزوّد الجديدة)

أول دفعة من تنقيح الواجهة على الأسطح الجديدة، متحقّق منها حيّاً.

### النسخ (Copy)
- إزالة التنوين من أسطح المزوّد الجديدة (الربحية، لوحة توزيع الطلب المجمّع، نوافذ إسناد الشاحنة/السائق، أحداث نشاط الأسطول): «تلقائيًا»→«تلقائيا»، «سائقًا»→«سائقا»، «طلباً»→«طلبا»، «متاحًا»→«متاحا» — وفق أسلوب النسخ (بلا تنوين).

### صفحة الربحية
- لم تعد تُظهر زر «إعادة الضبط» وواجهة الـ fallback أثناء تحميل طلب الـ API (كان يظهر للحظة ثم يختفي)؛ الآن يظهر فقط عند فشل الجلب فعلاً.
- جدول الفواتير أصبح قابلاً للتمرير أفقياً داخل بطاقته على الشاشات الضيّقة (min-width + overflow-x-auto)، فلا تمرير أفقي للصفحة كلها على الجوال.

### التحقق
- على 3003 (عرض الجوال 479px): لا تمرير أفقي للصفحة، الجدول يمرّر داخل بطاقته، لا وميض لزر إعادة الضبط، وعنوان «الربحية» يظهر صحيحاً في القائمة الجانبية (بعد تنظيف كاش `.next` القديم).
- أسطح العميل/الأدمن الجديدة فُحِصت لنفس مشاكل النسخ وهي نظيفة.
- `tsc --noEmit` نظيف على carrier / client / admin.

> ملاحظة: هذه الدفعة الأولى؛ يمكن المتابعة بصقل أسطح العميل/الأدمن والتفاصيل الخاصة بعرض سطح المكتب.

author: contactsamie
body:
## What

**Discovery without the whole list**
- `GET /api/search?q=remember a birthday` returns only the matching routes, scripts and flows, best first. Each comes with how to call it; a script or flow comes with the exact `run` request, its inputs as `<placeholders>`.
  - Options: `?in=routes,scripts,flows`, `?group=`, `?limit=`.
  - Rare words count more, and the words are compared by stem.
- Every route and group now has **tags**: the words someone would say to find it ("status", "job", "cancel", "birthday").
  - Scripts and flows can declare their own tags with a `# Tags: weather forecast` header line. They are listed as `tags` in `/api/scripts` and `/api/flows`.
- `GET /api/endpoints?brief=true` returns the groups alone. `?q=` on endpoints is a route search.

**`next` on every JSON answer**
- Each answer carries `[{method, path, why}]`: the calls that usually follow, with path values and ids filled in.
- Errors point to where to look instead (a 404 route gets a search for its words). `?next=false` leaves it out.
- An async run's 202 says how to come back with the request id, so a client doesn't need to know that ahead of time.

**Each result handed over once**
- A request waited for, streamed or refused is `delivered` in its own answer.
- An async request is delivered by the first read of `/api/requests/{id}` once it's over (`?peek=true` only looks). After that it's `cleared`: the request still says how it ended, without the output, and points to the run.
- `GET /api/requests/open` lists the requests not collected yet, oldest first, each `pending` or `ready`. `/api/health` counts them.
- `DELETE /api/requests/{id}` clears one. On an async request still waiting for the click, it takes it back: the card goes and the state is `withdrawn`.
- `POST /api/requests/clear` clears every request that's over.

**Prompts and docs**
- PROMPT-ASSISTANT and the in-app AI Agent instructions now say: search first, follow `next`, send runs with async, collect once, use the open list.
- API.md, `/api/doc`, AGENTS-GUIDE, RECIPES, FLOW-GUIDE and README are updated to match.

## Behaviour change
Reading `/api/requests/{id}` again after a result was handed over no longer includes `run` (its output). `state`, `ok`, `run_id` and `run_url` are still there.

## Tests
- `swift test` on Linux: 288 tests pass.
- New `DiscoveryTests` cover search ranking, tags, brief groups, `next` hints (every hint in the table points at a real route), hand-once collection, the open list's order, dismiss, clear and withdraw.
- The Mac app target isn't built here; it doesn't use any of the changed types.

author: amirf1389
body:
## Summary

- **Detection:** `bridge/detect.js` read `HKLM\SOFTWARE\ASIO` in one registry view only, so a 32-bit driver (or any driver in the other view) was never seen. Both views are read now (`/reg:64` and `/reg:32`); each driver carries its bitness. Drivers of the other bitness than the server are reported (`asioWrongBitness`) and the page says so (a 32-bit driver cannot be loaded into a 64-bit server).
- **Detect / undetect flapping:** a registry read that timed out made every driver vanish for one scan. A failed read is retried once; when it still fails the drivers seen in the last ten minutes are kept (`asioStale`). A missing key still means no drivers.
- **Event loop:** the synchronous RtAudio device probe loads every ASIO driver and blocked the whole server each time the page asked (audio sockets stutter). Its result is reused for 15 s unless a rescan is requested (`?force=1`).
- The existing RtAudio logic that keeps a driver listed while another program has it open (`mergeAsio`) is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] New test with a fake `reg.exe`: both views, bitness, retry, stale memory, the ten-minute limit, a missing key clearing the list.
- [x] `node --test bridge/test.js`: 129 pass / 30 fail; the 30 failures are the same as on `main` (deleted `platforms/` sources).
- [ ] Not run on Windows (real `reg.exe`, real drivers).
- CodeQL jobs are expected to fail for the existing no-runner reason.
