body:
## Résumé

Dernière étape de la mise en parité de Fitila IA Flutter sur la référence web (#149 corrigeait déjà le contenu/fonction de l'écran texte). Il restait un écart architectural explicitement signalé après #149 : le mode vocal était une page séparée (`Navigator.push`), avec son propre historique, alors que la référence web (`FitilaIA.tsx`) bascule `voiceMode` **en place** sur le même composant, en passant sa fonction `sendMessage` existante en `onAsk` à `FitilaIAVoice` — texte et vocal partagent donc le même fil de conversation et le même assistant.

## Changements

- **`fitila_ia_voice_page.dart`** : `FitilaIaVoicePage` prend désormais `onExit`/`onAsk` optionnels (comme les props `onExit`/`onAsk` de `FitilaIAVoice.tsx`). Sans eux (usage autonome), elle retombe sur `Navigator.pop` et sur l'assistant général direct.
- **Suppression du recadrage « Code foncier »** : en auditant `FitilaIAVoice.tsx` pour implémenter correctement cette unification, j'ai trouvé que l'écran vocal Flutter envoyait un `systemPrompt` recadrant *tout* l'assistant sur le Code foncier, et affichait 3 boutons de démarrage thématiques — aucun des deux n'existe côté web pour cet écran (grep confirmé : zéro `systemPrompt`, zéro bouton de démarrage dans `FitilaIAVoice.tsx`). Ce recadrage contredisait directement la consigne de parité (« Fitila IA du flutter mobile doit avoir même contenu et même fonction que celui du web »), donc je l'ai retiré en même temps — c'est une conséquence nécessaire d'une vraie unification, pas un changement indépendant. **Tem IA** (l'assistant RAG local dédié au Code foncier, écran distinct) n'est pas concerné.
- **`main.dart` (`AiScreen`)** : extraction de `_ask(text) -> Future<String?>` à partir de `_send()`, partagée par le composeur texte et le mode vocal (comme `sendMessage` sur le web). Nouveau booléen `_voiceMode` ; `build()` bascule en place sur `FitilaIaVoicePage(onExit: ..., onAsk: _ask)` au lieu de naviguer vers une page séparée.

## Plan de test

- [x] Équilibre des accolades vérifié sur les deux fichiers modifiés (outil manuel, Dart non disponible dans ce bac à sable)
- [x] Aucun test existant ne référence les boutons de démarrage ou le system prompt supprimés (`grep` sur `test/`)

author: jverzani
body:
This fixes a slow first call to `integrate` from compiled code. In a fresh session the README example `integrate(sin(x), (x, 0, pi))` takes about 20 s. Any user function calling `integrate` hits the same delay.

**Cause:** the definite integral calls `integrate(val, x)` from a compiled method. Julia then infers the whole integrator for the concrete term type. That costs about 20 s and 13 GiB on Julia 1.13.
- v1.1.0 took 0.04 s.
- The cost started with `e709244` in #8, which added `@nospecialize` to the term arguments.
- `@nospecialize` stops specialization but not inference. The cost grew with the code: 8 s at #8, 12 s at #11, 20 s on main.

**Fix:** `Base.@nospecializeinfer` on `integrate(ex, x)` and `risch_integrate(f, x)`, which stops inference at the entry point. Measured in a fresh session with SymEngine:

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `integrate(sin(x), (x, 0, pi))` | 20.3 s | 0.04 s |
| `user(ex, x) = integrate(ex, x)` | ≈ 20 s | 0.02 s |
| top-level `integrate(sin(x), x)` | 2.9 s | 2.7 s |

**Test:** `test/test_compile.jl` runs a definite integral and calls from user functions in a new process, after one top-level call. It expects them to finish in under 5 s. Without the fix it fails at 20.0 s. The full suite passes locally.

This is independent of #24.

author: smshagor-dev
body:
## Trust boundary
The operator's Docker cleanup verification can take time. Previously the worker audit ledger cleared **every** unconfirmed cleanup row after an empty-container probe, including a row created by another worker after that probe began. This could allow a newly failed worker's unconfirmed cleanup to be marked checked without a fresh probe.

## Change
Snapshot the **exact ordered unresolved audit IDs before** invoking Docker CLI. After a successful probe, acquire `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on the existing SQLite WAL database, reject any still-running workers, and require that the unresolved audit ID set exactly matches the pre-probe set. Only then atomically change the fixed audit codes and commit. A new hold causes a retryable failure and leaves all holds intact.

## Regression
Native core test models two approved scans: one reports a cleanup hold, a probe takes its snapshot, and a second reports a new unconfirmed cleanup before release. The release fails closed, does not mark either as checked, and blocks new worker claims. A subsequent independently represented fresh snapshot may be released after a new probe. Existing tests cover startup recovery and active worker rejection.

## Scope
No model-driven shell access, no network scanner expansion, no PostgreSQL. This does not pretend to prevent privileged Docker daemon manipulation; the configured daemon still requires operator trust. Wait for Rust, Windows, Go, Python, frontend and Tauri checks before merge.

author: el-bri-ga
body:
Fixes #1456

Under `fsync_mode = on_commit`, `DiskLog::advance_commit_offset` wrote the replica state through (create, fsync, rename, directory fsync) before returning. A follower calls it on almost every replicated batch and the leader at the end of every pass, so a durable `Quorum` ack cost about three fsyncs per replica instead of one.

## Change

- The commit offset is raised in memory at once (truncation, `reset_to` and retention see it immediately) and written behind in every mode. Under `on_commit` a single writer per log starts at once and loops until disk has caught up, so one write in flight carries every advance made while it runs. `Periodic`/`None` keep the once-a-second rule.
- Still synchronous: `accept_generation` (a fence is durable before it is answered), `hold_retention_at_commit`, `restore_to`, `shutdown` and `close`. A failed write is retried once a second as before. A closed log still refuses the advance.
- Docs: `docs/storage-format.md`, `docs/durable-storage.md`, `docs/replication-design.md` ("Divergence and truncation" now says why a lagging on-disk commit offset is acceptable), docs-site storage format.

## Tests

`felix-storage` `disk_log::tests::replica_state`:
- `an_advance_does_not_wait_on_a_replica_state_write`: holds the writer's lock (a slow write in flight); the advance must return within 2 s, truncation below the new offset is refused before the write lands, disk is behind and never ahead, and after the write a reopen without shutdown reads it back.
- `advances_coalesce_into_few_replica_state_writes`: 200 advances, at most 2 writes.
- `a_raised_generation_is_written_through_while_the_commit_offset_is_behind`: a raise reopened at once is on disk with the commit offset before it.
- `a_failed_commit_offset_write_is_retried_on_its_own` now lets the background write fail before unblocking.

I reverted the fix (made the `on_commit` branch write through again) and ran these: the first two and the retry test failed, then passed once I restored the fix. Ran locally: `felix-storage`, `felix-replication`, `felix-broker --test durable_streams`, `task lint`, `task docs:evidence`.

## Review notes

- **Weaker on-disk commit offset, on purpose.** Failure scenario: a follower answers batch N carrying commit C, then crashes before the background write lands, and reopens guarding C' < C. Records in [C', C) are on its disk (data is fsynced before the answer) but could be cut by a leader that asked to, which only a leader that lost committed records would do. A leader at an accepted generation holds every committed record. The window already existed: a client is acked when the leader's mark passes its record, and followers learn that mark only from the next batch (the leader's own advance also runs after `publish_mark`). So acknowledged records were never all covered by a persisted commit offset. This widens the window by one replica-state write. Retention only holds more with a lower offset, and a fence answer reporting a lower one makes promotion compare more of the log.
- **FelixShard model.** On a crash the model keeps `hwm` (capped at the surviving log) in every mode, so it never modelled Periodic's lag either. I marked the commit `Spec-Unaffected`. If you want the lag modelled (crash lowers `hwm` to any earlier value), that is a separate spec change.
- One-in-flight load still writes roughly once per batch, but off the ack path, so it overlaps the next data fsync instead of adding to the ack. Under load the writes coalesce. I did not add a minimum spacing.
- #1481 adds metrics in `replica_state::store`; I left them alone, so expect no conflict beyond context.


## Review follow-up

- **Lost wakeup.** The commit writer and the retry task now clear their flag with `swap(false, AcqRel)` instead of a store. As a read-modify-write, it reads an advance's earlier `swap(true)`, so the next load sees that advance's offset. `an_advance_as_the_writer_finishes_still_reaches_disk` stresses this window, but it is a memory-ordering race, and it did not fail reliably with the old store in place (3 runs passed).
- **Write after close (pre-existing).** `close` now sets `closed` under the `replica_persisted` lock, so a write that found the log open lands before `close` returns. `close_waits_for_a_replica_state_write_in_flight` holds the flush lock and the writer's lock to pin that window. It failed 3 of 3 runs without the fix and passes with it. `accept_generation` and `give_up_generation` still do not check `closed`, which predates this PR and is out of its scope.

Registers the reviewed, manually dispatched isolated Preview recovery workflow on the default branch. The diff adds only `.github/workflows/preview-recovery-drill.yml`; the existing application tree remains unchanged.

The workflow checks out an explicit reviewed ops source SHA, verifies its Python digest, and uses the existing `preview` environment SSH route. author: ormastes
body:
## What (closes the T-EV1 gap found by #4451)
- **Problem:** the eviction planner decided per entry, so it could keep a TLDR and evict the object that TLDR points to.
- **`CacheEntryUseV1.references`:** a new field (default empty) listing the version keys, in the same branch, that an entry needs. Example: TLDR -> object.
- **New step 3b, reference closure (after the storage step):** any evicted entry referenced by a kept entry is restored, repeated until nothing changes.
  - Restored entries are added back to the disk and memory totals.
  - The evict list is rebuilt to exclude them.
  - Restored entries are still subject to the memory-unload step, which only unmaps and never deletes.
- **Consequences:**
  - Eviction never leaves a dangling reference.
  - The plan may stay over a cap; the publish path's admit-before-plan rejection answers that.
  - A referent is evicted together with its referrer once the referrer is also gone.
- **Ledger edges:** the daemon queue's `use` / `complete` ops accept an optional `references: <key>,...` field, so the live ledger carries the edges.

## Evidence (Rust seed)
- `cache_eviction_plan_v1_spec` 9/9. The new cases:
  - A kept TLDR keeps its 100-byte object even though storage is capped at 50; `disk_bytes_after` is 110 (over the cap, so admission rejects new writes).
  - With a tighter cap, the referrer and the referent are evicted together.
- `cache_daemon_queue_v1_spec` 6/6. The new case: a referenced object recorded through `use ... references:` survives `evict`.
- `check-cache-formal-source-binding.shs` passes; no bound declaration changed.

**Formal coordination:** this discharges T-EV1's precondition. For every evicted entry, no kept entry in the same branch references its version key. Step 3b establishes exactly that fixpoint invariant.

author: ehdataai
body:
## Summary

Implement LAB07 Phase C for out-of-sample spatial rank stability in mineral prospectivity analysis.

This phase extends the preceding uncertainty analysis with candidate-level rank stability summaries.

## Scope

- Reconstruct OOS rank information across 10 replicates.
- Summarize rank stability for 6,300 candidate grid cells.
- Quantify candidate support across available OOS replicates.
- Compute top-1%, top-5%, and top-10% ranking frequencies.
- Generate rank_stability.csv and phase_c_manifest.json.
- Provide a reproducible execution script and regression tests.

## Reproducibility and integrity

Local ERL V2 evidence recorded before publication:

- Targeted tests: 17.
- Full regression tests: 217.
- Pre-commit checks: passed.
- Gitleaks pre-commit scan: passed.
- SHA-256 integrity controls: passed.
- GitHub commit signature: verified.
- Oracle loaded: false.
- Oracle used: false.

These are local checkpoint results; GitHub CI must be evaluated independently.

## Methodological limitations

- Ranking stability is not equivalent to calibrated mineral-deposit probability.
- Top-k frequencies describe selection stability across the implemented replicates.
- The 10 replicates should not be interpreted as sufficient for inferential precision without additional Monte Carlo error analysis.
- Spatial dependence and effective information must be considered in scientific interpretation.
- No claim of complete uncertainty calibration is made.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Verify GitHub Actions checks.
- [ ] Review data contracts and deterministic reproduction.
- [ ] Check spatial leakage and OOS separation.
- [ ] Review scientific interpretation of rank frequencies.
- [ ] Confirm artifacts contain no secrets or sensitive data.
- [ ] Confirm documentation and executable permissions.
- [ ] Authorize merge only after the review gates pass.

## Project status

LAB07 Phase C is complete at its recorded local QA checkpoint.

LAB07 Phase D remains pending.

author: anovelbot-dependencies[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`12.14.0` → `12.15.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.14.0/12.15.0) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.15.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.14.0/12.15.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.15.0): pnpm 12.15

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.14.0...v12.15.0)

This release lets `pnpm-workspace.yaml` delegate settings to other files and config dependencies with `include`, adds `lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` and tar-registry support, accepts zstd-compressed registry responses, and honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install`. It also rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested and speeds up workspace installs and macOS file linking.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new `include` field. Each source may define only the settings the root manifest delegates to it. Every setting has one owner. Commands that change settings write each one to the file that owns it. A relative path in an included file is relative to that file. See [Splitting Settings Across Files](https://pnpm.io/config-includes).

  A config dependency supplies its settings through the YAML file named in the `pnpm.config` field of its `package.json`. The new `bootConfig` setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies and the pnpm version from `packageManager`.

- Added the `lockfile.integrityTarget` setting. With `integrityTarget: tar`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins the hash of every package's uncompressed tar, so the lockfile no longer changes when a registry recompresses its tarballs or serves them as tars. pnpm learns a version's tar hash from the store or by downloading it once. `pnpm audit signatures` ties the tar hash to the signed `.tgz` integrity.

  ```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  lockfile:
    integrityTarget: tar
  ```

- pnpm can now install from a registry that serves uncompressed tars with zstd or gzip content coding. `pnpm-lock.yaml` records the hash of each tar. Declare such a registry with `serverType: pnpr` in `registries` to keep tarball URLs out of the lockfile. See [Tar registries](https://pnpm.io/registries#tar-registries).

  pnpm now decodes the content coding of tarball downloads itself. It rejects a zstd response whose window is larger than 8 MiB.

  Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. It caps the bytes the files of one package may unpack to, 4 GiB by default.

- Registry revisions now always pin the hash of the uncompressed tar, the original included. pnpm records an original selected through the revision protocol, for example with a `+r0` specifier, as `revision: 0` in the lockfile and fetches it from the registry's digest route. pnpm checks a revision's tar whether the registry sends it as a tar, gzip, or zstd. Revision metadata must list revision 0 and mark the selected revision. pnpm rejects incomplete revision metadata with `ERR_PNPM_MALFORMED_METADATA`.

- pnpm now accepts zstd-compressed responses. Registries that serve zstd send package metadata in fewer bytes than with gzip, most of all the full metadata that settings such as `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicy` read.

- `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install` now use the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable as an upper bound for timestamps in `node_modules/.modules.yaml` and `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. With an equivalently prepared deploy target and an epoch no later than the timestamps that would otherwise be recorded, deploying the same project twice produces identical files [#​17171](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17171).

- `pnpm update --interactive` now highlights the row under the cursor in cyan while keeping the colors of its version changes.

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NAME_MISMATCH` if a registry returns metadata for a package other than the one requested. Before, pnpm installed the package under the name in the metadata, so `allowBuilds` rules for the requested package did not apply to it.

- `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune` and `trustPolicyExcludePrune` now keep exclusions for resolved configuration dependencies and their transitive dependencies [#​17142](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17142).

##### Resolving dependencies

- When `pnpm install` resolves a dependency again, it now reuses a version that the install already resolved for the same package, as a fresh install does. Before, it kept the version the lockfile pinned and added a second copy of the package. A locked version still stays when nothing else in the install prefers another version. To pin a transitive dependency on purpose, use `overrides` [#​17084](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17084).

- When another workspace project adds a different version of a package, a project's auto-installed peer on that package now moves to the version a fresh install picks. It used to stay on its locked version while any other project still accepted that version [#​17058](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17058).

- A package that lists the same dependency in `dependencies` and as an optional peer now gets the peer bound when a project adds a provider for it later. The lockfile now records every peer a package declares, including one its own dependency supplies [#​17056](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17056).

- `pnpm install --prod` and `pnpm deploy --prod` no longer drop a dependency that a package declares both as an optional peer and as its own dependency, when the package resolved it as its own dependency and a dev dependency provides the same package under another alias.

- `pnpm install` with an existing lockfile and a second `pnpm dedupe` now keep optional peer bindings that point into a dependency cycle or back into the dependent package. Before, the second run dropped the optional peer binding from the lockfile snapshot key.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now preserve own-dependency and peer-dependency bindings when reusing a lockfile whose peer suffixes were hashed by `peersSuffixMaxLength`.

  Upgrading a direct dependency in one workspace project now refreshes matching transitive pins in sibling projects during the same `pnpm install` pass.

- With `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot: false`, a workspace project no longer binds a peer to a version that only another project's dependencies provide. pnpm now auto-installs a version that satisfies the peer range for that project. Before, the project got a version outside the range, with no peer warning.

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, and `pnpm update` now reuse the lockfile's resolution for dependencies that take part in a dependency cycle, such as `mlly` and `pkg-types`. They re-resolved those packages and everything that depends on them from the registry before [pnpm/tasks#130](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/130).

- pnpm now measures a `pnpm.overrides` entry written as a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, from the directory holding `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. It used to be measured from each package the override rewrote. The install then linked a directory that does not exist, or failed if workspace packages were injected [#​17010](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17010).

- `pnpm install` now removes config dependencies that are no longer d

## Summary

Maintainer decisions of 2026-10-24 for the unreleased 0.18.0 (follow-ups of #459/PR #466 and #461/PR #464):

- **`exceptions.validation_details` defaults to `true`**: clients get the validator's reason as `detail`, and Connexion's unescaped request-validation messages are filtered out by default. Template, model docstring, docs, unit tests, example comments and the integration test (`POST /pets` with `{}` now gets `'name' is a required property`, checked locally against the petstore spec) are updated. The test fixture for Connexion's validation logger now removes FOCA's process-wide filter for each test, since apps of other tests add it by default now.

author: kennymcsimpson
body:
`get_json_schema()` shallow-copies each field's `json_schema_extra`, then fills in nested `items` or `additionalProperties` dictionaries in place. This modifies the caller's metadata. If two item classes reuse that metadata, generating a schema for `list[str]` first makes a subsequent `list[int]` schema incorrectly report string items. The same issue affects mapping values and nested containers.

Deep-copy field schema metadata before type inference in the dataclass, TypedDict, attrs, Pydantic and common adapter paths. Add 15 regressions across those five item types, checking that shared metadata stays unchanged and that consecutive schemas infer their own element/value types.

Validation on Windows / Python 3.13:

- All 15 new cases fail before the fix and pass afterward.
- `tox -e extra,py313,docs`: 288 passed / 1 skipped with all extras; 176 passed / 113 skipped without extras; README doctests passed. The all-extras suite reports 99% coverage, with all statements covered.
- Pinned Mypy 2.4.0 passes on all 6 source files. Pinned Pylint passes at 10/10, and every configured pre-commit hook passes. These checks used an LF checkout of the same files to match the repository's required line endings.
- `tox -e twinecheck`: source distribution builds and passes Twine validation.
- After moving the regressions into a separate file to stay within Pylint's module length limit, both schema test modules pass with and without extras.

The remaining Python/platform matrix and minimum dependency versions were not run locally. AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used for investigation, implementation and automated verification.

author: gburd
body:
DRAFT: depends on the unmerged fork base (#1455/#1456 + the S1-S3 base + the four CONF_fork fixes). Targets the arena-reclaim branch.

## What this does
S4 of the fork-stack decomposition: per-process signal dispositions and cross-address-space timer parking.

Three commits:
- per-process signal dispositions plus delivery of a blocked SIGCHLD to its handler (the postmaster PM_RUN wall): give each fork-child address space its own copy of signal_actions[], seeded from the parent, so a child resetting its inherited SIGCHLD to default no longer clobbers the parent's reaper handler; and track real sigwait consumers so a blocked-but-not-sigwaiting process still runs the handler.
- park an application thread's timers off the per-CPU list across address spaces (the IRQ-context copy-on-write wall): on every app-thread switch-out, park its stack timers in its own address space; a per-CPU identity-memory wakeup timer still wakes blocked parked threads on time, so the per-CPU list never contains a foreign-address-space stack timer that the timer IRQ would dereference.
- validate that a shmid names a live shm segment in shmctl/shmat/shmdt (rejects a stale id after a reboot).

## Mechanism
The timer-park change keeps the per-CPU timer list free of foreign-address-space stack timers so the timer IRQ never follows a wild link in a non-preemptable context. All changes are under CONF_fork; the non-fork path is unchanged.

## Evidence: build-gate and the teardown-clean acceptance
- Build-gate: build with conf_fork=1 fs=zfs conf_zfs=openzfs image=tests, EXIT 0. CONF_fork resolves to 1 in the generated config.
- ACCEPTANCE (proven before and after): the dedicated regression tst-fork-irq-cow aborts on the base (without the timer-park) with "Assertion failed: sched::preemptable() (page_fault:38)" reached from the idle-CPU timer interrupt walking a fork child's stack timer in a foreign address space, and passes with 0 failures on this branch ("child exited normally, no foreign-address-space timer-IRQ abort"). The IRQ-context copy-on-write teardown wall is cleared by this branch. This is the headline result and it stands on its own.

## Dependency chain
This branch stacks on the arena-reclaim branch (the S1-S3 base plus the four CONF_fork fixes). S5 stacks on this; S6 on S5.

## Note on serving PostgreSQL
Serving stock PostgreSQL under fork-per-connection load needs more than S4-S6: it additionally needs the sched teardown/work-steal set (staged as the S7 branch) and the restored identity-heap allocation guards, which are entangled with the receive-path rework. See the result writeup for the corrected decomposition.

body:
## Summary

A doc gets a pinning test only for what a person, a tool or an agent copies, runs or parses. The test takes its expectation from the code, or runs the doc's own example through the real module. Prose about the app's behaviour gets no docs test: the behaviour tests and browser scenarios pin the behaviour.

```diff
 test/web, test/snapshot
-  71 docs-test files, ~393 KB of sentence regexes (65 *-docs, docs-agree x2, ...)
+  kanban-skill-contract   config keys, starter, role trio, nesting fields, pills: from the code
+  notes-kit-contract      file names, frontmatter keys, path placeholders: through the real stores
+  doc-examples            the docs' search and slice examples run through search.js
+  snapshot-contract       apply payload shapes; the module list derived from build_editor.py
+  doc-paths               every repo path a doc names exists
+  handles-in-skill, testing-docs (derived from package.json), docs-utf8
 docs-pinned-check.js
-  any doc edit needs a docs test in the same diff
+  only a contract doc needs one: kanban SKILL.md, apply-protocol.md, cross-harness.md,
+  the README's config.yaml and Starter config sections
```

- `docs/testing.md` states the rule in place of "A docs change brings its docs test".
- Before a test was cut, the behaviour it described was checked for a behaviour test. Where none existed, one was added first:
  - a new `test/snapshot/limits.test.js` (9 tests: what the snapshot leaves out, such as notes, todos, the hover set and the `l m i n ?` keys);
  - 11 more checks in existing behaviour tests (pill counts under a slice cut, a `slice:` cut surviving a reload, derived values never written to a card, ...).
- Doc-sentence pins inside 14 behaviour test files went too; pins that read code stay.
- `docs/cross-harness.md`'s module list gained `ids.js`, `markdown.js`, `code-libs.js` and `code-blocks.js`. The new contract test derives the list from `build_editor.py` and found them missing.

## Evidence

- **Before:** 71 docs-test files, about 393 KB.
  **After:** 8, about 66 KB. 104 files, +1315 / -6020.
- Every original file is accounted for in the builder's table: kept, merged into which contract test, or cut with the behaviour test or scenario that covers it.
- Unit suite 7812, 0 failures, after merging main (8303 before, less the cut sentence tests, plus the new contract and behaviour tests).
- The contract tests were mutation-checked on a sample of doc edits: each catches a changed command, key, path or payload.
- Browser: `hotkeys` (41 checks, 4x throttle), whose comment changed.
- CI green on `08591b5`: test and browser, first try (run 40107729222).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** tests

- Main is merged in (`08591b5`). PR #132 had edited a comment in `role-trio-docs.test.js`, which this deletes; the conflict was resolved by keeping the deletion.
- A doc can now drift from the app's behaviour with no test failing. The behaviour itself stays pinned, and the three `SKILL.md` trims that follow need this to land first.

author: jofalinj
body:
Online orders now confirm only from server-verified captured Razorpay payments or checked staff UPI verification. Lost callbacks recover through an issued HMAC capability; pending, failed, refunded and late payments stay unconfirmed and cannot silently start a second checkout. The database records inventory/invoices once, releases expired reservations once, reconciles cumulative refunds, and prevents direct browser writes from forging online payment evidence.

Manual UPI and guest tracking now use rate-limited Worker proxies with service-only database RPCs. Admin Orders exposes payment/refund review and secure invoices. Legacy direct WhatsApp functions are retired, and the Worker sender remains explicitly disabled until approved-template, credentials, consent and test-allowlist gates are satisfied. Existing main storefront/domain fixes are preserved.

Validation before PR: 197 unit assertions, 60 Worker behavior tests, 7 Selenium payment recovery fixtures (phone/tablet, reload before callback, refunds, safe expiry), lint, static/Pages builds, npm audit (zero vulnerabilities), disposable PostgreSQL/PGlite migration and post-settlement suites. CI additionally runs PostgreSQL 17 with all settlement migrations. Isolated Supabase integration and authenticated staff E2E remain skipped without their separate test environment; no real payments, refunds or messages were sent.

Deployment: apply harden_checkout_settlement_refunds before the new RPC callers, retire the two legacy Edge Functions with JWT verification retained, merge only after CI, then verify the existing rainbow-api Worker/main build and byte-for-byte live storefront assets. Razorpay remains TEST-only. Historical delivered/unpaid data needs merchant reconciliation; tax/account onboarding and WhatsApp enablement are outside this TEST release.

After the `LGTM` approval on #180, the approval path enabled auto-merge. # Change

**Problem.** Both purge paths deleted the Gmail message, spam review and sync state rows for the grant. The inbox cache (`app_lifeops.life_inbox_messages`) also keeps each Gmail message's subject, snippet, sender email and sender name, under `gmail_account_id = <grant id>`. Nothing deleted those rows. author: b1-centauro
body:
## Summary

The rust-rcs-client E2EE work needs two small additions to the core. Both are behind the `e2ee` feature.

- **`mls::key_package_info(key_package) -> Result<KeyPackageInfo>`** decodes a KeyPackage and checks its signature and lifetime (RFC 9420 §10.1). It returns `KeyPackageInfo { ciphersuite, credential, signature_key }`.
  - **Why it's needed:** a client must check the KeyPackages its Home KDS returns against the Participant it asked for (RCC.16 A.4.1.2, `RcsCredentialValidator::validate_query`). `add_members` can't do that: it checks credentials through `validate_addition`, which doesn't know who was asked for.
  - **Errors:** `BadFormat` if the input isn't an MLS message, `UnexpectedMessage` if it's another kind of MLS message, `Rejected` if the KeyPackage fails validation.
  - **Shared code:** the decoding and validation are the same as in `MlsConversation::read_key_package()`, which now calls the shared code too.
- **`mls::SignatureKeyPair`** is now re-exported from `openmls_basic_credential`. `MlsClient::with_credential` already takes one, and a client needs it to make the key its Home KDS certifies, without depending on the crate directly.

## Tests

- `a_key_package_tells_of_its_client_once_checked`:
  - for a valid KeyPackage, the cipher suite, credential and signature key match the client that made it;
  - a KeyPackage with a flipped signature byte is `Rejected`;
  - bytes that aren't MLS give `BadFormat`;
  - a Welcome gives `UnexpectedMessage`.
- `a_key_package_from_the_kds_is_checked_for_the_participant_asked_for`: with the Annex A fixtures, Bob's KeyPackage passes `validate_query` for Bob's tel URI and fails with `Identity` for Alice's.

## Validation

- **Tests:** `cargo test --features e2ee --lib`: 191 pass. `cargo test --lib`: 132 pass. rust-rcs-client's 96 tests (with `e2ee`) pass against this branch.
- **Mutation check:** dropping the signature key fails a test, and so does returning another client's credential. Skipping validation can't be written: OpenMLS only produces a `KeyPackage` by validating one.
- **Formatting and warnings:** `cargo fmt --check` is clean. Warnings are unchanged at 79.

author: aa-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary
Migration-only PR for AA-835 slice S3 (root ADR 0004a; contracts supply.hotel.v1 / supply.service.v1, root R1).

- `booking.outbox` gets the `supply` stream: new columns `entity_type` (hotel|service), `entity_id` and `supply_version`, and the event types `supply.upsert` and `supply.deactivate`. The new CHECK `outbox_supply_chk` makes a supply row name only its entity and version, with no b2b ids or codes. A b2b row can never carry the supply columns. It is NULL-safe: a NULL makes the CHECK false, not unknown. A partial index covers `feed_seq` for the supply stream.
- `supply_version` BIGINT on `hotels` and `services`. It is 1 at insert. A BEFORE trigger adds +1 on a material change of the contract facts. Any write of the column also counts as exactly one bump, so the version can never jump or go back. Notes, links, source refs and audit columns are not material.
- A room type insert or material change bumps its hotel. A photo insert, a usage_rights change or a removal bumps its entity.
- An AFTER trigger `supply_outbox` writes one supply outbox row per insert and per new version. The event is `supply.deactivate` while the entity is inactive and `supply.upsert` while it is active, which matches the contract rule that `change` follows `facts.status`.
- New table `booking.entity_media` for supplier photos:
  - The CHECK derives the key from the row: `supply-media/<type>/<entity>/<id>.<ext>`. A bucket-name CHECK accepts `aa-booking-<env>-supply-media-<12 digits>` only.
  - Allowed types are JPEG, PNG and WebP, up to 10 MB, with a hex sha256.
  - `usage_rights` is false by default. Status is `active` or `removed`, and removed is final. Only one active copy of the same bytes per entity.
  - There is no FK to the entity: the bump trigger refuses a photo of a missing entity.
  - Role `booking` gets SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of `usage_rights`, `status` and `updated_*` only. No DELETE.
- Views `v_supply_hotels`, `v_supply_services`, `v_supply_media` and `v_supply_outbox`:
  - All are security_barrier and facts only: no supplier, rate, notes, links or staff/audit columns.
  - Hotel and service views carry room types and active photos as JSON.
  - `v_supply_outbox` shows only supply rows that have a `feed_seq`.
  - SELECT goes to `cis_app`. They are read-only for `booking`.
- The file starts and ends with guard DO blocks:
  - Before: it runs as bk_owner, cis_app exists, bk-010, bk-017 and bk-022 are in place.
  - After: cis_app reads only the 4 views and none of the 5 base tables, the views are security_barrier, and booking cannot delete photos.
- Existing tests adjusted:
  - bk-017: the exact set of cis_app grants now includes the supply views.
  - bk-018: allowlist `v_supply_hotels.name` / `.address` and `v_supply_services.working_title` (mirrored into the Infra PII_ALLOWLIST in the copy PR).
  - bk-022: `outbox.entity_type` is a new CHECKed text column.
  - `purge_supply` also deletes photos.
- `CONTEXT.md` gets a bk-023 section. Implementation notes, with the reverse recipe, are in `docs/implementation-notes/AA-835.md`.
- Not in this PR: no `REQUIRED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS` change (that comes in S4, after the apply), no backfill of outbox rows for existing hotels and services (a deliberate touch `SET supply_version = supply_version + 1` emits one; this avoids surprise paid CIS drafts), and no app code.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_migration_guard.py`: 105 passed.
- [x] Full integration suite on a local PostgreSQL 16 scratch cluster (CI uses 15), with the RDS role shape from bootstrap_roles: 372 passed. The new `test_bk023_schema.py` and `test_bk023_supply.py` (24 tests) cover:
  - Re-running the file is a no-op. Owner is bk_owner.
  - Grants for booking and cis_app. Exact view column lists, with no forbidden fields.
  - The stream CHECKs and the entity_media CHECKs.
  - A material update gives exactly 1 bump and 1 row. Notes and links give none.
  - A direct supply_version write is still +1.
  - Room types bump the hotel, and both hotels when a room type moves.
  - deactivate and reactivate.
  - Photo bumps, removed is final, the unique-bytes rule, no DELETE or key move, missing entity refused.

author: anatwork14
body:
## Summary
Resolves #21. Delivers provider-independent storage abstraction, Google Drive API v3 resumable chunked upload with Range query recovery, deterministic bit-reproducible source snapshots with secret filtering, Ubuntu Workspace Broker for multi-client read-only attach, M8 monitoring dashboard integration, and automatic checkpoint publication policies.

## Implemented Functionality
1. **Storage Abstraction (`colab_adapter/storage/`)**:
   - Provider-independent `ArtifactStore` Protocol and immutable `StoredArtifact` records.
   - `LocalArtifactStore` for atomic local SSD commits and multi-tier verification.
   - `GoogleDriveArtifactStore` implementing official Google Drive v3 resumable upload protocol (1 MiB chunks) with Range status query recovery (`Range: bytes */total`), exponential backoff on 429/500, Drive quota exceeded handling (403), token expiration refresh (401), and remote MD5/size verification.
   - `PublicationManifest` with atomic disk persistence.
   - `TransferJournal` and `TransferRecord` with monotonic lifecycle states:
     `LOCAL_STAGED -> LOCAL_VERIFIED -> UPLOAD_PENDING -> UPLOADING -> DRIVE_VERIFIED -> PUBLISHED`.
2. **Background Upload Processing (`ArtifactUploadWorker`)**:
   - Asynchronous queue worker with bounded concurrency.
   - Persistent journal task recovery across process restarts.
   - Local checkpoint preservation on cloud failure (isolated training status).
3. **Reproducibility & Code Snapshots (`colab_adapter/reproducibility.py`)**:
   - Deterministic bit-reproducible `source_snapshot.tar.gz` (normalized gzip/tar headers, mtime=0, uid=0).
   - Strict secret filtering: excludes `.env`, `*.key`, `*.pem`, `id_rsa`, `__pycache__`, `.git/`.
   - Comprehensive `RunManifest`, `source_manifest.json`, and `environment.json`.
4. **Cross-Device Workspace Broker (`colab_adapter/broker.py`)**:
   - Ubuntu-hosted `WorkspaceBroker` for multi-client read-only session inspection.
   - Constant-time bearer token validation and audit logging.
   - Historical inspection of expired/terminated runs without cloud VM allocation.
   - Rejection of unmanaged sessions and rejection of writable attach.
5. **M8 Dashboard Integration**:
   - Added endpoints: `/api/v1/runs/<id>/artifacts`, `/api/v1/runs/<id>/drive`, `/api/v1/runs/<id>/manifest`.
   - Enhanced embedded SPA dashboard with Google Drive publication panel and checkpoint continuity.
   - Historical run discovery from disk manifests.
6. **Automatic Checkpoint Policy (`colab_adapter/checkpoint_policy.py`)**:
   - Minimum interval throttling between cloud checkpoint publications.
   - Multi-tier validation before publishing.
   - Local retention management (`keep_last`) strictly preserving at least 1 verified local checkpoint, never deleting remote Drive objects.

## Test Commands & Verification
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
- **Result:** **142 tests passing** (0 errors, 0 failures, 1 skipped) in 8.3s.
- 7 new comprehensive test suites added in `tests/`:
  - `test_storage_abstraction.py` (6 tests)
  - `test_google_drive_store.py` (6 tests)
  - `test_reproducibility.py` (5 tests)
  - `test_checkpoint_policy.py` (5 tests)
  - `test_upload_worker.py` (3 tests)
  - `test_workspace_broker.py` (5 tests)
  - `test_drive_and_broker_e2e.py` (1 test)

## Security Impact
- **Decoupled Auth:** Drive OAuth is completely decoupled from Colab CLI OAuth.
- **Protected Secrets:** Credentials stored in server-side files with strict `0600` permissions. No tokens exposed to browser, Colab VM, or logs.
- **Zero Allocations on Attach:** Viewing or attaching to runs never provisions cloud VMs.
- **Read-Only Enforced:** Dashboard and broker enforce strictly read-only access (HTTP 405 on mutations).

## Integration Status & Limitations
- **Current State:** 100% offline verified and tested against mocked Drive API and Colab contracts.
- **Live Verification Status:** **IMPLEMENTATION READY — LIVE DRIVE VALIDATION PENDING USER APPROVAL.**
- No live Google Drive write, real OAuth consent, or Colab GPU allocation was executed without user consent.
- Writable cross-device execution deferred to future release with single-writer lease.

Não se via quando os apontamentos de uma aula tinham sido gerados pela última vez. A data só aparecia no menu Gerar, sem hora, o que torna difícil saber se uma aula já foi regenerada com as regras novas.

author: valentinf28
body:
Les flux mobiles recevaient les états REST bruts de Home Assistant : les métadonnées de registre nécessaires à la validation des mesures manquaient et la date de réaffirmation des capteurs stables pouvait être périmée. Le bilan énergétique devenait indisponible alors que le portail disposait des mesures.

Les lectures `ha.states` du relais et `GET /states` du canal local chiffré partagent maintenant le lecteur de mesures réelles déjà utilisé par l’inventaire. Les capteurs de puissance reçoivent uniquement quatre champs de leur registre : plateforme, nom natif, modèle et numéro de série. Le filtrage des appareils autorisés et les commandes ne changent pas. Aucune mesure absente n’est remplacée par zéro et aucune date n’est générée au téléchargement.

Version 0.6.37 basée sur l’arbre exact installé 0.6.34 (`4829a7da8e470b537b54f53175c400a99b82ae6f`). Les candidats scènes 0.6.35 et saisons 0.6.36 ne sont pas inclus. `main` vérifiée à `5531a53b4142d6b8012beeb2e427377ae639e623` avec ce même arbre.

Validation : 429 tests dans 65 modules en processus isolés ; nouveaux tests du véritable dispatch relais, du canal SecretBox et de son exclusion d’une autre maison, de conservation des anciennes dates en cas d’échec et de passage inchangé des autres appels. Manifeste des 54 fichiers régénéré et validé. Qualification CI : https://github.com/Valentinf28/agent-123-domotique/actions/runs/40101548218

Installation matérielle non effectuée. Elle nécessite une revue distincte du paquet et du retour arrière, une sauvegarde privée préalable et la conservation de l’image 0.6.34. Le retour arrière porte seulement sur le code de l’add-on, sans restauration globale Home Assistant ni remplacement de `/data`.

_Requested by **Joep**_

The macOS build now ships as a proper installer, `SpaceMan-macOS.dmg`, in place of the zip: a window with SpaceMan and an Applications link to drag it onto, on a background with an arrow and a strip of treemap tiles.

- `tool/make_dmg.sh` builds the app and the DMG. It uses dmgbuild, which writes the Finder layout without scripting Finder, so it works on headless CI. It installs into `build/dmg-venv` when dmgbuild is missing.

- CI imports a Developer ID certificate into a temporary keychain when `MACOS_CERT_P12` is set and passes the Apple ID secrets through. Without secrets it still builds an unsigned DMG.
- The background is generated by `tool/generate_icons.dart` from the palette (1x and 2x, combined into a Retina TIFF at build time).
- The README documents the secrets and how to get a Developer ID certificate. The release notes describe the DMG.

Tested locally: the DMG builds (20 MB), and its `.DS_Store` has a 640x400 icon view with the app at (170,190) and Applications at (470,190). Signed with the local Developer ID certificate, `codesign --verify --strict --deep` passes and `spctl` rejects it only as "Unnotarized Developer ID". Notarization itself is untested because no notary credentials are available.

body:
## Why
The second review of #372 found two problems. First, "How a turn ends" rewrote `$M/told` only when the number of open lines changed. A turn that cleared one `local` line and told one new line kept the count the same and wrote nothing, so the new line was told again on the next turn. Second, autopilot-full's hand-over still asked for a recap at the close, which "How a turn ends" now forbids.

## What changed
- `features/home/skills/home/SKILL.md`: the block sets a `changed` flag when it drops a cleared line or adds a told one, and rewrites `told` on that flag instead of on `o != k` (F7).
- `features/home/skills/home/playbooks/autopilot-full.md`: the `Hand over` paragraph now applies only when the user asks, so closing the queue goes through "How a turn ends" like any other turn (F8).

## Scope
- Covers F7 and F8 only.
- Leaves out `orchestrate.md:38` and `shipping.md:34`, which also say "at the close". They are not in this brief's Where.

## Blast radius
This touches only how a home ends a turn and when autopilot-full recaps. The rewrite now runs in every case it ran before, plus the clear-and-tell case.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest features/home/tests/test_quiet_turns.py`: the new test `test_a_turn_that_clears_one_local_line_and_tells_one_new_line_keeps_both` fails on the test commit (the cleared line `stop local x: a` still shows on status) and passes with the fix. All 15 tests pass.

author: bld75
body:
Constats R4 et R14 de la revue du 24 octobre. **Empilée sur #102, elle-même sur #100** : seul le dernier commit est propre à cette PR.

**R4. `peek(key, freshAfter?)`.** (La signature est arrivée sur main avec #104 : un instant en ms ; cette PR l'emploie partout.) `peek` lisait toujours le cache du centre, même quand la mémoire de l'isolat avait une copie fraîche. Sur un isolat chaud, l'accueil faisait 17 lectures du cache du centre pour ses tuiles, une page commune ou `/aujourdhui` une dizaine, `resume_du_jour` une dizaine. Avec un seuil, une copie en mémoire obtenue depuis cet instant suffit ; sinon, comme avant, la plus récente de tous les magasins (et KV derrière pour les copies partagées, #102). Les appelants qui lisent des copies de pages passent `now - FRESH_SECONDS` : `tileCopies`, `readCopies`, la météo d'un secteur, les randonnées autour d'un lieu, le volcan du trafic ; les nouvelles de la route `now - ROAD_NEWS_STALE_SECONDS`. Les autres `peek` (presse, agenda, sport, sitemap) sont inchangés.

**R14. Une seule lecture dans `snapshot`.** Une page périmée sur un isolat froid lisait le cache du centre deux fois (`get(KEEP)` puis `get(FRESH)`). Maintenant :
- un `peek(key, now - FRESH_SECONDS)` lit la copie ;
- puis `Cache.getFrom(key, copie, secondes, construction)` sert ou reconstruit à partir de cette copie, sans relire les magasins (la copie lue reste celle servie si la source échoue).

Le `peek` avec seuil a déjà demandé au centre dès que la mémoire n'était pas fraîche : une copie plus récente d'un autre isolat est donc trouvée comme avant.

Sous-requêtes : en moins seulement. 0 lecture de tuile sur un isolat chaud aux copies fraîches, et 1 lecture au lieu de 2 pour une page périmée.

Tests :
- un isolat chaud sert `/` deux fois : 17 lectures de tuiles la première fois, 0 la seconde ;
- une page dont la copie a une heure, sur un isolat neuf : 1 seule lecture de sa clé dans le cache du centre, et la copie est reconstruite ;
- `cache.test.ts` : `peek` avec seuil n'interroge pas le magasin lent quand la mémoire est fraîche, l'interroge sinon ; `getFrom` sert ou reconstruit sans lire les magasins.
- Les deux tests de `web.test.ts` échouent sur le code d'avant.

Vérifié : `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run` (549 tests, après rebase sur #104).

author: ohah
body:
## 의도

EW3에서 저장소 재구축이 큰 문서 지연의 주된 몫이 아닌 것을 확인했습니다. 이번에는 편집과 프레임을 분리하고 파싱·접힘·색칠·표시 재구축의 어느 구간이 남은 비용을 차지하는지 좁힙니다.

## 구현

저장소 밖의 제품 소스 사본에만 시계를 주입하는 도구와 집계기·실패 주입을 추가했습니다. 제품 알고리즘·UX·스레딩은 바꾸지 않았습니다.

| 일반 입력 p50 | build.zig | Swift | 3.13MB 합성 Zig |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 편집+프레임 | 9.52ms | 9.54ms | 73.39ms |
| C 파싱 | 2.96ms | 0.82ms | 20.52ms |
| 접힘 캐시 조회 | 0.64ms | 0.61ms | 14.91ms |
| 표시 재구축 | 0.28ms | 0.53ms | 7.22ms |
| 구문 색 | 1.45ms | 1.81ms | 0.40ms |

모든 뷰의 괄호 목록·판정을 완료하고 입력을 시작합니다. 이전 EW3의 준비 조건과 달라 48.71→73.39ms를 제품 회귀나 괄호 자체 비용으로 해석하지 않습니다. 외부 부하와 allocator 배치도 통제하지 않았습니다. 하위 포함 시간과 중앙값을 단순 합산하지 않습니다.

다음 개선 대상으로 Maru가 제어하는 접힘 캐시 조회와 표식 재구축을 권고합니다. 후보 전체의 정렬·행 조회와 모든 줄의 표식 이진 탐색을 확인했지만, 개선 폭은 별도 구현 대조로 검증해야 합니다.

## 다이어그램

```mermaid
flowchart TD
 A["insertText / undoEdit"] --> B["refreshViewAfterEditImpl"]
 B --> C["syntaxEdit: onEditSpan / reparse"]
 C --> D["Provider.onEdit → C parser"]
 B --> E["ensureFoldRanges / rebuildVisible"]
 A --> F["appendPaneFrame"]
 F --> G["advanceSyntax → promoteFoldRangesToSyntax"]
 G --> H["foldSpansCached"]
 G --> I["installFoldRanges → rebuildVisible"]
 F --> J["syntaxColors / minimapSide / buildPaneOps"]
```

## 문서 정합성

- [x] 계획 인덱스·개발 명령·검증 매트릭스와 EW3 후속 링크를 동기화했습니다.
- `docs/plans/editor-frame-attribution.md`가 방법·판정·한계를, `tools/editor-frame-measure/results.md`가 전체 25조건의 구간별 p50을 보관합니다. p95와 키별 원시는 외부 산출물에 보존합니다.

## Clean-room 근거

- [x] Maru의 기존 제품 판정자와 독립 관측 코드만 사용했습니다. 외부 구현 복사는 없습니다.
- 새 의존성·VT 프로토콜 변경이 없습니다.

## 전략 영향 평가

- [x] private 사본에서만 계측하며 제품에 전역 관측 상태를 추가하지 않습니다.
- [x] 저장소·파싱 상한·실패 원자성·스레딩·UI 정책을 변경하지 않습니다.
- [x] 함수 경과시간을 CPU 전용 시간이나 GUI 입력 지연으로 확대하지 않습니다.

## 테스트

- 원문 5개 × 일반 입력·구조 편집·붙여넣기·Undo·공유 분할 × 3회: 성능 75회/855개 입력.
- 별도 정확성 25회/285개 입력: 키마다 버퍼/문서 본문·모든 뷰의 줄 내용·전체 순회 접힘 결과, 예상 byte/줄 수와 최종 상태를 대조했습니다.
- 원문·바이너리·계측 소스 해시, 키 대응과 부모 시간 경계를 검사했습니다. 괄호 준비 기록도 필수입니다.
- 키 대응·편집/프레임의 겹침·프레임 자식 경계·편집 자식 경계·포함 시간 이중 계산을 각각 누락/변형한 독립 결함 5개를 메모리 사본에 주입해 런타임에서 검출했습니다. 원본 전후 대조군 7개 통과. 컴파일 오류를 성공으로 세지 않았습니다.
- 준비가 파싱·접힘에만 머물던 조건을 보강했습니다. 이전 중간 실행은 `preliminary*`에 보존하고 최종 집계에서 제외했습니다.
- `check-doc-links`, `check-doc-line-refs`, Python 문법·단위 검사와 diff 공백 검사가 통과했습니다.

## E2E/관측 가능성

제품 메인 `3d04eefcc4dc45b6fa0ea8d05883867739518ab9`의 실제 편집·pane 프레임 함수 경로를 사용합니다. 일반 뷰 800×600, 같은 문서의 실제 공유 분할 각각 400×600입니다. 새 공유 뷰의 첫 접힘 캐시 구축도 전체 시간에 포함합니다.

증거: `/Users/yoonhb/.cache/maru-agent-artifacts/editor-frame-measure/`의 `inputs.json`, `setup-1.json`, `binaries.json`, `hardware.json`, `frame-summary.json`, `run-*.log`, `verify-*.log`. 독립 실패 주입은 `editor-frame-measure-review-final-ready/results.json`과 원본 전후·결함별 로그에 보존했습니다.

## UI 시각 검증

author: drneski
body:
Lightning-paid fireworks for the hub. A firework is a purchase, not a donation: it makes no bananas and never touches the pile, the leaderboard or the tally. Everyone on the island sees every show. The server side is bananapayserver's `feature/fireworks` branch, a general purchase API (its `protocol.md` v0.3) with fireworks as the first category. It isn't deployed yet.

**Merging this puts the stand on the island.** Until bananapayserver's purchase API is deployed with its migration and purchase settings, the stand's prices read CLOSED. With no backend at all (a static host, or a page opened from disk) it simulates, as the donation kiosk does.

## Concept

The stand's look (`docs/images/fireworks-concept-stand.webp`): the canopy and counter, the FIREWORKS sign with LIGHT UP OBL and rockets on it, BUY A FIREWORK on the left and TOP LAUNCHES on the right. The stand in `43ce909` follows it, keeping the real fireworks and prices (the Bolt is 69 sats, and TOP LAUNCHES lists the fireworks that exist).

![Fireworks stand concept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OogaBoogaX/oogaboogaland/3fd56224b8084029ab8bc545b0f58cbd846eaffd/docs/images/fireworks-concept-stand.webp)

The first concept sheet (`docs/images/fireworks-concept-sheet.webp`): the three fireworks and the MVP.

![Fireworks concept sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OogaBoogaX/oogaboogaland/3fd56224b8084029ab8bc545b0f58cbd846eaffd/docs/images/fireworks-concept-sheet.webp)

## Step 1: the engine (`60b5751`)

- **`fireworks.js`**: GPU-driven sprites flown analytically in the vertex shader. Each burst is seeded from its id, so every page draws the same show. Per-tier sprite caps (60k, 30k, 15k), a queue past the cap, and writing in 1 ms slices. Ooga Pop, Lightning Bolt, ₿ Mega Blast and the show pack.
- **`fireworks-audio.js`**: pooled, synthesized launch and burst sound with distance delay, suspended after 10 s of quiet.
- **`gl-renderer.js`**: the sprite stage, the bursts' light on the island, sea glints and sky glow. **`canvas-renderer.js`**: up to 1,500 of the sparks alight, as squares.
- **`scene-hub.js`**: the show bursts above the Timechain Sphere, 150 m up. Rockets leave the rock north of its stairs, clearing rock by more than 20 m and the Sphere's shell by more than 8 m.
- **`director.js`**: the quality auto-tier takes no evidence while a show is up (`holdTier`).
- **Nothing at rest**: no sprite program, buffer, data or audio context before the first launch.

## Step 2: the stand (`b1814e7`, `1875214`, `58a9e1e`, `43ce909`)

- **`stand-kiosk.js`**: the stand's screen, in the donation popup's dialog and the Factory kiosk's letters and QR.
  - A list of items at the server's prices; the invoice is made the moment one is chosen.
  - Pays through the browser's WebLN wallet in one click, and only inside the visitor's own click. OPEN WALLET (a `lightning:` link) and the QR are there too.
  - SIGN IN TO BUY while only signed-in visitors may buy, and a free PREVIEW that only the visitor sees.
  - It knows nothing of what an item does, so the stand can later become an OBL store.
- **`stand-models.js`** (`43ce909`): the stand as a small attraction, to the concept above.
  - A timber booth in eighth-of-a-metre voxels with a red and white striped canopy, a scalloped valance and bunting that sways in the wind.
  - A merchant counter with the terminal built in (BUY HERE), a painted cloth, and shelves of firework boxes and bundles.
  - The FIREWORKS sign with LIGHT UP OBL and a marquee of bulbs that chase round it, four oversized voxel rockets standing on it, and gold starbursts that twinkle.
  - A vendor Ooga in a straw hat; lanterns that light the counter at night.
  - BUY A FIREWORK on the left (the three fireworks, their icons and the server's prices) and TOP LAUNCHES on the right under a crown and banner.
- **`scene-hub.js`**:
  - The stand sits on open grass right of the Sphere's stairs, beside the path down from them; its ground and the strip before it are claimed, so palms and scatter stay clear. Space at the counter, or a tap on it or the menu, opens its screen.
  - TOP LAUNCHES ranks the fireworks by launches over the last seven days, from bananapayserver's `purchaseCounts`; a tap opens it, with the top ten buyers on the dialog's second page. With no API the page counts its own launches.
  - `onFirework` launches each paid firework at the server's `launchAt`, with a countdown toast.
  - After paying, the buyer's view glides up to watch, then back home.
- **`donations.js`**, on bananapayserver's purchase API:
  - `purchase(category, item)` and `purchaseTotals(category)`.
  - `status.catalogue`, the `purchase` message (a firework's carries `slot` and `launchAt`; other categories are ignored for now), each category's `purchaseBoard`, and `purchaseCounts` (each item's paid purchases over seven days).
  - Category and item names are checked exactly as bananapayserver allows them.
  - The server's clock, estimated from each purchase's `at`; the fastest sample wins.
  - The scenes hear a paid firework as `{ id, kind, slot, launchAt, login, mine }`, the same with or without the API.
  - A simulated purchase with no API behind the page.
- **`director.js`**: each paid firework goes to the active scene, or becomes a toast in any other; the buyer's own closes the stand's dialog.
- **Worker**: purchases have their own prefix. `POST /purchases/buy` and `POST /purchases/mine` go on to bananapayserver with the body, the signed-in buyer and the visitor's address, through the same checks as donations. `/purchases/*` runs the Worker first in all three wrangler configs; the old `/donations/purchase*` paths answer 404. The socket stays `/donations/socket`.
- **Privacy** (AGENTS.md):
  - A signed-in purchase is kept in bananapayserver's D1 with the GitHub id and login, and the login is shown with the firework and on the plaque.
  - An anonymous purchase, once everyone may buy, carries only coarse counts.
  - The browser's own count of purchases stays in localStorage (`oogaboogaland.bought`).
- **From reviewing the stand** (`1875214`):
  - The lantern post hangs outward, so its arm no longer hides the F of FIREWORKS.
  - The plaque has PLAYER, LAUNCHED and SATS columns, and a long login is cut with an ellipsis.
  - While the view watches a firework, the act button, the hint and the touch sticks step aside; the countdown stays.

## Performance

Two different kinds of cost: the stand is a static prop that is always there and costs almost nothing, and the fireworks are a temporary event that costs nothing until someone buys one and a bounded amount while it flies.

### The stand: a static prop, minimal impact

| What | Cost | How it was measured |
|---|---|---|
| Hub build | 25–30 ms of a ~3 s build (about 1%) | performance marks round its build, four boots |
| Geometry | about 9,400 faces in 40 geometries on 54 nodes, the vendor included | counted in the page; the hub holds about 940 geometry records |
| Pictures | 4 (the two boards, the cloth, the terminal's glass), about half a million texels | uploaded once; repainted only when the prices or the launch counts change |
| Lights | 2 lanterns light the counter at night | inside each tier's point-light budget (32 / 20 / 10); the boards' lanterns only glow |
| Collision | its timber joins the island's solids | the same solid-mesh tests every prop uses |

- **Beyond 30 m nothing of it moves.** Each frame it only compares what its boards show against what they last painted: identity checks, no allocation.
- **Within 30 m** six stars and three marquee groups change their glow, the vendor turns his head, and every 1–2 s five sparks come from the island's shared effects pool. None of it allocates, adds a draw or touches the GPU beyond a per-instance glow value.
- **Its models are built once per visit and cached,** like every other builder, and released with the hub's other geometry when the visit ends.
- **Canvas 2D** draws the same geometry; the sign's lettering is two

author: zyx1121
body:
Closes #51. Closes #114. Closes #115.

**#51.1, an unanswered reserve**: `reserve` now tells a refusal (`Refused`: the system said no, or signing in failed, so nothing was submitted) from no clear answer (`Unanswered`: a timeout or a body without an id). After an unanswered one, `placeBooking` waits 3 s, reads the room's public listing (it carries reservation ids) and releases the lab's reservations of exactly that room and span that no portal booking holds. The member gets a clear message either way, including when the system shows nothing yet.

**Leases instead of locks**: bookings take short leases in a new `booking_leases` table (migration 0044): one per member and day, one per room and day. Waiting holds no connection, and a lease left by a dead process runs out after 3 minutes. The room lease covers the reserve and the insert, so the clean-up never meets another member's booking of that room half done.

**#114**: a hand booking and the standing meeting catch-up take the same member-and-day lease. Inside it the catch-up checks for a hand booking, and the hand booking checks for a standing booking of the same span and picks its room from a fresh read.

**#115**:
1. A lab hold with no portal booking no longer stops a series for good. A hold of exactly the span (maybe this week's own unanswered reserve) still stops it with the usual mail. A wider one, such as the old Monday 411 hold, is logged and another room is picked. Every room is checked, and an exact hold wins.
2. `bookOccurrence` returns booked, skipped or the failure, so 先訂好 N 場 counts only real bookings.
3. Only a hand booking of the same span (no series) counts as that week.

**#51.2** was already fixed by #112: each daily run books every unsettled day within 7 days, so a missed day is made up.

Verified on sandbox against a fake department system:
- A hanging or non-JSON reserve leaves no hold, and the member is told.
- Another member's reservation is never released.
- With the series booked first, a hand booking of the same span is refused.
- Hand and series at once give 1 booking, and the series reports booked 0 with no error.
- An unrelated overlapping meeting does not stop the series.
- 4 members hit a hanging system at once: 4 clear errors, 0 orphan holds, 0 leases left.
- 8 members book at once with no pool errors.

Dual review. Codex round 1 found 4 problems, round 2 found 3 more: releasing another member's reservation, lock waiters filling the pool, and an exact hold hidden behind a wider one. All are fixed above. The reviewer passed, and its notes (login errors read as timeouts, the first match only, 1 room checked) are fixed too.

author: jgoyvaerts
body:
The `with_table` point from the #408 review, which didn't go in with #420.

With reserved table regions (no-map systems such as the T6040), `with_table` reached a page-table page outside the two regions through `Page::borrow_phys_unchecked()`. That is undefined behaviour when the page is other no-map memory without a struct page. When `reserved` is set it now uses the checked `Page::borrow_phys()` and refuses such a page with `-EIO`. Systems without reserved regions keep the unchecked borrow of a page-table page they allocated, as before.

On the coherency question, the commit documents what holds and what is assumed:
- **Holds:** the one clean and invalidate of the reserved regions runs after the boot, when the host has already written entries (fixed kernel objects are mapped before `boot()`). That's safe because the T6040 also sets `UatQuirks::clean_tables`, so every host table store is cleaned to the PoC as it's made, and the invalidate drops only clean lines.
- **Assumed:** not invalidating again relies on the firmware no longer writing the tables the host walks once it has booted. We haven't proven that with a trace. Our J616s has run this way since its GPU came up, and we've never traced a fault to a stale table. The comment says so rather than presenting it as a fact.

The `invalidate_reserved_tables()` comment in `mmu.rs` said this ran "before the first host edit", which isn't true; it's corrected too.

As you said in the review, this path can go once the boot loader puts the ranges in `/memory`. Until then it's what the T6040 runs on.

**Tested:** on our J616s since 7.3.0-m4.17 (daily kernel `jgoyvaerts/linux` `m4/aurora-7.3`, now this commit on 420a1c8f5): GPU desktop, GL and Vulkan, no `-EIO` from this path. KUnit (asahi, QEMU) 120/120.

**Base:** `integration/aurora` (`420a1c8f5`). Built with W=1 (`CONFIG_DRM_ASAHI=m`, `CONFIG_DRM_ASAHI_G16=y`): no new warnings (the tip's own `fetch_update` deprecations and the unused `MM` static remain with our rustc 1.99); checkpatch --strict clean.

author: copilot
body:
The `Build android-x64` job fails at CMake configure because `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/28.2.13676358/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake` doesn't exist. The runner image doesn't ship the NDK version pinned in `ANDROID_NDK_VER`. The Ninja and compiler errors in the log follow from that failure.

- **Workflow (`.github/workflows/build.yml`)**
  - Adds an `Install Android NDK` step before the build steps. It runs only for Android matrix entries, so `android-arm64` gets the same fix.
  - It installs the pinned NDK and platform with `sdkmanager`, reusing the existing `ANDROID_NDK_VER` and `ANDROID_PLATFORM_VER`:

```yaml
- name: Install Android NDK
  if: ${{ contains(matrix.platform.name, 'android') }}
  shell: bash
  run: |
    "${ANDROID_HOME}/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager" --install "ndk;${ANDROID_NDK_VER}" "platforms;android-${ANDROID_PLATFORM_VER}"
```

The fix is unverified until the workflow runs on this branch. It assumes `sdkmanager` is at `$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/` on `ubuntu-latest`.

author: castlemilk
body:
Stacked on the P1 PR. It retargets to main when P1 merges.

`github.com/google/generative-ai-go` was archived on 2026-10-12. Its stream reader broke on Go 1.27 and works only because gax-go is pinned at v2.27.0. It also cannot send back thought signatures, which Gemini 3.x tool calling requires. This moves chat's Gemini adapter onto `google.golang.org/genai`.

**Adapter (`provider_genai.go`)**
- **Own transcript:** it keeps its own `[]*genai.Content` and replays the model's full Content verbatim (thought signatures, function-call parts, signature-only parts).
- **Tool results:** these go back as one user-role Content of FunctionResponse parts, in order.
- **Thought parts** never reach the user.
- **ToolConfig:** Auto → nil, Required → ANY, None → NONE.
- **Usage:** taken from the last chunk.
- **Errors:** mapped to `ProviderError` (`genai.APIError` 429/5xx are retryable; a cancel is not).
- **Automatic continuation** is off.

**Parity with the legacy SDK (from the Opus review)**
- **Blocked replies:** a blocked prompt or a SAFETY/RECITATION/BLOCKLIST/PROHIBITED/SPII finish is now an error again. genai does not raise one, so these would have been stored as empty or truncated answers. `Reached` reflects only the chunks before the block, so the `chat_usage_events` accounting matches P1.
- **Streaming:** text in a chunk that also carries a function call is not streamed, as in P1. Otherwise "Let me check." would be glued to the answer.
- **Mutation tests:** all 12 mutants fail their tests.

**Live eval:** 56 turns, gates 0.95.

| | P1 (legacy) | P1b (genai) |
|---|---|---|
| Correct | 48/48 | 48/48 |
| Grounded | 48/48 | 48/48 |
| Errors | 0 | 0 |
| Median total | 3.16 s | 2.94 s |

**Token cost.** Prompt tokens are about 7% higher and cache hits about 8% lower, which the review traced to replaying thought signatures. Gemini bills the previous call's reasoning as input (about 80 tokens per later call), and a unique signature limits prefix-cache reuse across repeated identical questions. Signatures are required for Gemini 3, so this is the intended cost. The first call of every turn is token-identical.

**Dependencies.** genai becomes a direct dependency of `services`, with `gorilla/websocket` and `go-cmp` indirect. `generative-ai-go` stays for the batch jobs until P1c, and so does the gax regression test.

**Verification:** build, vet, `-short`/`-cover`/`-race`, arm64 vet, tidy and golangci-lint v2.15.0 all pass.

## What (client request, 24 Oct)
1. **Contact lists**: each uploaded sheet is saved to a named list (new or existing). A student can be in several lists. The Contacts page can filter by list.

- `redeem_invitation` now also checks the new tables.
- The migration only adds tables and functions; it doesn't change existing data.

## Also fixed
The import read existing contacts and exclusions in one request, which stops at 1,000 rows. Watim has 1,241 contacts, so these reads are now paged.

- New CI database test `supabase/ci/verify-contact-lists.sql` covers isolation, the membership guard, agent vs admin delete, and delete-with-contacts keeping shared contacts.

author: rakeshgangwar
body:
A board holds one open question per run. When Salaam had two pending strict decisions (Pi asked for two reviews in parallel), the bridge offered both at once. The second question cancelled the first, and the run looped on "Strict question cancelled" (`run_e1505c872e9249f7` on staging).

The bridge now offers only the oldest pending decision, ordered by expiry and then request id. The next one goes out once that one is answered and leaves Salaam's pending list, or expires. A decision that was never offered never enters the hub's decision table, so expiry recovery still sees only the one it published.

Tests:
- The selector unit test, and a drive-loop test where Salaam returns two pending decisions (newest first). Both were red before the change.
- Revert-check: removing the ordering turns both red.

Local parity on workbench, hub `bun test`: 4091 pass. Three tests failed locally:
- the two typecheck-baseline tests, which run out of memory on workbench;
- `broker.stream`, which also failed locally before and passes on GitHub.

The strict suites (`salaam-work`, `salaam-dispatch-trace`, `salaam-one-driver` and the bridge unit tests) are all green.

author: markjungeblut
body:
## Summary
Builds the legal notice at `/impressum` as the mockup's overlay. On wide screens it is a right-hand sidebar over the dimmed page; on narrow screens it is a full-screen sheet. It is a native `<dialog>`:

- It is prerendered `open`, so the notice is in the static HTML and readable without JavaScript.
- After render it becomes modal, which puts it above the header with a backdrop, traps focus, makes the page behind inert and lets Escape close it.
- The Close link, a backdrop click and Escape all close it to `/`. The page keeps its scroll position, and focus returns to the header link.

What else changed:

- **Content:** the details and German wording come from `docs/mockup/ImpressumPage.tsx`. The heading now cites **§ 5 DDG**, replacing the source's § 5 TMG. The email address is a mailto link, and the text carries `lang="de"`.
- **App shell:** the router outlet moves outside `<main>`. A CSS-only `html:has(dialog[open])` rule stops the page behind from scrolling.
- **Review fixes:**
  - a drag that ends over the backdrop no longer closes the dialog;
  - an early close isn't undone by the modal upgrade;
  - scrolling the sheet doesn't carry into the page on iOS.

Known gap: phones have no link to the Impressum until the mobile menu lands, and that menu must include one. Plan: `docs/plans/0009-impressum-overlay.md`.

## Type of change
feat — the Impressum overlay is a new user-facing page.

## Test plan
- New `impressum-page.spec.ts` with 10 tests. jsdom has no dialog support, so the spec fakes the browser's behaviour. The tests cover:
  - the full content;
  - the dialog becoming modal, and not leaving the route while it does;
  - each way of closing (Close link, backdrop click, Escape);
  - a click inside the panel and a drag onto the backdrop, neither of which closes it;
  - an early close that the upgrade must not undo.
- `npm run verify` passes.
- Checked `dist/.../browser/impressum/index.html`: it contains `<dialog open>`, the full content and no placeholder data.
- Checked the static build in headless Chrome:
  - At 1440×900 the modal panel is 680px wide and the page grid is unchanged.
  - Focus starts on Close, and Tab stays inside the dialog.
  - Escape returns to `/` with the scroll position kept and focus back on the header link.
  - A backdrop click closes it; a click inside or a drag to the backdrop does not.
  - At 390×844 it is a full-screen sheet with a 56×44 Close target.
  - Without JavaScript the panel sits above the header.

## Definition of Done
- [x] Build passes
- [x] Typecheck passes (where separate from the build)
- [x] All tests pass (new logic has new tests)
- [x] Lint checks pass
- [x] Format checks pass

author: liennguyenhp
body:
Fixes #285.

## What was wrong

`speech_voices` was unusable against any OpenAI-audio-compatible gateway that does not publish `GET /audio/voices` - even though that listing is documented as **optional** in two places and `VOICES_OUT` already allows `"voices": null`:

| Where | What it says |
|---|---|
| `scripts/setup-steps/70-speech.sh:3` | `optional voice listing` |
| `commands/odoo-setup.md:643` | ``optional `GET <base_url>/audio/voices` `` |
| `scripts/mcp/odoo_media/tools_speech.py` | `VOICES_OUT` declares `"voices": {"type": [..., "null"]}` |

`speech_client.voices()` turned every failure, a 404 included, into a fatal `SpeechError`. Because the MCP handler calls `voices()` **before** `models()` inside one `try`, that raise also discarded the model ids - which the same gateway does serve. The registry description meanwhile promised the opposite of the two docs above: *"a gateway that publishes none answers an error"*.

## What this changes

- `voices()` returns `None` on HTTP 404 - the listing is simply not published, which is an answer, not a failure.
- Every other refusal still raises: 401, TLS, a 5xx, a dead host. Those mean the value or the endpoint is wrong and must stay loud. That distinction is the point of the fix, not an accident of it.
- `speech_voices` therefore still returns `models`, `tts_model_guess` and `stt_model_guess`, with `voices: null`. The output schema already permitted this - no schema change needed.
- The tool description and the two module docstrings stop promising an error and say what actually happens.

No change to the handler body, no new option, no new configuration key.

## Test

`tests/test_speech_setup.py::test_an_endpoint_that_publishes_no_voice_listing_still_answers_with_its_models` stands up a LiteLLM-shaped gateway where `/models` answers and `/audio/voices` is not published, and asserts three things:

1. `voices()` reads as "none published" (`None`),
2. `models()` still returns both ids,
3. a gateway answering **401** still raises - so the fix cannot quietly swallow a real failure.

Proven to fail for the right reason: with the patch reverted the test goes red on `urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 404: Not Found`, which is exactly the behaviour it guards. With the patch it passes.

`tests/test_speech_setup.py` as a whole: 18 passed. The one reported error is `tests/conftest.py:329` iterating `/proc` at session teardown, which does not exist on macOS - pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

## Verified against a real gateway

Found on a LiteLLM gateway fronting VieNeu-TTS and Kokoro-82M:

| Path | Status |
|---|---|
| `/v1/models` | 401 (exists, wants auth) |
| `/v1/audio/voices` | 404 (not published) |
| `/v1/voices` | 404 (not published) |
| `/v1/audio/speech` | 405 (exists, GET is the wrong method) |

`speech_probe` passes on both configured languages against that same endpoint, WER 0 - only the enumeration tool was broken.

## Note for reviewers

A 404 from an **explicitly configured** `tts.voices_url` is treated the same as a missing default listing. Distinguishing the two - so a typo'd `voices_url` is reported rather than read as "none published" - is arguably more correct, but it is a separate behaviour nobody has asked for, so it is deliberately left out of this change.
