author: 1kebron
body:
Main `668276c9459c63843018e0ead78ecb7b302501bf` globally forces `undici@6.27.0`, affected by [GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c / CVE-2026-109869](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c). A malicious remote server can send more than five content codings and close before the body; an orphaned stream error can terminate a Node process even if fetch rejection is caught. The affected 6.x range is >=6.23.0 <6.29.1.

Advance the existing exact override and sole runtime lock record to **6.29.1**. This is the narrow shared dependency-selection boundary and avoids a major upgrade.

Changes:
- `package.json`: exact existing undici override 6.27.0 → 6.29.1.
- `bun.lock`: same exact override and runtime resolution/SRI. Repository-pinned Bun 1.3.9 adds `configVersion: 0` during normalization.
- Delete obsolete `bun.lockb`, which encodes a separate legacy graph (including undici 5.28.4). Docker/CI consume the text lock. This prevents an alternative stale install graph from remaining.
- Add root `Agent.md` with user-required implementation policies and draft-only email policy.
- All 1,972 unrelated package records and every other manifest field remain unchanged.

Reachability and native build vectors:
- `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@5.0.47` loads npm `Agent` and `fetch` in `src/safe-node-fetch.ts:146–160`; the application declares AI SDK consumers.
- `node-gyp@12.4.0/lib/download.js:2,19` imports npm `Agent, EnvHttpProxyAgent, RetryAgent, fetch` and uses fetch for downloads. Native build chain: electron-builder → app-builder-lib → @electron/rebuild 4.2.0 → node-gyp 12.4.0 → undici. A malicious/compromised download endpoint is therefore relevant during build tooling execution.
- `@connectrpc/connect-node@1.7.0` uses Undici Headers; application dynamically imports its parent @cursor/sdk. Optional `@electron/get@5.0.0` uses EnvHttpProxyAgent/setGlobalDispatcher.
- Existing consumer ranges are ^7.29.0, ^6.25.0, ^5.28.4 and optional ^7.24.4. The cross-major overrides already exist on main; this patch retains the 6.x major and does not introduce that constraint. Archive source confirms 6.29.1 still exports all the above consumer APIs. Runtime compatibility across those inherited major mismatches is not claimed verified.
- Application ambient fetch paths, Node built-in fetch, Bun native fetch and embedded Electron runtime Undici are separate implementations; this npm pin does not patch those runtimes. Deployed artifacts were not inspected.

Registry integrity and provenance:
- [Canonical npm metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/undici/6.29.1) and [archive](https://registry.npmjs.org/undici/-/undici-6.29.1.tgz) independently downloaded as data.
- Computed SHA-512 exactly matches npm and lock:
  `sha512-EvRlUt/QqAEvXdQeRMYUfwOQsfzpDztykrG2owGEE/rBOBoYv9uF39ZzsNDh4lTFHhTr2XOZjKkYgueD12ZmGA==`
- SHA-1: `a3317c5df0236e0633727d9a7bd4f7ed195d8575`.
- Official Git tag `v6.29.1` and npm `gitHead` both identify `8c57f6c68c95465338ae97bfc991cb1513d2f76e`.
- Both npm ECDSA registry signatures verify via OpenSSL against the published npm key `SHA256:DhQ8wR5APBvFHLF/+Tc+AYvPOdTpcIDqOhxsBHRwC7U`.
- [Published attestations](https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/undici@6.29.1) contain matching archive SHA-512 and SLSA source commit, repository nodejs/undici, workflow .github/workflows/release.yml on v6.x. Their Sigstore certificate/transparency trust chain was not independently verified; this is a record of published provenance, not a provenance-verification claim.
- Node engine remains >=18.17; no runtime/optional dependencies added. No native binary/addon or binding.gyp in archive. Existing llhttp WASM is embedded in JavaScript files; no native build was run. Upstream prepare/build scripts exist and were not invoked.
- Four consumer archive hashes also match their existing lock SRIs.

Validation:
1. PASS syntax/data boundary: standard-library Python parses manifest and lock as data, confirms exact pin/resolution/SRI, checks all package identities including nested/aliased copies, and proves every unrelated graph record unchanged. `git diff --check` passes.
2. PASS scoped security substitute: checks reject vulnerable baseline and injected nested/aliased vulnerable resolutions. Archive source validates content-coding count and aborts before allocating the body stream; lowercasing, splitting and trimming are retained. This is source/resolution evidence, not an executed exploit reproduction.
3. PASS package-manager acceptance: repository-pinned Bun 1.3.9 `bun install --lockfile-only --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --cache-dir <task-cache>`; repeated with byte-identical lock (SHA-256 `be938f949b9ec688090bf19274be5b15aa4e5db466cdfa2aa9ae54ba6b95ffe4`). No node_modules created. This validates lock resolution, not a full install.
4. Static legitimate-behavior evidence: unchanged Node engine/runtime dependency metadata and required public exports, unchanged consumer records/callers. Dynamic legitimate-response behavior is unverified.
5. NOT RUN: dynamic exploit/ordinary-response controls, package/application tests, lint, typecheck, builds or lifecycle hooks, because the task explicitly prohibits package execution. Complete runtime security verification remains blocked by that constraint. No claim that the original runtime crash was experimentally shown not to reproduce.

Prepared in a fresh isolated clone in this projectless task workspace. No existing checkout, credentials, chat or deployment was modified. No merge performed. Leave this draft for human review; runtime checks can be performed separately in an authorized environment.
Independent fresh read-only investigation and adversarial patch review completed; no concrete surviving resolution bypass or change-induced regression found. Immediately before publication, refreshed main and all 19 open PR heads and confirmed that every lock graph still selects undici 6.27.0. PR #18 remains proxy-addr/source-map-js only; #19 remains ws-only. No equivalent open undici fix was found.

author: khoa-yelo
body:
Main's `test-compat (macos-latest, 3.12)` job, which runs only on push, fails 239 tests. Every one of them runs a FarmShare Slurm script that needs GNU `sha256sum`, `flock`, `realpath -e` or `stat -c`. Four more need x87 80-bit long double (wallenius on arm64).

**The change:**
- **GNU probe:** a once-per-session probe in `tests/helpers/gnu_userland.py`. The shared script runners, `Sandbox.run` and `M10Sandbox.popen`, skip with "FarmShare/GNU userland only" when the probe fails, so future script tests are covered automatically.
- **Markers:** `gnu_userland` and `x87_longdouble`.
- **Guard test:** a Linux-only test requires the probe to pass, so a broken probe can't silently skip the script tests on FarmShare or ubuntu.
- **Checks:** with the GNU tools present, 988 pass and 0 fail. With them hidden behind stubs, all 235 GNU failures skip. 13 new probe tests.
- **What stays:** the scripts are untouched (FarmShare-only, G19), and the bash 3.2 check is unaffected. The macOS result will show on main after merge, because PR CI doesn't run that job.

**Scope on macOS (review S1):** the guard skips every sandboxed script test there (about 384), including about 149 that happened to pass, because the scripts are FarmShare-only (G19). Linux skips none.

author: kyngkai909
body:
On `command.useclear.org`, every section request was blocked at the browser's preflight:

> Request header field x-command-session is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers in preflight response.

## Why
The Command Center sends its session in `X-Command-Session` on every request once someone is signed in (`apps/command/src/live/api.ts`; the API reads it in `routes/command.ts`). That header wasn't in the API's CORS `allowedHeaders`, so sign-in worked but every section showed "Couldn't reach the protocol."

## The fix
- `X-Command-Session` is added to `allowedHeaders` in `apps/api/src/index.ts`.
- `services/command/cors.test.ts` reads the Command app's API client and checks that every header it sets is in the allowlist. A header added there later fails in CI instead of in the browser.

## Checked
- API: `bun test src` 1247 pass, 0 fail.
- Member: 846 pass, 0 fail (its tests read API source).
- Merchant: 235 pass, 0 fail.

The other CORS problem, the `command.useclear.org` origin itself, was a Railway variable and is already fixed (`CORS_ORIGIN`).

author: moark-peralta-study-repo
body:
feat: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint provider

Lets the learner run the harness on their own model stack — an LLM router
(llmrouter), LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama or any gateway speaking the OpenAI
chat-completions protocol — instead of a fixed provider catalog.

- Settings > Providers > Custom endpoint: paste a base URL + key, Connect.
  The URL is normalized (a bare host gets /v1), then {base}/models is
  fetched with the key; the discovered models federate into every picker
  (slots, per-session, background roles) as the `custom` provider.
- Discovery is the save gate: a wrong URL or key fails in the form with
  the endpoint's own message and nothing is stored. Keys mask through the
  existing keys seam under CUSTOM_ENDPOINT_API_KEY; the URL lives in
  data/endpoint.json.
- The record reaches the agent layer through pushed globalThis state (the
  chatgpt-bridge precedent) so the agent layer keeps its no-store-import
  rule and a URL change is live on the next request, no restart.
- Unknown metadata takes pi's honest defaults: contextWindow 0 renders as
  a usage-only meter (compaction falls back), no reasoning levels, zero
  cost; an advertised context length / image modality is honored.
- app/ routes come through the @/src/server barrel only; keys.ts offers
  the custom key in the roster once a URL exists.

Tests: pure URL/parse/gate units, live-state + engine-resolution units, a
render smoke test, and the catalog test exempts custom models from the
contextWindow>0 pin. Gates: typecheck, lint, build, 2037/2038 (the single
failure is a pre-existing SVG-font case that fails on upstream too).

author: jgoyvaerts
body:
The firmware-identity point from the #408 review: the T6040 chose its firmware build only from `apple,firmware-version`, and the init-data hash covers the driver's own constants, so neither proves which build is loaded. This reuses the G16 backend's check instead of adding a second one.

### DT (commits 1-2)
- `fw-text` reserved region on the J616s GPU node: the text segment of the loaded GPU firmware (ADT `gfx-asc` `segment-ranges[0]`, 0x60000 bytes), after the five regions it already has. Like them, the node stays disabled until a boot loader fills it.
- Binding (its own commit): `fw-text` allowed as the sixth `memory-region-names` entry, and in the T6040 branch's list.

### Driver (commit 3)
- **Shared `fwid` module:** G16's loaded-TEXT identity (`g16/identity.rs` + the SHA-256 glue) moves to `drivers/gpu/drm/asahi/fwid.{rs,c}`, built for every asahi build. It hashes the image with the entropy bytes of its GKTS and ECAP records zeroed, plus the segment sizes. A build entry names its two record offsets, which are checked and zeroed exactly as G16 did with its fixed offsets. Only an unknown image has its records found by their tags, so it's reported with a digest that stays the same across boots (a new variant, like the 8-core J713 image in #389, is then one more `FirmwareBuild` entry). **G16 behaves as before:** the T8132 entry keeps its offsets (0x5c8df / 0x5c9c2) and digest.
- **G17:** a `Build` now carries its `FirmwareBuild`. After `apple,firmware-version` selects the build, `identify_image()` measures the `fw-text` region against it, with the `fw-data` region's size as the DATA size. A missing region, a different image or a different size refuses the GPU (`ENODEV`, with "GPU firmware image not admitted" and the measured digest in the log).
- **T6040:** the 25G83 image as measured on a J616s with macOS 26.6.2: TEXT 0x60000, DATA 0x138000, entropy at 0x59839 / 0x5991c, SHA-256 `03df7548…63876dcd`.

This answers fbalazsy's `.701.1` question on #408. A Recovery-installed 26.6.2 (`mBoot-18000.161.10.701.1`) is admitted when its loaded TEXT is this image, and refused when it isn't. A tree whose `fw-text` address doesn't match the unit is refused the same way, rather than running the GPU with the wrong layouts. A tree without `fw-text` no longer gets the GPU, which matters little while the J616s node ships disabled.

Not in this PR:
- **Sharing the region names** (`shared-l2` vs `l2-pagetables`; both are the firmware kernel window's L2 page). Boot loaders fill these regions by name (ours does, from `gfx-shared-l2-region`), so renaming now would make an installed loader's GPU fill fail on the next kernel. I'd do it together with an m1n1 T6040 `dt_set_gpu`, so the name changes once, in the tree and in the loaders.
- The leakage coefficients.
- m1n1 filling `fw-text`. Our loader fills it from `segment-ranges[0]` today, and that `dt_set_gpu` would do the same.

**Tested:** J616s, macOS 26.6.2 boot firmware, our loader filling the GPU node from the ADT. Every boot since 7.3.0-m4.17 logs `GPU firmware build: Apple GFX 25G83 for T6040 (normalized loaded image)`, with the desktop on the GPU. KUnit (asahi, QEMU) 120/120 on the daily tree. This branch builds on 420a1c8f5 with no new warnings, and the binding and the J616s DTB pass `dt_binding_check`/`CHECK_DTBS`. The final `fwid` lookup (a known build checked at its own offsets) was checked against a dump of the J616s TEXT: same digest and offsets.

**Base:** `integration/aurora` (`420a1c8f5`). Built with W=1 (`CONFIG_DRM_ASAHI=m`, both with and without `CONFIG_DRM_ASAHI_G16`): the same warnings as the base, none in the files touched here. checkpatch --strict clean, apart from the generic MAINTAINERS note for the new `fwid.{rs,c}` (drm/asahi has no MAINTAINERS entry).

author: vveliev
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - This fork keeps its own recovery and control-plane fixes on the prerelease branch.
> - Upstream master has 988 commits that prerelease does not contain, including a split of the 30k-line heartbeat service into modules and 94 new migrations.
> - The fork needs those upstream changes while keeping its own fixes.
> - This pull request merges upstream master at bf223596a into prerelease.
> - The benefit is a current prerelease branch with both histories preserved.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Previous sync PR: https://github.com/vveliev/paperclip/pull/43. This PR continues that series.

**What happened?**

The fork's prerelease branch at c0afc702f is behind upstream master by 988 commits and has 51 fork commits of its own.

**Expected behavior**

Prerelease should contain upstream master and keep the fork's recovery, blocked-issue descriptor, cross-issue cap, skill-read, and orphan-lease fixes.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Fetch upstream master and fork prerelease.
2. Compare the branches with `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/prerelease...upstream/master`.
3. Before this merge, the result is `51 988`.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Fork base: c0afc702f. Upstream tip: bf223596a.

**Deployment mode**

Built from source. The merged code applies to all deployment modes.

## What Changed

- Merge 988 upstream commits into the fork's prerelease history with a merge commit.
- Resolve 16 conflicted files.
- Re-apply the fork's four `heartbeat.ts` deltas onto upstream's new module split: the local orphan-lease recovery moves to `server/src/services/heartbeat/recovery.ts`, the BLA-687 `unblockDescriptor` on the worktree-preflight blocked write moves to `server/src/services/heartbeat/queue.ts`, and the `sweepRecoveryActionsForResolvedPlatformCauses` passthrough stays in `server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`.
- Keep the fork's per-stage startup recovery isolation in `server/src/index.ts` and add upstream's `timeStartupRecovery` timing wrappers inside it.
- Keep the fork's GIF-49 terminal-conflict tolerance in `server/src/services/recovery/service.ts` and add a thunk-based variant for upstream's transaction-scoped issue service calls, so the BLA-687 `unblockDescriptor` writes survive the new transaction plumbing.
- Keep the fork's recovery-action expiry (BLA-1074) and cause-change reclassification (BLA-1084) beside upstream's native-run activity projection and execution-control write queue in `server/src/services/issue-recovery-actions.ts`.
- Keep the fork's stale `sourceLocator` fallback to the materialized `__runtime__` copy on top of upstream's binary-safe skill file read in `server/src/services/company-skills.ts`, and drop the unreachable duplicate tail left by an earlier rebase.
- Keep the fork's lock-based own-issue detection in `server/src/services/cross-issue-influence-limit.ts` and take upstream's tighter null guard on the source-issue comparison. Keep the fork's BLA-582 and GIF-41 tests and adopt upstream's stricter `sourceIssueId: null` assertion.
- Take upstream's recomputed resume condition in the comment route; the fork's `willTransitionIssueOutOfTerminalStatus` gate on workspace reopen stays.
- Take upstream's marker-based ownership probe in `scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh` in place of the fork's weekly background audit. Both solve the same slow-boot problem; upstream's version runs the full walk once per marker change instead of weekly.
- Drop the fork's `migratePg` import in `packages/db/src/client.ts` because upstream replaced the drizzle migrator; the fork's `applyDatabaseInvariants` wrapper stays.
- Merge both sides' new tests in the agent-permissions and server-startup suites. Keep the fork's GIF-125 pin on both `reconcileResolvedDependencyWakes` call sites.
- Take upstream's test helpers for the execution-workspaces fixtures. Keep the fork's assignee seeding and the finalize-barrier test in the issues-service suite.

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed under Node 24.21.0 with the merged lockfile.
- `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/server exec tsc --noEmit` passed with no errors, after building shared, db, plugin-sdk, adapter-utils, and the runner TypeScript output.
- The merge first left one type error: upstream added a new `readLoadedSkillFile` caller without the fork's `companyId` argument. This PR fixes it.
- Targeted Vitest runs on every conflicted test file passed:
  - `server-startup-feedback-export.test.ts`: 41 passed
  - `agent-permissions-routes.test.ts`: 98 passed
  - `issues-service.test.ts`: 161 passed
  - `cross-issue-influence-limit.test.ts`, `execution-workspaces-service.test.ts`, `sandbox-callback-bridge.test.ts`: passed in the combined run
- The fork's GIF-125 startup test failed after the merge because upstream now starts the scheduler interval after startup housekeeping settles. The test now selects the scheduler interval by its delay, the same way the upstream tests do. The assertion is unchanged.
- In the first combined run, two suites hit setup hook timeouts on this host. Both passed when run alone with a longer hook timeout.
- Full `pnpm test:run` and `pnpm build` were not run locally. CI must verify the broad upstream merge.

## Risks

- This merge imports 94 new migrations and runtime behavior changes. Take a database dump before rolling the image out; `PAPERCLIP_MIGRATION_AUTO_APPLY` applies them unattended.
- The GIF-49 terminal-conflict tolerance now also wraps transaction-scoped issue writes. A 409 from the terminal-status guard is thrown before any SQL runs, so the transaction stays usable.
- The docker entrypoint loses the fork's weekly deep ownership audit. A deep-tree ownership mismatch is now caught only when the marker is missing or the node UID/GID changes.
- No history is discarded. This PR uses a merge commit and no force push.

## Model Used

- Anthropic Claude models in Claude Code resolved the merge conflicts and prepared the sync: Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`) and Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`), with tool use and code execution. Existing upstream and fork authors remain in the preserved commit history.

author: nh13
body:
Cuts CI compute across every job, and the workflow's wall time, without dropping any check. Measured baseline (median of the last 6 `main` runs): the canonical AVX2 row set the wall time at 585 s; the eight build jobs together spent about 50 runner-minutes per run, and every merge ran the full workflow three times (PR, merge queue, push to `main`).

## What changes

**Run less of the same thing**
- A new push to a PR branch cancels that PR's run still in progress. merge_group and push runs are never cancelled, because each gets its own concurrency group.
- Push to `main` runs only coverage (Codecov's baseline) plus a new build-only `warm-caches` job. The merge-queue run already tested the exact commit that lands, so the full push run was a duplicate (about 50 runner-minutes per merge).
- The rescue kernel-equivalence sweeps (`rescue_band_harness`, `rescue_prune_eq`) run at full job counts once per kernel and compiler family (canonical AVX2/clang-19, ARM64 NEON/clang-19, AVX2/g++). The no-mimalloc, single-binary and macOS rows run every configuration and seed at about a fifth of the jobs, with floors so each per-batch draw and vacuity check still bites. The longest harness runs now start first, and the avx2/avx512bw fuzz runs go side by side.
- PR runs are lighter unless they touch a kernel, a kernel harness or the build (`.github/scripts/ci-depth.sh`, which falls back to full whenever it cannot compute the diff). A light PR run reduces the rescue sweeps on every row, skips the AVX-512BW kswv unit tests, and skips the MSan padded-lane gate (not a required check). The merge-queue run, which tests the exact commit that lands, always runs at full depth. Every required check still reports on PRs.
- The no-mimalloc and single-binary rows link without LTO. They exist to cover the allocator and the bare-`make` multi-tier build. The full-LTO link is single-threaded and ccache cannot cache it. Full LTO stays covered on the canonical, canonical-regressions and ARM64 rows, and by the release workflow's tarball check.
- The coverage job builds at `-O1` (a new `COVERAGE_OPT` knob; the default stays `-O0` for local line-by-line reports). A test/ stamp keyed on `COVERAGE`/`COVERAGE_OPT` makes an incremental switch recompile the test objects. Locally the instrumented unit tests drop from 74 s to 15 s, and line coverage moves from 99.52% to 99.49% because a few inlined lines are attributed to their callers.
- Upstream bwa's chr22 parity alignment is cached: it depends only on the bwa build, its index, the reads and the script, never on the bwa-mem3 commit, but was recomputed by seven jobs per run.

**Cache what is rebuilt**
- ccache on every compiling job via compiler-named shims (CXX/CC and everything that inspects them keep their plain values). `-march=native` compiles are keyed on the host's resolved CPU features, so native objects are never shared across runner CPUs. PR and merge-queue runs restore only; `warm-caches` saves main's cache per configuration and prunes superseded entries.
- The clang-19 install refreshes only the llvm apt list, skips unused recommends (naming `libclang-rt-19-dev` for the sanitizer runtimes), and caches the `.deb`s. apt still verifies each one against the fingerprint-checked signed index.

**Make slow tests cheap without weakening them**
- `make_dedup_reads.sh`: one awk pass instead of a fork per record, with byte-identical output (run 8 times per canonical job).
- `thread_determinism.sh`: the slow-pipe legs, which sleep at the consumer's pace, run on a 10k-pair prefix with the same batch boundaries; the many-batch file-sink checks stay on the full fixture.
- `chain_flat_replay_identity.sh`: one 36 kb read instead of four. It still exceeds the Pass-3 index's 32-bucket walk and takes the full scan on every path. This script ran in three jobs at about 45 s each and now takes about 4 s.
- `test/run_unit_tests.sh` builds its ~30 standalone test binaries with one make job per CPU instead of serially (26 s of the macOS row's 45 s step). A failed parallel build is re-run serially for a readable error.
- Unit tests run as concurrent doctest shards (`test/run_unit_shards.sh`), every case exactly once, coverage's run included.

**Shorten the critical path**
- New `canonical-regressions` job: the canonical row's 41 binary-only regression steps move there verbatim and run alongside the matrix, building the same configuration from the same compiler cache. The row keeps everything that needs its built tree.

## Validation
- Each script change was checked locally on arm64 against the old version: byte-identical fixtures, identical PASS sets, vacuity counters, and negative controls that still fail. The reduced harness sweep passes all 30 configurations, and every test case runs exactly once across shards.
- actionlint and every `test/regression/*lint*.sh` pass. A step-accounting check confirms no step was lost or duplicated in the job split.
- What only this PR's CI can show: cache hit rates, the x86 reduced-sweep vacuity checks, and the real per-job times. Note that ccache only pays off after the first push to `main` warms it, so this PR's own runs build cold.

## Needs a settings change before merge
The new job, `Linux x86_64 AVX2 (mimalloc) — regressions`, must be added to `main`'s required status checks, or the 41 regressions it now runs would no longer block merges.

## Depends on #632 for the kt_for_prefix flake
`kt_for_prefix`'s unit cases time their slow item with fixed sleeps, so they can fail when every core is busy, which sharding makes routine. #632 replaces those sleeps with gates. This PR leaves the test unchanged, so #632 should land first or alongside it.

* **Developer Workflow**
  * Pull-request checks use lighter runs for selected changes and full validation for merge-queue runs and changes requiring broader checks.
  * Unit tests run in parallel shards with clearer failure reporting; standalone test builds can also use parallel compilation.

author: albatrossvpn
body:
Before: on Android the local proxy listened on 127.0.0.1:10808 with no login, so any app on the phone could use the VPN through it or learn its exit address. Xray's local ports had no login either. Signing in and connecting called the account service directly, which shows its name to the network, and the Worker mirror of the app's lists (same name) was fetched directly too. Crowd reports could go direct. Log lines named servers, hosts and IP addresses, and tun2socks logged visited sites.

After: wherever only the app uses the local proxy (Android, Windows TUN mode) it gets a random port and a random login for each connection; Windows proxy mode keeps the open port because the system proxy cannot log in. Xray's local ports need a per-set login. Account calls go through the VPN, or a tested server, and directly only as a last resort; a direct call resolves the name over DNS-over-HTTPS and uses ECH when the service publishes a key, with time limits so a blocked ECH handshake still falls back in time. The Worker mirror is used only through the VPN or that private client. Crowd reports only go through the VPN. Log lines carry no links, addresses, host names or server names, app.log is redacted and removed on a normal exit, and tun2socks is silent.

How: `privateProxy` decides when the mixed inbound gets `users`; tun2socks is given `socks5://user:pass@host:port`. `tunnelFirst` orders account calls (a 429 from a shared server tries another way in); connecting trusts the last answer and the meter asks through the VPN at its first step. `ech.go` asks both DNS-over-HTTPS servers at once (one lookup per name, warmed while servers are tried), sets `EncryptedClientHelloConfigList`, retries with the server's retry configs, then without ECH; the request deadline reaches the dial through a context value, and a refused key is skipped for a few minutes. `Fetcher.Private` and `sources.IsWorker` keep the Worker off plain direct calls. `Redact` filters every engine log line and the app.log writer. A new `Commit identities` workflow fails on any commit whose author or committer address is not a noreply address (it prints the commit, never the address), and the backend deploy checks that ECH is on for the account domain.

Tests: `TestPrivateProxy`, `TestProxyLogin`, `TestRedact`, `TestPrivateDirect`, `TestPrivateDial` (real ECH server, a stalled ECH handshake, a deadline), `TestHTTPSCache`, `TestWorkerNotDirect`, `TestXrayPortsNeedLogin`, `TestBusy`, updated `TestAccountGate` and crowd test.

author: olegbrok
body:
## Problem

`scripts/claude_account.py switch --restart` writes the new token to `.env`, calls `/admin/restart`, and reverted `.env` when that call took longer than 30 s. The daemon runs its startup layout pre-flight before it answers, which can take minutes on a large data root. The client then reverted `.env` while the restart still went ahead, so the new process came up on the old token.

## Fix

- The restart request gets a named 600 s timeout (`RESTART_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S`).
- The response body is classified strictly: a 2xx JSON body counts as accepted only when `restarting` is `true` and there is no `error` key. A refusal prints the error (or a short pre-flight summary) and reverts at once, without waiting.
- Transport errors: only a typed `ConnectionRefusedError` raised before any response (directly or as `URLError.reason`) means the request was never delivered, so the client reverts at once. Timeouts, resets, broken pipes, `RemoteDisconnected`, untyped reasons, incomplete reads and invalid JSON are treated as unknown outcomes. Any error while reading the body is also unknown. Nothing is decided by matching error message text.
- Accepted and unknown outcomes both keep the new token in `.env` through a single generation wait of `RESTART_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_S = 900` s, because a new process can take minutes to boot even after it was accepted. The client reverts only after that deadline. The two deadline messages stay distinct. If the restart was accepted, the message says the new process never came up. If the outcome was unknown, it says a restart could still be in flight, and tells you to check the generation and then which token `.env` holds.
- `switch` without `--restart` is unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/test_claude_account.py`: 63 existing cases plus 26 new ones, 89 in total. They cover the classification table (including odd 2xx JSON shapes), the real urllib error wrapping, uncertainty while reading the response, backup/revert ordering on each exit path, the shared long wait, and a slow boot after an accepted restart: the old process stays visible until 30 s, the API is unavailable during boot, and the new generation appears at 360 s. In that case the token is kept and nothing is reverted.

With the production code unchanged from `main`, the first commit's new cases fail (21 failed / 67 passed). The slow-boot case also fails on the first commit alone (1 failed / 88 passed). Single edits each make a named test fail and pass again once restored: relaxing `ok is False`, setting the wait back to 90 s, and loosening the strict `restarting is True` check.

`ruff check .` is clean and `uv.lock` is unchanged. CI runs the full suite.

No UI change, so there are no screenshots.

body:
Governance issue #1986.

## Decision and scope

Correct the two demonstrated CI failures in #1982 with one compliant, verified candidate. The protected workflow moves from the reviewed v3.2.0 SHA to the reviewed v3.3.0 release SHA and its two strict regression fixtures move together. This replaces the Dependabot-authored protected-path proposal; no author policy or assertions are relaxed.

## Files changed

Exactly three paths, four lines replaced:

- `.github/workflows/founder-authority-guard.yml`
- `tests/test_workflow_action_pins.py`
- `tests/test_founder_authority_publisher_workflow.py`

## Upstream review

The upstream v3.3.0 tag and release (published 2026-10-12T23:42:23Z) point to GitHub-verified commit `64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510`. The 13-commit comparison from v3.2.0 changes no action-owned main.js/lib logic. Node24 and the four permission inputs this workflow uses remain compatible. New optional permission inputs have no defaults; the existing permission collection only includes nonempty inputs. Current-repository scope, output use and normal post-job token revocation remain unchanged.

References: https://github.com/actions/create-github-app-token/releases/tag/v3.3.0 and https://github.com/actions/create-github-app-token/compare/v3.2.0...v3.3.0.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Reproduced the original mismatch: 2 failed, 5 passed in the two affected test files.
- [x] Retain exact 40-character pins, reviewed-version equality, trusted-base checkout, expected App identity/installation, and checks:write plus contents/issues/pull-requests:read only.
- [x] GitHub verifies implementation commit `9192347da205647d950dab157abe8e2623c4b428` as valid; author and committer map to Voxterrae.
- [x] Focused pin, publisher and authority-policy tests pass.
- [x] Fresh hosted CI on this head.
- [ ] Protected human review.

## Validation

author: kje7713-dev
body:
## Purpose
Fix the predictable first-pass novel length shortfall without introducing another terminal failure mode. Production Oct 24: 29 first-pass sections projected only 78,077 words, forcing 19 later expansion additions and causing plot-continuity problems.

## Implementation
- The existing allocation stage budgets a **per-beat container mix** using real midpoint contributions: scene (1,300 tokens), developedScene (2,250), setPiece (3,500), sceneSequence (5,000), chapter (5,500).
- The existing single outline-generation call uses **strict, typed named slots** per beat. Each slot permits exactly its planned container, so the model cannot silently change the container mix while keeping the section count unchanged.
- The slot response is flattened back into the existing ordered `Suggestion[]` before validation, persistence and acceptance. Legacy arrays/checkpoints and all non-novel formats retain their existing contracts.
- **Failure-averse behavior:** if a planner mix is oversized, inconsistent, or partially missing, the pipeline deterministically falls back to the existing chapter-equivalent conservative allocation and preserves the optional expansion path. A poorly sized plan is not a new terminal error. The current bounded retry, provider-error and author-obligation paths remain unchanged.
- Adds telemetry comparing planned and realized first-pass container counts per Story Arc beat; no new user-facing warnings or failure gates.
- Preserves 115,000-word preferred goal, 125,000-word projection cap, 2% expansion tolerance, credits, provider selection, existing recovery/checkpoints, iOS output, and expansion best-valid fallback. **No additional LLM calls or stages.**

## Tests
- 40-section mixed plan of ~120,769 projected words fits in one first pass without section-count normalization.
- Strict schema requires a specific container for each named slot; flattening restores the original section array and canonical Story Arc IDs.
- Inconsistent and over-cap planner mixes use safe legacy fallback instead of terminating.
- Non-novel planner stays on its original three-field schema.
- Existing Deno lifecycle/resume, output-validation and other CI tests.

## Merge criteria
**Keep draft; do not deploy** until required CI passes and the provider supports the larger strict schema in a controlled preproduction test. CI verifies deterministic projection and schema validity, **not** that every live model generation produces a good story or that provider outages are impossible. After deployment, compare `plannerContainerCountsByBeat` vs `firstPassActualContainerCountsByBeat`, first-pass projected words, expansion rounds, final accepted sections and credits in the first real run.

A valid outline should always be preserved if optional expansion adds nothing. Avoid creating new fatal validation on length or type allocation.

author: operaciones-max
body:
## Resumen

Las actas ya generadas siguen mostrando el **rayo anterior** (y, en algunos casos, el monto asignado de $1.000.000). El código actual **ya genera** los PDF con el logo nuevo y $3.000.000 (comprobado), pero un PDF guardado no cambia solo. Este PR permite **regenerar el PDF guardado** de un reporte ya firmado. El diff contra `master` son 5 archivos.

## Qué cambia

- **Admin → Reportes:** botón **«↻ Regenerar PDF»** en los reportes **Firmado** y **Enviado FX**. Genera el acta de nuevo en el navegador (mismas facturas y firmas, fecha del reporte, logo y monto asignado actuales), la sube a Storage y **reemplaza el archivo guardado**. No aparece en los reportes «Pendiente Admin».
- **`PATCH /api/legalizaciones/[id]` con `regenerarPdf: true`:** solo **administrador**; solo reportes ya **firmados**; la URL debe ser del Storage. Cambia **únicamente el archivo**: no toca la firma ni el estado (un «Enviado FX» sigue «Enviado FX») y **no envía avisos**.
- La subida del PDF a Storage se comparte entre la firma del administrador y la regeneración (`subirPdfLegalizacion` en `lib/legalizacion-pdf-client.ts`).
- **Form Finance:** el texto de ayuda de «Actualizar PDF» menciona también el logo anterior (para el coordinador, «Actualizar PDF» ya genera una copia con el logo y el monto actuales para descargar).

## Permisos

- El coordinador **no** puede reemplazar archivos guardados (403): no se amplió ningún permiso. Quien necesite el PDF guardado corregido para todos pide al administrador que lo regenere.

## Cómo se verificó

Contra un Supabase simulado en memoria (no el real), con el Storage simulado ahora guardando los archivos subidos:
- **18 chequeos nuevos.** Servidor: el coordinador recibe 403; un reporte sin firmar, 400; una URL fuera del Storage o inválida, 400; nada cambia en esos casos. Interfaz: el botón aparece en Firmado y Enviado FX y no en Pendiente Admin; al regenerar, el reporte guarda una URL nueva, el estado y la firma no cambian; el archivo guardado es un PDF real que dice «Monto Asignado: $3.000.000», «Valor a Reembolsar $165.000» y «Ejecutado 6 %», y su logo es **idéntico** (diferencia de píxeles 0,00) al de `lib/logo-pdf.ts` (el rayo blanco sobre negro enviado).
- Suites anteriores en verde: 65 de flujos, 36 de interfaz (incluye la firma del administrador, refactorizada para compartir la subida), 25 del monto en Form Finance, 36 de Form Finance, 29 de edición y 25 del envío de la legalización.
- `tsc --noEmit`, `next build` y `next lint` (solo el aviso previo de `AgregarFacturaModal`).

## Qué no se probó

- Supabase real ni el Storage real (límites de tamaño, permisos del bucket).
- La causa exacta de que se hayan guardado PDF con el logo anterior después del despliegue: lo más probable es que la firma se hiciera desde una pestaña abierta con una versión anterior de la aplicación (el PDF se genera en el navegador de quien firma).

## Notas para el despliegue

- Sin migraciones ni variables de entorno nuevas.
- Para que los PDF salgan siempre con la versión actual, quien firma debe recargar la aplicación después de cada despliegue.

Closes #8. Closes #9.

## Replay log (FR-P2)
- **Engine:** `set_mode`, `focus_region` and `apply` log each action with its simulated minute. A refused action that changed nothing isn't logged. Automatic mode switches inside a step aren't logged either, because the replay repeats them on its own. The world's `NewWorld` settings are recorded too.
- **Save format:** `MODEL_VERSION` is now 2. The log is written after the state, as JSON inside a bincode string, so it isn't part of `state_hash()`.
- **Replay** (`replay.rs`): `Replay` rebuilds the world from its settings and applies each entry at its recorded minute. A `ReplayScript` (JSON) also carries the end time and the original state hash, so a replay can report whether it ended up identical.
- **WASM:** `Engine::replay_script` and a `ReplayRun` class (`advance`, `progress`, `matches`, `finish`).
- **App:** the World tab has **Export replay log** and **Replay from the start**. **Open** accepts a replay `.json`. A replay runs in slices with a progress card and can be stopped, and the current world stays open until it finishes.

author: jannef
body:
Closes #243

The class tables for the warrior, barbarian, paladin, and monk (design `docs/design/progression.md` §4.2–4.5), with bonus talent picks from each class's trees. All 36 entries are in, including the 7 actives.

## What's in it
- **Data**: each class file (`data/classes/NN-id.toml`) gets `bonus_talents = { levels, trees }` and `[[class.ability]]` rows (`level`, `id`, `name`, `description`, `learn`, `effects`, `systems`, `requires_alignment`). Their effects use the `TalentEffect` kinds, so `TalentMods` sums them with the talents. New kinds are inserted by group. The README documents the fields.
- **Not saved** (design §10.2): `Talents` now has a `#[serde(skip)]` list of class abilities. It is set in `World::assemble`, so on new worlds and on loads, and by `World::class_level` on each level-up. Saves, replays, and the state hash never contain it.
- **Level-ups**: each level's new abilities say their `learn` line ("You can now rage."). Mighty thews' stat gift is handed out once. Hardened's hit points come for each level past `hp_level`. Bonus picks are `Due::bonus`:
  - only a talent from the class's trees spends one ("Your class's pick is from Weaponcraft or Guard."), and such a talent spends a bonus pick before the level's own;
  - `settle_due` drops a bonus pick when nothing in those trees can be taken;
  - `levelup:auto` spends bonus picks too.
- **Actives**: `Ability::Class(ClassActive)` (the menu's Class group) and `Action::Use` (`use:rage`, `use:smite:E`). All of them live in `world/class_ability.rs`; each hot file gets one line.
- **Passives**: each is one read at its hook. `docs/dev/progression.md` has the table.
- **Statuses**: new `spent`, `drained`, `radiant`, in the buffs/cooldowns group. Holy radiance shines as a light source in `LightCache`.
- **Dumps**: new `class` layer (`Rage (used)`). `progress` shows `1 bonus talent`, and the JSON `due` gains `bonus`.
- **Wiki**: generated `class-levels.md` (included in Classes, "What each level gives"). Abilities rows say who has each active. The by-system table gets a class abilities column.
- **Docs**: spec §8 "Class abilities" (08i), plus notes in 06 and 08c; `docs/dev/progression.md` and `screens.md`; CLAUDE.md for `use:` and the `class` layer.
- **xtask golden**: `xp:N` and `levelup:auto` now count as free steps, so a manifest walk can level up.

## Decisions where the design left room
- **Lay on hands** costs mana in the design, and the mana PR (#262) isn't merged. Until then it uses a cooldown: two degrees of **Drained** (10 min). Avatar ("half the mana") makes that one degree.
- **Cooldown lengths**: one **Spent** status with degrees covers both: Smite 1 degree (5 min), Quivering palm 2 degrees (10 min). Veteran's wind uses the existing **Winded** (15 min, not the design's 10). It is shared with the Second wind talent, so using either winds you for both.
- **Unstoppable** "once per rage": holding the last hit point ends the rage, so Exhausted follows. This also matches where R1 is going (spending rage).
- **Mighty rage**: Raging's raises doubled (`raise_percent`) and Exhausted eases twice as fast. No second rage status.
- **Cleaving strike with the Cleave talent**: two sources of cleave act as great cleave.
- **"No body armour"** means nothing worn in a `body_armor` slot (the Body slot). Cloaks, gloves, and helmets don't count.
- **Alignment**: only the paladin's actives require Good (greyed out with "you have strayed"). Passives don't check alignment.
- **Quivering palm** is refused with a weapon in hand. **Smite** puts its dice in the profile's `extra` die; a magic weapon's extra die is folded into the damage bonus at its average.
- **Whirlwind** is one blow at each adjacent hostile, clockwise from north. Each blow gets the end-of-attack free blows. It costs one melee price and one exertion.
- **No per-ability keys**: following Second wind's example, none of the actives gets a `KeyCommand`. The abilities menu and its repeat key use them. This also leaves the Controls goldens unchanged.
- **Coverage**: `min_class` stays 0 until all 15 classes have tables. Class abilities are counted, though.
- **Saves change**: new status ids and the new `Due::bonus` field. `FORMAT_VERSION` is untouched.

## Verified (on Linux; no macOS here)
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`: all green.
  - New `world/class_tests.rs` (12 tests): abilities by level and through save/restore (not in the JSON, hash unchanged), bonus picks, each passive's rule, each active and its cooldown, a strayed paladin refused, replay and save round trip.
  - Existing talent tests run on content with the class tables stripped, so the warrior's bonus picks stay out of their way.
- `cargo xtask wiki`: I read `class-levels.md`, `abilities.md`, and `talents-by-system.md`.
- Replay: `replay --create --scenario showcase --character human,male,barbarian --actions "use:rage wait*2 use:rage xp:250000 levelup:auto wait"`, then `--verify` passes. The dump shows the `class` and `abilities` layers ("Rage (class): you are raging").
- Captures at `--scale 1` with `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan`. I looked at the paladin's abilities menu: Lay on hands greyed as "you are drained", Drained on the status bar, Smite usable.
- `cargo xtask golden`: 100 of 101 entries match. The one failure is the new `abilities-menu-class` entry (in `tests/golden/manifest/character.toml`), which has no reference yet. The golden update run is 40112042494.

Not covered by a capture: Holy radiance's light on the map. Only a unit test covers the status toggle; the light source itself goes through the same path as a glowing item's.

author: nikolaichuk7
body:
## What this changes

On a Compute Engine Confidential VM the chip's SEV-SNP launch measurement is Google's UEFI: Google precomputes it per vCPU count (its launch endorsement), and the operating system is read from the disk after launch. The chip alone therefore does not see the kernel, and a file sealed with the chip's derived key opens under another kernel on the same chip. The boot after the firmware is measured into the instance's vTPM.

`gcp-sev-snp-vtpm` holds both:

- **Attestation.** The chip's report names the vTPM's attestation key in the second half of REPORT_DATA; the key's quote over `sha256:0-9` (the firmware, GRUB, the kernel, its command line and initrd) carries the challenger's nonce. The verifier checks the chip as `gcp-sev-snp` does, the key's certificate to Google's EK/AK root (pinned) and to the instance's project, and the boot to `pcr_digests`, which a peer or destination of this family must name.
- **Sealing.** `tee.sealer: both` nests the chip's key inside the vTPM's sealed object under the boot's PCR policy. It is the family's default. A file opens on this chip and on the pinned boot only.
- **Daemons.** `sagvd`, `acp-compute` and `acp-bootstrap` accept the family as host, peer and registry destination. `identity` prints the boot digest to pin. A delegated (RATS) Verifier is refused for it, since those read only the chip's report.

## What shows it (C53)

`scripts/hardware-test/gcp-sev-snp/boot-chain`, four boots of one n2d SEV-SNP instance. Run `20261024T160531Z` reports `RESULT: PASS` on twelve checks:

- The chip's measurement was the same under kernels 7.0.0-1014-gcp and 7.0.0-1013-gcp, and the chip-sealed text opened under both.
- The shipping verifier, with the second boot pinned, accepted that boot after a plain reboot, during which no PCR moved.
- It refused the other kernel, which moved PCRs 8, 9 and 10.
- The chip-and-vTPM file opened after the reboot and was refused under the other kernel.

Offline tests run on boot B's real evidence. The verifier accepts it and refuses seven altered forms: another boot, another project, another selection, another nonce, a changed signature, another instance's key, and a report without its quote.

## Checks run locally

`make fmt-check vet build build-fips terminology license-headers dep-allowlist dep-depth`, `go test ./...` (88 packages), `make test-integration`, race on the touched packages, FIPS-only tests on the touched packages, `make coverage-thresholds` (tee 88.1%, product 91.7%), golangci-lint (darwin and linux), Semgrep 1.86.0 with the project rules (the 10 baseline warnings only), gitleaks on the branch history, DCO.

## What stays the platform's

The vTPM on Compute Engine SEV-SNP is Google's software, outside the TEE. Google's own documentation says so. The boot is held to it as the firmware is held to Google's UEFI. A boot the chip itself measures needs the operator's own SEV-SNP host and is a separate decision.

author: kappa16
body:
CLOSE #1177 

## Summary

Adds an **optional, badge-earning identity verification flow** for campaign creators to build backer trust. Creators can verify their **email**, **phone** and **government ID**. Completing all three earns a **"Verified Creator"** badge, shown on every campaign by that creator and in search results.

Verification is opt-in. It never blocks creating or running a campaign, and unverified creators get no negative marker.

| Verified steps | Status       | What backers see                       |
| -------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 0 of 3         | `unverified` | Nothing                                |
| 1–2 of 3       | `partial`    | Subdued chip: "2 of 3 identity checks" |
| 3 of 3         | `verified`   | **Verified Creator** badge             |

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **Verification steps documented clearly.** New guide `docs/creator-identity-verification.md` covers:
  - creator walkthrough and code rules
  - what the badge means for backers
  - privacy, full API with examples, error codes and configuration

  It's linked from `README.md` and `docs/campaign-verification.md`, and the endpoints are added to `docs/openapi.yaml`.
- [x] **Verified campaigns display a badge** on the campaign detail page, campaign directory cards, the discovery grid and the creator profile header.
- [x] **Verification status surfaced in search results.**
  - Every result from `GET /api/campaigns/search` includes a `verification` summary.
  - Both search UIs show badges and have a **"Verified creators only"** filter (`?verified=true`).
  - When relevance is equal, verified creators rank first, then partially verified ones. Relevance stays the primary signal.

## How it works

Verification belongs to the creator's **Stellar address**, so earning or losing the badge updates all of that creator's campaigns at once.

1. **Prove address ownership.** The creator signs a one-time challenge message with their wallet (no transaction, no fees). This returns a 1-hour session token, so nobody can verify or withdraw on someone else's behalf. Raw ed25519 and SEP-53 (`signMessage`) signatures are both accepted.
2. **Email:** a 6-digit code by email.
3. **Phone:** a 6-digit code by SMS (E.164 format).
4. **Government ID:**
   - The creator uploads a passport, national ID or driver's licence to a **private** storage prefix.
   - It is approved or rejected by an admin (`ADMIN_API_KEY`).
   - Rejections include a reason, and the creator can resubmit.

Code rules:
- 10-minute expiry
- 5 attempts per code
- 60 s resend cooldown
- stored as salted hashes and compared in constant time

Changing the verified email or phone resets that step, so the badge drops until the new contact is confirmed. Creators can **withdraw** at any time, which erases their data and removes the badge everywhere.

UI: a step-by-step wizard at `/creators/<address>/verification`. It's reachable from a new **Verification** tab on the creator profile and from a "Get the Verified Creator badge" link the creator sees on their own campaign page.

## API

| Method   | Path                                                         | Auth          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
| `GET`    | `/api/creators/{address}/verification`                       | Public (owner view with session) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/creators/{address}/verification`                       | Creator session |
| `POST`   | `/api/creators/{address}/verification/session`               | None (wallet signature) |
| `POST`   | `/api/creators/{address}/verification/email`                 | Creator session |
| `POST`   | `/api/creators/{address}/verification/phone`                 | Creator session |
| `POST`   | `/api/creators/{address}/verification/government-id/upload`  | Creator session |
| `POST`   | `/api/creators/{address}/verification/government-id`         | Creator session |
| `PATCH`  | `/api/creators/{address}/verification/government-id`         | Admin |
| `GET`    | `/api/admin/creator-verifications`                           | Admin |

Changes to existing endpoints are additive only:
- `GET /api/campaigns/search`: new `verified=true|false` param (other values return `400`), and a `verification` field on each result.
- `GET /api/campaigns`: new `verified=true|false` param, plus `creatorVerification`, `verified`, `verificationStatus` and `verificationBadges` on each campaign.
- GraphQL: `campaigns(filter: { verifiedOnly })`, and `phoneVerified`, `governmentIdVerified`, `status` and `isVerified` on `CampaignVerification`.

## Privacy & security

- The public status shows **outcomes only**, with no PII. Email and phone are stored as a masked display form plus a salted hash, visible only to the creator's own session.
- ID documents use a dedicated private prefix, `creator-identity/<address>/`, separate from public evidence. Submissions referencing anything outside the creator's own prefix are rejected, and the document reference is never returned publicly.
- Pending/rejected states and rejection reasons are visible only to the creator and admins.
- Admin endpoints fail closed (`503`) when `ADMIN_API_KEY` is unset.
- `CREATOR_VERIFICATION_DEV_CODES=true` echoes codes in responses for local development only. It is ignored when `NODE_ENV=production`.

## Testing

43 new tests across 7 files, all passing:

| Test file | Tests |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/creator-verification.test.ts` | 8 |
| `services/creator-identity-verification.service.test.ts` | 16 |
| `app/api/creators/[address]/verification/route.test.ts` | 4 (one covers the full flow end to end) |
| `services/campaign-search.verification.test.ts` | 5 |
| `components/creator/CreatorVerificationBadge.test.tsx` | 6 |
| `components/creator/CreatorVerificationWizard.test.tsx` | 3 |
| `components/modules/campaigns/CampaignSearch.test.tsx` | +1 |

The end-to-end route test runs: wallet session → email → phone → ID submission → admin approval → badge appears in search and listings → withdrawal removes it. It also covers the 401, 403, 400 and 409 error paths.

Full suite compared against `main`:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Test files failed / passed | 67 / 226 | 66 / 233 |
| Tests failed / passed | 158 / 2440 | **157 / 2484** |
| Newly failing tests (compared by name) | — | **0** |
| `tsc --noEmit` errors | 75 | 75 (identical set, none new) |
| ESLint errors on new or changed lines | — | 0 |

- **Fixed along the way:** `campaign-search.service.test.ts › combines category, funding goal range, and days remaining filters` was failing on `main` because the in-memory search provider ignored the goal-range and days-remaining filters. It now applies them.
- The remaining 157 failures already fail on `main` and are unrelated (e.g. missing jest-dom matchers, GraphQL `Unknown type "ImpactMetric"`).

### Manual check

1. Set `CREATOR_VERIFICATION_DEV_CODES=true` and `ADMIN_API_KEY=<key>` in `apps/web/.env.local`, then run `pnpm --filter @fundable/web dev`.
2. Open `/creators/<your-address>/verification`, connect the matching wallet and sign.
3. Complete email and phone using the `devCode` returned by the API. The chip should read "2 of 3 identity checks".
4. Submit an ID (requires S3 configuration), then approve it:
   `curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"decision":"approve","reviewer":"me"}' localhost:3000/api/creators/<address>/verification/government-id`
5. Confirm the **Verified Creator** badge on the campaign page, `/campaigns` and search, and that "Verified creators only" filters correctly.

## ⚠️ Notes for reviewers

- **`next build` is blocked by two route-slug conflicts that already exist on `main`.** Next.js rejects different dynamic segment names at the same level:
  - `app/api/creators/[address]` vs `app/api/creators/[id]` (from `[id]/tier`)
  - `app/campaigns/[campaignId]` vs `app/(overview)/campaigns/[id]`

author: beatlayer[bot]
body:
`bl-cli mcp` never polled the shell, so work that only `Shell::poll` finishes (a stem separation's files and tracks) never landed headless. The window polls every frame; the stdio transport didn't.

## What changed

- `bl_agent::stdio::serve` now polls the shell before every message and every 50 ms while it waits for input. A thread reads standard input one line at a time; the transport reads through a small `BufRead` that puts a `notifications/initialized` line (which the server answers with nothing) before each real line and in each idle wait. The transport's own stop hook, which already runs after each message, calls `Shell::poll`. A poll never writes to standard output, and replies stay one per line and in order. The kit's `lspk_agent::stdio::serve_until` is unchanged.
- `serve` now takes `impl BufRead + Send + 'static`; `bl-cli mcp` passes a `BufReader` over `stdin()`.
- Spec: stem-separation R14 says the headless run polls, and that headless packages go to `Packages` in the system's temporary folder on purpose (a headless shell has no application-data folder, which keeps it apart from the app's settings). A run that needs the packages again downloads them again.

## Tests

- `crates/agent/tests/stdio.rs`, `a_file_lands_while_an_agent_keeps_asking`: a processed file is written on its worker thread while the scripted agent sends `ping` until the file lands. It checks the file lands and that there is one reply per request, in order, with nothing else on the output.
- `a_file_lands_while_no_one_asks_anything`: the input stays quiet until the file lands; it checks the file lands and the output is empty.
- Both fail without the `shell.poll()` call (confirmed by removing it: "the file never landed").

## Open points

- The acceptance asks for a stub separation. There is no stub seam: `crates/shell/tests/stems.rs` runs real separation only where `BL_STEMS_RUNTIME` and `BL_STEMS_MODEL` name the packages, which aren't on this machine. So the tests use a processed file (`start_processed`, landed by `poll_processed`), which is the same poll that lands a separation's stems (`write_stems` starts processed files). A test of the real separation through `serve` would need those packages.
- Other processed-file commands (freeze, bounce, reverse, crop, consolidate, slice) already wait for their file inside the command, so they weren't stuck; stems were the one that relied on a poll.
- A standard-input read error now ends the session as end of input, where before `serve` returned the `io::Error`.

## `cargo xtask check --affected` (macOS)

format, clippy, test clock, layers, ui parity reference, command reference, keymap, one test binary per crate, licences/advisories/bans/sources, deny self-test and private terms all pass. Tests: 2506 of 2508 pass. The two failures are not from this change: `bl-cli m2_assistant::the_command_takes_no_key_and_the_binary_records_and_refuses` fails here with "A default keychain could not be found" (the worker account has no keychain, and the test doesn't touch `mcp`), and `bl-shell scales::the_playhead_entering_a_clip_makes_its_scale_the_current_scale` failed once under load and passed on rerun.

## Summary

Contained Codex crews currently discover Flotilla's seven hooks from both the crew home and command-line overrides, so each occurrence is delivered twice. Keep invocation ownership (including its trust records) and remove only Flotilla-owned home handlers during contained preparation. Unrelated home hooks remain intact.

```diff
 contained crew prepare
-  install seven home hooks + home trust records
+  remove previous-generation Flotilla home hooks
 launch
   keep seven invocation hooks + invocation trust records
```

Closes #3823

## Evidence

**Revised operator acceptance is met by the recorded real launches.** The operator confirmed that the fleet already carries the earlier trust fix, so a before-fix `Hooks need review` capture is no longer required. The required comparison is duplicate definitions/firing without this fix versus one definition/firing per occurrence with this fix, all seven trusted. Real Codex discovery and the hook sink demonstrate that comparison below, including exit/relaunch in the same homes. The observed unpatched launches did not show hook review.

Starting a fresh crew on feta after the roll remains the operator step, tracked in [#3827](https://github.com/flotilla-org/flotilla/issues/3827).

Real `codex-cli 0.160.0` ran inside this vessel in cleat (`120x42`). A PATH stand-in recorded the unchanged `flotilla hook` command's argv and native JSON stdin.

### Exact home and command-line conditions tried

All commands used `--no-daemon`, no explicit model, the same `printf hook-probe-3823` brief, `-c notify=[]`, `-c features.hooks=true`, seven `-c hooks.<Event>` definitions, and seven enabled/trusted CLI state records keyed to `/<session-flags>/config.toml:<event>:0:0`. Events: SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, Interrupt. The exact fixed command and staged config are retained with the measurement evidence; only hooks/list is a test fixture.

| Unpatched fresh | `/tmp/codex-3823-before/home`; adapter-installed seven home definitions and matching home trust records | `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` | No hook review; tool turn completed |

| Patched exit/relaunch | Same after home after `/quit`; no restaging or config/trust/auth edits | Identical saved command and launch environment | No hook review; tool turn completed; each event delivered once |

The relaunch used the same command, not `codex resume`. Both composers were ready after their turns.

## Что сделано и почему

**Импорт оборудования из XML — одно окно.** Второе окно мастера заново читало файл через Проводник Windows и обрывалось. Теперь план строится справа в первом окне из уже прочитанных байтов, путь запоминается при первой загрузке. Группа «…-001ABC» = три установки 001A/B/C, каждая своей системой; ревизия B обновляет те же три. Кнопка «Пути установок» — перевыбор папок через Проводник Flux.

**Аудит программ (теги, оборудование, E3Flux, каталог, Проводник, документы)** — исправлено:
- удаление установки оставляло позиции и «занятые» теги; удаление категории справочника — сирот; удаление проекта на SQLite — все проектные записи (теперь одна транзакция, служебный «Общий диск» не удаляется);
- теги не видели изменений справочника без перезахода; окна оборудования не закрывались по Esc;

**Документы Flux.** Таблица растёт дальше Z при прокрутке и масштабе. Привязки параметров переживают правку в Excel (схема на скрытом листе и в customXml, адреса — определённые имена). author: silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

FormCalc `Round()` no longer returns infinity for large values with decimal places.

Cause: `Round` computes `(a * k).round() / k` with `k = 10^places`. When `a * k` exceeds f64::MAX, the product becomes infinity, so `Round(1e300, 12)` returned infinity instead of 1e300.

Fix: `Round` checks whether the scaled product is finite. If it is not, it returns `a` unchanged, since a value that large has no fractional digits to round. Ordinary rounding is unchanged.

## How you verified it

- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`
- [ ] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` (if you touched crate boundaries or any asset)

- Regression test `round_keeps_huge_values_finite` fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-js round_keeps_huge_values_finite`.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Never-crash

- [ ] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests, unless it is provably infallible with a comment saying why
- [ ] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions (`get`, and strings only at char boundaries); checked or saturating arithmetic; allocations sized by input are capped; recursion is bounded
- [ ] No `unsafe`
- [ ] Any crash this fixes has a small synthetic regression test

## Provenance

- [ ] No asset from an Adobe product, and no Adobe icon recreated, traced or imitated
- [ ] No font files committed here (they live in [storytold/craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts))
- [ ] No GPL/AGPL code copied in — MuPDF, Ghostscript, Poppler, veraPDF and DSS may only be run as external oracle processes
- [ ] Behaviour comes from the specification or black-box observation, **not** from reading another implementation's source
- [ ] Every new asset has an `ATTRIBUTION.toml` entry and `cargo xtask assets` passes

## Security

- [ ] `--root` confinement still holds on every path, including ones reached by nested tool dispatch
- [ ] MCP and the UI control channel stay opt-in, loopback-only and token-authenticated
- [ ] No new outbound network access (that decision is the owner's)

## Parity and reach

- [ ] `parity/acrobat-features.toml` updated in this PR, with `notes` saying what is *still* missing — `shipped` means "exists and tested", not "as good as Acrobat"
- [ ] Reachable headlessly through an `automation` tool where that applies (`AGENTS.md` §3), so agents can drive it and not just the UI
- [ ] Docs updated if this changes a documented behaviour (`docs/`, crate README)

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Other FormCalc functions and the clamping of the places argument are deliberately left unchanged.

No existing issue is linked to this PR.

author: ypark
body:
Stacked on #57 (base `go-rescore-and-view`): GO/GMT terms that hold up biologically, found by auditing a real PBMC run.

## What the audit found
On a 27-cluster PBMC run with `--go` (4,867 terms):
- **The term q tested something other than the effect shown beside it.** The test reused the cell types' fgsea setup. Two near-identical ribosomal sets got p 2e-34 and 0.3; a term with a negative effect got a significant positive NES; NK-cell killing had q = 1 in clear NK clusters, while spliceosome, ribosome and OXPHOS terms were significant almost everywhere.
- **One GO curation artifact topped every T and B cluster** (q ~ 1e-30): "negative regulation of myoblast fusion" is 46 ribosomal proteins annotated by a single NAS (untraced author statement) paper.
- **`annotate_genes` showed 0 markers for a coarse label** such as `natural_killer_cell`, because the panel names the type `NK`.

## Changes
- **A new term test** (`src/annotate/term_test.rs`):
  - Each term's effect (legume-enrichment's `ontology_module_score`) is tested against 200 random gene sets with the term's own expression-stratum profile, using the cell types' `GeneStrata`.
  - Random genes don't co-vary as a term's do, so the decoys' spread is widened by how much more the term varies over the clusters than they do, measured by MAD.
  - p is the normal tail and q is BH within each cluster. Outputs are `cluster_term_{z,p,q_values}.parquet`, and the signature has a `z` column.
  - A test holds the decoys' effect equal to the library's.
- **GAF evidence filter:** NAS and ND annotations are left out, through a filtered copy kept in the cache, made once per source file and written atomically. Recorded as `go_dropped_evidence`.
- **Merge previews test terms too:** the test now takes about a second, so a preview shows the merged cluster's terms with their effect and q.
- **Coarse labels in `annotate_genes`:** measured on their member types' markers, listed in `group_of`.
- **Agent guidance:** the MCP instructions and README say how to weigh a term's effect and q.

## Results on PBMC
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Terms per cluster at q < 0.05 | up to 32% (by test design) | median 0.3%, max 4% |
| NK clusters | NK killing q = 1 | NK-cell immunity q 2e-8 to 2e-10 |
| T and B clusters | "myoblast fusion" q 1e-30 | gone; ribosome no longer significant |
| Whole `annotate --go` run | ~7 min | ~5 s |

Monocytes now lead with lysosome, LPS signalling and ficolin-1 granules; platelets with aggregation and alpha granules; B cells and cDC with MHC-II; plasmablasts with immunoglobulin and kinetochore. K14 (labelled NK, called T/MAIT) shows chemokine receptors, which supports the T call.

## Trade-offs (in the README)
- A cell type split over many clusters shares its programmes among them, so they test weaker in each than their effect reads. Example: monocytes' "inflammatory response" across 8 clusters.
- The test reads pooled cluster profiles and has no sample permutation, unlike the cell types' test. A donor-driven programme in a one-donor cluster is not discounted.
- A term whose strata hold little besides its own genes is reported as untestable (NaN).

## Not done here
- The NAS/ND filter and the inline effect would sit better upstream: an evidence denylist in data-beans' `GafOpts`, and a public module-effect function in legume-enrichment. Both live in other crates; the code notes this and tests guard the copies.
- The TUI's Markers view still reads a coarse label's own markers, since that view also drives marker edits.

## Checks
- `cargo test`: 744 passed. `cargo clippy --all-targets`: only the two dead-code warnings already on main. `--features metal` builds.
- On PBMC with a release build: annotate with `--go` (CLI and MCP), then preview, relabel and review a merge of the two NK clusters over MCP, then `lupin view` in a real terminal.

author: germanbluefox
body:
With the new `@svrooij/sonos` backend, radio streams showed up as `track(0)` and `current_station`/`current_title` stayed empty. The reason: radio was only detected from the class in the current track's metadata, and SONOS often reports a stream there as a plain `object.item`. `toTrack` now detects radio the same way the old discovery backend does: an `audioBroadcast` class in the current track or the transport metadata, or a stream URI (`x-sonosapi-stream:`, `x-sonosapi-radio:`, `x-rincon-mp3radio:`, `x-sonosapi-hls:`, `aac:`, `hls-radio:`, `x-sonosprog-http:`) as transport or track URI. Line-in is still checked first. `applyTransportEvent` now remembers the last track and transport data, so the type is worked out again when only the transport changes. For streams, `stationName` is taken from the transport metadata title and the title from the stream content; if the event does not carry the stream content, it is read from the position info instead. Unit tests cover radio detection via the transport URI, line-in and normal tracks, and the transport-only update (#363).

Fixes #363

author: ywachh77
body:
## Problem

The scheduled cycle evaluated **the minute it woke into**.

GitHub's cron does not land on minute boundaries. Across a day of live runs the
wake-up fell anywhere from `:03` to `:58` past the minute. The charter discards
anything sealed more than ten seconds after a minute opens, because backdating
an entry that already happened is a lie.

So scheduled cycles were discarded for being **late** far more often than for
being wrong.

Measured on the live `heartbeats` table:

| seal_state | count |
|---|---|
| ABSTAIN | 19 |
| **DISCARDED_LATE** | **2** |
| SIGNAL | **0** |

Zero signals in eleven hours. But two of those cycles *did* find a real setup —
sealed 14.2s and 46.6s after the minute opened — and both were thrown away for
a timing artefact rather than because the market was untradeable.

## Solution

`_sealable_stamp()` rolls the cycle forward to the next minute when the current
one can no longer be sealed honestly.

Predicting a minute that has not opened is **not backdated** — its entry price
does not exist yet. It is exactly what `/signals` has always done; the scheduled
path was the only one that did not.

A wake-up inside the seal window is left untouched, so nothing changes for a
runner that is actually on time.

## Tests

4 new in `tests/test_runner.py` (54 in file); full suite **555 tests, OK**.

Verified non-vacuous by reverting the one-line call and re-running: the
end-to-end test — which asserts the cycle targeted `10:44` rather than the
missed `10:43` — fails.

`scripts/smoke.py` is unchanged (33 signals, 75.8% [59.0%–87.2%], +11.1 pips,
EDGE_INCONCLUSIVE). The simulation steps on exact minute boundaries, where the
latency is zero and the roll never triggers, so the replay was never affected by
this bug — only the real cron-driven path was.

## What this does and does not promise

It removes the reason a valid setup could never become a signal. It does not
promise signals: the gates still have to agree, and nineteen of twenty-one
cycles abstained on the merits. The market has been in a RANGE regime all day
and the cost gate correctly refused one cycle outright — *"no horizon up to
120m can pay a 1.20 pip spread at 0.36 pips of M1 ATR — the market is too
quiet to trade, not too hard to predict."*

author: maaronfanberg-lab
body:
# Phase 0 and reliability foundation: executable, offline, unmerged

This is the **first implementation slice** of the six-round conversation-science plan, not another prompt rewrite. It does not change Sarah, Mara, Jules, Owen or Allen in the live Room. The PR targets the separate research branch, **not main**.

### Code written
- Typed `chosen_silence` vs model/validation/infrastructure failure, heartbeat coalescing, watchdog status, explicit two-step durable state confirmation.
- Event/decision/source ID invariants; Git main commit evidence requirement, conflicting generations/source IDs rejected, event-hash verification on mirror confirmation and Git-input ACK.
- In-memory FakeGit/FakeWorker (oldest-20/50-max queue, crashes before/after publish and ACK, competing publication, stale mirror, version resync, 500-event catch-up). This is not yet a real Worker implementation.
- Read-only public-feed corpus sampling, preserving negative controls and explicit witness provenance, with tests against the actual published feed.
- Credential/Git-worktree isolation guard for future sandbox experiments.
- Two CI workflows for existing Room regressions and isolated new fault probes.

### Results and adversarial help
- Initial replay corpus test **failed**, exposing oversampling of question-shaped turns. Fixed it and reran.
- A real-code Claude review identified false watchdog health, excess commits on model failure, bad silence inference, forked delivery and false ACK/byte confirmation. Reworked the code and expanded tests.
- A second real-code Claude review identified simulator double-writer, source-ID reuse, fake Git authority and mirror corruption problems. Reworked source identity, CAS, independent FakeRemote and byte-audit behavior; added regression tests.
- Latest **Room presence and group CI: PASS** https://github.com/maaronfanberg-lab/me-/actions/runs/40113732332
- Latest **offline protocol and fault-injection CI: PASS** https://github.com/maaronfanberg-lab/me-/actions/runs/40113732349
- Separate Emily/Olivia checkpoint workflow also appears failed on this branch and on earlier main runs; it is unrelated to this PR's Room test suites and is not counted as a Room pass.

### Honest limitations
The fake simulator's security booleans are not Cloudflare OIDC verification; its in-memory crashes are not actual process/file restarts. Worker event-history and resync endpoints still need real design, review and implementation. A malformed accepted queue entry requires an explicit durable dead-letter design. Most importantly, NO real human-conversation outcome has been tested or improved by this reliability slice. The actual agents' speech generation is not wired to these modules.

### Documentation
[Engineering log and accepted/rejected reviewer findings](docs/research/room-offline-foundation-implementation-log-20261024.md).
[Reviewed full plan](docs/research/room-human-conversation-implementation-plan-20261024.md) in the parent branch.

**Remain draft, unmerged, default-off.** Next gates: process-restart durability, real Worker mirror history and ACK semantics, model action-fidelity ablation, double-annotated conversation corpus, and only then opportunity-based natural turn-taking/grounding. No anti-repetition rule, canned response, or fixed topic rotation was added.

author: mits87
body:
CI rebuilds sqlc and discards JavaScript build caches between runs, while every main push starts all jobs. Cache the pinned sqlc executable, Turbo tasks and Next compiler data; run affected jobs on pushes and PRs.

- Compare the entire push range, including both sides of renames; run everything if the base is unavailable. Keep main runs independent so a later filtered push cannot cancel required coverage.
- Run full CI and cross-client checks nightly and manually. Full CI bypasses Turbo task results, and `make release` requires a successful full run for the exact commit.
- Include build-time URLs, Node configuration and OpenAPI inputs in Turbo hashes. Add push path filters to cross-client and n8n, retaining full scheduled/manual runs.

Validation: five change-selector tests, actionlint, unchanged generated SQL, Turbo cache-hit and environment-invalidation checks. `pnpm check` passed all 40 tasks without cached results (4m46s). All hosted CI, cross-client and CodeQL checks passed. A targeted dashboard rerun restored the cache: 6/6 Turbo tasks hit, and the whole job dropped from 2m38s to 43s on the same commit. The sqlc binary cache was saved successfully; its warm restore was not separately rerun. The full-run Turbo bypass was verified locally.
