body: ## What The character counter at `/counter/` now shows a live snippet preview while you type. Title, description, and custom-limit modes all update the card. - **Google** is measured in pixels with a single canvas (`measureText`), Arial 20px bold for titles and Arial 14px for descriptions. Desktop budgets are 600px / 920px; phone budgets are 560px / 680px. The cut keeps the last whole word and adds `…`. - **Yandex** stays on characters: title 60, description warns after 160 and can run to about 200. There is no public pixel limit, so none is invented. - A pixel or character bar turns amber near the limit and red when the line will be cut. The part that stays is in the snippet; the tail is shown underneath («обрежется в выдаче» / «может обрезаться»). - Custom limit ≤ 80 is previewed as a title, otherwise as a description. If that limit is tighter than the engine, the preview cuts there too. - Empty state shows a short example plus «Подставить пример». «Скопировать» and «Очистить» appear once there is text. - Page meta stays the marketer copy. Visible lead is the shorter «ты» line. Canonical is `https://www.spidytools.ru/counter/`. Limits live in `app/counter/serp-limits.ts` so they can be tuned later. No Three.js, no ads, no hero or UTM changes. ## Where - `app/counter/counter-tool.tsx` — modes, example/copy, preview under the field - `app/counter/serp-preview.tsx` — Google / Yandex card - `app/counter/serp-limits.ts`, `app/counter/serp-truncate.ts` — budgets and word-boundary cuts - `app/counter/page.tsx` — H1, lead, title, description, canonical ## How to test 1. Open `/counter/` on desktop. 2. Empty state: example snippet, hint, button «Подставить пример». No «Нет данных». 3. Press «Подставить пример» on **Заголовок**. Google should cut the title (about 776 / 600 px) and show the tail in red. Switch to **Яндекс**: cut after ~60 characters, amber «Может обрезаться». 4. **Описание** + «Подставить пример». Google cuts by width (about 1305 / 920 px). Yandex keeps the line, paints the part after 160 amber, and says it can still show up to ~200. 5. **Телефон** (or a narrow window): Google title budget becomes 560 px and the card stacks under the field. 6. **Свой лимит** 40 looks like a title; 120 looks like a description. 7. Optional: 40 `M`s fit the 60-character counter but exceed 600 px. 70 `i`s exceed 60 characters but still fit the Google width. 8. `prefers-reduced-motion`: the preview itself does not animate. ## Checks - `npx tsx --test app/counter/serp-truncate.test.ts` — 11 passing - `npx eslint` on the counter files - `npx next build` — static export succeeded - Desktop and 390px layouts checked in Chrome. Canvas width matched a DOM span of the same Arial string (about 598 px vs 598 px for the visible title). Not merged and not deployed. ## Preview [Empty counter with an example snippet](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-eb4209b8-92bc-5423-b4c1-9998c64bb98f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fserp_empty_desktop.png) [Google title cut at 600px with the tail called out](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-eb4209b8-92bc-5423-b4c1-9998c64bb98f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fserp_title_google_cut.png) [Yandex description with the amber tail after 160 characters](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-eb4209b8-92bc-5423-b4c1-9998c64bb98f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fserp_description_yandex_soft.png) [Phone width using the 560px Google title budget](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-eb4209b8-92bc-5423-b4c1-9998c64bb98f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fserp_title_mobile.png) [serp_preview_title_description_yandex.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-eb4209b8-92bc-5423-b4c1-9998c64bb98f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fserp_preview_title_description_yandex.mp4) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: nickdchristian
body:
**Stacked on #116** (it reuses its removal helper); merge that first.

**Breaking:** turning GuardDuty or Security Hub off in the config now turns it off on the next deploy. Until now `enabled: false` left both running and billing.

**GuardDuty is suspended, not disabled:**
- auto-enable for new members is turned off, then every member account is suspended (`StopMonitoringMembers`);
- [suspended accounts keep their findings and aren't charged](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/suspending-guardduty-member-account-from-admin.html); the delegation stays, so `enabled: true` resumes them: suspended members are restarted with `StartMonitoringMembers` instead of being added again;
- GuardDuty stays on in the audit account: AWS says [all member accounts must be disassociated or deleted before you can suspend](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_suspend-disable.html), and disassociating would undo what turning it back on resumes. The result says so. Its own usage is the only remaining cost.

**Security Hub is disabled**, because it can't be suspended. It runs the same steps as `destroy --disable-security-services`. Before it does, the deploy and the dry run warn that [AWS deletes archived findings after 30 days and active findings after 90](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-disable.html) unless it's turned back on first.

Both only act where the audit account is still the service's delegated administrator, so organizations that never turned them on, or already turned them off, aren't touched. The dry run shows GuardDuty as `SUSPEND` and Security Hub as `DELETE`.

Sets `search_binder = "jev"` in `infra/dfo-prod/apis/env.auto.tfvars`, so prod search binds each query with TypeSafe's Jev model and falls back to Gemini, as dev already does. Prod and dev then run the same binder, and an end-to-end check on dev predicts prod. Today they split: "Private sector investment mobilised by the European Union in Africa" refuses on dev and, on prod's Gemini binder, sometimes answers with private sector instrument disbursements.

The stack mounts `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` from `dfo-prod-typesafe-api-key` whenever the binder is not `gemini`. That secret exists in prod-fin-observatory with version 1 enabled, and the apis runtime account reads it under its project-level `secretAccessor`, the same grant dev uses. `search_jev_traffic_pct` keeps its default of 100.

# data: 审核 GRB200224B（T0 系 bot 误植 DDOTI 观测窗口末刻，改 GBM 触发时刻；补 MASTER/DDOTI 6 条上限）

## 源

- 源 ID：GRB200224B
- 审核人：`wa1kmoon@zcode`
- 类型：原为纯信息源（无 lc）→ 本 PR 新建 `lc/GRB200224B.csv`（6 行上限）
- 多目标文献线索：无

## 数据来源

- GCN 27174（Fermi GBM Final Real-time Localization）：https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/27174 —— 触发时刻 05:05:49 UT、GBM 触发号 604213554 / 200224212、RA=177.9 Dec=-28.9（统计误差 3.1 度）、likely LONG；已实际打开核对，与仓内档案一致
- GCN 27175（MASTER-OAFA 上限表）：https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/27175 —— 5 条带 Tmid-T0 的 C（clear）波段上限
- GCN 27181（更名通告）：https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/27181 —— 604213554/200224212 于 05:05:49 触发者定名 GRB 200224B
- GCN 27215（DDOTI/OAN 上限）：https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/27215 —— 窗口 06:47–12:16 UT、10σ 限深 w=19.45
- FERMIGBRST 目录快照 `external/fermi_gbm/heasarc_fermigbrst.tdat.gz`（bn200224212 行：name=GRB200224212、ra=177.9、dec=-28.87、error_radius=3.08 度、trigger_time MJD 58903.212375913、T90=299.525 s；获取日期 2026-07-21，表版本 2026-07-19）
- 同日划界依据：GCN 27173/27176/27177/27182/27189/27191/27222/27240（均指向 Swift 200224A 位置 16h35m +41°37′）、GCN 27183（IPN，200224C）、`external/swift_bat`（200224A 触发 958141，03:24:49.304Z）

## 与原库的差异及推理

- `T0`: `2020-02-24T12:16:00Z` → `2020-02-24T05:05:49.279Z`。原值为 bot 误植：12:16:00 恰为 DDOTI/OAN 观测窗口的结束时刻（GCN 27215 原文「from 2020-02-24 06:47 to 2020-02-24 12:16 UTC」），非触发时刻（`t0_note` 的 meta trigger-time 说法不成立，属提示词 §3.2 / Issue #84 已实锤的观测窗口误植模式）。真实触发时刻按 GCN 27174（05:05:49 UT，触发 604213554.278888）+ FERMIGBRST 目录（MJD 58903.212375913 = 05:05:49.279Z，快照 UTC 列与原始 MJD 逐毫秒复核一致）改写，亚秒取触发仪器目录值。原值已留 `comment`/`t0_note` 备查。
- `T0_ref`: null → GCN 27174 + FERMIGBRST bn200224212 行（见上）。
- `dec`: -28.9 → -28.87。177.9/-28.9 为 GCN 27174 初报形（非 float32 污染）；目录值更精（ra 目录值同为 177.9，不变），按 §4「目录晚于 Circular 者为准」精化。
- `pos_error`: null → 3.08，`pos_error_unit`: arcsec → deg；`pos_error_confidence`: → `1sigma`。取 FERMIGBRST `error_radius=3.08` 度（GCN 初报 3.1 度为其舍入）；置信水平依据 tdat 列定义、GCN 27174「statistical uncertainty」与库内 fermi_gbm README「统计 1σ」（GRB090227B 同例）。
- `Trigger_Instrument`: `Fermi` → `Fermi/GBM`（细化；SCHEMA 示例风格）。
- `tag`: [] → `['grb']`；`sub_tag`: [] → `['lgrb']`。依据 GCN 27174「likely LONG GRB」+ FERMIGBRST T90=299.525±2.862 s（50-300 keV）。
- `alias`: [] → `['GRB 200224B', 'GRB200224212', 'bn200224212']`。GRB200224212 = FERMIGBRST `name` 字段原名（GCN 27174/27181 原文亦用 200224212）；bn200224212 = `trigger_name` 与 GBM 数据目录名；parse.py 自拼三位小数形 `GRB 200224.212` 不收（GRB190507B/190606A/191202A 前例裁定）。
- `articles`: [] → 4 篇实际使用的 GCN（title 逐字取自仓内档案 subject 字段，含 GCN 27175 subject 原有的双空格）。
- `extra_data.t0_note`/`t0_basis` 改写（bot 失真时间基准说明，允许改）：`meta_trigger` → `fermigbrst_trigger_time`，原值留 comment。
- 新建 `lc/GRB200224B.csv`：6 行（5 行 MASTER-OAFA + 1 行 DDOTI，全部 upperlimit=y）。MASTER 5 条取自 GCN 27175 原文表（Tmid-T0=640/800/801/992/1204 s，Expt=120/440/140/180/180 s），`time` 取原文 Tmid-T0、`time_err`=半曝光；Filter C 为 clear（unfiltred）→ `band=G`（2026-10-12 裁定）；DDOTI 取自 GCN 27215（窗口 06:47–12:16 UT，`time`=窗口中点 09:31:30 UT=+15940.721 s、`time_err`=半宽 9870 s，约定口径；10σ 限深 w=19.45；DDOTI w 为白光无滤光片 → `band=G`，不新增 filters.json 键）。两篇通告均未声明星等系统，`mag_system` 留空 + comment 注明（§3.3 默认动作）。
- `mjd` 全部由 T0+time 换算、保留 7 位小数，csv 模块回读 + 独立复算校验通过（差 <0.5 s）；行尾 CRLF。

## T0 与去重

- 标准 `T0` 及依据：`2020-02-24T05:05:49.279Z`（GBM 触发 604213554；GCN 27174 整秒一致，FERMIGBRST 目录亚秒值）。无 `T0_offset`（触发时刻即真实爆发时刻，无显著偏移）。
- `T0_offset`：无。
- 去重情况：lc 全部为本 PR 新增行，无重复；无 X 射线行（band 为能量串）存在，未涉及 X 射线处置。MASTER 5 行为同一通告表内的 5 次独立曝光/合成（时刻、坐标各异），非同一次测量的转引，全部保留。

## 零测光 / 行数偏少时必填（§3.3，2026-10-24 新增）

- 仓内快照：`gcn/archive` 45889 篇（python 全档扫描 + grep 分批双路，结果一致；其中本源相关 4 篇：27174/27181/27175/27215，2 篇含光学数值；另有 1 篇 GCN 27172 与 27208 分别属 200224A/200224C）；`external/rssgrbag` 0 命中；`external/grbsn_webtool` 0 命中；`external/uvot_grb`、`swift_bat`、`swiftgrbba`、`konus_wind`、`agile_mcal`、`fermi_lat` 均 0 命中（本源 GBM-only）
- 外部检索：GCN 站核对 2 篇（27174 实开、内容与档案一致；27215 同平台）；**ADS 或 SciX** 命中 0 篇（无 API token 未查，历史实测 401/WAF）；arXiv API 兜底 `all:200224B` / `GRB200224B` / `200224212` / `"GRB 200224B"` 均 0 命中；TNS 不适用（无 AT/SN 编号）
- 结论：有可用测光——GCN 27175 与 27215 的 6 条上限均有明确时间锚点（Tmid-T0 或观测窗口），按 §3.3「有时间锚点的上限必须入库」全部入 lc
- 本 PR 新增行数：6

## 校验

- `python3 tools/validate.py` 末行：`校验完成：2585 个 info / 2376 个 lc；0 个错误，2 个警告`（两条警告均为 main 存量基线：零测光留证普查 44 项、alias 伪形普查 220 项，详见待决事项 ②）
- 独立子代理核查结论（§6）：**PASS**（独立核查子代理与本审核无利益关联，一轮通过）。核查内容：T0 三路互证（GCN 27174 原文/fermigbrst tdat MJD 58903.212375913 python 复算/normalized 逐毫秒）+ 核查新增两条独立旁证（GCN 27175 "579 sec after trigger"、GCN 27215 "1.68 to 7.16 hours" 反算自洽）；原值 12:16:00 全档案唯一归属 GCN 27215 DDOTI 窗口结束——误植第 8 例实锤；dec −28.87 与 pos_error 3.08deg 取目录精化值合规（§4 第 6 类：目录晚于 Circular；GCN 27175 正文即引 R=3.08）；confidence=1sigma 依据充分（fermi_gbm README 两处明文"全部为 1σ 统计误差、不存在 90%"+GRB090227B 同例）；lc 6 行逐格核对（MASTER 5 行原表内在自洽 Date Time+Expt/2≈Tmid；DDOTI 窗口中点 15940.721/半宽 9870 复算精确；mjd 6 行复算最大差 0.004 s）；DDOTI 宽场上限入库裁定合规（§3.3 只禁无时间锚上限，§3.8 窗口行口径已照做）；alias 三项背书 grep 实证、parse.py 自拼形未收；同日划界逐篇核对；validate/alias 计数 219→220 实测一致——**PASS**。

## 待决事项

无（A 档无）。备注两条（B 档，已按默认动作处理）：
① `mag_system` 留空：GCN 27175/27215 均未声明星等系统（MASTER 用 USNO-B 系定标、DDOTI 用 APASS 定标，但通告原文未标注系统），按 §3.3 留空 + comment。
② alias `GRB200224212`（FERMIGBRST tdat name 字段官方名、GCN 27174/27181 背书）会使命令级 `alias 伪形普查` 计数 +1（正则 `^GRB ?\d{9}$` 无法区分官方 9 位名与导入拼接伪形）；已审源 GRB090227A/090227B/090228A 均保留同形态官方名，本 PR 从先例保留。若维护者希望官方名豁免该普查，需调整 `tools/validate.py` 的正则或加白名单，属工具侧裁决。

author: voces
body:
This PR changes docs only. The render-parse ratchet stays at ty-string-parse **119** (ty-render 58), and no baseline moves.

## What was probed
Slice C1 (`l1-mono-bind-by-type`) has five open entries:
- `annFnDecompose` / `annArrowAt`
- `monoTyParamOf` / `nameIsArray`
- `monoSubstAnn` / `unionMemberCount`
- `monoSubstAnn` / `splitUnionAtoms`, twice

For each entry, the spelling's answer was logged next to the arena answer for the type the caller hands down. At depth 0 that is the annotation node's type. Deeper, the type is aligned through:
- map values
- record fields
- fn parameters and returns
- parens
- `[]` runs

Population: the self-compile and 16,646 tests/corpus files on 02dd23e36, plus the 3,242 inventory witnesses.

| entry | agree | disagree (files) | no type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `annFnDecompose` / `annArrowAt` | 2,879 | 65 (26) | 181,685 |
| `monoTyParamOf` / `nameIsArray` | 19,290 | 77 (17) | 8,248 |
| `monoSubstAnn` / `unionMemberCount` | 5,130 | 104 (68) | 2,753 |
| `monoSubstAnn` / `splitUnionAtoms` (the annotation) | 1,502 | 66 (46) | 237 |
| `monoSubstAnn` / `splitUnionAtoms` (the re-split) | 0 | 0 | 3,279 |

## Why none swaps
The probe recorded up to three disagreements per file, and every one fell into a named class. None was a missing pin.
- **Grouping parens.** For `((T)=>void)` and `(T|null)`, the spelling leaves the work to the paren arm, which keeps the group. A typed test sees through the parens and would rebuild the spelling without them, and then a following `[]` binds into the last arm (D1896).
- **Literal-union aliases.** In `T|K`, where `K` is a literal-union alias, the spelling keeps `K` as one atom, and box tags count it positionally. The arena flattens it into its literals.
- **Retyped `T[]` nodes.** A `T[]` annotation whose node the clone already retyped to the instance (`string[]`) keeps the type parameter only in its spelling.
- **The re-split.** It reads the walker's own substituted output, which has no arena type.

All five wait on step 1, the substitution on types (D3).

## Recorded in
- the five ledger rows' `status` fields
- the C1 table cell and section in `render-parse-residue-2026-10.md`
- the L6 log in `architecture-refactor-plan.md`

## Checks
The instrumentation was a scratch branch and has been reverted. The diff is docs only.
- Preflight: `PREFLIGHT PASS b6bfc6e69` (rep-fuzz, filed witnesses --strict, every ratchet, seed size, lint-self, inventory refs, capability probes).
- There is no identity run, because there is no compiler change.

Before: Bridge Curve and Bridge Edge had one tension shared by both ends, and it only stretched the G1 poles.

After: both bridge panels have G1, G2 and G3 TENSION rows with a start and an end field each, as in Plasticity. The G1 tension changes how far the bridge holds each end's direction, G2 tension reshapes the curvature poles without changing the curvature it meets, and G3 tension only moves the third pole. D still sets the G1 tension at both ends; the HUD shows `TENSION a / b`.

How: `bridgeSide` now reparameterises the end's arc-length derivatives by s(u) = L₁u + αu²/2 + βu³/6 (L₁ = t1·L, α = (t2−1)L₁, β = (t3−1)L₁), so each tension changes the poles but never the continuity. `endTensions` reads a number or `[start, end]` for each. New test checks that each tension moves only its poles and keeps curvature and dκ/ds. Desktop shot: shots/bridge-tensions.png.

author: rainsupreme
body:
Builds on #129 and shows its two commits until that merges; the change here is the last two commits. Together they are the first two slices of #115.

The ci_health store and statistics had no way to be filled. sync.py lists a workflow's runs from GitHub Actions, stores the ones the store has not seen, and for each failed run fetches its jobs and, for each failed job, downloads the log once, parses it and stores the failures. A workflow the store already knows is listed from a few days before its newest stored run, and a run first seen while still running is refreshed once it has a conclusion. A log GitHub no longer has (about 90 days) is recorded as expired and never asked for again; the job's conclusion still counts in the history. The weekly release-branch run is split into one synthetic run per branch and its logs fetched within a budget of API calls per pass, newest first, so the backlog is worked through over several days and steady state costs only the newest week.

This is the prototype's service layer with its httpx client replaced by a small RunsClient protocol (list runs, list jobs, one job log, compare two commits). The real implementation is PyGithub plus the shared ArtifactClient, so the token stays off GitHub's redirect to storage and an expired log is an empty answer rather than an error. The protocol also satisfies blame's CommitComparer, so one client serves both, and the sync is tested against an in-memory fake.

main.py is the command line: sync, scorecard and blame, each writing JSON. Nothing writes to a repository, an issue or a comment. A refused token exits non-zero so a dead token never passes as a quiet day. The store gains close(), which folds the write-ahead log into the database file, since the workflow uploads that file alone.

ci-health.yml runs at 06:00 UTC and carries the store from run to run as an artifact of its own, the way backport-eligibility carries its result files: each run restores the newest history an earlier successful run uploaded, syncs, computes, and uploads the history and a report. This needs no branch to push to and no repository setting. The App token reads actions, contents and metadata on valkey-io/valkey, and the Daily listing is limited to unstable, since Daily also runs on pull requests that no report covers.

Not in this PR: the dashboard and Slack report that present the JSON, and the ingestion of [JOB-FAILURE] causes through the detector's job_failures reader, which lands with the dashboard where issue links are first consumed.

Tested against the live API: a sync of five days of Daily on unstable, then scorecard and blame over it, and a second sync that listed only from three days before the newest stored run.

Tests: 45 new; suite passes on 3.9 and 3.12; ruff and mypy clean.

author: hakarrr
body:
Comparing Dotty with a mapping containing both numeric and string keys raises `TypeError` because `__eq__` sorts the keys:

```python
dotty({'name': 'sample', 1: 'one'}) == {'name': 'sample', 1: 'one'}
# TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'
```

Compare mappings directly instead. The order of dictionary entries does not affect equality, and keys do not need to be orderable. Convert `other.items()` to a dict to preserve the existing mapping-like operand interface and compare equal content even when `other` is an OrderedDict.

Add tests for equal mixed-key mappings in different insertion orders, Dotty and OrderedDict operands, both comparison directions, differing keys/values/lengths, and nested mixed-key dictionaries. Eight new subcases fail before the fix; the nested comparison and existing non-mapping controls pass.

Validation: untouched baseline79pytest tests pass on3.11. Fixed82fullpytest tests pass onCPython3.9,3.10,3.11,3.12;95%branch-aware coverage. Project-pinned pytest7.1.2 and lint plugins pass;sdist/wheel build,twine,docs and git diff checks pass. Docs used Sphinx4.3.2 and lockfile sphinxcontrib versions and compatible Jinja2 3.0.3. author: jitsusama
body:
### 💡 TL;DR

The launcher's learned order now takes a typed start only by a lead of two picks, and a name typed whole beats what was learned. Mistakes already learned heal on their own, and every match still shows.

### 🧩 Problem

Joel wants the launcher to remember which match he means for what he types, changing order without hiding anything. Instead one stray pick could take a word for good. On his laptop "slack" typed whole landed on Slack's theme, "light" on virt-manager down to the single letter "l", "time" and "volume" on keyboard keys, and "a" on the NixOS manual. Latches were seeded from every past pick and held after two picks in a row, so these never went away.

### 🔧 Solution

A latch is now worked out from the picks whenever the launcher asks for one, rather than stored once and kept.

- **Lead of two:** a row takes a start once it has been picked for it two more times than any other row. Picks for longer words count toward their starts.
- **Whole names win:** when what's typed is a row's whole name, no other row holds it unless picked for exactly that text twice.
- **Gone rows count for nothing:** a closed window or an expired notice can't hold a latch. Their picks are dropped once older than the half-life, and a kind with no rows yet keeps its picks.
- **Rows that can't be undone** (Reboot, Power off) still latch only once their first word is whole.

The picks file's format is unchanged, and the old latches file is read.

### 🔬 Validation

- Checked: `tests/ranking.qml` (the-launcher-lands-where-it-did), 63 checks; the new file fails against the old Rank.js.
- Checked: Joel's real picks run through the new rules: "slack", "light", "time", "volume", "tme" and "a" no longer latch, while "sl", "sus", "caff", "lo" and "donot" still do.
- Checked: `run-subtests vm-desktop-launcher-goes-places "learns" "a word typed whole" "enough"` and `changed-checks --build --no-vm` passed.
- Watch: some short starts move by his counts: "s" to Slack, "c" to Chrome, "l" to Lock.

author: siracozmen01
body:
## Problem

Closes #40. On 32-bit x86 (i686):

- `m3World.misuseCount` and `busyCount` are `volatile long long`, which a struct aligns to 4 on i686. Clang therefore cannot make their atomics in `src/misuse.c` lock-free. It warns with `-Watomic-alignment`, which is an error under `MAUL3D_WERROR`, and calls `libatomic`, which the build does not link. GCC builds them, but a misaligned 64-bit atomic is not guaranteed atomic.
- `CMakeLists.txt` chooses `-mavx2 -mfma` from `CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR`. An `-m32` build on an x86-64 host keeps the host's processor name, so it was built for AVX2.

## Change

- `alignas(8)` on both counters in `src/world_internal.h`. On x86-64 and the other 64-bit targets they were already 8-aligned, so nothing moves there.
- The AVX2 backend is chosen only when `CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P` is 8.

## Verification

- i686 in the CI image (`ci-cpp:2026.10.6`), built as maul-tween's `linux-i686-gcc-14` preset builds: `CMAKE_C_FLAGS=-m32 -msse2 -mfpmath=sse`, Release, `MAUL3D_WERROR=ON`.
  - gcc-14 and clang-20 both build with no warnings. Before this change clang-20 failed on `-Watomic-alignment`, and with that error downgraded the link failed on `__atomic_load` and `__atomic_compare_exchange`.
  - Neither build's flags hold `-mavx2`.
  - 55 of 56 tests pass with both compilers, `test_fpenv` and `golden_hostile` among them. `golden` fails only on `JOURNAL_TAPE`, the same hash under both compilers. The journal's records have other sizes on i686. That format defect is tracked separately and is not touched here. The i686 CI cell comes with its fix, so it lands green.
- Local x86-64, on a4649b3 (on main 3d4d349): clang-20 ASan 55/55, gcc-14 Release 56/56, the gcc-14 bench build 56/56, and the shared build 50/50 with the exports test. golden and the bench pins pass.
- The checks job's steps pass locally:
  - clang-format
  - the family checks
  - the bindings check
  - clang-tidy 20 on `src/misuse.c`
  - `family_sync --check` against v0.0.16, which main carries until #39 lands

author: mikepsinn
body:
### Description of Change

Every nightly "Build Downloadable Artifacts" run from 13 to 24 October failed in **Publish the GitHub release**, with `HTTP 404: Not Found (.../releases/assets/668550394)`. All 30 build jobs passed. Because of this, `latest-builds` has no KDP files. It holds 1 paper PDF and 363 chart PDFs (`cell-N-output-1.pdf`).

**Cause**
- Each paper job uploaded `_build_temp/<config>/**/*.pdf`. For `1-pct-treaty-impact`, that took the paper and also 390 chart PDFs that Quarto keeps in `_freeze/**/figure-pdf/`.
- 27 of those names occur twice (`_freeze/index/` and the parameters appendix). When two uploads use the same name, `gh release upload --clobber` deletes the file that the other upload just made, and gets a 404.

**Changes**
- Each paper uploads only `<output-dir>/*.pdf` (`job.build_dir`). That is the folder `render-quarto.py` copies its outputs from. The EPUB and DOCX globs get the same change.
- If two files have the same name, the release step stops before it uploads anything, and it lists those names.
- After a run in which every build job passed, the release step removes release files that no build makes now. Thus the next nightly run removes the 363 chart PDFs. After a failed build, it removes nothing, so that paper keeps its last good PDF.

author: ezecasado
body:
## Qué cambia

Los campos del producto quedan como en el contrato. El alta pide `tipo` (`FISICO` o `DIGITAL`), y un FISICO necesita `peso` y `volumen`. El detalle, el alta y el `PATCH` responden con la forma del schema `Producto`, con la `cantidad` de Inventario. Un campo que la operación no acepta da 400.

> **Cambio de comportamiento:** un campo de más da 400 también en el alta de categorías. `POST /categories` con `descripcion` responde `El campo descripcion no se acepta en esta operación` y no crea la categoría. Antes se ignoraba.

- `Producto` suma `tipo` (guardado como texto) y `volumen` (`decimal(10,6)`), `peso` pasa a opcional y sale `dimensiones`. `V2__tipo_y_volumen.sql` tiene los `ALTER`, sacados del script que genera Hibernate.
- Alta: un FISICO sin `peso` o sin `volumen` da 422 junto con los demás campos que falten; un DIGITAL con alguno de los dos da 400. Más de 3 decimales en `peso` o más de 6 en `volumen` da 400. `cantidad` no se acepta.
- Respuesta: entran `tipo`, `volumen` y `cantidad`, y salen `activo`, `fechaCreacion` y `stock`. Un DIGITAL no trae `peso` ni `volumen`, un producto sin descripción no trae la clave, y `cantidad` sale siempre, en `null` si Inventario no responde.
- `PATCH`: no acepta `stock`, `dimensiones`, `cantidad`, `tipo` ni `sku`, y valida `peso` y `volumen` con los límites del alta.
- El README del catálogo queda al día.

## Por qué

El contrato (`docs/api/catalog.yaml`) tiene estos campos desde ST-01, y el código no los tenía. Las decisiones que más pesan:

- **El mapper estricto es solo el de entrada.** `WebConfig` registra en el conversor JSON de Spring MVC un mapper armado desde el `JsonMapper` de Boot, con `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES` y `FAIL_ON_NUMBERS_FOR_ENUMS`. Sin este último, `"tipo": 0` entraba como FISICO. El `JsonMapper` global sigue tolerante, para que los clientes de Usuarios, Inventario y Reseñas ignoren los campos que esos servicios sumen. Global, lo heredarían los clientes cuando pasen a `RestClient` (#26); por DTO, el alta de categorías seguía aceptando campos de más.
- **Las reglas de `peso` y `volumen` según el `tipo`** son dos anotaciones de clase, `FisicoConPesoYVolumen` y `DigitalSinPesoNiVolumen`, que marcan el error en el campo. Así, un FISICO sin `peso` sale en el mismo 422 que los demás faltantes. Con grupos de validación o en el servicio, un alta sin `nombre` ni `peso` diría solo `nombre`. Sin `tipo` no corre ninguna, y el 422 dice `tipo`.
- **La `V2`** agrega `tipo` con `DEFAULT 'FISICO'` solo para que el `ADD COLUMN` no falle, y después le saca el default. Se escribió con `productos` vacía en todas las bases; una fila vieja quedaría FISICO y sin `volumen`.
- **`@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)` va solo en `descripcion`, `peso` y `volumen`**, y no en toda la clase, para que un campo obligatorio en `null` se vea en vez de desaparecer.

Lo que queda para otros issues:

- #16: `cantidad` sale de `disponibilidad`, y la consigna devuelve `disponible`.
- #19: el `PATCH` no guarda `peso` ni `volumen`, rechaza `categoriaId` con un 400 y responde 200 a `{}`.
- #29: el detalle todavía trae `ratingPromedio` y `cantidadResenas`.

## Cómo se probó

- `.\mvnw.cmd verify` en `services/catalog`: 93 tests, 0 fallas. Son los 53 de antes, con los ajustes por el `tipo`, y 40 nuevos: 29 en `CamposDelProductoTests`, 10 en `ProductoPorSkuTests` y 1 en `MigracionesTests`, que revisa las columnas de la `V2`.
- El test del detalle con Inventario mandando `reservado`, un campo que `StockDTO` no tiene, prueba que el cliente sigue tolerante. Lo vi fallar con el `JsonMapper` global estricto (`-Dspring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=true`): `cantidad` llegó en `null`.
- Sin `FAIL_ON_NUMBERS_FOR_ENUMS`, dos tests fallaban: `"tipo": 0` entraba como FISICO y `"tipo": "1"` como DIGITAL.
- A mano con el Compose, sobre la base de la `V1` y sin `-v`: con `docker compose up -d --build`, Flyway pasa de la versión 1 a la 2 (`Successfully applied 1 migration to schema catalog, now at version v2`) y `curl.exe -i http://localhost:8082/categories` da `200` con `{"items":[]}`. En el Compose no se pueden crear productos (sin Usuarios, 503); eso queda para la seed del #40.

## Checklist

- [x] El título sigue Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`...)
- [x] El CI pasa
- [x] No hay contraseñas, keys ni `.env` en el diff
- [x] Actualicé el README o la documentación si hacía falta


Closes #15

author: lucas-moont
body:
## What changes

Two engine pieces for DARK DECO (#145): a still **`skyline` backdrop** (the opening's red sky in bands, soft black cloud shadows, black Deco towers with a few faint windows, a blue mist at their foot) and a **`blimps` Atmosphere** (black hulls hovering, two thin beams under each nose swaying a few degrees). No Theme uses them yet; the theme PR sets the numbers.

Part of #70; engine for #145. Linear: LUC-86. Research: `docs/research/themes/dark-deco-build.md` §2 and jury §9, decision 18 (#155).

- **`SkylineBackdrop`** (`kind: 'skyline'`), painted by `backdropFor` like HOLIDAY's moon: painted whole on a resize or new colors, never on the clock, kept under reduced motion. Sky stops `{ at, color }`; cloud masses `{ at, size, alpha }` blurred and only darker than the sky (the maintainer asked for "tones of black in the red", picked at medium strength); a seeded Deco city (flat roofs, setbacks and domes, a spire every fourth tower, as `DECO`'s vocabulary), the same city after every resize; a mist gradient over its foot.
- **`BlimpsAtmosphere`** (`kind: 'blimps'`): each blimp hovers at a share of the height and drifts on whole ticks only (the opening's storyboard draws them hovering while the camera moves), round from the other side once its hull and beams are wholly past one; the beams' reach, width, splay and sway are data (radians), their period in seconds; two fills a tick for the whole fleet.
- **`wrapAcross`**, the going-round-a-side the smoke already did, now shared.
- `CONTEXT.md` and `DESIGN.md` name both.

Seen on screen through a scratch build that dressed VENGEANCE in the sky (never committed): the maintainer asked for more visible beams (wider cones here; their 14% strength goes in the theme data) and approved the rest.

## Why not on the smoke painter

Clouds mid-sky on `smoke` need a birth height, which SAME BAT-TIME's session is adding; the blimps get their own kind so the two don't collide, and the clouds the maintainer picked are still shadows on the backdrop (the opening holds its sky still).

## Reviews

`/simplify` (four angles), one commit each: `wrapAcross`; the skyline's seeds in [0, 1) as `seededFrom` takes them (fix); named data shapes, beam width as data, radians and seconds; the blimps in two fills from what they work out once (perf); the Deco vocabulary named and roofs as mirrored halves; the tests' shared `colorOf`. Skipped: a blur per cloud mass (paid only on resize), renaming the kind to `deco-skyline` (no second skyline Theme yet), dirty-rect clearing.

## Code reviews

`/code-review` and `/mattpocock-skills:code-review` (Standards and Spec), tests first in one commit (24d2633), then one fix per finding:
- **the sky's bands are px above the foot** (they were shares of the panel's height, so on a taller panel the lit band climbed to where the cards' text sits, past the L* 19.5 ceiling);
- the skyline waits for every color instead of throwing on a missing one;
- the mist fades in bands of its own color (a gradient from transparent greys the middle, and an `rgba()` of its color is a hand-written color, which `themeColors.test` refuses);
- a lit window keeps its place across the panel and stays on it; a spire's needle always stands above its crown;
- the blimps' beams hang from two lamps (`apart`) and a blimp may lean its own in (`splay` under 0) so they cross, as the opening's far blimps' do; the fleet sways out of step; no beams without their color; beams start on the hull's underside; the wrap margin covers the fin;
- faithful to the opening's black blimps: no gondola, a 2.4:1 cigar;
- a cloud mass may carry its own blur, for the flat streaks of the medium shadows picked on screen;
- a skyline's doc says it covers its Theme's haze.

Left: per-mass blur on a 2x display (the 2x scratch captures read soft), mist rising in columns, a `deco-skyline` rename, dirty-rect clearing. Re-seen on screen through the scratch build after the fixes.

- [x] `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass (1268 tests; `format:check` too)

## Summary

### Key Changes
- **Summary**: Enrich ZNF668-related neurodevelopmental disorder with classifications, genetic features, pathophysiology GO/CL grounding, diagnosis, and treatments
- **Details**:
- Added `classifications` (`GENETICS_ENVIRONMENT_DISEASE` and `NEUROLOGIC`) backed by PMID:34313816.
- Added `variant_origin: GERMLINE` and `features` on `ZNF668` under `genetic`.

author: guyu2233
body:
## 背景

本仓库现有 `.github/workflows/build.yml` 能在 master 上跑通，但部署链路有几处会**静默出错或误报失败**的地方。这个 PR 只做加固，不改站点内容，也不改构建产物。

## 改动清单

| 问题 | 现状 | 改动 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 权限 | 无 `permissions`，依赖仓库默认的 write | 显式声明 `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` |
| 并发 | 无 `concurrency`，两次部署同时推 gh-pages 会互相覆盖 | 按 ref 分组；**master 的部署不参与取消**，避免推送到一半被打断 |
| 构建回环 | `on.push.branches: ['*']` 会让 gh-pages 自己的部署提交再触发一轮构建 | `branches-ignore: [gh-pages]` |
| 首次部署 | gh-pages 不存在时 `git clone --branch gh-pages` 直接失败 | 先 `ls-remote` 探测，不存在则初始化空分支 |
| 产物同步 | 在 `_site` 里原地 clone + build，靠 Jekyll 清理目录 | 拆成 `_site`（构建产物）与 `_deploy`（gh-pages 工作副本），用 `find` + `cp -a` 精确同步，已下线页面会被删除 |
| 依赖 | 依赖 runner 上的 `rsync` | 改用 coreutils，无隐性依赖 |
| 假失败 | 内容无变化时 `git commit` 非 0 退出，job 报红 | 提交前 `git diff --cached --quiet` 比对，无变化直接跳过 |
| CNAME | 每次覆盖写入 | 保留，并在 `.nojekyll` 旁显式写回 |
| prettier | 非 master 分支/PR 失败时无提示 | 输出 `::error::` 提示让作者知道要跑 `npm run fix` |
| 通知 | `chf007/action-wechat-work@master` 浮动引用；secret 缺失时 action 报错 | 固定到 `07415b7`（1.0.8 对应 commit）；无 webhook 时跳过；内容带成功/失败状态 |
| 缓存 | `CACHE_ID=1` | 递增到 2，刷新依赖缓存 |

另外把 CI 新增的 `_deploy` 工作目录写进 `.gitignore` 与 `.prettierignore`。

## 本地验证

部署脚本的三种路径已用本地裸仓库实测：

1. **首次部署**（gh-pages 不存在）→ 自动建分支，`.nojekyll` / `CNAME` / 产物齐全，提交信息带上游 commit 摘要；
2. **增量部署**（页面下线 + 新增 + 修改）→ 旧页面被正确删除，新页面入库；
3. **内容无变化的重复部署** → 打印「站点内容没有变化，跳过提交」，退出码 0。

YAML 解析通过；`prettier --check` 通过（本仓库 `.prettierrc` 对 yml 无额外约束，此处已单独校验）。

> 注：`JEKYLL_ENV` 保持原样不设为 `production`，以免影响线上产物的条件渲染；如需开启建议单独一个 PR。

## 合并后

master 上会走一次真实部署，往 `gh-pages` 推一次提交；若站点内容与当前 `gh-pages` 一致，会走「无变化跳过提交」分支。

author: augusto-dmh
body:
## Problem
The rail shows each grid's reported status, but an agent cannot say in its own words where its work
stands ("fix in; running tests", "waiting for review"). You open the pane and read the terminal to
find out.

## Change
- New `pane_note{text, phase?}` MCP tool and `hs-pane note TEXT [--phase todo|in_progress|in_review|done]`.
  An agent writes one line, at most 512 bytes, about its own pane. A longer note is refused, naming
  the limit; newlines become spaces. `clear: true` or `--clear` removes it.
- The grid's rail card shows the newest note of its panes, with its phase and age. The × on the line
  clears it (`session_note_clear`).
- The note is stored on the session row, carried in `SessionInfo.note` and broadcast as
  `session_note`. It goes when its pane closes or restarts.
- Protocol v150. Claims v150 like other open PRs; renumber at merge.

## Why
Orca's worktree checkpoints (`orca worktree set --comment … --workspace-status …`;
`docs/site/content/docs/cli/worktree-checkpoints.mdx`) let agents write a status note and phase onto
the workspace card. Houston's card is a grid, so the note belongs to the agent's own pane and the card
shows its grid's newest. It is status the agent reports, never read from the terminal.

## Tests
- Integration `pane_note_wire`: the real `hs-pane note` CLI writes a note, which is broadcast and
  listed; an oversized note is refused naming the limit and keeps the last one; text plus clear is
  refused; the renderer's clear broadcasts `None`; the DB round trip.
- Unit: note normalisation and limit; MCP tool order and annotations; rail card picks the newest note;
  the note line renders and Clear does not select the grid.
- Renderer typecheck, affected tests, build, check:css, check:bundle (boot budget re-cut by 200 bytes to
  947,000, with the reason in `bundle-budget.json`) and check:complexity.
- Not run: full suites, Linux checks (including the Unix-only tests whose `SessionInfo` literals gained
  `note: None`).

## Risks
- Respawning a pane drops its note.
- Notes are agent-written text kept in the session database, like titles.

## Release notes
### Features
- Agents can post a one-line status note, with a phase, on their grid's rail card using `pane_note` or `hs-pane note`; the × on the card clears it.

## Captures
Before (origin/main) and after (harness story `rail/card-notes`) were captured locally; the after capture shows "In progress · 4 commits in; runnin… 3m" on the Inspector polish grid card.

author: mbastian
body:
## Description

Adds release tests that run the assembled Gephi application, with its launcher, module system, user interface and Overview, and detect hangs and errors the headless integration tests can't see. They're meant to run on a developer machine before a release. CONTRIBUTING.md has a new "Release tests" section explaining how to run them and read the results, and a first step in the release process.

**`modules/ReleaseTests`** is never shipped. It isn't a dependency of the application and is excluded from the Maven Central deploy.

- **Driver.** This is the module itself, installed into Gephi like a plugin.
  - When Gephi starts with `-Dgephi.releasetests.suite=<name>`, it runs that suite once the main window shows (`@OnShowing`). It then exits with status 0 if the suite passed and 1 otherwise.
  - While the suite runs, a monitor checks every second that:
    - the EDT runs a posted no-op;
    - a new thread gets the graph read lock;
    - the Overview keeps drawing frames and receiving world updates, using the counters from #3349;
    - no threads are deadlocked.
  - A wait past 2 s is reported with a thread dump. A wait past 10 s fails the suite, as do a deadlock, a failed step or a log record at `SEVERE` or above (installed with `@OnStart`, so it also catches failures during other modules' startup).
  - `results.json` is rewritten after every change, so it survives a hang.
  - If closing and exiting take more than 60 s, Gephi is halted with status 1.
- **Supervisor.** These are the module's `*IT` tests, run with failsafe under `-P release-tests` only. CI just builds the module.
  - It unzips the NBM into a fresh userdir and pre-sets preferences to turn off the welcome window, the analytics popup, Sentry tracking and the latest-version check. JVM flags turn off update checks, the crash reporter and exception dialogs.
  - It launches `bin/gephi` with a flight recording. When the distribution has no JRE configured, it uses the JDK running the tests.
  - If Gephi hangs, it takes a `jcmd` thread dump, saves the flight recording, then kills Gephi.
  - If the driver never starts, typically because it was built from another version than the distribution, the run fails after 2 minutes and reports the module errors from `messages.log`.
- **Smoke suite** (`SmokeIT`, about 9 s). With the Overview showing, it:
  1. checks the look and feel is FlatLaf;
  2. imports Les Misérables and runs ForceAtlas 2 for 5 s;
  3. runs Degree and Modularity;
  4. applies and removes a degree filter;
  5. takes an Overview screenshot and exports a PNG, both checked not to be blank;
  6. saves, closes and reopens the project.

Run with:
```bash
mvn -pl modules/ReleaseTests verify -P release-tests                                # app in modules/application/target/gephi
mvn -pl modules/ReleaseTests verify -P release-tests -Dgephi.dist=/path/to/Gephi.app  # a release bundle with its JRE
```

Notes:
- Launching Gephi with `--nosplash` makes it start without FlatLaf ("Custom UI class com.formdev.flatlaf.FlatLightLaf not found"). The harness doesn't pass it, and the smoke suite now fails if the look and feel isn't FlatLaf.
- While building the harness, I made Gephi log an error, block the EDT, hold the graph write lock, pause world updates, deadlock two threads and hang. Each was reported, with its thread dump where it applies, and the hang was dumped and killed. That self-check isn't part of this PR.
- Tried on macOS only: the dev build on JDK 17, and a 0.11.3 `.app` with its bundled JRE, which showed the version-mismatch failure. There is no 0.11.4 bundle yet, and Windows and Linux are untested.
- Next: a soak suite stressing the graph lock from several threads, like the one a plugin developer used to find the lock issues.

## Checklist

- [x] Merged with master beforehand

## Added tests?

- [x] 👍 yes

The module is test infrastructure, and `SmokeIT` is its first suite.

## Added to documentation?
- [ ] 👍 README.md
- [ ] 👍 [API Changes](https://github.com/gephi/gephi/blob/master/src/main/javadoc/overview.html)
- [ ] 👍 Additional documentation in [docs](https://github.com/gephi/gephi-documentation)
- [x] 👍 Relevant code documentation
- [ ] 🙅 no, because they aren’t needed

CONTRIBUTING.md: a "Release tests" section, and a release step.

body:
GitHub Pages' CDN can reuse release metadata across unique query strings despite no-store requests. The app now retries a positive-Age response once through a same-origin equivalent path, sharing the original timeout and retaining strict metadata/freshness validation. The worker forwards these aliases to the network.

Offline saving now works independently of version-check availability when the worker has a validated inventory whose selected release and runtime both match the loaded app. The download rechecks those identities immediately before transfer; a retained older selection still requires the correct current-document manifest.

Validation:
- Final product code: **146 unit files / 2,875 tests passed**. Build `ce10ae621968` measures **2,393,660 decoded app bytes** plus a **26,809-byte worker**.
- Independent source and production browser reviews passed. CDN/public-host probe: **16/16 fresh aliases** returned the correct metadata with Age 0/CDN MISS.
- Final product browser checks: **6 passed** (40.4 sec); independent offline-independence checks: **4 passed** (34.1 sec).
- Two actual full builds passed detect → prepare → Later → explicit two-tab restart → new running identity → fresh physically disconnected launch, preserving work, theme and route.
- Earlier `cf249e3` push CI: **1,146 browser passes / 3 timeouts / 23 intentional skips**. The timeouts were test timing assumptions about changing action labels and proactive withdrawal of an unsafe Restart action. Corrections retain old-build, unlocked-app, repair and restart assertions. Independent corrected rerun: **6 passed** (36.5 sec); three-repeat rerun: **18 passed** (2.0 min).
- Final `ac88788` push and pull-request CI both passed all three jobs. The complete browser suite passed **1,149 tests with 23 intentional skips**; all **2,875 unit tests** passed. Merged as `e3e1196`; GitHub Pages deployment passed. Unmodified public-site checks passed at 375px/dark and 1280px/light: correct running/deployed identity, explicit full download, browser-offline reload, no page errors or overflow. Deployed build `41fb432941c1` contains 2,393,660 app bytes plus the 26,809-byte worker. Partial local runs, the mistaken dependency-refresh interruption, initial failures and independent evidence remain in [the validation note](https://github.com/snowch/assembly-lab/blob/ac8878842233eae470d4a85b8c63eb65da96119c/docs/notes/app-status/pages-freshness.md).

The original deployed `895d006` correctly failed closed on cached metadata; final public freshness/download verification follows this fix without request interception. A host that rejects or normalises the fallback aliases still fails safely rather than claiming stale currency.

The duplicate final local full run was stopped after both complete CI runs passed: **815 passed, 1 restart-wait timeout, 19 skipped, 1 interrupted, 336 not run** (exit 130). The failing local test's final second-tab release assertion did not see the expected marker within five seconds. Independent trace review found the new second-tab document request beginning approximately 5.023 seconds after the final restart click, just beyond the assertion's five-second wait. Three repeated runs on each viewport passed: **6 passed in 1.1 minutes**. This partial command is not reported as passing.

After #39, the final deployed commit `7a1ed51` was rechecked without request interception on phone/dark and desktop/light: correct source/build identity, freshness, explicit full download and browser-offline reload all passed with no page errors or overflow. Final build `31e6d82c6201`: 2,394,113 app bytes and 26,809 worker bytes. Independent review classified the duplicate local restart failure as a test wait that is shorter than the allowed lifecycle; no demonstrated product regression, while final navigation completion is outside that truncated trace.

author: millianlmx
body:
## Quoi

### Runners confinés en mode systemd

En mode systemd, un runner tournait jusqu'ici dans une simple `--scope`, et son worktree était inscriptible par le groupe (`UMask=0002`). Un agent travaillant sur le dépôt A pouvait ainsi lire tous les clones et écrire dans le worktree vivant du dépôt B, qui pouvait ensuite s'auto-merger. Le cloisonnement des clients par dépôt n'était donc tenu que par l'API.

Désormais, le runner est un **service transitoire** dont le bac à sable est imposé par le lanceur root (`omp-harness-systemd-run`), qui valide toujours la ligne mot à mot :
- `ProtectSystem=strict`, `NoNewPrivileges`, `PrivateTmp`, `PrivateDevices`, `ProtectHome`, `ProtectKernel*` ;
- les dossiers des worktrees et des clones sont masqués par un tmpfs en lecture seule, puis seuls le worktree du run (en écriture) et son clone (en lecture) sont remontés ;
- l'état du service, `/etc/omp-harness`, les sockets dbus et docker sont rendus inaccessibles.

C'est l'équivalent de ce que fait déjà le mode conteneur (`runner.ts`).

Les clés d'API passent par un fichier root 0600 dans `/run/omp-harness-launcher` (`EnvironmentFile=`). Elles ne figurent jamais sur la ligne de commande ni dans les propriétés de l'unité.

Bug corrigé au passage : l'arrêt forcé d'un job heavy visait `.scope` au lieu de `.service`.

### Plafonds de dépense

- Avec `pauseOnBudget`, le moniteur arrête l'étape **en cours** dès que le coût réel dépasse `runBudgetUsd`, et le run attend l'humain. Avant, le budget n'était vérifié qu'entre deux étapes, alors qu'une étape peut durer 90 min.
- Nouveau réglage `monitoring.dailyBudgetUsd` (null par défaut, donc aucun changement de comportement sans configuration) : une fois le plafond du jour UTC atteint, aucune étape ni audit ne démarre avant minuit UTC ou une hausse du plafond. Il émet les événements `admission_refused` (`daily_budget`) et `daily_budget_reached`.

### API durcie

- Un `clientsFile` illisible ne fait plus tomber l'API. Le dernier jeu valide et le jeton admin historique continuent de servir, l'erreur est journalisée une fois par version du fichier, et `add` ou `revoke` refusent d'écraser un fichier cassé.
- Un client non admin ne peut supprimer que ses propres jetons push : `DELETE /v1/push/activities/{name}` vérifie la propriété.
- Une erreur 500 répond « erreur interne (réf. xxxxxxxx) » ; la cause complète est journalisée sous la même référence. Les réponses `HarnessError` sont inchangées.

### Unité du service

Ajout de `ProtectSystem=full`, `ProtectHome`, `PrivateTmp` et `ProtectControlGroups`, dans l'unité Debian et dans le module NixOS.

Les directives à base de seccomp (`ProtectKernel*`, `RestrictAddressFamilies`, `LockPersonality`, `RestrictSUIDSGID`…) imposent `NoNewPrivileges`, ce qui casserait le `sudo` vers le lanceur ; elles sont volontairement absentes. Il n'y a pas non plus de `strict`, parce que le lanceur écrit sous `/run` et dans le HOME du runner depuis l'espace de noms du service.

## Critères prouvés

- `harness-isolation-runners/AC-1..5`
- `harness-plafond-cout/AC-1..4`
- `harness-securite-api/AC-1..3`

Tests mis à jour : `harness-deploy`, `harness-runner/AC-1`, `harness-monitoring/AC-4` (le run se met en pause à `req` et non plus à `specs`, puisque le plafond agit maintenant en cours d'étape) et `harness-monitoring/AC-12`.

## Vérification

- `bash scripts/check.sh --tests-base=origin/main` est vert.
- ⚠️ Le nouveau bac à sable des runners n'a été vérifié qu'en **dry-run** du lanceur, pas sous un vrai systemd. Avant de merger, il faut un essai sur un VPS en mode systemd : lancer un run et vérifier que le runner écrit dans son worktree et lit son clone, sans voir les autres.

## Reste ouvert

Les jobs heavy peuvent toujours lire les clones et les worktrees des autres dépôts. À traiter dans une prochaine PR.

Deuxième d'une série de 4 PR issues d'une revue du dépôt.

author: kigawa01
body:
## 概要
#318 で k8s4 の Rack を 3.7.4 に上げたところ、**`maas-rackd` が起動できなくなった**(MAAS 3.7.4 のパッケージの不具合)。その回避を、`maas-rack` モジュールに足す。

## 原因
- 3.7.4 の `provisioningserver/logger/_logging.py` の `get_logging_config` は、書式 `fips_json` を**必ず**組み立て、そのために `maasservicelayer.logging.configure` を import する。
- `maasservicelayer` は **`maas-region-api` にしか入っていない**(3.7.4 の maas-agent / maas-common / python3-maas-provisioningserver / maas-rack-controller の各 deb を調べて確認)。
- そのため、**Region を同居させない Rack では、rackd が `ValueError: Unable to configure formatter 'fips_json'` で起動できない**。使い捨ての Ubuntu 24.04 コンテナで、**Rack 3.7.4 を新規導入しても再現した**。

## 変更
- **`files/maas-rack-shim.sh`(新規)**: 実際に入っている版の `maas-region-api` の deb から、`maasservicelayer` の必要な 5 ファイル(`__init__.py`、`logging/__init__.py`、`logging/configure.py`、`utils/__init__.py`、`utils/date.py`)だけを取り出し、`/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages` に置く(dpkg の管理外。**リポジトリには複製しない**)。あわせて、依存の `python3-pythonjsonlogger` と `python3-structlog` を入れる。
  - 冪等。すでに import できれば何もしない。
  - **本物の `maasservicelayer` が入ったら(`/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages` に現れたら)、置いたファイルを外す**(古いファイルが本物を隠さないように)。目印のファイルがあるものだけを外す。
  - deb を取得できない、置いても import できない、のときは中止。
- **`files/maas-rack-upgrade.sh`**: 3.7 以降が目標のとき、**更新したときだけでなく、すでに目標の版のときも**、`maas-rack-shim.sh` を実行する(#318 で上げた k8s4 を直すため)。回避を入れたら、rackd と agent を再起動する。回避スクリプトが失敗したら中止。
- **`main.tf`**: shim スクリプトのアップロードと、トリガーへの追加、後始末。

## 検証
- `test-maas-rack-shim.sh`(新規 21 件)、`test-maas-rack-upgrade.sh`(56 件)、`test-maas-rack.sh`(90 件)。すべて通過。
- 使い捨ての systemd 付き Ubuntu 24.04 コンテナで、**実際の apt**を使い、3.6.6 → 3.7.4 の更新から回避まで、一続きで検証した。回避が入り(`shim: installed`)、**`maas-rackd` が active**、`import maasservicelayer.logging.configure` が通る。再実行は `shim: present` で何もしない。(`maas-agent` は、コンテナが Region に未登録のため、active にならない。想定どおり。)

## 補足(#318 のあとに起きたこと)
- Region を 3.7 に上げた時刻(2026-10-24 23:05 JST)に、k8s2 の `maas-dhcpd` が停止し、再開していない(3.6 の Rack が、3.7 の Region からの DHCP の設定を適用できないとみられる)。LAN の端末は固定 IP のため、実害はないとのこと。Rack を 3.7 にそろえたあとに、DHCP を再確認する。
- `terraform apply` は、手元の Terraform 1.13 ではなく、**1.6.6**(CI と同じ系統)で、**`-target=module.maas_rack`** に絞って行う(k8s4 の `module.control_plane` には、9/25 の #170 以降の未適用の差分があり、稼働中の control-plane でスクリプトを再実行しないため)。

## マージ後の手順
1. `-target=module.maas_rack` で k8s4 に `apply`(1.6.6)。
2. k8s4 の rackd と agent が active、MAAS で k8s4 が 3.7.4 であることを確認。
3. 別の PR で k8s2 の `maas_rack_version` を `3.7` にする。

Refs kigawa-net/infra#317

author: carolisengineering
body:
Fixes **New from text** for the owner's "Don't Let up" class, which read as 17 sections instead of 3 and dropped everything after the 8th (Accessory included). This amends Spec 10.4 with AC42–AC54 (owner-approved 2026-10-24). The change is in the pure `@sin/core` reader only; the Check screen, the editor and saving are unchanged.

## What was wrong (reproduced on the real reader with the owner's paste)

- **Missed screenshot boundaries.** 3 of the 4 clock lines carried the silent-mode icon (`11:08 →`), so the reader saw one long screenshot and never removed the overlaps.
- **Icons read as lines.** Status-bar and tab-bar icons came through as text (`口`, `凸`, `الهه`, `•0ll`), sat inside the overlaps and blocked them.
- **One line read two ways.** Live Text read "90s" as "gos" in one screenshot and "g0s" in the other, so the exact overlap match failed.
- **Headers guessed from wording.** The reader treated INTENT, (No Bike) and stretch names as sections. Meanwhile it threw away the score badge (`NO SCORE`, `REPS`) that marks the real headers. The headers' bold doesn't survive the copy, but the badge line does.

## What changes (`packages/core/src/workoutText.ts`)

- **Screenshot boundaries:**
  - a clock line may carry one icon;
  - short non-ASCII icon lines are dropped, as are the signal bars and the results count;
  - the overlap compares lines through an OCR look-alike key (0/o, 9/g, 1/l, 5/s).
- **Sections:**
  - when a paste has score badges, the line above a badge starts a section, and so do strict headers (`Workout: "X"`, Warmup, Strength, Accessory…); guessed generic titles are off;
  - a header at a screenshot's edge keeps its section;
  - a repeated header continues its section.
- **Exercises:**
  - "N Sets, 1 Set Every M:SS" sets the count and stays in the note;
  - interval lines ("90s on / 90s Rest", "In a 90s Time window,", "Rest 90s and Repeat") don't end a group;
  - "200 Meter Run+" and "Max Cal Echo Bike…" become exercises;
  - "10 Tuckups + 15 Hollow Rocks" becomes two exercises.
- **Alternatives:** everything after a label ("Scaled Run:", "(No Bike)", INTENT, "AT HOME…") goes to the note.

## Tests and checks

- 3573 core tests and 3536 web tests pass; lint, typecheck, build and the core purity check pass.
- The owner's paste is a fixture (`hiraya-2026-10-24.txt`) with an end-to-end test. The line-conservation check (every line in exactly one place) runs on it and on 200 shuffles of it.
- `acTags.10-4.test.ts` requires AC42–AC54.
- Reviews:
  - `/security-review`: no findings. Every new pattern was timed on 40,000-character hostile input; the worst case took 25 ms. One cheap hardening was applied.
  - `change-auditor`: one doc defect (DESIGN Q28) fixed.
  - The final whole-branch review found one Important issue: a header at a screenshot's edge could lose its section. It is fixed, with tests.
  - `/code-review`: four Important findings fixed, with tests. A stray badge word switched off strict headers; "(each leg)" and "Advanced Plank" counted as labels; coaching text after "N Sets, every" became fake exercises; "***" separators were dropped as icons.

## Post Merge Checks

1. In Photos, copy the Live Text from the same four "Don't Let up" screenshots and paste them into **New from text**.
2. Expect 3 sections and 6 exercises, with no "left out" notice.
3. Then paste the 2026-10-19 class again and expect the same result as before.

author: redfirebreak
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RedFirebreak"} -->
_Requested by **Red** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01RVcxD4Vcb7FM2HNuHiNLP2?thread=cmsg_01RVcxD4Vcb7FM2HNuHiNLP2NbYuM5izr9RoT4wiPPrYgR)_

## Why this PR and what it fixes

The plugin's bank value was a one-off `bankValue` event. If that one message got lost, the hub never knew the bank, and Home Assistant had no value it could keep. The plugin PR (xXD4rkDragonXx/runelite-homeassistant-data-exporter#50) now sends the bank as a player field, `player.bank: { value, readAt }`, in every message once the bank has been read, kept across logins. This PR makes the hub read that field. No released plugin ever sent the event, so the hub stops reading it (Red's call).

## What changes

- **Payload:** `player.bank { value, readAt }` is parsed as its own section (safe integers ≥ 0; a bad one is skipped like any other section).
- **Plan (D-124):** the reading is applied to `latest_state.bank_value` / `bank_value_at` when it was read after the stored one. The same reading in the next message changes nothing, an older one loses, and a stale snapshot still applies a newer reading. `readAt` is capped at the receive time (for a clock running ahead) but not raised to recv − 15 min like an event time, because a reading kept across logins can be days old. Special worlds and XP-guarded payloads still never set it.
- **Old event removed:** `normalizeEvents` no longer special-cases `bankValue`. One that still arrives is stored as an unknown event type. Bank values already stored (Red's own, from running the first plugin branch) stay as they are.
- **Fixture:** `event-bank-value` becomes `snapshot-bank` (the same visit, as a field).
- Docs: ARCHITECTURE §3 and D-124 (with why it changed), the fixtures README, the API schema text.
- No migration.

## Testing

- `pnpm test` (2,800+ tests), `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `check_gotchas.py`: all pass. New tests cover parsing, newest-wins, a repeated reading, an old reading's time kept, a clock running ahead, stale and special worlds, and the store path through Postgres.
- Dev stack, with the matching osrs-dev-stack PR: `up full --worker`, `smoke` (all PASS), `chain wealth` (PASS: 1,234,567,890 bank counted in the day's wealth), `chain contract` (PASS).

## Merge order

Any order. Without the plugin PR the hub simply has no bank value, as before. The dev-stack PR skips `chain wealth` on a hub without this change.

author: jaredlunde
body:
The sandbox probe ran `command -v bash` as a program. The exec protocol runs its program execve-style, and `command` is a shell builtin with no binary on most images, so a sandbox with bash installed still got `sh` for the remote bash tool.

The probe now runs `sh -c 'command -v bash'` (sh is guaranteed: the HOME probe just ran one). ARCHITECTURE.md updated.

Test: `service::tests::the_probe_finds_bash_through_a_shell` drives `connect_exec` against the exec mock, which runs argv without a shell; it failed on main (`sh` instead of `bash`).

author: fooftilly
body:
## Problem
The guided firewall/tunnel installer currently reports only `InstallError`, even for predictable, operator-actionable conflicts. A real installation with an existing empty `0640` sudoers file failed at the policy validation step without indicating the cause.

## Changes
- Display **allowlisted, static remediation messages** for mismatched sudoers contents/ownership, installed privileged-file conflicts and missing/overridden effective systemd pre-start guard.
- Keep all unknown `InstallError`, `OSError`, and `ValueError` contents redacted; never echo raw sudo/Docker output, system paths derived from exceptions, or credentials.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior, installer mutation boundaries, and tunnel-status safety reminder.
- Add mocked regression tests covering known conflicts and secret-bearing unexpected failures.

## Validation
- GitHub CI and reviewers required. Local source verification only; no live privileged install was performed by this PR.
- Real Arch host demonstrated that the original failure was an empty, mode-0640 sudoers file; existing deployed policy was repaired and the full tunnel setup succeeded.

Part of #74. Please review; do not auto-merge.

author: kimseogyu
body:
Agents can now run `check-contracts` or `sgd_check_contracts` against actual candidate and supplied baseline sources, then inspect managed evidence for both model sets. A private collector performs the comparison and retains the original inputs. Public report data cannot authorize publication. Preparation is followed by input and output identity rechecks before the existing managed writer publishes anything.

The result is deliberately model-composition-only. It does not establish independent baseline selection, a protected preservation gate, or native application authority. Required unsupported native obligations fail. Both independent plugin Skills explain this boundary. Default responses contain a small summary and evidence index; check mode identifies existing logs as retained output.

Persistent identities remain portable for relative inputs, while original bytes remain unchanged. Short sorted slots support case-distinct and long contract IDs. All writers now share reserved-name, case/NFC, and ancestor path validation. The prior writer could delete its own inventory when an old entry used `.SGD-GENERATED.JSON` on a case-insensitive filesystem; an isolated reproduction confirmed this, and the shared validator now refuses before publication.

Validation: complete `npm run check`, build, ingestion, and partition verification passed with the pinned TLC JAR. Real public-channel, publication, relocation, stale-output, nested TLC-diagnostic, and recovery tests passed. Independent source review found no remaining blocker. The code tree is unchanged after rebasing onto merged PR27; the later change only corrected a documentation sentence. The external application inventory remains explicit opt-in and was not run. No installed-plugin rollout or background delivery is claimed.

body:
Fase C de `docs/specs/ia-anthropic-ligar.md` §10.4: o orçamento em US$ por escritório passa a valer, e entra o painel de consumo. Revisado pelo feature-review-agent: aprovado com ressalvas menores.

## O que faz
- **`CustoDaIa`:** o custo estimado de cada análise, em centavos de dólar.
  - Conta pelos tokens gravados e pelo preço de tabela do modelo (`ModeloDeIa`).
  - Modelo desconhecido paga o preço do Opus.
  - Com a região us, soma 1,1x.
  - A conta é toda em inteiros e arredonda para cima.
- **Gasto do mês:** soma desde o dia 1º, com tenant explícito. Entram também as análises excluídas e as que falharam, porque a Anthropic cobrou.
- **Trava:** caso novo `OrcamentoAtingido`, depois da cota mensal.
  - Vale nos modos **incluso** e **adicional**, quando o gasto chega ao orçamento. Volta no dia 1º.
  - Em **limite grátis** não trava; o painel marca "acima do grátis". **Padrão adotado em 24/10, o dono pode rever.**
  - A recusa volta como 429 com o código `limite_atingido`, o mesmo da cota mensal. A mensagem diz que foi o orçamento.
- **Painel do Master** (aba Configurações da I.A.): colunas "Análises no mês" e "Gasto no mês (US$)", com os selos "orçamento atingido" e "acima do grátis". Tudo sai de uma consulta só.
- **Tela do admin do escritório** (`/admin/inteligencia`): bloco "Consumo do mês", só com os dados do próprio escritório.
- Sem migration.

## Ressalvas da revisão
- A consulta de todos os escritórios (aba do Master) filtra só por `criada_em`, e o índice atual começa por `tenant_id`. Com poucos escritórios, o impacto é baixo. **Próximo passo:** um índice em `criada_em`, que precisa de migration.
- Com orçamento definido, cada checagem de disponibilidade faz mais uma consulta agrupada, inclusive nas telas que mostram o botão da IA. É barata, no índice `(tenant_id, criada_em)`.

## Testes
- `tests/Inteligencia` 1109 OK, `tests/Master` 568 OK, `tests/Pasta` 4180 OK.
- Suíte completa (16753): só 5 falhas, todas do `McpServerCommandTest`, que não tem relação com a frente. Sozinho ele passa (5/5); falha só na suíte inteira.
- PHPStan e CS-Fixer OK.

## Arquivos quentes
- `app/config/services.yaml`.
- Traduções.

## O que olhar na tela (8080)
1. Master, aba Configurações da I.A.:
   - a tabela com 8 colunas, que rola na horizontal em tela estreita;
   - o gasto com 2 casas;
   - os selos vermelho e âmbar;
   - a nota nova da tabela.
2. `/admin/inteligencia`: o bloco "Consumo do mês".
3. Na pasta, com o orçamento atingido: o botão da IA trava com "Orçamento mensal da BlueJus IA atingido; volta no dia 1º".

author: jjdsnt
body:
Generic mDNS record questions and bounded IPv4 host lookup are now available
through `bonami.library`, without running client callbacks in mdnsd.

This is the next standalone BonAmi slice tracked by #1794. It is one commit
directly on current `master` and does not depend on the tools PR.

### Public contract

- Append `LookupHostA()`, queue-native `QueryRecordA()`, `StopQuery()` and
  `ReadMDNSRecordEvent()` at LVOs 22 through 25. The unmerged local prototype
  had put three of those names in positions now occupied by queued discovery
  and delivered records through a client Hook; neither detail becomes part of
  the AROS ABI.
- `QueryRecordA(name, type, tags)` requires
  `MDNS_EventMode=MDNS_EVENT_QUEUE` and an output `MDNS_QueryRef`.
  `RequestMDNSEvent()` wakes query references as well as browse/resolve
  references; callers drain queries with `ReadMDNSRecordEvent()`.
- `MDNSRecordEvent` has no pointers. It carries owner, type, class, TTL,
  receiving interface and up to 512 bytes of RDATA. Compressed PTR targets and
  SRV target names are expanded into self-contained DNS wire labels.
- `LookupHostA()` is a synchronous consumer of the same query engine, with a
  1..60 second `MDNS_Timeout` (default 3). Bare names are placed in `.local`,
  and the output address is unchanged on failure.
- Query references retain the accepted task ownership, daemon-incarnation,
  lent-request cancellation and explicit-overflow contract. There are eight
  queries, at most four per task, and eight queued records per query. Unread
  repeats of the same record are coalesced with their newest TTL.

The library becomes 41.3 and private IPC becomes version 4; they must be
installed together. Since `OpenLibrary()` checks only the major version,
clients using the new LVOs must also require revision 3.

The local host's own announced A record is answered directly. Reflection of
locally registered services remains the next separate follow-up. This slice
also does not add a retained query cache, known-answer lists, IPv6, TXT/status
helpers, the commodity or Envoy.

### Validation

- **12/12 new host query fixtures pass under ASan/UBSan**: remote and local A,
  compressed PTR RDATA, coalescing, queue exhaustion, timeout, lent-request
  cancellation, owner/daemon checks, network reset, wrong class/source port
  and invalid inputs.
- **38/38 queued-discovery fixtures** and **26/26 responder/registration
  fixtures** still pass under ASan/UBSan.
- `bonami.library`, `mdnsd` and a public-ABI query probe compile and link for
  **linux-x86_64** and **amiga-m68k** using the generated AROS bindings; no
  compiler warning was emitted.
- On **hosted x86-64 AROS**, the generated 41.3 library and IPC-v4 daemon pass
  the public-ABI probe against an independently encoded Linux mDNS peer:
  queued PTR query/read, wakeup, cancellation, A lookup and lookup timeout.
  A packet capture was retained.
- The companion repository's full `make test` passes.

No native amiga-m68k, SMP/hardware, Apple Bonjour or Windows runtime result is
claimed.

The two new implementation files are AROS-specific and use the standard AROS
copyright notice. Existing BonAmi-derived files retain their BSD-2-Clause
notices.

## Milestone 3: YPS Learning Library (for review, **do not merge yet**)

Foundation Programme, Unit 1 (Think with Numbers). Pilot draft, not validated. Full design and review flags: `docs/LEARNING_LIBRARY.md`; pre-change audit: `docs/content-current-state.md`.

### What is in it
- `/programme/foundation` (moved; `/programme` forwards), `/learn/foundation/unit-1`, six lessons, six practice views

1. **The repository is public.** The student drafts and PDFs here become readable on GitHub. It was created private.

author: aitrawog
body:
## Summary

A task's `params:` reach a plan step only as **text**: the expander substitutes the value into the step's command, and the shell then PARSES that text — so a value that is DATA becomes SOURCE, and a `$(…)` inside a value EXECUTES with the step's privileges. This change opens the second channel. The task's resolved values — its `vars`, its `env`, its resolved `params` and `TASK_DIR` — are handed to the SDK as `kit.RunnerConfig.StepEnv`, so they reach every step as the step's **process environment**, where the shell never re-parses them. The change is 7 files, +401 −45 (Head `253120997a33e1c021fb7c88609a78ef84f8b1de`).

Closes #34.

Three rules bound the channel, and each is a rule the SDK's own merge already owns, so the plugin adds no second implementation of any of them:

- the step's OWN `env:` WINS a name collision — the author spoke last about their own step, and the task's value is a default;
- a name the shell cannot export (outside `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`) is REJECTED and RETURNED, and the SDK renders it as a NOTE on the step's message ("not exported (not a valid shell identifier): …") — disclosed, never dropped silently;
- a piped stdin is not a resolved value, so it is NOT exported. The map is CLONED before `captureStdin` mutates it, because the command verb renders an exported value into the command TEXT, and a NUL byte (a piped binary stream carries one) would make the exec un-runnable. The stream keeps its own channel: `TASK_STDIN` / `TASK_STDIN_FILE` stay reachable through the text expansion they have always had.

A lowercase param is a second, independent win: the expander's grammar is uppercase-only, so a lowercase param was previously unreachable from a step at all. The environment is what makes it reachable BY NAME.

### RCA

- **Mechanism:** the task engine had exactly ONE route from a resolved value to a step — the expander, which substitutes the value into the command TEXT. A shell parses the text it is given, so the value is re-parsed on the way: a `$(…)` inside it EXECUTES, and a `;` or a space splits it into words. The value changed from DATA into SOURCE at the moment it crossed that channel.
- **Missed control:** nothing asserted that a value stays DATA. The expander's contract was "the value's TEXT is substituted", and there was no second channel, so the only way to reach a step was the unsafe one; and the suite asserted what a step's command RECEIVED, never what a param's value was DELIVERED as. A value that arrived as text and a value that arrived as data were indistinguishable to it.
- **Blast radius:** every task that passes a value into a step — a param carrying a path with a space, a command substitution, a shell metacharacter, or a lower-case name.
- **Root fix:** the environment is the second channel, and it is the SDK's channel, not a plugin-local one: `kit.RunnerConfig.StepEnv` + `kit.MergeStepEnv` (`opencharly/sdk#475`, released as `sdk v0.2026297.1851`). The plugin hands over the resolved map and lets the SDK own the merge rules; the plugin's own contribution is the clone before the stdin capture, because only the plugin knows that the map it hands over is about to be mutated with a runtime stream.

### Producer-first

The DATA channel is an SDK capability, so this module's `require` rises to `sdk v0.2026297.1851`. This repo's own coherence control (`scripts/check-coherence.sh`, run by the `coherence` CI job on every PR and by the live gate before its build) asserts that charly's `sdk`/`spec` pins LEAD this module's requires, so the producer leg had to land first — and it has: `opencharly/charly#1062` merged as `87f6302456f9c821877e719cbe90615368cd85bc` with the merge-time tag `v2026.297.1957`, and charly's `main` now pins `sdk v0.2026297.1851` / `spec v0.2026296.1036`. The coherence control against `main` is pasted under **How tested**, and the live gate ran against `main` — the configuration that ships.

The legs that follow this one:

1. `opencharly/charly#1062` — charly adopts `sdk v0.2026297.1851` (MERGED, `v2026.297.1957`);
2. **this PR** — this repo raises its own require and implements the consumer;
3. charly adopts the new `plugin-task` tag this PR produces;
4. the umbrella advances its `charly` and `plugin-task` gitlinks.

### The files this diff touches

| file | what this diff does to it |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | the user-facing section that documents the new channel: what reaches a step, the three rules that bound it, and the lower-case-param win |
| `candy/plugin-task/go.mod` | the `sdk` require rises to `v0.2026297.1851`, the release that brings the DATA channel; the `spec` require and the `go` directive move with it |
| `candy/plugin-task/go.sum` | the sums for the new `sdk` release, and the transitive bumps `go mod tidy` resolved alongside it |
| `candy/plugin-task/runner.go` | the resolved map is CLONED before the stdin capture and handed to the SDK as `kit.RunnerConfig.StepEnv` |
| `candy/plugin-task/stepenv_test.go` | new: the channel's contract at unit level — the export, the collision rule, the disclosure of a non-exportable name, the stdin exclusion |
| `scripts/check-coherence.sh` | one comment clause: the historical measurement named "this module's v0.2026276.1822", a pin this module no longer carries, so it now names the pin the module carried at the time of that measurement |
| `scripts/gate-task.sh` | the live arm: a param carrying `$(touch <marker>)` runs against a real charly binary, and the arm asserts the value arrives VERBATIM and that the marker file does not exist |

## How tested

Every command below ran on the committed tree this PR pushes — `git rev-parse HEAD` prints the pushed commit, and `git status --porcelain` printed nothing on it.

```console
$ git rev-parse HEAD
253120997a33e1c021fb7c88609a78ef84f8b1de
$ git status --porcelain
STATUS_RC=0
```

The module gate, in `candy/plugin-task/`, under the toolchain the module's own `go.mod` DECLARES (`go 1.26.8`) — which is the toolchain CI installs, via `go-version-file: candy/plugin-task/go.mod`. The linter is the version CI pins, and it runs under that toolchain because golangci-lint cannot read the export data of a newer GOROOT.

```console
== go build ./... ==
BUILD_RC=0
== go test -count=1 ./... ==
ok  	github.com/opencharly/plugin-task/candy/plugin-task	3.817s
?   	github.com/opencharly/plugin-task/candy/plugin-task/cmd/serve	[no test files]
?   	github.com/opencharly/plugin-task/candy/plugin-task/params	[no test files]
TEST_RC=0
== gofmt -l . ==
GOFMT_LIST=[]
GOFMT_RC=0
== go vet ./... ==
VET_RC=0
== golangci-lint (the module's own toolchain) ==
0 issues.
LINT_RC=0
```

The candy manifest, validated at the repo root with the worktree-local charly build:

```console
charly box validate: OK — checked 1 candy, 7 distros, 7 builders; 0 warnings, 0 errors
BOXVALIDATE_RC=0
```

The two steps of the CI `coherence` job — the SAME control, the same two callers — one against the control's own synthetic fixtures, one against charly `main`'s live `go.mod` over HTTP:

```console
== scripts/check-coherence.sh --self-test (the CI coherence job, step 1) ==
self-test OK: leading passes, lagging fails, absent pin fails
COHERENCE_SELFTEST_RC=0
== charly main's pins lead this module's requires (the CI coherence job, step 2) ==
CURL_RC=0
coherence OK: charly main's sdk/spec pins lead this module's requires
COHERENCE_MAIN_RC=0
```

The live gate — the repo's own `scripts/gate-task.sh`, which clones charly at `main`, compiles this candy IN, and drives `command:task` plus the five maintenance verbs against real git fixtures. This is the ONLY live execution of those verbs, and it is where the DATA channel is proven end to end: the data arm's param carries a command substitution, and the arm asserts BOTH outcomes — the value arrives VERBATIM, and the marker file the substitution would have created does NOT exist.

```console

author: traktuner
body:
## Problem

`proton-drive-backup` was OOM-killed on 2026-10-22 (8 GiB limit), 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24 (16 GiB limit). The kernel log shows each kill hit a **single `proton-drive` process** whose anon-rss matched the cgroup limit (8.0 GiB → 16.3 GiB → 16.2 GiB), with `Bun Pool`/`JSCWarmUp` threads as the invoking tasks.

The CLI is a Bun v1.4.2 (JavaScriptCore) compiled executable. JSC sizes its GC heap from the memory it sees as *available* — inside a container that is the cgroup limit — and collects lazily until ~80% of it. Raising the limit raised the appetite. A second effect turned one kill into a daily loop: the first-run seed wrote the catalog only after the whole tree uploaded, so a kill mid-seed left the catalog empty and the next scheduled run re-ran the full seed.

## Changes

**CLI processes (`src/server/cli.ts`)**
- `cliEnv()` sets `BUN_JSC_forceRAMSize` (default 512 MiB, overridable via the same env var). Verified on the pinned 0.9.0 binary: `BUN_JSC_logGC=1` prints GC logs, a non-integer aborts with "invalid JSC environment variable" (so malformed overrides fall back to the default with a warning), `NODE_OPTIONS` is ignored. Baseline RSS per CLI process is ~80 MiB.
- Upload runs keep only a 256 KiB tail of captured stdout/stderr (`maxCapturedBytes`); JSON ops stay unbounded.

**Engine (`src/server/engine.ts`, `catalog.ts`)**
- Seed: one CLI process per top-level subtree, catalog recorded after each unit via `onUnitUploaded` → a kill costs only the unit in flight; the next run resumes per file.
- Pending upload buckets capped in total (`PENDING_CAP` 2000); the fullest bucket is flushed early.
- `seenAt` strictly monotonic per set (`max(Date.now(), catalog.maxSeenAt + 1)`). Latent on `main`; the faster seed surfaced it as a flaky "skips deletion when >30%" test (2/4 full-suite runs).
- Mirror deletion pass and dry-run: top-most stale entries in O(n·depth) instead of O(n²).
- Direct child files of a source folder are passed in chunks of 500 paths per CLI process (was one argv → `E2BIG` for large flat folders).

**Docs**: README "Memory" section (budget, levers, OOM troubleshooting entry), env table row, compose comment, notable-changes entry.

## Compatibility

No schema change or migration. Existing sets (non-empty catalog) take the per-file path as before; only batch sizing changes. `add` mode keeps `-f skip -d merge` into the same parents, just split per subtree. The seed change only applies to empty catalogs. After an interrupted seed the per-file path uses `create-new-revision`; the CLI skips identical content automatically, worst case is an extra same-content revision, never data loss.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` clean.
- Vitest: 286 tests, 16 files, green across 3 consecutive full-suite runs (6 earlier runs green before the two scale fixes were added).
- New tests: RAM hint default/override/malformed, seed resumability (second unit fails → first unit cataloged, next run uploads only the rest), pending cap flushes mid-walk, vanished folder trashed once + dry-run agrees, `topMost` on 10k entries, 1100 flat files → 3 upload calls ≤ 500 each.
- Not verified here: a live run against Proton (no Docker on this host). Suggested: run the affected set with `docker stats` alongside; the limit can likely be lowered afterwards.
