author: redfellow
body:
## Change

The live map now explains newly observed outbreak and Field Lab contacts with brief grouped notices and a current-outing Recent contacts sheet. It distinguishes provisional estimates, points held until the outing qualifies, known cooldowns and matching authoritative outcomes.

Contact summaries are saved locally by account, outing and world. Restore and screen-off catch-up populate the log silently; refreshes and navigation do not repeat notices. The sheet shares space with Nearby, destination details and cleanup notices while preserving pause/finish controls. GPS matching, scoring and upload payloads are unchanged.

## Validation

- 13 focused reducer, SQLite persistence and controller tests passed, including retry after a transient storage failure.
- Mobile TypeScript and Expo Android JavaScript export passed.
- Strict OpenSpec validation, documentation link checks and diff checks passed.
- Independent source review approved after the storage-retry finding was fixed.

## Remaining acceptance

author: pedrolucas167
body:
Corrige três corridas: claim/transições da fila Redis agora são atômicos com leases e tokens, entradas/saídas e limite dos clubes são serializados no PostgreSQL, e a publicação de recomendações compara a geração do cache para impedir dados antigos após invalidação.

A verificação dos pontos de entrada revelou que o worker não era iniciado pelo runtime. Enqueue agora agenda uma execução via Next after; uma rota cron autenticada recupera trabalho pendente, declarada diariamente às 13:00 UTC na Vercel. Cada chamada executa um job com limite de função de 60 segundos. Sem novos enqueues ou consumidor persistente, retries/backlog avançam no cron diário. Workers antigos devem ser encerrados ao atualizar o protocolo.

Validação: 180 testes unitários e 49 de integração aprovados na implementação base. Nesta etapa, cinco testes novos exercitam handlers reais com NextRequest/NextResponse, Redis e PostgreSQL locais isolados: enqueue/callback/persistência, workers e callbacks concorrentes, cron sem credencial, lease abandonado/retry/falha terminal e capacidade/erros HTTP de clubes. Os cinco testes de cache pela rota de recomendações foram rechecados, assim como os quatro testes unitários do worker. TypeScript e lint dos arquivos alterados sem erros (avisos de console preexistentes no worker).

Autenticação, agendamento de after e Wikipedia/embeddings são controlados pelo harness; não houve teste de produção ou de transporte HTTP completo. A configuração cron só será ativada após deploy. Nenhuma alteração de schema ou migration necessária. Limitações e operação em docs/CONCURRENCY.md.

author: ppuup7777
body:
Stopgap for #141422 (and takes the deterministic amplifier out of #144133's repro): `session.resume` runs the banner's display-only tool-availability computation **inline**, and that computation runs live `check_fn` network probes for `web` / `image_gen` / `video_gen` / `connections` — measured **21–36 s** on a slow-egress host, on **every** resume (three consecutive calls in one process: 30.99 / 30.51 / 30.49 s; per-toolset: web 15.2 s, connections 5.2 s, video_gen 5.1 s, image_gen 5.1 s). The Desktop's session-class RPC budget is a fixed 30 s, so an affected profile can never be resumed in the UI: the owner finishes ~10–40 s after the client has gone, and the reply is dropped (`tui_gateway.ws: ws response send failed peer=… method=session.resume`). Field measurements: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141422#issuecomment-6388186225

## What this does

`gateway/session_local_inventory.py` now serves `info["tool_availability"]` from a **process-wide TTL cache** filled by a background thread:

- cold cache → answers `{}` immediately (what the banner shows before its first availability check anyway) while a daemon thread probes;
- warm cache → instant, no probe;
- expired → keeps serving the stale value, refreshes in the background;
- a failed probe keeps the warm value and clears the inflight key.

`HERMES_TOOL_AVAILABILITY_TTL_S` tunes the window (default 600 s, `0` = always recompute in the background, never block). Measured after the patch: cold `0.00 s -> {}`, warm `0.00 s -> {3 unavailable toolsets}`.

## Why this is safe

Nothing gates runtime behaviour on this map — `agent_init` reads `check_toolset_requirements()`; the availability dict only colours banner rows. A seconds-old or briefly empty snapshot changes banner colouring, nothing else.

## Scope / framing

This is deliberately a **stopgap**, not the long-term answer — #141422's async-resume direction is the real fix for "resume waits on inventory at all". The TTL cache removes the deterministic 30 s budget breach today, cheaply (+56/−2 in the gateway file). Independently worth bounding later: the `check_fn` probes themselves (e.g. `check_web_api_key` spending 16.7 s when the web backend is unreachable) — they also cost the CLI banner and `hermes doctor`.

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_tool_availability_ttl_cache.py` pins the contract — cold never blocks (with a probe that would hang the test if awaited), warm serves without reprobing, expired serves stale while refreshing, failed probe keeps the warm value and unwedges the key.

author: gamesbyian
body:
## Reproduced current-package integrity defect

On current main preimage `tools/assemble_windows_package.py` blob `feece6a2cb7ab99151c08b243911d75a94eceda3`, `validate_windows_portable_paths()` checked path syntax, Windows-reserved device stems and case-aliased ancestor spellings, but **allowed a file path that is itself the parent of another file path**, e.g. `mods/assets/catalog` and `mods/assets/catalog/item.toml`. Such two file entries are representable in a crafted ZIP manifest but cannot both be materialized by an ordinary Windows extractor. The existing per-ancestor spelling map sees the same spelling and accepts it.

## Source change

Add a bounded set-membership check for any file path that is the ancestor of another file path (case-insensitively). Keep the existing device-name and case-collision validation unchanged. This applies to both package-source and archive-consumer validation through the one canonical `validate_windows_portable_paths` path. New independent tests exercise direct two-entry collisions, deeper prefix collision, casefold-equivalent prefix collision, the required-shipping-files consumer and valid sibling layouts. **No ROM files, launcher, executable, UI, profile or release ledger changes.**

## H26 recovery provenance

Inspired by the *separately verified* first-party nested `qa04_zip_preflight.py` read-only ZIP-local namespace audit, preserved in Evidence Drive `142bXAi_4D-928Wz7FntyRbVzTYvt_sJZ` (whole SHA-256 `601d6131f90b427f29c53d0cee5be69cb4bacde467fda45e45b8144d5b18be00`, selected source member SHA-256 `28728223fadf9fc7cb2debd60e3a909ae1946220901b0501af1e96c5960a71e2`). The historical file demonstrated that a ZIP's central membership can be individually valid yet nonextractable as a whole. This PR is an **independently derived, current Windows package-specific** negative and three-line-policy change, not retransmission of historical held source or a competing recovery ZIP parser.

## Evidence and integration

Two commits: test-only `58c71c41524891463470a9e749784d741c21264b`; minimal source change `89732ed07662661bed8c28d7b7e01eb628648bfb`. GitHub readback confirms source blob `6f6dbedcf4bf0002a71416a9391e9719b040a83e` and new test blob `b0083a93d786408978629ce1d754fd9c8ac4cfd2`. Exact-head CI pending. Owner/Agent 3 should independently check latest main and branch protections before merging.

**Limits:** A synthetic cross-platform ZIP path preflight is not Windows physical extraction evidence, an actual malicious artifact observed in production, original/native gameplay parity or release QA acceptance. No release credit.

## Final exact-head qualification

- Exact head `89732ed07662661bed8c28d7b7e01eb628648bfb`, source Git blob `6f6dbedcf4bf0002a71416a9391e9719b040a83e`, new regression test Git blob `b0083a93d786408978629ce1d754fd9c8ac4cfd2`, both read back through GitHub.

- [Repository hygiene 40128098038](https://github.com/gamesbyian/UR-Recomp/actions/runs/40128098038): **GREEN**.
- [Windows portable consumer PE contract 40128098042](https://github.com/gamesbyian/UR-Recomp/actions/runs/40128098042): **GREEN**.

body:
## Qué cambia

### 💞 Vuestra historia con él (Colección)
Una línea del tiempo con la llegada del huevo, el nacimiento, cada cambio de fase (`p.album`) y los momentos celebrados (`p.moments`). Enseña los 8 más recientes y tiene un botón "Ver los N momentos".

### 💑 Cuando estáis juntos
Con `state.main.together`:
- La escena se llena de corazones que suben y aparece 💑.
- El pollito pone cara de enamorado (expresión `love`) y dice frases nuevas.

Al pulsar "Ya nos hemos separado" se guarda `apartAt`: durante 3 horas el pollito está triste, y durante 6 dice frases de echaros de menos.

### 🌠 Lluvia de estrellas · a dúo (Mascota → Minijuegos)
Minijuego en directo para los dos (`games/coop`):
- Uno invita y al otro le llega un aviso. La fila del minijuego brilla con "Unirme".
- La partida empieza a la vez en los dos móviles (4 s de cuenta atrás) y dura 40 s.
- Las estrellas salen de una semilla común, así que los dos ven lo mismo. Lo que atrapa uno desaparece para el otro.
- Se ve el pollito del otro con su nombre: su posición se manda cada ~260 ms.
- 💛 Los corazones dorados solo cuentan si los dos pollitos están debajo a la vez.
- La meta son 45 puntos entre los dos. El premio llega a 40 🪙 por partida, con un máximo de 3 partidas pagadas al día. Cada partida se paga una sola vez por pareja, en una transacción.

### ⚡ Apertura con mala cobertura (`sw.js`)
- Antes la app esperaba siempre a la red. Ahora, si la página tarda más de 2,5 s, abre con la copia guardada y la versión nueva se guarda para la próxima vez.
- Para no mezclar versiones: si la página sale de la copia guardada, el resto de archivos de esa pantalla también. Con red normal todo funciona igual que antes.

### Avisos con la app cerrada

author: jonas-ekeli
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jonas-ekeli"} -->
_Requested by **Jonas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VzQnDUXtvTCCxEXLiiKVhL?thread=cmsg_01VzQnDUXtvTCCxEXLiiKVhLLuv7PgNSB7F9WT5Kwv3KCw)_

## What was wrong
With the mouse over the outline (or the app bar), the wheel scrolled the whole page past the app into an empty grey area. The cause: each node row in the outline carries a screen-reader-only status label (`.visually-hidden`, `position: absolute`). None of its ancestors is positioned, so its containing block is the page itself, not the outline's scrolling list. Rows below the outline's fold therefore stuck out under the window, the page became ~90 px taller than the window, and any wheel that wasn't taken by a pane scrolled the page.

## Fix (D187)
- `.visually-hidden` is pinned to its containing block's corner (`top: 0; left: 0`) instead of sitting where its row is.
- `.app` becomes the containing block for anything absolute inside it and clips it (`position: relative; overflow: clip`). `clip` rather than `hidden`, so focus or `scrollIntoView` can't scroll the app frame either. Dialogs and menus are `position: fixed` and aren't affected. The start page is outside `.app` and still scrolls as a page.

Either change alone removes the extra height (checked at 1400×850 and 1100×600, on Canvas, with a node open, History and Analyses).

## Tests
- New `e2e/page-scroll.spec.ts` (T-UI-63): in a 1100×600 window, the page is never taller than the window and stays at the top after the wheel over the node list, the outline, the app bar, the canvas, the node panel, History and Analyses. It fails on main and passes here.
- Ran locally: page-scroll, outline, commands, app-bar, node-panel, energy-drawer, controls, start-page, settings and node-cards specs all pass; `npm run lint` clean.

Spec: D187 in 08, T-UI-63 in 07.

## Cosa fa
Prima fase del monitoraggio automatico indipendente dall'iPhone. Aggiunge un modulo **solo lettura** per salvare su SQLite le serie settimanali ufficiali CFTC TFF Futures Only e Disaggregated Futures Only per 14 contratti tracciati (11 TFF, 3 Disaggregated) usando gli stessi codici/fields del frontend esistente.

- Solo due richieste a dataset ogni sei ore, con secondo host ufficiale in caso di errore. Nessun API token, servizio a pagamento o operazione di trading.
- Attivo di default **solo se l'utente aveva già approvato il collector cTrader** (`REMURA_COLLECTOR_ENABLED=1`). Può essere disattivato esplicitamente con `REMURA_COT_SYNC_ENABLED=0` senza interferire con prezzi e altri feed.
- SQLite privato: massimo 420 giorni, date CFTC effettive, nessun dato inventato nelle chiusure/weekend, aggiornamento idempotente, conservazione della storia buona quando CFTC è indisponibile.
- Endpoint privato `GET /private-api/cot/status` espone **soltanto** copertura, date di riferimento e stato; non restituisce esposizioni, credenziali o conti. Il Radar Squali mostra lo stato dell'archivio al click della scansione.
- **Non genera né invia segnali/notifiche**: il prossimo step sarà unire l'archivio VPS al prezzo verificato, calcolare transizioni sul server e solo poi aggiungere Telegram opt-in con deduplicazione.
- v1.32 e timestamp 24/10/2026 22:01 Italia visibili in alto su tutte le pagine; service worker aggiornato.

## Sicurezza e deployment
Questa PR modifica file `scripts/` e workflow `.github/`: l'autoupdater REMURA **richiederà installazione manuale sicura** dopo entrambi i controlli CI verdi. Nessuna copia/sovrascrittura di `private/` o token, rollback code-only già presente in install(). Test offline per normalizzazione, SQLite, endpoint e blocco su dati CFTC invalidi.

_Requested by **Gustavo Toigo** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01J4yrznHj3qjCziiQvANS3X?thread=cmsg_01J4yrznHj3qjCziiQvANS3XLesBS5ThDZZF2RqAFWRjFb)_

## Problema
Quem não tem YouTube Premium nem bloqueador recebe anúncios no player incorporado. A IFrame API não avisa quando o anúncio começa: o player diz "tocando", mas o tempo da música fica parado. O `SyncEngine` via isso como atraso e fazia `seek`/`play` a cada 500 ms, o que deixava a tela do anúncio travada sobre o vídeo. Além disso, a camada `player-shield` cobria o iframe e impedia clicar em "Pular anúncio".

## Mudanças (só `apps/web`)
- `SyncEngine`: detecta anúncio (tocando com o tempo parado por 1,5 s), mostra o estado `ad` e não mexe no player até a música voltar a andar; aí força a correção para a posição da sala.
- Anúncio que não sai em 90 s: recarrega o vídeo na posição da sala.
- Estado `unstarted` (pode ser início de anúncio) e o botão "Clique para ouvir junto" agora só dão `play()`, sem `seek`; a posição é corrigida assim que tocar.
- Durante o anúncio, os controles do EchoRoom saem da frente do vídeo (cliques vão para o YouTube) e aparecem um aviso e o status "Anúncio do YouTube…".
- 3 testes novos em `tests/sync.test.ts`.

## Testes
`npm test -w apps/web` (55 passaram) e `npm run build -w apps/web`. Não deu para reproduzir um anúncio real daqui; vale testar com uma conta sem Premium e sem bloqueador.

Redaction does not run on the stored record. It runs on a copy at report render and on findings GET. At-rest confidentiality is in this same change. Each object gets a random AES-256-GCM data key. author: sirhartley
body:
Stage 6 of the `docs/COMBAT_SHIPS.md` implementation plan: eight steps, one commit each, in order.

## Design defaults I chose (change any of them)

- Restoration runs in combat only. Partial progress is kept between battles.
- Restoration does not drain the Reliquary's replacement rate.
- Recovered fighters still out when a battle ends count as returned.
- The early Reliquary's extra ROD drone applies whenever it is in the fleet, including alongside the real Reliquary.

## Changes

**6.1 Fighter store** (`FighterStore`, `TenderBays`)
- Each Reliquary has a store keyed by fleet member id, kept in sector persistent data.
- The cap is 10 (new setting "Reliquary recovered fighter capacity"). It counts fighters aboard, restoring and out on a launch.
- `WreckTracker` reads the wing id while the fighter is still alive and adds it to the store when the wreck lands. Drones stop claiming wrecks while the store is full.
- Restoration works like a bay replacement: wing refit time × `getFighterRefitTimeMult`, advanced at the shared replacement rate. It pauses while the ship is overloaded, venting or out of CR.
- Only player ships in real campaign battles use the saved store. The simulator and missions work on a copy, so practice salvage never reaches the save.
- `FishingShips.reconcile` drops the stores of ships that have left the fleet.

**6.2 Salvage Launch** (`catchrelease_salvage_launch`, `SalvageLaunchStats`, `RecoveredWings`)
- Replaces `targetingfeed`. One activation launches every restored fighter, grouped into wings of their normal size.
- Each wing spawns from `LB 2`/`LB 3`. It gets the Reliquary as source ship but **no source bay**. Research found that a bay builds whatever wing asks it, so a recovered wing with a bay as source would be rebuilt endlessly.
- The spawn then:
  - trims surplus members;
  - calls `removeDeployed(wing, false)`;
  - gives each fighter the ship's CR and every hullmod's fighter effects (so no wrecks).
- Without a bay, vanilla never brings them home, so `RecoveredWings` gives a fighter a return AI when its AI wants a refit or the Reliquary pulls fighters back. It lands at `LB 1` and goes back into the store. A fighter that is destroyed is gone.
- `COMBAT_SHIPS.md` is corrected: `SwarmLauncherEffect` neither trims members nor sets CR.

**6.3 Launch AI** (`SalvageLaunchAI`): launches when an enemy target is within 3,000 and either two fighters are ready or every fighter aboard is.

**6.4 Combat status:** one `maintainStatusForPlayerShip` line per stored fighter type (ready/restoring), plus a "BAYS FULL" line. It uses vanilla's `icon_tactical_bdeck` glyph for now.

**6.5 Refit display** (`RefitStoreView`)
- On refit open, each Reliquary with stored fighters gets its own variant on a copy of its hull spec. The copy is made with `clone()` through `ReflectionUtils`, filtered by return type to skip the bridge method.
- Up to 4 stored wing types are appended as built-in wings, so they show as locked bays. Salvage Bays adds those bays only for entity-less stats, which is how the refit builds them, so combat never sees them.
- **Research found the open callback fires after the refit already shows a clone of the first ship.** So the watcher also swaps the *displayed* variant and resyncs the panel, using the same method names LunaLib's `refreshVariant` uses.
- If that resync fails, the swap is reverted. Otherwise the next field-refit save would charge CR for the "missing" wings.
- While open, the watcher re-applies the copy after a hull restore. It reverts everything when the tab changes.
- Stray stored wings are stripped from saved variants on load.

**6.6 Tooltip:** the Salvage Bays tooltip lists the store (sprite, name, count, ready/restoring). It is the fallback whenever the refit bays are not shown.

**6.7 Discard panel** (`FighterStoreRefitButton`): a "Recovered fighters" entry under LunaLib's Additional Options on each Reliquary.
- It lists each stored fighter with its sprite, state and restoration bar.
- "Discard" and "Discard all" each need a second press to confirm.
- The tooltip says a discarded fighter is gone for good, gives no LPC, and that undo won't bring it back.
- Research found neither `advance` nor `onPanelClose` can detect the refit closing, so the tab polling stays.

**6.8 Early Reliquary**
- New skin `catchrelease_rod_ship_early`. It is identical in combat because the combat and refit code finds Reliquaries by their inherited Salvage Bays hullmod.
- It repeats its own `no_drop`/`no_sell`/`no_bp_drop`, since skins don't inherit tags.
- `FishingShips` has a `ROD_EARLY` entry: it opens the ROD second slot with no module. Either ship can hold the slot without undoing what the other provides.
- `getDroneCount` adds +1 while the early Reliquary is aboard.
- Nothing grants it yet, so this commit has no Changelog entry.
- Release packaging now ships `.variant` (5.1) and `.skin` files.

**Checks**
- `tools/FighterStoreChecks`: cap, restoration, launch grouping, return/loss, launch rule, refit revert.
- `tools/FishingShipChecks`: extended for the two-ships-one-rig rules.

**Docs**
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`: new rows, registration, load order.
- `UI.md`: status lines, refit swap, tooltip and panel contracts.
- `COMBAT_SHIPS.md`: steps ticked, corrections.
- `FISHERMAN_CHAIN.md`: early Reliquary paragraph.
- `RELEASE.md` and the Changelog.

**Player-facing text that has not had an Editor pass:**
- the Salvage Launch name, description and HUD text ("NO FIGHTERS READY", "%d READY");
- the status lines;
- the tooltip lines;
- the panel's button name, tooltip, heading, row states, buttons and footer;
- the new setting's name and description.

## Validation

**Compile gate** on the exact remote revision `f4a940ecb2f576aac193f38b700a7f85edeac54a`:
- Command: `git archive` of `jars/src` into a clean directory, then `javac --release 17 -encoding UTF-8 -cp <starfarer.api, Graphics, LazyLib, LunaLib, MagicLib, lwjgl, lwjgl_util, json, log4j, lw_Console> -d <empty out> @src.txt`.
- Java: OpenJDK 17.0.20.1.
- Result: 425 files, exit 0, no errors. The Console Commands classes were compiled.

**Checks passed:**
- FighterStoreChecks, SalvageChecks, FishingShipChecks (479);
- FishingParityChecks, DroneSteeringCheck, AbilityTooltipCheck (1292);
- TugAIChecks, TetherChecks;
- PlayerSettingsChecks (1627), ReleaseBuildChecks (68).

## Not tested in game

**The refit swap is the main risk.** No game is available here, so the plan's spike was not run. Please check:
- the spec `clone()` works;
- the stored wings show as locked bays on the *first* ship shown;
- a field refit (away from a dock) charges no CR;
- discarding updates the bays;
- closing the refit leaves the ship normal;
- restoring D-mods keeps the bays.

If anything goes wrong, the log says so and the tooltip still lists the store.

**Also to try:**
- Salvage in one battle, check restoration progress, then launch in the next battle.
- Recovered fighters come back to rearm and go back into the store.
- Destroyed recovered fighters leave no wrecks and are gone.
- Launched wings don't appear as deployed ships or cost DP.
- The status lines show in combat.
- The discard panel works.
- The early Reliquary (spawn it by console) gives the ROD rig a second slot and one extra drone, but no Reployment Bays.

Visible change: `from urwidtrees import *` no longer brings in the submodule names `decoration`, `nested`, `tree`, `version` and `widgets`. The classes, `urwidtrees.__version__` and imports such as `from urwidtrees.widgets import TreeBox` are unchanged. `docs/examples` is not linted.

Best merged after the `bump-actions` PR, so that both jobs use the same checkout version.

## Review findings and resolution

**review-correctness**: nothing that must change.
- The smaller star-import surface. Stated above.
- The lint job uses checkout v7 while the test job uses v4 until `bump-actions` is merged. Stated above.
- A local unpinned ruff with a user configuration reports more. Left; CI is pinned, and adding a project ruff config is optional.

**review-design**:
- Must change: an unpinned `pipx run ruff` takes the latest ruff, which reports 24 findings today, so the job would fail on its first run. Fixed by pinning `ruff==0.15.4`.

author: martin-janci
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes one bug and makes six simplifications in code from #1008, #1010, #1011 and #1014. Apart from the bug fix, nothing users can see changes.

### Bug: Toolkit's access notice could disappear (#1008)

**Before:** `Toolkit.svelte` runs `check()` again every time the hub status changes. If an earlier check was still waiting on `loadCatalogConfig()` when the hub went unavailable, the newer check set `access = 'unavailable'`. The earlier check then finished and overwrote it with `'unknown'`. The notice disappeared, and Add and Sync became clickable again.

**After:** only the latest check may set `access`. This uses the same sequence guard as `ConversationPanel`'s probe. A new test holds the catalog answer back until after the hub goes unavailable, and checks that the notice stays and Sync stays disabled. The test fails against the old component.

### Simplifications (behaviour unchanged)

- **`status_candidate` (`sessions/reconcile.rs`, #1010):** a `Working` pane already returns early, so the stored-`blocked` exception can only match `Idle`. The match now says that. The doc comment also said only `Blocked` takes effect without waiting for an agents pass, which stopped being true; it now matches the code.
- **`planner.rs` (#1011):** `check_merge_waves` and `check_merge_change` each built the plan graph themselves. They now share one module-level `graph_of`.
- **`store/orchestration.rs` (#1011):** `mission_events` and `mission_events_of_kinds` repeated the same `MissionEventRow` mapping. They now share one `event_row` function.
- **fleet agents (#1014):** `runner.rs`'s `SCAN_MAX_JOBS` duplicated `definition.rs`'s `MAX_SCAN_JOBS`; both are 10. The runner now uses the one constant.
- **`handle_stop_for_worker` (`tasks.rs`, #1011):** a loop stopped a task being added to the finished list twice. But one list holds open tasks and the other holds done runs, both read under one lock, so they never share a task. The loop is now a plain `extend`.
- **assets (#1008):** `toolkit_skills.ts`, `AssetList.svelte` and `assets_inbox.ts` each tested for a fleet-internal asset. They now share one `isInternal()` from `assets.ts`.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo fleet-lint` (clippy, `-D warnings`) are clean, after merging `main`.
- `cargo fleet-test` passes for the touched modules, 0 failures: `sessions::`, `orchestrate::`, `fleet_agents::`, `service::tasks`, `reconcile_tests`, `hooks::`, `work::`, `task_report`, `decide::` and `store::orchestration`.
- `pnpm check` reports 0 errors. The pre-commit hook ran `scripts/ci-local.sh --frontend-only` and every check passed: the full vitest suite (547 files, 8,707 tests) and the build.
- `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` is clean once `main`'s zod/undici override is merged in.

Fixes #35
Head: 718b0ffb4e4988b535c0391d5395590ced513ef6

Gestures has proofs in `src/classify.bats` (8 lemmas) and `src/pointer.bats` (7 lemmas); its other modules have none. No signature changed.

## Evidence

Setup: compiler built from `bootstrap/c` at gestures' `.github/bats-version` (8bdd8b2); repository at the pinned `.github/repository-version` (27c4400); quire's checker from a fresh clone of bats-lang/quire.

### Which solver CI runs

`package-check.yml` (pinned 27c4400 in `check.yml`) calls `bats-lang/bats/.github/actions/setup@8e978dfe7fac83726730361329c91b0e829beaad`. That action's header says it installs libgmp-dev and then, by bats itself, "the GMP build of ATS2 (bats ats2 install)" (step `Install ATS2 (patsopt)`: `run: bats ats2 install`), "the constraint solver does infinite-precision arithmetic". So CI runs the GMP solver, and the GMP run below is the CI run (HOME=/home/user/gmp-438-home, whose patsopt links libgmp.so.10; the default `/root/.bats` build does not). A fixture that CI's solver accepted would show as a red `tests/static` run (`FAIL reject/NAME: should be rejected`); it cannot here, because both fixtures are rejected by the GMP solver (below). They are also rejected by the int build, so the result does not depend on the solver.

### Why CI was red at 07ce01f, and the fix

Run 40129422466 stopped at `error: working tree is dirty (commit or stash changes before upload)` right after the 17 `expect_test.py` tests. Root cause: my `git add -A` had committed `tests/static/__pycache__/expect.cpython-313.pyc`; CI's Python rewrote that tracked file, so the `bats upload` inside `run.sh` saw a modified tree. (`-I` also ignores `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, so the variable I had set did nothing.) Before the fix, in a clean clone of 07ce01f:

```
$ python3 -I tests/static/expect_test.py >/dev/null 2>&1; git status --porcelain
 M tests/static/__pycache__/expect.cpython-313.pyc
```

Fix at 718b0ff: the pyc is untracked, `__pycache__/` is in `.gitignore` (as in sha256's), and `run.sh` runs both scripts with `python3 -B -I`. After, in a clean clone of 718b0ff, the same command leaves `git status --porcelain` empty and `git ls-files | grep -c pycache` prints 0.

The CI sequence of `package-check.yml` at the pinned commit (bats check, bats test, tests/static/run.sh, whose upload is the dirty-tree check) at the new head, in the working checkout:

```
$ bats check --repository REPO
check passed (library)
$ bats test --repository REPO
no tests found
$ tests/static/run.sh REPO
.................

$ git status --porcelain

```

author: kacper-serewis
body:
## Summary

- **Panels switch together.** Each panel used to send frames independently, so some lagged a frame behind. The new `FrameSender` has every panel upload its tile, then wait up to 250 ms for the panels uploading the same frame before sending the validation, so the wall changes as one picture.
- **A slow panel can't stall the wall.** Logging showed that a panel which waits too long between frame ack and validation answers `05 00 01 80 03` and ignores the next handshake, so the wait is capped and the handshake-ack timeout is lowered from 5 s to 1.5 s.
- **Stable code signing.** `build-app.sh` signs with the first "Apple Development" identity (override with `SIGN_IDENTITY`). Ad-hoc signatures change on every build, which made macOS forget the app's permissions.
- Uploads and panel notifications are logged at debug level (`log stream --level debug --predicate 'subsystem == "nl.serewis.bklight"'`).

## Testing

- `swift build`, `swift test`
- Ran against the 4-panel wall: ~1.3 frames/s per panel over 40 s with one recovered timeout, versus repeated 5 s stalls before.

## What changed
`tools/build-host.py` now adds `?v=<sha1 of the file, 10 chars>` to every `js/` and `css/` link in the packaged index.html. spindecks.app caches the game's scripts in the browser for 4 hours, so without this an update could take hours to reach players.

This is deployed in fin6490/Tools as the High Roller cache-busting PR.

body:
Fourth layer of W42, on top of #307: T3's scripts menu in the chat header, its "Add Action" dialog, `t3.json` imports, shortcuts and `scripts.run`.

Decisions: **D1471** (a script's `previewUrl`, `autoOpenPreview`, T3's helpers), **D1472** (`scripts.run`), **D1473** (the scripts control), **D1474** (the "Add Action" dialog), **D1475** (`script.<id>.run`). Opening the preview at a script's URL (D1480) and `runOnSettle` (D1476) are the next layers.

## Summary

```text
jhin.source-control
  scripts.run { threadId, scriptId } (terminals.write) → { terminalId }
    terminal script-<id> in the thread's worktree, else the project's folder
    a busy one (a program running, or another folder) → script-<id>-2, -3, …
    typed: export JHIN_PROJECT_ROOT=…; [export JHIN_WORKTREE_PATH=…;] <command>   (posix / fish / PowerShell)

jhin.project-scripts (new client plugin)
  chat.header.actions  jhin.project-scripts.control  (order -110, before the git actions)
    no scripts:     [+ Add action]          t3.json only: [🔧 Actions ▾]
    scripts:        [▶ Greet | ▾ Script actions]
                        Greet  ⌃⌥G  ⚙ Edit Greet
                        ── From t3.json ──  Lint ⤓

author: giovaniif
body:
Closes #912

## Root cause

The desktop window shows one machine: the selected machine, which is This Mac after each start. The first run (12c) and New mate post the mate to the machine of the pick (the server over SSH). Then they only set `#/mates/<name>`. The mate page and the Mates home read the stream of the machine in view (This Mac), which has no mates. Thus:

1. The mate page shows "There is no mate ada-lovelace." The mate is on the server.
2. The home shows the first run (12a) again, because This Mac has 0 mates.
3. A restart always opens This Mac, because `machines.json` did not keep the selected machine (ADR 0063 dropped it). The server login stays, but the window does not open it.

The missing `~/.crew/mates/<id>` dir is normal. The daemon makes it at the first conversation.

## Fix

- `crew_server_open {id, route}`: opens the machine at a `#/…` route (`servers::routed`).
- `Servers.show(key, route)`: when the machine of the new mate is not the machine in view, the first run and New mate open that machine at the mate page. Else they only set the hash.
- `machines.json` keeps `selected` (not for This Mac). The start code already opens the selected machine. ADR 0063 and `desktop/AGENTS.md` are updated.
- verify: `iso up --second` gives the devbox login its device (before, the devbox page showed Add to Home Screen), and `app drive` follows the new window when the app opens a machine. New recipe in `features/environments.md`: new mate on devbox → mate page → home → app restart.

## Repro (base, real app, `iso up --second`, New mate on devbox)

Same cause as the SSH first run. The verify harness cannot SSH, so the repro uses the `url` machine devbox.

| Mate page after Create | Home after that |
|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giovaniif/crew/21c3db9a29fec55fd617414c8486207bf2660324/912/app-base-mate-page.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giovaniif/crew/21c3db9a29fec55fd617414c8486207bf2660324/912/app-base-home.png) |

## Fix (head, real app)

| Mate page after Create | Home | After an app restart |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giovaniif/crew/21c3db9a29fec55fd617414c8486207bf2660324/912/app-remote-mate-page.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giovaniif/crew/21c3db9a29fec55fd617414c8486207bf2660324/912/app-remote-mate-home.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giovaniif/crew/21c3db9a29fec55fd617414c8486207bf2660324/912/app-remote-mate-restart.png) |

## Validate

- `cd web && npx vitest run`: 59 files, 875 tests pass. New: FirstMate (SSH create opens `ssh:devbox` at `#/mates/test-ada`; This Mac create does not reopen), NewMate (same two).
- `cargo test` in `desktop/src-tauri`: all pass. New: `a_machine_opens_at_the_route_that_the_page_asked_for`, the store keeps the selected machine.
- `go test ./scripts/verify/`: ok.

## Notes

- The page of an SSH machine gets no server IPC (ADR 0059 security), so in that window the hub features (Environments of other machines) are limited, as for any opened server today. A hub-wide home and mate page (all machines in one window) is the long-term design. This PR is the minimal fix.

author: lazyalexander
body:
## Problem and result

The log-report acceptance previously simulated a workbook edit with Python. This change adds a staged, optional operator harness and evidence from **two real LibreOffice GUI edits and XLSX saves**. The host commits v2 and v3, then generates an editable three-slide PPT from explicitly pinned v2 after v3 exists. The PPT contains v2's note, excludes v3's, and records the v2 input revision. Settled scratch is reclaimed while all formal workbook versions remain readable.

Stacks on #5 (still unmerged); uses the existing host revision from lazyalexander/an-agent#102. No host/core changes or new execution backend. Please review and merge; this PR is not auto-merged.

## Responsibility boundaries

- The independent CLI kit retains its existing document adapters and requirements.
- A replaceable, trusted desktop operator performs actual UI editing/saving; this is not an untrusted coding-agent sandbox or a new shuttle ABI.
- an-agent owns approved-byte revision custody, fixed input bindings and settled scratch reclamation.
- Loom packages the explicit source allowlist. psutil/matplotlib are optional operator observation dependencies, not Loom or host runtime dependencies.

## Evidence and limits

`examples/log-report/acceptance/native-office/` contains portable acceptance, measured action sequence, lifecycle and CPU/RSS plots, raw samples and limitations. Native documents remain local to avoid publishing editor-added personal metadata. GUI steps were directly observed and read-only validation inspected the actual saved bytes; producer properties corroborate LibreOffice but do not authenticate a human author.

The trace retains a failed file-dialog attempt and operator-assisted restart. The working copy was relocated unchanged to a visible dedicated temporary directory before successful GUI editing. A `/tmp` symlink submission was explicitly refused; the canonical path succeeded without relaxing the gate. A separate expired initial-launch capture is excluded. UI timing includes tool/operator waits and is not a performance benchmark. Process/document/scratch/artifact lifecycles do not demonstrate VM/spool hot-loading. RSS and CPU are sampled, may miss short processes/bursts, and are not energy or system-wide measurements.

## Validation

- Real macOS ARM64 LibreOffice 26.8.1 GUI saves, approved v2/v3 commits, fixed-v2 PPT generation, provenance checks and scratch/formal-artifact read-back: PASS.
- Three domain tests and four negative observation qualification tests: PASS. The latter refuse expired captures, missing editor observations and a restarted editor still running after an earlier exit, and inaccessible measurements being misclassified as unload.
- cargo fmt, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo quality --base origin/main, isolated quality-tool tests: PASS.
- Example check/build/pack: PASS. CI adds only observation-gate fixture tests; it does not claim a real GUI run.

body:
Closes #580

## Tóm tắt
- **Cache theo loại (server)** `server/src/staticCache.ts`: `/assets/*-<hash>.*` immutable 1 năm; `index.html` no-cache (ETag giữ); asset không hash có `?v=` thì immutable 1 năm, không có `?v=` thì ảnh / âm thanh 7 ngày + stale-while-revalidate, json no-cache. Lý do chọn `?v=<hash nội dung shared/assets>` (tính trong `vite.config.ts`, `__ASSET_V__`): một hằng duy nhất, không phải sinh bản sao có hash của hàng nghìn file, và chỉ đổi khi asset thật sự đổi. Chỗ để C5 (#556) cắm atlas: mọi URL đi qua `assetUrl()`.
- **Client tải bền**: `assetUrl.ts` (URL có phiên bản, `fetchAsset`, `loadImageRetry`), `loaderRetry.ts` (Phaser: thử lại cả 5xx / 408 / 429, mà Phaser mặc định bỏ qua, có backoff 0,4 / 1,2 / 3,6 / 8 / 8 giây), `maxParallelDownloads` 12; `lpcRig.ts` có hàng đợi tải riêng (cùng mức), thử lại, và tải lại sheet lỗi hẳn sau 30 giây rồi ghép lại tổ hợp; âm thanh, manifest giao diện, minimap, xem trước LPC cũng dùng.
- **Nén**: Cloudflare đã nén br cho HTML / JS / JSON (kiểm bằng curl trên prod) → không thêm `compression` ở origin.
- **Chia bundle**: Phaser thành chunk riêng (JS chính 2,47 MB → 0,99 MB + Phaser 1,48 MB; đổi code game không tải lại Phaser).
- **Thử lỗi**: `GAME_TEST=1 ASSET_FAIL_RATE=0.3` trả 504 ngẫu nhiên cho request png / json / ogg / m4a.
- Tài liệu: `docs/deploy.md` mục "Cache tài sản tĩnh và Cloudflare" (Cache Rules, Browser TTL "Respect existing headers", bỏ qua `/api`, `/matchmake`).

## Đo (Chrome headless, localhost, vào Thánh Hồn Thôn, tài khoản LPC; so với `origin/main`)
| | main | PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lần 1: request / byte mạng | 616 / 13,39 MB | 617 / 13,40 MB |
| Lần 2 (cache từ lần 1): byte mạng | 0,20 MB (598 request revalidate về server + 18 × 304) | 0 MB, request tới mạng gần như bằng 0 (600 từ cache; 16 còn lại là bộ nhớ đệm / tệp vào trang) |
| Thời gian vào game sau bấm #go (lần 1 / 2) | ~12,5–13,6 s / ~8,9–10,2 s | ~14,1 s / ~9,3–9,9 s |
Thời gian vào game ở máy là CPU / giải mã ~600 texture nên gần như không đổi; lợi ích là số vòng revalidate qua Cloudflare → ingress → pod (616 → ~0) trên prod.
- **Chặn 30% request** (504): bản main hỏng ~175 file vĩnh viễn (`load.totalFailed` 175); PR với 5 lần thử lại: 266 phản hồi 504 được hấp thụ, `totalFailed` 0–1 ở lần đầu (xác suất còn lại ~0,07% mỗi file), lần 2 = 0, đủ 870 texture. Thử trước khi có sửa onLoad cho 5xx: `totalFailed` 175 (Phaser không thử lại 504).

`npm run check`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:static-cache --prefix server` (mới), `test:audio`, `test:predict`, bot:local looks3 + cold (xem bình luận), không dùng DB thật.

author: thomashendrickx
body:
## Summary

The trierarch plugin holds the one list of trusted repositories (aeolus-fleet#384, as Thomas decided: one list in the trierarch plugin, true across all trierarchs, no core change). It sends the whole list to every trierarch. A crew request names a trusted repository by its name as `workspace.repository`, so common's crew settings and core do not change.

```
TRUSTED_REPOSITORIES='{"hemma":"git@github.com:ThomasHendrickx/hemma.git"}'
  loadConfig -> readTrustedRepositories   # refuses: a name that is a path, http, file://, a path, ext::,
                                          # a user on https (a token), an ssh password, a user or host
                                          # starting with -, a list over one 64 KB message
every pass, per fleet:
  label -> declare rules -> declare scopes
  -> shareTrustedRepositories             # new
       for each trierarch ship not retired, not yet sent by this process:
         ship/send application/vnd.aeolus.trierarch.trusted-repositories+json
                   {"repositories":[{"name":"hemma","url":"git@github.com:..."}]}
  -> assign crews                         # unchanged: a trierarch that can clone reports the names

machines.join setup line:
- npx @aeolus-fleet/trierarch init --fleet-url <url> --ship-id <id> --secret <secret>
+ npx @aeolus-fleet/trierarch init --fleet-url <url> --ship-id <id> --plugin-ship-id <its own ship> --secret <secret>
```

A trierarch holds only `crew:run`, so it cannot read a sender's kind, and a ship's type is any ship's to pick. The setup line therefore names the trierarch plugin's own ship, and the trierarch takes the list from that ship id alone.

`ship/send` is already in compatibility.md for the trierarch plugin, so `MINIMUM_CORE_VERSION` stays. An empty list is sent too, so a trierarch drops what left the list. A restart sends the list to every trierarch again under a new idempotency key, which is how a changed list arrives. A refused send waits for the next pass. The trierarch side (take the list from that ship only, offer the names, clone on demand with the machine's own access, trust the clone) is the companion PR, ThomasHendrickx/aeolus-fleet-trierarch#18.

## Evidence

Red, then green, by name:

- `trusted-repositories.test.ts`: 24 tests, including `refuses a remote helper that runs a command`, `refuses an https URL with a token as its user`, `refuses an ssh URL whose user reads as an option` and `refuses a list that does not fit one message`.
- `share-trusted-repositories.test.ts`: `sends the list to every trierarch`, `sends an empty list too, so a trierarch stops trusting what left it`, `sends a trierarch the list once across passes`, `sends a trierarch that joins later the list on the next pass`, `sends every trierarch the list again after a restart of the trierarch plugin, under a new key`, `sends nothing to a retired trierarch or a ship of another type`, `sends a trierarch whose send was refused the list again on the next pass, and the others meanwhile`, and the two refusals.
- `join-machine.test.ts`: `answers its starting prompt as the fleet issued it, and a setup line for the machine built from its fields, naming the trierarch plugin's ship the trusted repositories come from`, and against a real fleet `a machine joining > commissions a ship of type trierarch ... and answers its starting prompt and setup line`.
- `config.test.ts`: `reads the trusted repositories as JSON of names to git URLs`, `refuses trusted repositories that are not JSON`, `refuses a trusted repository whose URL holds a credential`.
- Against a real fleet, `the trusted repositories against a real fleet (aeolus-fleet#384) > a pass sends a joined trierarch the trusted repositories once, as the trierarch plugin's ship` first failed with `expected [] to deeply equal [ { …(3) } ]`, and passes now.

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm test` (39 files, 455 tests) are green.

## Walk

A person sees this only together with the trierarch side, when a request is crewed in a repository the machine never had. The Walk is in ThomasHendrickx/aeolus-fleet-trierarch#18.

## Merge danger

- Door: two-way. Unset, `TRUSTED_REPOSITORIES` is an empty list. Each trierarch gets one small message per plugin start, and a trierarch before the companion PR acks it as one it does not handle. The new setup line needs a trierarch that knows `--plugin-ship-id` (the companion PR): release both on the same 0.31.0 train, since `npx @aeolus-fleet/trierarch` takes the latest.
- Machines joined before take no list until their operator runs `aeolus-trierarch init --plugin-ship-id <id>` once (fine before 1.0).
- Blast radius: small. A wrong list only changes what trierarchs may clone, and every URL is checked at start.

Part of ThomasHendrickx/aeolus-fleet#384 (closed by ThomasHendrickx/aeolus-fleet-trierarch#18).

author: banditf
body:
Test lab found that a rebuilt 0.1.0 MSI installs next to the existing one.

**Fix:** `<MajorUpgrade AllowSameVersionUpgrades="yes" …/>` in `app/wix/main.wxs`.
- The product code is `*`, so it changes with every build. Without this, MSI treats a same-version build as a different product.
- **ICE61** warns about `AllowSameVersionUpgrades`. That's expected and accepted: Foxglove is one product line, so a same-version MSI is always a rebuild of it. A comment in `main.wxs` says so. It's a warning, not an error, and the build doesn't fail on it.

**Throwaway test builds:** the app workflow gets an optional `workflow_dispatch` input, `test_version`.
- The exe's Cargo version and the MSI version are both set to it.
- The artifact is named `foxglove-windows-<version>-test`.
- The release job still runs only on `app-v*` tags. No tag or release is created.

**Runs on this branch**
- [40134329689](https://github.com/BanditF/foxglove/actions/runs/40134329689), with `test_version=0.1.1`: the throwaway **0.1.1-test** MSI for On-call's #90 upgrade and downgrade steps (artifact `foxglove-windows-0.1.1-test`).
- [40134337051](https://github.com/BanditF/foxglove/actions/runs/40134337051): the plain 0.1.0 build with the fix.
- Both linux jobs pass. The windows jobs are still running; I'll post the results here.

**Not checked here:** installing a same-version rebuild over 0.1.0, then upgrading to 0.1.1 and downgrading from it. That's the #90 MSI row.

I'll forward-port this to main with the same workflow input.

author: renee77
body:
## Why

The Kotlin Toolchain has no built-in coverage. Its `jacoco-maven-plugin` support attaches
the JaCoCo agent to the test JVM and renders an HTML report, so we can measure NFR-03
from the command line.

## How to use

    ./kotlin task :server:jacoco-maven-plugin.report

- HTML report: `build/maven-target/reports/jacoco/index.html`
- IntelliJ: Run → Show Coverage Data… (Ctrl+Alt+F6) → + → `build/maven-target/jacoco.exec`

## Good to know

- The agent also runs on a plain `./kotlin test`.
- `jacoco.exec` is appended on every run; the toolchain rejects the `append` parameter.
  Delete the file first for a measurement of only the latest run.
- The report path is relative to `server/`, because the toolchain does not resolve
  `${project.reporting.outputDirectory}` and does not support references in `module.yaml`.

## Verification

- `./kotlin task :server:jacoco-maven-plugin.report`: 647/647 tests pass, report generated.
- `./kotlin test`: 647/647 tests pass.
- First measurement: 98.1% line coverage in total, 95.7% for the service layer (NFR-03: ≥ 80%).

Follow-up to #536 after the reopen. The blank project page did not reproduce on the current prod build (all project entry points, cold and in-app, show the skeleton then the project; no API errors in 24 h of access logs). The most likely cause is a tab or desktop window opened before the 20:29 deploy, still running the bundle from before #536 with no error boundary. Nothing moved an open tab onto a new build, so the first import of a pruned chunk blanked it. Evidence and what was ruled out are on STUP-377.

author: madhusuthanan-b
body:
## Summary

Two things:

1. **A working link to the interactive explorer, today.** GitHub Pages isn't enabled yet, so the README now links through [raw.githack](https://raw.githack.com/Madhusuthanan-B/compiledmind-radar/main/explorer/index.html). It serves files from this public repo with the right content types, so the page and its `radar.js` load without any setup. The Pages URL stays as a secondary link for when it's turned on.
2. **A `radar-explorer` skill** that keeps the explorer up to date every time a new signal (OKF note) is captured or changed, and ships it as a merged PR.

## The skill (`.claude/skills/radar-explorer/SKILL.md`)

Triggers on: a new signal captured, a verdict or experience change, a note renamed, moved or deleted, changed links, or a request to update or check the explorer. Steps:

1. Check the note's frontmatter: title, description, one verdict tag, topic tags, experience, capture date. Links must be relative Markdown links.
2. Add `## Related` links and backlinks, so the explorer can draw both directions.
3. Run `python tools/build-radar.py` (chart SVGs, README stamps, `explorer/radar.js`), then the `radar-chart` skill for the README table.
4. Run `node tools/explorer-snapshot.js` to check the explorer.
5. When the picture changes, retake the README screenshots with `--shots` and look at them.
6. Commit everything together on a `signal/…` branch, open a PR with a clear title and description, and merge to main.
7. Report the explorer link, PR link, signal count and whether screenshots were retaken.

The `radar-chart` skill now hands over to this one.

## The check script (`tools/explorer-snapshot.js`)

- **Data checks:** fails on links to missing notes, a map or panel count that differs from the data, page errors, or sideways scrolling, in both light and dark.
- **`--shots`:** retakes `assets/explorer-{light,dark}.png` at 1440×860 (2×) with a chosen signal selected (`--focus`, default `agent-loop`).
- **`EXPLORER_LIBS=<node_modules>`:** serves the pinned libraries and the repo's own fonts locally when the CDN can't be reached. That is how it was run here: 25 signals, 174 links, ok. The retaken screenshots match the previous ones.

## Changes

- `.claude/skills/radar-explorer/SKILL.md`: new skill.
- `tools/explorer-snapshot.js`: new check and screenshot script.
- `.claude/skills/radar-chart/SKILL.md`: points to the new skill.
- `README.md`, `knowledge/README.md`: the explorer links now use raw.githack, with Pages as the secondary link.
- `assets/explorer-*.png`: retaken by the new script; visually the same as before.

author: starpit
body:
Part of #863.

| `e_spans bench_first_ttft_spans_overhead`, SmolLM2-135M on an M5 | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| default lengths | 2048, 8192, 16384 | 2048, 8176 |
| result | fails at 8192: `prompt is 8192 tokens but this model serves at most 8192` | passes: 118.3 / 120.7 ms at 2048 (without / with spans), 608.6 / 597.7 ms at 8176 |

- **Wrong:** the bench ran its default lengths whatever the model served. SmolLM2 serves 8192 tokens, so the 8192-token prompt, with no room for its one decode token, was refused, and 16384 would have been too.
- **Fix:** a default length past the context runs at the longest prompt the model serves: whole 16-token blocks, one decode token short of `max_model_len` (8176 on SmolLM2). The clamped lengths are deduplicated. An explicit `SPANS_TTFT_LENS` is run as asked. The comments that put SmolLM's context at 2048 now say SmolLM2's 8192.
- **Checked:** the bench passes on an M5 with #864's `SMOLLM` applied locally (not part of this PR). clippy `-D warnings` and rustfmt are clean.

author: leonardosantos16
body:
## Contexto

O `opportunities.service.ts` tinha mais de 500 linhas e misturava os 9 casos de uso, queries Prisma, regra de listagem, visibilidade e criação de erros. O controller carregava todos os schemas zod. Este PR reorganiza a camada de aplicação sem mudar o comportamento da API: os testes de rota, que passam pela API com banco real, seguem iguais e verdes.

## O que muda

- **Erros em classes**: `AppError` virou abstrata, com subclasses por caso (`OpportunityNotFoundError`, `FinalStageError`, `StageConflictError`, `InvalidTransitionError`, `MissingValueOrItemsError`, `ForbiddenError`, `ValidationError`...). Não sobrou nenhum `new AppError(status, code, ...)` espalhado.
- **Schemas zod** saíram do controller para `src/schemas/`.
- **Regras do board no domínio**: filtro por janela de 30 dias, busca sem acento, situação, ordenação e `needsAttention` agora estão em `domain/board.ts`, como função pura com testes unitários.
- **Repositórios atrás de interfaces**: `OpportunityRepository` (separado em `Reader` e `Writer`), `CompanyRepository`, `UserRepository` e `HealthRepository`, com implementações Prisma em `repositories/prisma/`. Um `UnitOfWork` entrega os repositórios ligados à transação, então o Prisma não aparece fora dessa pasta.
- **Tipos e DTOs**: os tipos de dados ficam em `src/types/`. Os DTOs de request vêm de `z.infer` sobre os schemas, e os de response tipam o presenter (`src/presenters/`) e o retorno de cada use case.
- **Use cases em classes**: uma classe por caso de uso, com `execute` e dependências recebidas pelo construtor. `OpportunityActionRunner` concentra o fluxo comum: carregar a oportunidade visível, barrar etapa final, executar na transação e recarregar o detalhe. A pasta `services/` foi removida.
- **Controllers em classes**, montados em `src/container.ts`, que é o único ponto que instancia as implementações Prisma. `createApp` aceita `{ clock, prisma }`.

## Decisões

- As linhas retornadas pelos repositórios usam os tipos de payload do Prisma, isolados em `types/opportunity-rows.types.ts`. Mapear para entidades próprias seria o "DDD completo" que o ADR 0001 rejeitou.
- `changeStage` lança `StageConflictError` dentro do repositório, porque é detecção de conflito de concorrência (update condicional à etapa de origem).
- Sem container de injeção de dependência, já que a montagem manual no `container.ts` basta para este tamanho.
- `domain/` continua em funções puras.

## Testes

- Os testes de rota não mudaram.
- Novos testes unitários, sem banco:
  - `domain/board`: 9 casos.
  - Use cases com repositórios mockados: 7 casos, cobrindo `OpportunityActionRunner`, `MoveOpportunityUseCase` e `CreateOpportunityUseCase`.
- Testes adaptados à nova estrutura, com a mesma cobertura:
  - o antigo `visibility.test.ts` agora testa `PrismaOpportunityRepository`;
  - o teste de `STAGE_CONFLICT` usa `UnitOfWork` + `changeStage`;
  - o teste de identidade monta `requireUser` com o use case.
- `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` foi desligada só em `tests/`, porque dá falso positivo com mocks do vitest.

author: rudycelekli
body:
The backend-service pattern in the Cursor SDK skill exposes `POST /agents/:userId/send` and starts a cloud agent with `CURSOR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` on every request that reaches it. It never checks who sent the request. Anyone who can reach the port can send any prompt against the team's workspace repository and spend the service account's usage. Because `userId` comes straight from the URL, a caller can also resume another user's durable agent and read its conversation through follow-ups. The pattern is meant to be copied into a real service, and as written it ships an open proxy for the team's key.

The route now reads a bearer token and resolves it through a `sessionUsers` map. That map is a placeholder for the app's login or session store, in the same way `userAgents` stands in for the database. The route returns `401` before any SDK call unless the token belongs to the `userId` in the path. The "Why this shape" notes gain one line explaining the check, and the rest of the handler is unchanged.

Validation: the new `cursor-sdk/tests/backend-auth.test.cjs` extracts the documented route and runs it against mocked `express` and `@cursor/sdk` modules. On `origin/main`, a request with no credentials gets `200` and starts an agent, and the other two cases throw `ReferenceError` because there is no caller check yet. After this change, a request with no credentials and a request using another user's token both return `401` without creating an agent, and the owner's token still runs the agent. The test needs Node 24 for `await using`, so I ran it with `npx -y node@24 --test cursor-sdk/tests/backend-auth.test.cjs`. I also ran `node scripts/validate-plugins.mjs` (with `ajv` and `ajv-formats` installed), `node scripts/generate-pstack-harness-trees.mjs --check` and `git diff --check`, and all three pass.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation and example-pattern hardening plus regression tests; no production service code paths change in this repo.
> 
> **Overview**
> The **backend service** example in `patterns.md` now requires a **Bearer token** and checks it against a `sessionUsers` stand-in before any agent create/resume or SDK spend. Missing or mismatched credentials return **401** and never touch the service account key.
> 
> The “Why this shape” section calls out that ownership of `:userId` must be verified because the route runs arbitrary prompts on shared infrastructure.
> 
> **`backend-auth.test.cjs`** pulls the documented Express handler out of the markdown, runs it in a VM with mocked Express/SDK, and asserts: no auth → 401 with zero agents; another user’s token → 401; owner’s token → 200 and one agent run.
>

author: whiteflight
body:
# Description

Replaces `http-request-mock` with [MSW](https://mswjs.io) (Mock Service Worker) for the mocked backend in the demo app.
`http-request-mock` was last released in October 2024 and has about 15 thousand weekly downloads. MSW is actively released and has about 14 million.

- `apps/web/src/mock-setup.js` is now `mock-setup.ts`, with typed MSW handlers for the same services (`SokAdress`, `SokPerson`, `TestData`, `SokOrganisation`, `SokBolagsEngagemang`, `SokKonton`) and the same 750 ms delay.
- `index.tsx` waits for the worker to start before rendering, since MSW starts asynchronously. Requests with no handler (config files, plugins) pass through.
- `apps/web/public/mockServiceWorker.js` is the worker file generated by `msw init`. It is MIT-licensed and must not be edited, so its licence is recorded in `REUSE.toml` and `LICENSES/MIT.txt` is added. It has to match the installed `msw` version, so regenerate it with `msw init` when `msw` is upgraded.
- `http-request-mock` is removed from `react-mla`, where nothing imported it (it was only used by the demo).
- The `uuid` pnpm override is removed. It was needed because `http-request-mock` pulled in `@ngneat/falso` and the vulnerable `uuid` 8. `uuid` now resolves only to 14.0.3 through `vis-data` and `vis-network`, and `pnpm audit` is clean.
- The unused `SokRelation` mock is removed. No config calls it and its handler used a data file that was never imported.
- The lockfile drops 9 packages.

The service worker is only loaded by the demo app. It is not part of the published `react-mla` or web component packages.

Verification: `tsc` passes in `react-mla`, `web` and `webcomponent-mla`, ESLint passes, the unit tests pass, a frozen install passes under the default age policy, and the REUSE linter reports 235 of 235 files compliant. In Chromium against both the dev server and a production build with `vite preview`, the service worker controls the page on first load, the person and company searches return mock results, and dragging a result onto the chart works, with no console errors. I did not test the deployed GitHub Pages URL, which is served from the `/mla/` sub-path, so please check the demo after the first deploy.

author: alagbefranc
body:
Migration: yes

Builds the renewal, expiry and fee part of DEC-02 from #182 (spec: `docs/spec/gaps/DEC.md` on the gap branch). The follow-up checklist, conditions summary and delivery record are in the other DEC-02 PR.

## What's built
1. **Renewal reminder / successor — built.**
   - **Who can get one:** only an applicant who uses the portal and has "Remind me before a deadline" on, backed by a granted consent record that is stored on the row.
   - **Otherwise refused:** the database refuses, and the card shows why: no applicant, no portal access, no contact choices saved, or the choice is turned off.
   - **Required:** staff state the scope of the new service (10–2000 characters).
   - **What it creates:** a Pipeline lead tagged `renewal`, never an invoice. A test checks this, and it's audited.
   - **Not offered on sample matters.**
   - **What the client sees:** only "Renewal reminders" on portal Home. No email is sent.
2. **Expiry reminders — built.**
   - Staff enter the expiry date printed on the issued document, from a confirmed approval, and can link the stored file.
   - It creates an internal reminder task.
3. **Renewal timing from official pages — partly built.**
   - **Built: the entry path.** Staff enter a canada.ca or gc.ca timing with:
     - the exact wording from the page;
     - a number of days, only if the page states one;
     - the URL with its section anchor;
     - the form number and its date modified;
     - the date checked and any "current to" date;
     - a page snapshot fetched by the server.
   - **Review:** a licensed member approves with step-up.
   - **Reminder date:** with an approved timing, it's the expiry minus those days. Otherwise staff choose the date, and it reads "Reminder date chosen by the firm". There's no default anywhere.
   - **Not captured:** any timing content, because canada.ca timed out.
4. **Renewal fee shown to the client — built.**
   - Staff pick the fee only from the approved IRCC fee list (FIN-06's `government_fee_references`).
   - The client sees the amount, link and retrieval date only while that fee is still in the currently approved list. Otherwise nothing is shown.

## Migration
`20261025210000_dec_renewal.sql`:
- **New tables:**
  - `renewal_timings`, following GOV-01's `submission_requirements` pattern, with its source in `official_sources` / `source_snapshots`;
  - `decision_renewals`.

  Both have forced RLS. Recorded facts can't be changed (enforced by trigger).
- **New functions:** `propose_`, `review_` and `retire_renewal_timing`, `renewal_contact_state`, `record_issued_expiry`, `set_renewal_reminder`, `cancel_decision_renewal`, `portal_renewal_reminders`, and the helper `app.renewal_current_fee`.
- **No existing function is redefined.** `app.federal_official_url`, `app.matter_program_key`, the `app.gov_*` helpers, `app.create_task`, `app.set_task_status` and `public.create_lead` are reused unchanged.

**One UI change:** this removes the old "Add expiry reminder" quick row from the Decisions view. It set the reminder date to the expiry date by default.

## Test, merge and deploy (@swe)
**Local checks on 3c6c046** (latest main): typegen, tsc, lint (2 known warnings), `check:migrations`, full vitest (242 files, 2,505 passed, 1 skipped), and the build. New tests are in `tests/dec-renewal.rls.test.ts` (5) and `tests/dec-renewal-present.test.tsx` (6).

**Checks on app.casevoya.ca (Test Firm, ON-2026-0008 or another non-sample matter), after the migration and a deploy:**
1. As a licensed consultant, record and confirm an approval, then open `?tab=decisions`. *Pass:* an "Expiry and renewal" card appears with a line about the client's contact choices.
2. Record an expiry: "Study permit", an expiry date, a reminder date, and "The firm's choice". *Pass:* the row shows "Reminder date chosen by the firm", and Tasks has "Renewal review: … expires …" due that day.
3. Record an expiry again with no reminder date. *Pass:* "Choose the reminder date… no date is set for you", and nothing is saved.
4. As the client, turn "Remind me before a deadline" off, then reload as staff. *Pass:* the card says the choice is off, and there's no Set renewal reminder button.
5. As the client, turn it back on. As staff, click Set renewal reminder, enter the scope, pick an approved IRCC fee if there is one, and save. *Pass:*
   - the toast says it's set and nothing was billed;
   - the row shows "Client reminder set" with a link to the lead;
   - the lead is in the Pipeline tagged `renewal`;
   - Billing is unchanged.
6. As the client, open portal Home. *Pass:* "Renewal reminders" shows the document, expiry, review date and scope. The fee, with "IRCC fee list, retrieved <date>", shows only if it's in the approved list.
7. Add an IRCC renewal timing with a canada.ca URL and anchor, then approve it as a licensed consultant with step-up. *Pass:* it's listed with its link, date checked and page hash. If the page couldn't be fetched, the toast says so and Approve isn't offered (see the note below).

**Merge notes:**
- **Overlaps with the other DEC-02 PR:** both change the Decisions tab (`government-present.ts`, `matter-government.tsx`), `use-sheet.ts`, `matter-load.ts`, the portal Home files, `database.types.ts` and the docs. Expect conflicts; keep both sides.
- **Follow-up with #220:** #220 lets a licensed reviewer approve an official entry without a page snapshot, by attestation. Renewal timings here still require a snapshot. Once #220 is merged, I'll align this PR with it so all official entries follow one rule.

**Deploy:** `git checkout main && git pull && pnpm run deploy:app` from a clean checkout (`docs/DEPLOY.md`).

**If a check fails:** comment here with the step number and what you saw.

## Official content
- **Captured:** none. canada.ca timed out. The IRCC fee list and ircc.canada.ca help centre did respond.
- **Left to capture through the new path:**
  - renewal and extension timing for the PR card, study permit, work permit and visitor record, and PR status / CoPR next steps, each with its URL and anchor, form and date modified, and "current to" date;
  - the matching renewal fees, from each firm's approved fee list.

body:
Closes #4.

Applies the decisions from the evaluation trial recorded on #4 (every pending rule run as `'error'` against the design system's `src/` tree, 115 files, with synthetic controls; the typed rules run separately with a typed program).

## Decisions

- **39 rules → `'error'`** in `src/react-pending.ts`, each with its trial result on the entry: the compiler family (purity, immutability, refs, globals, static-components, set-state-in-effect/render, error-boundaries, unsupported-syntax, use-memo), the Children family, clone/context/createRef family, **no-duplicate-key** from the jsx-key family (its sibling **no-implicit-key** is one of the three typed-linting 'off' rules below), JSX leak/key rules, DOM rules, all six `web-api-no-leaked-*` rules, and the three naming-convention rules. 41 of the trialled rules reported **0 findings** on the design system.
- **`immutability` → `'error'`** despite its 4 trial findings: they are a single site (MemorizationSessionPage's `blankOrdinal` render-mutation), filed as spudly/design-system#135 to refactor before `reactPending` is restored. Nothing breaks today — `reactPending` is composed nowhere.
- **3 rules stay `'off'` with a substantive rationale**: `no-implicit-children`, `no-implicit-key`, `no-implicit-ref` require type information. Enabling them was verified to **crash** lint runs without typed parser setup (the restored composition throws on an untyped file), and no consumer runs typed linting today — TS files are ignored pending the typescript-eslint restoration and JS files lint untyped. Their typed trial found 0 findings; they are flagged on their entries for re-evaluation at restoration (#8), when typed linting exists.
- **Hooks source (the issue's adjacent decision)**: `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` stays the source for the classic hooks rules — `@eslint-react/rules-of-hooks` and `exhaustive-deps` stay `'off'`. For the React Compiler diagnostics that exist under both namespaces, the **@eslint-react versions are the single source**; the react-hooks duplicates in `src/react.ts` are now recorded there as `'off'` *by decision* (not undecided), so restoration cannot double-report.
- No undecided entries remain anywhere in the @eslint-react set.

## Tests

- New `test/reactPendingDecisions.test.mjs`: pins all 39 `'error'` severities plus the decided-`'off'` sets, and proves the restored composition (react + reactPending) fires a newly enabled rule (`no-children-map` on `Children.map`) and stays silent on the direct-map equivalent.
- Mutation check: flipping `no-children-map` back to `'off'` fails 2 of the new tests; reverted and re-verified green.
- Full suite locally: 341 tests, 337 pass, 4 skipped, 0 fail. `npm run lint` (dogfood), `prettier:check`, `typecheck`, and `check-rules` (0 deprecated / 0 unknown / 0 missing) all clean.
- Changeset: minor, with the no-consumer-impact note (`reactPending` is still composed nowhere; restoration remains #8).

Note for spudly/eslint-config#13 (open, merge-ready): its per-rule fixture enumeration counts `reactPending` as composed — after this lands, the newly enabled rules are already covered by the enumeration there (they were counted as configured), but its fixture set may want the three `no-implicit-*` severities re-checked against this PR's rationale if it lands second.

author: hectorvent
body:
## Summary

Phase 2b of #350, on top of the merged phases 1 to 3 (only with `FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_COMPUTE_MOCK=false`): container VMs. An instance whose metadata has a `gce-container-declaration` (Terraform `metadata`, `gcloud compute instances create-with-container`) runs the declared container, as konlet does on Container-Optimized OS.

- **Where it runs**: a second container, `<instance container>_klt`, started on every boot after the startup scripts, in the instance container's network (konlet uses the VM's host network). It shares the instance's address, so the metadata server answers it as that instance.
- **What is read** (konlet's YAML keys): `image`, `command` (entrypoint), `args`, `env`, `stdin`, `tty`, `securityContext.privileged`, `restartPolicy` (Always by default, OnFailure, Never), and `emptyDir` with `medium: Memory` as tmpfs.
- **Refusals**: declarations konlet refuses (not exactly one container, unknown restart policy, a mount without its volume, an unused volume, another `emptyDir` medium) are reported with konlet's messages on serial port 1 and start nothing; the instance still runs. `hostPath` and `gcePersistentDisk` volumes are skipped with a serial port line.
- **Lifecycle**: read at boot, so `setMetadata` applies at the next start or reset. Stop and delete remove the container after the shutdown scripts; reset replaces it; after an emulator restart a declared container whose instance is not RUNNING is removed.
- **Serial port 1**: konlet's lines (`konlet-startup[1]: Configured container ...`) and the container's output, one line each.
- Core: `ContainerSpec`/`ContainerBuilder` gain a restart policy, TTY and open STDIN (defaults unchanged for existing callers). `snakeyaml` is already on the classpath through `quarkus-config-yaml`; it is now declared explicitly.

Refs #350

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [x] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`)
- [ ] Docs / chore

## GCP Compatibility

The declaration shape, validation messages and Docker mapping follow konlet's source (`gce-containers-startup/types/api.go`, `runtime/runtime.go`, `volumes/volumes.go`); boot-time reading follows konlet's metadata provider and the "deploying containers" docs; startup scripts first follows the `konlet-startup` unit ordering. Terraform's own acceptance-test declaration parses as expected. Verified with `ComputeContainerDeclarationTest`, `ComputeInstanceRuntimeTest` and a smoke run against a real Docker daemon (20/20: shared network, metadata identity, tmpfs, restart policy, stop, setMetadata then start, reset, delete, invalid declaration). Not compared against live Compute Engine.

## Checklist

- [x] `./mvnw test` passes locally (Compute, Cloud Run, GKE and container core: 513/0)
- [x] New or updated integration test added
- [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I have no more than 2 open, non-draft pull requests and no more than 4 open pull requests in total (drafts included) in this repository (maintainers and dependency bots are exempt).

author: ash1688
body:
Closes #176

## What changes

Every game now opens with an **MVP** build, measured in developer-days.
- **Size** = `mvp.baseDevDays[product] × mvp.modelShare[model]`. Placeholder shares: on-prem 1.0, IaaS 0.85, PaaS 0.65, SaaS 0.40. Placeholder base sizes are e-commerce 22, assistant 24, payments 26, games 26, social 28 and video 30. With the starting two developers that's 11–15 days played on-prem and 4–6 on SaaS.
- **Until it's done:** all developer output goes into it, features can't be started (`mvp_first`), developers are never flagged idle, and there are no users and no growth. Staff are still paid.
- **Launch** happens on the first day the MVP is done and servers can serve users. From then the existing 20/30/50% ramp runs unchanged.
- **Hosting bills start at go-live.** Before the first users arrive, no model running costs, rent, or power and cooling are charged, and the runway leaves them out. On-prem kit can still be bought on day 1 and arrives on day 5, inside the build. Kit is still paid for up front when bought.
- **More developers finish sooner.** Agency developers count at their usual (half) output.
- Time stops with "Your MVP is done".

## Code

- `sim/src/mvp.ts`: a new pure module. Given product, model, progress and developer output, it returns progress, total, days left, estimated launch day and whether it's done. It also plays a day's work on the MVP.
- `launch.ts` waits for the MVP, and its launch-day estimate combines the MVP's day with server readiness. `sim.ts` plays MVP work right after hires arrive and gates hosting bills on go-live. `features.ts` refuses builds before the MVP is done. There's a new `sim.mvp(state)` view.
- New config `mvp.baseDevDays.*` and `mvp.modelShare.*`, with config schema fields (People → MVP). State version bumped to 39 for `state.mvp`.
- Server `CompanyView.mvp`.
- Web:
  - The **features panel** shows an MVP block before launch: a progress bar (developer-days done of the total), days left, and **estimated launch day**. Build buttons are disabled until the MVP is done.
  - Home's launch card gets a "Build your MVP" checklist step and updated copy.
- The text-play status line shows MVP progress (`sim/scripts/textPlay.ts`).
- `CONTEXT.md` adds **MVP** and **Go-live**.

## Tests

- New `sim/test/mvp.test.ts`, written against the public sim API. It covers:
  - 0 users and growth before completion, with salaries paid
  - the ramp after completion
  - size by model (SaaS shortest, on-prem longest) and by product
  - the 10–15 day bound on-prem
  - more and agency developers finishing sooner
  - no developers giving no progress
  - features waiting until the MVP is done
  - the pause
  - hosting bills from go-live, and the runway
  - on-prem kit arriving during the MVP
  - an MVP of no size launching at once
- Existing tests that aren't about the MVP (sim, api, products, shares, textPlay, server) now run with an MVP of no size, so they keep testing what they were written for. A few `sim.test.ts` assertions about pre-launch running costs and power now expect the new go-live rule.
- **Gameplay fingerprints updated (`-u`)**: the MVP changes every default-config game. Launch is later, the early days have no hosting bills, and everything after that shifts.
- e2e: the main e2e server runs with a new optional `GAME_MVP=off` env (documented in the README), because those flows are about play after launch. The timed server keeps the MVP.

Results: sim 784/784, server 232/232 (own test DB), e2e 49/49, web `vue-tsc` and build pass. I also checked the features panel and Home card by hand in a browser against the default config: an IaaS shop on day 4 shows "6 of 18.7 developer-days, 7 days left… Estimated launch: day 11", with Build buttons disabled.

## Balance (placeholders; tuning is #181)

Sensible strategy, 3 seeds, before → after:
- **Break-even:** on-prem moves from about d54–65 to d70–79, and IaaS from about d48–50 to d61–67.
- **Launch day:** on-prem moves from d5 to d12–16, and IaaS from d2 to d11–13.
- **IaaS rescues:** 1 of 3 seeds of IaaS ecommerce and social is now rescued, because cash dips harder.

This is roughly on the new 60–75 target, with the slow end and the IaaS cash dip left for the tuning slice.

author: venamartin
body:
## What

A download that's running when its pack is republished now recovers. Before, Retry kept failing until the user removed the download and started again.

## Why

traxmapmaker republishes packs in place (same key, new bytes, new sha256). A download caught by that can end in two ways:
- **Interrupted, then resumed:** background_downloader compares the 206 response's ETag with the one it stored. It fails the resume when they differ ("Cannot resume: ETag is not identical, or is weak"). So a file is never spliced from old and new bytes.
- **Finished against an old catalogue entry:** the new file fails `PackManager.install`'s SHA-256 check.

Either way the row showed "Failed" with Retry. Retry restarted with the `PackIndexEntry` the download began with, which still had the old sha256, so the new build failed the check every time.

## Fix

- **`MapPacksService.resume`:** a failed download drops its record and starts again from the catalogue's current entry.
- **A download rejected after "Checking":** the service fetches the catalogue again. If the pack's sha256 changed, it downloads the new build without waiting for Retry.
- **Cost:** Offline maps already refreshes the catalogue every time it opens. So a pack is downloaded twice only when a publish lands between opening the screen and tapping Download.

## Testing

`test/services/map_packs_service_test.dart`: 23 passed, including 3 new tests:
- Retry downloads the current build;
- a rejected download fetches the catalogue and starts the new build;
- a rejected download of the current build waits for Retry.

`flutter analyze`: clean on the changed files.
