- `pve-config.sh` — the driver. Discovers `stages/phase<N>/NN-name.sh`,
  runs them as child processes, and supports `--list`, `--phase`,
  `--stage`, `--force`, `--reconfigure`, `--dry-run`, `--config`,
  `--non-interactive` and `--help`.
- `lib/common.sh` — logging, `run_cmd` with secret redaction, and the
  converging file helpers (`write_file`, `ensure_line_in_file`,
  `backup_file`) that make re-running a stage safe.
- `lib/config.sh` — a strict parser for the generated files. They are
  parsed, never sourced, so a tampered config cannot hand the shell a
  command. Secrets live in a separate 0600 file.
- `lib/detect.sh` — derives hostname, FQDN, interfaces, addressing, RAM,
  CPU count and the Debian suite, degrading safely when a source is absent.
- `lib/state.sh` — phase-qualified completion markers plus the boot id
  gating that keeps phase 2 from starting before the host reboots.
- `lib/schema.sh` — the declarative key schema the driver resolves up
  front, which is what makes every run after the first unattended.
- `examples/` — commented templates for both generated files.
- `tests/` — 174 bats tests and a PATH-injected mock command directory.

## Notes

- Tests use plain bats only and pass as a non-root user with no Proxmox
  tooling present.
- The schema is seeded with the keys the framework itself can justify;
  later PRs extend it alongside the stages that read them.

author: tihonove
body:
Closes #819

## What

Bumps `@tuidom/*` to **0.17.3**, which carries tuidom/tuidom#64: `encodeKeyForPty` no longer encodes Ctrl+Shift+letter as a control byte. It returns `""`, so `TerminalViewElement` writes nothing to the PTY and does not `preventDefault`; the keydown stays with the workbench.

Reference: xterm.js `Keyboard.ts` (`evaluateKeyboardEvent`) emits the control byte for a letter only for `ctrlKey && !shiftKey && !altKey && !metaKey`. This prepares the next task in the chain (terminal-first dispatch with the skip-shell list): without it, Ctrl+Shift+E/F/G would reach the shell as `^E`/`^F`/`^G` on kitty/CSI-u tiers.

Unchanged: Ctrl+letter without Shift, Ctrl+Space/[/\\/], special keys, Alt/Meta prefix; Ctrl+Alt+letter and Ctrl+Shift+non-letter (out of scope). The dispatcher is untouched.

## Tests

- tuidom: `encodeKeyForPty` (Ctrl+A…Z → bytes, Ctrl+Shift+A…Z → `""`) and `TerminalViewElement` (Ctrl+Shift+E → no write, `defaultPrevented === false`).
- diode: `terminalPanelComponent.keys.test.ts` — with the terminal focused, Ctrl+Y reaches the shell as `^Y`, Ctrl+Shift+Y (unbound in the workbench) writes nothing. On 0.17.2 the second test fails with `["\x19"]`.

## How to reproduce

On a kitty/CSI-u terminal: open the terminal (Ctrl+`), press Ctrl+Shift+Y — nothing is written to the shell (before: `^Y`, i.e. yank in bash). Ctrl+A still moves the shell cursor to the line start. On the legacy tier the outer terminal drops Shift anyway, so nothing changes there (expected per the issue).

No demo scenario: there is nothing visible to capture.

body:
## Summary

BAN-11's design Stage spawned the `prototyper`. The Agent tool always runs subagents in the background, so the Stage ended its turn to wait. `claude -p` stops background tasks 10 minutes after the last turn, and it killed the prototyper partway through Variant b. `claude` exited 0 and left no result.

```diff
 headless Stage (claude -p)
-  --model <account default: Sonnet>
+  --model opus
+  env CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0     # wait up to the Stage's own 3h limit
   design / implement / review-round / acceptance-fix
-    spawn prototyper | implementer  (background, killed at 10 min)
+    follow .claude/agents/<builder>.md itself     # stages.md § Builders
     spawn spec-, correctness-, ui-reviewer         # still subagents: independent of the author
```

Live mode is unchanged: `/work-issue` still spawns the builders, so a long build stays out of the Maintainer's session. One shared rule, `stages.md` § Builders, and each spawn site points to it.

## Evidence

- **Before:** BAN-11, `/work/logs/BAN-11/2026-10-24T21-13-03Z-design.jsonl`: `Background tasks still running 10m after the last turn (subagent "Build BAN-11 Variants"); stopping them.` then `claude exited 0` and no Stage result.
- **After:** `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 claude -p` with a subagent that sleeps, then echoes: the main agent is woken by its report and ends `GOT PINEAPPLE-42` (2 turns). `plan.test.ts` pins `--model opus` and the env var; all 390 runner tests, typecheck, lint and format pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** Runner

Every headless Stage now carries a whole build plus triage in one context, and every Stage bills Opus. The implement Stage's triage now judges code the Stage wrote itself. The reviewers stay independent of it.

author: ineersa
body:
## Summary

- Upgrade Symfony components to 8.2 and MCP SDK main with its Amp compatibility fix; use Symfony AmpHttpClient for LLM HTTP.
- Replace the LLM process pool with one consumer using the native Symfony Messenger Worker and a bounded Amp/Fiber execution strategy.
- Add `runtime.llm_concurrency`, a positive integer defaulting to **10**. Remove `runtime.llm_worker_count`. HTTP connections remain at the Amp default six per host; tool parallelism is unchanged.
- Schedule Messenger lease renewal through Revolt during suspended HTTP, with native queue waiting and graceful shutdown.
- Update settings/docs and ignore generated Symfony configuration schema.

## Validation and gate fixes

Focused tests, PHPStan, dead-code checks, Deptrac, formatting, docs and PHAR smoke passed. Latest controller replay: **34 tests, 1,759 assertions**; lock-store/factory checks: **5 tests, 35 assertions**. The CODE-REVIEW transition runs full `castor check` for this revision.

- Fixed test-kernel boot order: class-level boot opened a DAMA transaction before PHPUnit preparation, causing a second BEGIN and disabling rollback. Initial boot now occurs in setUp; the malformed-JSON regression remains.
- Routed the named Amp client through the test HTTP fixture factory. It previously bypassed replay and could contact the real provider.
- Removed test-only production metrics and replaced elapsed-time overlap assertions with DeferredFuture barriers.
- Merged current main and preserved the user's deleted background-process timing test.

### Removed flaky tests and coverage gaps

Following the root test policy, no sleeps, polling retries or larger timeouts were added:

1. Removed the new `LlmFiberConsumeKeepaliveProcessTest` and its exclusive helper: timing windows, >10-second duration, and an external absolute fixture path. **Lost:** repeatable real-broker renewal during suspended HTTP and actual command timer firing. Command wiring and deterministic overlap tests do not replace this proof.
2. Removed `HeadlessControllerSessionOwnerLockProcessTest::testSecondControllerForSameSessionIsRejectedWithoutRuntimeReady` and exclusive helpers. Its teardown joined the controller root but sampled grandchildren immediately after SIGKILL, without synchronization. **Lost:** full-controller same-session rejection, rejected-controller absence of runtime.ready, and that case's cleanup proof. Lock-store exclusivity/coordinator barriers and factory checks remain, but are not equivalent protocol proof.

Global leak gates and other topology hard assertions remain unchanged. Passing replay still emitted unknown-PID ownership warnings while the QA leak check passed. The broader shared-harness post-kill race is not claimed fixed.

## Live evidence

Manual PHAR smoke used Sol 6.1 / low for the parent, installed ext-uv/UvDriver and one LLM consumer. Conversation, read, bash, code_mode and parallel scouts completed. Scouts used configured Luna / medium. Owned TUIs exited through Ctrl+D.

Ten scouts each read six files and were asked for a 2,000–3,000-token essay. Both comparison arms used one consumer, HTTP limit six and temporarily ten tool workers; tool settings were restored.

| Metric | Capacity 6 | Capacity 10 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Completed scouts | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Batch wall time | 129 s | 68 s |
| Median / p95 latency | 73 / 128 s | 53 / 68 s |
| Final essay output tokens | 22,595 | 19,706 |
| Sampled LLM peak PSS | 91.4 MiB | 85.5 MiB |
| Sampled whole-tree peak PSS | 1,445.5 MiB | 1,434.6 MiB |

One clean pair is not a controlled speedup estimate: input/output volumes differ; memory sampling interval was 1.5 seconds. An operator-cancelled capacity-six run was excluded. Journals establish child-lifetime overlap, not simultaneous provider occupancy. HTTP/2 occupancy was not observed. No matched full-app old-pool/new-consumer memory comparison exists. Earlier isolated real-handler experiments are not full-session savings.

## Review notes

User will review manually; no automated approval claimed. Broader shared-state isolation and retry/reset behavior merit scrutiny. Global Castor has a Console 8.1/project Console 8.2 mixed-loading issue for `--help`; normal test/list commands work. No global tool/vendor patch applied.

External evidence: `/home/ineersa/projects/agent-core-tasks/reports/memory-07-feasibility/` including `gate-fixes/`, `live-smoke/REPORT.md` and `live-capacity-6-vs-10/REPORT.md`. Task metadata/transcripts are not committed.

author: bad3r
body:
## Summary

Slice C5 of the workloads RFC: the Windows 11 pipeline (part of #601).

- **Seed CD-ROM**: `windows.seedIso` builds the `XSEED` ISO without secrets, holding:
  - `autounattend.xml`, rendered from Nix attrs;
  - `$WinPEDriver$` with viostor, vioscsi, and NetKVM for w11/amd64;
  - `virtio-win-guest-tools.exe`;
  - Win32-OpenSSH 10.4.0.0p1 and WinFsp 2.1 MSIs, hash-pinned and checked against GitHub's asset digests;
  - `firstlogon.ps1`.
- **Answer file**:
  - `Windows 11 Pro`, picked by image name. The Business ISO is volume-licence media: `sources/EI.CFG` in its UDF tree reads `[Channel] volume`, `[VL] 1`. That is why no setup key is needed; consumer media would stop at the key page.
  - No LabConfig bypasses.
  - Computer name is the guest name.
  - `PreventDeviceEncryption` is set.
  - One local admin with a blank password and a single autologon.
- **Seed attachment**: the seed is the `<guest>-seed` entry of `workloads.images`, attached through a new `install.images` list. virtio-win is attached the same way, as an image, so a stale out-link after a nixpkgs bump matters only before the first define.
- **Provisioning**: a libvirt qemu hook queues `workloads-provision@<guest>` with `--no-block`.
  - The hook is installed through `hooks.qemu` plus a tmpfiles link and a libvirtd `reloadTriggers`, because `libvirtd-config` only relinks hooks when libvirtd starts.
  - `_provision.py` presses Enter at the installer's boot prompt while the OS disk is still empty, then waits for the guest agent and `firstlogon.ps1`.
  - Probe/apply steps, in order:
    - the password via `virDomainSetUserPassword`;
    - `administrators_authorized_keys`;
    - Remote Desktop and declared services, scoped to the bridge gateway;
    - last, an optional product key through the licensing calls behind `slmgr /ipk` and `/ato`, with the key on stdin.
  - The unit has `restartIfChanged = false`.
  - C6 (virtiofs) and C7 (Office) slot in as further steps.
- **Golden copy**: `workloads-golden@<guest>` makes a sparse copy of disks, NVRAM, swtpm state, and inactive XML. It runs only while the guest is shut off. Restore is a documented procedure.
- **Review round**: deadlines on the agent waits, bounded retries of the first-logon probe, and the OpenSSH installer's rule found by `sshd.exe`. Errors log at `<3>`. A golden copy fails if the guest's files change during the copy. Added a `systemctl reload libvirtd` fallback for the hook.
- **Missing inputs**:
  - A missing media source warns instead of failing the switch, and a present source with the wrong hash still fails.
  - A new guest stays undefined, with a warning, until its install media are staged and its install-image out-links are current. This is the same pattern as #626.
- **songbird**:
  - `win11` on `desktop` (offset 11): 12 GiB, 6 vCPUs on P-cores 0-7, a 128 GiB disk, and `autostart` off.
  - The ISO path and hash live in `policy.nix`.
  - The guest stays gated on `secrets/workloads.yaml`, which the secrets gitlink bump (`5913735`) now provides.

## Test plan

- [x] `nix build path:.#checks.x86_64-linux.workloads-vms`: all subtests pass, including a new missing-medium/wrong-hash scenario.
- [x] Seed ISO built twice with `--rebuild` to check reproducibility. Contents inspected with `xorriso -find` and 7-Zip, and the answer file with `xmllint`.
- [x] win11 domain XML passes the `virt-xml-validate` derivation, with the seed on `sdc` and no boot order.
- [x] Scratch unit tests (outside the tree; the repo has no Python test harness) of `_provision.py` against a fake qemu-ga cover:
  - step order and probe/apply/re-probe;
  - that secrets never reach argv;
  - the firstlogon failure path;
  - the boot-key gating;
  - plus the golden copy and `pending_install`.
- [x] Reconciler subcommands smoke-tested on libvirt's `test:///default`.
- [x] `nix flake check path:. --accept-flake-config --no-build --offline`
- [x] `nix build "path:.#nixosConfigurations.songbird.config.system.build.toplevel"` with win11 enabled. The closure holds no ISO or MSI.
- [x] `legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.workloads.{win11-seed,virtio-win}` build.
- [x] treefmt, the pre-commit manual stage, and docs-style.
- [ ] Acceptance on songbird (needs polkit, so it is a user step): follow "Install the win11 guest" in `docs/hosts/songbird/songbird-runbook-vms.md`. Unattended install, SSH key login, and RDP with the sops password should all work.
- [ ] memtest86+ pass, then `systemctl start workloads-golden@win11`.

author: timchang87
body:
Closes SLO-33. Decision record: `docs/adr/0001-one-instance-per-worktree.md`.

## Summary

Each checkout gets its own sidecar port, data folder, Electron profile and `.mcp.json`, so parallel Claude sessions in separate worktrees never collide.

```text
<checkout>/.env   (gitignored, written by `npm run worktree -- setup`)
  SLOWGLASS_PORT   main: 47821          worktree: hash(path) → 47822–48821, first free + unclaimed
  SLOWGLASS_HOME   main: ~/Music/slowglass   worktree: <worktree>/.slowglass/
  SLOWGLASS_LABEL  main: (none)         worktree: branch name → window title
```

```diff
 settings (app main process and sidecar Settings.from_env)
-  environment → defaults
+  environment → checkout .env → defaults
+  userData = $SLOWGLASS_HOME/electron

 SidecarSupervisor.launch
+  if port is held by another process
+    status "blocked": "port N is in use…; run `npm run worktree -- setup --repick`"
+    retry with backoff (never switch ports: .mcp.json points at it)
   spawn sidecar
```

```diff
+scripts/worktree.mjs        # setup [--repick] | new <branch> [base] | rm <branch> [--force]
+package.json               # npm run worktree
+.claude/settings.json      # SessionStart: setup when .env is missing (covers Claude Code worktrees)
-.mcp.json
+.mcp.json.example          # setup writes each checkout's .mcp.json with its port
+docs/adr/0001-one-instance-per-worktree.md
```

`rm` stops the worktree's app, `uv` and sidecar (processes running from its path), then removes it. It refuses on uncommitted or unpushed work unless `--force`, and keeps the branch.

## Evidence

- **Before:** two checkouts both bind 47821 and share `~/Music/slowglass/slowglass.db`; every Claude session's `.mcp.json` points at the same sidecar.
  **After:** in a scratch clone, `new feat/a` and `new feat/b` got ports 48780 and 48161; both sidecars ran at once, each with its own `.slowglass/slowglass.db`. The real app launched in a worktree with an empty environment and came up on that worktree's port with its profile in `.slowglass/electron`. `rm` stopped all 7 of its processes and left the other worktree's sidecar running.
- **Before:** an impostor on the port showed `sidecar restarting…` forever.
  **After:** `sidecar blocked: port N is in use…` naming `--repick` (e2e).
- New tests:
  ```text
  sidecar: .env sets home and port · environment wins over .env · migrations have a single head
  e2e:     label shows in window title · no label → plain title · userData == $SLOWGLASS_HOME/electron
  ```
  `uv run pytest` 10 passed · `uv run mypy` clean · `npm run typecheck` clean · `npm run test:e2e` 11 passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting restores the old behaviour. The main checkout's `.env` pins the same port and home it used before.

**Blast Radius:** development

Every checkout (including main) needs `npm run worktree -- setup` once after pulling, since `.mcp.json` is no longer tracked; the SessionStart hook does this automatically when `.env` is missing. The main checkout's Electron profile moves from `~/Library/Application Support/slowglass-app` to `~/Music/slowglass/electron` (nothing is stored there yet). `new` only works from bases that include this change.

author: howlil
body:
## Scope
After M5 (#10) and H1 (#11) merges, add a Windows ZIP distribution, semver patch release workflow, per-user installer, and non-blocking staged automatic updater.

## Distribution and updater
- Version on first release `v0.1.0`, then increase patch on eligible `master` pushes.
- Windows build and all CTest checks gate `gh release create`.
- Release asset: `LYNX-windows-x64.zip`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`; ZIP includes native EXE, `VERSION`, installer and update helper.
- Native process starts an adjacent PowerShell checker on startup, periodically every six hours (network throttled to 24h), and via tray "Check for updates".
- The updater fetches GitHub Releases latest over HTTPS, pins release asset names, verifies SHA-256, and stages the archive under the current user's LocalAppData.
- On normal window teardown LYNX starts an out-of-process apply helper which waits until the process exits, revalidates the archive, extracts **only exact filenames**, and replaces the files in user-writable install directory. No running EXE is forcibly terminated.
- No elevation; automatic updates are not present if the standalone CI EXE is used without its helpers.

## Security and limitations
The first early-access binary has no Authenticode signature. SHA-256 is an integrity check, **not authenticated publisher identity**, since the checksum is downloaded from the same release. Code signing and signed-manifest verification remain release hardening work. Native desktop acceptance (DPI/Narrator/media) is not claimed.

## Verification
- Windows CI builds and CTest, PowerShell syntax parse and updater checksum self-test.
- Linux portable CTest.
- Release workflow runs its own Windows build/test again before publication.
- Draft until CI and code review complete.

## 概要

review-raven#144 の O1（#279）の段階4。永続台帳の**保持期限による削除**を追加する。内部面を有効にしたときだけ動き、既存の挙動は変わらない。

## 変更

- **削除**（`ledger.purgeExpired`）: 起動時と、以後 1 時間ごと（`runRetention`）に、期限を過ぎた行を削除する。保持期間は `THREAD_OWL_RETENTION_DAYS`（既定 30。契約の下限 30 日以上、3650 日以下。範囲外は起動失敗）
- **各表は自分の時計で数え、互いに独立**（契約の「保持期間は互いに独立」）:
  - 取消記録: **確定した時刻**から数える（要求から確定まで間があっても、要求の時刻では数えない）。**要求中（未確定）の取消は削除しない**（旧候補の起動・投稿を拒否し続けるため）
  - 結果索引: 投稿の時刻から
  - outbox（結果・候補の通知）: 送信を終えた（delivered・rejected・failed）時刻から。送信待ち（pending）は削除しない
  - 候補: 受付から期限を過ぎ、書込みが進行中でなく、結果・取消記録・送信待ちの通知が残っていないものだけ
- 削除の失敗はログに残して止まらず、次の周期で再試行する。停止時は実行中の 1 回を終えてから台帳を閉じる
- 待機（`abortableSleep`）を結果の配送と共通化

## 検証

- `check` / `typecheck` / `build` / `test`（995 件）通過
- 変異 6 件（要求中の取消の削除、書込み中の候補の削除、取消の時計を要求時刻にする、起動時に削除しない、下限未満の許可、など）をテストが検出。送信待ちの状態条件の除去は、`finished_at` が NULL の行が比較から外れるため等価な変異（条件は意図を明示するために残した）

実際の review-raven＋gateway 経由の相互接続は未検証（Mcp-Docker#392 / #393）。`comment_id` と review ID が同じ数値になる極小の衝突可能性（`results` の `UNIQUE(cycle_id, comment_id)`）は、実害が無視できるため据え置き。

author: yoavgeva
body:
Review round 8: API conformance and leak coverage. Stacked on #50.

## Debug for the cache and its guards

`ShardedCache`, `ShardedCacheGuard`, `PlaceholderGuard`, and `GuardResult` had no `Debug`, so a type holding a cache could not derive it (Rust API guideline C-DEBUG). quick_cache implements `Debug` for its cache and guards.

- The cache prints its counts and limits, not its entries, so it needs no bounds on its keys or values: `ShardedCache { len: 1, weight: 1, capacity: 100, max_weight: None, shards: 1, .. }`.
- The read guard prints `ShardedCacheGuard { .. }`.
- The placeholder guard prints its key, and `GuardResult` its value, when they are `Debug`.

`caches_guards_and_results_print_for_debugging` failed to compile before this change. It also checks that a struct holding a `ShardedCache<u64, RefCell<()>>` derives `Debug`.

## Superseded loads leak no slot or value

A load superseded by a write (#49) fills a slot it never publishes, then drops the value and gives the slot back. A test now supersedes 20,000 loads and checks both. Each check fails when its half of the bail path is removed: without the give-back, 320,512 bytes of slots stayed handed out; without the drop, 20,000 values stayed alive.

## A seed-dependent flake in a probation test

`keys_evicted_from_probation_return_to_the_main_area` asserted that one key the ghost never saw starts in probation. The ghost is a filter, and under about 1 hash seed in 300 its words remembered that key by chance, admitting it straight to the main area. #50's every-feature job failed this way. The test now inserts 20 fresh keys and requires 17 in probation. Over 1,000 seeds, 20 started there in 932, 19 in 65, and 18 in 3.

## Docs: against quick_cache with `u64` keys and values

The published comparison used 32-byte keys and 64-byte `Arc` payloads, which cost both caches hashing and reference counts and hide ShardedCache's fixed work per operation. A scratch benchmark at 50,000 entries ran `get` hits on resident keys and upserts of the seeded keys into an exactly full cache. Each figure is the range over three runs of the best of seven:

| Workload | macOS 1T | macOS 8T | Linux 1T | Linux 8T |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Resident hit | -7 to -13% | +806 to +830% | -2 to +3% | +694 to +715% |
| Upsert into a full cache | -56 to -60% | -1 to +6% | -53 to -54% | -15 to +31% |

The single-thread upsert gap is the design's: each write fills a new entry and retires the old one, where quick_cache overwrites in place under its shard lock. Profiling found no cheaper path. Prefetching the next free slot for writing, and skipping the prefetch of the next slot to free when values have no destructor, were both within noise. The README now says this, and its maturity note names the x86_64 runners its x86 figures came from. The design doc gets the table.

## Docs: max_weight is split over the shards

`ShardedCacheBuilder::max_weight` did not say that each shard holds an equal share of the limit. A value heavier than the limit over the shard count is never cached. By default a 1,000,000-entry cache on 16 threads has 256 shards, and with a 1-GiB limit it refuses values over 4 MiB, `insert` returning false. The doc now says so, and that fewer shards let heavier values in. The design doc's correctness evidence also lists the loader tests from #49-#51.

## The README's example runs as a doctest

The README's example, unlike the crate docs' similar one, was compiled nowhere. It now runs as a doctest through a `#[cfg(doctest)]` item that includes the README. Renaming one method call in it fails the doc tests.

## Probe: an update workload

The probe's replace and delete-reinsert workloads run at four times their key count, so that every seeded key stays resident for both caches. They never wrote to a full cache, and #50's needless eviction prefetch went unseen there. The new `update` workload upserts the seeded keys into a cache of exactly their count: mostly replacements, plus reinsertions of the few that seeding evicted. The comparison scripts, and so the bench workflow, run it. Against quick_cache on macOS, five paired runs, median and range:

| Entries | 1T | 8T |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50,000 | +11% (+5 to +19%) | +10% (-9 to +15%) |
| 1,000,000 | +56% (+49 to +58%) | +58% (+50 to +89%) |

With the probe's 32-byte keys and `Arc` payloads, ShardedCache leads here, unlike with `u64` keys and values above. The README and the design doc record both.

## Probe: a read-through workload

The probe measured no loader, though `get_or_insert_with` is how many callers read a cache. The `read-through` workload issues turnover's reads, each through the cache's loader. That is `get_or_insert_with` for ShardedCache and quick_cache, and a read with an insert on a miss for the direct cache, which has no loader. Each read must hit or load. The probe's adapter test now also runs both ShardedCache backends on every workload. Against quick_cache on macOS, five paired runs:

| Entries | 1T | 8T |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50,000 | -3% (-6 to +2%) | +32% (+19 to +69%) |
| 1,000,000 | +13% (+0 to +29%) | +61% (+51 to +67%) |

Against #48's head (the probe built on both), seven paired runs at 50,000 entries moved by -1% on one thread and -2% at eight, within noise. #49's listing of loads under the shard lock costs this mix nothing measurable.

## Two real-time tests skipped under Miri

A full `cargo miri nextest` run of the arena and segment-cache unit tests (which CI's Miri jobs leave out) failed two `MutableSegmentCache` tests. Each gives entries 100 to 300 ms to live and sleeps part of that, but Miri's clock advances with interpretation and outran the sleeps. They are now ignored under Miri, with that reason.

This is the third of three PRs that lay the backend out in layers. It is stacked on #39, which is stacked on #38; merge them in that order.

This PR turns snapshot assembly into a function. Static export can then read saved results without starting a preview service. It also moves the server, preview service, CLI, proof steps and gallery export into `glitnir.service`, and documents the layers.

A panel review of the whole layering (behaviour, release, compatibility, architecture) found nothing Critical. The fixes for its other findings are here.

## Changes
- **`glitnir.preview.snapshot`:** `build_snapshot(path, text, fingerprint, state, providers)` with a frozen `PreviewState`.

author: itsandrewm
body:
### What
- Add a second, independent verify session between a validated draft review and posting. It judges blocking findings and suggestions, keeps or drops each, and sets final severity before the review event is chosen.
- Keep it globally off with `VERIFY_MODEL: ""`. Repositories can override or opt out only after an operator selects a passing default.
- Add a source-backed historical replay harness, scoring tests, credential preflight, and a shared $2 spend guard for model evaluation.

### Why
- #31's audit found false findings and severity errors that can change whether a pull request requests changes. A verifier must catch those without dropping or demoting true blockers.
- Neither evaluated model met the agreed activation bar. [Results on #31](https://github.com/ItsAndrewM/ai-review-agent/issues/31#issuecomment-6389469628): GLM completed three runs but broke the true-blocker rule and missed severity targets; Kimi missed all three required `await` demotions in both full runs. Its third run stopped at the approved spend cap, but could not have changed that majority outcome. This PR makes the off-by-default implementation reviewable without enabling a failing model.

### How to test
1. Run `pnpm check` (lint, Worker and Node TypeScript checks, and 1,421 unit tests in 53 files).
2. Run `pnpm verify:replay --inspect`: it should show 24 findings, four documented nitpick exclusions, and no corpus problems. This command makes no model requests.
3. With `VERIFY_MODEL` empty, existing reviews do not enter the verify session. The tests cover candidate selection, verdict application, severity caps, duplicate and missing verdicts, retry/backstop, stale-head refusal, tool isolation, rendering, and the replay scoring boundaries.

The production live check from the plan has **not** run; it requires a coordinated shared deploy window. Verify is not enabled by this PR.

### High level code differences
- `src/review/verify.ts` and `verify-tools.ts`: pure verdict decisions, prompt/context and retry behavior, and the isolated four-tool verify extension.
- `src/pull-request.ts`, `src/review/flight.ts`, `render.ts`, `check.ts`, and configuration: wire the pass into the single flight, account for usage, and display verified/unverified outcomes.
- `tools/verify-replay/` and `test/verify-replay-*.test.ts`: reconstruct findings at their historical Git heads; run the same prompt and tool contracts offline; score the three-run bar and preserve result/spend journals.
- `docs/design.md`, `docs/setup.md`, README and the #31 spec/plan: record the measured result and why the default remains off.

Refs #31. The issue remains open for the live check and a future verifier that passes the bar.

body:
I pointed claude at #3863 and this is the first of two PRs that should fix it. I read through these changes, and they look fine to me.

---

Part of #3863.

Before: if you wrote one segment's diameter on a section with 3-d points before anything had read its diameters, for example right after `pt3dadd`, the other 3-d points' diameters were replaced by 500 µm, NEURON's default. This happened with HOC `sec.diam(x) = d` and `sec.diam(a:b) = d1:d2`, with Python `sec(x).diam = d`, and with the C API's `nrn_rangevar_set`.

After: such a write changes only the 3-d points in the written segment, and the result is the same whether or not anything read diam first.

## Example

Three 3-d points 10 µm apart, all diam 3, nseg = 3, then `diam(0.5) = 42`:

| | 3-d diameters | segment diameters |
|---|---|---|
| before, fresh section | 500, 42, 500 | 347.3, 118.3, 347.3 |
| before, diam read first | 3, 42, 3 | 16, 35.5, 16 |
| after, either case | 3, 42, 3 | 16, 35.5, 16 |

## Why it happened

After `pt3dadd`, a section's segment diameters are derived from its 3-d points only at the next area recompute (the section's `recalc_area_` flag). Until then, each segment holds its old diameter, which for a new section is the 500 µm default. Every diam write ends with `nrn_diam_change`, which copies each segment's diameter into the 3-d points that lie in it (as the `pt3dconst` documentation describes). So the untouched segments' stale 500s were copied over the diameters given to `pt3dadd`.

## The fix

Before writing a segment diameter on a section with 3-d points, finish the pending recompute with NEURON's existing `nrn_area_ri`. The getters already do this (`seg.diam` in Python, `nrn_segment_diam_get`), and HOC already did it for compound assignments such as `diam(x) += d`. No formulas change; the existing recompute runs earlier. Sections without 3-d points are not affected, and neither is whole-section `sec.diam = d`, which writes every segment. `nrn_rangevar_set_nothrow` already recomputed before writing.

This changes results for HOC and Python models that set a segment diameter on a fresh 3-d section before anything read it. Those models had been silently given 500 µm diameters, so the old results were wrong.

## Commits

1. **C API:** `nrn_rangevar_set` (for diam).
2. **HOC:** `range_interpolate_single` (`sec.diam(x) = d`) and `range_interpolate` (`sec.diam(a:b) = d1:d2`) in `cabcode.cpp`.
3. **Python:** the segment setter (`sec(x).diam = d`) in `nrnpy_nrn.cpp`.

## How it was tested

Each test compares a write on a fresh section with the same write on an identical section that was read first. It also checks that the unwritten 3-d points keep their 3 µm.

- `test/api/diam3d_pending.cpp` (new): `nrn_rangevar_set`.
- `test/hoctests/tests/test_diam3d_pending.py` (new): HOC `diam(x)`, HOC `diam(a:b)` and Python `seg.diam`.

Each test fails on the commit before its fix and passes with it. Full `ctest` locally (Linux, NMODL on, no MPI or InterViews): all new and changed tests pass. Eight unrelated tests fail identically on an unmodified master build on the same machine: `basic_tests` (pytest and coreneuron), `cover_tests`, `test_nonlin_py`, `test_vlag_py`, `test_kschan_py`, `test_random_py` and `external_nrntest`.

The companion C API pull request (`issue3863-capi-diam`) makes `nrn_segment_diam_set` propagate to 3-d points, and it includes the same pre-write recompute there. The two branches merge cleanly in either order.

author: sloppamadewithlove
body:
The previous Windows ZIP exposed a worker executable and failed during native menu startup. This repair produces one Windows test Setup and one player shortcut, with the automatic windowless worker under `_internal`. It fixes the private game-package file view, preserves the original menu initializer, and uses RLBot's supported offline launch arguments.

The native frontend maps to My Career, Training, Garage, Workshop, Community, Settings and Exit. Authored pause/results menus bind actions to the current activity and require completed scores to save before returning. The worker initializes NumPy before reading its command pipe: the previous order reproducibly deadlocked on Windows. Frontend text now fits its bounds and keeps standings on separate lines; an active match no longer appears as an abandoned fixture.

The native launcher now keeps the validated executable quoted and passes the same four fixed RLBot options without unnecessary quotes. Controlled game tests isolated the old argument formatting as a connection failure; the exact canonical-command guard remains enforced. Startup cancellation also retains ownership during cleanup and rejects late messages from a timed-out activity. Native builds now keep legacy fullscreen drawing and input capture disabled even while a native menu is loading; the gameplay HUD remains nonblocking.

Validation and limits:

- Integrated revision `7e3338d` passed both Windows CI pipelines, including install/reinstall/uninstall, plus 952 Python tests (15 skipped), 27 plugin tests and 13 launcher/file-view tests.
- The NumPy regression passed with real redirected Python and Pythonw workers. An independent GPT-6 Luna Max repeat reproduced the old hang and initialized the actual Necto controller in about four seconds with the fix.
- The text change passed the focused native layout test and 86 Python checks; its authored bytecode and pins were rebuilt and checked. Grok 4.7 High reviewed the change.
- The launcher change passed 162 independent checks. Startup cancellation passed 108 focused checks and independent Luna review, with Grok's source design advice.
- Live native frontend, unfinished-fixture recovery and career-rule buttons worked in a copied test profile. Integrated source `68448b7` completed a real offline 1v1 with Necto, saved its actual 0–54 result once, cleared the pending fixture and acknowledged the durable receipt. That mostly unattended run used a private bridge command to start the activity; it does not prove the rebuilt native Play button.
- Actual Escape, Game options/Back, Resume, and canceling the unfinished Return confirmation passed. The authored results screen became ready and showed the saved result. Its actual Return click exposed a further bug: SDK disconnect reached the title screen and the legacy fullscreen overlay took control. Native Return remains under repair; service Idle alone is not navigation acceptance.
- The exact `68448b7` CI pipeline passed frozen smoke and installer lifecycle. Luna verified all 4,470 downloaded bundle files and nine corresponding source archives. Its installer remains held because of the observed Return bug and missing exact frozen game acceptance.
- Repository and intended runtime reviews found no credible personal-path, account-ID, API-token or private-key leak. Proprietary game packages and private diagnostics are excluded.

The user paused for a new session. The completed repair checkpoint and [full handoff](https://github.com/sloppamadewithlove/my-career-training/blob/fix/windows-startup-and-download/docs/SESSION_HANDOFF_2026-10-24.md) are pushed through `830169d`. Partial Return headers are preserved separately on `fix/native-return-shell-ready` through `5c643f1`; that branch is explicitly unfinished and not buildable or mergeable yet.

Keep this PR draft until live acceptance passes. The existing [My Career Training site](https://my-career-training.vercel.app/) holds the broken download while the replacement is tested. No replacement player release is claimed here.

author: k4pran
body:
Closes #59

Issue #59 (MX-30) is done: harmony, fretboard frames and figured bass now import as timed events, and the work is committed in two commits on `agent/issue-59` (`29685a8` for the code and tests, `a73547d` for the docs). A previous session had left the model and most of the parser uncommitted; I checked it, fixed one gap and added the fixtures, tests and docs.

**Code**
- **Model:** `sheetmusic-model/.../score/Harmony.kt` adds `HarmonyEvent` and `FiguredBassEvent`.
  - A `HarmonyEvent` holds one or more stacked chords. Each chord has a root (a pitch, a numeral or a function), a kind (every MusicXML 4.0 value, with its `text` and symbol attributes), an inversion, a bass and degrees. A harmony can also carry a fretboard frame with fingerings and barres.
  - A `FiguredBassEvent` holds figures with prefix, number, suffix and extension.
- **Timing:**
  - A harmony's onset is where it was written plus its `offset`, so a change in the middle of a note lands at the exact point. An offset that would put it before the measure start is reported as discarded (S22) and the harmony is placed at the start.
  - Figured bass sits at the next note, plus the durations of any earlier figures under that note.
- **The fix I added:** a harmony with no `<staff>` now takes the staff of the next note. Fixture 71d says each staff should get its own fret diagrams; before this they all landed on staff 1.
- **Bad input:** an empty `figured-bass` (74b) or empty `figure` is dropped with a `RECOVERED_VALUE` warning, which strict parsing treats as a failure. Unknown values and malformed structure are fatal errors.

**Tests**
- Embedded W3C fixtures 45k, 46g, 71a–71d, 71f, 71g, 74a and 74b, unmodified.
- New `HarmonyImportTest` checks the facts each fixture's description states, plus inline cases for the text and symbol attributes, offsets and invalid input. 71f has no `none` chord, so the "every kind" check uses 71b and 71f together.
- Five existing tests changed: F21 now expects its harmony and figured bass to be imported rather than discarded, and three parser tests no longer use `<harmony/>` as a stand-in for unsupported content.

**Docs:** S22 in `spec-coverage.md` now lists what is implemented and what is tested as separate columns. There's a new MX-30 section in `risks-and-gaps.md` and a new `harmony-import.md`, and I updated the compliance audit, fixture manifest, test plan, version-4.0 notes and third-party notices.

**Gaps left open (recorded in `risks-and-gaps.md`)**
- In 71g, two harmonies under one note have no `offset`, so they share the note's onset in source order. MusicXML doesn't say where inside the note the second one falls.
- Figure extension lines are kept on each figure but not joined into spans.
- Nothing is drawn yet; the renderer doesn't use these events.

**Results**
- `:musicxml-parser:jvmTest`: 360 tests, 0 failures.
- `:musicxml-parser:testAndroidHostTest`: 350 tests, 0 failures.
- `:sheetmusic-model:allTests` passes.
- iOS: main and test klibs compile. Linking and simulator runs need macOS and weren't run.
- Full W3C suite run: strict accepts 126 files (up from 117) and nothing is discarded as S22 any more. All the target fixtures import cleanly; 74b gets the intended diagnostic.
- `./gradlew build` has two failures that this branch didn't cause:
  - `:musicxml-parser:compileCommonMainKotlinMetadata` fails at `ScoreXmlReader.kt:125` (unresolved `range`), a file this branch doesn't touch.
  - The JS/Wasm browser tests for `sheetmusic-compose` can't launch Chrome on this machine.

author: christopherowen
body:
A chat request with `prompt_logprobs` (or `echo`) kills EngineCore in candidate 4 and in production (spark-ds41f-1022), as seen in run `tilelang-ports-controls`.

**Cause:** sink rejection (vLLM 0221, on by default for DeepSeek V4.1 since 0223) holds back the token that the prompt's last step samples. That step therefore has no output for the request, but it carries the prompt logprobs that `PromptLogprobsWorker` returns. The scheduler's "no partial prefill outputs" assertion (`scheduler.py:3424`) then fails.

**Fix:** vLLM 0266 keeps such a step's prompt logprobs on the request and emits them with the request's first output. Tests:
- 15 scheduler tests fail at the production assertion without 0266 and pass with it;
- the scheduler suites otherwise match candidate 4 (CPU).

**Record:** `experiments/2026-10-24-prompt-logprobs-sink/README.md` holds the root cause, the patch and candidate 4's series with 0266.

**The lab check, not yet run:** spec `serving-check.json`, four arms on the ring. Candidate 4 and the promoted recipe each run with and without 0266's two-file overlay. The check covers:
- the crashing request, its prompt logprobs and `echo`;
- a teacher-forced comparison;
- temperature-0 digests of the other requests.

**Production:** affected, unchanged. The README lists stopgap options for the owner; nothing is deployed.

author: danfry1
body:
## Summary
Dependabot proposes grouped weekly updates that are at least 7 days old.

## Why
Actions in this repository are pinned to commit SHAs; without version updates those pins, and the dependencies, go stale and miss fixes. The 7-day cooldown gives a bad or hijacked release time to be pulled before it is proposed.

## Changes
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: adds Dependabot for cargo and github-actions.

author: oleg-tkachuk
body:
`monorepo:doctor` reads the root Taskfile's local includes and warns about a top-level var some components declare and others do not: those land in one pool, so the others read that value.

`release:doctor` warns when `.task/remote`, Task's checksum lock for modules fetched over git, is ignored by git or not committed.

The README's gitignore advice for the lock was wrong: `.task/` followed by `!.task/remote/` re-includes nothing, because git does not look inside an excluded directory. It now says `.task/*`. Consumers who followed the old advice have no committed lock.

author: ri0806123789
body:
> #245 の出し直しです。#245 の CI で、管理コンソールのバックエンドの Windows ジョブ（4件）が、追加したテストの文字コードで失敗しました。その修正コミットを、ルールセット（PR 必須）のため既存ブランチへ push できなかったので、新しいブランチで出し直します。#245 との差分は最後のコミット（テストのみ）だけです。

## 解決する課題と変更後の動作

### #222 夏時間をまたぐ繰り返しリマインダー

基準のタイムゾーン（`REMINDER_TIMEZONE`）を夏時間のある地域（例: `America/New_York`）へ変えた場合、夏時間の終了で同じ時刻が二度現れる時間帯に停止明けの次回時刻を計算すると、現在より前の時刻を返していました（例: 二度目の 01:15 = 06:15 UTC から計算して 05:30 UTC を返す）。DB はその時刻を `pending` のまま保存し、次の見回りで同じ繰り返しを取り直していました。日次・週次・月次とも同じです。

変更後は、次回時刻を UTC で現在と比べて必ず未来まで進めます。曖昧な時刻は1回目、存在しない時刻は進める前のオフセットで解釈して後ろへずらします（02:30 → 03:30）。

あわせて、夏時間の開始で 03:30 へずらした日次・週次の予定が、翌回以降も 03:30 のまま戻らない問題も直しました（月次と同じく初回の時刻から次回を作ります）。既定の `Asia/Tokyo` では動作は変わりません。

### #223 管理コンソールのペルソナ表示

`personas.json` が無い・`default` を省略した構成では、ボットが先頭のペルソナで応答しているのに、サーバー画面は「—」を表示していました。存在しない `default` や保存値では、そのファイル名を稼働中のペルソナのように表示していました。

変更後は、サーバー上の `prompts/` からボットと同じ規則で実際に応答に使うペルソナを推定して表示します。既定に従っている場合は「（既定）」を添えます。保存したファイルが見つからない場合は保存値を注記で分けて示し、ペルソナが無いときは組み込みの標準であることを表示します。一覧の読み直し時点の都合で、直後のファイル変更が反映前のことがある旨も案内します。

## 変更内容

- `src/persona_bot/services/reminder_service.py`
  - 候補をローカルの暦で作り、`_local_to_utc`（`fold=0` で曖昧・存在しない時刻の解釈を固定）で UTC に直してから現在と比較する
  - 日次・週次は、アンカーからの回数を数えてアンカーの壁時計の時刻で次回を作る
- `src/persona_bot/core/database.py`: `reminder_claim_due` で、次回時刻が現在以前なら `pending` に残さず繰り返しを止める（再クレームと同じ比較で判定する安全網）
- `tools/console/backend/remote_scripts/insights.py`
  - `personas.py` がある版では、ボットを import せずに一覧・表示名・既定の規則を再現する
  - 出力に `persona_source`（saved / default / missing）・`persona_missing`・`persona_builtin` と全体の `persona_estimated` を追加する
  - 旧版は従来どおり `choices.py` の固定の選択肢で表示する
- `tools/console/frontend/src/personaView.ts`（新規）・`pages/GuildsPage.tsx`・`types.ts`: 「（既定）」の表示と、欠損・組み込み・推定の注記
- `tools/console/backend/tests/fake_ssh_server.py`: 模擬出力を新しい項目に合わせる
- 説明文: `CLAUDE.md`・`README.md`（ver0.1.8(BETA) の不具合修正）・`tools/console/README.md`
- テストの修正（#245 の CI 失敗への対応）: ボット本体の `load_persona_catalog` を動かす子プロセスを `-X utf8` で起動する
  - 子プロセスは `-I`（隔離モード）で起動しているため、`PYTHONIOENCODING` が無視されていた
  - そのため英語版 Windows（cp1252）では、ボットの日本語の警告を標準出力へ書けずに失敗していた
  - 手元の Windows は標準出力が UTF-8 だったため再現しなかった

ボット本体（`src/`）は #222 の修正だけで、#223 はコンソール側だけの変更です。依存の追加はありません。

## 動作確認

Windows 11・Python 3.13（ボットとコンソールのバックエンドそれぞれの仮想環境）・Node.js 24 で確認しました。

| 確認内容・コマンド | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `python -m pip check` | 成功（No broken requirements found） |
| `python -B -m unittest discover -s tests`（ボット） | 1007件成功 |
| 全ソースの構文確認・メッセージ分割の確認（`CONTRIBUTING.md`） | 成功 |
| `python -m compileall -q src deploy tests tools/console/backend/remote_scripts tools/console/backend/tests tools/console/dev_launcher.py` | 成功 |
| `tools/console/backend`: `python -B -m unittest discover -s tests` | 217件成功 |
| `tools/console/frontend`: `node --test` | 137件成功 |
| `tools/console/frontend`: `npm run build`（`tsc --noEmit && vite build`） | 成功 |
| #222 の新テストを修正前の実装で実行 | 12件失敗（過去の時刻・再クレーム・夏時間開始後のずれを検出） |
| #245 の CI | Windows のコンソールのバックエンド4件が `UnicodeEncodeError` で失敗、それ以外の20件は成功 → `-X utf8` で修正（このPRの CI で再確認） |
| `python -I -X utf8 -c "import sys; print(sys.flags.utf8_mode)"` | `1`（隔離モードでも UTF-8 モードが有効になることを確認） |
| #223 の新テストを修正前の `insights.py` で実行 | 全件失敗。表示名だけの比較でも Issue の4構成すべてでボットと不一致 |

追加した主な回帰テスト:

- `tests/services/test_reminder_service.py`
  - 夏時間の終了・開始の前後を15分刻みで走査し、日次・週次・月次とも未来の時刻を返すことを確認
  - 二度目の時間帯からの追い付き、存在しない時刻を一度だけずらして戻ること
  - `Asia/Tokyo`・通常日・月末丸め・追い付き上限が従来どおりであること
  - 一時 DB で、同時刻の連続クレームで同じ予定を取り直さないこと
- `tests/core/test_database.py`: 現在以前の次回時刻で繰り返しを止め、再クレームしないこと
- `tools/console/backend/tests/test_remote_scripts.py`
  - 設定ファイルなし・`default` 省略・存在しない `default`・保存ファイルの欠損・テンプレートだけ・形の誤った保存値の各構成
  - `test_estimate_matches_bot_catalog_rules`: 8つの構成と11種の保存値について、ボット本体の `load_persona_catalog` と結果を突き合わせる
- `tools/console/frontend/tests/personaView.test.mjs`: 表示文と、バックエンドの出力項目・型定義の一致

## 未確認の範囲・壊れやすい点

- 実際の Discord・SSH 接続先・ブラウザでの画面表示は未確認です。実際の夏時間の切り替えでのリマインダー通知も未確認です（時刻を固定した単体テストと一時 DB で確認しました）。
- 夏時間の終了日に、停止明けの時点で既に1回目の時刻（例: 01:30 EDT）を過ぎていた場合、2回目の 01:30 では通知せず次の周期へ進めます（過ぎた回をまとめて通知しない従来の方針どおり）。
- ★ ボットの `personas.py` の一覧の作り方や保存値の扱いを変えたら、`insights.py` も直す必要があります。食い違いは `test_estimate_matches_bot_catalog_rules` が検出します。
- ★ `next_occurrence` の比較を壁時計どうしに戻すと #222 が再発します。

## セルフチェック

- [x] 差分にAPIキー・Discordトークン・個人情報・ローカルの絶対パスを含めていません。
- [x] 変更に応じた確認を実施し、結果と未確認の範囲を記載しました。

author: rfulwell
body:
## Why
Every file was served cache-first, so installed clients only got new code when someone remembered to hand-bump `SW_VERSION` in `sw.js`. Missing that once would leave everyone with the app installed on old data, including next year's nominees, until they tapped "hard refresh". This needs to reach existing installs before the 2027 nominations are announced.

## Changes
- **`deploy.yml`**: writes the commit's short SHA into `SW_VERSION`, so `sw.js` changes on every deploy. The step now fails if either the `APP_VERSION` or the `SW_VERSION` replacement doesn't happen.
- **`sw.js`**:
  - Pages and `.html`/`.js`/`.css`/`.json` files load from the network first and fall back to the cache when offline or after 3 seconds. A late network response still refreshes the cache.
  - Images stay cache-first.
  - Precaching bypasses the browser's HTTP cache, so a new worker never stores stale copies.
  - Cache keys ignore the query string, so every share link uses the one cached copy of the app instead of adding its own entry.
  - Google Fonts get their own cache that survives updates, so the fonts work offline.
  - Redirected responses are never cached.
- **`app.js`**: checks for a new worker whenever the app comes back to the foreground. Installed apps on iOS can stay open for days.
- **`playwright.config.js`**: reads the browser path from `CHROMIUM_PATH` instead of a hardcoded `/root/.cache/...` path.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: documents the caching rules, adds "never bump `SW_VERSION` by hand" and "`sw.js` must stay at `/sw.js`", and fixes the version format.

## Backward compatibility
- `sw.js` keeps its path, so the v9 worker already installed on clients finds this one and replaces itself normally.
- The only thing cleared on upgrade is the old cache of app files. localStorage isn't touched.
- The new upgrade test installs the exact v9 worker (`tests/fixtures/sw-v9.js`) with saved watched items and predictions, then upgrades it. It checks that the v9 cache is gone, the app loads, and the data is unchanged.

## Testing
- New `tests/service-worker.spec.js` has 7 tests: precaching, online loads come from the network, offline fallback, slow-network fallback, share links offline, no cache entry per share link, and the v9 upgrade. They passed 3–5 times in a row with no flakes.
- The online-load and share-link tests fail against the old `sw.js`, and the slow-network test fails if the fallback is turned off, so they do catch regressions.
- Full suite: 446 passed, 21 failed. The same 21 fail on `main` without this change:
  - The sharing tests use 21-character `?p=` links that stopped working when the app went to 24 categories.
  - A few nominee data checks disagree with `app.js`.
  - One source-link layout check fails.
- Ran the deploy's version step on a copy of the files: it produced `APP_VERSION = '1.2.119'` and `SW_VERSION = 'c54546a'`.

Merging deploys straight to production.

author: siggerzz
body:
## Why

Patch and digest updates merge straight into `main` with `ignoreTests: true`, so nothing checks them. The only CI is `flux-diff`, which posts a comment and can't fail. A broken update (a missing file, a chart version that doesn't exist, values a chart rejects) lands on `main` and Flux tries to apply it.

## What changes

**New `Flux Local` workflow** (`flux-local test --enable-helm`). It builds every Flux Kustomization and renders every HelmRelease through its chart, the same way onedr0p's home-ops did before they moved to their own tooling. It runs on:
- every PR to `main`
- every push to a `renovate/**` branch. Renovate's branch automerges never open a PR, so without this they'd have no check to wait on.

**Renovate: removed all four `ignoreTests: true`** (GitHub Actions, Helm patches, Docker patches and digests, mise tools). Branch automerges now wait for `Flux Local Test` to pass. If it fails, Renovate opens a PR instead of merging, so you see the problem.

It uses the same flux-local version (`v7.11.0`) as `flux-diff`, so Renovate updates both together.

## Checks

- Locally against `main`: **112 passed** in about 50 seconds.
- On a throwaway copy, a missing file in a `kustomization.yaml` failed the test, and so did a chart version that doesn't exist (sonarr `app-template` 5.99.0). Exit code 1 in both cases.
- `renovate-config-validator --strict` passes.

## Risk

None to the cluster. Auto-merges take a few minutes longer while the test runs. If a chart registry is down, auto-merges pause until the test passes again.

body:
Milestone B7 of the Schools plan (decision 0046, `docs/spec/schools.md` §11). The branch is merged with `main` as of #90; the chasing migration was renumbered to 00219 because `main` now carries 00217 (subflows) and 00218 (AI steps).

## What's in it (migration 00219)
- **Debtors:** `GET /v1/schools/debtors` (and `?format=csv`): every student with a balance on a sent term invoice, current and earlier open terms, by class. Aging by whole Lagos days past the oldest open invoice's due date: not due, 0–7, 7–14, 14–30, over 30, with totals per bucket. Filters by class, bucket, and promise or plan. Names masked unless `?reveal=true` (audited).
- **The reminder ladder:** `POST /v1/schools/reminders` with up to 50 students (more is refused with a clear message) and a rung, `Idempotency-Key` required; the whole result is stored under the key, so a retry replays it and sends nothing.
  - Grouped by family: one message per guardian naming every selected child with their balances summed, with a fresh family link via `SendFamily` (WhatsApp/Telegram where tapped in, else SMS).
  - Skipped with the reason: nothing due, no family, a promise not yet due, a plan in good standing or settled, or the family was already sent that rung today. Plans in arrears are reminded.
  - Wording per rung is a school setting with `{balance} {child} {account_number} {due_date} {link}`; unknown placeholders are refused and `{link}` is appended when missing.
  - `schools@1` `send_reminders` (students or a class, rung or `auto`, same cap) for the template.
- **Promises to pay:** `school_promises`, one open per student, note sealed, withdrawable. A promise past its date is decided once: kept if the balance moved, else `missed` (a Debtors flag and a notice to `school.manage`). Never deleted.
- **Plan standing:** `schools.PlanStanding(student, term)`: payments since the plan's approval against the instalments due so far, with `plan_grace_days` (0–60, default 0). `good`, `arrears` (with the missed instalments) or `settled`. Arrears are recorded once per instalment with one notice to bursars. Clearance is unchanged (B8).
- **Checks:** promises and plans are checked hourly on the invoice tick and on demand (`POST /v1/schools/chasing/check`).
- **Templates:** `school-fee-reminders` (two weekdays, `rung: auto`, up to 50 oldest-due first, then a summary to the owner) and `school-plan-decided` (every 15 minutes over decisions not yet told, sharing B6's once-only key, so it never double-sends; it tells the bursar when nobody could be reached). No new trigger type.
- **Web:** the Debtors page (aging totals, filters, select up to 50 with a counter, choose a rung, results with skips and why, record a promise, CSV, "Check promises and plans now"), reminder wording with a preview and plan grace in settings, promises and plan standing on the student page.
- **Docs:** `docs/schools.md`, `docs/templates.md`, and the plan's B7 Built note.

## Not yet
- A promise made on its due date is decided the day after.
- Template keywords avoid "debtors", "overdue" and "chase" so the existing reminder templates keep their place; `school-fee-reminders` needs "school" or "fees" in the goal.

## Checks
On the agent's tree before the merge with `main`: golangci-lint (0 issues), docsite, manifest validation, `aieval -compare`, Go tests for schools, connectors, templates, tools and the whole `./api/` (612s), `pnpm lint/typecheck/test` (web 450), Playwright 51/51 including a new `chasing.spec.ts`.
After merging `main` and renumbering the migration: build, vet, lint, docsite, validation and `aieval -compare` pass, and the db, schools, templates and schools-connector packages pass. The full Go and Playwright suites are running again on the merged head; any fix will be pushed to this PR.

## Why
Anthropic credits are exhausted, causing all 20 paid agent tasks to fail nightly. Separately, the weekly upstream vendor sync fails its pinned AIGF assertions (upstream has new risks/controls and changed OWASP references), so it never opens a reviewable sync PR.

## Changes
- Remove scheduled and PR-label triggers for `llm-evals`; use **manual dispatch only**, with an explicit unchecked `confirm_paid_api_calls` checkbox. Without that opt-in the tier-C job skips without making any Anthropic calls.
- Preserve the last actually measured baseline metrics; prevent skipped/unapproved runs from publishing.
- Keep free/offline deterministic and retrieval testing in normal CI.
- Run drift tests after vendor resync as before, but always create a reviewable upstream-sync PR when content changed; *then* mark the vendor-check workflow failed if the drift tests failed. Do not auto-merge changed upstream content.
- Update README to describe manual opt-in and the age of published agent metrics.

## Follow-up (separate PR)
Re-sync AIGF data and update targeted assertions / golden fixtures. Upstream now includes a new risk `ri-30`, mitigations `mi-24`/`mi-25`, updated OWASP LLM reference keys, and the merged upstream fix for the YAML issue reported in FINOS PR #380. Only change assertions after examining the source and verifying mappings.

## Validation
Review the GitHub Actions `ci` checks on this PR. No paid agent run has been triggered. A manual `llm-evals` dispatch with the checkbox unchecked should skip the tier-C job.

No changes to production server behavior or API keys.

Implementa `specs/rentas-fiscalizacion-v1.md`: expediente de fiscalización, ficha de inspección, RD por diferencias y multas (RM).

- **Fase A:** modelo y migración `20261025120000_rentas_fiscalizacion`, series `FIS`/`RM`, tributo `MULTA`, Maestros de fiscalizadores e infracciones (176.1, 176.2, 178.1) y reglas puras con tests.

- **Corrección:** lo declarado es, por cuota, lo mayor entre la cuenta corriente y lo que el motor determina sin la ficha. Antes, un predio inscrito por DJ y aún sin calcular se cobraba como omitido y con multa 178.1, porque el predial va por contribuyente. Esa parte sube sin RD ni multa.

author: francespo
body:
## Problem

The all-time dashboard (`meta-snapshot?days=0`) returned **26,174 lists with every pilot** to render **four cards**:

- **55 MB** of JSON (6.6 MB compressed)
- **16–27 s** to build, the single biggest item in the warm-up

The frontend sorts those lists by games / entries / win rate and shows the top four.

## Change

- New `lists_limit` query param (0 = all, default, so the public API is unchanged).
- When set, the snapshot keeps the **union of the top N lists by games, entries and win rate** (games >= 3, matching the frontend's win-rate filter) *before* fetching pilots. The visible top four is therefore present for every sort key.
- The dashboard sends `lists_limit=100`; the SvelteKit meta-snapshot proxy forwards the param.
- Warm list aligned with the real UI routes: dashboard default (**since last points update**), all-time and 90 days, xwa + legacy, all with `lists_limit=100`. The unused `time_range=points_update` duplicates are gone.
- Pages (lists, ships, squadrons, cards pilots/upgrades) were already warmed for **all-time and points-update**; their cache keys ignore pagination, so warming page 0 covers pages 1..N for the same filters. Verified on production: page 0/1/5/50 all ~90–125 ms.

## Measured (production data, local stack, cold)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| All-time dashboard compute | 27.1 s | **6.7 s** |
| Payload | 55.1 MB / 6.6 MB gzip | **666 KB / ~80 KB gzip** |
| Lists in payload | 26,174 | 211 |

Totals, factions, ships, pilots, upgrades: **identical**. Top 4 lists **identical for all four sort keys**, including the pilots shown in the cards.

## Tests

- Stable CI suite: **98 passed**.
- 3 new unit tests for the top-N union (leaders preserved, dedup, no-op when 0/large).
- `npm run check`: 0 errors.
- End-to-end comparison full vs limited on a production dump (above).

## Risk

Backward compatible: without `lists_limit` the endpoint behaves exactly as before. External consumers asking for the full list still get it.

body:
Closes #106

Hooks and skills run with the consuming project's cwd, so a bare `uv run` (or bare `python`) picks the consumer's venv, which has no `cc_*` modules. Every entry point now pins the plugin's own project:

- `hooks/hooks.json` — all 3 commands (`Stop`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`): `uv run --project \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\" python -m cc_...`
- `skills/speak/SKILL.md` — same prefix.
- `skills/listen/SKILL.md`, `skills/see/SKILL.md` — had bare `python -m cc_stt` / `python -m cc_vlm` (same failure, flagged as "likely" in the issue); now use the same prefix.

The braced `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` form is deliberate: per the [plugin reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#where-each-variable-resolves), skill Markdown bodies get `${...}` substituted inline when loaded, while the variable is **not** exported to the Bash tool's environment — so a bare `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in a skill would expand to empty. Hooks get it both ways; it's double-quoted per the doc's shell-form guidance.

New guard tests in `tests/test_plugin_config.py` (`TestCommandsResolveAgainstPluginRoot`): every hook command and every runnable `python -m cc_*` line in the three SKILL.md files must start with the pinned prefix.

Also: CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry; #106 removed from the roadmap's tracked list. Separate commit sorts the imports in `tests/test_setup_models.py` (pre-existing ruff I001 on `main`; same hunk as #138/#139).

## Done-when / verification

- Tests RED first (4 failed), GREEN after; `make validate`: ruff, pyright strict 0 errors, 408 passed. markdownlint clean.
- Consumer simulation: from another uv project's directory (own `pyproject.toml` + `.venv`), `uv run --project <plugin-root> python -m cc_vlm --help` resolves the plugin env and prints usage.
- **Not verified here:** the live `/reload-plugins` + `/speak hello` check from a consuming project — needs an interactive Claude Code session with audio. Owner to confirm after merge.

author: serchfga
body:
## Qué es

T-601, segunda de dos solicitudes: **los tramos del bote** (RN-13, RF-511, RF-707). La primera (los periodos) está en `main` desde la 59.

Decisiones de Sergio del 2026-10-23 que aplican:
- tramos marginales, con el porcentaje efectivo hacia abajo al punto base;
- alumno activo es una suscripción pagada vigente al último instante del mes: cuenta la gracia y la cancelada con días pagados; no cuentan cortesías, pendientes ni cuentas suspendidas por fraude;
- solo base: la pantalla (PA-85) y sus permisos, después.

## Lo que entra

Una migración, `t601_tramos`, y la semilla.

- **`pool_tiers`**, que escribe entero una sola función, `private.set_pool_tiers(periodo, umbrales, porcentajes)` (`security definer`, que nadie de la aplicación ejecuta todavía). Valida el juego: el primer umbral en 0, umbrales que crecen, porcentajes de 1 a `BOTE_PCT_TECHO` de su periodo que no bajan; sin techo, lanza. Cancela el juego que hubiera en ese periodo y escribe el nuevo. Solo en read committed, con un candado consultivo: un juego a la vez. Pide el código reciente, como un parámetro. Su guardián deja escribir solo al dueño de la tabla (desde esa función o la sesión del dueño), pone los autores y las horas, y de un tramo solo deja cancelar, una vez; no se borra ni se vacía. Auditoría de configuración.
- **El tramo de 0 es el porcentaje base.** `pool_bps` ya no lee `BOTE_PCT_BASE`: la función escribe la versión de `BOTE_PCT_BASE` del periodo cuando no es su tramo de 0, y la de cada periodo posterior con juego propio, para que el panel diga lo mismo. El servidor ya no la escribe ni la cancela por fuera.
- **RF-707 por instante**, para quien no es la sesión del dueño: un parámetro del reparto rige exactamente desde el inicio de su periodo, y ese periodo no ha empezado; ningún parámetro rige hacia atrás; no se cancela una versión que ya rige; y no cambia un tramo de un periodo que ya empezó. Lo revisa un disparador de restricción **diferido y sin `security definer`**, al confirmar, con el rol de la sesión y la hora del reloj. Es «sesión del dueño» la que entró como el dueño de la tabla y no cambió de rol: el servidor no hereda la excepción por correr dentro de una función `security definer`. El servidor solo puede preguntar dónde empieza un periodo (`private.period_start()`). Si cambia de rol antes de confirmar, la revisión falla cerrada, y una cancelación del sistema no se firma después. `guard_parameter_change` no cambia.
- **Los alumnos activos de un instante** (`private.active_students_at()`): cuentas activas y sin suspensión por fraude, con alguna suscripción no pendiente, creada a esa hora, que daba acceso por pago o por gracia según RN-01 (la gracia con el parámetro de la hora de la falla; sin él, lanza).
- **La foto**: al empezar la corrida completa de cada noche, antes de consolidar y de detectar, cada periodo abierto o en cierre que ya terminó recibe sus alumnos activos en su último instante y su porcentaje (columna nueva `payout_periods.pool_bps`; nulo si el mes no tiene juego), una vez, en orden y cada uno en su bloque. El guardián de `payout_periods` solo la deja escribir así. **Sin foto, el periodo no pasa a cierre** (el paso lo dice con `photo_missing`, y el guardián tampoco lo deja) y la corrida del paso termina fallida; esa corrida dice también qué fotos se tomaron.
- **`private.pool_bps()`**, misma firma: el guardado; si no, con los alumnos de la foto o, sin ella, los de ahora o los del último instante; tramos marginales; y **no baja**: si el periodo anterior tiene fila y juego, el mayor de los dos.
- **El vigilante**, el área `periods`, suma la tabla, las funciones (con sus dos excepciones: `period_start` la ejecuta el servidor, y ella y `set_pool_tiers` son `security definer`), los disparadores, y que los de RF-707 sean diferidos.
- **La semilla** escribe el tramo de 0 (60 %) desde 202610 con la función, y `BOTE_REGLA_TRAMO` pasa a decidido.

**`business_parameters` es común con el carril B** (hay que avisarle): gana dos disparadores (`business_parameters_origin` y `business_parameters_timing`), su índice único cuenta solo las versiones vivas (con `effective_from` atado al inicio del periodo, una cancelada impediría volver a programar el mes), y una cancelación ya no pide persona (la hace también el sistema).

## Lo que corrigieron las dos revisiones independientes del plan

1. El servidor podía cambiar el periodo en curso con un parámetro del reparto que empezaba en el pasado: ahora rige exactamente desde el inicio de un periodo que no ha empezado.
2. El disparador diferido fallaba al escribir el servidor y no funcionaba con las pruebas: los tramos se escriben con una sola función bajo un candado, y el disparador solo pide al servidor `period_start`.
3. La excepción del dueño se habría colado por cualquier función `security definer`: ahora es solo la sesión del dueño.
4. La foto no podía calcular su propio porcentaje y ningún periodo habría pasado a cierre; las pruebas que leen el porcentaje de un mes terminado se rompían el 1 de noviembre; un mes sin juego se quedaba abierto para siempre.

## Lo que corrigió la revisión independiente del diff

1. **(Alta, comprobado)** El servidor podía saltarse RF-707 cambiando de rol a `authenticated` antes de confirmar: así no veía la definición del parámetro y la revisión lo tomaba por uno que no es del reparto. Ahora falla cerrada.
2. Los tramos no pedían el código reciente (cambiar el tramo de 0 sí, por escribir `BOTE_PCT_BASE`): ahora sí, como un parámetro.
3. Una cancelación del sistema se podía «firmar» después: ya no.
4. Escribir los tramos de un periodo anterior desfasaba el porcentaje base de uno posterior con juego propio: ahora se escriben los dos.
5. El guardián de los periodos no exigía la foto para pasar a cierre: ahora sí.
6. Huecos de prueba: el disparador de RF-707 en los tramos, la gracia de la hora de la falla, los bordes iguales de los alumnos activos, mensajes exactos, y avisos para el carril B en el `CLAUDE.md` (la hora del reloj al confirmar, el índice de las versiones vivas, la cancelación sin persona).

Mutaciones a mano, función por función: 112, en una tanda limpia con una corrida sin mutar antes. Mueren 111; la que vive es equivalente (la restricción `payout_periods_pool_bps_with_students` rechaza lo mismo que el guardián). Una tanda anterior daba por muertas once de RF-707 que en realidad no compilaban (el guion recreaba mal un bloque); corregido el guion, dos vivieron y llevaron a dos pruebas nuevas.

## Pruebas

- **pgTAP `41_tramos`** (184): los marginales a mano en cada borde, cada validación, reemplazar un juego, la versión de `BOTE_PCT_BASE`, RF-707 como el servidor (también dentro de una función del dueño, cancelar y volver a programar, con la revisión diferida), los alumnos activos caso por caso, la foto, el guardián, el paso a cierre sin foto, `pool_bps` con «no baja» y su cadena, y el vigilante.
- **Integración `51-tramos`**: los marginales contra un oráculo en TypeScript (400 juegos al azar); los alumnos activos contra `resolveAccountAccess()` con cuentas y suscripciones al azar; dos juegos a la vez (el segundo espera el candado, aunque sea de otro periodo); fuera de read committed; y RF-707 al confirmar con la conexión de verdad del servidor. **`49-periodos`** ahora toma la foto antes del paso directo, revisa la foto en la corrida, y una foto que falla de verdad.
- Ajustes: la 04 (otro parámetro del reparto, desde el inicio de su periodo), la 33 y la 34 (el porcentaje de los tramos), la 40 (la foto antes del paso, la columna nueva), y la 26, 29, 30 y 31, que apagaban los disparadores de los parámetros y miraban el vigilante con ellos apagados.

## Verificación

- `typecheck`, `lint` y `test` (5 794).
- `db:reset` y `test:db` (36 archivos, 2 863), con `41_tramos` (184); `test:int` (39 archivos, 725), y `test:db` otra vez.
- `test:e2e` (130) y `test:e2e:equipo` entero (33).
- `pnpm db:orden`: la migración va despu

author: danialmesbahi
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"danialmesbahi"} -->
_Requested by **Dani** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01CmWHHYyTDbrG8FPTvcNXoS?thread=cmsg_01CmWHHYyTDbrG8FPTvcNXoSHfysUJuqdVC27VFBbFJWRA)_

Pre-launch bug sweep across the bot, payments, landing site and panel. Do not merge until Dani approves (merging to `main` deploys).

## Payments
- **Unverified payment recovery** (`app/main.py`, `app/services/payment.py`): every minute the bot asks ZarinPal (`pg/v4/payment/unVerified.json`) for payments it collected but nobody verified, and verifies the ones that belong to our unpaid orders. Before this, a customer who paid but closed the tab, lost signal or hit a busy server before our callback ran was never verified, and ZarinPal would reverse the payment. The fulfillment worker then sends the usual "payment succeeded" message with the form button. It runs only in production with `PAYMENT_MODE=zarinpal`. A failed listing only logs.
- **Callback concurrency**: callbacks used to get a plain-text 503 as soon as 4 verifications were running, and the Redis lock then blocked the customer's retry for 20 s. Now a callback waits up to 10 s for one of 8 slots. The lock is kept for 20 s only after a definite gateway rejection, so replay protection still holds, and in every other case it is released at once.
- **Retry pages**: every failure that can follow a real payment (verify outage, timeout, busy server, Redis down, DB error after a verified payment) now shows the branded page with a «بررسی دوباره» button. The button re-runs verification for the same payment. A browser that loads the callback twice gets a "checking…" page that refreshes itself.
- **Repriced or withdrawn course**: an unpaid order for a course whose price changed, or that was deactivated, is cancelled. It is no longer charged the old amount. Picking the course again starts a fresh checkout at the current price.
- **Double tap**: a second concurrent tap on the same course used to reply "این دوره قبلاً خریده شده". It now stays silent while the first tap sends the payment message.
- **Courses without a questionnaire**: the success page no longer says "complete the registration form". It links to the order instead.

## Bot
- During a profile edit, the generic edit handler (the edit router runs before the customer router) saved `/start …` links and main-menu buttons as the new value. That included the payment page's "back to bot" link and the site's buy links. They now leave the edit.

## Landing site
- When the panel had no active course, the site showed the placeholder programs with made-up prices, including in the JSON-LD offers. It now shows a short notice instead.
- When the panel API is unreachable, the placeholder cards hide their prices («قیمت دقیق در ربات»), and JSON-LD lists only live offers. `llms.txt` follows the same rules.

## Panel
- The catalog price error said the minimum is 1,000 toman. It now gives the 1,500 toman ZarinPal minimum the server enforces.

## Verification
- `pytest`: 284 passed. New tests are in `tests/test_payment_recovery.py`, `tests/test_security_regressions.py` and `tests/test_client_workflow.py`. The edit-swallow test fails without the fix.
- `alembic upgrade head`, `verify_client_workflow.py`, `check_secrets.py --tracked`: pass.
- site: `pnpm lint` and `pnpm build` pass. Rendered locally against a fake catalog API in three states: empty catalog, live catalog, API down.
- web: `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass.
- Not tested against the real ZarinPal API from here. After deploy, one real payment and the bot log (no `Could not list unverified ZarinPal payments` warnings) will confirm the recovery call.
